core_fields.title: AI-Powered Early Warning System for Crop Loss Prevention and Food Security
core_fields.description: DeepLeaf is building an AI-powered crop health intelligence system that detects diseases, pests, and nutrient deficiencies early using nothing more than a single leaf image. We deliver a real-time, field-level intelligence at scale, that enables farmers and agribusinesses to identify risks early, significantly reduce pre-harvest losses by more than 60%, cut unnecessary chemical use, increase yields, and produce safer, residue-free food in a more sustainable way.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder and commercial farmers alike lose a significant share of their harvest because crop diseases, pests, and nutrient deficiencies are often detected too late. By the time visible damage appears, yields have already dropped, chemicals are overused, and food quality is compromised. This challenge directly affects food security, farmer incomes, environmental health, and the affordability of safe food. This project addresses that gap through an AI-powered crop health intelligence platform that enables early, accurate detection of crop stress before losses occur. Using a simple image of a leaf and real-time field data, the system identifies hundreds of diseases, pests, and nutrient deficiencies across multiple crops and delivers clear, actionable recommendations. This allows farmers, agribusinesses, and public programs to intervene early, target treatments precisely, and make informed decisions at scale. The solution is grounded in advances in computer vision, machine learning, and agronomic science. By training AI models on diverse, real-world crop data, the platform recognizes subtle visual patterns invisible to the human eye signals that indicate emerging threats long before widespread damage. The immediate benefits include reduced pre-harvest losses, lower production costs, improved yields, and reduced reliance on blanket pesticide application. Over time, the project supports healthier soils, safer food, lower chemical residues, improved farmer livelihoods, and more resilient food systems. At scale, it strengthens national food security while promoting sustainable, climate-smart agriculture that benefits communities, consumers, and the environment.

core_fields.abstract: Food systems in emerging markets face persistent challenges: unsafe food, lack of transparency, post-harvest losses, unsustainable practices and low consumer trust. Smallholder farmers are often excluded from premium markets due to the inability to verify quality, origin and sustainability claims. WaziEats addresses this by combining blockchain for immutable data records and AI-driven analytics for quality prediction, risk alerts and supply chain optimization. 1.Farmers, aggregators, and processors upload production and handling data via mobile tools. 2.AI models analyze this data to predict spoilage risks, flag food safety issues and optimize logistics. 3. While traceability solutions exist, most are costly and inaccessible to small producers or focus only on compliance rather than farmer and consumer benefits. Immediate benefits include improved food safety, reduced losses, higher farmer incomes through access to trusted markets and informed consumer choice while Long-term benefits include more sustainable farming practices, reduced environmental footprint and more resilient and equitable food systems.

core_fields.title: Valorising Agricultural Sidestreams into Functional Food Ingredients through Koji-based Solid-State Fermentation
core_fields.description: This project will assess the feasibility of converting broken rice, rice bran and coffee husk, all agricultural sidestreams, into functional food ingredients using solid-state fermentation with Aspergillus oryzae (commonly known as Koji fungus). The project will generate foundational data on enzymatic profiles, fermentation performance data, and preliminary functional and scalability insights, demonstrating how underutilized agricultural by-products can be transformed into clean-label ingredients that enhance flavour, support salt reduction, and enable more sustainable food production.
core_fields.abstract: Large volumes of agricultural sidestreams such as coffee pulp or rice by-products are underutilized or discarded, despite containing valuable nutrients and functional compounds. At the same time, food producers face increasing pressure to reduce salt, sugar, and artificial additives while maintaining taste, affordability, and production efficiency. This creates a gap between available raw materials and scalable, natural solutions for healthier and more sustainable food production. This project addresses that gap by applying solid-state fermentation using optimized Aspergillus oryzae strains to convert agricultural sidestreams into functional food ingredients. Through controlled fermentation, the microorganism produces natural enzymes that break down complex compounds and generate flavour-enhancing and functional properties. The project will generate enzymatic profiles and fermentation performance data to assess whether a selected sidestream can be safely and efficiently transformed into a food-grade ingredient. The scientific insight behind this approach comes from research conducted by one of the co-founders, which demonstrated the strong substrate induction capabilities of A. oryzae. This research showed that the microorganism adapts its enzymatic output depending on the composition of the substrate, enabling targeted enzyme production when fermenting specific agricultural sidestreams. This insight informed the decision to use solid-state fermentation as a flexible and efficient method to valorise diverse by-products. Immediate benefits include reduced agricultural waste, improved resource efficiency, and new value streams for producers. Over time, this approach supports cleaner-label, lower-salt foods, more affordable nutrition, and more circular, resilient food systems benefiting producers, consumers, communities, and the environment.

core_fields.title: Automated modularized Solar-Powered Cold Storage to Extend Fresh Produce Shelf Life.
core_fields.description: This project develops automated modularized, solar-powered, pay-as-you-store cold storage units inside urban and peri-urban markets to reduce fresh produce spoilage among vendors. By extending shelf life by up to 15 days, vendors can avoid losses, stabilize daily income and reduce food waste. The solution is affordable, scalable and designed around vendors daily cashflow, bringing reliable cold storage directly where produce is sold.
core_fields.abstract: Fresh-produce vendors in urban and peri-urban markets lose a significant portion of their fruits and vegetables every day because they lack access to affordable and reliable cold storage. This problem is especially relevant in informal markets, where most vendors operate on thin margins, depend on daily cashflow and cannot afford traditional cold rooms designed for exporters or large agribusinesses. As a result, food spoils quickly, incomes remain unstable and large volumes of edible food are wasted. This project solves the problem by introducing automated modular, solar-powered cold units installed directly inside markets. Vendors rent on a pay-as-you-store basis, paying a small daily fee per crate via mobile money. The system extends produce shelf life by up to 10 15 days, allowing vendors to confidently stock more, reduce spoilage and avoid frequent trips to wholesale markets. The innovation is driven by a key insight: the biggest gap in the cold chain exists at the last mile of informal markets. By modularizing storage into small units with automation, IoT-based temperature monitoring and flexible pricing, cold storage becomes accessible to vendors previously excluded from the cold chain. Integration of second-life EV batteries ensures reliable, off-grid operation while reducing electronic waste. Immediate benefits include higher vendor incomes, reduced food losses and improved food quality for consumers. Long-term benefits include strengthened market resilience, improved urban food security, empowerment of women-led businesses and reduced environmental impact through lower food waste and sustainable energy use.

core_fields.title: From Waste to Food Security: Advanced Innovative Biopolymer Coatings for Sustainable Produce Preservation
core_fields.description: This proposal addresses global postharvest losses of fruits and vegetables, which waste resources and harm food security. The innovation introduces a biopolymer coating made from sodium alginate, valorized eggshell nanoparticles and essential oils, applied with robotic arms and packaged in biodegradable baskets. This coating extends shelf life by up to four weeks, offering controlled antimicrobial protection without synthetic preservatives. The solution is novel, sustainable, and scalable, reducing waste, lowering emissions, and improving profitability,
core_fields.abstract: Globally, 40 50% of fresh produce spoils before reaching consumers, particularly in regions where cold-chain infrastructure is limited. This problem reduces food availability, raises prices, wastes land and water resources, and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions from decomposing food. Our proposed innovation introduces a simple and advanced biopolymer coating that extends the shelf life of fresh produce by up to four weeks. The solution valorizes waste eggshells, converting them into spherical calcium carbonate nanoparticles. These particles are etched with hydrochloric acid in a mixture of alginate polymer and essential oils. The process releases calcium ions that crosslink the alginate, forming a protective gel coating, while the hollow nanoparticles absorb and gradually release essential oils with antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. Fruits are dipped in this coating solution using robotic arms for uniformity, instantly dried, and packaged in biodegradable porous baskets. This approach is novel because it transforms eggshell waste into high-value nanoparticles, introduces a controlled release mechanism for essential oils, and integrates robotic automation with sustainable packaging. Unlike existing methods that rely on direct essential oil application or synthetic preservatives, this solution is safer, more natural, and more effective. The scientific insight lies in recognizing eggshells as a rich source of calcium carbonate and engineering them into nanoparticles that both strengthen the coating and deliver natural preservatives. The benefits are immediate and wide-ranging: consumers enjoy fresher and safer produce, farmers and retailers reduce losses and increase profits, communities gain improved food security, and society benefits from reduced waste, and lower emissions

Many young people and women in urban communities lack practical skills, income opportunities, and access to safe food production methods. At the same time, cities depend heavily on long food supply chains and chemically grown food, which increases costs, environmental damage, and food insecurity. Project 5,000 addresses this challenge by training youth and women in organic vegetable gardening and providing them with a ready to use starter kit. This enables participants to grow food in small spaces such as backyards, containers, and unused plots. The food can be used for household consumption and sold locally to generate income, creating immediate livelihood opportunities and reducing reliance on unstable food markets. The solution is guided by proven urban agriculture and ecosystem restoration practices seen in cities such as Curitiba, Brazil, where urban gardens have improved food access, reduced waste, lowered emissions, and strengthened community resilience. Scientific evidence shows that small scale organic farming improves soil health, reduces chemical pollution, supports biodiversity, and lowers greenhouse gas emissions by shortening food supply chain.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Safety, Sustainability, and Equity in Raw Cow Milk Systems in Cambodia
core_fields.description: This project evaluates the microbial and chemical quality of raw cow milk sold in Phnom Penh to generate Cambodia s first baseline dataset for milk safety standards. Forty samples will be analyzed to identify contamination risks and nutrient status. The project also trains students and laboratory staff in food safety analysis and produces policy recommendations to support safer milk production, improved regulation, reduced foodborne risks, and greater consumer trust in locally produced dairy products.
core_fields.abstract: This project presents a comprehensive, evidence-based strategy for enhancing raw cow milk's quality, safety, and marketability in Cambodia. Combining scientific milk analysis with capacity building and policy translation a strategy not yet used in the nation's dairy industry is the fundamental innovation. The problem addressed is the lack of national data on microbial and chemical contaminants in raw cow milk. Without baseline standards, farmers lose money from spoiled and subpar products, consumers are exposed to preventable foodborne risks, and regulators are unable to effectively enforce the Food Safety Law. This gap is especially relevant as demand for fresh milk rises alongside Cambodia s growing dairy industry. The solution evaluates contamination, nutrient integrity, and quality indicators in market samples using standardized microbiological and chemical testing techniques. Insights from international Codex and AOAC standards guided the design, ensuring results that are scientifically valid and adaptable to national regulations. The project also strengthens laboratory and human capacity by training students, technicians, and early-career researchers in food safety analysis and quality assurance. Immediate advantages include better identification of contaminated milk, lower risk of foodborne illness, and increased trust in dairy produced locally. Farmers gain clearer guidance on hygienic handling and practices that reduce losses and improve product value. Regulators receive evidence to develop enforceable national standards. Long-term benefits to consumers, communities, and the environment include decreased waste, improved nutrition, and increased food system resilience as a result of the project's support for a safer, more sustainable, and more competitive dairy industry.

core_fields.title: Pumping water uphill to increase sustainable food production in remote areas
core_fields.description: Upland waterless communities are faced with migration to urban areas because of a combination of negative factors, leaving behind an aging population and threatened food security. The environment-friendly AIDFI ram pump reverses this process by making drinking and household water easily available in increased volume and by that solving the many water-related challenges and provide opportunities for vegetable growing and animal raising. After the set up of three installations in uncovered provinces, conferences will be held to popularize the technology.
core_fields.abstract: Among several locally developed technologies for basic needs of the poor, the AIDFI Hydraulic Ram Pump became the flagship since most households in waterless upland communities expressed easy access to water as their number one priority. The environment friendly pumps are installed in remote areas where most beneficiaries are engaged in subsistence rainfed agriculture. Lack of water limits the possibility to grow vegetables or raise animals around the house, and their farms have often just one crop which is endangered by sudden or prolonged droughts caused by Climate Change. There is no chance for a second crop or to diversify the farm. Combined with years of erosion and lowering production, young people migrate to cities. Through the AIDFI ram pump water is brought up 24/7 without electricity or fuel from lower situated springs, streams or rivers to the houses and farms. The uniqueness is that the AIDFI ram pump systems with locally available spare parts are packaged in a holistic program with training of local technicians, set up of water associations, monitoring app, after service sales and impact data gathering. The increased volume of water now easily available benefits the families in terms of health, sanitation, time and money saved, water-related livelihoods like vegetable growing and animal raising. The vegetables and meat are for consumption of the families for improved nutrition and sold for extra income on nearby local markets. AIDFI knows from previous installed system that there is an immediate decrease in illegal logging and charcoal making as result.

core_fields.title: Pigs to Plants and Graceful Garden
core_fields.description: Pigs to Plants is an innovative programme that supports informal farmers in South Africa to transition from farming animals to farming plants including indigenous vegetables and premium crops that build soil health as well as providing food, such as mushrooms. Graceful Garden is an added value brand that builds sustainability into the Pigs to Plants programme, supporting farmers during their transitions and enhancing their income whilst offering an attractive blueprint for replication elsewhere.
core_fields.abstract: Around 1.6 million pigs live in dire conditions in informal settlements and townships around South Africa.. The multiple negative impacts affect all of society - suffering of animals, degradation of the environment, extreme violence in the heart of vulnerable communities, spread of animal disease, zoonotic disease, risks to human health, parasite load and, because of agricultural subsidies of feed and medication, anti-microbial resistance. Informal pig farming is a time bomb waiting to explode in vulnerable Southern African communities. Pigs to Plants transforms all these negative impacts into positive impacts. Farmers surrender their pigs or trade out and in return receive training, resources and on-going support to build income generating vegetable gardens. Mushrooms are used to rebuild soils, support water retention and provide premium crops. The community, including children, no longer witness the violent deaths of animals. Spaces transform from filthy, parasitic holes into lush, verdant, green gardens. Food security is improved, replacing diseased animal flesh with nutrient dense vegetables. Farmers pass their skills on to family members including their children. The community unites to support one another. Our programme has been running for five years, has undertaken 17 transitions and all the above impacts have been recorded. The programme is currently reliant on grant funding and Graceful Garden will make it sustainable through the production of vegetable/salad packs and through reviving ancients skills of preserving and making sauces, pickles and other added value items that will render the whole programme sustainable and more attractive for replication in other areas.

core_fields.title: Nutri-Win: Climate-Smart Nutrition Innovation Empowering Smallholder Farmers and Strengthening Food Security in Nigeria
core_fields.description: Nutri-Win empowers rural smallholder farmers in Nigeria through climate-smart agronomic practices while producing and distributing highly nutritious Nutri-Win Cereal to vulnerable communities. By linking farmers to reliable markets, reducing post-harvest losses, and promoting nutrition, the project addresses food insecurity, malnutrition, and climate resilience simultaneously. Over 24 months, Nutri-Win will scale production, strengthen supply chains, deliver farmer training, and ensure equitable cereal distribution to improve health, livelihoods, and sustainable food systems, while promoting mutually beneficial collaborations.
core_fields.abstract: Nutri-Win is an integrated nutrition intervention and climate-smart food system innovation designed to tackle the interconnected challenges of malnutrition, food insecurity, and climate vulnerability in Nigeria. Millions of low-income households, especially children, pregnant and lactating women, and marginalized communities, lack access to affordable, nutrient-dense foods, while rural smallholder farmers face declining yields, post-harvest losses, and limited market access. Nutri-Win addresses these problems through a dual-impact model that combines the production of a highly nutritious, affordable, ready-to-eat cereal with a climate-smart smallholder farmers support programme. The innovation uses agro-processing technology to transform locally sourced climate-resilient crops (such as sorghum, millet, soybeans, and legumes) into Nutri-Win Cereal - a fortified, shelf-stable product that meets the nutritional needs of vulnerable groups. Simultaneously, Nutri-Win trains smallholder farmers in regenerative and climate-smart agronomic practices, enabling them to improve soil health, increase productivity, and strengthen climate resilience. Farmers are then linked directly to Nutri-Win as guaranteed off-takers, reducing post-harvest losses and increasing income stability. This approach emerged from insights in public health nutrition, climate-smart agriculture research, and food commercialization models showing that nutrition and climate outcomes improve most when local markets, smallholders, and vulnerable consumers are connected in a circular system. Immediate benefits include improved dietary diversity, reduced micronutrient deficiencies, higher farmer income, and reduced crop waste. Long-term benefits include resilient food systems, strengthened rural livelihoods, lower environmental footprints through regenerative practices, and consistent access to nutritious foods for communities historically left behind.

core_fields.title: Strengthening Nutrition in Staple crops through Climate-Smart Technology (SNIT Project)
core_fields.description: This project seeks to strengthens biofortified crops like Vitamin A maize and OFSP value chains by addressing crop segregation, traceability, and market access challenges. It deploys a digital traceability platform integrating geospatial and blockchain technologies to track biofortified crops from farm to market. The project improves food safety, aggregation, and commercialization while increasing incomes for over 2,000 women and youth farmers and processors within 24 months, contributing to improved nutrition and climate resilience.
core_fields.abstract: North Nigeria, using Kaduna State as a pilot, faces severe malnutrition, with over 60% of under-five children affected by Vitamin A deficiency due to weak food systems, poor post-harvest handling, limited access to fortified foods, and climate-related agricultural disruptions (UNICEF 2024; NBS 2022). A critical barrier in biofortification is the mixing of biofortified crops, such as Vitamin A maize and orange-fleshed sweet potato (OFSP), with conventional crops, undermining traceability, food safety, market differentiation, nutritional impact, and income incentives for farmers and processors. This project introduces a digital traceability and aggregation system to track biofortified crops from farm to market. Leveraging a mobile- and web-based platform integrated with geospatial mapping, blockchain technology, and AI-driven analytics, farmers and aggregators record production, location, and handling data. This ensures crops remain segregated, verifiable, and traceable throughout storage, processing, and distribution, while strengthening aggregation and market linkages. The solution builds on evidence from biofortification science, climate-smart agriculture, and supply-chain management, demonstrating that identity preservation, traceability, and market incentives are essential for sustained adoption. It integrates existing prototypes developed by Lutam Farms (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A_bTbQagUN-4UDc0hELbGCYeuwScsUE_/view?usp=sharing) and Meaningful Solution Ltd (https://mslgis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/f452c7716c324bb891c50919db84d5e3) into a single app, enabling real-time monitoring of climate risks and crop health, product authentication, food safety, and optimized processing and market planning for MSMEs. Immediate benefits include improved food safety, reduced post-harvest losses, and higher prices for farmers. Long-term impacts include increased adoption of biofortified crops, higher incomes for women- and youth-led enterprises, enhanced nutrition for consumers and school programs, and strengthened environmental and climate resilience

core_fields.title: The Soil Revolution: Scaling a Regenerative Fertilizer for Ethiopia's Food Security
core_fields.description: We are scaling the production and distribution of our patented, granulated organic fertilizer. Our innovative "Waste-to-Wealth" model restores Ethiopia's degraded agricultural land, directly boosting smallholder farmer income and climate resilience. This project is a commercially-driven, sustainable solution designed to enhance food security at its root, by rebuilding the health of our soil. It is a proven, de-risked, and market-ready innovation poised for national scale-up.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Ethiopian smallholder farmers are trapped in a poverty cycle driven by a critical market failure. Their soil is severely degraded, and the only solution offered, expensive, imported chemical fertilizer, further damages their land and erodes their profits. Our innovation is a systemic solution to this crisis. Solution: We use a patented granulation technology to transform methane-emitting urban organic waste into a high-quality, easy-to-use granulated compost. This insight that usability, not just quality, is the key to adoption that is what makes our solution unique. By creating a standardized, dry granule, we solve the core practical barriers (bulkiness, labor) of traditional compost. Benefits: The immediate benefit for farmers is a 40-60% more cost-effective input that boosts yields by a proven 15%+, directly increasing their income. The sustainable benefit is the restoration of their soil's organic matter, which enhances long-term fertility and builds crucial resilience to drought. For society and the environment, we mitigate methane, sequester carbon, and build a more food-secure, self-sufficient Ethiopia.

core_fields.title: Dairy Goat Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato Tree System: Rehabilitating Lands and Enhancing Child Nutrition in Ethiopia's Vulnerable Regions
core_fields.description: This project pioneers Ethiopia s first integrated dairy goat orange-fleshed sweet potato (OFSP) tree system with digital soil monitoring to reduce child stunting by 15% for 500 households in Gacho Baba District, Gamo zone. It restores 20 50 ha of degraded land, raises household incomes by $400 600, and empowers 300 women through cooperatives. Building on AMU-led pilots and partnerships with FAO, ICARDA, and CIP, it advances Ethiopia s Seqota Declaration, CRGE Strategy, and SDGs 2, 3, 5, 13, and 15.
core_fields.abstract: Ethiopia faces land degradation (34% of farmland) and child stunting (36.8%), driven by vitamin A, protein, and calcium deficiencies. Gacho Baba District (in Gamo Zone) faces 60 70% food insecurity, with stunting rates exceeding 40%, exacerbated by erosion, landslides, and drought (Tadesse et al., 2024a - 2025). This project deploys a closed-loop dairy goat OFSP tree system using Sesbania, Leucaena, and Moringa trees. It provides 200 300 ml of goat milk and 100 g OFSP daily per child, addressing nutrient gaps. Manure and crop residues recycle into compost, enhancing soil fertility by 25%. Women-led cooperatives and digital soil sensors ensure equitable access and scalability. Unlike single crop or livestock programs, this model uniquely combines biofortified OFSP, dairy goats, and nitrogen-fixing trees with digital soil monitoring to address malnutrition and land degradation simultaneously. It targets landslide-prone areas, linking nutrition with ecosystem regeneration. The system reduces stunting by 15% within three years, increases household incomes by $400 600 annually via milk and carbon credit sales, and strengthens climate resilience. Soil fertility improves, and biodiversity rises with tree integration. The initiative builds on AMU s successful pilots (+13% milk yield, +39.8% soil fertility, 70% adoption) and partnerships with FAO, ICARDA, and CIP for national replication.

core_fields.title: Year-Round Mushroom Value Chain: Sustainable Cultivation, Processing & Equitable Access to Trusted Healthy Diets.
core_fields.description: This project promotes year-round mushroom production and processing using sustainable, climate-smart practices to ensure a consistent supply of safe, nutritious, and affordable food. By integrating modern cultivation methods with local resource use, it reduces waste, supports smallholder farmers, and strengthens community livelihoods. The initiative enhances food security and equitable access to healthy diets while building consumer trust in locally produced, high-quality mushroom products.
core_fields.abstract: system using controlled-environment cultivation and circular bioresource management. Mushrooms are rich in high-quality proteins, vitamins (B-complex, D), minerals, and bioactive compounds such as β-glucans and ergothioneine, which enhance immune function and reduce chronic disease risks. Scientifically, the project employs optimized substrate formulations from agricultural residues (e.g., rice straw, sawdust, maize cobs) enriched with natural nitrogen sources to maximize mycelial colonization and yield. Technical innovations include the use of low-energy humidity and temperature control systems to maintain optimal growing conditions (24 30 C, 80 90% RH), enabling consistent production regardless of seasonal variations. Processing technologies such as solar-assisted drying and hygienic grinding preserve nutrient integrity while extending shelf life and minimizing post-harvest losses. Packaging uses biodegradable materials, supporting environmental sustainability. The project integrates Good Agricultural and Manufacturing Practices (GAP and GMP), ensuring food safety and quality traceability from spawn to finished product. Through farmer training, digital monitoring, and cooperative marketing, it builds capacity among smallholders, particularly women and youth. Sustainably, the system recycles spent substrate as organic compost, reducing waste and improving soil health. For end users, the project delivers affordable, nutritious, and trustworthy mushroom-based foods that support balanced diets, address protein deficiencies, and lower dependence on imported animal proteins. By linking science, innovation, and equitable access, this initiative advances resilient local food systems and contributes directly to the UN Sustainable Development Goals on Zero Hunger, Health, and Responsible Consumption.

core_fields.title: Agroprocessing, value addition and financing small holder farmers
core_fields.description: We are revolutionizing the agroprocessing industry with our cutting edge, sustainable dehydration techniques. Our state-of-the-art solar-powered greenhouses combines innovative technology with traditional drying methods, ensuring high-quality, nutrient rich products with a shelf life of over 72 months. We are committed to environmental sustainability, utilizing solar energy to power our operations and minimizing our carbon footprint. Our diverse product range, including versatile powders for smoothies and health-conscious snacks, caters to a growing market of health-oriented consumers.
core_fields.abstract: In our ongoing commitment to supporting smallholder farmers, we've identified a significant challenge they face in selling fresh farm produce at major marketplaces. Lack of access to cold storage, combined with power cuts and load shedding, further compounds this issue. To address these challenges, we've developed an innovative and cost-effective solution a sun drying process that leverages natural resources. Smallholder farmers often struggle to sell their fresh farm produce at major marketplaces due to the absence of cold rooms for storage. The reliance on markets to purchase all their farm produce leaves them vulnerable, especially in the face of power cuts and load shedding that impact those with cold storage facilities. In response to these challenges, we have introduced a sun drying process that provides a more accessible and affordable alternative for smallholder farmers. By harnessing natural resources like wind and the sun, we've created a method that not only addresses the storage issue but also preserves the vital nutrients in fruits, vegetables, and meat. Our sun drying process is a cost-effective alternative to traditional methods, eliminating the need for expensive cold rooms. Aside from the direct benefits to smallholder farmers, our sun drying process aligns with sustainable practices by minimizing energy consumption and relying on renewable resources, contributing to a more eco-friendly approach to agribusiness. We believe that the adoption of our sun drying process will not only empower smallholder farmers economically but also enhance the resilience of their communities by providing a reliable and sustainable methods.

core_fields.title: DIGIROOTS Digitising Regenerative Food Futures in Pakistan
core_fields.description: DIGIROOTS introduces a digital traceability and regenerative farming platform that connects smallholders, women farmers, and local markets. Combining blockchain, GIS mapping, and community-led innovation will enhance nutritious food production, reduce waste, and build climate resilience. Over 18-month pilot, it will engage 300 farmers (50% women) across Sindh and Punjab, achieve an estimated 20% reduction in food loss, and improve access to affordable, locally grown, and healthy food for more than 3,000 households.
core_fields.abstract: Pakistan s food systems face interconnected challenges of low productivity, post-harvest losses, poor nutrition access, and declining consumer trust. Smallholders, especially women and youth remain, marginalised from markets due to weak technology access, lack of transparency, and limited recognition of sustainable practices. The proposed digital platform introduces traceability and verification tools that connect regenerative producers with buyers through blockchain, GIS mapping, and mobile-based data entry systems. The initiative draws on CUSP s field experience in regenerative agriculture and inclusive market development. It digitises farm-level information to validate climate-positive practices, reduce food waste, and improve accountability across value chains. Integrated spatial data on soil health, water use, and food loss hotspots allows communities and policymakers to make evidence-driven decisions for food security. Global research by FAO and CGIAR shows that such systems can raise smallholder incomes by 25 35% while cutting post-harvest losses by up to 30%. Immediate outcomes include expanded market access, reduced transaction costs, and better income stability for smallholders. Schools and local nutrition programmes gain access to verified, affordable produce at consistent quality. Over time, the model will establish community-driven trust chains that enhance equity, affordability, and food safety. Grounded in regenerative agriculture and circular economy principles, the innovation aligns digital transformation with traditional food cultures. It strengthens both livelihoods and ecosystems, offering a scalable pathway for Pakistan to advance sustainable, transparent, and resilient food systems within planetary boundaries.

core_fields.title: Empowering Health Workers to Unlock Local Nutrition in East Nusa Tenggara
core_fields.description: In East Nusa Tenggara, we re proving that the solution to stunting is already in our backyards. The 1000 Days Fund trains community health workers to help families rediscover the nutrition all around them moringa in their gardens, fish from their seas, and protein from their herds. Through simple, joyful food education and local leadership, we re turning the myth of food scarcity into a movement for thriving mothers and children.
core_fields.abstract: East Nusa Tenggara (NTT), Indonesia, is often seen as food-insecure, yet it overflows with nutritious local foods moringa, fish, eggs, corn, and cassava. The real challenge isn t availability but awareness: families often overlook these local treasures and rely on instant noodles or rice-heavy diets that lead to chronic undernutrition and stunting. Our innovation flips this narrative by training community health workers (CHWs) to become nutrition coaches who teach families how to turn what they already have into balanced, diverse meals. Through the Kader Academy (our digital training platform) and hands-on mentoring in two NTT districts, CHWs learn to promote dietary diversity using local ingredients, home gardens, and simple recipes rooted in local culture. The scientific foundation comes from behavioral science and maternal nutrition research showing that trusted messengers especially women CHWs drive lasting change in food behavior. This model has been externally validated: CHWs trained through our system are 23 times more likely to conduct home visits, leading to measurable gains in antenatal care, breastfeeding, and stunting reduction. Immediate benefits include improved maternal diets, healthier pregnancies, and confident CHWs who lead with local pride. Sustainable benefits include reduced stunting, resilient village food systems, stronger local economies, and revived appreciation for indigenous foods proof that the solution to malnutrition is already growing in our backyards.

core_fields.title: Circular Sago: Turning Mill Waste into Affordable Farm Inputs
core_fields.description: We convert sago-mill liquid and fiber waste into peat-ready biofertilizer, biochar soil amendment, and a protein feed ingredient, distributed via women- and youth-led micro-franchises. A 12-month pilot with three mills in Meranti and Indragiri Hilir will cut effluent pollution by ≥60%, lower fertilizer costs 20 30%, and lift smallholder yields 15 25%, proving scalable economics for a circular, climate-positive sago economy.
core_fields.abstract: When sago is processed, leftover liquid and fiber often flow into village canals. People smell it, fish suffer, and the mill still has a waste problem. Just a few kilometers away, farmers grow food on peat soils that are sour and low in nutrients. They pay a lot for chemical fertilizer, but the results are disappointing. We close that gap. At the mill, we place simple, low-cost modules that turn sago waste into three peat-ready products: 1. Liquid biofertilizer: gently aerated and enriched with helpful microbes, then buffered with ash/biochar so it s low-salt and peat-friendly. 2. Biochar soil booster: made from dried press-cake to hold moisture and nutrients in peat. 3. Protein fiber: a dried, clean ingredient to cut poultry/fish feed costs. Local women and youth run micro-franchises to bottle, pack, and sell these products, with agronomy advice included, so farmers know how to use them and trust what they buy. Why this works: Sago waste still contains nutrients and carbon. With the right microbes and pH balance, it becomes a safe, effective fertilizer; biochar locks in carbon and improves fertilizer efficiency; the screened fiber becomes affordable feed. What it means on the ground: fewer complaints around mills, cleaner water, 20 30% lower fertilizer spending, 15 25% higher yields, and new income for local kiosks. Environmentally, we target ≥60% lower effluent load, avoid methane from open discharge, and store carbon in biochar. In 12 months with three mills, we ll prove the economics, certify quality, and reach about 500 participants.

core_fields.title: Circular AgriTech for Nutritious Food, Zero Waste, and Climate-Smart Livelihoods
core_fields.description: SEHub s circular farming model transforms organic waste into high-value insect protein and bio-fertilizer through BSF technology, supporting efficient poultry production and climate-smart urban gardening. The integrated system enhances nutrition, reduces food waste, and increases productivity while using minimal resources. By providing affordable inputs, training, and market linkages, the project enables vulnerable households to access nutritious, sustainable, and trusted foods, driving equitable improvements across local food systems.
core_fields.abstract: SEHub s innovation is a controlled, evidence-based circular farming model integrating Black Soldier Fly (BSF) bioconversion, safe poultry farming, and space-efficient urban gardening to improve nutrition, reduce waste, and reduce food costs in low-resource communities. It addresses high feed prices, limited access to nutrient-rich foods, and the growing challenge of unmanaged organic waste in urban settlements. Safety and scientific oversight are central to the design. SEHub was trained and technically guided by the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE) a global leader in insect research that periodically supports, monitors, and reinforces best practices in waste pre-sorting, quality control, and safe handling protocols across the BSF value chain. This includes guidance on mitigating heavy metal contamination risks, maintaining hygienic production conditions, and managing potential disease transmission points. The BSF lifecycle and its non-pest, non-vector nature are explained to farmers through structured training. Simple biosecurity measures protect poultry and gardens, while standardized rearing kits ensure safe and consistent technology transfer. The scientific basis of the solution lies in BSF larvae s proven ability to efficiently convert clean organic by-products into high-quality protein and nutrient-rich frass under controlled conditions. This lowers feed costs, enhances soil fertility, and minimizes environmental load. Immediate benefits include affordable, safe vegetables and poultry products, reduced feed costs, and new income opportunities. Long-term benefits include lower waste accumulation, reduced emissions, improved soil health, and stronger local food security. SEHub differentiates itself through its integration of ICIPE-backed safety protocols, community-based scaling, and practical, affordable implementation model.

core_fields.title: Making fish farmers climate resilient through sustainable aquaculture technologies and practices to ensure food security
core_fields.description: The project will provide fish farmers with a farm management platform and a water quality device that will enable them to obtain real-time advisory support and get water quality management tips on a daily basis. This will help them reduce high fish mortality and improve their yield and income while reducing methane emissions from fish loss. The project will reach 2,000 fish farmers in Ghana, of whom 45% will be females and young people.
core_fields.abstract: In Ghana, 7 out of 10 people depend on fish for their protein source. With declining marine fish, the potential of aquaculture to bridge the over 250M annual fish deficit gap is imperative, as this is at the intersection of food security, national nutrition support, and farmers' livelihoods. But fish farmers on average lose over 45% representing over 64,000mt of fish loss per production cycle to poor water quality and disease outbreaks. This leads to lost income, food insecurity, and methane emissions as a result of fish loss. Aquamet exists to solve this problem. We provide a locally manufactured solar-powered water quality monitoring device that provides critical water quality data remotely to fish farmers and gives them advisory and real-time recommendations to prevent disease outbreaks and fish losses. The solution imprvoes fish farmers yield by reducing fish mortalities and cuts methane emissions of fish loss.

core_fields.title: "Sustainable Food Systems Through Climate-Resilient Seeds, Market Access, and Farmer Empowerment"
core_fields.description: NOBA Africa Agro-Allied Limited is developing a Digital Marketplace and Smart Aggregation System that connects smallholder farmers directly to reliable buyers. The project combines a mobile trading platform with physical smart aggregation hubs for storage, digital weighing, quality testing, and logistics coordination. This system increases farmer income, reduces post-harvest losses, improves transparency, and strengthens market access for rural communities across Nigeria.
core_fields.abstract: The Digital Marketplace and Smart Aggregation System developed by NOBA Africa Agro-Allied Limited addresses one of the biggest challenges faced by smallholder farmers: lack of fair, reliable, and transparent market access. Farmers often depend on middlemen, receive low prices, face inconsistent demand, and lose a significant portion of their harvest due to poor storage and uncoordinated logistics. This reduces income, discourages investment in farming, and limits food system efficiency. Our innovation solves this by integrating digital technology with physical aggregation hubs. Farmers use a simple mobile platform to list available produce, view real-time market prices, and connect directly to verified buyers. At the same time, smart aggregation hubs provide digital weighing, quality verification, solar-powered storage, and data-driven logistics coordination. This dual approach ensures that farmers not only find buyers but can also preserve quality, reduce losses, and deliver efficiently. The solution is driven by insights from climate-smart agriculture, digital inclusion, and Nigeria s rapidly expanding mobile connectivity. Advances in digital traceability, low-cost sensors, and cloud-based data systems made it possible to design a platform that is both affordable and scalable for rural communities.

core_fields.title: Moody Pop: Scaling Affordable Fortified Porridge for Hidden Hunger
core_fields.description: Moody Pop is McLives flagship innovation: a fortified porridge flour and ready to eat porridge sold in biodegradable cups and retail packs. Made from soybeans, wheat, coconut and milk sourced directly from farmers and fortified with iron, zinc, vitamin B12 and folate, Moody Pop provides a complete meal in minutes. The product addresses malnutrition, food affordability and employment by delivering nutritious meals to busy urban students and workers at just about TZS 1,000 per serving.
core_fields.abstract: Moody Pop combines food technology, sustainable processing and inclusive distribution to solve a triple challenge: malnutrition, unaffordable nutritious foods and low farmer incomes. Unlike imported breakfast cereals or unfortified local porridges, Moody Pop is enriched with critical micronutrients and uses 100 % locally sourced ingredients. Our innovation lies in three areas: Product: we blend soy, wheat and coconut using a patent pending fortification formula that delivers iron, zinc, vitamin B12 and folate; the product comes as flour for household use and as ready to eat porridge kept hot in heat retaining paper cups. Processing: manual mixers, solar dryers and small‑scale mills enable low energy, zero waste manufacturing; coconut husks are repurposed as biomass fuel and nutrient losses are minimised. Distribution & packaging: electric cargo bikes and micro to franchised kiosks take the porridge directly to customers in schools, hospitals and bus terminals, while biodegradable cups and recyclable paper bags reduce plastic waste. By integrating local sourcing, micronutrient fortification, green processing and last mile delivery, Moody Pop offers a unique, affordable and nutritious product that is unmatched by competitors.

core_fields.title: Coffee Waste to Circular Cellulose for Food Packaging
core_fields.description: Hera Materials develops circular, compostable biomaterials to replace single-use plastics in the food supply chain. We currently use biomass and cellulosic residues to produce packaging that is recyclable as paper and home-compostable. Through this project, we will develop a biological process to transform coffee waste collected from local caf s into high-quality cellulose, using bacteria and enzymes, to integrate it as an input for Woodpack and strengthen the circular economy.
core_fields.abstract: Hera Materials develops circular, compostable biomaterials designed to replace conventional plastics used in food packaging. Our materials are currently based on biomass and cellulosic residues, enabling the production of flexible films that are recyclable as paper and home-compostable. The problem we address is twofold: the significant environmental impact of single-use plastics and the underutilization of high-volume food waste, such as spent coffee grounds, which are currently disposed of mainly in landfills. Through this project, we will conduct research and development to transform coffee waste collected from Caf Le n, Ritual N made, and Caf Circular into high-quality, high-density cellulose. This process will be carried out using bacteria and enzymes, in collaboration with Codebreaker.bio. The resulting cellulose will be integrated as an input into Woodpack, and the process will be designed to be replicable and accessible, allowing future adaptation to other food residues with similar characteristics. Formulation optimization will be supported by our artificial intelligence platform, Marie Curie AI. The benefits include reduced plastic waste and coffee residue, the creation of local value chains, and progress toward more circular and resilient food systems.

core_fields.title: Scaling Community-Based Group Buying to Reduce Food Waste and Improve Access in Ethiopia
core_fields.description: This project expands a community-based group buying model that reduces food loss and makes nutritious food more affordable for Ethiopian households. By pooling household orders and delivering to organised group points, logistics costs fall and fewer products spoil in transit. ChipChip also sources directly from farmers using production data to match supply with demand. The approach lowers prices for families and provides farmers with a more predictable sales channel.
core_fields.abstract: On the supply side, ChipChip sources produce directly from farmers through trained sourcing coordinators. We maintain production data from over 1,500 farmers, including harvest timing, expected volumes, and crop types, which helps us plan procurement and reduce uncertainty for growers. Farmers benefit because they can sell larger volumes at once and avoid price pressure from intermediaries. Consumers benefit from fresher products and savings of up to 20 25% on everyday foods. The core mechanism is straightforward: when household demand is pooled into group orders and routing is coordinated, unit logistics costs fall and less food is lost in transit. By strengthening community-based logistics, the model reduces waste and makes nutritious food more accessible. Ethiopia s food system faces significant inefficiencies that contribute to widespread food insecurity, defined as a lack of regular access to affordable, nutritious food. More broadly, in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), an estimated 30% of total production is lost post-harvest, equating to over $4 billion lost each year. The core challenge is not insufficient production but a supply chain that lacks coordination, capital, and infrastructure. Farmers often sell at lower farmgate prices due to limited market access, while many urban families spend a large share of their income on food that has moved through several steps before reaching them. ChipChip adapts the Ethiopian group-buying tradition Kircha into a digital, community-based ordering system. core_fields.title: Sprouted Sorghum for Sustainable and Nutritious Food Systems in Kenya
core_fields.description: Kiasili Farm s Sprouted Sorghum for Sustainable and Nutritious Food Systems in Kenya empowers smallholder farmers to grow and process climate-resilient sorghum using regenerative practices. The project links farmers to premium markets through value addition, improving household income while enhancing food security and soil health. By integrating Indigenous crops, green finance, and digital tracking via the Jazamiti App, Kiasili drives equitable, low-carbon food systems that nourish people and the planet.
core_fields.abstract: Kiasili Farm s innovation Sprouted Sorghum for Sustainable and Nutritious Food Systems in Kenya addresses the twin challenges of malnutrition and climate vulnerability among smallholder farmers. In Kenya, over 30% of households face food insecurity, and traditional grains like maize are increasingly failing under erratic rainfall and poor soils. Meanwhile, Indigenous and Traditional Food Crops such as sorghum remain undervalued, despite their resilience, high nutritional value, and cultural significance. Our innovation transforms sorghum into a value-added, sprouted product that enhances its nutritional profile, digestibility, and market appeal. The process involves controlled germination and solar-powered drying, developed through local research on bioavailability of micronutrients in sprouted grains. Farmers are trained in regenerative agriculture and connected to markets such as 254 Brewery where they earn up to 50% more per kilogram for value-added sorghum. We also integrate climate and digital innovation through the Jazamiti App, which tracks tree planting, soil health, and carbon sequestration, aligning with Kenya s goal of planting 15 billion trees by 2032. This data-driven approach creates transparency, access to carbon credits, and better ecosystem management. Immediate benefits include increased farmer income, improved nutrition, and reduced food waste through crop diversification. Sustainable benefits extend to restored soils, carbon sequestration (6 metric tons to date), and greater resilience for rural communities facing climate stress. By merging Indigenous knowledge, agri-fintech tools, and science-backed processing, Kiasili is reimagining local food systems as engines of equity, nutrition, and planetary health.

core_fields.title: Climate-Smart Orchard Revolution: Model Nursery for Nutrition, Livelihoods, and Biodiversity
core_fields.description: This project will establish a scalable climate-smart fruit tree hub in Zimbabwe to strengthen resilient, sustainable food systems. Using grafting and polybag nursery management, the hub will produce mango, citrus, and avocado seedlings that fruit within 2 3 years and survive above 80%. It will train 100 women and youth, distribute 15,000 seedlings, and enhance biodiversity, planetary health, diets, and rural livelihoods, supporting Seeding the Future s goals for resilient nutrition, inclusive empowerment, and sustainable food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Zimbabwe s smallholder fruit tree sector faces critical constraints: poor-quality seedlings cause delayed fruiting, reduce survival, and weaken the resilience of local food systems. This innovation establishes a scalable fruit tree hub that produces high-quality, climate-resilient grafted seedlings year-round. Grafting joins elite scion wood from disease-resistant mango, citrus, and avocado varieties to well-adapted rootstocks, producing uniform trees that fruit within 2 3 years instead of 7 10 years for seed-grown plants. Polybag nursery management ensures seedlings are grown in sterilized media, improving nutrient uptake, reducing disease pressure, and minimizing transplant shock. This approach consistently achieves 75 85% survival rates, enabling reliable orchard establishment and enhancing the resilience of smallholder food systems. Over 24 months, 100 women and youth will be trained in grafting and nursery management, creating local champions capable of replicating the hub model. The hub will produce and distribute 15,000 superior seedlings to households, schools, and community groups. Perennial orchards will stabilize soils, restore biodiversity, improve planetary health, diversify diets, and generate income, enhancing food system resilience. Immediate benefits include access to high-quality planting material, improved nutrition, and livelihood opportunities for women and youth. Long-term impacts encompass strengthened agroecosystems, gender-inclusive economic empowerment, sustainable orchard expansion, and contributions to resilient, equitable, and biodiversity-supportive food systems, fully aligning with Seeding the Future s Global Food Systems thrust and its three focus areas: resilient nutrition, empowerment, and planetary health.

core_fields.title: Sewage Sludge-based Biochar
core_fields.description: SoilLogia transforms sewage sludge into biochar, creating a sustainable soil amendment while capturing carbon. Our approach reduces waste, improves soil health, and mitigates climate change. Currently pre-revenue, we are conducting chemical analysis and pilot studies to optimize biochar quality. Funded by the founder, this project demonstrates a practical, scalable solution at the intersection of agriculture, waste management, and carbon removal.
core_fields.abstract: SoilLogia addresses two urgent problems: the accumulation of sewage sludge as waste and the loss of soil health in agricultural systems. Sewage sludge disposal contributes to environmental pollution, while degraded soils reduce crop productivity and resilience. Our innovation converts sewage sludge into biochar, a stable, carbon-rich material that can be applied to soils. This approach leverages pyrolysis technology, transforming waste into a valuable soil amendment while simultaneously sequestering carbon, helping mitigate climate change. The solution emerged from scientific insights showing that biochar improves soil structure, increases water retention, enhances nutrient availability, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions from soil. Immediate benefits include improved soil fertility for farmers, reduced waste management costs for municipalities, and a scalable pathway for carbon removal. Longer-term sustainable impacts extend to enhanced food security, healthier soils, and reduced environmental pollution, benefiting communities and ecosystems. By turning a problematic waste stream into a practical agricultural input, SoilLogia creates a closed-loop, circular solution that aligns environmental and agricultural needs. This innovation is relevant and timely as governments and organizations worldwide seek low-cost, scalable methods for carbon sequestration and sustainable agriculture. By demonstrating that sewage sludge can be safely and effectively converted into biochar, SoilLogia bridges waste management, climate mitigation, and soil restoration in a single, science-backed solution.

core_fields.title: Establishing Replate in India

core_fields.abstract: Replate uses technology to provide a seamless experience for donors to donate surplus food. They use our website to easily schedule pickups. We also have the ability to support various kinds of corporate structures, allowing us to support many different kinds of donors. We provide detailed impact statistics, graphs, charts, and reports to donors to track donations over time, driving source reduction and encouraging nutritious donations. Given the population and scale of India, there is scope for immense human impact here. Food recovery qualifies as a valid CSR activity. As a Section 8 NGO Replate will seamlessly fit into a company's CSR goals. Our platform easily provides all documentation required by law, and much more receipts, weights, impact stats etc.

core_fields.title: Escalating a novel design of a Seed Planter into the African Continental Free Trade Area
core_fields.description: The initiative proliferates outcomes of a Innovate UK project previously conducted within North-Eastern Nigeria, into the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACFTA). It features the design and adaptation of a novel seed planter to soil properties within four ACFTA nations. Critical properties of soil are exploited with finite element analysis and mechanical optimization to enhance planter performance. The planter's design parameters are therefore sustainably optimized to reflect the strenuosity of soils within four ACTA nations.
core_fields.abstract: Prevailing Poverty and hunger in the African Continental Free Trade Area (ACFTA) are principally due to relatively low production capacities, consequently causing over reliance on costly imported goods. Most small and medium scale farmers are unable to afford heavy agricultural machinery for their moderately sized expanse of land. They therefore rely on arduous farming techniques to cultivate these lands. Secondly, the life span of certain imported agricultural machinery is usually short since they are rarely adapted to unique soil profiles of the ACFTA terrain. Thirdly, the importation and transportation of agricultural machinery into ACFTA is contributing to global emission of greenhouse gases. This innovation addresses these issues from a planting perspective, by exploiting outcomes realized from a preliminary project. This project redesigns a planter with a computer aided engineering technique by exploiting certain localized soil properties, such as bulk density and penetration resistance of the indigenous ACFTA soil. This would efficiently advance several sustainable development goals especially goals 1(No poverty), 2 (Zero hunger) and 3(Good health and wellbeing). On the preliminary project, our approach increased planter sales by six folds with several positive feedback from farmers in northeastern Nigeria. This novel planter has the propensity to benefit the vast populace in ACFTA, however, there is a need to adapt its features to soil profiles in the ACTA region. The innovation sustainably ameliorates the arduous planting duties of farmers while minimizing soil compaction arising from excessive utilization of expensive machinery, consequently enhancing root health, plant growth and crop yield.

core_fields.title: Seaweed for Climate-Resilient Livelihoods and Carbon Credit Innovation
core_fields.description: This project empowers small-scale seaweed farmers in the Philippines by integrating sustainable seaweed cultivation with carbon credit generation and market access. Farmers receive training, monitoring tools, and support to participate in verified carbon credit programs, creating additional income while promoting climate resilience. By linking livelihoods, environmental stewardship, and inclusive value chains, the project strengthens food system sustainability, diversifies farmer revenue, and demonstrates a scalable model for regenerative coastal economies.
core_fields.abstract: The project addresses the dual challenges of low incomes for small-scale seaweed farmers and the underutilized climate mitigation potential of seaweed cultivation. Coastal farmers in the Philippines rely on seaweed as a primary livelihood but face volatile market prices and limited access to financial incentives. At the same time, seaweed sequesters carbon, yet farmers receive no direct benefits from this ecosystem service. Our innovation combines inclusive value chain development with carbon credit monetization. Farmers are trained in sustainable cultivation, monitoring, and data collection, enabling participation in verified carbon credit programs. A digital or cooperative platform connects farmers to buyers, markets, and carbon registries, ensuring transparent tracking of both product sales and carbon sequestration. Scientific insights on seaweed growth rates, carbon uptake, and coastal ecosystem interactions guide monitoring and verification processes. Immediate benefits include increased and diversified income streams, enhanced climate resilience, and access to markets for smallholder farmers. Communities gain improved livelihoods, strengthened local food systems, and engagement in regenerative environmental practices. For society and the environment, the project promotes sustainable aquaculture, reduces carbon emissions, and demonstrates a scalable model for integrating food production with climate action. By aligning economic incentives with environmental stewardship, this approach empowers farmers to sustain their livelihoods while contributing to global climate solutions. This solution is relevant because it directly ties economic benefits to regenerative practices, creating a self-reinforcing system where farmers are financially motivated to adopt sustainable techniques, producing measurable outcomes for climate mitigation, local food security, and community resilience.

core_fields.title: Development and Field Validation of Solid-Phase Citronella Repellent Blocks for Fruit Fly IPM in Tanzania
core_fields.description: Fruit flies cause major horticultural losses in Tanzania, yet current Integrated Pest Management (IPM) lacks a durable repellent. This project will develop and field-tests a long-lasting solid-phase citronella repellent block made from locally sourced wax, providing a cost-effective Push component. Integrated with existing Pull traps, the system will reduce infestation, improve fruit quality, and offer smallholders a sustainable, non-chemical, locally manufacturable solution to enhance yields, market access, and regional food security.
core_fields.abstract: Fruit flies cause substantial losses of up to 80% in Tanzania s horticultural sector, limiting farmer income and blocking access to lucrative export markets. Current control methods are costly, short-lived, and mostly depend on chemical sprays that affect consumers' and farmers' health. A significant limitation in fruit fly integrated pest management (IPM) has been the lack of a durable and affordable repellent that can protect fruit throughout the season. This project introduces a solid-phase citronella repellent block, a simple yet scientifically proven innovation that gradually releases natural citronella essential oil using a wax base. Citronella is recognized for its ability to deter major fruit fly species, but its efficacy in liquid form diminishes rapidly. When integrated into solid wax, it provides a long-lasting, weather-resistant, and non-toxic repellent that can remain effective for several weeks to months. The innovation is based on three primary insights: Fruit fly behavior: they avoid citrus-scented and citronella volatiles. Material science: wax matrices can stabilize essential oils and provide controlled, steady release. Local feasibility resources: Tanzania has ready access to beeswax, citronella oil, and basic molding technologies. By integrating these blocks with existing pull controls such as male annihilation traps, farmers gain a robust push-pull system that reduces infestation without relying on synthetic insecticides. Benefits include: Increased marketable produce and reduced losses Affordable, locally manufacturable technology Greater food security and income stability for smallholders. An eco-friendly option that is safe for households, academic institutions, communities, biodiversity, producers and society.

core_fields.title: Thandizani: Community-Driven Innovation for Resilient Food Systems in Lundazi
core_fields.description: Thandizani's Lundazi project advances the Seeding The Future Global Food System Challenge by fostering inclusive, community-driven innovation. The initiative reduces food insecurity, improves livelihoods, and ensures equitable access to nutritious diets. By uniting farmers, researchers, and entrepreneurs, it drives scalable innovations that strengthen resilience, sustainability, and equity, building a future-ready food ecosystem that uplifts communities while safeguarding the environment.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description The Lundazi initiative introduces a community-driven model that integrates indigenous knowledge with modern agricultural practices to build resilient food systems. The problem it addresses is persistent food insecurity, driven by climate variability, limited access to resources, and inequitable food distribution. This challenge is highly relevant as rural communities face rising vulnerability to hunger and malnutrition, threatening both livelihoods and long-term sustainability. How the Problem is Solved The solution lies in empowering local communities to co-create innovations such as climate-smart farming techniques, diversified crop production, and inclusive market linkages while embedding modern insights like soil health management, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and digital tools for knowledge sharing. By valuing traditional wisdom alongside scientific advances, the initiative ensures solutions are culturally appropriate, practical, and widely adopted. Scientific and Technical Insight The approach is informed by agroecology and systems thinking: recognizing that food security depends not only on yields but also on biodiversity, equitable access, and environmental stewardship. Insights from climate science, nutrition research, and participatory development shaped this integrated solution. Immediate and Sustainable Benefits Consumers & Schools: Access to diverse, nutritious diets improves health and learning outcomes. Farmers & Producers: Increased yields, reduced risks, and fairer market opportunities strengthen incomes. Communities & Society: Greater resilience to climate shocks, reduced poverty, and stronger social cohesion. Environment: Sustainable practices protect soils, conserve water, and preserve biodiversity. By merging local wisdom with modern science, the initiative creates lasting pathways to food security, equity, and environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Spiral School Gardens: Water-Smart Outdoor Classrooms for Ethiopia
core_fields.description: Our project turns Ethiopian schoolyards into outdoor living classrooms built around water-smart spiral gardens. Each 50-foot spiral grows a mix of vegetables, beans, and herbs using minimal water, while students learn simple, practical lessons in science, nutrition, and farming. We will build three spiral gardens with local partners, support school meals, inspire home gardens, and create an easy-to-copy model that helps families improve diets and resilience in the dry regions of Ethiopia.
core_fields.abstract: In many parts of Ethiopia, families rely on small, rain-fed farms and children eat too few vegetables and pulses. Drought, poor soils, and limited water make it hard to grow enough healthy food, and most teaching about agriculture and nutrition happens only on a blackboard. Students rarely get practical skills they can use at home, and schoolyards are often bare, unused spaces. Our innovation is the Spiral School Garden: a 50-foot, water-smart spiral bed that turns a schoolyard into an outdoor living classroom. The spiral layout and simple drip or root-tube irrigation system concentrate water at plant roots, protect soil with mulch, and make it easy to grow many crops in a small area. Students sit between the rows while teachers use the garden for lessons in science, nutrition, math, and basic farming. This solution grew from two insights: first, that circular planting patterns and targeted irrigation can increase yield per square metre while using far less water; second, that children learn and remember more when they can see, touch, and taste what they are being taught. Immediate benefits include fresh vegetables and beans for school meals, more engaging classes, and simple home-garden ideas that students share with their families. Over time, Spiral School Gardens can improve diet diversity, strengthen local farming skills, conserve water and soil, and help schools and communities become more resilient to a changing climate.

core_fields.title: Harvest Heroes (Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Success)
core_fields.description: Our project utilises precision farming technology, specifically drones, sensors, and AI, to implement organic farming techniques by monitoring soil and crop data, including soil health, elevation, water level, nutrient levels, pH, and crop health. The implementation of our data-driven approach ensures improved crop performance through climate-smart, precise application of agricultural inputs like fertilisers using spray drones, minimising waste and increasing yield by up to 20%.
core_fields.abstract: The Harvest Heroes Project introduces a precision agriculture innovation that helps smallholder farmers overcome the chronic challenges of low yields, pest outbreaks, crop diseases, and climate-induced flooding. Many farmers in the communities we work, still rely on guesswork for planting, spraying, and monitoring their crops, leading to wasted inputs, financial losses, and unstable food production. This problem is especially relevant today as climate change intensifies unstable weather conditions and increases the vulnerability of rural farming communities. Our solution uses drone technology, AI-powered crop monitoring, and real-time weather and field data to give farmers clear, actionable insights on the health of their crops. Drones detect early signs of pests, diseases, nutrient stress, and flood risks, while precision spraying ensures the exact amount of fertilizer or pesticide is applied only where needed. This reduces waste, lowers production costs, and protects the environment. The scientific insight behind this innovation comes from combining remote sensing, GIS mapping, and plant health indices, which are already used in advanced commercial agriculture but are rarely accessible to these smallholder farmers. By simplifying this technology into an easy-to-use service model, the Harvest Heroes project brings world-class crop intelligence directly to underserved farmers. The benefits are immediate and long-term: Farmers see higher yields, reduced input waste, and improved profits. Communities gain a more stable food supply and climate resilience. Consumers enjoy safer and more reliable produce. and The environment benefits from reduced chemical overuse.

core_fields.title: Wastexus: Mobile Sensor-Driven Waste-to-Resource System for Safe Irrigation and Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: Over 38 million Nigerian smallholder farmers struggle with unsafe water, poor sanitation, and declining soil health. This project brings a mobile, affordable waste-to-resource system directly to rural communities, transforming harmful waste into safe irrigation water and usable nutrients. By making water cleaner, crops safer, and farming more sustainable, the solution empowers farmers, protects families, and builds healthier, more resilient food systems where they are needed most.
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria s agricultural communities face a critical challenge: untreated waste contaminates soil, water sources, and food, increasing disease risks and reducing crop productivity. With limited sanitation infrastructure especially in rural areas, farmers often rely on unsafe water for irrigation, threatening food safety and undermining the resilience of local food systems. Our innovation, a mobile, sensor-driven waste-to-resource system, directly addresses this challenge by transforming wastewater into safe irrigation water and recoverable nutrients at the point of need. Designed as a compact, portable unit powered by a hybrid solar battery system, it operates reliably in off-grid farming communities, independent of an unstable national electricity supply. This mobility eliminates reliance on costly centralized treatment plants and enables decentralized sanitation where infrastructure is weak or nonexistent. The system integrates biological treatment, membrane filtration, and real-time sensor monitoring to ensure effluent meets safe reuse standards. Continuous sensing of key struvite ions (magnesium-nitrogen-phosphorus), pH, temperature, turbidity, and flow parameters optimizes treatment efficiency and guarantees safety. The scientific insight behind this solution combines environmental biotechnology with low-energy, membrane-based separation to achieve effective pathogen removal while retaining valuable nutrients. Immediate benefits include access to clean irrigation water, reduced contamination risks, healthier soils, and improved crop quality. Long-term impacts include lower disease burden, reduced environmental pollution, stronger food safety, and greater agricultural resilience. By recovering nutrients, the system supports regenerative agriculture and reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers. Ultimately, this innovation provides an affordable, scalable pathway for rural communities to safeguard health, increase productivity, and build a more sustainable, circular food system.

core_fields.title: Farm and Flourish Madagascar
core_fields.description: This project scales a proven conservation agriculture and stewardship model to at least 45,000 additional smallholder farmers in rural Madagascar from 2026 2028, using a hub-and-spoke, demonstration-plot approach. Farmers learn to feed a family of six on 1/16 ha with yields 4 9 times higher than conventional practice while restoring soils and reducing input waste. Evidence from Zimbabwe and Rwanda shows national-level impacts on maize and rice yields and erosion reduction, now being replicated in Madagascar.
core_fields.abstract: In Madagascar, most rural families depend on 1 2 ha of land yet still face chronic food insecurity, soil degradation, and vulnerability to climate shocks. Conventional responses (food aid, input subsidies, mechanization, and credit) are costly, hard to sustain, and inaccessible. The core problem is not simply low yields, but also a missing practical system that helps farmers transform very small plots and limited cash into reliable, climate-resilient food and income. The innovation combines a highly specified regenerative micro-plot system ( Pfumvudza ) with integrated financial stewardship training. Agronomically, farmers learn to feed a family of six on a 39 m x 16 m plot (1/16 ha) using zero tillage, permanent planting stations, mulching, precise spacing, and simple crop rotation. Behaviorally, they are coached to manage time, inputs, and cash on time, at standard, without waste, and with dignity, and to plan ahead for reinvestment, savings, and generosity rather than dependency. Similar conservation agriculture approaches exist, but Pfumvudza is novel in how it compresses technical principles, plot design, and stewardship behaviours into a standardised model that can be executed with hand tools by elderly, land-constrained, or labour-limited households. The key insight is that optimisation at micro-scale (density, water capture, soil cover, and disciplined management) can unlock 4 9x yield gains and significant income improvements without new machinery or large external inputs, as demonstrated in Zimbabwe and Rwanda. Immediate benefits include higher staple yields, lower labour and input costs, and reduced hunger; over time, households build assets, resilience, and opportunities for themselves.
