core_fields.title: Fisher Led Digital Food System Transformation for Equitable, Traceable and Climate Smart Seafood
core_fields.description: ABALOBI strengthens food security and coastal livelihoods by helping small-scale fishers use digital tools to log their catch, access transparent markets and improve incomes. We combine traceability, community-supported training and inclusive financial services to rebuild seafood value chains from the first mile. This project will expand our hubs, onboard more fishers and grow our food security network so communities can access affordable, high-quality quality and sustainably harvested seafood.
core_fields.abstract: ABALOBI addresses a major weakness in global food systems. Small-scale fishers provide essential nutrition to millions, yet they are trapped in informal, low-value value and opaque seafood chains. They often sell to middlemen at unstable prices, cannot prove income, have limited access to markets or finance, and face rising ecological pressures. Communities and consumers struggle to access affordable, high-quality quality and traceable seafood. We solve this through a fisher-led, technology-enabled model that transforms the first mile of the seafood chain. Fishers use the ABALOBI FISHER and MONITOR apps to log catch, track income, and create a digital traceability record that verifies legality, quality and temperature control. This data connects directly to ABALOBI s Marketplace and Food Security channels, where seafood is sold through fair and transparent systems. Community-supported hubs provide training, post-harvest quality control, cold chain access and on-site support. These hubs strengthen cooperative governance, create local jobs and expand the availability of safe, nutritious seafood in low-income areas. The core insight behind this model is that small-scale fisheries improve when fishers become data-empowered participants in the value chain. By linking scientific monitoring, local ecological knowledge and digital traceability, ABALOBI builds trust, equity and resilience throughout the system. Immediate benefits include higher incomes, reduced vulnerability, access to savings and microcredit, better handling practices and increased availability of affordable seafood for households and schools. Long-term benefits include reduced pressure on vulnerable species, stronger cooperatives, transparent markets and healthier, more resilient coastal food systems and communities.

core_fields.title: NutriLoops: Surplus-Based NutriKits for Vulnerable and Marginalized Communities in Bangladesh
core_fields.description: This project turns local surplus vegetables, pulses and small fish into affordable, nutritious food packets made by trained women s groups, focusing on young children, mothers, adolescent girls and older people. An environment-friendly food vehicle delivers these packets to rural schools, urban slums and climate-vulnerable wetlands, river islands and indigenous communities. Empty packets act as tickets for free health and nutrition counselling and simple growth checks, encouraging families to return them for recycling.
core_fields.abstract: In many parts of Bangladesh, families struggle with two linked problems at the same time: children and vulnerable adults eat mostly plain rice with very few vegetables, pulses or fish, while local markets and small farmers often throw away surplus or ugly but perfectly safe produce. This is especially severe in urban slums and climate-vulnerable areas such as wetlands, river islands and remote indigenous communities, where access to affordable, nutritious food is limited. Our innovation connects these two problems in a simple way. Trained women s groups collect safe surplus vegetables, pulses and small fish from local markets and farmers and turn them into shelf-stable, easy-to-cook food packets using basic solar or efficient drying and mixing techniques. An environment-friendly food vehicle then delivers these packets on regular routes to rural schools, urban slums and hard-to-reach communities. A key insight is that we can use the empty food packet itself as a ticket . Families who bring back used packets receive free health and nutrition counselling and simple growth checks for their children. This creates a strong incentive not to throw packets away. The vehicle collects them and sends them for recycling, reducing litter and plastic waste. Immediate benefits include affordable, nutritious meals for young children, mothers, adolescent girls and older people; a new income source for women processors; and an extra market for farmers surplus. Over time, communities gain a reliable, low-cost source of better food, less waste in local markets and cleaner environments in very poor and climate-exposed areas.

core_fields.title: NutriLake: Nutritious Cereal-Omena Snacks Empowering Fisherfolk in Riparian Communities of Lake Victoria
core_fields.description: We intend to commercialize an innovative extruded cereal-omena snack developed through the EU-funded AIRTEA project. This nutritious product valorizes omena (small native fish, Rastrineobola argentea) into affordable, shelf-stable snacks while creating sustainable income for fisherfolk cooperatives around Lake Victoria. core_fields.abstract: Problem: Lake Victoria's fisherfolk communities face poverty, food insecurity, and high post-harvest fish losses (30-40%). Omena (Rastrineobola argentea), a nutritious indigenous fish, suffers quality degradation and price volatility. Meanwhile, Kenya experiences high child malnutrition rates, with limited affordable, nutrient-dense snacks available. Solution: Our innovation transforms omena into extruded cereal-based snacks combining locally-sourced grains (maize, sorghum) with dried, milled omena. Extrusion technology developed in a previous EU-funded project, AIRTEA (https://library.wur.nl/WebQuery/leap4fnssa-projects/713), creates shelf-stable, ready-to-eat products rich in protein, omega-3 fatty acids, calcium, and iron. Novelty: This is East Africa's first commercially viable omena-fortified extruded snack. Unlike traditional sun-dried omena (prone to contamination and spoilage), our process ensures food safety, extends shelf-life, and creates appealing products for children and adults. Benefits: Nutritional: Each serving provides 25-30% daily protein requirements and essential micronutrients, combating malnutrition Economic: Creates 200+ jobs for fisherfolk (60% women) through cooperative-based production Environmental: Reduces fish waste by 40%, utilizing smaller/damaged omena unsuitable for direct sale Social: Empowers women processors with technical skills and stable incomes Market: Affordable pricing (30-40% cheaper than imported protein snacks) ensures accessibility Similar solutions: Moringa/insect-fortified snacks exist, but none utilize indigenous fish resources with community-centered production models in East Africa.

core_fields.title: Scaling Urban Compost Production Systems for Greener and Cleaner Cities
core_fields.description: Our project transforms Addis Ababa s food waste into high-quality organic compost, supporting sustainable agriculture and a circular economy. By scaling collection, production, and distribution, we aim to supply households, farmers, and green city initiatives with organic compost. Lem Chaka also empowers women and youth, raises awareness about sustainable living, and promotes climate-resilient agricultural systems. With expanded infrastructure, skilled personnel, and a retail hub, we can meet growing demand and strengthen sustainable ecosystems in the city.
core_fields.abstract: Lem Chaka addresses a critical problem in Addis Ababa: 70% of the city s waste is organic, and improper disposal contributes to landfills, public health risks, greenhouse gas emissions, soil degradation and environmental contamination. Simultaneously, farmers and urban growers face limited access to high-quality, chemical-free fertilizers to improve crop yields and soil health. Recognizing this, Lem Chaka developed an innovative solution to transform food waste from hotels and other sources into nutrient-rich organic compost derived from food waste, carbon materials, animal manure and effective micro-organisms. Scientific insights on composting, soil fertility, and circular economy principles guided the process, ensuring the compost is safe, effective, and scalable. The innovation benefits multiple stakeholders: farmers and households gain affordable, high-quality compost that improves crop productivity and nutrition; schools, residents of Addis Ababa and community gardens can grow healthy food locally; and citywide green initiatives receive reliable inputs for landscaping, reforestation, and river restoration initiatives. Environmentally, the project reduces methane emissions from landfills, decreases reliance on chemical fertilizers, and promotes sustainable waste management. Socially, it creates jobs (especially for women and youth) and market linkages, but also raises awareness on sustainable consumption and responsible waste disposal. By integrating collection, processing, distribution, and education, Lem Chaka not only solves an immediate waste and soil problem but also creates a sustainable, replicable model for urban food systems. With expanded capacity and partnerships, the project can scale rapidly, amplifying its impact on food security, environmental sustainability, and climate resilience in Addis Ababa and beyond.

core_fields.title: Empowering Rural Households Through GISHE-Famer Organizations and Youth Driven Climate-Smart Food System Innovation.
core_fields.description: This project strengthens rural food security by scaling AMPATH s GISHE model to integrate climate-smart agriculture, financial inclusion, health services, and market access. Through empowered community groups and Farmer Service Centres, 18,000 people will increase climate-resilient food production, grow savings, access health insurance, and secure sustainable markets. The initiative builds resilient, healthy, and economically stable rural households through a community-driven, scalable food system innovation model.
core_fields.abstract: This project introduces a unique Group Integrated Saving and for Health Empowerment (GISHE)-driven, climate-smart food system innovation that integrates agriculture, health, finance, and markets into one community-owned platform. It solves the persistent challenge of low farm productivity, climate vulnerability, and household poverty problems that traditional agricultural projects rarely address together. Rural households often face interconnected barriers: degraded soils, unpredictable rainfall, limited savings, lack of health insurance, and no reliable market access. These combined pressures keep families trapped in cycles of food insecurity and poor health. The innovation is relevant because climate shocks and rising production costs are worsening these vulnerabilities, especially for women and youth. The solution applies a scientific and systems-based insight: food security improves when households strengthen three pillars simultaneously health, financial resilience, and climate-smart production. GISHE groups serve as platforms where farmers learn regenerative agriculture, adopt diversified crops, access microcredit, enroll in health insurance, and connect to markets. Farmer Service Centres then act as rural agribusiness hubs offering inputs, mechanization, climate advisory services, and aggregation. The innovation s technical strengths include; 1. Digital group management (DreamSave) for transparency and data-driven decisions. 2. Climate-smart extension through lead farmers and demonstration sites. 3. Health integration, reducing productivity losses from untreated illnesses. 4. Market-led production, strengthening income stability. Immediate benefits include increased yields, reduced crop losses, access to inputs and insurance, improved health and nutrition, and stronger savings. Sustainable benefits include resilient food systems, empowered women and youth, climate-adapted farming practices, strengthened farmer organizations, and thriving community enterprises.

core_fields.title: Intergenerational Bio-Custodians: Scalable Bio-Fertilizer Systems and Agri-Heritage Valorization for Remote Islands
core_fields.description: Intergenerational Bio-Custodians empowers Chiloe's remote smaller islands to transform organic waste into standardized bio-fertilizer through inclusive, elder-led systems. The model creates a regenerative island-to-island value flow while revitalizing agricultural heritage through hands-on, low-tech learning experiences for younger generations. Grounded in GIAHS stewardship and enabled by an institutional platform with strong territorial and educational capacity, the initiative strengthens intergenerational bonds and offers a scalable pathway for resilient island food systems worldwide.
core_fields.abstract: Intergenerational Bio-Custodians introduces a regenerative island-to-island circular system enabling the smaller islands of Chiloe to convert organic waste into standardized biofertilizer through inclusive microbiodigesters operated by elder knowledge holders. The innovation addresses two intertwined challenges: unmanaged organic waste in remote islands and the erosion of Chilo s GIAHS agricultural heritage as intergenerational transmission weakens. Microbiodigesters use simple, intuitive interfaces that allow elders to operate them confidently, positioning them as active contributors to a regenerative economy. The archipelago's main island functions as a coordination and refinement hub, receiving biofertilizer from smaller islands and preparing it for territorial use, creating a dignified and mutually reinforcing flow of value. A core innovation lies in the pedagogical layer. A collection of low-tech, craft-based educational devices, mechanically activated by biodigester processes, makes circularity tangible for children and youth. These devices form mobile learning environments that travel between islands, translating sustainability into embodied experience. Grounded in Futures Literacy and Active Hope, they enable young people to explore desirable futures through hands-on interaction rather than abstract instruction. Mini-biodigesters and foldable micro-gardens complete the cycle from waste to biofertilizer to plant growth. This bidirectional design allows learning to flow both ways, from elders to youth through agricultural knowledge, and from youth back to communities through imagination and care. Supported by multidisciplinary expertise and institutional infrastructure, the model delivers immediate environmental and social benefits while laying the foundation for a scalable, culturally grounded approach to food system regeneration in vulnerable island territories.

core_fields.title: HydroHarvest: Sustainable Food Systems and Water Solutions for Drought-Prone Communities
core_fields.description: HydroHarvest empowers drought-prone communities in Kenya by combining sustainable water management with hydroponic farming. Through the construction of sand dams, solar-powered water systems, and greenhouse-based hydroponics, we enable year-round food production with minimal water use. Our project promotes organic farming, enhances food security, and builds climate resilience, providing communities with the tools to sustainably grow crops, improve livelihoods, and combat the impacts of drought.
core_fields.abstract: The HydroHarvest project addresses the dual challenges of water scarcity and food insecurity in Kenya s drought-prone regions. These areas face irregular rainfall, unreliable water sources, and poor soil quality, which severely limit agricultural productivity and access to food. Our solution combines hydroponic farming with sustainable water management systems. By building sand dams to capture and store water underground, and using solar-powered pumps to distribute water to households and farms, we create a reliable water supply for both daily use and agriculture. Inside greenhouses, hydroponic systems will allow for water-efficient crop production, using up to 90% less water than traditional farming methods. Organic fertilizers will be used to boost soil and plant health while reducing environmental impact. The scientific insight behind this solution stems from research on water-efficient farming techniques and renewable energy solutions. Hydroponics is a proven method to grow crops with minimal water, while sand dams and solar energy provide a sustainable means of water collection and distribution. Benefits: For farmers: Increased crop yields, year-round production, reduced water use, and healthier vegetables grown using organic fertilizers , contributing to improved incomes. For communities: Reliable access to clean water for drinking and irrigation, improving overall health and quality of life. For the environment: Sustainable farming reduces pressure on natural ecosystems and minimizes water waste. For society: Promotes food security, reduces dependency on external aid, and empowers communities to combat climate change. Relevance: It's important because it combines resource efficiency, climate resilience, and community empowerment, while producing healthier organic crops

core_fields.title: Closing the Loop: A Circular, Climate-Smart Nutrition System for Rwanda
core_fields.description: Solid Africa is building Rwanda s public nutrition infrastructure by linking smallholder farmers to clean, efficient institutional kitchens serving hospitals and schools. This project strengthens the system through regenerative agriculture training, upgraded composting capacity, a rice-drying station to reduce post-harvest loss, and expanded natural fertilizer adoption. Together, these innovations cut spoilage, restore soils, stabilize farmer incomes, and reduce emissions creating a scalable, climate-resilient, circular nutrition model ready for national adoption.
core_fields.abstract: Solid Africa s Farm-to-Plate system connects 7,000+ smallholder farmers to centralized kitchens serving public hospitals and schools. This project strengthens the model by addressing soil depletion, food loss, fertilizer dependency, and methane emissions transforming a linear food economy into a circular nutrition system that regenerates land while feeding people well. Rwanda loses 30 40% of food post-harvest (FAO 2019), much of it preventable. Composting capacity is currently insufficient relative to kitchen throughput, and many cooperatives lack post-harvest handling infrastructure. Meanwhile, one in three children is stunted (UNICEF 2020), making climate-smart nutrition delivery a population-level priority. Our innovation introduces four climate-smart upgrades: Rice Drying Station Reduces moisture loss by 20 35%, increasing farmer revenue and stabilizing supply for institutional kitchens. Composting Hub Upgrade Expands aerobic composting capacity, diverting organic waste from landfill while producing natural fertilizer that replaces synthetics and restores soil organic carbon. Regenerative Agriculture Training Trains 6,000 farmers in intercropping, mulching, rotation, and water-retention techniques that build healthy, climate-resilient soils. Natural Fertilizer Adoption Farmers adopt compost production and use at scale, reducing external input costs and increasing crop nutrient density. Together, these upgrades complete a closed loop waste → fertilizer → soil → harvest → nutrition enabling national scalability through government integration and advancing the blueprint Solid Africa was designed to deliver.

core_fields.title: Transforming Liberia s Agriculture: Mechanization, Genetics, Aquaculture, and Vocational Training Hub
core_fields.description: The Liberia Agricultural Transformation Hub (Tumutu PPP) integrates mechanization, improved livestock genetics, poultry hatchery, aquaculture, and vocational training to strengthen food security. Anchored in coalition governance and government institutions, it delivers affordable protein, regenerative practices, and farmer education. With transparent monitoring and equitable distribution, the hub reduces import dependence, empowers youth and women, and creates a scalable, sustainable model for national agricultural transformation and community resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The Liberia Agricultural Transformation Hub (Tumutu PPP) addresses the urgent problem of low agricultural productivity, dependence on food imports, and fragile rural livelihoods. This challenge is highly relevant as Liberia faces rising food insecurity, limited mechanization, and inadequate protein supply. The innovation solves these problems by integrating mechanization services, improved livestock genetics, poultry hatchery, aquaculture nurseries, and vocational training into a single coalition anchored hub. Farmers access pay per use mechanization, weekly chick and fingerling distribution, and structured training through LABS and Tumutu School. TAL s CRM/ERP monitoring system ensures reproducibility, transparency, and donor credibility. It is novel because it combines science, technology, governance, and education in one PPP framework: mechanization is linked directly to soil fertility testing; breedingstock is scientifically validated for climate resilience; aquaculture reduces pressure on wild fish stocks; and vocational curricula embed regenerative practices. While similar mechanization or hatchery projects exist, they often fail due to lack of governance, monitoring, or integration. Tumutu PPP uniquely unites coalition governance, government anchoring, and community accountability. Scientific and technical insights such as crossbreeding pigs (Landrace Large White), goats (Boer Kalahari Red), and precision soil fertility management led to this solution. Data from pilots show yield increases of 20 30%, hatchery survival rates above 85%, and farmer adoption of Good Farm Practice guidelines. Immediate benefits: affordable protein, mechanization access, farmer training, and community trust. Sustainable benefits: healthier soils, reduced imports, climate resilience, equitable access, and replication across counties transforming food security for farmers, schools, communities, and society.

core_fields.title: Piloting municipality operated seed banking approach in Nepal
core_fields.description: For three decades, non-profits in Nepal have established community seed banks (CSBs) to conserve and improve access to traditional seeds. However, sustaining CSB s work after the non-profit grants has been difficult. Nepal s new constitution has decentralized significant powers and resources to the municipalities. The project leverages this opportunity to develop a municipal agrobiodiversity management plan to sustain and deliver the public good of seed conservation and access through a publicly funded and managed seed bank.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers rely on local crop diversity to manage risks and earn their livelihoods. Rich genetic diversity in traditional crops and varieties hold great potential for sustainable development. Yet, such diversity is rarely available in the formal seed system. Instead, it is rapidly disappearing in developing countries. Community seed banks (CSBs), operated by non-profit organizations and communities, have stepped up to conserve local varieties and provide access to their seeds. In 2024, 1716 varieties of 75 crops were conserved by 28 CSBs in Nepal. In 2023, they produced 26 tons of seeds per CSB, significantly improving equitable access to diverse quality seeds. Despite these successes, it is a challenge to sustain CSB activities as they heavily rely on non-profit grants. Public goods like access to diversity in seed need long-term support from the public sector as private sector is unlikely to have the incentive to participate. The new constitution of Nepal has decentralized significant legislative, judiciary, and executive functions and resources to 753 municipalities. Consequently, municipalities are delivering better education and health services. There is a novel opportunity to leverage municipalities expanded resources to sustain vital public goods of local seed conservation and quality seed access. There is limited awareness on crop diversity and CSBs in municipal offices. Therefore, the proposed seed grant intends to help Samudayek Biu Bank Nepal (CSB Association) raise awareness of municipal office holders, develop participatory agrobiodiversity plan, and pilot long-term support of CSBs using public funds to secure the public good of seed diversity.

core_fields.title: Bank Nkhonde
core_fields.description: Banki nkhonde is a digital financial inclusion platform designed to empower unbanked smallholder farmers in rural Malawi. Bank Nkhonde digitizes Malawi's traditional village banking groups, enabling unbanked rural farmers to build a financial identity, save securely, and access formal financial services through smartphone and USSD platforms. By linking community savings groups to commercial banks and agribusiness support tools, Bank Nkhonde strengthens financial inclusion, improves farm investment capacity, and enhances resilience across rural food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Banki Nkhonde for Agriculture is a digital financial inclusion platform that modernizes Malawi's traditional village banking system through a combination of smartphone interfaces (mobile app, web portal, chatbot) and USSD access for users without smartphones. In rural Malawi, more than 70% of smallholder farmers remain unbanked and rely on informal savings groups that are paper-based, difficult to track and not recognized by financial institutions. This financial invisibility limits their ability to invest in seeds, fertilizer, tools and safe storage, contributing to low yields and high post-harvest losses. Banki Nkhonde addresses this gap by digitizing village savings and loan operations. Through the app, website, chatbot or USSD, farmers can record contributions, manage group loans, automate reminders and build individual and group financial profiles that function as a digital credit history. This innovation is grounded in the insight that digital identity + structured group savings + mobile accessibility can unlock formal financial pathways for underserved farmers. The platform integrates agriculture-focused features such as input-purchasing modules, savings goals for seasonal farming needs, market price information and climate-smart advisories. These enhance financial planning, reduce vulnerability to climate variability and support better farm decision-making. Immediate benefits include secure savings, improved transparency, accurate digital records and timely access to small loans for agricultural inputs. Long-term, farmers gain stronger financial credibility, increased productivity, reduced post-harvest losses, improved household food security and greater resilience to economic and climate shocks. Banki Nkhonde strengthens the financial foundation of rural farming communities, contributing to a more inclusive and sustainable food system.

core_fields.title: Building Drought and Hunger Resilience Through Natural Root-Boosting Soil Helpers.
core_fields.description: This project builds drought and hunger resilience in Kenya's drylands by using natural, tiny root helpers, scientifically known as mycorrhizal fungi. These organisms form microscopic hyphal networks that extend far beyond the plant's roots, enabling crops to access water and nutrients from distant soil areas. Women and youth will produce root-helper powders and pellets locally, helping farmers restore soil health, boost yields, and adapt to climate stress affordably.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation introduces a natural, low-cost soil restoration approach that helps plant roots access water and nutrients from deeper and wider soil zones by using tiny root helpers, scientifically known as Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF). The project addresses a major problem in Kenya's dry regions: severely degraded soils, weakened by drought, erosion, and overcultivation. These soils hold little moisture, limit nutrient uptake, and cause frequent crop failure, hunger, and declining resilience among smallholder farmers. AMF offer a relevant and powerful solution because they naturally attach to plant roots and form hyphal networks, microscopic, thread-like structures that extend far beyond the root zone. These networks function like natural extensions of the plant's root system, enabling crops to absorb more water and essential nutrients such as phosphorus and nitrogen. Scientific insights from soil microbiology show that AMF are abundant in healthy ecosystems (forests, old banana groves, termite mounds) but become depleted in degraded farmlands. The innovation utilizes simple local materials, including maize bran, compost, charcoal dust, and rice husks, to produce root-helper powder, soil-boosting pellets, and root-guard sheets, thereby multiplying AMF. These products can be applied during planting to revive soil biology and strengthen crops. Immediate benefits include improved germination, stronger root development, higher drought tolerance, and increased yields. Over time, AMF enhance soil structure, moisture retention, and nutrient cycling, creating a self-sustaining regenerative system. End users, farmers, schools with gardens, rural communities, and the environment benefit from reduced dependence on chemicals, improved food security, restored soils, and greater resilience to climate

core_fields.title: Food for Learning Africa
core_fields.description: Onechild Africa is scaling a hub-and-spoke school nutrition system that delivers safe, affordable, and highly nutritious meals to children in low-income communities. By sourcing directly from local farmers and preparing meals in centralized production kitchens, we reduce food waste, improve nutritional quality, and increase efficiency. This project will expand from serving 500 children daily to 1,000 daily, addressing malnutrition, supporting local agriculture, and improving educational outcomes nationwide.
core_fields.abstract: Rwanda continues to face a significant burden of child malnutrition, with national stunting rates remaining at about 33 percent and diet diversity still low among school-age children. Hunger and inadequate nutrition limit children s ability to concentrate, learn, and remain in school, while many smallholder farmers continue to struggle with unstable demand and post-harvest losses that weaken rural livelihoods. Our school-nutrition innovation directly responds to these interconnected challenges in a way that is both sustainable and scalable within the Rwandan context. Our model is built around a centralized, hub-and-spoke food system that prepares safe, standardized, highly nutritious meals in regional production kitchens before distributing them efficiently to partner schools. By sourcing directly from Rwandan farmers and aligning menus with seasonal harvests, we reduce food waste, stabilize farmer income, strengthen rural value chains, and ensure that children receive fresh, culturally appropriate meals. Each meal remains affordable at approximately $0.10 $0.15 while supplying nearly 40 percent of a child s daily nutritional needs, which supports improved concentration, higher attendance, and healthier long-term development. Centralized kitchens allow for strict safety and hygiene standards, batch cooking dramatically lowers cost per meal, and seasonally informed procurement creates predictable markets for farmers. Standardized recipes and cold-chain controls further reduce spoilage and ensure consistent quality across all schools served. This integrated system delivers immediate improvements in child nutrition, learning outcomes, and school participation, while simultaneously creating reliable economic opportunities for farmers. Our model strengthens local agriculture, reduces environmental impact through efficient logistics, and expands equitable access to nutritious meals.

core_fields.title: Community Greenhouses for Year-Round Local Food Security
core_fields.description: We build affordable, climate-smart greenhouses that let schools and communities grow food year-round. Our design improves local food security, reduces reliance on long supply chains, and teaches regenerative practices. This project focuses on installing a 96x30 community greenhouse and training program that gives families consistent access to fresh produce while building skills, resilience, and long-term health benefits for underserved areas.
core_fields.abstract: Communities and schools across the United States face rising food insecurity, short growing seasons, and dependence on long, costly supply chains. My innovation is an affordable, climate-smart greenhouse system that lets communities grow fresh food year-round, even in harsh climates, while teaching regenerative skills that build long-term resilience. The greenhouse combines passive solar design, double-layer insulation, thermal mass, and automated climate controls to stabilize temperatures and reduce energy use. This makes year-round production possible at a cost that schools, tribes, and small communities can realistically adopt. The system is paired with a hands-on education and training program that helps students, families, and community members learn seed-to-harvest skills, soil health practices, and simple regenerative methods they can continue using independently. The insight behind this work came from recognizing that most greenhouse models in the U.S. are either too expensive, too fragile, or too energy-intensive for communities with limited resources. By simplifying the design, optimizing it for cold regions, and integrating education directly into the build, the solution creates immediate and lasting benefits. The impact is direct: communities gain reliable access to nutrient-dense produce, schools receive an outdoor classroom for science and climate education, producers reduce risk from climate instability, and families build skills that strengthen self-reliance. At a broader level, this innovation supports healthier diets, reduces emissions from transported food, keeps food dollars local, and helps communities adapt to a rapidly changing climate. The result is a practical, scalable model for resilient local food systems.

core_fields.title: CEF-M: digital tool for comprehensive and integrated management of family farms in the Sahel
core_fields.description: CEF-M is a mobile digital tool, designed collaboratively with Malian farmers to combat food insecurity exacerbated by environmental stress and poor institutional support. It provides accessible, local-language voice instructions and contextual illustrations to guide smallholder farmers through their agricultural year, supporting decision-making, planning, monitoring, and evaluation based on agroecological principles, thus addressing the high illiteracy rates that render traditional documentation useless.
core_fields.abstract: Agriculture and livestock keeping are practiced by 60% to 80% of the Sahelian population, yet most farmers and herders experience chronic food insecurity. They face significant environmental challenges, including soil fertility decline and climate variability, worsened by structural issues, including insufficient formal education and inadequate national agricultural extension service support. Smallholder farmers must independently manage their farms to meet family food, fodder and financial needs. The digital tool for the Management Advisory for Family Farms (Conseil l Exploitation Agricole Familiale - Mobile, CEF-M, in French) is an innovative solution designed collaboratively with and for farmers. By offering voice instructions in the local language and contextualised illustrations to guide users through their agricultural year, it documents activities and supports farmer decision making following agroecological principles. The CEF-M emerged from Arouna Dissa s doctoral research, conducted between 2017 and 2022 in the Koutiala region of Mali (Dissa, 2023). This research highlighted a real need for advice and support in agricultural management, coupled with very low adoption of existing tools, particularly those based on written documentation (paper sheets, notebooks) which are unsuitable in a context marked by high illiteracy rates. An analytical inventory of management tools was conducted, including surveying producers experiences of these. The tool is now in process of digitalisation, and is currently formed of ODK forms and a web platform to centralise, store, and visualise farmer data. Farm management topics support 3 essential modules: 1) effective planning, 2) monitoring and 3) evaluation, towards improving yields and overall productivity.

core_fields.title: Developing and Validating Cashew Milk: A Scalable, Nutritious Food Product to Combat Food Loss
core_fields.description: The goal of this initiative is to create wholesome cashew milk that can be consumed on a daily basis. Focusing on the first phase, the initiative will create a standardized formulation through product development and conduct physical, proximate, and sensory analyses. The project reduces food loss, promotes local agribusiness, and provides consumers with a plant-based, healthful option by creating a value-added beverage that can be consumed every day.
core_fields.abstract: This research aims to address the underutilization of non-export grade cashew nuts and the growing demand for nutritious, plant-based milk alternatives. In Cambodia, cashew cultivation plays a significant role in supporting rural live hoods. However, many cashew nuts that do not meet export standards are sold at low prices, leading to reduced income for farmers. At the same time, consumer and institutions such as schools are increasingly seeking healthier, dairy-free alternatives due to lactose intolerance, health awareness, and environmental concerns. The proposed study introduces an innovation solution by transforming locally sourced cashews nut into nutritious, high-quality cashew milk product. The first phase focus on comprehensive product development using physical, proximate, and sensory analyses, to establish a standardized, safe and appealing formulation. The scientific and technical processes will ensure consistent product quality, desirable taste and texture, flavor, and balanced nutritional composition suitable for local consumption. This innovation provides immediate and long-term benefits. It enhances farmer s income through value addition to lower-grade cashew nuts and creates new opportunities for local processing and small-scale production. For consumers, it offers an affordable, nutritious, and lactose-free beverage that support healthy diet. core_fields.title: Feed the Future with our Hands
core_fields.description: "Feed the Future with Our Hands" is our Nutrition Line project that champions food security. core_fields.abstract: Payless is transforming locally grown bananas and plantains into nutrient-rich snacks and baby foods - as an innovative approach to food security and child nutrition. Chronic malnutrition affects 35.5% of children under five in Liberia, a challenge made worse by limited affordable nutritious foods and heavy dependence on imports. At the same time, banana farmers face low market demand, high post-harvest losses, and unstable income. Our innovation directly addresses these issues by turning an abundant local crop into accessible, nutritious, and value-added products. Using simple and efficient food-processing methods, we convert bananas and plantains into high-energy chips, and working to introduce a 100% banana fortified baby food designed for children aged 6 months to 6 years. The scientific foundation for this solution lies in the natural nutritional profile of bananas and plantains: they provide complex carbohydrates, potassium, fiber, essential vitamins, and natural energy - making them ideal for early childhood nutrition. Our production system is designed to ensure minimal waste; every part of the harvest is used productively, and by-products are repurposed through circular production to improve soil health. Immediate benefits include improved access to affordable, healthy snacks, better nutrition for babies and young children, and reliable market opportunities for smallholder farmers. Over the long term, the initiative strengthens local food systems, reduces post-harvest losses and stabilizes farmer livelihoods. It also contributes to job creation and national economic growth through value addition and a steady supply of nutritious food.

core_fields.title: Harvesting Opportunity: A Global Tool to Measure and Reduce On-Farm Food Loss
core_fields.description: World Wildlife Fund s Food Loss and Waste Team is applying for the Growth Grant to scale adoption of the Global Farm Loss Tool (GFLT) to smallholders in Latin America to reduce on-farm food loss and create market channels that turn the loss into economic opportunity for growers, all while getting more food to people. Additionally, this grant would unlock new functions to make the Tool easier and more valuable to use for growers.
core_fields.abstract: Reducing food waste is an environmental, social and economic imperative. Food production has the largest global environmental impact of any human activity, accounting for 70% of biodiversity loss, 70% of freshwater use, 50% of soil erosion, and one-third of all greenhouse gas emissions. To bring food production in line with what the planet can support, WWF is elevating food loss as a critical priority for food system transformation. Nearly 40% of the world s food production goes uneaten, and a recent WWF study revealed that 1.2 billion tons or 15% of all food produced is lost annually on farms. That s enough to feed the world s undernourished population at least three times over! Adding to the challenge, most growers and buyers lack data on the volume and causes of their food loss, limiting their ability to take action. Producing food that goes uneaten unnecessarily exacerbates the environmental impacts of agriculture, while costing growers time, money, and resources. WWF developed the Global Farm Loss Tool (GFLT) as a way for growers and food businesses to easily quantify, categorize, and reduce loss. The GFLT unlocks loss solutions through data, allowing growers and buyers to revalorize surplus, reducing the environmental impacts of production (GHG mitigation, freshwater) and boosting revenues for both growers and buyers. WWF s network of 80 offices is well positioned to drive widespread adoption of the GFLT, opening whole-chain solutions that strengthen regional food systems and integrate into WWF s wider sustainable production initiatives.

core_fields.title: The Affordable Nutrition Coalition
core_fields.description: Tailored Food combines evidence-based diet research with the expansion of nutritious, culturally rooted food enterprises across the Global South. Our Affordable Nutrition Coalition project is in the process of synthesizing global insights on plant-based diets for children, while we continue to expand practical work partnering with local entrepreneurs to produce affordable, nutrient-dense foods using indigenous crops. Together, these innovations expand access to healthy diets, reduce environmental impact, and strengthen local economies.
core_fields.abstract: The novelty of our approach lies in integrating bottom up and top down influence simultaneously. No similar model simultaneously influences global nutrition policy and strengthens local food economies through culturally tailored products.Tailored Food has gained a key insight over the last 10 years of working on food systems with the world s largest institutions; mainstream food-system decision makers, including government ministries, multilateral agencies, development banks, and large NGOs, consistently base funding and programmatic decisions on two factors: evidence they recognize as rigorous, and relationships with people they trust. In order to influence change, Tailored Food has built the Affordable Nutrition Coalition in partnership with the EAT Foundation, the University of Bonn and the Research Institute for Plant-based Nutrition. Currently 4 Phd candidates are conducting the 38-country globally-representative research study, which will then inform cost-effective, culturally aligned plant-based nutrition strategies for children in low and middle income countries. In order to bring this information to influential policy makers, the Affordable Nutrition Coalition will need to translate the evidence into short, mainstream-ready materials that focus on the issue areas that matter to food system decision makers, such as economic prosperity, food affordability, and resilient communities. Engaging with and equipping influencers with talking points, to be able to bring this messaging to where it needs to be heard. Combining rigorous diet research worthy of the attention of mainstream food systems stakeholders, with the practical scaling of local food enterprises is Tailored Food's two-part approach to food systems change.

core_fields.title: Transforming Agri-Supply Chains with Data for Safe, Affordable, Nutritious Food
core_fields.description: Mbibo (previously FarmDirect), founded by Producers Direct (www.producersdirect.org), is a data-powered platform that unifies fragmented farm-gate, market, and transport data into a single intelligent source used by buyers to directly connect with farmers. This enables buyers to access verified-quality, affordable produce at farm-gate prices while reducing post-harvest losses by enabling pre-harvest sales. The model increases farmer incomes, lowers buyer costs, and strengthens transparency, efficiency, and resilience across rural and underserved agricultural supply chains.
core_fields.abstract: Mbibo is a data-powered agri-supply chain innovation that solves the persistent problem of fragmented, unavailable, and unreliable agricultural data in Uganda. Smallholder farmers, especially women in unstructured value chains, lack real-time information on prices, demand, and quality requirements. Buyers struggle to efficiently source consistent, high-quality produce, while transporters operate with minimal coordination resulting in high post-harvest losses, inefficiencies, and unaffordable nutritious foods for low-income consumers. Mbibo addresses this by unifying data across the entire supply chain into a single, truthful intelligence source. Community youth agents collect verified, ground-truth data on produce availability, maturity, quality, prices, and delivery conditions from rural villages. This data is harmonized and processed into actionable insights that enable direct, transparent transactions between farmers and buyers. Buyers use the platform to access real-time, verified supply; place orders; and coordinate last-mile delivery through agents. The key insight behind this solution is that data scarcity not food scarcity is a major driver of food insecurity. By creating structured data where none existed, Mbibo allows the entire supply chain to operate efficiently with accuracy, transparency, and predictability. Benefits to users include: - Farmers earn higher and more stable incomes - Buyers access fresher, affordable, traceable produce at farm-gate prices - Youth earn daily income as data collectors and delivery agents - Post-harvest losses decrease through pre-harvest sales and demand forecasting

It thrives in tropical climates, requires minimal inputs, improves soil structure, and contributes to environmental restoration. Research shows breadfruit is high in fibre, vitamins, complex carbohydrates, and essential minerals, making it valuable for household nutrition and school feeding. MNYPA is introducing breadfruit as a regenerative, community led food and livelihood system. In partnership with Isa Constellations, which provides seedlings and agronomy support, we are working with community farmers to establish youth managed breadfruit orchards. To reduce food loss and increase accessibility, we are developing prototypes of value-added products including breadfruit flour, porridge mixes, and dried chips. These products extend shelf life, enhance convenience, and strengthen consumer acceptability. The innovation provides immediate benefits such as improved diet diversity, new livelihood opportunities for youth, and better economic prospects for farmers. It also delivers long term environmental and community value by restoring degraded land, increasing biodiversity, reducing waste, and building a sustainable and resilient local food system that can scale across Uganda.

core_fields.title: Core-E: The Farmer-Powered Economic Intelligence Engine for a Resilient Food System
core_fields.description: Core-E is an economic intelligence engine that helps farmers reduce loss and increase income by identifying the highest-value use for each crop in real time. By turning field data into immediate economic decisions, Core-E enables farmers to access new markets, improve resilience, and supply communities with more affordable, fresher food. This project builds and validates the Core-E engine to deliver economic and social benefits across the food system.
core_fields.abstract: Millions of tons of crops are lost every year because farmers lack real-time information about alternative uses and market opportunities beyond traditional buyers. When crops fall outside cosmetic standards, when demand shifts unexpectedly, or when global disruptions depress prices, farmers absorb the loss. This reduces income, increases food costs, weakens rural economies, and wastes resources that required land, labor, water, and fuel to produce. The result is a system where the people who feed communities are often the least economically secure within it. Core-E solves this problem by serving as an adaptive economic intelligence engine that analyzes crop characteristics, demand signals, and downstream applications to determine the highest-value use for each harvest in real time. Instead of one path for produce, Core-E evaluates multiple revenue pathways such as food markets, bioplastics, fermentation inputs, nutrient extraction, or regenerative soil products and guides farmers toward the option that delivers the most value with the least waste. The insight behind Core-E emerged from recognizing that agriculture has precision tools for planting and harvesting, but lacks precision tools for economic decision-making. Machinery performs the physical work; Core-E performs the thinking. Immediate benefits include higher farmer income, reduced waste, and more affordable fresh food for consumers. Sustainable benefits include resilient rural economies, greater food availability for schools and communities, reduced emissions from agricultural waste, and increased participation of small and underserved producers in high-value markets. Core-E helps farmers not only grow food but grow opportunity, resilience, and shared prosperity.

core_fields.title: LandPrint - Natural capital ratings to finance the regenerative food transition
core_fields.description: Natural capital is essential to the food system but continues to be eroded because it is not valued. LandPrint digital ratings offer the foundation to price natural capital and the risks from its degradation. This project builds automated workflows using digital technologies to generate natural capital ratings that reflect sustainable land use. These ratings unlock financial incentives, reduce risk, and accelerate the adoption of sustainable and regenerative agriculture among smallholders.
core_fields.abstract: Science clearly shows that natural capital underpins global food systems, generating over US$ 50 trillion in ecosystem services each year. Farmers manage about 50% of the global productive lands. Yet these assets keep degrading because of unsustainable farming practices that drive 80%t of water depletion, 25% of GHG emissions, and nearly 90% of soil erosion and deforestation. A core reason is that financial institutions and corporations do not include natural resource degradation in their physical or financial risk assessments. As a result, farmers are not rewarded for maintaining healthy soils, water, and ecosystems. Since financing and crop prices are not indexed to environmental quality, producers see no income stream from sustainability and struggle to invest in regeneration. Our innovation solves this structural failure by transforming natural capital into a financial asset through automated digital ratings. These ratings quantify soil health, water retention, vegetation cover, and carbon and convert them into a standardized risk and performance score. This allows banks and buyers to integrate natural capital into credit pricing, procurement decisions, and incentive schemes. Powered by machine learning, remote sensing, and field verified indicators, LandPrint automates data collection and rating workflows, making the system low cost, scalable, and appropriate for smallholder environments. Farmers gain clear insights on environmental health while receiving financial signals that reward sustainable land use. Immediate benefits include better credit terms, new financial incentives, and reduced climate and production risks. Over time, restored natural capital boosts yields, lowers input dependence, and strengthens food systems resilience.

Sustainability: Our AI driven smart metering minimizes water waste and eliminates carbon emissions by replacing diesel generators. By shifting from selling pumps to selling reliable water we turn a scarce resource into a trusted utility for rural regeneration.

core_fields.title: NutriScreen: Linking Farmer GAP Practices to Safer, Low-Cost Food Monitoring
core_fields.description: NutriScreen: Linking Farmer GAP Practices to Safer, Low-Cost Food Monitoring creates a workable, laboratory-supported system that links market-level food safety with upstream farm practices. It lowers foodborne risks, minimizes waste, and guarantees safe, wholesome, and reliable foods by evaluating farmer GAP compliance and testing for microbial contamination and spoilage. The tools, which are inexpensive and simple to use, support equitable and sustainable food systems in Cambodia while empowering small vendors.
core_fields.abstract: NutriScreen: Linking Farmer GAP Practices to Safer, Low-Cost Food Monitoring addresses the ongoing issue of microbial contamination and food spoilage in Cambodian wet markets. Foodborne illnesses, needless waste, and diminished consumer trust result from smallholder farmers' and market vendors' lack of access to reasonably priced instruments for evaluating food safety. The innovation combines evaluations of farmer adherence to Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) with laboratory testing of high-risk foods (fish, meat, and vegetables). Microbial contamination and spoilage patterns are identified by laboratory results, and upstream practices that contribute to these risks are identified by GAP assessments. By connecting these insights, NutriScreen creates simple monitoring tools and useful, affordable advice that vendors can use on a daily basis to ensure food safety. The solution is based on scientific understanding of food spoilage dynamics, microbial contamination, and how farm-level practices affect the quality of food downstream. It ensures accuracy while maintaining viability for small-scale markets by converting laboratory insights into practical, field-ready interventions. Consumers will benefit immediately from safer, fresher food, less waste, and higher vendor awareness and adherence to safe handling procedures. Better farm-to-market hygiene, increased community confidence in regional foods, increased farmer adoption of GAP, and a long-term decrease in foodborne illnesses are examples of sustainable benefits. NutriScreen enhances food security, encourages fair access to nutrient-dense food, and supports environmentally friendly food handling techniques by developing a scalable, low-cost system.

core_fields.title: SoilProfit Groundnuts Programme: Regenerating Soils, Restoring Yields, Transforming Livelihoods
core_fields.description: The SoilProfit Groundnuts, a regenerative groundnuts production model dramatically increases groundnut yields in The Gambia from a national average of 0.5 1.2 t/ha to verified yields exceeding 3.0 t/ha. By applying regenerative soil restoration, biological inoculants, micronutrient balancing, and climate-resilient agronomy, the model ensures food security, farmer income growth, and environmental recovery. This project scales a proven prototype into regional hubs that enable equitable access to sustainable, nutritious, affordable groundnut produce.
core_fields.abstract: The SoilProfit Groundnuts module addresses three interconnected challenges: declining soil fertility, climate-stressed production, and persistently low groundnut yields in The Gambia. National yields have stagnated at 0.8 1.2 t/ha, dropping to 0.5 t/ha in 2024 season. Farmers rely on degraded soils with poor microbiome activity, inadequate nutrient cycling, and minimal regenerative inputs. This innovation introduces a scientifically optimized regenerative groundnut system built on soil microbiome activation, balanced micronutrient supply, biological nitrogen fixation, compost-mineral blends, and precision planting protocols. The novelty lies in its integration: unlike isolated interventions, this module delivers a holistic, soil-first regenerative system tailored to semi-arid West African soils. Comparable solutions exist globally, but none have achieved the verified yield jump up to 300% over national averages documented in Gambian field prototypes. Scientific insights on microbial nutrient water interaction guided the formulation, especially the synergy between Ca, Mg balance, rhizobia activation, and moisture retention. Immediate benefits include increased yields, reduced input costs, improved seed quality, and restored soil organic matter. Long-term benefits include resilience to drought, improved food system stability, reduced dependency on imported fertilizers, and strengthened farmer livelihoods. Consumers, schools, processors, and communities benefit from greater supply of safe, affordable, high-quality groundnuts.

core_fields.title: Upcycling plant-based beverage by-products into clean-label alternatives to synthetic food additives
core_fields.description: NOIET develops natural fermented ingredients that replace synthetic preservatives and antioxidants in processed foods. By upcycling plant-based beverage by-products, we create clean-label, multifunctional ingredients that improve shelf life, stability, and nutritional value. Our proprietary multi-microbial fermentation process transforms waste into high-value functionality, advancing a more circular and sustainable food system. This innovation enables manufacturers to reduce reliance on artificial additives while enhancing product naturality, performance, and consumer trust.
core_fields.abstract: The food industry relies heavily on synthetic preservatives and antioxidants (E-number additives) to guarantee shelf life and product stability. While effective, these additives are petrochemical-derived, offer no nutritional value, and are increasingly rejected by consumers seeking transparency and clean-label products. At the same time, the global production of plant-based beverages generates 228,000 tons of nutrient-rich by-products each year, most of which are discarded or downgraded, contributing to waste and inefficiencies across the food system. NOIET addresses both problems through NOIFERM, a natural fermented ingredient that replaces synthetic additives while valorizing industrial by-products. Our innovation is based on a proprietary multi-microbial fermentation process that converts oat and rice beverage by-products into a clean-label, multifunctional ingredient with natural antioxidant and preservative activity. Unlike single-strain fermentations, our microbial consortium produces bioactive compounds more efficiently and eliminates residual sugars, resulting in a stable, nutritionally rich, and fully natural ingredient. The scientific insight behind the solution lies in leveraging microbial synergies to generate natural defense molecules, such as antioxidant metabolites and antimicrobial peptides, that protect foods from oxidation and spoilage. The ingredient is dried at controlled temperatures to preserve protein integrity and ensure microbiological stability, creating a versatile powdered ingredient suitable for bakery, plant-based, snack, and sport nutrition. NOIFERM delivers immediate benefits for producers by improving shelf life, replacing E-numbers, and enabling cleaner formulations. The long-term sustainable benefits include reduced food waste, lower reliance on petrochemical additives, new revenue opportunities for by-product suppliers, and a more circular, resilient food system that benefits industry and consumers

core_fields.title: Building Resilient Food Systems through Nature-Based Wastewater Reuse in Rural Costa Rica
core_fields.description: Ridge to Reefs (RTR) and Wildlife Conservation Association (WCA) will expand wastewater improvements at a Nosara high school by creating a wastewater to agroforestry garden that doubles as an educational resource. The garden, fed by a septic tank and a Bioreactor Garden nature-based treatment system, will produce safe, nutritious food for students, faculty, and the community. RTR and the University of Costa Rica s Biosystems Engineering department will develop design workshops for students and communities.
core_fields.abstract: The Bioreactor Garden (BG) and its paired agroforestry production system together turn wastewater into clean water and safe, nutritious food using plants, organic media, and beneficial microorganisms. After filtering wastewater through a septic tank and BG, effluent is safely used to irrigate tree crops and agroforestry gardens that provide diverse, resilient food production at household or community scale, directly addressing food security while solving a sanitation challenge. This combined BG agroforestry system is especially appealing in places such as Costa Rica where cost savings, food security benefits, and preventative health impacts align with local needs, particularly for low-income families, schools, and rural communities. RTR s team of ecological engineers, agronomists and restoration scientists developed the BG agroforestry system after years of witnessing wastewater pollution in food insecure areas and recognizing that human wastewater, when treated adequately, provides vital nutrients for food production. By pairing denitrifying wastewater treatment with productive agroforestry plots, the innovation solves multiple problems at once: affordable wastewater treatment, pollution reduction, and reliable food production in rural, low-income areas facing water scarcity and high input costs. It also upcycles local waste materials such as glass sand and invasive species woodchips or biochar to support local, circular economies and mitigate carbon emissions. Installed at households, schools and neighborhoods, BG agroforestry systems reduce cost of living by providing fresh food while protecting people from untreated sewage and safeguarding coastal ecosystems from nutrient pollution, offering a scalable, nature-based pathway to food security and sustainable communities.

core_fields.title: Refugee Sustainable Food and Nutrition Innovation Hub (RSFNIH)
core_fields.description: The Refugee Sustainable Food and Nutrition Innovation Hub (RSFNIH) empowers vulnerable refugees in Nakivale Settlement through climate-smart farming, food preservation, nutrition education, and entrepreneurship. By training women, teenage girls, and orphans, the project reduces food insecurity, improves dietary diversity, and creates income opportunities. With seed funding, RSFNIH builds self-reliance, strengthens local food systems, and offers a scalable model for sustainable refugee livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: The Refugee Sustainable Food and Nutrition Innovation Hub (RSFNIH) addresses chronic food insecurity, poor dietary diversity, and limited livelihoods in Nakivale Refugee Settlement. Refugees often rely on unstable food aid and consume mainly maize and beans, leading to malnutrition. This innovation is relevant because it empowers vulnerable groups orphans, single mothers, and teenage girls who are most affected by hunger and poverty. The solution integrates climate-smart agriculture, food preservation, nutrition education, and entrepreneurship into one community-driven hub. Sack gardens, vertical farming, and agroecology training enable households to grow nutrient-rich vegetables in limited spaces. Solar dryers and food processing equipment reduce waste and extend shelf life, while nutrition education improves dietary practices. Entrepreneurship training and Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) create income opportunities from value-added products such as dried vegetables and organic fertilizers. This approach is guided by scientific insights into climate-resilient farming, food safety, and nutrition science, ensuring both immediate and long-term impact. Refugees gain practical skills, access to diverse foods, and tools to build micro-enterprises. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition, reduced food waste, and new income streams for women and youth. Sustainable benefits include decreased dependency on food aid, stronger local food systems, climate resilience, and a replicable model for other refugee settlements. Ultimately, RSFNIH transforms refugees from aid recipients into active producers, entrepreneurs, and community leaders, strengthening both livelihoods and environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Scaling up wheat physiological pre-breeding nurseries with widened genetic diversity
core_fields.description: Wheat supplies 20% of global daily calories and protein but faces substantial threats from climate change. CIMMYT, through the IWYP translational hub and HeDWIC project, validates and introgresses key traits to improve wheat. This effort has produced two wheat nurseries over a decade and distributed 700 improved lines to more than 2000 partners, leading to nine direct variety releases. With further support, CIMMYT will expand genetic diversity, strengthen germplasm improvement, and accelerate delivery of climate-resilient
core_fields.abstract: Wheat is one of the most important staples providing 20% calories and protein for our daily dietary. However, its productivity is constrained by fast changing climates as heat and drought cause significant yield loss without proper adaptation. This necessitates the improvement of wheat germplasm to sustain yield production, therefore food and nutritional security for 10 billion people around 2050. At CIMMYT, we have established the IWYP translational hub (iwyp.org) and HeDWIC consortium (https://hedwic.org/), and through them we have been collaborating with worldwide partners to validate potential traits, alleles and haplotypes discovered from academic research, and have been developing wheat germplasm with improved yield potential and stress resilience. In this process, wide genetic diversity of wheat landraces, wild relatives has been introgressed into bread wheat through physioloical pre-breeding pipeline where desirables traits have been selected and pyramided together. The improved wheat germplasm has been formed as two nurseries (WYCYT for yield potential condition and SATYN for heat and drought conditions) and 700 lines have been distributed to more than 2000 partners worldwide over the last decade. Among them, nine lines have been directly released as varieties in Pakistan, Iran, Egypt, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. The two varieties in Pakistan have been produced over 700 tons and reached over 14000 farmers in 2024. With this strong foundation, this grant will definitely provide further support to widen wheat genetic diversity (novel alleles for wheat dwarfism and synthetic lines), to scale up improved wheat nurseries, to engage with breeders and farmers for a greater impact.

core_fields.title: Sun-Gari+: Solar-Powered Bio-Fortification of Cassava for Climate and Nutrition Resilience
core_fields.description: HELPSUSDEV introduces "Sun-Gari+," a climate-smart innovation transforming Cameroon's cassava value chain. We replace deforestation-heavy wood processing with Hybrid Solar Dryers, reducing carbon emissions and post-harvest waste. Simultaneously, we bio-fortify the cassava with local Moringa and Soy to combat malnutrition. This circular model empowers 500 women farmers to produce a safe, affordable, and nutrient-dense super-food, ensuring food security while staying within planetary boundaries.
core_fields.abstract: In rural Cameroon, traditional Gari processing relies on wood fires, causing massive deforestation and respiratory health issues for women. Furthermore, standard Gari is high-starch but nutrient-poor, contributing to hidden hunger, while 40% of the cassava harvest is lost to spoilage. "Sun-Gari+" integrates Hybrid Solar Thermal Technology with Food-to-Food Fortification. We replace open-air drying/frying with poly-tunnel solar dryers equipped with biomass backup fans. This reduces wood consumption by 70% and ensures consistent, hygienic drying regardless of weather. Our scientific insight is that low-temperature solar drying preserves heat-sensitive micronutrients better than frying. We utilize this to blend cassava mash with Moringa oleifera leaf powder (rich in Vitamin A/Iron) and Soy (Protein) before fermentation. This transforms a basic carbohydrate staple into a "complete meal." Benefits: Consumers: Access to an affordable, culturally trusted staple that meets 30% of daily Vitamin A and Iron needs for children. Farmers: Reduction of post-harvest loss from 40% to 5%, increasing incomes for women's cooperatives. Environment: Saving an estimated 200 tons of CO2/year by eliminating wood fuel and reducing methane from rotting waste.

core_fields.title: Scaling innovative water storage for resilient, agroecological food production
core_fields.description: The project will provide assistance and accompaniment for 50 families (approximately 300 individuals) to build small reservoirs on their farms to ensure water collection and storage for micro-irrigation. This will enable irrigation on up to 10 acres and will focus on small-scale organic vegetable production for sale and home consumption. Successful field trials confirmed this is a viable alternative and necessary to improve water availability, generate employment, ensure food security and income generation for families.
core_fields.abstract: The project proposes the construction of 50 reservoirs waterproofed with HDPE geomembrane and the provision of micro-irrigation accessories for 50 vegetable producers in Rabinal, located in the Dry Corridor of Guatemala, characterized by a semi-arid climate, increasingly unpredictable rainfall, and stony soils. This innovation seeks to mitigate the effects of drought by ensuring water availability during the dry season, which currently limits agricultural production, reduces family income, and compromises local food supply. The innovative solution consists of capturing and storing water during the rainy season directly into reservoirs, enabling constant and efficient micro-irrigation, when rainfall is limited. The strategy is an innovation on ACPC's experience in efficient water management and development of organic bio-inputs (fertilizers, soil amendments, bio-pesticides). Results across our member farms demonstrate that combining HDPE geomembranes with localized irrigation systems increases water availability, reduces losses, and improves crop yields. This innovation builds on that foundation by integrating new, aquaculture and bio-input components to the system, further increasing yields and economic benefits to families. Immediate benefits include year-round horticultural production, job creation in reservoir construction and product marketing, and increased family income. In the medium and long term, the initiative promotes food security, a constant supply to local markets, the strengthening of sustainable agriculture, and resilience to droughts through the efficient use of water resources. The initiative directly impacts producers, families, communities, and consumers, promoting local agricultural and economic development and contributing to environmental protection.

core_fields.title: Advancing Digital Monitoring and Consumer Information System for Healthier Pre-Packaged Food Environment in Nigeria; NigeFE-FLAIR
core_fields.description: This project aims to collect data, harmonize, and develop a robust digital architecture housing data on over 10,000 pre-packaged food products. Using a rigorous, multimodal framework for food labelling extraction and healthiness classification based on predefined index criteria, the system will establish adaptive monitoring capabilities through its capacity to learn from new data inputs. These product attributes will be integrated with consumer requirements and preferences to deliver personalized, scientifically grounded healthier pre-packaged food recommendations
core_fields.abstract: Two major global conversations currently shape public health priorities. First, is the unprecedented rise in childhood obesity, which has now surpassed undernutrition worldwide. Second, is the aggressive dominance of ultra-processed in the global food market and health impacts associated with their consumption highlighted by the Lancet Series. Evidence have established that most pre-packaged foods are unhealthy, and diets high in critical macronutrients, are a major modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases (NCDs). In Nigeria, NCDs account for approximately one-third of adult deaths. Improving the healthiness of pre-packaged food environment has endorsed as an effective strategy for obesity/NCDs prevention and management, as outlined in the WHO Acceleration Plan to Stop Obesity and WHO Best Buys for NCD prevention. Hence, the development of an AI-assisted digital system to monitor the pre-packaged food environment and systematically assess product healthiness using internationally recognized standards (WHO Nutrient Profiling Model for Africa, the NOVA classification of foods by processing level, INFORMAS food labelling and promotion evaluation frameworks, and the Technoserve Micronutrient Fortification Index, alongside gathering data on price and location-specific availability remains an important step. These attributes will feed into a consumer-facing recommender system that delivers real-time, personalized recommendations based on relative healthiness index, affordability, and availability. Through this solution, consumers are empowered to make informed guided choices, health educators have access to powerful resource for consumer education. Overtime, continuous monitoring will generate actionable evidence to support regulation, stimulate healthier consumer demand, and incentivize food industry reformulation and compliance.

core_fields.title: Empowering Kenya's Food Systems with Accessible Circular Clean-Technologies Repairs and Maintenance
core_fields.description: Kijani Testing Ltd, a Kenyan social enterprise, provides circular repairs for solar pumps and cooling systems, tackling East Africa's off-grid solar gaps (~6.6M kits sold yearly, 20% repaired). This reduces e-waste, extends lifespans, prevents diesel use, boosts yields (18-25%), cuts post-harvest losses (50%), creates jobs, and improves food security. With $100K funding, we'll scale to three more counties, train 30 technicians, and serve >2,500 farmers over three years.
core_fields.abstract: Kijani Testing Ltd address the critical problem of premature clean-tech appliance failure (e.g., solar water pumps, fridges) among small-scale farmers. Farmers invest in these devices for irrigation and preservation, but poorly implemented warranties and a lack of local repair mechanisms cause crop losses, food spoilage, e-waste, and encourage farmers to return to the use of dirty fuel generators. This systemic issue is stark: GOGLA 2024 data shows over 6.6 million solar kits sold annually in East Africa, with 75% failing within the first three years per SolarAid's 2024 report and Kenyan studies. This widespread unreliability exacerbates food insecurity and environmental damage, posing a critical threat to Kenya s food resilience. Our solution provides fast, affordable repairs through a network of trained local technicians; add to this, our unique "circular" approach recovers, tests, and reuses genuine parts, significantly reducing repair costs and e-waste. This extends product lifespans, transforming costly investments into sustainable, reliable tools for food systems. Some of the immediate benefits to farmers include reliable access to essential tools, reduced financial burdens from premature replacements, and improved food production/storage. Communities also gain local jobs and enhanced trust in clean energy, while environmentally, we prevent e-waste and conserve resources, fostering a more resilient and sustainable food system in Kenya.
