core_fields.title: Transforming education institutions as food waste reduction and responsible consumption agents
core_fields.description: Thirty percent of our food goes wasted, making organic waste the most dominant waste in Indonesia. Food waste dominantly contributes to the methane emissions, worsening the climate. At the same time, public involvement, particularly students and young generations, is needed for effective promotion of circular food systems, where food waste turns back into food systems. Therefore, our project focuses on promoting food waste bioconversion in the education institutions in Indonesia.
core_fields.abstract: There are 4 issues I would like to highlight. First, there is a high quantity of food waste that is not properly managed. Second, the increase of the food price is driven by unaffordability of fertiliser in the agriculture sector and animal feed in the poultry and fishery sectors. Third, the use of inorganic fertiliser altered soil quality while artificial animal feeds might pose long-term health issues. And last, academic institutions like schools and universities are less engaged in the waste management process. Therefore, the solution that we offer is to promote food waste bioconversion initiatives within academic institution. One way to help degrade food waste while producing nutrient sources in food production is by using bioconversion agents, such as black soldier fly (BSF) larvae where one kilogram of BSF larvae can convert 3-4 kilograms of food waste into fertilisers while the BSF larvae themselves can be harvested for the protein-rich animal fodders, making BSF larvae a promising agent to tackle food waste and nutrient source affordability issues. The use of BSFL would be beneficial in Asia, especially in countries where the technology for processing organic waste is not readily available. Not to mention that the academic institutions play important role in educating next generation. Therefore, it offers an opportunity to simultaneously resolve the global food waste and food security problems with substantial potential to contribute to a circular bioeconomy and sustainable food systems. The immediate and sustainable benefits to end users are school students, local farmers and the environments.

core_fields.title: Microorganisms Fighting Chronic Hunger. Using Regenerative Biotechnology for Resilient Dairy and Meat Supply Chains
core_fields.description: Tierra de Monte transforms food systems by regenerating primary production at scale. Through proven microbial biotechnology, agronomic accompaniment, and farmer-led learning networks, we enable supply chains to produce safer, more nutritious, and affordable food while restoring soils, biodiversity, and climate function. With over a decade of commercial deployment across 85,000+ hectares, we address structural drivers of chronic hunger by replacing toxic inputs, increasing producer profitability, and stabilizing food supply - making resilient production viable and
core_fields.abstract: This project introduces an integrated regenerative biotechnological approach that addresses the entire primary production system - from soil and forage to animal health, facilities, and nutrient circularity while explicitly lowering costs and risk for farmers and consumers. Tierra de Monte deploys non-GMO microbial consortia, combined with agronomic and zoosanitary advisory, to restore biological functions across land, animals, and processes as one system. At the field level, microbial biotechnology regenerates soils, improves pasture and forage productivity, and suppresses pests naturally, reducing dependence on pesticides and synthetic fertilizers. Higher-quality forage and biologically enhanced silage improve animal nutrition, reduce disease pressure, and sustitute the need for chemical insecticides in livestock management. At facilities, biological pest control improves working conditions and animal welfare. Manure produced without toxic residues is treated biologically and reintegrated into fields, closing nutrient cycles, rebuilding soil organic matter, and sequestering carbon. This innovation is grounded in proprietary microbial consortia design, fermentation, formulation, and quality-control protocols, combined with standardized field diagnostics, assessment and application systems. These biotechnological processes enable reproducible biological performance at scale, translating complex soil plant animal interactions into deployable, measurable, and economically viable regenerative solutions. Across more than 85,000 hectares, this approach has increased productivity by 10 120% while reducing pesticide use by up to 100% and fertilizer inputs by 15 75%. Applied to dairy and meat systems, these gains translate into lower production costs, greater stability for farmers, safer food for consumers, and a scalable pathway to make nutritious food more accessible and affordable, directly addressing hunger and food-system resilience.

core_fields.title: Smart Hermetic Storage and Digital Grain Traceability for Safe, Nutritious Food Systems
core_fields.description: Silo Africa deploys smart hermetic silos, IoT monitoring, and a digital grain marketplace to reduce post-harvest losses, prevent aflatoxin, and improve farmer incomes. The project enables smallholders especially women to safely store grain, verify quality, access finance, and sell to structured markets. By combining storage, traceability, and fair market linkages, the initiative increases food safety, year-round availability, and climate resilience for rural communities.
core_fields.abstract: Across East Africa, up to 30% of staple grains are lost after harvest due to pests, moisture, mold, and aflatoxin contamination. These losses undermine food availability, household nutrition, farmer incomes, and climate resilience. Traditional methods sacks, chemicals, open cribs are unsafe, ineffective, and environmentally harmful. Silo Africa introduces an integrated, science-driven solution combining hermetic metal silos, IoT quality monitoring, and the KuzaTrade digital marketplace. Hermetic storage eliminates oxygen, preventing pests and aflatoxin formation without chemicals. Solar-powered sensors monitor temperature, humidity, and CO₂, sending alerts to farmers via SMS/USSD to prevent spoilage. Grain delivered to community hubs is weighed, graded, moisture-tested, and recorded as a digital receipt, enabling traceability and trusted transactions. These scientific and technical insights airtight preservation, real-time environmental sensing, and digital verification address the root causes of post-harvest loss. End users benefit immediately through safer, longer-lasting grain, improved household food reserves, and higher market prices for quality-verified deliveries. Women s groups and cooperatives gain community storage infrastructure, predictable income, and reduced exposure to toxins. Youth benefit from fabrication, maintenance, and extension jobs. Environmentally, the solution reduces food waste and eliminates chemical pesticides. Sustainably, the model integrates local manufacturing, subscription-based monitoring, and structured buyer demand, ensuring long-term viability and scale.

core_fields.title: Agro-Yield Plus Project
core_fields.description: Agro-Yield Plus Project is dedicated to boosting farm profitability by supplying high-quality and improved seedlings for commercial cash crops. ReLeaf Solutions utilizes superior genetics to produce plants that are disease-resistant, climate resistant and fast-growing. Our goal is to provide smallholder farmers with the strongest possible start, ensuring higher survival rates, increased harvest yields, and a maximum return on investment for the agricultural season.
core_fields.abstract: Many farmers suffer from low productivity due to " climate and transplant shocks" and poor genetic quality. Traditional seedlings often have weak root systems and low disease resistance, leading to high mortality rates in the field. This results in wasted resources, lower incomes for farmers, and inconsistent food supply for the community. Our Innovation & Technical Insight Agro-Yield Plus solves this by industrializing the "nursery phase" through controlled-environment agriculture. Instead of open-field sowing, we utilize a scientifically optimized hardening-off protocol. This process gradually exposes seedlings to external conditions while they are still in the nursery, thickening the plant's cuticle and strengthening root biomass. Combined with the selection of hybrid varieties that exhibit superior genetic vigor, we produce a "field-ready" plant that is biologically programmed to thrive immediately upon planting

core_fields.title: Farm Assist
core_fields.description: Farm Assist is an AI‑powered advisory platform that delivers real‑time, localized farming guidance to smallholder farmers in Ghana. Using simple mobile access (SMS, voice, and app), it provides tailored insights on soil health, planting, pests, and climate adaptation. Co‑created with farmers and partners, Farm Assist bridges the agricultural extension gap with practical, data‑driven advice that boosts yields, resilience and sustainable farming practices.
core_fields.abstract: Farm Assist tackles a critical gap in rural Ghana s food system: smallholder farmers lack timely, localized information on soil health, weather, pests, and climate risks, yet agriculture employs over 70% of Ghana s rural population and underpins food security and incomes. Access to reliable climate and agronomic information is shown to significantly increase smallholder productivity and resilience, but traditional extension services are limited and digital tools often fail to reach low‑resource farmers. Our innovation uses artificial intelligence to transform complex climate, soil, and agronomy data into simple, actionable guidance delivered via basic mobile phones (SMS/voice and light apps). By integrating satellite data with farmer and extension feedback, Farm Assist personalizes recommendations in local languages, addressing barriers like digital literacy and connectivity. This approach is informed by research showing that ICT tools boost farm productivity when they are accessible, context‑appropriate, and technology is paired with local training. Farm Assist is a human‑centered solution built from farmer co‑design and scientific insights. It empowers farmers to make better decisions about planting, soil care, and climate adaptation, improving yields, income stability and food security. Immediate benefits include reduced risk of crop loss and increased adoption of climate‑smart practices, while long‑term benefits include stronger rural livelihoods, healthier soils, and more resilient food systems. Farm Assist bridges science and community knowledge, helping to unlock digital agriculture s potential for smallholder impact.

core_fields.title: Scaling Climate-Resilient Seed Systems for Inclusive Smallholder Productivity and Food Security
core_fields.description: Smallholder farmers in Northern Uganda lose an estimated 20-35% of cereals and legumes due to poor storage, pests, moisture, and weak market access, undermining food security, incomes, and seed quality. Equator Seeds Limited, together with Equator Commodities Impex Ltd, proposes an integrated solution combining hermetic storage, last-mile seed distribution, climate-smart extension, and structured markets in Gulu, Omoro, and Nwoya to reduce losses, preserve quality, and increase farmer incomes and resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The solution integrates hermetic storage technologies (PICS bags, metal silos, and community cocoons) directly into Equator Seeds Limited's last-mile seed kiosk network and Equator Commodities Impex Ltd's structured market system. Hermetic storage creates an airtight, oxygen-limited environment that naturally stops insects and mold without chemicals, preserving both grain quality and seed germination. Farmers are trained in drying, moisture control, and safe storage, while digital tools (USSD and QR traceability) strengthen seed quality assurance and ordering. The scientific insight behind this approach is well-established post-harvest biology: insect respiration and fungal growth collapse in low-oxygen, low-moisture conditions. By embedding this proven technology within a commercial seed-to-market model, adoption becomes practical, scalable, and sustainable. Immediate benefits include 30-50% reduction in post-harvest losses, safer food with lower aflatoxin levels, improved seed germination, and the ability for farmers to store and sell when prices are higher. Sustainably, farmers gain higher incomes (≈20%), stronger climate resilience, reduced chemical use, better nutrition, and more reliable grain supplies for markets benefiting communities, buyers, and the environment alike.

core_fields.title: Automated Livestock Brooding System with Remote Monitoring & Control App: Broodiinnox
core_fields.description: Broodiinnox is an automated livestock brooding system that intelligently senses and regulates temperature based on livestock animal age and needs, cutting costs, saving labor, and ensuring healthier, more productive farms. It has a capacity to brood different livestock like chicks, ducks, turkeys, piglets, and rabbits. The farmer select what they want to brood, and the system does the rest work. It's also monitored and controlled remotely by using our dedicated web and mobile application.
core_fields.abstract: Broodiinnox is an automated, renewable-energy-powered livestock brooding system designed to improve survival and growth of young animals such as chicks, piglets, and rabbits. It addresses a critical challenge faced by livestock farmers in Rwanda and Africa: providing safe, reliable, and affordable heat during the brooding stage. Today, over 95% of Rwanda s poultry farmers rely on charcoal-based brooders (NIRDA, 2020). These systems are costly, labor-intensive, and unreliable, consuming up to 15% of household income while still causing 20% mortality due to temperature fluctuations, smoke inhalation, and related respiratory diseases. Charcoal use also drives deforestation about 380 hectares cleared weekly around Kigali and releases large volumes of greenhouse gases, undermining climate and public health goals. Broodiinnox replaces polluting fuels with a smart, clean-energy solution. Using environmental sensors and automation, the system precisely regulates temperature according to animal age and ambient conditions, eliminating constant manual supervision and reducing human error. It is powered by solar or hydro-electricity with battery backup, making it suitable for both on-grid and off-grid farms. Zone-specific heating minimizes energy waste, while a mobile and web platform enables remote monitoring and alerts. The solution is grounded in field research, including interviews with 191 farmers across 13 districts and validation with researchers from the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources. Broodiinnox delivers immediate and sustainable benefits: up to 30% reduction in operational costs, lower livestock mortality, higher farmer incomes, reduced deforestation and emissions, improved air quality, 60 direct jobs to date, increased affordability of animal products, and greater youth participation in technology-enabled

core_fields.title: From Soybean to Jack Bean: A Greener Future for Tempeh
core_fields.description: This project scales innovative jack bean tempeh to preserve Indonesia s plant-based food traditions while reducing reliance on less healthy, unsustainable foods. Partnering with youth- and women-led enterprises, we will reach 100,000 people through direct consumption, school feeding, and value chains. Expanding from Sumatra and Java to Bali and Sulawesi/Borneo, the project will support 1,000 farmers, enable 8 tons of jack bean tempeh production, while promoting regenerative farming and strategic marketing approaches.
core_fields.abstract: In Indonesia, rising incomes and urbanisation have accelerated a dietary shift toward animal-source foods, with red meat expected to grow 1321% by 2050. This transition increases food-related GHG emissions exponentially compared to traditionally plant-rich Indonesian diet. Tempeh, a popular protein-rich Indonesians protein food, depends on 2 million tons of imported soybeans annually, creating supply vulnerabilities and high GHG emissions. As a globally traded commodity, price fluctuations force small/medium producers to absorb losses or reduce quality. Sustainability concerns stem from reliance on large-scale U.S. monoculture systems dependent on fertilizers and pesticides. Our innovation introduces jack bean tempeh (JBT) as Indonesia's first commercially viable alternative using climate-resilient indigenous legumes. Jack beans are drought-resistant, thrive in harsh conditions, and improve soil through nitrogen fixation. GAIN's 2025 nutritional Life Cycle Assessment of 90 Indonesian foods confirms tempeh ranks among top proteins for combined nutritional and environmental benefits, requiring only 355g to match 1,016g white rice nutritional value (Ortenzi et al., 2025). JBT enhances these advantages through high 1.7:1 conversion (1 kg JB produces 1.7 kg tempeh), 29% protein, lowest fat (1.73%), high fiber (11.3%). Building on our pilot in 2024, we will work with 1,000 farmers to cultivate jack bean and 6 SMEs to produce JBT to reach an estimated 100,000 consumers across retail and schools. The benefits of this project include 9 tons of nitrogen fixation, preventing 8 tons of soybean imports and developing a sustainable, stable local value chain for JBT across Indonesia.

core_fields.title: Climate-Smart Rice Value Chain Innovation for Nutritious, Sustainable, and Inclusive Food Systems in Nigeria
core_fields.description: The project strengthens Nigeria s rice value chain by enabling smallholder rice farmers to produce biofortified, zinc-rich FARO 71 and 72 rice using nutrient-dense inputs and climate-smart Good Agricultural Practices. Farmers receive certified seeds, fertilizers, and agronomic training through our input credit scheme, repaid with paddy at harvest. Harvested paddy is processed into nutrient-rich brown, whole-grain rice at our solar-powered rice mill, reducing emissions, improving yields, increasing farmer incomes, and delivering healthier food to local markets.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder rice farmers in Nigeria face low yields, poor nutrition, and weak market access due to traditional varieties, poor inputs, and climate-vulnerable practices. This traps them in poverty and food insecurity. Our innovation tackles this with an integrated system combining nutrient-dense seeds, climate-smart training, and value addition. We introduce zinc-rich FARO 71 and 72 rice varieties, which address micronutrient deficiencies and offer strong yield potential. Combined with balanced fertilizers and Good Agricultural Practices, farmers grow a healthier, faster-maturing crop that withstands climate stress. Research confirms biofortified rice improves nutrition and performs well in flood-prone Ibaji. Secondly, farmers receive these inputs and climate training on credit via community-led Accountability Groups, removing the financial barrier to adoption. Thirdly, we enable local value addition through Hemam s solar-powered rice mill. Instead of selling raw paddy cheaply, farmers process harvests into premium whole-grain head rice. For instance, two tons of paddy sold raw yield about ₦700,000. Processed, it produces 1.5 tons of head rice worth ₦1.8 million. After costs, farmers net about ₦1.4 million, doubling their income. Together, these innovations raise yields, strengthen climate resilience, improve nutrition, and open profitable markets for Ibaji farmers.

core_fields.title: Improving Cassava Value Chains in South Ethiopia through innovative production, processing and Post-Harvest Loss Reduction
core_fields.description: Cassava is a vital food security crop in Southern Ethiopia. However, limited understanding of its indigenous knowledge, genetic diversity, and varietal options hinders its productivity and resilience. Additionally, inadequate data on post-harvest losses, food safety, and processing methods also hinder improvement and development of efficient value chain. Therefore, this project aims to enhance productivity, nutritional quality, and reduce post-harvest losses of cassava value chains for safe utilization and crop s resilience.
core_fields.abstract: Cassava (Manihot esculenta Crantz) is a vital, climate-resilient crop, serving as a food for over 8 million people in southern Ethiopia with a significant potential to improve food security and income in Ethiopia a whole. Its production faces challenges like poor variety selection, inadequate planting materials, post-harvest losses, toxic cyanide levels, and processing issues. Addressing these issues is critical for improving the livelihoods, ensuring safe consumption, and increasing the utilization of cassava in Ethiopia agriculture. This project will analyze local and improved cassava varieties at morphological, genetic, and physicochemical levels, including cyanide content and mineral composition. We will evaluate agronomic practices, develop better propagation and post-harvest handling, and prototype innovative processing to reduce losses. Selected resilient, high-yielding, market-preferred cassava varieties will be promoted by integrating indigenous knowledge with scientific analysis to produce safer, higher-quality cassava products. While previous studies focused on cassava cultivation and basic post-harvest handling, this project integrates comprehensive genetic, physicochemical, and socio-economic assessments tailored to different varieties. We will introduce a prototype processing machine and new strategies for reducing losses, innovative for Ethiopia. Existing solutions do not fully address genetic diversity, safety concerns, and processing efficiency simultaneously. Building on advances in molecular genetics, crop morphology, and food safety, understanding genetic diversity and cyanide levels will guide breeding for resilience and safety. Physicochemical data will guide the development of efficient, safe processing machines. Beneficiaries include farmers gaining high-yield, safe varieties; consumers accessing safer products; and processors benefiting from improved methods, reducing losses, and expanding markets.

core_fields.title: Swadesham: Decentralised Rural Food Processing for Nutrition and Livelihoods
core_fields.description: Swadesham pilots a decentralised food processing model that enables small farmers and women-led groups to convert local agricultural produce into safe, nutritious, and affordable food close to consumption points. By combining shared micro-processing infrastructure, skill training, and local market integration, the project reduces rural value leakage, improves incomes, lowers transport emissions, and strengthens food system resilience. The pilot will generate practical, replicable learnings for scaling community-based food systems in India
core_fields.abstract: Problem Small and marginal farmers contribute a significant share of food production but capture limited value because processing, packaging, and branding largely occur outside rural areas. As a result, villages depend heavily on external food supplies, experience post-harvest losses, low incomes, nutrition-poor diets, and higher emissions from long supply chains. These challenges weaken rural livelihoods and local food system resilience. Innovation & Solution Swadesham introduces a decentralised food processing framework built around shared micro-processing units operated by women-led groups and small producers. The model integrates access to appropriate machines, skill training, food safety practices, demand mapping, and local distribution through nearby retailers. A small coordination hub supports aggregation, quality control, and logistics while keeping processing close to villages. This approach shortens supply chains, improves traceability and food quality, and enables local value addition without reliance on large factories. Benefits & Sustainability Immediate benefits include increased incomes for farmers and women, reduced post-harvest loss, improved access to safe and nutritious food for consumers, and lower transport-related emissions. The innovation is informed by field pilots and designed to be modular, low-cost, and replicable across districts. All operational learnings and tools are structured for non-exclusive adoption, supporting long-term, scalable transformation of local food systems.

core_fields.title: Amazonia Veg A Digital Ecosystem to Accelerate Plant-Based Food Systems from the Amazon
core_fields.description: Amazonia Veg is a digital-first ecosystem designed to accelerate the adoption of plant-based diets rooted in Amazonian diversity. Through education, communication, community engagement, and market activation, the project promotes healthy, affordable, and sustainable food systems while strengthening local producers and reducing pressure on forests. The initiative combines food system innovation, cultural identity, and digital scalability to create measurable impact for and from the Amazon.
core_fields.abstract: Background and Rationale The global food system is a major driver of climate change, biodiversity loss, and food insecurity. In the Amazon, livestock expansion remains one of the primary causes of deforestation, while traditional plant-based food knowledge and biodiversity-based diets are undervalued and underutilized. Amazonia Veg addresses this challenge by creating a digital ecosystem that connects communication, education, entrepreneurship, and food system narratives centered on plant-based diets originating from the Amazon. The innovation lies in integrating digital storytelling, capacity-building, and market activation with cultural and territorial identity. Benefits The project increases access to reliable information on healthy diets, supports forest conservation by reducing demand for livestock-based products, creates economic opportunities for local producers and entrepreneurs, and strengthens the cultural value of Amazonian food systems. Its digital-first model ensures scalability, low operational costs, and replication potential.

core_fields.title: Grofunder: Peer-to-Peer Lending for Resilient and Profitable Smallholder Farming
core_fields.description: Grofunder is a peer-to-peer lending platform designed to unlock access to finance for smallholder farmers in Kenya, enabling them to increase production, grow incomes and improve livelihoods. Despite employing over 70% of Africa s workforce, smallholder farmers face a massive agrifinance gap of $170bn, largely due to lack of collateral and credit history. Grofunder bridges this gap by allowing investors to fund farmers directly, while derisking investments through data-driven credit scoring, agronomic support & market access.
core_fields.abstract: Problem and relevance: Smallholder farmers in Kenya are locked out of finance due to lack of collateral and credit history, despite the sector s critical role in employment, food security, and rural livelihoods. Agriculture employs over 70% of Africans, yet the agrifinance gap is estimated at $170bn (FAO). Many farmers cannot access the capital needed to buy inputs or optimize yields, which limits production, perpetuates poverty, and increases reliance on food imports. Solution and novelty: Grofunder is a peer-to-peer lending platform connecting small investors and impact investors directly to farmers. Investors earn returns, while farmers receive high-quality inputs on credit, agronomic support, and market access post-harvest. Our approach is novel because it blends micro-investor participation with farm-level risk management using agronomic guidance and data-driven monitoring to derisk investments. Unlike traditional banks or cooperatives, Grofunder offers a digital, transparent, and inclusive model that allows anyone to support agriculture while receiving returns. Benefits to end users: Farmers: increased yields, higher incomes, reduced risk, access to inputs, agronomic support, market access Investors: financial returns with impact Communities: strengthened local food system, reduced food import dependency Environment: regenerative practices, reduced chemical use, higher productivity per acre limiting deforestation

core_fields.title: Jafife : Smart Solar Dryer Integrated with Agri-Food Platform
core_fields.description: JAFIFE is an agri-tech Platform for smart solar dryer based in Fez, Morocco. The platform, though relatively young, is already profitable. It provides an integrated and decentralized agri-food processing platform. The platform is based on digitalized smart solar dryers that dry agricultural produce. The process transforms agri-products into natural ingredients that are integrated into the core of the agri-food industry processes, thus adding value in a sustainable supply chain.
core_fields.abstract: African agriculture faces major challenges that hamper its productivity and sustainability. Food waste, which reaches 30% of harvested produce, is a critical issue, resulting from product perishability, lack of adequate storage infrastructure and distance from markets. The agri-food supply chain is also fragmented, lacking coordination and access to information, leading to inefficiencies and economic losses. farmers, who represent 80% of the sector, suffer from four major problems: Significant post-harvest losses due to the impact of climate and overproduction Insufficient mastery of drying techniques High equipment costs and energy consumption, Limited market access Jafife is an agricultural and agri-food processing platform based on the use of digitalized solar dryers connected to a mobile application. This application guides the machine installation and the drying process, allowing for real-time monitoring of operations. The platform also manages harvesting and inventory. Products: Digitalized Solar Drying, Solar platform, Marketplace linking farmer with industry , Dried products ,Coloring ingredients Afterward, the dried products are collected. Some are marketed through our partners, while the rest are processed into ingredients and natural colorings for the agri-food industry. Thanks to AI across the entire agri-food supply chain, from farm to factory, inefficiencies are reduced, traceability is improved, and a circular economy is fostered where food waste is minimized by 30% and agricultural value is maximized by 45%. Jafife has demonstrated rapid growth, connecting with over 500 farmers in Morocco within a year and expanding its reach to 80+ farmers in C te d'Ivoire, Senegal,.

core_fields.title: AG Dried Tomato Powder: Reducing Post-Harvest Losses and Enhancing Nutrition in Nigeria
core_fields.description: AG Dried Tomato Powder converts surplus and wasted tomatoes from smallholder farms into safe, nutritious, and shelf-stable powder using affordable solar drying technology. This innovation reduces post-harvest losses, extends tomato availability year-round, and increases farmers income while providing consumers with a healthy, convenient alternative to fresh tomatoes. The project promotes food security, reduces waste, and supports sustainable local value chains in Nigeria.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description: Nigeria is the 14th largest tomato producer globally, yet over 45% of harvested tomatoes perish before reaching consumers due to poor preservation and weak cold-chain systems. This results in economic loss for smallholder farmers, seasonal scarcity, and rising prices for consumers. AG Dried Tomato Powder offers an innovative, sustainable solution by transforming excess and wasted tomatoes into safe, nutritious, and shelf-stable powder using low-cost solar drying technology. The process preserves up to 90% of the nutritional value, reduces moisture to prevent spoilage, and ensures product safety through temperature-controlled drying and hygienic packaging. The innovation combines traditional sun-drying knowledge with modern solar dehydration principles, ensuring affordability, efficiency, and scalability for rural contexts. It empowers local processors, particularly women and youth, to adopt climate-friendly food preservation methods that reduce waste and increase income. Immediate benefits include: 1. Farmers: Reduced post-harvest losses and higher earnings through extended marketability. 2. Consumers: Year-round access to affordable, nutritious tomato-based products. 3. Communities: Local employment and improved food security. 4. Environment: Lower greenhouse gas emissions from reduced waste and minimal energy use. In the long term, AG Dried Tomato Powder supports sustainable value chains, promotes climate resilience, and contributes to Zero Hunger and Responsible Consumption goals by turning post-harvest waste into opportunity.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Land Conservation Project: Nimba Processing Hub
core_fields.description: Youth Glow proposes the establishment of a central cassava processing facility in Nimba County. Building on the Sustainable Land Conservation Project, the facility will enable farming cooperatives to process raw products into flour, gari for a small fee. This innovation reduces post harvest losses, improves nutrition, and increases household incomes. Cooperative ownership and a subscription model ensure sustainability while strengthening local food systems and empowering women and youth cassava producers in the region.
core_fields.abstract: Cassava is Liberia s second most important staple after rice, consumed by over 80% of households. In Nimba County, smallholder farmers produce cassava primarily for subsistence, yet post harvest losses reach 30 40% due to lack of processing and storage facilities. Raw cassava and informal gari production fetch low market prices, limiting incomes and nutritional impact. Women and youth, who make up 70% of cassava producers, lack access to modern processing technologies and structured markets. Youth Glow s innovation establishes a central cassava processing hub in Nimba, equipped with flour and gari units, drying racks, and packaging systems. Cooperatives will subscribe and pay a modest fee to process raw cassava into flour and gari, ensuring cost recovery and sustainability. The scientific and technical insight is that value addition reduces perishability, extends shelf life from 2 3 days to 6 12 months, and increases product value by up to 50% compared to raw cassava. Immediate benefits include hygienically processed cassava flour and gari reaching households, schools, and local markets, improving dietary diversity and food safety. Farmers gain higher incomes, while women and youth acquire technical skills in processing, packaging, and cooperative management. Sustainable benefits extend to society and the environment. Value addition reduces waste, strengthens food systems, and discourages unsustainable land use practices. Cooperative ownership and subscription fees guarantee long; term viability, while nutrition awareness campaigns ensure improved diets. By building on the Sustainable Land Conservation Project, this innovation creates a scalable model for food security and climate smart livelihoods in Liberia.

core_fields.title: Transformation of Ethiopia's honey sector by Scaling Sustainable Honey and Hive-Based production and Food Systems
core_fields.description: Lal aims to scale a climate-smart, nutrition-enhancing honey value chain that empowers 30,000 smallholder beekeepers across Ethiopia. The holistic 10-year program expands production from 80 to 2,400 tons by improving production yields, WASH, food safety, and income opportunities especially for women and youth. Phase II, beginning in year 5, adds value-added hive products, cosmetics, and candles for export. This initiative strengthens rural livelihoods, enhances biodiversity, and builds a resilient, sustainable food system aligned with WHH goals.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation introduces a sustainable, fully integrated value chain for honey production that strengthens nutrition, livelihoods, and environmental resilience in rural Ethiopia. Despite Ethiopia s high potential, honey productivity remains low due to outdated beekeeping practices, limited access to improved hives, weak infrastructure, WASH standards, and minimal value addition. These challenges reduce incomes, increase contamination risks, and prevent smallholders especially women and youth from participating in high-value markets. This project provides a solution by combining improved beekeeping technology, research, community training, WASH-compliant processing, and value-added manufacturing into a single scalable model. The approach is grounded in scientific and technical insights from apiculture research, demonstrating that improved hives, controlled harvesting techniques, and clean-processing environments can double to triple honey yields while ensuring food safety. Additionally, pollination science shows that expanded beekeeping increases biodiversity, enhances soil health, and supports climate adaptation for smallholder farmers. By introducing improved hives, protective gear, standardized harvesting tools, and clean water systems for honey extraction, and processing, the project significantly reduces contamination and preserves the nutritional integrity of honey. Phase II advances local manufacturing propolis extracts, bee venom, pollen, cosmetics, and beeswax candles creating higher-value products and expanding market opportunities. The benefits are immediate and sustainable: Beekeepers gain higher incomes, safer working conditions, and resilient livelihoods. Consumers receive nutritious, safe, and affordable natural products. Communities benefit from job creation and the strong participation of women and youth. Schools and institutions access locally sourced, nutrient-rich honey. The environment gains from increased pollination, restored ecosystems, and reduced environmental degradation.

core_fields.title: Damila Nature Food for Nutritious and Sustainable Flour for Children and Families in Uganda
core_fields.description: Damila Nature Food is an innovative, nutrient-dense flour made from locally grown yellow maize, roasted soybeans, silver fish, and milk powder. It addresses child malnutrition and food insecurity in Northern Uganda through sustainable sourcing, solar-powered processing, and zero-waste production. By empowering women and smallholder farmers, the project strengthens local food systems while ensuring equitable access to safe, affordable, and healthy nutrition for vulnerable households and schools.
core_fields.abstract: Damila Nature Food was developed to tackle persistent child malnutrition and food insecurity in Uganda, where nutritious and affordable foods are often inaccessible to low-income families. The innovation combines yellow maize, roasted soybeans, silver fish, and powdered milk into a balanced, high-protein flour suitable for both children and adults. The innovation s uniqueness lies in its community-based, circular production model. Ingredients are sourced from local farmers practicing regenerative agriculture, while processing is done using solar-powered dryers and mills, minimizing food loss, emissions, and energy costs. The production process also uses biodegradable packaging to reduce plastic waste. Scientifically, the flour s formulation ensures a complete amino acid profile, boosting immunity and cognitive development among children. The approach draws from both traditional Ugandan dietary practices and modern food technology, bridging local knowledge and science to provide sustainable nutrition solutions. Immediate benefits: affordable access to nutritious food, improved child health, and income generation for women and youth cooperatives. Long-term benefits: enhanced food security, reduced post-harvest losses, climate-smart local food systems, and economic empowerment across rural communities in Northern Uganda. By aligning nutrition, sustainability, and equity, Damila Nature Food contributes directly to building resilient, inclusive, and environmentally responsible food systems.

core_fields.title: E-Hoe: Solar-Powered Electric Hoe for Sustainable and Equitable Food Production by Smallholders in Africa.
core_fields.description: Smallholder farmers in Africa face labor-intensive cultivation and limited mechanization options, leading to delayed planting, reduced crop diversity, and soil degradation, which collectively threaten farm productivity and long-term sustainability. Our project aims to scale a solar-powered electric hoe for smallholders in Ghana. Building on a prototype developed in Germany, the project will conduct field trials in Ghana to co-design local adaptations, build local maintenance capacity, and evaluate impacts on labor, crop diversity, and soil health.
core_fields.abstract: In many smallholder farms in Africa, tillage and weeding are performed manually due to limited mechanization options. This manual work increases drudgery and discourages youth from farming. While animal traction, chemical weed control and tractors can reduce labor, their use is limited by high investment costs, fodder and veterinary service requirements, and growing environmental and health concerns, making mechanization largely accessible only to wealthier farmers. These challenges often result in delayed planting, reduced crop diversity and degraded soils, undermining productivity and sustainability of smallholder farms. The solar-powered Electric Hoe (E-Hoe), developed at the University of Kassel, FG Agrartechnik, Germany with African partners, addresses these challenges by providing an affordable, efficient, zero-emission and scalable mechanization solution. The E-Hoe adapts mature, mass-produced E-bike technology for agriculture, replacing human power (60-80 Watts) with a 250 Watts DC drive. Its design supports attachments for weeding, cultivation and ploughing, while solar panels enable off-grid use. While small tractors and single-wheel hoes exist, none combine lightweight design, DC drive, affordability, ergonomic operation and locally available parts. Field tests show that the E-Hoe matches the output of two working donkeys, delivering labor savings and work quality. Immediate benefits of the E-Hoe include expanded cultivated areas, increased crop diversity and reduced drudgery. These outcomes are expected to support safe and nutritious food production and foster equitable access to agricultural productivity for resource-poor farmers, including youth. Beyond the farm, the E-Hoe promotes sustainable, regenerative agriculture by reducing emissions, preserving soil health and strengthening local skills among farmers and artisans.

core_fields.title: Digital and Sustainable Food Systems for Smallholder Farmers in the Congo Basin
core_fields.description: MVUTU is a technology-driven platform that connects smallholder farmers in Congo to local and regional markets, providing data-driven insights, quality inputs, financing, and a cold chain for perishable goods. By reducing post-harvest losses, increasing market access, and promoting sustainable farming practices, MVUTU boosts farmer incomes, strengthens food security, and ensures equitable access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food. The platform is scalable, climate-conscious, and designed for long-term impact on local food systems.
core_fields.abstract: MVUTU addresses the critical challenge of post-harvest losses and limited market access for smallholder farmers in Congo, where nearly half of fruits and vegetables never reach consumers. This gap depresses farmer incomes, undermines food security, and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. The problem is particularly acute in sub-Saharan Africa, where traditional supply chains are fragmented, inefficient, and biased toward intermediaries rather than producers. MVUTU s innovation integrates data science, demand-matching technologies, and solar-powered cold storage to transform food systems. Our platform provides farmers with actionable insights on what to grow, when, and for whom, while facilitating access to high-quality inputs, financing, and expert agronomic advice. MVUTU aggregates demand from B2B and B2C clients and guarantees markets for farmers, ensuring fair pricing and reducing reliance on intermediaries. Our solar-powered modular cold storage units, mvutuBox, extend the shelf life of perishable produce from 2 to 21 days, dramatically reducing losses. Immediate benefits include higher incomes for farmers, reliable access to fresh produce for markets, and improved nutrition for consumers. Sustainable benefits include enhanced food system resilience, reduced environmental impact through lower waste, and equitable economic opportunities, particularly for women farmers who face barriers to land ownership and market participation. By combining technology, logistics, and community engagement, MVUTU creates a replicable model that empowers smallholder farmers, strengthens local food systems, and contributes to global goals of zero hunger, sustainable agriculture, and climate action.

core_fields.title: Revolutionizing Maize Production and processing in Liberia to increase food security and improve nutrition.
core_fields.description: Our project seeks to revolutionize the maize production and value chain in Liberia by empowering local farmers, particularly women, through the establishment of an efficient and inclusive supply chain system. By leveraging technology and providing essential resources, we aim to enhance productivity, improve livelihoods, and foster sustainable agricultural practices. The agricultural sector is predominantly sustained by women, who constitute approximately 80% of the agricultural labor force and are responsible for 93% of food crop production.
core_fields.abstract: According to the Global Hunger Index (https://www.globalhungerindex.org/liberia.html), a 2024 report, Liberia s hunger index rate is 31.9, which is considered Serious . A significant factor exacerbating this issue is the widespread lack of knowledge about food nutrition and inadequate nutritional foods and hunger, particularly among breastfeeding mothers and women who often struggle to provide adequate nutrition for themselves and their babies. Sadly, many children become stunted by the age of five. In several parts of Liberia, children and youth who are in school cannot afford to get a day's meal to keep them happy and in school. Children and youth in these rural and rural-urban communities boycott classes just to find something to eat during school hours, but they don't return to the school's campus. Not only that these vulnerable groups boycott classroom activities, but they also tend to perform poorly in school. Liberia is facing a severe nutrition crisis, with a substantial portion of its young children experiencing malnutrition, which can lead to long-term health, cognitive, and economic consequences. The solution proposed is modeled through the following: To improve the livelihood of women and other unrepresented groups, we establish groups as agriculture cooperatives that are empowered with all the needed resources to engage in corn farming on a larger scale, starting with training in sustainable farming and technology, land cultivation, planting, and post-harvesting. Producing nutritional agriculture and food products made from corn/maize that are rich in proteins, affordable, and promote a healthy life, and end hunger.

core_fields.title: SmartSoil+: Circular Biochar and Vermicompost Innovation for Resilient Food Systems in Rwanda
core_fields.description: VERMIFARM Ltd is a Rwandan green enterprise transforming organic waste into biochar-enhanced vermicompost and vermiwash to restore soil fertility and strengthen food security. Through its SmartSoil+ initiative, the company empowers youth and women to produce sustainable fertilizers that boost yields, cut emissions, and reduce input costs. VERMIFARM champions a circular, climate-smart bioeconomy, creating regenerative, inclusive, and nature-positive farming systems across Rwanda.
core_fields.abstract: VERMIFARM Ltd s SmartSoil+ innovation transforms agricultural and municipal organic waste into biochar-enhanced vermicompost and vermiwash, creating a circular solution to soil degradation, waste pollution, and food insecurity. Rwanda s smallholder farmers face declining yields due to depleted soils, high fertilizer prices, and erratic rainfall, while cities produce over 20,000 tonnes of organic waste daily, with less than 2% recycled. This innovation directly addresses both challenges restoring soil fertility and reducing waste-related emissions. The SmartSoil+ process integrates biochar (from rice husks and crop residues) with vermicomposting (earthworm-driven decomposition) to produce organic fertilizers rich in carbon, nutrients, and beneficial microbes. This scientific combination improves soil structure, enhances nutrient retention, and boosts microbial activity resulting in higher yields, improved water retention, and long-term soil regeneration. The addition of IoT-based soil sensors allows farmers to monitor soil moisture and nutrient levels in real time, ensuring efficient and data-driven fertilizer use. Immediate benefits include 30% yield increases, 40% reduction in fertilizer costs, and employment for women and youth through waste collection, composting, and sales. Schools and communities gain access to cleaner environments and practical environmental education. Sustainable benefits include reduced methane emissions, carbon sequestration, and enhanced food and nutrition security. By merging science, local knowledge, and community ownership, SmartSoil+ provides a scalable, climate-resilient pathway for transforming waste into wealth benefiting farmers, ecosystems, and society at large.

core_fields.title: Promoting smart food monitoring, cutting food losses, and educating consumers for sustainable Tajikistan food systems
core_fields.description: The Consumers Union of Tajikistan is launching a smart solution to boost food security through a digital platform, FoodWatch TJ, which helps stakeholders check product info, report safety concerns, and improve market transparency. The project also includes public education campaigns to promote healthy eating and reduce food waste. By combining tech and awareness, the initiative aims to ensure safer food, cut losses, and involve communities in building sustainable food systems nationwide.
core_fields.abstract: In Tajikistan, many consumers struggle to access safe and nutritious food, while high food losses occur across the supply chain from markets to households. Causes include low transparency in food quality, weak consumer protection, insufficient data for decision-making, and limited awareness about healthy consumption. These issues lead to health risks, economic losses, and environmental impact, making the problem urgent. Our innovation, FoodWatch TJ, addresses this challenge by combining community engagement with digital technology. Since 2023, the Consumer Union of Tajikistan has piloted a volunteer monitoring network: ten trained volunteers assess product quality in markets across two Dushanbe districts, identifying unsafe or poor-quality items. The pilot demonstrated strong engagement and feasibility of citizen-led monitoring. Building on this, the project will expand to five major cities using the FoodWatch TJ mobile platform, enabling citizens to: Check verified product information (origin, composition, compliance) Report food safety issues in real time Receive guidance on healthy diets and reducing food waste Digital analytics will aggregate data, generate trust-based ratings for retailers and products, and alert authorities for rapid response. Complementary Zero Waste Food and Healthy Diet campaigns will provide practical knowledge to reduce household food waste and promote healthier choices. Immediate and sustainable benefits include: broader access to safe food, lower household and retail losses, improved public health, reduced environmental burden, and reliable data for evidence-based policymaking. By combining technology, citizen science, and behavior change, this innovation is scalable, sustainable, and designed to deliver long-term positive transformation for Tajikistan's food systems.

core_fields.title: Regenerative Water-Reuse and Seed Biodiversity System for Nutritious, Equitable Food Production in Mauritius
core_fields.description: This project creates a circular, climate-resilient farming system by recycling wetland-treated water through sub-irrigation and preserving seed diversity with heirloom and open-pollinated varieties. By reducing nutrient runoff, conserving water, and strengthening local crop resilience, the project supports healthy, affordable food production while staying within planetary boundaries related to biogeochemical flows, freshwater use, and biodiversity.
core_fields.abstract: As a Small Island Developing State (SIDS), Mauritius faces accelerating climate pressures intense rainfall causing erosion and flooding, and prolonged droughts driving water scarcity. These extremes increasingly threaten national food security. The agricultural sector, however, has not kept pace with global advancements. With a mean farmer age of ~55 and more than 60% above 50, the sector relies heavily on conventional methods, limited innovation uptake, and high dependency on synthetic fertilisers often used in excess due to declining soil fertility and lack of alternative systems. This contributes to nutrient loss, reduced profitability, and environmental degradation. Mauritius currently has no constructed wetlands for agricultural water management, and this project will establish the country s first surface-flow constructed wetland and its first integrated wetland sub-irrigation system. While such systems are common internationally, introducing them in Mauritius represents a major step toward modernising climate-smart agriculture in a SIDS context. The wetland captures nutrient-rich agricultural runoff, removes sediments and excess nitrogen and phosphorus through natural ecological processes, and reuses the filtered water via tile drains to stabilise soil moisture during dry spells. This circular approach reduces fertiliser losses, lowers freshwater extraction, improves soil structure, and strengthens resilience against both floods and drought. A complementary seed-saving program for open-pollinated, climate-adapted varieties enhances agro-biodiversity, reduces seed costs, and expands access to nutrient-dense crops. The innovation lies in adapting globally proven ecological engineering to a new island context closing loops in water, nutrients, and seeds. Benefits include reduced inputs, healthier soils, improved food quality, and a modernised, climate-resilient agricultural system for Mauritius.

core_fields.title: Promoting Smallholder Farmers' Access to Virus-Free Planting Material for Orange Fleshed Sweet Potatoes in Zimbabwe
core_fields.description: We intend to catalyze access to resilient, scalable, farmer-led seed systems which guarantees equitable access to disease/virus-free, Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato planting materials for smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe. Access to disease-free quality OFSP planting materials will result in higher crop yields, increased household income, enhanced dietary intake of vitamin A, and long-term adoption of clean seed systems and sustainable farming practices for smallholder farmers.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe lack access to reliable sources of high quality- and disease-free, Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato (OFSP) vines, and they often recycle planting material from previous seasons which increases the risk of disease spread resulting in reduced crop yield and quality. We will: (i) establish a OFSP Demonstration Garden (vine production and multiplication centre) at in Seke Rural District, (ii) produce disease-free OFSP vines (clean planting material) through tissue culturing and (iii) distribute 10,000 disease/virus-free quality OFSP vines to 100 farmers for quality production of OFSPs. This pilot will test our core value proposition that strengthening the supply chain for clean OFSP vines directly translates into measurable agronomic and health benefits at the community level and by focusing on the production, distribution and adoption of certified OFSP planting materials (vines), we will demonstrate that smallholder farmers can achieve better harvests, reduce crop losses due to disease, and attain improved household incomes and nutrition. Our solution will lead to improved access to disease-free, OFSP vines resulting in higher crop yields, increased household income, enhanced dietary intake of vitamin A, and long-term adoption of clean seed systems and sustainable farming practices by 100 smallholder farmers and their households.

core_fields.title: Women-Led Circular Food Innovation for Health and Sustainability
core_fields.description: Balai Gizi Keluarga by Kalimaya Indonesia is a community-based nutrition empowerment project that integrates a nutrition education kitchen, micro-lab, and women's entrepreneurship training. Using local ingredients like dates and cassava, the program promotes zero-waste food innovation while empowering mothers to produce and sell healthy products, improving family nutrition and supporting sustainable livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: In Indonesia, millions of families, especially in rural areas, struggle with limited access to nutritious foods, while women face economic barriers and local agricultural waste remains underutilized. Our innovation addresses these intertwined challenges through Balai Gizi Keluarga, a women-led circular food system that transforms local agricultural by-products (such as cassava and date seeds) into nutritious, eco-friendly food products under the Alunna brand. The innovation lies in combining nutrition science, food technology, and circular economy principles to create high-value products that tackle both malnutrition and food waste. Through small-scale community kitchens, women are trained to process surplus crops and natural ingredients into functional foods, like low-sugar snacks, plant-based drinks, and iron-rich date seed beverages, without preservatives. Scientifically, our approach utilizes nutrient retention techniques and waste valorization processes to maximize the nutritional and environmental value of local crops. Technologically, it empowers women with accessible production tools and zero-waste packaging systems. The immediate benefits include improved income opportunities for women and healthier food options for local families. Long-term, the initiative promotes sustainable agriculture, reduces food waste, strengthens community nutrition resilience, and builds a replicable model of circular food entrepreneurship across rural Indonesia.

core_fields.title: Feed-as-You-Go: Transitioning to Dynamic, Demand-oriented, and Ecosystem-Centered Feeding Approaches in Aquaculture
core_fields.description: WorldFish has co-developed affordable, science-based, ecosystem-centered solutions to counter rising fish feeds costs and sustainability challenges in aquaculture. This project will significantly scale-up a Feed-as-You-Go approach that reduces dependence on commercial feeds by enhancing in-pond primary productivity, nutrient cycling, and ecosystem stability. By enabling real-time ecosystem monitoring and greater use of locally available feed ingredients, the approach strengthens farmer decision-making and promotes more resilient, cost-efficient aquaculture systems.
core_fields.abstract: Aquaculture systems rely heavily on commercial feeds, which represents 60-80% of production costs. Yet most ponds convert nutrients inefficiently with over 60% inputs lost to sediments, and less than 10% of natural primary production captured as fish biomass. This results in wasted nutrients, poor water quality, and reduced productivity. Pond ecosystems naturally generate abundant planktonic, microbial, and detrital food resources, often 3-5 times greater than the harvested fish biomass, indicating that these endogenous resources remain largely underutilized. The proposed innovation addresses this inefficiency by shifting from fixed feeding schedules to an adaptive, ecosystem-centered Feed-as-You-Go approach. Continuous monitoring of natural food availability informs real-time adjustments to supplemental feeding. This ensures that natural trophic resources are neither overexploited nor overlooked, leading to more efficient nutrient use and a more stable pond food web. Two novel components underpin this approach: a farmer-friendly toolkit that quantifies natural food availability and guides adaptive feeding decisions; and low-cost fish feed formulations engineered to enhance internal nutrient cycling. By adjusting dietary carbon-to-nitrogen ratios and incorporating slowly degradable carbon sources, the system stimulates microbial and planktonic productivity and promotes feces-driven nutrient recycling. Unlike traditional fertilization, manuring, or biofloc technologies, which can increase energy use or environmental footprint, this solution is low-cost, low-energy, and suited to a wide range of pond systems. For farmers, the approach reduces reliance on expensive feeds, improves feed conversion efficiency, and enhances profitability. For consumers and ecosystems, it supports healthier fish products, cleaner water, and a more resilient production aligned with circular bioeconomy principles.

core_fields.title: Regenerative Insect Micro-Farms for Nutritious, Affordable Food in Rural Madagascar
core_fields.description: We will expand community-run Black Soldier Fly micro-farms in northern Madagascar, building on 210 successful units. Households convert kitchen and poultry waste into insect protein and frass fertilizer, producing more eggs, fish, and vegetables while restoring soil and lowering costs. We will establish 150 new farms led by women and youth, strengthening a regenerative food system that improves nutrition, income, and climate resilience while reducing waste and pressure on forests and fisheries.
core_fields.abstract: Rural families in Madagascar face a triple challenge: declining soil fertility, rising food prices, and shrinking forest resources. Farmers struggle to maintain yields as soils degrade, while protein-rich foods such as chicken and fish remain expensive and out of reach for many households. Reliance on fishmeal increases pressure on coastal fisheries, and declining soil health pushes communities to clear new land for crops. Rural households urgently need locally controlled systems that improve nutrition and income without degrading ecosystems or depending on costly inputs. Our innovation is a community-run Black Soldier Fly (BSF) micro-farm system that converts household food scraps and poultry manure into two valuable products: nutrient-rich larvae for poultry and fish feed, and frass fertilizer that regenerates soils and increases crop yields. BSF production requires no irrigation, land clearing, or chemical inputs, relying only on locally available waste streams. Larvae replace expensive purchased feed ingredients, lowering household costs and reducing pressure on fisheries. Frass improves soil organic matter, boosts yields of vegetables and staple crops, strengthens water-holding capacity, and enhances climate resilience. We began insect-farming pilots in 2017 and transitioned to BSF systems in 2022 based on field learning and farmer feedback. Today, 210 micro-farms operate across three regions, led largely by women and youth, with adoption rates above ninety percent and documented improvements in poultry and vegetable production. We will now expand to one hundred fifty additional micro-farms in northern Madagascar through training, local fabrication, and farmer-to-farmer learning, building a regenerative, community-led food system.

core_fields.title: Silage making and nutrient supplement production in improving dairy feed security and milk productivity
core_fields.description: Following the PhD, and outreach activities, five existing farmers` training centers (FTCs) will be equipped with drums, and chopping machines (220v electric machines). Forage and nutrient supplements (NS) materials will be collected. Silage and NS production will be performed with training, demonstrations, and research activities. Dairy farmers, youth, and stakeholders will be trained by considering 40% disadvantaged groups. Training and research will focus on feed conservation, feed commercialization, milk production, and marketing activities.
core_fields.abstract: In Ethiopia, the feed conservation practices are inefficient in maintaining the quality of dairy feeds. Farmers conserve feed after drying and leaf shattering in open areas. This system is resulting in feed quantity and quality deterioration. This is mainly due to the sunlight, rainfall, invasion of termites, and rodents. As a result, dairy performances (e.g. milk production) are reduced by 35% during the dry seasons. Through our innovative approaches in the conservation of feeds from crop by-products in the form of silage and supplementation of dairy animals have improved year-round feed security well as the milk productivity from 60 to 80%/cow/day. As a result, the farmers are going for the better productive dairy animals (e.g breed selection) than the less productive ones. They are keeping animals in their backyard (zero grazing)by shifting from free grazing, which was the cause of degradation. Consequently, dairy productivity has improved, while greenhouse gas (e.g. CH4, CO2) emissions are reduced. Farmers also enabled to collect organic manure and bio-gas production. The young graduates will be trained to be business owners by selling forage chopping machines, providing chopping service, and supplying different inputs for the smallholder farmers. The forage chopping service for smallholder dairy farmers will be practiced through contractual agreements. These arrangements will ensure the sustainability of projects. Last but not least, the project will provide two PhD (at least one Female candidate) and two MSc local scholarships to work on the evaluation of the interventions made, and also intensify and sustain the technologies introduced.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Nutrition and Food Security with a Maize-Bran and Wheat Flour Blend in Bakery Products.
core_fields.description: This project aims to improve nutrition and food security in Dar es Salaam by producing affordable, healthy baked goods using a blend of maize-bran flour and refined wheat flour. By transforming maize bran which is often sold as low-value animal feed, into nutritious bakery products, the project offers accessible food options for communities, reduces food loss and heavy reliance on costly refined wheat flour, all while promoting better health and food affordability in Dar-es-Salaam region.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation tackles the challenge of making bakery products affordable and nutritious, especially in Tanzania where wheat is expensive and bread is made from refined flour. Traditionally, bakery products are made from refined wheat flour, but this innovation uses a blend of maize-bran flour and refined wheat flour to create nutritious bakery products. The problem being solved is twofold: limited access to affordable and nutritious bakery products, and underutilization of maize bran, which is often sold as low-value animal feed. By incorporating maize-bran flour and optimizing the mix with wheat flour, the nutritional value of bakery products is significantly increased by boosting protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals while maintaining taste and quality. Scientific studies and experiments have shown that using bioactivated cereal mixtures, spontaneous fermentation, and precise control of baking conditions can improve the physical, chemical, and sensory qualities of bakery products. Optimizing ingredient ratios has led to products with up to three times the nutritional value of standard bakery products, and high consumer acceptance. This aligns with published articles in Journal of Food and Nutrition Sciences, Slovak Journal of Food Science, and Wiley Food Science and Nutrition, which discusses blended wheat-maize-flour products. Immediate benefits include healthier and more affordable bakery products for consumers. Sustainable benefits extend to improved nutrition for communities, reduction of food loss through maize-bran utilization, and increased value for maize millers and bakeries. This innovation supports food security, economic opportunity, and a more sustainable food system by transforming a common byproduct into a nutritious staple food.

core_fields.title: Evaluation of Celery (Apium graveolens) Extract for Aphid Control on Cabbage
core_fields.description: Growing of cabbage plants has been seriously reported to be affected by Aphids. To be able to produce a handful amount of cabbage, a lot of insecticides has been used, with a resultant residue remaining on the cabbage leaves, affecting human health. We carried out a laboratory test and proved the potential of using Apium graveolens for cabbage Aphid management. This project seeks to pilot the innovation in the field experiments.
core_fields.abstract: Cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) is a major vegetable crop, but its production is seriously affected by cabbage aphids (Brevicoryne brassicae L.), which cause severe yield and quality losses. Farmers especially at the study site of Ngarenanyuki in Meru district in Tanzania mainly rely on synthetic insecticides to control aphids. The effects being caused by the insecticides are enormous including health and environmental. A need to use an environmentally friendly and safe product therefore exists. we conducted a Laboratory observation and determined that celery (Apium graveolens) solution when applied onto cabbage, Aphids were found dead in a substantial number. These findings suggest that celery contains bioactive compounds such as flavonoids, phthalides, terpenoids, and furanocoumarins with insecticidal effects. Celery is a high value crop, potentially reported as a good source for many pharamaceutical bioactive compounds. However, scientific data on the use of celery extracts for aphid control are limited, and the mechanisms responsible for these effects are not well understood. Therefore, it is necessary to evaluate the efficacy of celery extracts against cabbage aphids, identify the active components, and pilot its use in Integrated Pest Management systems before being proposed for scaling.

core_fields.title: Community Legume Improvement Program (CLIP)
core_fields.description: CLIP will support 100 smallholder farmers in Kasenengwa district, prioritizing women, youth, and persons with disabilities. The project will promote legume production, provide a peanut grinding mill, train farmers in quality seed production, and establish a community seed storage facility. A pass-on model will be used, where new farmers contribute 30% of input costs to ensure sustainability. A community committee will manage milling unit, which will operate on a small service fee of $0.0769/kg.
core_fields.abstract: Kasenengwa District faces chronic low nutrition, high food insecurity, and low smallholder incomes. Nationally, 32% of children are stunted, and over 70% of farmers rely on recycled seed and low-input agronomy, producing average groundnut yields of 0.5-0.8 t/ha. These constraints lead to low productivity, high post-harvest losses, and limited household nutrition. Big Harvest Agritech (BIGHAT) will introduce an integrated legume productivity and market system to address these challenges. The model will combine certified legume seed, improved agronomy, demonstration plots and farmer training, community processing via a peanut mill, and structured market linkages. Certified seed and modern varieties, combined with climate-smart practices, timely planting, proper spacing, integrated pest management, and safe post-harvest handling to raise yields by 0.6 to estimate to 0.9-1.2 t/ha. Legumes will enhance soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation (30-100 kg N/ha), accelerating recovery on degraded plots. Implementation will establish four demonstration plots and train 100 farmers (50% women, 45% youth, 5% PWDs), alongside a community peanut mill processing 50 tonnes/season. Expected immediate benefits include higher yields, 20%-40% reduced post-harvest losses, improved household nutrition, and increased income from value-added products. Over 3-5 years, the approach will deliver sustainable gains: improved soil fertility, strengthened local markets, economically viable processing services, and empowered women and youth.

By combining technology, training, and empowerment, this innovation tackles multiple challenges simultaneously nutrition, economic opportunity, and environmental sustainability demonstrating a holistic, scalable solution with measurable social, economic, and environmental impact for communities in the Global South.

core_fields.title: Smart biocapsules for sustainable agriculture: reducing agrochemical use and enhancing food safety globally
core_fields.description: We develop innovative protein-based biocapsules that enable precise, on-demand delivery of inputs in agriculture. These biodegradable, non-toxic capsules reduce agrochemical usage by up to 90%, enhance crop protection, and improve food safety. By integrating biosensors that detect pathogens or environmental conditions, our technology promotes sustainable farming, lowers costs, and minimizes environmental impact. This project advances global food systems by improving access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food while addressing planetary health challenges.
core_fields.abstract: The global food system faces critical challenges: excessive agrochemical use leads to environmental damage, high costs, and growing resistance from pathogens, while only 1-5% of applied chemicals reach their intended target. This problem is relevant because it exacerbates environmental degradation, compromises food safety, and increases economic burdens on farmers, hindering sustainable agriculture worldwide. These inefficiencies contribute to unsafe food, soil degradation, and climate change, as highlighted by organizations such as the FAO, which reports that excessive agrochemical use is a leading driver of environmental harm in agriculture. Vexxel addresses this with smart, protein-based biocapsules, an innovative, biodegradable, and non-toxic solution. These biocapsules integrate advanced biosensors that detect pathogens or environmental conditions and release active compounds precisely when needed. For example, pilot tests have shown a 90% reduction in agrochemical usage, cutting farmers' costs by 60% while ensuring effective pathogen control. This approach not only minimizes environmental impact but also makes sustainable farming more accessible and profitable. This solution is rooted in cutting-edge protein engineering, leveraging proprietary nanotechnology that ensures scalability and adaptability to existing agricultural practices. Unlike traditional methods, Vexxel s technology empowers nature to decide when inputs are required, reducing waste and increasing efficiency. Immediate benefits include safer food, healthier soils, and lower costs for farmers, enabling them to meet regulatory demands and export to premium markets. To put it in perspective, at scale, treating 30,000 hectares with Vexxel's biocapsules reduces 77,000 tons of CO₂eq, equivalent to avoiding 320,833 short-haul flights (e.g., Madrid to Paris).

core_fields.title: Project NutriShala- Sourcing locally grown Iron pearl millets from smallholder farmers for school Meals
core_fields.description: Millets Now sources locally grown, iron-rich pearl millet directly from smallholder farmers. Using patented Hydro NIR technology and innovative formulations developed with Self-Help Groups, we created Nutri Dabba a wholesome mix of laddus, cookies, Nutri Bars, iron pearl millet chivda, and khakhra. Designed for school-going children, these foods are delicious, safe, and nutritionally powerful. Today, Nutri Dabba serves 1 lakh children, linking production with consumption to advance SDG 2: Zero Hunger.
core_fields.abstract: Iron-deficiency anaemia affects over 2 billion people globally, and in India every second school-going child is anaemic. Current approaches such as iron folic acid supplementation and food fortification often face low compliance and fail to address sociocultural, dietary, and systemic challenges. To overcome these gaps, we developed a sustainable, community-driven, food-based solution rooted in local agriculture and scientific validation. We source iron-rich pearl millet directly from smallholder farmers, strengthening rural value chains while improving farmer incomes. Using our patented and NIFTEM-T (Government of India) validated technology, we extend the shelf life of pearl millet from 10 days to over 180 days without compromising nutrition. This process works through lipase inactivation, improving iron bioavailability at a processing cost of less than ₹1 per kg. Building on this innovation, we created Nutri Dabba a range of nutrient-dense products including laddus, cookies, Nutri Bars, khakhra, and malt. Developed using AI-enabled Hydro NIR technology, these products ensure consistent quality, food safety, and enhanced nutrient retention. A unique millet fruit formulation improves taste and iron absorption, with no side effects. Nutri Dabba delivers immediate and long-term benefits: nutritious meals for school going children, assured procurement and higher income for farmers, livelihoods for local producer groups, and promotion of pearl millet a climate-smart, low-water crop. This scalable model strengthens nutrition security, supports rural livelihoods, and offers a sustainable pathway to reduce iron-deficiency anaemia in India.

core_fields.abstract: Innovation: NutriBroyeur a locally manufactured, mobile feed mill (OAPI-protected, n 00096) that safely grinds grains (maize, millet, groundnut) and crop residues (straw, stalks) into high-quality, balanced livestock feed. core_fields.title: PEACE CROPs BONAVADA: Regenerative Food Systems and Sustainable Livelihoods for Forest Communities
