core_fields.title: Climate-Resilient Livestock Farming for Food Security and the Environment
core_fields.description: This project promotes climate-resilient livestock farming to improve food security, farmer incomes, and environmental sustainability. It supports smallholder farmers through sustainable livestock production, in-person training, and practical guidance on animal health, feeding, and methane-reducing practices. By strengthening sustainable livestock value chains, AgroLivex contributes to a more equitable and resilient food system.
core_fields.abstract: Livestock plays a critical role in food security and livelihoods across Africa, yet current livestock systems are inefficient, environmentally damaging, and exclude smallholder farmers from fair and reliable markets. Many farmers face low productivity due to high feed costs, limited access to practical training, weak animal health services, and a lack of affordable, climate-resilient production methods. These challenges contribute to food insecurity, income instability, and increased greenhouse gas emissions. This project introduces a climate-resilient livestock farming model that combines sustainable livestock production, in-person farmer training, and a digital support system. The innovation focuses on improving feeding efficiency, animal health management, and farm practices that reduce methane emissions while increasing productivity. Farmers receive in-person training and continuous support to adopt proven, low-cost practices that improve weight gain, animal survival, and overall farm performance. The solution is informed by field experience, farmer feedback, and tested livestock management practices adapted to local conditions. A demonstration-based approach allows farmers to see and apply practical solutions rather than relying on theory alone. Improved production efficiency lowers costs, reduces waste, and increases the availability of affordable, nutritious animal-source foods for local markets. By strengthening sustainable livestock value chains, the project delivers immediate benefits to farmers through higher incomes and resilience, while contributing to long-term environmental sustainability and a more equitable, trusted, and resilient food system.

core_fields.title: Resilient Queen Bee Breeding and Crop Pollination Hub
core_fields.description: Resilient Queen Bee Breeding and Crop Pollination Hub is a community-based center for the selective breeding and mass distribution of endemic, climate-resilient honeybee queens. The center concurrently runs a Pollination-as-a-Service (PaaS) arm, training of apiculture farmers, sale of hives and honey and its products and leasing genetically superior, locally adapted bee colonies specifically to farms practicing certified regenerative agriculture, ensuring robust crop yields and a sustainable supply of safe and nutritious food.
core_fields.abstract: The project addresses the critical problem of global pollinator decline and climate-induced crop instability which is a highly relevant threat to sustainable food security, by focusing on a genetic resilience as a biological solution. This problem is solved through the key insight that endemic, selectively-bred queen bees provide superior resistance to regional diseases and climate stress, making them a more reliable and sustainable pollinator than non-native stock; the technical solution involves establishing a community-based center for the mass distribution of these superior queens alongside a Pollination-as-a-Service (PaaS) that deploys the colonies to regenerative farms, ensuring high-quality, pesticide-free crop yields. Immediate benefits include reliable, safe food supply for consumers, increased income and stable yields for farmers, and stronger, healthier colonies for beekeepers, while sustainable benefits include the long-term protection of local bee genetics, the promotion of biodiversity and regenerative agriculture, and the mitigation of environmental impacts associated with bee loss and unstable food chains.

core_fields.title: LIVING SOIL, RESILIENT FIELD: Soil Restoration and Sustainable Production of Healthy Foods.
core_fields.description: The Living Soil, Resilient Field project combats agricultural degradation through an integrated poultry and crop system. This regenerative solution restores soil health by neutralizing pH and increasing nutrients while producing free-range eggs. As a scalable circular economy model, it integrates regenerative practices into the educational curriculum, provides short-term income, ensures environmental sustainability, and strengthens peasant food sovereignty practices
core_fields.abstract: This project addresses the critical degradation of agricultural soils and water scarcity in the Maule Region, relevant factors that threaten the sustainability of family farming and the generational loss of peasant practices. Our approach tackles these issues through ecologically respectful and sustainable methods. The solution consists of implementing an integrated agro-poultry system that fosters symbiosis between free-range hens and vegetable crops to regenerate soils, rather than eroding them through conventional tillage practices. It has been demonstrated through empirical results that by applying this agro-poultry system, the controlled incorporation of manure (guano) neutralizes soil pH transitioning from alkaline 9 to neutral 7 and drastically increases Phosphorus and Potassium levels, resulting in fertile soil and healthy plant development. This prototype, adapted and accessible to rural and peasant communities, acts as a tool for soil healing. The immediate benefits include the acquisition of knowledge and skills within educational communities to optimally sustain the system, collaborative work, the development of a circular economy, and an innovative, replicable ecological seal to raise awareness in the community and surrounding areas. The long-term sustainable benefits are the restoration of soil fertility, mitigation of water scarcity through increased water retention, production of pollution-free food, and the promotion of outdoor nature-based education.

Immediate benefits include improved access to nutritious meals for children, increased school attendance, and reduced short-term hunger. Sustainable benefits include stronger local food supply chains, community ownership of feeding programmes, and a scalable model that can be replicated across regions. By linking food access, education, and community systems, the project contributes to healthier children and more inclusive local food systems.

The problem we address is the underutilization and neglect of local biodiversity, where nutrient-rich fruits such as masawu, tsubvu, and nyii are often wasted or undervalued. Our solution integrates community-driven sourcing from youth and women-led clusters in Mutasa, Bocha, Chipinge, and Marange with eco-friendly agro-processing techniques that preserve nutrients and extend shelf life. Packaging innovations include nutrition panels and heritage storytelling blurbs, which educate consumers and promote biodiversity conservation. Immediate benefits include: - Consumers: Affordable, nutrient-dense snacks and beverages that support healthier diets. - Farmers & Producers: New income streams through fair-trade sourcing and value addition. - Communities & Schools: Access to culturally relevant nutrition education and healthier food options. - Society and Environment: Conservation of indigenous fruits species, reduced food waste and strengthened urban-rural linkages.

core_fields.abstract: The SEED-IN Hub is a disability- and orphan-inclusive regenerative food hub in Shkoder, Albania, building on a successful 6-month pilot. It addresses the combined challenges of food insecurity, limited access to nutritious food, unemployment, and social exclusion among orphan persons with disabilities. The project is relevant because these individuals often lack opportunities to contribute actively to their communities and access healthy, affordable food. The hub features an accessible greenhouse for seed cultivation and small-scale food production. Adaptive tools, universal design principles, and simplified workflows enable participants with physical, intellectual, and psychosocial disabilities to safely produce food primarily for their own households, enhancing nutrition and self-sufficiency. Insights from regenerative agriculture, inclusive design, and prior pilot experience guided this solution, ensuring feasibility, sustainability, and efficiency. Immediate benefits include skill development, employment incentives, improved nutrition, and social inclusion for participants. Sustainable benefits extend to reduced food waste, strengthened local food resilience, and a replicable model that can be adapted in other communities. By embedding disability and orphan inclusion into food system design, the SEED-IN Hub transforms participants from passive recipients into active contributors and innovators, promoting equity, environmental stewardship, and community empowerment. This approach demonstrates a practical, evidence-based innovation that simultaneously advances sustainable agriculture, equitable access to food, and inclusive employment, providing a scalable blueprint for resilient and socially inclusive local food systems.

core_fields.title: Nourishing Dodoma: Scaling FPS-Adapted Opportunity Crops to Build Resilience in Tanzania's Drylands using NbS.
core_fields.description: This project scales a proven innovation by integrating Food Plant Solutions' (FPS) science-based methodology into LEAD Foundation's ecosystem restoration model in semi-arid Dodoma, Tanzania. We will identify and promote 15 high-yielding, nutrient-dense, climate-resilient crops using Nature-based Solutions (NbS). This intervention targets stunting and poverty by empowering 5,000 small-scale producers (70% women) with the knowledge and tools to grow and utilize the most nutritious local plants, creating a scalable, affordable, and resilient food system.
core_fields.abstract: Dodoma suffers from high climate vulnerability, severe land degradation and chronic malnutrition. The region needs solutions that simultaneously reverse land degradation and boost nutrition using drought-resilient crops. The innovation is a dual-intensity strategy: 1. Ecological and Physical Intensification (LEAD): LEAD will use advanced Conservation Agriculture techniques under the umbrella of Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to maximize water and soil health. This includes promoting Zai pits and other in-situ water harvesting such as Fanya Juu/Chini trences,agroferstry and cover crops for nitrogen fixation and soil cover, and compost and biochar production to establish highly fertile micro-environments. This base also uses proven techniques like Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) for landscape resilience. 2. Nutritional Intensification (FPS): FPS will leverage its database to precisely identify the 10-15 most nutrient-dense, drought-tolerant Opportunity Crops such as specific millets and indigenous leafy vegetables best suited to these NbS micro-environments. LEAD's team will then deliver hands-on training on cultivation and making these foods appealing to consumers through a Training of Trainer (ToT) approach so as to reach a wider audience. This combination will ensure that the land restoration efforts directly translate into nutrient-dense, climate-resilient food production, offering benefits for income, health, and environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Year-Round Agroforestry Farming for Climate-Resilient Livelihoods in Northern Ghana
core_fields.description: The project promotes year-round agroforestry farming to support rural women and youth in Northern Ghana. By integrating trees, crops, and climate-smart practices, it improves food security, increases incomes, and reduces climate risks. The initiative strengthens skills, value addition, and market access, enabling sustainable livelihoods while restoring degraded landscapes and building long-term community resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation addresses seasonal hunger, low farm incomes, and climate vulnerability affecting rural women and youth in Northern Ghana. Rain-fed farming limits production to a short season, leading to food shortages, unstable incomes, and land degradation. This problem is relevant as climate change is increasing droughts, erratic rainfall, and poverty among smallholder farmers. The project solves this by introducing year-round agroforestry farming that integrates trees, crops, and sustainable land management practices. Drought-tolerant trees and perennial crops are combined with vegetables and staples, supported by soil improvement techniques such as mulching, composting, and water conservation. Agroforestry improves soil fertility, moisture retention, and microclimates, enabling continuous production beyond the rainy season. The solution is guided by scientific evidence that trees enhance nutrient cycling, reduce erosion, improve water infiltration, and increase resilience to climate stress. Lessons from climate-smart agriculture and indigenous farming knowledge informed the design, ensuring it is low-cost, practical, and locally adaptable. Immediate benefits include year-round food availability, diversified incomes, and improved nutrition for farming households. Sustainable benefits include restored soils, reduced deforestation pressure, increased carbon sequestration, and stronger women-led enterprises. Communities benefit from improved food security, climate resilience, and environmental restoration, contributing to long-term rural development and ecosystem health.

core_fields.title: Women-Led Environmental-friendly Agriculture for Nutrition and Resilient Livelihoods Contributing to Sustainable Food Systems, Ethiopia.
core_fields.description: This initiative empowers rural women in Sodo, Ethiopia through Village Saving and Loan Associations, climate-smart farming, and solar-powered water systems (drill shallow-well). By integrating poultry, and vegetables production with clean energy, improved storage, and eco-friendly preservation, households have better diets, reduced food loss, and increased sustainable income. Training in resilient farming, crop rotation, and drought-resistant seeds enhance productivity. The project supports SDGs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13 and Ethiopia s Nationally Determined Contributions.
core_fields.abstract: Communities in rural Ethiopia face persistent malnutrition, low diet diversity, and food insecurity, driven by degraded soils, unreliable rain-fed agriculture, and limited access to credit and markets. Women-headed households are financially and disproportionately affected, relying on firewood collection or petty trades to offset agricultural losses. These barriers restrict their economic livelihood leaving children vulnerable to poor nutrition, school dropouts, and risks of violence. This project introduces solar power to supply water for domestic/irrigation use, and vegetable and poultry production. Women-led nutrition hubs will serve as an integrated solution, empowering women to end malnutrition through using locally available crops and animal products. Organized through Village Saving and Loan Associations, women gain access to savings, credit, and financial literacy while collectively managing nutrition hubs. Solar pumps provide reliable water, enabling year-round vegetable production and reducing dependence on rainfall or costly fuel. Meat, eggs, and vegetables ensure continuous access to micronutrient-rich foods. Innovation merges nutrition-sensitive agriculture, renewable clean energy, and inclusive-finance. Climate-smart practices such as vermicompost, crop rotation, and manure composting regenerate soils and reduce reliance on chemical inputs. Training in safe food handling, preservation, and post-harvest management minimizes losses and improves marketability. Surplus products are linked to local markets, generating steady income for their families. Nutrition education, including infant and young child feeding, ensures households consume food in ways that maximize health benefits. Immediate benefits include improved diets and increased income. Sustainable impacts include empowered women, regenerated ecosystems, and resilient food systems that strengthen livelihoods and community well-being.

core_fields.title: Innovative Manual Stair-Climbing and All-Terrain Wheelchair Mobility Solution
core_fields.description: This project develops an innovative, affordable manual wheelchair that enables users to safely climb stairs and move across all terrains. Designed with wheelchair users and medical professionals, the solution improves mobility, independence, and access to buildings, schools, and public spaces. The project also includes localized manufacturing and mobile repair services, ensuring durability, quick support, and long-term accessibility for people with reduced mobility in urban and rural communities.
core_fields.abstract: Wheelchair Doctor s innovation addresses a critical mobility and accessibility problem faced by people with reduced mobility: the lack of suitable wheelchairs for stairs, uneven terrain, and harsh environments, combined with limited access to affordable repairs. In many communities, especially in townships, rural areas, schools, and older buildings, wheelchair users are excluded from education, work, and social life because stairs and rough surfaces make movement unsafe or impossible. The core innovation is a 100% manual stair-climbing wheelchair and all-terrain wheelchair system. The technology uses a specially engineered wheel mechanism that functions as a normal circular wheel on flat surfaces and transforms into a segmented or adaptive wheel when climbing stairs or navigating uneven ground. This allows users to safely ascend and descend stairs while seated, with minimal assistance, without relying on electricity, batteries, or expensive motors. This solution was informed by years of hands-on wheelchair repair work, direct engagement with wheelchair users, occupational therapists, and medical professionals, and problem validation in schools, hospitals, and rural communities. The insight was that most wheelchairs are designed for ideal urban conditions, while African environments demand durability, adaptability, and low-maintenance solutions. The immediate benefits include improved independence, dignity, and access to buildings for wheelchair users; reduced caregiver strain; and safer mobility in schools, homes, and public spaces. Sustainable benefits include longer wheelchair lifespan, lower repair costs, local manufacturing and job creation, reduced dependence on imported devices, and inclusive communities where people with disabilities can fully participate in education, work, and society.

core_fields.title: Harnessing Innovations for Scaling the School-Plus-Home Garden cum Biodiversity and Enterprise Model
core_fields.description: The School-plus-Home Gardens cum Biodiversity Enhancement and Enterprise (SHGBEE) is an integrated, community-based food system model, proven to reduce child malnutrition while strengthening biodiversity and local economic resilience. It transforms schools into Agri-Enterprise Hubs by integrating sustainable food production, nutrition, and entrepreneurship. The project will enhance the SHGBEE Toolkit, build the capacity of schools and communities to upscale SHGBEE in Lao PDR, Thailand, and Vietnam, and develop a Knowledge Replication Platform for global scaling.
core_fields.abstract: In 2022, an estimated 390 million children and adolescents worldwide were overweight, including 160 million living with obesity, while 190 million were underweight due to inadequate nutrition (WHO, 2024). This dual burden underscores that school-age children are increasingly affected not only by food scarcity but also by unhealthy diets. As central institutions during children s formative years, schools play a critical role in shaping lifelong nutrition behaviors and influencing households and communities. In this context, the SHGBEE model offers a proven approach to addressing child malnutrition while strengthening community resilience. By transforming schools into functional Agri-Enterprise Hubs, SHGBEE integrates nutrition, education, biodiversity enhancement, and enterprise development into a self-sustaining system grounded in experiential, regenerative, and research-based learning. The model improves access to nutritious food, reduces household food expenditures, promotes organic and climate-resilient farming practices, and creates livelihood opportunities for families and communities. To enable replication and scaling in pilot countries and beyond, the project will develop the SHGBEE Innovation Toolkit, a validated, digitized package of modular protocols that integrates nutrition, education, biodiversity, and enterprise components into a coherent and adaptable system. The toolkit includes low-cost garden prototypes, regenerative soil management modules, climate-resilient crop portfolios, school-to-home learning loops, and community integration mechanisms. To further enhance accessibility, reach, and impact, the project will establish the SHGBEE Knowledge Replication Platform (KRP), an open-source system providing implementation support, standardized monitoring and evaluation tools, knowledge resources, and agri-enterprise cost return analyses to ensure scalable and financially sustainable adoption.

core_fields.title: Pollination as Food System Infrastructure for Regenerative, Inclusive, Women-Led Agriculture
core_fields.description: Our work at Humble Bee builds pollination as essential food system infrastructure by enabling women smallholder farmers to manage bee colonies that increase crop yields, diversity, and nutrition while generating low-barrier resilient incomes. Through scientific beekeeping, planned hive migration, and guaranteed fair-forward buy-back, the model restores pollinators, strengthens climate resilience, and improves food security. By making nature restoration economically viable and women-led, the project delivers regenerative, inclusive, and scalable food system transformation in India.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers (85% with 1 acre land) in the Global South face rising climate risks, low crop productivity, and unstable incomes. A major but overlooked cause is the loss of pollinators over decades. Many food crops depend on insect pollination, yet pesticide use, habitat loss, and climate change have sharply reduced bee populations. This quietly lowers yields, nutrition, and farmer incomes, while pushing farmers, especially women (the invisible hands of agriculture), into distress. Our innovation treats pollination as essential food system infrastructure, not an afterthought. The project enables women smallholder farmers to own and manage bee colonies through scientific beekeeping. Women receive training, precision-engineered beehives, access to affordable credit, and on-ground pooled bee migration support. Bee colonies are strategically placed and seasonally migrated across crop flowering calendars, ensuring consistent pollination and multiple honey harvests each year. Guaranteed fair-trade buybacks de-risk incomes. The insight behind this solution is simple but powerful: beekeeping becomes viable and bankable only at scale and with systems support. While individual farmers with a few hives struggle, clustered beekeeping enables efficient migration, better colony health, higher yields, and reliable income. Pollination increases crop yields and quality by 15 35% across oilseeds, pulses, fruits, vegetables, and spices, directly improving food availability and nutrition. Immediate benefits include higher and more stable incomes for women farmers, improved crop productivity, and additional food from diverse crops. Long-term benefits include restored pollinator populations, reduced pesticide dependence, healthier soils, and more resilient, regenerative food systems. The solution strengthens livelihoods, ecosystems, and food security sustainably.

core_fields.title: Ecohut: Future Grows inside
core_fields.description: EcoHut is a solar-powered, climate-smart farming system that combines hydroponics, aquaponics, IoT monitoring, and treated industrial wastewater to grow food in polluted or resource-scarce areas. It transforms wastewater into a valuable input, advances key SDGs, and builds resilience against hunger, malnutrition in school children, climate, and water challenges. Designed for inclusion and local ownership, EcoHut trains women and youth in green skills and offers scalable micro-franchising for sustainable food security and economic growth.
core_fields.abstract: EcoHut introduces climate-smart, closed-loop farming system designed to address the challenges of water pollution, declining agricultural productivity, and climate stress in industrial regions like Khurri-anwala, Punjab. The area faces untreated textile effluents, toxic groundwater, soil salinity, and water scarcity which reduced crop yields, harmed livestock, and community livelihoods. EcoHut solves these problems by integrating hydroponics, aquaponics, solar energy, and industrial wastewater treatment into a single modular system. Using a multi-stage filtration unit enhanced with IoT, polluted industrial wastewater is purified and safely reused for crop and fodder production, re-ducing freshwater demand by up to 90%. Aquaponics converts fish waste into natural fertilizer, elim-inating chemical inputs, while hydroponics ensures year-round, soil-free cultivation for human and animals even in degraded landscapes. Solar panels fully power operations, lowering energy costs and carbon emissions. Another addition is the provision of nutrient-rich vegetables and greens to local schools, directly helping to reduce malnutrition among school-aged children. The project also incorporates 2-mobile solar-powered cold storage units repurposed from used logistics containers, reducing losses and extending product shelf life for community. Continuous monitoring through AI-enabled dashboards ensures optimal water quality, nutrient bal-ance, and temperature, improving system reliability and resilience against climate shocks. Immediate benefits to users include: Safe, nutrient-rich food and fresh fodder for local households and livestock Reduced exposure to polluted water and contaminated produce Lower farming costs through water and energy efficiency Income generation through high-value crops and micro-enterprise models EcoHut empowers women and youth with green skills, restores local ecosystems.

core_fields.title: Instant Nutritious Solution Made from Local Grains (Millet, Sorghum, Corn) and Milk
core_fields.description: The FASO RIIBO PAALGA project aims to produce instant milk powder on an industrial scale. This nutritious blend of cereals and powdered milk will enable quick preparation of balanced meals for children and adults. The goal is to meet nutritional needs with a convenient, accessible, and locally sourced product, thereby promoting food security.
core_fields.abstract: In Burkina Faso, the production of instant milk-based infant formula made from local cereals (millet, sorghum) is virtually non-existent. Most of the instant milk-based formulas available on the market are imported, and those produced locally require preparation. In view of this, the Faso Riibo company has developed a formula for this type of infant formula and plans to produce it on a large scale for the Burkinabe population in order to improve their nutritional needs. The innovative product offered is an instant milk flour, a ready-to-use mixture of cereals and powdered milk. It solves a twofold problem: malnutrition, particularly among children, and the lack of time to prepare balanced meals at home. Its relevance is strong in a context where nutritional needs are critical and time is limited. The solution is technical and practical: the product is designed to be reconstituted instantly with hot or cold water, without cooking. This specific formulation, based on knowledge of nutrition and food technology, guarantees a balanced intake of essential nutrients. The immediate benefits for consumers are speed of preparation, ease of use, and meal variety. The long-term benefits are a tangible improvement in the nutritional status of vulnerable populations, a contribution to the fight against food deficiencies, and the sustainable promotion of healthy and accessible food through awareness campaigns.

core_fields.title: CHARLENE: Eco-friendly cuisine based on the use of cassava and its waste products
core_fields.description: The project aims to produce ecological charcoal in Mb r , Adamaoua, to protect public health, preserve the environment, and sustainably improve the incomes of employees and local households. It valorizes cassava peels through a circular system producing ecological charcoal, improved stoves, and fire starters. The project includes training, community awareness, reforestation, rapid financial autonomy, and contributes to national sustainable development and climate goals.
core_fields.abstract: Description of the Innovation and Its Benefits The innovation addresses the environmental, health, and economic problems caused by cassava peel waste and reliance on traditional charcoal. In many communities, cassava peels are discarded, polluting water sources, while wood charcoal use contributes to deforestation and indoor air pollution. Our solution transforms cassava peels into ecological charcoal, paired with improved cookstoves and allume-feux, creating a circular, sustainable energy system. This approach was informed by research on waste-to-energy conversion, carbonization processes, and efficient stove design. Immediate benefits include cleaner cooking, reduced smoke exposure, lower fuel costs, and income generation for women and local producers. Sustainable benefits include waste recycling, reforestation, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved public health, enhanced food safety, and long-term environmental protection. Communities, schools, farmers, and households gain safer, affordable energy while contributing to climate resilience and circular economy practices.

core_fields.title: Strengthening Food Systems and Nutrition through Sustainable Fruit Value Chain in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan
core_fields.description: Launched in 2024, GAIN s Nutritious Fruit Bars project reduces post-harvest fruit loss in Pakistan, up to 50% in Gilgit-Baltistan, by turning surplus produce into affordable, protein-rich snacks. Currently working with 10 SMEs, we produce 1,000 bars daily and have created 100 jobs for women and youth. With this funding, we will expand to 10 more villages, supporting 10 new SMEs, and engaging 1,500 farmers using solar drying, hermetic storage, and circular processing reaching 200,000 consumers.
core_fields.abstract: The project tackles key food-system challenges in Pakistan: high post-harvest fruit losses, widespread micronutrient and protein deficiencies, low food-safety standards among small processors, and environmental impacts from waste. With up to 30% of fruit lost post-harvest and micronutrient deficiencies affecting more than half the population, the initiative aims to transform surplus local fruit into safe, nutritious, and affordable snacks. The solution uses an integrated model connecting local small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with global expertise from Arla Food Ingredients to produce fortified, protein-balanced fruit bars, a new category for Pakistan. In collaboration with public partners such as PCSIR, the project developed standardized recipes, food-safety protocols, and training on responsible business conduct, improved processing, and eco-friendly methods. This innovation is unique in its combination of locally sourced fruits (like apricots and mulberries) with protein enrichment and micronutrient fortification (vitamins A and D, zinc, and iron). Unlike existing snack products, it provides a nutritious, low-cost option tailored to children, women, and low-income consumers, while significantly reducing fruit waste. End users benefit directly and sustainably. Consumers gain access to healthier snacks; farmers access higher-value local markets; SMEs boost sales while adopting safer, greener operations; and schools can integrate the bars into meal programs. Environmentally, the project minimizes post-harvest losses, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and supports a more circular, resilient food system.

core_fields.title: Scaling Vermitechnology for Regenerative Soil Health and Smallholder Farmers Resilience
core_fields.description: This projects scales vermitechnology to transform organic waste into high-quality vermicompost and liquid biofertilizer that regenerate soil health and strengthen smallholder farmers resilience. By improving soil fertility, reducing input costs, and lowering environmental impacts, the initiative offers a practical climate-smart solution for resource-constrained communities. Through pilot demostrations, farmer training, and emerging market linkages, the project will demonstrates a sustainable pathway to increase yields, climate-adaptive farming, and the development of circular, regenerative agricultural systems in Ethiopia.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Ethiopia face declining soil fertility, rising input costs, and increasing climate stress, all of which undermine productivity and food security. This project introduces an integrated vermitechnology innovation, combining vermiculture and vermicomposting to regenerate soil health using locally available organic waste resources. Vermicompost is scientifically proven to be rich in nutrients, humic substances, beneficial microorganisms, and plat-growth regulators that enhance soil structure, nutrient availability, and water-holding capacity of the soils (Garc a et al., 2024). These properties make it a highly relevant climate-smart alternative to chemical fertilizers, whose production is energy intensive and environmentally harmful conventional practices. The innovation works by cultivating earthworms to bio-oxidize organic waste into high-quality vermicompost and liquid biofertilizer. This process improves soil biological activity, increase plant growth, and reduce environmental pollution associated with unmanaged waste streams (Oyege and Bhaskar, 2023). The scientific insight behind this solution lies in the synergistic action of earthworms and microorganisms, which accelerates decomposition and produces stable organic amendments with superior agronomic benefits (Babu et al., 2025). Immediate benefits to farmers include reduced fertilizer costs, improved soil fertility, and higher crop yield. School and communities gain from cleaner environments and practical learning opportunities in circular resource management. Over the long term, vermitechnology strengthens climate resilience by enhancing soil organic matter, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from waste, and restoring degraded soils over time, while promoting regenerative agricultural practices. At scale, this innovation supports healthier diets, sustainable production systems, and environmentally responsible food systems that benefit society and the ecosystem.

core_fields.title: Optimizing PROVIDENCE-AGRO SARL's Processing Capacity for the Sustainable and Healthy Availability of NTFP-Derived Products
core_fields.description: The project aims to promote the sustainable processing of high-value-added non-timber forest products by installing a semi-industrial processing unit in the Centre-South region of Burkina Faso. The objective is to acquire appropriate production equipment, carry out facility improvements and establish working capital for raw material purchases, in order to increase production, structure the local value chain, improve the quality of product offerings on the local and national market.
core_fields.abstract: In 2024, Mrs. Assanata SANOU/OUEDRAOGO invented shea vinegar, which she presented at the 17th edition of the International Handicrafts Fair of Ouagadougou (SIAO). She then received the innovation award from the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Burkina Faso (CCI). As part of the "Seeding the Future" call for projects, the company PROVIDENCE-AGRO SARL plans to make this gem of a product available locally and nationally to revolutionize people's consumption. The project aims to develop an artisanal unit for processing shea into food vinegar enriched with spirulina, an innovative product with high nutritional and economic value. This aligns with an approach to valorize Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) and combat malnutrition in Burkina Faso. The process utilizes fermentable residues from shea, liana, tamarind (juice or pulp) from traditional production, transforming them via lacto-fermentation into natural vinegar. This vinegar is then enriched with local spirulina, cultivated in the region, to offer a product rich in iron, proteins, and antioxidants. This innovation will, on one hand, introduce a healthy and innovative local product to the Burkinabe market, strengthening the population's nutritional security. Secondly, it will create income-generating activities for local women shea collectors and processors.

core_fields.title: Project REGENESIS: Regenerative pathways to food security
core_fields.description: Project REGENESIS delivers a regenerative, nutrition-sensitive, and inclusive food systems innovation that integrates climate-smart mechanization, low-tillage practices, post-harvest infrastructure, and circular green energy solutions. By reducing food loss, restoring soil health, promoting nutritious crop varieties, and converting agricultural waste into biofuels, the initiative strengthens food system resilience while improving affordability, safety, and trust.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses a critical food systems challenge: how to produce, process, and deliver healthy food without degrading the environment or excluding smallholder farmers. Many systems today face declining soil health from intensive tillage, high food loss, fossil fuel dependence, and limited access to affordable nutrition. These inefficiencies raise costs and push agriculture beyond planetary boundaries. Project REGENESIS addresses this by integrating regenerative mechanization, post-harvest infrastructure, and circular energy solutions into a single, scalable model. Hello Tractor s digital platform coordinates climate-smart services across the maize value chain. Tractors equipped with low-tillage rippers are digitally scheduled to minimize soil disturbance, enhance soil organic carbon, and reduce fuel use. Micro combine harvesters are dispatched to ensure timely harvesting, significantly reducing field losses and preserving grain quality. Green Mechanization Hubs, managed through Hello Tractor s technology, integrate post-harvest storage to support aggregation, quality control, and traceability. These hubs also convert crop residues into biofuels to power operations, displacing fossil fuels and eliminating agricultural waste. This solution is grounded in scientific evidence showing that regenerative tillage restores soil health, timely harvesting reduces loss, and circular bioenergy lowers emissions. Hello Tractor s technology provides the precision, data, and accountability needed to scale these practices efficiently. The project is expected to reduce food loss by 25 to 30%, increase yields by 20 to 40%, raise farmer incomes by up to 30%, cut emissions intensity by 15 to 25%, improve soil health, and create over 500 green jobs, delivering safer, affordable food to consumer communities.

core_fields.title: AQUAPONICS ACCELERATED: A model to transform global systems for nutritious food security and sustainable livelihoods
core_fields.description: Our project strengthens local food systems by using climate-smart aquaponics to produce nutritious food while creating income and skills for vulnerable communities. Through modular, low-water systems, hands-on training, and local market linkages, we enable families, schools, and cooperatives to grow food sustainably, improve nutrition, and build pathways toward self-reliance and long-term resilience.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation is a modular, plug-and-play aquaponics system that integrates fish farming and vegetable production in a closed-loop, climate-smart food system. It addresses the urgent challenge of food insecurity, water scarcity, youth unemployment, and limited access to practical agricultural skills, particularly in under-resourced schools and communities. This innovation builds on proven experience and learning enabled by prior support, including the Growth Grant awarded in 2022 to our affiliated organisation, INMED Partnerships for Children. That support strengthened our technical capacity, implementation models, and evidence base, directly informing the design, refinement, and scalable approach of the modular, plug-and-play aquaponics system described in this application. Traditional farming methods often require large amounts of water, land, and inputs, making them inaccessible and vulnerable to climate shocks. Our solution uses up to 90% less water, recycles nutrients naturally, and can operate in small spaces with minimal external inputs. The system is designed to be affordable, easy to maintain, and scalable, enabling adoption by schools, households, cooperatives, and small producers. The innovation is grounded in aquaculture and plant science, applying proven principles of nutrient cycling, biological filtration, and ecosystem balance. These scientific insights allow fish waste to fertilize plants, while plants naturally clean the water, eliminating the need for chemical fertilizers and reducing environmental harm. Immediate benefits include access to fresh, nutritious food; hands-on learning for students; and income opportunities for small producers. Long-term benefits include improved household nutrition, climate resilience, green jobs, reduced water use, and strengthened local food systems.

core_fields.title: Scrap2Crop - Compost & Biochar Hub for Gokak
core_fields.description: Scrap2Crop converts vegetable market waste and sugarcane residue in Gokak into high-quality compost-biochar blends using solar-powered processing systems. This project reduces open burning, uncontrolled dumping, and soil degradation, while providing farmers with affordable, nutrient-rich soil inputs. By integrating waste recovery with renewable energy, Scrap2Crop improves soil fertility, crop quality, and farmer resilience, while strengthening sustainable local food systems, builds circular agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: Gokak generates around 0.5-1 tonne wet vegetable waste and 200-1000 tonnes dry sugarcane residue that are currently dumped or openly burned, causing methane emissions, air pollution, soil degradation, and rising agricultural input costs. Farmers increasingly depend on chemical fertilizers, which reduce soil health and long-term productivity. Scrap2Crop addresses this problem through a circular, decentralized system that transforms these two waste streams into a stabilized compost-biochar blend (70% and 30%). The innovation combines composting and biochar production. Compost supplies essential nutrients and organic matter, while biochar improves soil structure, carbon stability, water retention, and nutrient-holding capacity. Together, they increase nutrient availability, enhance microbial activity, and improve crop resilience by 20-40% and more effectively than either input alone. Scrap2Crop uses a solar-powered dryer for pre-processing, a low-emission pyrolysis kilns for biochar production, a shredder for feedstock preparation, and 2 controlled composting units for stabilization. Waste is collected through structured agreements with APMC vendors and sugar factories. Scientific grounding comes from established research demonstrating that compost-biochar blends increase nutrient efficiency and soil biological activity by 20-30 percent. Immediate benefits include cleaner markets, reduced residue burning, and affordable organic inputs for farmers. Long-term benefits include improved soil organic carbon, lower fertilizer dependence, reduced methane emissions by 50-60%, and safer food production. Farmers experience cost savings of 25-35 percent and improved yield stability. Consumers benefit from cleaner production systems that support healthier, more resilient local food supplies. The approach strengthens climate resilience, local livelihoods, and long-term sustainability across smallholder farming communities.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Irrigation for Regenerative and Equitable Food Systems
core_fields.description: AgriSol is an innovative approach to food systems that allows smallholder farmers to produce safe, nutritious, and affordable food year-round using solar-powered irrigation. The project removes key barriers to irrigation access by combining clean energy, pay-as-you-go financing, cooperative-based distribution, and agroecological training. AgriSol increases productivity, income, and climate resilience, and promotes equitable access to food systems, especially for women farmers in West Africa.
core_fields.abstract: AgriSol addresses one of the most critical constraints in food systems in the Global South: the lack of reliable, affordable, and sustainable access to water for food production. In West Africa, most smallholder farmers rely on rain-fed agriculture, making food supply highly vulnerable to climate variability, droughts, and rising temperatures. Although solar irrigation is a proven and climate-friendly technology, adoption among smallholders remains limited due to high upfront costs, weak last-mile distribution, lack of technical support, and exclusion of women from asset-based financing. AgriSol is a last-mile food system innovation that integrates solar-powered irrigation, pay-as-you-go (PAYG) financing, community-based distribution, and agroecological training. Rather than innovating on technology alone, AgriSol innovates on how regenerative food production systems reach the most vulnerable farmers. The model enables farmers to acquire irrigation systems with minimal upfront payment, receive installation and maintenance support from trained local technicians, and adopt sustainable farming practices that improve yields and nutrition outcomes. The solution is grounded in evidence showing that irrigation significantly increases productivity, income, and resilience, while solar energy reduces operating costs and emissions. Immediate benefits include a 30 40% increase in crop yields, a 20 30% increase in farmer income, improved dietary diversity, and reduced reliance on fossil fuels. In the long term, AgriSol strengthens climate resilience, supports regenerative agriculture, and contributes to more equitable, sustainable food systems.

core_fields.title: Solar cooking as a service for rural schools
core_fields.description: Our project enables under-funded rural schools to replace firewood with locally manufactured solar cookstoves, combining photovoltaic panels, battery storage and a patented thermal conversion system delivered through an affordable pay-as-you-go service. Schools make small termly payments instead of purchasing fuel. Real‑time monitoring generates data for carbon credits that further subsidize costs. The result is smoke‑free kitchens, reliable meals for students, new jobs for women and artisans, and a scalable model for sustainable school feeding.
core_fields.abstract: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, more than four million rural schools rely on firewood to cook daily meals. In Kenya alone, an estimated 678,000 schools and institutions burn wood worth about US$15,000 per school each year. This practice exposes cooks and learners to hazardous smoke, accelerates deforestation, and drives up already stretched school operating costs. The resulting fuel poverty disrupts meal programs, leaving many children hungry, malnourished, and unable to learn effectively. Ecobora has developed a modular solar cookstove that replaces firewood entirely. Each unit combines a roof-mounted photovoltaic array, durable lithium-iron-phosphate battery storage, and a high-efficiency thermal cooker capable of boiling, frying, and steaming large volumes of food for institutional kitchens. A smart meter and IoT gateway track energy production, usage, and carbon reductions in real time. Through our cooking-energy-as-a-service model, schools pay about US$200 per term via mobile money to unlock the system, closely mirroring their existing expenditure on firewood. Excess solar power supports additional services such as lighting, refrigeration, and computer labs. The technology is novel because it delivers 100 percent solar cooking at scale, integrates digital monitoring to generate verifiable carbon credits, and bundles hardware, financing, installation, and after-sales service into one solution. Competing approaches rely on wood-gas or charcoal and still emit smoke. Inspired by the need to free children from collecting firewood, we designed a clean, affordable system using proven photovoltaic, thermal, and digital finance innovations. Benefits include 50 percent faster cooking, zero smoke exposure, up to 70 percent fuel cost savings, and meals for students.

core_fields.title: NutriPosh Scaling Inclusive School Nutrition Through Fortified, Data-Enabled Foods for Learning and Climate Resilience
core_fields.description: NutriPosh is transforming school-feeding ecosystem, in Uganda, by addressing hidden hunger and learning poverty through fortified composite flours made from maize and pumpkin. Grounded in community insight and scientific validation, the model uses digital systems for traceability, quality control, and real-time monitoring across a decentralized, climate-smart supply chain powered by solar energy and regenerative farming. Now serving 240,450 children and 2,701 farmers, NutriPosh demonstrates how data-enabled local innovation can achieve national-scale impact.
core_fields.abstract: Beyond product innovation, NutriPosh operates as a digitally enabled school-feeding system designed for scale, accountability, and resilience. A dedicated information management platform underpins the entire value chain, enabling batch-level traceability, quality assurance, farmer onboarding, digital payments, and real-time monitoring of school meal delivery. This technology allows decentralized fortification hubs and small millers to meet safety and nutrition standards typically reserved for large industrial processors, while ensuring transparency for schools, regulators, and partners. By integrating digital oversight with climate-smart production, NutriPosh transforms school feeding from a fragmented service into a coordinated system that links nutrition delivery, learning outcomes, farmer livelihoods, and environmental performance. Data generated across schools and supply networks supports continuous improvement, demand forecasting, and evidence-based decision-making, reducing waste and strengthening reliability in low-resource settings. This systems-level approach positions NutriPosh not only as a nutrition solution, but as a scalable model for modernizing school feeding in contexts where infrastructure, regulation, and market access remain uneven. Through the combination of local science, community participation, and digital innovation, NutriPosh demonstrates how inclusive food systems can be built to serve children, empower farmers, and deliver measurable educational and social impact at national scale.

core_fields.title: Ghana Api-Resilience Fund (GARF)
core_fields.description: The Gender-Smart Indigenous Apiculture Fund (GSIAF) is a blended finance vehicle mobilizing private capital for climate-resilient beekeeping and honey production in Northern Ghana. It de-risks investment for institutional investors via first-loss public capital and honey off-take contracts as collateral, replacing high-interest micro-loans with equitable, revenue-linked financing for marginalized farmers.
core_fields.abstract: The critical problem GSIAF addresses is the zero private financing available for smallholder agricultural livelihoods, like apiculture, in climate-vulnerable regions of Northern Ghana. Commercial lenders perceive these small, climate-adaptation projects as too high-risk, trapping marginalized indigenous farmers (particularly women) in cycles of low production and poverty, directly threatening household food security. Beekeeping is a climate-resilient livelihood, providing stable income and nutritious honey even when traditional farming fails due to drought. The innovation makes this vital climate adaptation livelihood scalable by solving the financing gap. Solution and Benefits GSIAF solves this by establishing a private equity-style blended finance vehicle. The core insight is that beekeeping's non-seasonal output (honey) can be a reliable form of collateral. We structure the fund with a 'junior tranche' of concessional philanthropic capital to absorb first-loss risk, effectively de-risking the 'senior tranche' of commercial debt and equity. The mechanism uses honey off-take contracts as collateral for working capital. This replaces conventional, high-interest micro-loans with revenue-linked, non-dilutive financing. This ensures that investment performance is directly tied to equitable impact through a clear profit-sharing model: 30% of revenue growth returns to marginalized farmers, fostering ownership and incentivizing higher productivity.

core_fields.title: Developing food products from nitrogen fixing, soil carbon sequestering trees in arid regions.
core_fields.description: To provide an incentive for local people to maintain their mesquite trees, we purchased 25 tons of pods from a cooperative of 120 families that were cleaned, processed, packaged and exported from our plant. Our food scientist liaison s with local, provincial and international agencies for certifications. Our Casa de Mesquite flour is exported to a fulfillment center in USA and sold on www.casademesquite.com, Amazon, Instagram and by brokers in bulk and retail packs.
core_fields.abstract: The nitrogen fixing tree of the genus Prosopis, known as mesquite in north America and algarrobo in south America, grows naturally on the floor of Death Valley California which is the hottest place on earth where the sugary Prosopis pods were a food source for the indigenous Panamint people before Europeans. In the California deserts , which have the highest temperatures in north American, mesquite pods were the most important food source for the Coahuila, Chemehuevi, and Shoshone people. As such, mesquite is the most heat tolerant nitrogen fixing food plant on the planet. Over the last 40 years in cooperation with the Forestry Dept of the Catholic University of Santiago del Estero, Argentina, Peter Felker and colleagues have cloned erect, thornless, highly salt tolerant clones that produced 4.5 tons of pods/ha as a 14-year average. To facilitate pod transport, we provided the pod cooperative with 2 meter tall, big bags. In 1984, Dan Meyers ETH PhD thesis provided the basis for milling Prosopis into useful fractions which we have incorporated. Before 2021 all Prosopis milling was done in 6 batch processes. From 2022 to 2025, all the batch processes were incorporated into a single line with variable speed controllers to optimize flour production, food safety and flavor/aroma. Now starting with field harvested pods with considerable foreign material, this assembly line system has a mesquite flour production of 150 kg/day(with foreign material eliminated, washed, dried, rough milling, sifting final milling), This production capacity is sufficient for industrial applications.

core_fields.title: Empowering Smallholder Farmers Through Smart Solar Drying Technology in Kenya
core_fields.description: Smart Solar Drying provides affordable access to solar-powered dryers through rent-to-own and drying-as-a-service models. The innovation reduces post-harvest losses by up to 45%, preserves food quality by shortening drying time to 2 3 days, and promotes renewable energy use in food production. By enabling affordable drying options, it supports small enterprises and cooperatives to process and market safe, nutritious food, strengthening local value chains and advancing sustainable, equitable, and climate-resilient food systems across Kenya.
core_fields.abstract: In Kenya, up to 40% of harvested produce is lost annually due to inefficient open-sun drying, contamination, unpredictable weather, and reliance on costly fuel-powered dryers. Smart Solar Drying addresses these challenges through a climate-resilient, affordable, and off-grid drying solution that improves food safety, preserves nutritional value, and increases farmer incomes. The Greenhouse Solar Dryer provides a clean, controlled environment that protects produce from contamination while maximizing solar energy. Its tables and racks expand drying capacity, and optimized airflow ensures even heat distribution for consistent, high-quality results. Integrated FarmShield IoT sensors continuously monitor temperature, humidity, and drying conditions, connecting to the FarmCloud platform to deliver real-time insights and alerts. This integration, powered by solar-driven HVAC fans and battery backups, ensures steady drying performance day and night, reducing losses and improving product quality. Through rent-to-own and drying-as-a-service models, Smart Solar Drying makes advanced technology affordable and accessible for cooperatives and enterprises. The innovation shortens drying time from seven to three days, reduces post-harvest losses by 45%, and helps farmer cooperatives and agri-enterprises in fruits, vegetables, and grains value chains deliver safe, nutritious, and market-ready products. In addition, by eliminating fuel and coal use, the system reduces approximately 282 tons of CO₂ emissions annually, contributing to cleaner production and environmental conservation. Overall, Smart Solar Drying promotes nutritious food, sustainable energy use, and equitable access, advancing a resilient and inclusive food system across Kenya.

core_fields.title: The Smart Tuber Project: Enhancing Tribal Livelihoods through Climate Resilient Agriculture
core_fields.description: The project aims to enhance sustainable livelihoods and food security by promoting 1,000 tuber crop cultivation units across 50 tribal villages. High-yield, climate-resilient crops like yam, sweet potato, and taro will be supported with drip irrigation and fencing. A Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) will be formed, and digital empowerment will be ensured through digital training for peer leaders to access agricultural apps and online services for improved productivity and market linkage.
core_fields.abstract: Tribal farmers in remote areas face declining farm productivity, erratic rainfall, and shrinking incomes due to dependence on traditional crops and limited access to technology. This project introduces climate-resilient tuber crop cultivation including yam, sweet potato, and taro as an innovative, low-risk livelihood model. These crops are drought-tolerant, pest-resistant, and adaptable to poor soils, making them ideal for fragile rainfed ecosystems. The innovation lies in integrating scientific crop selection, modern irrigation, and digital empowerment. Each of the 1,000 cultivation units will be equipped with drum-based drip irrigation systems and barbed fencing to ensure water efficiency and crop protection. Farmers will be organised into 50 clusters and federated under a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) for collective input procurement and market linkage. To bridge the digital divide, peer farmer from each cluster will be trained, who will use agriculture apps for crop advisory, weather forecasts, pest alerts, and market price updates. This use of digital agriculture enhances decision-making, reduces risk, and connects farmers to wider agri-value chains. The scientific insight driving this model comes from studies showing that tuber crops yield high biomass per hectare, improve soil health, and provide nutritional security, while being economically viable for smallholders. Immediate benefits include higher productivity, reduced input costs, and increased income for tribal farmers. Sustainable benefits include improved soil and water use efficiency, digital inclusion, community organisation, and enhanced climate resilience empowering farmers to secure their livelihoods and food systems for the future.

core_fields.title: Increasing Access to Bundled Affordable Inputs for Smallholder Productivity, Incomes, Nutrition, and Climate Resilience
core_fields.description: Afriseed s Bundled Input & Digital Linkage Model trains 5,000 smallholders (50% women, 30% youth), contracts 200 to produce 150 MT of biofortified beans and 150MT of millet and reaches 30,000 more farmers. By bundling nutritious seeds, vegetable packs, free agroforestry seedlings, and optional bio-organic fertilizers with the USSD/SMS early warning system, the USD 100,000 project will enhance yields by 40%, cut costs by 25%, and reduce climate losses by 30%, advancing inclusive, climate-smart, nutrition-sensitive farming.
core_fields.abstract: Zambia s smallholder farmers face severe productivity declines, malnutrition, and growing climate vulnerability driven by maize monocropping, high fertilizer costs, and limited access to resilient, nutritious crops. Over 60% of households live in poverty (UNICEF, 2024), while yields for beans and millet remain below half their potential due to poor seed quality and limited adoption of improved practices (FAO, 2023; Zamstats, 2024). The 2023/24 El Ni o event destroyed more than one million hectares of crops, highlighting the urgency for scalable climate-resilient solutions. Nearly 60% of farmers lack access to early warning systems (WMO, 2025), increasing exposure to droughts, floods, and pests. Micronutrient deficiencies are widespread, with iron deficiency anaemia persisting as a major public health issue (UNICEF, 2024). Afriseed s Bundled Input and Digital Linkage Model offers an integrated, science-based solution to strengthen productivity, nutrition, and resilience. The model bundles Iron- and Zinc-biofortified Mbereshi bean and nutrient-dense millet seed (2kg, 5kg, 10kg packs) with vegetable seed packs, free agroforestry seedlings, and optional bio-organic fertilizers. The Farmers Link digital platform, supported by USSD-based early warning alerts, delivers localized weather, pest, and market advisories, information proven to reduce potential disaster damage by up to 30% (WMO, 2025). Grounded in biofortification, regenerative agriculture, and data-driven advisory systems, this initiative aims to raise yields by up to 40%, cut input costs by 25%, and reduce climate losses by 30%, while improving dietary diversity, soil health, and market access, empowering women and youth to build a sustainable, nutrition-sensitive, and climate-resilient food system across Zambia.

core_fields.title: Fast tracking food and nutritional security by promoting participatory, evolutionary maize breeding in Chiapas, Mexico.
core_fields.description: Women farmers traditionally preserve the diversity of maize, which has a rich nutritional profile and is well-suited to low-input farming conditions; however, its potential remains limited by ongoing inbreeding, genetic erosion and limited seed availability. The project will train 1750 women farmers in participatory plant breeding and distribute seeds from evolutionary populations of indigenous maize on a large scale, thereby reducing the period of food insecurity for a critical number of rural families in Chiapas.
core_fields.abstract: The project will promote evolutionary maize populations that are genetically diverse and cultivated throughout the growing seasons, allowing farmers' preferences, natural selection, environmental conditions, pests and diseases to determine the genetic composition of maize over time. This initiative will apply a train-the-trainer approach to expand the use of nutritious evolutionary populations of indigenous maize adapted not only to climate change but also to the specific socio-economic needs of rural family farms. In phase I, 350 women farmers will be trained, exposing them to 80-100 varieties collected locally. These farmers will select the most promising plants, mix them to create Evolutionary Population 1 (EP 1). In phase 2, the 350 farmers trained in phase 1 will each bring five new farmers, for a total of 1750 women farmers to be trained in selecting EP 1. The selected EP1 seeds will be mixed to create EP2. In phase 3, the 350 farmers trained in phase 1 and the additional 1750 trained in phase 2 will distribute their EP2 to 10 farmers each, benefiting a total of 21000 farmers who will select seeds from the most promising plants to create EP 3. These populations will be distributed by the Territorial Action Group (TAG), an NGO-donors coalition, after the project ends. Participatory evolutionary maize breeding pilot cases implemented in Chiapas suggest that adopting evolutionary populations will exponentially increase seed diversity, increase yields by 15% to 30%, and reduce periods of food insecurity from 6 to 4 months among a critical number of family farmers.

core_fields.title: Ancestral Flavors for a Healthy Future: Development of Innovative and Nutritious Amazonian Snacks

core_fields.abstract: Ahuano Snacks introduces a food innovation based on the recovery of Amazonian crops cassava, Chinese potato, and plantain combined with natural ancestral spices that provide flavor, nutrition, and cultural value. The problem addressed is the lack of healthy, sustainable, and authentic options in the snack industry, a market dominated by ultra-processed products high in saturated fats and artificial additives. This affects consumer health and limits economic opportunities for small Amazonian farmers. The solution relies on low-impact processing techniques, controlled frying, reduced oil use, and the exclusive use of natural ingredients. The technical foundation comes from traditional Amazonian food practices combined with good manufacturing practices, quality control, functional nutrition, and food technology designed to preserve crunchiness, nutrients, and flavor without chemical additives. For consumers, the benefits include access to a healthier, more nutritious snack made without chemicals and enriched with Amazonian identity. For farmers, the project ensures stable purchases, fair prices, and the opportunity to strengthen sustainable production systems. For schools and communities, it serves as an educational model for conscious eating and bioeconomy. For producers, it generates added value, diversification, and access to national and international markets. Environmentally, the approach promotes agroecological practices, reduces waste, supports responsible supply chains, and revalues native species. Ahuano Snacks demonstrates that it is possible to combine health, tradition, and sustainable economic development, positioning the Amazon as a hub of nutritious foods with positive social impact.

Malnutrition leads to poor maternal health, stunted child growth, and higher mortality rates. This issue is highly relevant as it affects the health of future generations and has long-term economic and societal consequences. We propose an AI-powered digital platform that offers personalized, evidence-based dietary advice in local languages. The platform uses natural language processing (NLP) and AI to provide context-specific nutrition recommendations tailored to the individual's needs, available food resources, and cultural practices. The platform ensures accessibility to remote areas with limited healthcare infrastructure by using mobile technology. The scientific insight behind the solution is grounded in nutritional science, providing users with data-driven, culturally appropriate guidance to improve maternal and child nutrition. Immediate benefits include improved maternal health, reduced child malnutrition, and better immunity through nutrient-dense diets. The platform enables mothers and caregivers to make informed dietary choices, improving their overall health and well-being. Sustainable benefits include long-term improvements in dietary habits, empowering women and caregivers with nutrition knowledge. The solution also supports local agriculture by promoting the consumption of seasonal, locally grown foods, which strengthens local food systems and contributes to environmental sustainability by reducing reliance on processed, imported foods.

core_fields.title: Pilot Plant to Scale Circular Seaweed Side-Stream Upcycling into Food-Grade Potassium Chloride for Sodium Reduction
core_fields.description: Plantsalt will design, build and operate a small pilot line inside an Indonesian seaweed-processing plant to upcycle mineral-rich side streams into plant-based, lower-sodium mineral salt and a local bio-based fertilizer. The unit will run in repeated production campaigns, generating multi-ton batches for food manufacturer trials and farmer field tests. This de-risks scale-out to additional seaweed hubs in Indonesia and Southeast Asia and lays the foundation for broader sodium-reduction impact.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses two connected challenges: excessive sodium intake from processed foods - a major contributor to hypertension and cardiovascular disease - and the underuse of mineral-rich side streams in seaweed processing. Food manufacturers need practical ways to lower sodium without sacrificing taste or functionality, while processors often pay to treat or discard saline effluents that still contain valuable minerals and nutrients. Plantsalt upgrades an underused side stream from tropical seaweed processing in Indonesia into food-grade, plant-derived potassium chloride. The core insight is that these seaweed side streams naturally concentrate potassium and other minerals that are undesirable for the main seaweed product, but ideal for mineral recovery. Using selective purification, concentration and controlled crystallization, we produce food-grade potassium chloride as a clean-label ingredient used to formulate lower-sodium salt blends that partially replace NaCl in food applications while maintaining flavour, texture, and shelf-life. In parallel, nutrient-dense solids separated during purification are recovered and formulated as a biological fertilizer for local farmers. Immediate benefits include: manufacturers gaining a drop-in, clean-label ingredient to reduce sodium while maintaining sensory and functional performance; consumers accessing everyday foods with a healthier sodium-potassium balance and lower cardiovascular risk; farmers receiving a nutrient-rich fertilizer co-product; and seaweed processors turning disposal costs into revenue. Over time, the approach strengthens local value chains, reduces dependence on imported, fossil-intensive fertilizers, and supports more regenerative coastal economies. Because the unit operations are robust and scalable, the concept can be replicated with other seaweed processors across Indonesia and adapted to similar coastal regions.

core_fields.title: Making Food Rescue Count: Measuring Nutrition and Climate Impact at Scale in Malaysia
core_fields.description: TLFP operates a data-driven food rescue system that captures surplus produce from farms, markets and distributors and delivers it directly to charities and low-income communities. This project will scale digital tracking across TLFP s operations, capturing every kilogram rescued, meals enabled, CO₂ emissions avoided, adding nutrition and water-loss metrics. The result is a scalable, auditable model that links surplus along the supply chain to improved food security, public health and environmental outcomes.
core_fields.abstract: Malaysia s tropical climate supports diverse crops and livestock, yet the country imports 60% of food, contributing to high levels of food insecurity. Along the supply-chain, large quantities of edible food are lost at farms, wholesale markets, distributors and retailers due to oversupply. Approximately 4,000 tons of edible food is discarded daily. Meanwhile, low-income households face rising difficulty accessing nutritious food. B40 families the lowest 40% of income earners often survive on USD 1,000 a month for an entire family. Around 80% of their household budget goes towards food, often cheaper, carbohydrate-heavy diets. Many B40 children do not receive three meals-a-day. Demand for assistance from frontline charities continues to grow. Global statistics show for every one hungry person, four-times the amount of nutritious food is discarded daily. TLFP harnesses this potential through a proven fresh-food rescue system that re-diverts surplus produce, redistributing to charities and low-income communities. Over 80% of TLFP s distributed food consists of fresh vegetables, fruits and dairy -products rescued quickly due to their short shelf-life. The next step is to metricise and scale this system. TLFP tracks every kilogram rescued; nutritional category, source, destination, meals created and CO₂ emissions avoided- aiming to quantify the nutritional benefits delivered to households. This visibility improves planning, reduces spoilage and builds transparent reporting for communities, partners and government. Measuring predictable waste patterns and nutritional impact in real-time, this enables food rescue to become more efficient, scalable and equitable. Foodbanking is uniquely positioned as a healthy solution to level-up society whilst protecting the environment.

core_fields.title: LiVA s prebiotic sticker enabling SO2-free blueberry exports from emerging markets preserving flavor and quality.
core_fields.description: This project pilots LiVA s prebiotic sticker on blueberries across a full-year export supply chain from Morocco, South Africa, Chile, and Peru to Europe. The sticker enhances the fruit s natural beneficial microbiome, reducing spoilage and preserving taste, texture, and nutritional value. The pilot generates real-world data on quality and includes sensory panels to assess consumer satisfaction. Compared to chemical treatments (SO2), LiVA offers a scalable, chemical-free solution that reduces waste, cuts emissions, and improves grower profitability.
core_fields.abstract: Fresh produce often deteriorates during the last mile the most vulnerable stage of the supply chain where temperature fluctuations, long transit times, and limited infrastructure accelerate spoilage. This is part of a global crisis: 1.05 billion tonnes of food are wasted annually, equal to one-third of global production. Fruits and vegetables are the most affected, representing 45% of total waste. Poor cold-chain logistics alone drive 20% of these losses, contributing to severe economic and environmental damage. Globally, food waste costs USD 1 trillion each year and generates 8 10% of greenhouse-gas emissions, while food miles especially road transport account for around 50% of direct logistics emissions. Current preservation tools refrigeration, fungicides, coatings, and live microbial products are costly, infrastructure-dependent, crop-specific, or unreliable under fluctuating conditions. As global sourcing expands, especially from regions with limited cold-chain capacity, the challenge becomes even more relevant. LiVA introduces a new preservation paradigm. Instead of adding chemicals or live microbes, LiVA activates what already exists: the fruit s own beneficial bacteria. Our patented, food-grade prebiotic formulation selectively nourishes protective microbial communities on the fruit surface, enabling them to naturally suppress spoilage-related pathogens even under inconsistent temperatures and long journeys. LiVA s sticker integrates seamlessly into existing packaging, enabling fast, low-cost adoption at scale. The benefits are immediate and sustainable: extended shelf life; preserved flavor and firmness; reduced cooling dependency and CO2 emissions; up to 40% more saleable fruit in pilots; improved profitability for growers and exporters; and a safe, chemical-free, regulation-aligned solution for consumers and retailers.

core_fields.title: Evaluation of Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) an environment relevant to the prevention of subclinical mastitis
core_fields.description: Subclinical bovine mastitis is an infectious disease that causes economic losses to dairy production in South America. Frequent use of antibiotics leads to milk residues and antimicrobial resistance, both of which are public health problems. This study proposes to evaluate in vivo a biotherapeutic prototype based on lactic acid bacteria in animals selected according to milking practices. The effect will be assessed through clinical and microbiological monitoring, and analysis of inflammatory markers compared to control.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation proposes a novel biological input: a probiotic-based formulation derived from lactic acid bacteria (LAB) isolated from healthy bovine udders, developed as a functional teat sealant to prevent and mitigate bovine mastitis. The formulation is intended to reinforce the natural udder microbiome and competitively exclude pathogenic bacteria such as Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, thereby reducing infection pressure without the need for antibiotic interventions. The scientific rationale is supported by recent advances in microbial ecology and metagenomics, which demonstrate that a stable and well-structured mammary microbiome contributes to natural resistance against intramammary infections. These findings highlight a broader paradigm shift from chemical antimicrobial therapies toward sustainable, biologically based disease-control strategies, in line with successful applications of probiotics in human and veterinary medicine. The anticipated short-term benefits for dairy producers include reductions of up to 40% in mastitis incidence, leading to lower treatment costs and improved milk yield. In the long term, the use of a biological teat sealant is expected to decrease antibiotic residues

core_fields.title: Transforming Agro-Wastes into Eco-Leather and Biofertilizer for Sustainable Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project transforms cashewnut husks, banana stems, and animal skins into natural tannins, organic leather and biofertilizers that strengthn sustainable food systems.
