core_fields.abstract: Agricultural and livestock sectors in Tanzania generate large volumes of cashewnut husks, banana stems and animal skins, respectively, much of which goes to waste. At the same time, soil fertility is declining due to overuse of synthetic fertilizers, while the leather industry relies heavily on chromium-based tanning chemicals that pollute soil and water. Chrome effluent introduces toxic chromium, high salinity and other pollutants that suppress plant growth, reduce crop yields and contaminate food chains. These interconnected challenges undermine food security, environmental health and rural livelihoods. Our innovation addresses these issues by transforming agro-wastes and animal skins into three high-value, sustainable products: natural tannins for leather processing, organic leather and biofertilizers for soil regeneration. Using optimized green extraction techniques, tannins are derived from cashewnut husks and banana stems to replace toxic chromium chemicals. In parallel, residues from tannin extraction and leather trimmings are converted using Rhizobium Mycorrhizae consortia into nutrient-rich biofertilizer that restores soil health and reduces dependence on synthetic inputs. This circular solution reduces agro-waste pollution, prevents chromium contamination and creates value from materials previously discarded. Immediate benefits include safer tanning practices for SMEs, affordable biofertilizers for farmers, reduced chemical exposure and new green jobs in rural communities. Long-term benefits include improved soil fertility, stronger crop productivity, reduced environmental degradation, enhanced food safety and increased economic resilience across agriculture and livestock value chains.

core_fields.title: Circular Agriculture for Safe and Sustainable Food Production
core_fields.description: The project introduces a community climate currency model where rural farmers earn value by supplying biowaste such as farm waste, agro-processing waste and others for the production of nutrient rich organic fertilizer. By treating agricultural waste as a form of local currency, the model rewards climate-positive behavior, improves access to affordable organic inputs, and reduces reliance on synthetic fertilizers. This approach strengthens circular agriculture, lowers environmental pollution, and supports safe and sustainable food crop production.
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria doubles as a major agricultural hub in Africa and the waste capital of Africa generating one-fourth of the continent's total waste with 57% of these wastes as biowaste majorly from agricultural sources. Due to the unsustainable biowaste recovery systems, these wastes end up polluting the environment. There is also the challenge of soil degradation from the overuse of chemical fertilizers for food crop production in Nigeria. Our innovation introduces a community climate currency model to address these challenges. Farmers deliver crop residues and agro-processing waste to Scratop, where it is weighed and recorded. Each kilogram of waste earns the farmer climate credits, which can be redeemed for high-quality organic compost produced from the collected biowaste. By assigning tangible value to agricultural waste, the system incentivizes proper waste management, reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers, and embeds circular agriculture practices directly into local food systems. The scientific insight behind this solution is the proven capacity of organic compost and fertilizers to restore soil nutrients, improve soil structure, and increase crop yields while mitigating environmental pollution. By linking waste recovery to input access, we create a closed-loop system that aligns economic incentives with sustainable farming practices. Immediate benefits for farmers include affordable, nutrient-rich fertilizer, improved soil health, and reduced input costs. Communities benefit from reduced waste-related pollution, while the environment gains from lower chemical fertilizer use and increased soil carbon. Over time, this model strengthens farmer livelihoods, promotes safe food production, and establishes a scalable, climate-smart framework for resilient local food systems.

This project will build the "Capital Facilitation Module", a critical tech upgrade co-designed with financiers. This module will transform raw SME data into the structured reports lenders require, unlocking a qualified pipeline of investible SMEs and enabling them to access finance.
core_fields.abstract: The Problem Agricultural SMEs in Africa are a critical but "underserved sector" for lenders. Financiers cannot deploy capital because they lack the "verifiable, digitised data" needed to assess risk. Our open-source ERP, AgriOS, already allows SMEs to collect this data. However, the critical gap remains: there is no direct, trusted, or efficient "bridge" to get this data from the SME to the lender in a format they can use. How is the problem being solved? This project builds that bridge. The innovation is a new "Capital Facilitation Module" for the AgriOS platform. The key insight is that this tool cannot be built in isolation; it must be "co-designed" with "agricultural investors and lenders". We will use the funding to partner with financiers to build a "seamless, tech-facilitated process" that transforms raw SME operational data into the "verifiable, structured reports" that lenders need to deploy capital with confidence. What are the specific benefits to end-users? Immediate Benefits: SMEs using AgriOS will be able to securely transmit an "anonymised data package" to participating lenders for pre-qualification. Lenders gain access to a "qualified pipeline of opportunities", saving them time and money on due diligence. Sustainable Benefits: This module unlocks a scalable pathway to finance for hundreds of SMEs. It creates a new, digitally-enabled ecosystem that permanently lowers the risk and cost of SME lending, driving sustainable growth across the agricultural sector.

core_fields.title: Agroecology Now: Scaling Organic Inputsc, protein rich animal feed and Agroecology for Resilient Family Farming
core_fields.description: According to the World Bank, Liberia generates about 1.5 million kg of solid waste daily while 40 65% is organic. Amid unemployment, the Agroecology Now project proposes converting organic waste into compost, biopesticides, and protein-rich animal feed using Black Soldier Fly larvae. In 2025, Green Cities Inc. produced 44.8 MT of compost and 1,200 liters of biopesticides, produced 200kg protein enriched animal feed and supported informal work for about 2,000 youth and women.
core_fields.abstract: Liberia s smallholder farmers face declining soil fertility, rising chemical input costs, low crop diversity, and increasing pollution from biodegradable waste. Heavy reliance on synthetic fertilizers and pesticides accelerates soil acidification, reduces beneficial microbial life, and weakens long-term productivity. Chemical residues contaminate food and water, contributing to gastrointestinal illnesses and long-term endocrine risks. On the other hand, the cost of animal protein continues to rise, putting a burden on farmers and negatively affecting animal production. Together, these pressures reduce yields, degrade ecosystems, and worsen malnutrition in rural and peri-urban communities. Under the Agroecology Now initiative, Green Cities Inc. (GCI) advances a circular agroecology solution that converts urban market waste into certified organic fertilizers, plant-based biopesticides, and protein-rich animal feed. Using controlled aerobic composting, microbial activation, botanical extraction, and Black Soldier Fly technology, GCI produces safe, affordable agricultural inputs while reducing organic waste volumes and lowering feed costs. At the Bentol Innovation Farm, GCI tests and validates its inputs across vegetables, legumes, root crops, and cereals. Trials show improved soil structure, enhanced moisture retention, and increased nutrient availability, leading to stronger, more climate-resilient yields. Beyond production, the model integrates farmer field schools, demonstration plots, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture, promoting crops such as orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, legumes, and vegetables.

core_fields.title: Digital nutrition monitoring and community food hubs to improve maternal and child nutrition in Uyumbu
core_fields.description: The project introduces a digital nutrition monitoring system linked with community based Safe Food Hubs to transform maternal and child nutrition in Uyumbu and Nsogolo villages, Urambo District. The project integrates mobile data tracking, real time referrals and locally sourced nutritious foods to reduce malnutrition and improve dietary diversity. By combining technology, community health workers and smallholder farmers, NutriTech creates a scalable, equitable and health centered food system innovation for rural Tanzania.
core_fields.abstract: NutriTech Tanzania addresses persistent maternal and child undernutrition in Uyumbu Ward (population 19,855) and Nsogolo Village, Urambo District, where limited dietary diversity and weak nutrition monitoring contribute to high regional stunting rates (Tabora 30%). Local health facilities including Nsogolo Dispensary, lack reliable tools to track growth or link vulnerable households to safe, nutritious foods. At the same time more than 60 smallholder farmers in the ward rely on seasonal, low value crop sales while post-harvest losses of staple foods commonly exceed 20-30%. The innovation integrates digital nutrition monitoring with community based Safe Food Hubs to bridge this gap. A mobile and SMS nutrition platform enables community health workers to register and monitor at least 900 children under five and 200 pregnant women, capturing real time anthropometry and sending automated alerts for cases requiring follow-up. The system uses low-bandwidth, offline capable technology tailored for rural settings. Data from the app directly connects households to Safe Food Hubs established in Nsogolo and surrounding villages. These hubs aggregate produce from 60 local farmers, apply basic food safety and preservation processes (solar drying, clean packaging) and supply 3,000 affordable nutritious meal kits targeted at vulnerable households. This creates a circular, community driven system where nutrition needs identified digitally are met by local production. Immediate benefits include earlier detection of malnutrition, improved dietary diversity, safer foods, reduced losses for farmers and increased household income. Long term benefits include a data driven community nutrition system, strengthened farmer consumer linkages and a scalable model for resilient.

core_fields.title: SweetPot: Transforming Local Orange fleshed Sweetpotatoes into Nutritious Affordable foods to fight Malnutrition
core_fields.description: SweetPot addresses vitamin A deficiency (VAD) in Ghana which affects 70% of children under five, by transforming underutilized orange-fleshed sweet potatoes (OFSP) into nutritious, affordable foods. Our flagship product is a naturally sweetened, vitamin A-enriched yoghurt (dairy-plant-based hybrid style). This innovation tackles malnutrition, reduces post-harvest losses for farmers, and offers a healthier alternative to processed snacks. We are establishing a modular processing facility to scale our impact and launch new products.
core_fields.abstract: Ghana faces a double burden of malnutrition, with high rates of Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) alongside rising obesity. VAD affects 7 in 10 children, leading to impaired immunity and development, and costs Ghana 6.4% of its GDP. Concurrently, smallholder OFSP farmers suffer up to 70% post-harvest losses due to a lack of processing and market access. SweetPot's innovation is a platform for creating nutritious foods using biofortified OFSP. Our flagship product, SweetPot Yoghurt, proves this concept: it naturally provides 50% of a preschooler's Vitamin A Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) per serving, reduces added sugar by 80%, and adds dietary fiber, all derived from the OFSP itself. This application of OFSP beyond traditional uses into commercially viable mass-market products is not common. Our pipeline includes crisps, flakes, and baby food, all leveraging this same core innovation. The scientific knowledge leverages the high pro-vitamin A carotenoid content and functional properties of OFSP. Immediate benefits include a market-ready, healthy and natural, low-calorie yoghurt, and increased farmer income. Sustainable benefits are a scalable model for combating micronutrient deficiencies and a growing portfolio of OFSP products that reduce food waste, strengthen local agriculture, and provide affordable nutrition.

core_fields.title: Climate-Smart Nutritious Food Additive Project (CNFA)
core_fields.description: Farm On Wheels is introducing a climate-smart, community-based innovation that converts locally grown soybeans into affordable, protein-rich food additives through women- and youth-run processing hubs. Coupled with solar irrigation, regenerative farming, 0% input financing, and digital advisory, the project improves nutrition, reduces food losses, and strengthens equitable access to safe food in rural Nigeria. This model delivers inclusive, sustainable, and scalable transformation across the food system.
core_fields.abstract: Women and youth in rural Nigeria face low agricultural productivity, poor access to nutritious foods, high post-harvest losses, and climate-induced crop failures. Despite soybeans being one of the most nutrient-dense crops available, most smallholders sell raw beans at low prices due to limited processing capacity, weak market linkages, and lack of clean energy technologies. Farm On Wheels addresses these challenges with an integrated food-system innovation that brings together climate-smart production, community processing hubs, and nutrition focused value addition. The initiative empowers women and youth cooperatives with solar-powered irrigation systems to produce soybeans year-round; regenerative agriculture training to restore soil health; and 0% input financing to increase production and resilience. At the center of the innovation is small-scale equipment for transforming soybeans into affordable, shelf-stable food additives such as soybean flour, fortified blends, and protein boosters suitable for porridges, baked foods, complementary foods, and daily meals. These products improve dietary diversity and accessibility to protein for low-income households. Digital advisory via the UBI platform and radio programs also provides continuous guidance on agronomy, nutrition, and climate-smart practices. By linking production, processing, and nutrition, this model reduces food losses by 30 - 40%, enhances incomes, strengthens local food systems, and provides safe, trusted, nutritious food at low cost to underserved communities. It is scalable, community-owned, and designed for long-term sustainability.

core_fields.title: Resilient Food Systems: Affordable Seaweed Biostimulants for Smallholder Livelihoods and Food Security
core_fields.description: This project strengthens food security and farmer livelihoods by scaling affordable, regenerative seaweed-based biostimulants to 2,500 smallholder vegetable farmers in Indonesia. Through 50 demonstration plots, farmer training, and nutrition and soil assessments, the project increases yields, improves nutrient density, reduces chemical input dependence, and raises income stability. The initiative enhances community access to nutritious food while supporting climate-resilient and sustainable production in vulnerable, low-income farming areas.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Indonesia face declining soil fertility, rising costs of fertilizers and pesticides, and more frequent climate-related crop failures. These pressures reduce yields, destabilize income, and limit access to affordable, nutritious vegetables. AquaBloom addresses this problem by transforming tropical seaweed into an affordable, high-performance biostimulant that improves plant resilience, enhances nutrient uptake, and supports soil recovery. Seaweed contains natural bioactive compounds such as cytokinins, betaines, amino acids, and trace minerals. Through a controlled extraction and formulation process, AquaBloom preserves these compounds and delivers them in an accessible, low-cost product that requires almost no change to farmer practice. The innovation has already been validated at scale. AquaBloom s biostimulants have been tested across more than 27 food crops including chili, tomato, potato, mustard greens, leafy vegetables, rice, and corn and consistently deliver 20 30% yield improvements even in adverse growing conditions. Farmers report fast visible results and a strong return on investment. This project will bring the innovation to smallholder vegetable farmers through 50 demonstration plots and direct support for 2,500 farmers. Starter inputs, practical training, and simple advisory follow-up will help farmers adopt the product effectively. Laboratory testing will measure improvements in nutrient density, while field monitoring will track yield changes, reductions in chemical inputs, and improvements in soil health and farmer income. The expected benefits are higher and more reliable yields, lower input costs, more nutritious food in local markets, and stronger, more climate-resilient livelihoods. Over time, this model offers a scalable pathway to affordable, regenerative food production.

core_fields.title: THE BANANA BYPRODUCT BLUEPRINT: A SUSTAINABLE STRATEGY FOR COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT, FOOD SECURITY, AND BIO-INNOVATION
core_fields.description: Bananas are cultivated on over 66,000 hectares of farmland in South Ethiopia, producing a nutritious byproduct that is often discarded as waste. This project initiative is converting banana waste into value-added products (healthy foods, packaging materials, herbal drinks, biofuels, and nano-fertilizers) to strengthen the economy of the community for enhanced sustainability. This innovative model also provides an immediate income increase for farmers and communities, which will maintain long-standing environmental sustainability while enhancing sustainable agricultural livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation transforms discarded banana byproducts (stems, flowers, and sheaths) from South Ethiopia s abundant farmlands into high-value-added resources: functional food, fruit & vegetable preservation/packaging materials, herbal medicines, clean fuels, and nano-fertilizers. Also, this solution directly addresses multiple challenges: food insecurity (malnutrition), limited healthcare access (e.g., kidney stones), deforestation (reliance on firewood), and declining soil fertility caused by chemical fertilizers. Banana cultivation is abundant in South Ethiopia; this project is highly relevant because the banana biomass is readily available, empowering low-income farmers, women, and youth through implementing a sustainable, zero-waste model that creates jobs and protects the environment by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The problems are solved through distinct processing routes: Banana pseudo-stems and blossoms are converted into fortified-functional foods and herbal beverages (with phytochemical insights), packaging materials to combat malnutrition, herbal remedies, and food preserving materials, respectively. Sheaths and processing wastes are converted into briquettes and fermented to bioethanol and biobutanol (under waste-to-fuel bioenergy). Residues are processed into slow-release nano-fertilizers (nano-technology) to overcome declining soil fertility. Scientific insights from food science, phytochemistry, bioenergy, and nanotechnology underpin these conversions, allowing the effective creation of beneficial, market-ready products. Immediate and lasting deliverable benefits include affordable foods, food packaging materials, medicinal beverages, fuels, and nano-fertilizers coupled with improved incomes for farmers. Sustainable benefits include empowered women/youth entrepreneurs, strengthened food/energy security, and environmental protection (reduced deforestation and emissions), creating a holistic, resilient, circular economy that feeds, heals, powers, and sustains communities.

core_fields.title: Combating food insecurity in Africa: solar-powered circular valorization of food waste into nutritious, shelf-stable foods
core_fields.description: In urban areas of Cameroon, significant quantities of consumable food are wasted, while low-income households struggle to access nutritious foods. This initiative will design and test a small GreenDry Micro-Hub utilizing solar power to safely dehydrate excess fruits and vegetables into shelf-stable, nutrient-rich components. Collaborating with women's groups and market vendors, the model aims to minimize food waste, generate affordable nutritious options, and offer a scalable circular solution for urban populations.
core_fields.abstract: In many cities across Cameroon, vast amounts of edible fruits and vegetables are discarded daily from markets, while low-income households and school canteens struggle to find affordable and nutritious foods. This concurrently fuels food insecurity, food waste, and unnecessary greenhouse gas emissions from decomposing organic waste. The GreenDry Micro-Hub is a community-operated solar drying system that converts excess and imperfect market products into safe, nutrient-rich, shelf-stable ingredients. The innovation combines three components that are seldom combined: (i) a locally made, low-temperature, indirect solar dryer; (ii) a straightforward yet standardized protocol for pre-treatment and quality control (washing, blanching, slicing, hygiene checks) aimed at maintaining vitamins, fiber, and bioactive compounds; and (iii) a cooperative business model led by women and youth that transforms rescued food into sellable powders and flakes for porridges, stews, and school meals. The design is based on evidence that mild dehydration at controlled temperatures can preserve micronutrients and polyphenols while reducing moisture to levels that prevent microbial growth. It further develops our findings that reveal significant post-harvest losses, deficiencies in micronutrients, and the absence of affordable, convenient vegetable options in urban diets. Immediate and long-term advantages include (i) healthier and year-round ingredients for households and schools; (ii) fresh income opportunities for women and youth in processing; (iii) cleaner markets and decreased organic waste for local governments; and (iv) diminished climate impact via reduced food loss and less dependency on fossil-fuel drying technologies.

core_fields.title: Transforming African Agriculture through locally producible soil & plants health & growth bio-enhancer
core_fields.description: This project scales our patented Soil & Plants Health & Growth Bio-Enhancer across East and West Africa. Utilizing established partnerships and with the ultimate goal of local production, we will demonstrate how this solution regenerates soils, boosts yields, and drastically reduces synthetic inputs. By empowering farmers with an affordable, locally-made alternative, we break dependence on costly imports and initiate a systemic shift towards productive, climate-resilient, and self-sufficient regenerative agriculture in the region.
core_fields.abstract: Conventional agriculture is trapped in a devastating cycle: agrochemicals degrade soils, reducing natural fertility and forcing increased chemical use to maintain yields. This practice damages ecosystems, creates farmer dependency, and contributes significantly to climate change. For many developing nations, this cycle is particularly crippling, as the high cost of imported agrochemicals constitutes a major drain on precious foreign currency reserves, exacerbating trade deficits and critically undermining national food sovereignty. Our innovative solution is Soil & Plants Health & Growth Bio-Enhancers, produced via our patented InnoBioTech biotechnology. The breakthrough scientific insight was replicating and accelerating the natural, centuries-long process of microbial mineral weathering. We use trained consortia of natural probiotic bacteria to dissolve locally available minerals, creating powerful liquids teeming with bioavailable nutrients, produced by the microbes, and high concentrations of potent, naturally produced bioactive metabolites like phytohormones and organic acids. The benefits are immediate and sustainable. Farmers achieve reduced agrochemical costs (by at least 20%), increased yields (by 30% or more), and enhanced crop resilience to drought and disease, enabling a profitable transition to regenerative practices. For nations and food-insecure regions, our model enables local production of these biostimulants using local mineral resources and simple facilities. This drastically reduces costly imports, improves trade balances, and builds resilient, self-sufficient food systems, freeing them from volatile global supply chains. Society and the environment gain from healthier food with lower chemical residues, restored soil biodiversity, cleaner waterways, and significant carbon sequestration in revitalized soils, directly contributing to a more sustainable and food-secure world.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Organic Inputs for Livelihoods (SOIL)
core_fields.description: SOIL aims at strengthening Kyrgyzstan s transition to safe and nutritious food through wider access to entomophages. SOIL upgrades government capacity to expand green-champion-led distribution, and catalyzes market demand for healthy, chemical-free produce. SOIL will reach 6,300 farmers (30% women) and 31,500 community members through stronger supply systems, improved production environments, and targeted awareness efforts. The ambition to expand access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food supports national priorities for organic agriculture and long-term food-system resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The legacy of the Soviet Union s large collective farms continues to influence agricultural practices in Kyrgyzstan. In the post-independence transition, thousands of former field workers became independent farmers without the agronomic knowledge once held by state specialists. They inherited depleted soils, shrinking water resources, and a heavy dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Today, chemical inputs remain the default option, leaving farmers, consumers, and the environment exposed to high levels of chemical residue while household food budgets absorb rising input costs. Produce grown under these conditions lose essential vitamins and minerals, and long-term health risks are compounded as chemicals accumulate in soil, water, and diets. In 2019, the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) created the Organic Agriculture Department (OAD) to revive the country s former bio-factories and reintroduce entomophages, e.g. Trichogramma spp., Chrysopa carnea, and Habrobracon hebetor. Although these nature-based solutions (NBS) are available, most farmers are unaware of how accessible, affordable, and safer entomophages are than chemical alternatives. Evidence shows that entomophages reduce pesticide residue substantially compared to conventional practice supporting soil and human health. SOIL strengthens OAD s production capacity, modernizes its facilities, and establishes a reliable distribution system through trained green-champions who guide farmers and make entomophages directly available to communities. As OAD s supply becomes consistent and green-champions begin serving remote areas, farmers gain access to low-cost, effective pest control options that improve crop quality and enhance household nutrition. Over time, healthier soils, reduced chemical exposure, and more nutritious food create long-lasting benefits for families and the wider food system.

core_fields.abstract: CultivaHub addresses two urgent and interconnected challenges in the Global South: widespread food waste and declining soil fertility that limits smallholder productivity. Our innovation combines CleanerBox, an AI-powered smart bin that automatically sorts and processes food waste into high-quality organic fertilizer, with GreenSeed, enhanced potato seed varieties developed to improve yield, pest resistance, and climate resilience. CleanerBox integrates machine learning and IoT sensors to identify food waste, optimize moisture and temperature for rapid composting, and ensure consistent fertilizer quality. This allows households, markets, restaurants, and institutions to transform organic waste into a valuable agricultural input rather than sending it to landfills, reducing methane emissions and strengthening circular economy practices. GreenSeed complements this by providing smallholder farmers with improved, affordable potato seeds that grow faster, withstand climate stresses, and increase harvests. Combining regenerative fertilizer and resilient seeds provides a complete, accessible solution to soil degradation and low productivity. The scientific insight behind this innovation is the synergy between circular bio-resource recovery and climate-smart seed improvement, enabling farmers to reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers, restore soil health, and improve food security. Immediate benefits include increased yields, reduced input costs, improved crop nutrition, and lower greenhouse gas emissions. Long-term benefits include sustainable soil regeneration, higher farmer incomes, reduced food waste, and stronger, more equitable food systems for rural communities.

core_fields.title: Eco Char Syngas & Biochar System for Clean Cooking and Soil Regeneration

core_fields.abstract: Eco Char addresses two critical challenges in Kenya s food and education systems: heavy dependence on firewood for school cooking and declining soil fertility among farmers. Firewood is costly, accelerates deforestation, exposes cooks and students to smoke, and strains school budgets. Meanwhile, farmers face nutrient-poor soils and unaffordable inputs, reducing yields and food security. Our innovation is a waste-to-energy kiln that converts plastic and organic waste into two valuable outputs: clean syngas for institutional cooking, and biochar for soil regeneration. The scientific insight behind this solution lies in controlled pyrolysis, where waste is heated without oxygen to release combustible gases while retaining carbon in solid biochar form. This approach drastically reduces emissions, provides a renewable fuel, and improves soils without synthetic fertilizers.

core_fields.title: Unlocking Small-scale farmer Productivity Through Affordable On-Demand Mechanisation
core_fields.description: Cradle provides small-scale farmers with affordable, on-demand mechanisation so they can farm more efficiently and increase their yields without needing to buy machines. Farmers book services through a USSD platform and we deploy compact equipment with trained operators. By improving timeliness and reducing the cost and strain of manual labour, Cradle helps farmers farm more land, produce more food and ultimately earn more.
core_fields.abstract: Cradle is a farming-as-a-service innovation that gives small-scale farmers access to modern mechanisation without the cost of owning machines. The problem we address is simple but widespread: most farmers rely on slow, expensive manual labour, which delays key farm operations, reduces yields and limits the land they can farm. With rising food demand, this gap makes food systems less reliable and keeps farmers trapped in low productivity. Our shared-economy model removes financial barriers, use od compact machinery lowers costs & risks, and our USSD Platform removes technological barriers of access, where without a smart phone or internet connectivity our services are accessible. Our solution is informed by three insights: 1. Small farms need smaller machines. Most equipment on the market is too large or too costly for their land sizes. 2. Access matters more than ownership. Farmers want reliable service, not more assets to maintain. 3. Traditional financing solutions often leave small-scale farmers in debt for machinery they cannot fully use. Immediate benefits to farmers include faster land preparation, timely planting, reduced labour costs, and the ability to cultivate more land. The shared-economy model of machines that Cradle operates helps farmers get the most value from each machine, spreading costs across multiple farms and making services more affordable. For consumers, the result is more consistent food supply and better-quality produce. Communities benefit from increased farmer incomes, creation of skilled jobs and stronger food security.

core_fields.title: Accelerating Nutrition, Trade and Employment for women and youths through Vitamin A Maize Value-Chain (ANTVAM)

core_fields.abstract: The project model merges climate-smart agriculture, renewable energy, and digital intelligence to combat malnutrition and poverty in North west, Nigeria. The innovation links Vitamin A maize production with tech, solar-powered dehydration hubs, climate-smart training, and input support to enhance productivity, ensuring steady supply of nutritious Vitamin A maize for processors and consumers with market linkage. This innovation tackles Nigeria s severe nutrition insecurity (28.7% (57.4million), and food insecurity-38.6% (77.2million), and nearly two-thirds of children risk Vitamin A deficiency (NDHS-2018). Where Kano and Kaduna State records 60% child malnutrition (UNICEF 2025) and 60% unemployment (NBS-2022), with 75% living in poverty (World Bank 2025), and over 40% postharvest-lost annually. Meanwhile, maize is Nigerian s most consumed staple food but lacks beta-carotene. Thus, empowering over 3000 MSMEs (processors/farmers) as champions to switch to Vitamin A maize, which is rich in beta-carotene. Means there is solution to reduction in malnutrition, blindness and eventually death in under 5years children due to Vitamin A deficiency (UNICEF-2021). core_fields.title: Toolkit for Decision-Making and Deployment of Bundled Solutions to Reduce Post-Harvest Loss
core_fields.description: We will develop a practical, field-tested decision-support toolkit that helps governments, donors, CSOs, cooperatives and traders choose, bundle and deploy low-cost solutions to reduce post-harvest loss in key horticulture supply chains. Built on new comparative data from integrated pilot cycles, the toolkit delivers simple go/no-go guidance, basic cost benefit logic and clear implementation steps. It provides a replicable method for designing effective, low-resource post-harvest interventions in Nepal and similar contexts.
core_fields.abstract: Post-harvest losses in Nepal persist not because solutions are unknown, but because actors lack a practical way to decide which low-cost technologies fit their specific crops, distances, seasons and market conditions. Existing FLW toolkits outline concepts and global examples, but they do not offer a usable decision-making framework for governments, CSOs, cooperatives or traders working in low-resource horticulture supply chains. Our innovation is a grounded, field-tested decision-support toolkit that translates post-harvest science into simple, actionable guidance. Using new comparative data from integrated pilot cycles across four nutrition-sensitive supply chains, the toolkit provides clear go/no-go rules, basic cost benefit logic and step-by-step implementation pathways for feasible, low-cost technologies (MAP, ethylene absorbers, improved handling and thermal protection). It enables users to choose and bundle solutions appropriate to their corridor and operating conditions, rather than relying on one-size-fits-all interventions. The insight behind this solution comes from Mandala Agrifresh s role as trader, technology provider and technical advisor the only enterprise in Nepal dedicated to reducing post-harvest loss. Across multiple corridors, we have seen technologies fail when deployed without considering physiology, distance, temperature or actor incentives. A clear, comparable decision framework can unlock far more effective programming. Benefits are immediate and lasting. Farmers and traders gain income by reducing spoilage; women, especially in remote areas, gain greater control over time and harvest decisions; consumers access more reliable, affordable nutritious produce; governments avoid misaligned investments; and reduced waste lowers emissions and the resource footprint of food. The toolkit makes practical post-harvest solutions more adoptable, scalable and equitable.

core_fields.title: Cultivating Futures: An Incubation Model to Empower Sustainable Agri-Food Enterprises for Equitable Food Futures
core_fields.description: The project incubates 20 agri-based enterprises in Madhesh and Karnali Provinces through a 24 month program featuring design sprints, monthly masterclasses and one-on-one coaching, and pre-seed funding to develop innovative and circular business models. By prioritizing women, youth, and marginalized groups, it enhances nutrition, food security, access to affordable, appealing, and trusted food. The initiative strengthens regenerative practices, builds local capacity, and generates scalable, evidence-based solutions that drive inclusive, resilient, and environmentally sustainable agri-food systems.
core_fields.abstract: In Nepal, agriculture provides livelihoods to the majority of rural households and contributes roughly a quarter to the GDP. However, limited access to affordable finance, weak technical/managerial capacity, poor product quality/standards and limited cold-chain or post-harvest technology, fragmented market linkages and regulatory/formalization barriers persist. These structural weaknesses limit scaling, reduce profitability, and increase vulnerability to shocks. Food/organic waste is the largest single component of municipal waste where food/market waste and household kitchen waste dominate. Solid-waste assessments estimate national municipal solid waste generation at roughly 1,300 1,500 tonnes per day, with per-capita household generation commonly cited around 0.30 0.36 kg/person/day. Management challenges include poor source segregation, limited collection coverage, widespread open dumping, inadequate composting or treatment facilities, and weak regulation/enforcement. Leading to nutrient loss, local pollution and methane emissions. Sectorally, households, urban markets and post-harvest losses at farm/collection points are the main contributors. Incubation addresses binding constraints for agri enterprises. Incubators provide targeted mentoring, prototyping support (e.g., small-scale drying, processing equipment), product testing, branding and access to networks and early customers, accelerating time-to-market and improving survival/scaling rates for MSMEs. An agri-based incubation aligns directly with food & nutrition security, inclusive livelihoods, climate resilience and environmental stewardship. It supports post harvesting and edible food waste through improved processing/drying/preservation, enables value addition enterprises and green jobs, diverts organics from dumps, produces compost and lowers methane emissions. Also it supports increasing women s market participation in agri-value chain through target incubation.

core_fields.title: Indigenous Pleurotus Cultivation for Sustainable Livelihoods and Ecosystem Protection
core_fields.description: This project will establish three pilot mushroom production sites around Virunga NP to cultivate indigenous Musrooms. By providing communities with an affordable, nutritious protein source, it will help reduce malnutrition, poverty, and reliance on bushmeat. The initiative will also lessen pressure on wildlife and forests by promoting sustainable livelihoods. Additionally, it will strengthen local capacity for mushroom seed production and processing, enabling the creation of diverse nutritional products such as mushroom-enriched bread and cereal flour.
core_fields.abstract: Local Communities around Virunga NP face severe poverty, malnutrition and limited access to affordable, high-quality protein sources. These challenges have increased dependence on bushmeat and unsustainable farming practices, contributing to the loss of wildlife and the degradation of Virunga NP. At the same time, large volumes of agricultural residues such as maize stalks, bean stems, rice husks and banana waste are burned, despite their potential as substrates for mushroom cultivation. Although mushroom farming is well established in many countries, it remains underdeveloped in eastern DRC, where people still rely on sporadic mushroom harvesting inside natural forest ecosystems. Our project introduces pilot production sites dedicated to domesticating, multiplying and popularizing indigenous Pleurotus species valued by local communities. Preliminary research shows that locally developed strains are well adapted to local climates and agricultural substrates, ensuring resilience, affordability and cultural acceptance. The approach is grounded in scientific studies assessing adaptability, nutritional composition and substrate efficiency of these species. By isolating, domesticating and mass-producing high-quality spawn, then training farmers and setting up pilot production units, the project enables households to transform agricultural waste into protein-rich food using simple, low-cost techniques. The initiative also integrates mushroom processing to diversify local food products, including mushroom-enriched flour and bread. In the short term, the project will improve access to nutritious protein, create additional income for farmers. In the long term, it will strengthen food sovereignty, enhance livelihood resilience and support a circular, low-carbon food system that protects Virunga NP biodiversity.

core_fields.title: Zero Waste Route
core_fields.description: We propose developing software that identifies, designs, and coordinates routes to prevent food waste in greengrocers, street markets, and marketplaces. The platform will support the recovery and redistribution of fruits and vegetables to community kitchens, soup kitchens, and shelters, strengthening community food security, reducing supply chain losses, and preventing organic waste from being sent to landfills.
core_fields.abstract: Zero Waste Route introduces a digital innovation that connects small retailers such as greengrocers, street markets, and open-air markets with community organizations providing solidarity-based food services. It addresses the significant loss of fresh fruits and vegetables within the supply chain, particularly at small-scale points of sale where tools for coordination, traceability, and food recovery logistics are largely absent. These losses undermine community food security and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions when organic waste ends up in landfills. The solution is a software platform that identifies and designs optimal routes to recover edible food, coordinating its collection and real-time redistribution to community kitchens, soup kitchens, and shelters. The platform integrates simple but strategic data (volumes, schedules, location, and demand capacity) to enable faster decision-making, reduce losses, and support efficient logistics. Its design builds on technical and operational insights from circular economy models previously implemented in street markets across the Global South. Immediate benefits include improved access to fresh food for vulnerable communities, reduced waste management costs for retailers and vendors, and substantial decreases in food waste generation. In the long term, the platform strengthens local food security networks, generates evidence to inform public policy, and reduces the environmental impact associated with organic waste mismanagement.

core_fields.title: Regenerative Agroforestry for Community-Led Food and Climate Resilience in Haiti
core_fields.description: Grown in Haiti is scaling a Haitian-led regenerative agroforestry model that restores degraded land, strengthens local food systems, and builds climate resilience in rural mountain communities. Through seed sharing, demonstration plots, farmer training, and climate monitoring, the project supports farmers in transitioning to perennial, soil-building systems that increase food availability, reduce erosion, and withstand storms. The initiative prioritizes local leadership, long-term land stewardship, and practical, low-cost solutions rooted in local knowledge.
core_fields.abstract: Haiti faces severe deforestation, soil erosion, food insecurity, and increasing climate shocks, particularly in rural mountain regions where conventional agriculture has degraded land and weakened livelihoods. Grown in Haiti addresses this challenge through a community-led regenerative agroforestry model that combines local Creole agricultural knowledge with proven regenerative and syntropic practices. The innovation lies in treating regeneration as a long-term relationship rather than a short-term intervention. Instead of distributing inputs without follow-up, Grown in Haiti works alongside farmers to design perennial, multi-strata farm systems adapted to mountainous microclimates. Demonstration plots serve as living classrooms where farmers observe soil recovery, increased food production, and storm resilience firsthand. Seed sharing, nursery expansion, and a local seed bank ensure access to climate-adapted planting material without dependency on external supply chains. Scientific and technical insights informing the model include soil biology restoration through continuous ground cover, perennial root systems for erosion control, syntropic succession planting, and the use of climate data (weather stations, GPS mapping) to guide planting and monitoring decisions. The approach is intentionally low-cost and scalable, allowing replication across Southern Haiti. Immediate benefits include improved food availability, reduced erosion, and farmer access to trees, seeds, and training. Long-term benefits include restored ecosystems, increased climate resilience, diversified farm incomes, and strengthened community capacity to steward land independently. The model contributes to healthier diets, environmental restoration, and durable food systems led by local communities.

core_fields.title: Scaling Soil Health innovations for Sustainable Agriculture across Africa.
core_fields.description: Our project improves smallholder farming by upgrading our soil test kit and integrating a mobile diagnostic app. Farmers receive instant soil health insights and fertilizer recommendations tailored to their gardens. By making soil testing more affordable, accessible and digital we can help farmers increase yield and improve soil fertility. This innovation will strengthen food security and support climate-resilient agriculture across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers across Africa often grow food without knowing the true condition of their soils. Limited access to affordable soil testing leads to poor fertilizer use, low yields due to the nutrient-depleted soils. This challenge threatens food security, farmer income, and long-term soil health. Our innovation combines an improved soil test kit with a mobile diagnostic app that will instantly interprets soil results and provide recommendations. The kit measures key soil parameters that includes pH, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and nitrogen while the app uses AI powered algorithm models to generate actionable guidance on the fertilizer type, micro-dosing and crop suitability. The solution is based on soil chemistry testing methods and incorporating digital decision-support tools. We discovered that farmers struggle less with collecting soil samples but more with interpreting results and knowing what to do next. This has led us to pair physical testing with an easy-to-use digital advisor that converts raw data into practical steps tailored to local crops and climates.

core_fields.title: BetFam-Tea Farm Record Keeping Mobile Application
core_fields.description: Betfam is a digital record-keeping app designed for tea farmers to easily track daily harvests, payments, and farm performance. It replaces manual books with accurate, secure, and easy-to-use mobile tools. Betfam helps farmers make informed decisions, reduce conflicts, access transparent records, and improve productivity. The app aims to modernize farm management and strengthen farmer incomes through reliable data. We have also incorporated Artificial Farmer Assistant to the app.
core_fields.abstract: Tea farmers often rely on handwritten notebooks to track daily harvests, payments, and farm activities. These manual records are easily lost, inaccurate, or tampered with, leading to disputes, poor planning, and limited access to financial opportunities. As farms grow and buyers demand accountability, farmers need a reliable and transparent way to manage their data. Betfam introduces a simple, mobile-based digital record-keeping system designed specifically for tea farmers. The app allows farmers to record daily kilos, payments, expenses, and production trends in real time. Data is automatically stored, calculated, and presented in easy-to-understand summaries and charts. This removes guesswork and reduces errors caused by manual entries. The innovation is driven by the insight that farmers already use smartphones for communication and mobile money but lack tools tailored to their daily farm operations. By combining basic mobile technology with structured farm data management, Betfam provides an accessible, low-cost digital solution without requiring advanced technical skills. The immediate benefits include accurate daily records, instant access to historical data, better financial transparency, and reduced conflicts between farmers and buyers. Over time, the app helps farmers identify production patterns, forecast income, manage credit responsibly, and improve decision-making. For communities and the broader agricultural sector, Betfam promotes trust, enhances traceability, and supports more efficient supply chains. Ultimately, Betfam strengthens farmer livelihoods and contributes to sustainable agricultural development through digital transformation.

core_fields.title: Future Farms
core_fields.description: We will build a 30,000-square-foot greenhouse to validate our idea of a circular economy and a net-zero greenhouse. We will use our proprietary technology of an autonomous computer vision drone, mechanical solar arrays, and an HVAC system in our greenhouse. We will focus on crops that are imported. As we grow, we will finance farmers with the same technology and bring their supply chain within our existing system.
core_fields.abstract: Bangladesh is a net food importer and has a 38% post-harvest agricultural loss. Prices fluctuate up to 300% or more during off off-season. Bangladesh is also prone to floods and cyclones that wash away farmland. We believe that unless we can secure our food supply, we may fall into a global crisis. Our objective is to reduce Bangladesh's food import requirements and to improve the country's overall food security index. We will achieve this through building vertical farms and modern greenhouses to mitigate the supply shortage and to control the price fluctuation of 300-400% by keeping a steady supply. These will provide two things: Our products will be available in the market throughout the year (especially in off-seasons), and our products will be grown without any harmful chemicals. We plan to build different farms for different products. For example, right now, we have two vertical farm setups, one for microgreens and the other for lettuce. We grow microgreens from start to finish, but for the lettuce farm, we partner with local growers who give us 2-week-old lettuce plants to grow. After this, we plan to build greenhouses to grow tomatoes, bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, chilies, etc. These greenhouses will use our proprietary MPV of our HVAC system, as well as mechanical solar arrays. In short, we want to build food-producing factories that will be climate-resilient, environmentally friendly, and efficient.

core_fields.title: Nationwide Solar-Powered Irrigation Project
core_fields.description: This project will install solar-powered irrigation systems across Ghana to help smallholder farmers produce food year-round. It includes site assessments, equipment installation, farmer training, and ongoing technical support. By replacing unreliable rain-fed farming with clean, affordable irrigation, the project boosts crop yields, strengthens climate resilience, and improves household incomes while advancing national food security and sustainable agriculture goals.
core_fields.abstract: The project introduces a nationwide deployment of solar-powered irrigation systems, an innovative, climate-smart solution that replaces rain-dependent farming with reliable, renewable water access. The core problem addressed is the limited ability of smallholder farmers to produce food year-round due to unpredictable rainfall, rising fuel costs for diesel pumps, and increasing climate variability. This results in low yields, food insecurity, and reduced incomes problems that directly threaten livelihoods and national food supply. The innovation combines solar energy, efficient water pumps, digital monitoring, and farmer training into a scalable irrigation model. The solution is informed by scientific and technical insights that demonstrate how solar technologies dramatically reduce irrigation costs, increase water-use efficiency, and enable sustainable agricultural intensification without emissions or long-term operational expenses. The system provides continuous, low-cost water for crops, allowing farmers to grow multiple seasons per year. Remote monitoring ensures system reliability, while training empowers farmers and local technicians to operate and maintain the systems independently. Immediate benefits include lower production costs, increased yields, stable water supply, and enhanced income for farmers. Schools, communities, and institutions gain access to irrigated gardens for nutrition and learning. Sustainable long-term benefits include reduced carbon emissions, resilience to drought, improved food security, strengthened rural economies, and a local ecosystem of clean-energy service providers. The environment benefits from reduced groundwater stress, elimination of diesel use, and climate-resilient farming practices. This innovation directly advances national goals for sustainable agriculture, climate adaptation, and renewable energy adoption.

core_fields.title: From Import to Local: Increasing local food resilience and nutrition improvement through jackbean tempeh development
core_fields.description: Java, Indonesia, has several regions with the lowest minimum wages nationwide, averaging about USD 125 per month. As a result, meat consumption is limited, and soybean-based tempeh has become a primary affordable protein source. With 280 million residents consuming an average of 0.3 kg of tempeh per capita and 90% of soybeans being imported, national food security is increasingly vulnerable. This program proposes a pilot initiative to develop alternative tempeh using locally sourced bean.
core_fields.abstract: Indonesia s heavy reliance on imported soybeans covering more than 90% of national demand poses a critical risk to food and nutrition security, particularly in Java where low wages restrict access to animal-based protein. Tempeh is a key affordable protein source, yet its supply chain remains vulnerable to global market fluctuations and climate shocks affecting soybean-producing countries. This innovation introduces jackbean tempeh as a scalable, climate-resilient alternative developed through a combined approach of local legume cultivation, improved fermentation technology, and community-based processing models. Jackbean (Canavalia ensiformis) is a drought-tolerant, nitrogen-fixing legume naturally suited to degraded soils across Java. Scientific studies and field trials in Aceh Province and West Java show that jackbean protein composition and fermentation behavior are compatible with Rhizopus oligosporus, enabling high-quality tempeh with comparable texture and nutritional value to soybean tempeh. The solution integrates two innovations: 1. Agro-ecological crop diversification using jackbean intercropping to regenerate soil and reduce fertilizer dependence. Introducing Climate Smart cultivation. 2. A decentralized micro-processing model enabling small producers, women, and youth to produce jackbean tempeh using low-cost equipment. Creating sustainable consumption when production and consumption happened in one region. Immediate benefits include increased farmer income, reduced dependency on import commodity, and affordable protein access for low-wage households. Long-term benefits include soil restoration, lower carbon emissions from food transport, and stronger local food sovereignty. By linking farmers, schools, micro-entrepreneurs, and communities, the project creates a sustainable, locally managed food system that strengthens both nutrition and resilience across Java.

core_fields.title: Development of Guava leaf based edible coating as a natural preservative for agricultural produce
core_fields.description: Guava leaves water extracts have natural bioactive compounds which could potentially be used to formulate an edible coating to increase shelf life of the agricultural produce. The aim of this plant based formulation is to reduce the use of chemical preservatives and make people, community and related authorities aware and motivate them towards green and sustainable technology of food preservation. Ultimately, consumers will get nutritious food creating less food waste and ultimately less carbon footprint.
core_fields.abstract: Post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables in Nepal are estimated at 20-50%, posing a significant threat to livelihoods of farmers who depend primarily on agriculture. These losses primarily occur during transportation due to physical damage, limited access to cold storage conditions, and microbial spoilage that shortens shelf life of post harvest produce. To mitigate this loss, farmers rely on chemical preservatives and pesticides; however the lack of regulatory oversight and improper use of these substances poses serious risks to human health and environment. To address post-harvest losses in agricultural produce, our project aims to develop an edible coating derived from guava leaves which are widely available across Nepal and a renewable resource of raw material, regenerating naturally in each growing season. The potential of guava leaf water extract has been demonstrated in terms of phenolic and flavonoid content, antioxidant capacity, toxicity levels, and antimicrobial activity from our first phase of the project (Majhi et. al, 2023). The guava leaves based coating solution will be applied to post-harvested produce through spraying or dipping, which could extend shelf life by minimizing weight loss, preserving firmness, and enhancing resistance to spoilage causing microorganisms. This locally developed solution empowers farmers to increase the long-term availability of fresh food and presents an energy-efficient solution for post-harvest management for farmers, distributors and local vendors, eventually minimizing their economic burden. In turn, it supports broader access to safe, nutritious, eco- friendly alternatives contributing to national and global food security goals and better public health.

Sustainable benefits arise from youth entrepreneurship, creating jobs, reinvesting revenue to maintain services, and strengthening local food systems. Communities gain resilience to climate shocks, equitable access to trusted advisory services, and environmental benefits through regenerative practices that keep food systems within planetary boundaries.

core_fields.title: Democratizing Carbon Finance Through AI-Powered Verification for East African Smallholder Farmers
core_fields.description: AgriKonnekt reduces carbon verification costs 70% through AI, IoT, and satellite technology, making the $45 billion global carbon market accessible to African smallholder farmers for the first time. Our 12-month pilot with 1,500 Kenyan farmers generated 38% income increases, sequestered 18,000 tons CO2, achieving 88% retention. The Grant will expand to 3,000 farmers, validate commercial sustainability, and strengthen cooperative partnerships, proving smallholder carbon finance advances EA's climate mitigation, food security, gender equality, and economic equity.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Traditional carbon verification costs $50-100 per farmer, exceeding potential credit values for smallholder operations. Less than 10% of African farmers access carbon markets despite enormous sequestration potential (12 tons CO2 annually per farm). This market failure leaves 10 million East African farmers unable to monetize environmental benefits while facing climate vulnerability, income volatility, and adaptation resource constraints threatening food security for 600 million people. Solution: Our hybrid verification system combines IoT soil carbon sensors at cooperative level, satellite imagery validating land use, and AI algorithms processing data, reducing costs to $15 per farmer (70% reduction) while maintaining 95% accuracy. Cooperative distribution achieves $52 customer acquisition cost versus industry $200+, creating network effects and economies of scale. Mobile platforms function on basic phones offline in local languages, removing digital barriers. Direct mobile money payments, particularly benefiting women (52% of users), enable financial autonomy. Premium marketplace positioning ($5-7 per ton versus commodity $3) ensures farmers capture fair value. Scientific Insight: Regenerative agriculture practices (cover cropping, reduced tillage, organic amendments, agroforestry, crop diversification) sequester carbon while improving soil health, water retention, and productivity, not tradeoffs but synergies between climate mitigation and food security. Benefits: Farmers gain supplementary income ($380 annually), climate adaptation resources, improved productivity, and financial inclusion. Communities strengthen cooperative capacity and youth employment (25 positions created). Environment gains 36,000 tons CO2 sequestration from 6,000 hectares regenerative management. Markets gain verified, high-integrity African smallholder offsets. Society demonstrates inclusive climate finance where vulnerable communities become solution actors, advancing equity alongside environmental integrity.

core_fields.title: Feeding Tomorrow: Scaling Women-Led Solutions to Fight Baby Malnutrition with Climate-Resilient Indigenous Crops
core_fields.description: This project tackles severe baby malnutrition in Togo s Savannah region, where desertification and chronic food insecurity threaten infant health. With the Seed Grant, we piloted a women-led, climate-smart model in 10 villages boosting yields, reducing post-harvest losses, and introducing affordable baby formulas made from indigenous crops. This Growth Grant will extend these proven results across the wider region by scaling female farmer training, expanding indigenous crop processing, and improving nutrition for thousands of babies.
core_fields.abstract: A few years ago, our co-founder Ida did not have enough breastmilk for her baby. Like millions of African mothers, she could not afford milk-based formulas. The root cause is that female smallholder farmers are struggling with increased soil aridity and decreasing yields, yet their crops are exported abroad, incorporated into milk-based formulas, and imported back into our communities at prices too high for the very mothers who farmed these crops in the first place. Ida overcame her problem by mixing local vegetables to feed her baby, who grew healthy and strong. Eager to share her experience with other mothers, she created Baobaby. Our innovation consists of sourcing drought-resistant indigenous crops from female farmers and transforming them into nutritious alt-protein formulas that are distributed back into local communities. Scientifically, these indigenous crops are adapted to arid climates, nutrient-dense, and well suited for baby nutrition. Technically, decentralized solar-powered processing preserves nutrients and improves food safety. The Seed Grant enabled us to implement this model in 10 villages in the Savannah region of Togo by training 150 women in climate-resilient agriculture, reducing post-harvest losses by 50% through solar drying units, and providing low-cost formulas to over 7,000 babies. However, as the dry season now stretches up to seven months with little to no rain, these rain-fed farmers urgently need solar-powered borehole irrigation systems to sustain their livelihoods. This project aims to expand these results to 50 villages, train an additional 500 women, and equip them with solar drying units and irrigation systems.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Smart Crop Monitoring and Loss-Reduction System for Smallholder Farmers
core_fields.description: This project deploys Scaregrow, a solar-powered, sensor-driven smart farming device that helps smallholder farmers reduce crop losses caused by pests, diseases, and harsh weather. Scaregrow provides real-time monitoring, automated alerts, and AI-based agronomy insights through a mobile app, enabling farmers to make timely decisions. The initiative strengthens food security, improves yields and enhances climate resilience for vulnerable smallholders in Nigeria.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Nigeria experience significant crop losses due to pests, diseases, and unpredictable weather conditions. These losses can reach 30 50 percent of total yield, reducing food availability, income, and resilience. Many farmers lack access to timely information, early warnings, and affordable technologies that could help them respond to emerging threats before damage occurs. This makes food systems more fragile, especially under increasing climate pressure. Scaregrow addresses this challenge through a solar-powered, sensor-driven smart farming device that provides real-time environmental monitoring and automated risk alerts. By integrating IoT sensors with a mobile application, Scaregrow continuously measures key conditions around the farm, detects early signs of pest or disease presence, and sends actionable notifications directly to farmers phones. The device also connects to an AI-powered advisory system that offers agronomy guidance and pest or disease identification support, enabling farmers to make faster, data-driven decisions. The scientific insight behind this solution lies in combining low-cost sensing technology, renewable energy, and AI-assisted agronomy to create an accessible tool tailored to smallholder realities. Instead of relying on guesswork or delayed interventions, farmers gain immediate, accurate, and locally relevant insights. Immediate benefits include reduced crop losses, improved timing of interventions, and lower dependence on chemical treatments. Over time, Scaregrow promotes healthier ecosystems, increases yields, stabilizes household income, and enhances overall climate resilience. At scale, this innovation contributes to safer food, stronger rural economies, and more sustainable agricultural practices across vulnerable communities.

core_fields.title: Low-Carbon Blue Foods
core_fields.description: This project develops a new way to turn regenerative mussel biomass into safe, nutritious and affordable foods that support healthy diets while staying within planetary boundaries. By upcycling underused aquatic protein through low-energy processing, we aim to create appealing, culturally adaptable products that reduce waste, improve nutrient intake and expand access to high-quality protein for communities with limited food options. The project advances climate-positive, equitable and resilient blue food innovation.
core_fields.abstract: Many communities in the Global South face a dual challenge: limited access to affordable, nutrient-dense protein and food systems increasingly constrained by climate stress, land scarcity and rising costs of feed, fertiliser and freshwater. Mussels offer a uniquely powerful but underutilised solution. They are one of the world s most nutrient-rich and climate-positive proteins high in B12, iron, omega-3s and complete protein yet require none of the costly inputs that limit livestock and crop production. Our innovation develops a low-energy, scalable method to transform underused mussel biomass into shelf-stable, easy-to-distribute food formats suited for diverse contexts. These include nutritious biscuits, fortified flours, protein powders, seasoning mixes and dry meal bases that can be incorporated into local cooking traditions. Dry formats extend shelf life, reduce transport costs, and eliminate the need for refrigeration making them ideal for schools, community feeding programmes, humanitarian settings and households with unstable electricity. This solution builds on scientific insights into mussels exceptional nutrient density and on technical advances in milling, dehydration and protein fortification. It offers a practical way to reduce waste by upcycling mussel biomass that is often discarded or undervalued due to size or market limitations. The benefits are immediate and far-reaching: 1) Nutrition: provides accessible, bioavailable protein and critical micronutrients for children, pregnant women and low-income families. 2)Sustainability: supports regenerative aquaculture, reduces food waste and operates well within planetary boundaries. 3) Equity: delivers affordable, culturally adaptable foods that strengthen food security in communities most vulnerable to climate impacts.

core_fields.title: AI-Driven Biosurveillance to Anticipate Animal Diseases and Protect Global Food Security
core_fields.description: We developed a patented air-sampling device and a proprietary AI biosurveillance platform that together monitor, on a quarterly basis, over five million animals across multiple production cycles. This project aims to develop new predictive algorithms and disease-risk models for major poultry and swine pathogens. By enabling earlier detection and prevention, we will reduce losses, improve animal health, and strengthen the resilience and safety of global food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Animal diseases cause massive losses in global food systems, threaten farmer livelihoods, increase antibiotic dependence, and create pandemic risks. Most outbreaks are detected too late because current surveillance relies on clinical signs or limited diagnostic sampling. This delay results in preventable mortality, production losses, higher costs, and reduced food security. Our innovation is a patented air-sampling device combined with a proprietary AI biosurveillance platform that detects airborne pathogens before animals show symptoms. This approach generates the earliest possible signal of sanitary risk. The technology is already used to monitor, on a quarterly basis, over five million poultry and swine across multiple production cycles in Latin America and Asia. The insight behind the solution came from understanding that pathogens circulate in the air days to weeks before outbreaks become visible, and that this environmental pressure of infection can be quantified and modeled. By integrating molecular diagnostics, environmental microbiology, and machine-learning algorithms, we can detect silent pathogen circulation, predict risk trends, and guide early interventions. Immediate benefits include earlier detection of major diseases, reduced antibiotic use, lower mortality, better animal welfare, and higher productivity for farmers. Sustainable benefits include improved food system resilience, reduced economic vulnerability for producers, enhanced One Health protection, and lower pandemic risk for society. For low-resource regions, early warnings help protect food availability and farmer income. By shifting disease management from reactive to predictive, this innovation provides a scalable model for safer, more reliable, and more sustainable animal protein production worldwide.

core_fields.title: CARE-Maputo Project: Climate-Adapted Agriculture & Resilient Food Systems in APA-Maputo
core_fields.description: CARE Maputo Project strengthens food security in the Maputo Environmental Protection Area by establishing wildlife-safe community farming supported by solar irrigation and low-cost cold storage for fresh produce. Led by AMOR in partnership with APA-Maputo, the project stabilizes year-round access to nutritious food, reduces post-harvest losses, and diversifies household income through circular-economy incentives (Blue Coins). This proven, scalable model improves livelihoods, protects biodiversity, and builds climate-resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: CARE Maputo Project addresses chronic food insecurity in the Maputo Environmental Protection Area, where climate stress, human wildlife conflict, and weak post-harvest systems undermine local food availability and household livelihoods. In many communities, crops are repeatedly destroyed by wildlife, while fresh produce spoils within days due to the absence of basic storage and irrigation infrastructure. These challenges reduce access to nutritious food and increase vulnerability to unstable markets. The innovation integrates four proven components into a single, low-risk, conservation-compatible food system. First, wildlife-safe community farming is established outside ecological corridors mapped by APA-Maputo and protected through fencing and ecological deterrents, ensuring reliable production of vegetables and fresh foods. Second, solar-powered irrigation systems using pumps, water storage, and drip irrigation enable year-round cultivation, improve yields, and reduce dependence on rainfall and fossil fuels. Third, low-cost solar-powered cold storage for fresh produce located at the community farm allows vegetables to be safely stored for up to five to six days, reducing post-harvest losses, preserving nutritional value, and strengthening farmers bargaining power in local markets. Fourth, circular-economy income through Blue Coins provides complementary household revenue linked to waste collection, stabilizing food access while reinforcing environmental stewardship. The solution draws on applied knowledge from regenerative agriculture, renewable-energy engineering, human wildlife conflict mitigation, and circular-economy systems. All components rely on commercially available technologies and governance models already implemented by AMOR, making integration operationally low-risk and scalable. Immediate benefits include improved food availability, reduced losses, safer diets, and more stable household income for women, youth, and vulnerable households.

core_fields.title: Improving Vegetable Production Resilience through Innovative and Accessible Plant Virus Detection and Disease Mitigation
core_fields.description: Vegetable viruses severely threaten vegetable production; the threat is disproportionately greater in developing regions due to limited access to reliable diagnostic tools. The project will deliver customized multiplex recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) assay integrated into the lab-on-foil platform for rapid, point-of-care detection of major vegetable viruses in the developing world. Integrated with the updated VeggieMon; vegetable disease monitoring platform, results will guide farmers in adopting improved practices for sustainable viral disease management in vegetable crops.
core_fields.abstract: Expanding host ranges and geographic spread, intensified by climate change, are placing global vegetable crops at heightened risk of viral diseases. Effective management depends on timely, accurate detection, yet current diagnostic tools are often target-specific, resource- intensive, and inaccessible to many laboratories. This project addresses these gaps by developing multiplex RPA assays integrated into a lab- on-a-foil platform as a point-of-care diagnostic system for resource-limited settings, and by establishing a centralized, state-of-the-art virus genotyping facility at WorldVeg headquarters for robust strain-level monitoring of vegetable virus evolution worldwide. The new RPA tool will allow farmers, extension agents, and researchers to easily and simultaneously detect multiple viruses affecting tomato, pepper, cucurbits, and okra under field conditions. The system will be optimized for affordability, simplicity, and effective field use where laboratory resources are limited. This innovation will link with the VeggieMon disease database to deliver region-specific management recommendations by combining real-time RPA-based field diagnostics with strain-level genotyping of viral samples collected on FTA cards (safely preserve viral DNA and RNA without deterioration, pose no biosecurity risks, and allow hurdle-free global transportation compared with plant samples). A new VeggieMon mobile app will support tracking of FTA cards through QR codes, geotagged images, and AI-assisted validation. This integrated system will strengthen surveillance, improve diagnostic accuracy, and expand global capacity to monitor and manage emerging vegetable virus threats. Hands-on training and RPA support will build sustainable diagnostic skills, while VeggieMon provides actionable, diagnosis-based recommendations to farmers, reducing production risks and enhancing food and nutritional security.
