core_fields.title: Scaling Accessible Bio-fortified, Certified Beans Seed Among Smallholder Farmers in Kalumbila District.
core_fields.description: This project seeks to expand access to certified, nutritious, Zinc and Iron-biofortified Lui bean seed among smallholder farmers in Kalumbila Meheba Settlement. By contracting and training 200 farmers, (55%) women and (30%) youth as seed growers, the initiative aims to strengthen productivity, improve household nutrition, and promote adoption of good agricultural practices. Kagezi Seed Limited will offer market linkage, the project supports sustainable livelihoods and fosters long-term economic integration in this transitioning community.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation introduces a structured, community-based certified seed production model that empowers smallholder farmers, especially women and youth, to produce and access nutrient-dense, Zinc and Iron-biofortified Lui bean seed. This directly addresses a longstanding challenge: over 85% of Zambia's seed demand is supplied through the informal sector, where recycled and low-quality seed limits yields, nutrition, and resilience. For crops like beans, less than 5% of planted areas are supported by the formal seed systems in Zambia. In Kalumbila Meheba Settlement, farmers face limited access to certified seed, contributing to low productivity, poor nutrition outcomes, and slow adoption of good agricultural practices. The solution trains and contracts 200 smallholder farmers as certified seed growers, supported through farmer selection, seed production training with SCCI, procurement of essential machinery, ongoing mentorship, and guaranteed off-take by Kagezi Seed Limited. This approach is guided by agricultural research showing that biofortified beans significantly improve household nutrition while offering higher productivity under smallholder conditions. It also builds on the proven effectiveness of decentralized seed systems in improving last-mile access to quality seed. Immediate benefits include increased availability of certified, biofortified bean seed, higher yields, better nutrition for households, and improved income opportunities for participating farmers. Over time, the project strengthens local seed systems, promotes gender inclusion, enhances climate resilience through high-performing varieties, and reduces dependency on humanitarian support as Meheba transitions to a permanent settlement.

core_fields.title: Sustainable and regenerative strategies for safe, nutritious, and waste-free food systems
core_fields.description: The project will use the Kentegra Village Savings and Loans -KVSLA Agri-SMART Training Curriculum, covering 15 topics to train 850 farmers organized in 34 KVSLA groups. Farmers will gain skills in sustainable regenerative agriculture, syntropic agroforestry through provision of trees and fruit seedlings,organic fertilizer and post-harvest management. The project will supply 34 KVSLA groups with quality solar dryers to preserve pyrethrum and other foods, improving diets, increasing sustainable incomes, and strengthening long-term resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Synthetic pesticides increasingly face regulatory bans, resistance, and environmental concerns, yet existing botanical alternatives often suffer from poor quality consistency and unreliable supply. At the same time, smallholder farmers lack access to improved planting materials, technical knowledge, and secure markets. These challenges threaten food security, public health, and environmental sustainability. Kentegra is engaged in a farmer-centered pyrethrum biotechnology model that delivers safe, effective, and environmentally sustainable insect control solutions while improving smallholder farmer livelihoods. The innovation addresses three interconnected challenges: the over-reliance on synthetic insecticides, inconsistent supply of natural pest-control alternatives, and low, unstable rural incomes. Kentegra s solution is an integrated pyrethrum value-chain approach that links improved plant genetics, sustainable agronomy, standardized extraction, and global market access. High-pyrethrin planting material and farmer training increase yields and quality, while contract farming provides predictable income and reduces market risk. Centralized processing and rigorous quality control ensure consistent, compliant natural insecticide ingredients suitable for agricultural, household, and public-health use. The innovation is grounded in scientific insight that pyrethrum efficacy depends on quality and consistency rather than scale alone, and that biological actives must meet pharmaceutical-level standards to be commercially viable. By aligning farmer inclusion with market requirements, the model creates a resilient and scalable supply system. Immediate benefits include higher farmer incomes, safer pest-control products for consumers, and reliable inputs for manufacturers. Long-term impacts include reduced chemical pesticide use, protection of biodiversity and pollinators, strengthened rural economies, and climate-resilient agricultural systems aligned with sustainable development goals.

core_fields.title: Building safe and climate-resilient aquatic food systems in Zanzibar with Solar-powered Seaweed Drying Hubs.
core_fields.description: In Zanzibar, climate change poses major challenges to small-scale seaweed farmers. As many rely on traditional seaweed drying techniques, climate change exacerbates post-harvest seaweed spoilage, threatening farmers' livelihoods. Our project will establish two solar-powered seaweed drying hubs, each processing up to 2 tonnes per day and serving 200 farmers in Unguja Island. The hubs will reduce post-harvest losses of seaweed, improve product quality and safety, and boost the supply and income of seaweed farmers.
core_fields.abstract: The solar-powered seaweed drying technology developed by MAVUNOLAB has been tested and deployed in Zanzibar, demonstrating great potential in reducing post-harvest seaweed losses. Unlike sun drying, which is used by the majority of seaweed farmers in Zanzibar, MAVUNOLAB s solar drying technology enhances the quality of dried seaweed because harvested seaweed is placed inside drying racks, protecting it from dust, sand, and other potential damages and contaminants. Our hybrid solar-powered food driers are available in two sizes: a 200 kg drier and a 2-tonne greenhouse-style solar drier, enabling off-grid seaweed farmers to process and dry their seaweed throughout the day. In June 2025, MAVUNOLAB, in collaboration with the Zanzibar Ministry of Blue Economy, established its first solar-powered seaweed drying hub in Muungoni village, southwest Unguja, Zanzibar. The installed solar-powered seaweed drying facility has reduced seaweed drying time from 3 days when sun-dried to less than 10 hours, serving up to 70 seaweed farmers per month. This development has improved post-harvest management of huge volumes of harvested seaweed that would have been wasted, saving the livelihoods of more than 100 seaweed farmers. Today, MAVUNOLAB has received interest from seaweed farmers, local and international seaweed companies in need of our solar-powered seaweed drying technology. To meet the growing demand, our team is seeking $100,000 to establish two additional hybrid solar-powered seaweed drying hubs in two seaweed farming communities in Zanzibar, which is Africa s largest producer of seaweed. core_fields.title: Nourish Malawi: Local Ingredients, Global Impact
core_fields.description: The Moving Windmills Innovation Center in Kasungu, Malawi empowers smallholder farmers and youth to transform local crops into nutritious, market-ready foods. Building on our successful soy processing pilots, we are expanding into peanut-based value addition to combat malnutrition and create livelihoods. Through climate-smart demonstration plots, hands-on training, and local production, the project strengthens food security, promotes sustainable agriculture, and scales community-led innovation from Malawi to the world.
core_fields.abstract: In Malawi, according to the 2023 Malawi Demographic and Health Surveynearly 40% of children under five suffer from chronic malnutrition, while an analysis in 2024 revealed that smallholder farmers are increasingly vulnerable to climate change. Specifically, 92% of respondents reported reductions in household income, 33% of respondents reported declining crop yields, and 10% experienced food shortages. The Moving Windmills Innovation Center tackles this dual challenge by combining sustainable agriculture with local food processing to create nutritious, income-generating products. Our innovation focuses on value addition, turning locally grown soybeans and peanuts into high-protein, shelf-stable foods similar to Plumpy Nut, which can address childhood malnutrition while creating a new rural industry. Using simple, low-cost, and solar-powered equipment, farmers are trained to process, package, and sell these fortified foods directly from the Innovation Center. This approach reduces post-harvest losses, increases farmer income, and ensures nutritious foods remain affordable and accessible within communities. The technical insight comes from our fieldwork and collaborations with agricultural experts and nutritionists: both soy and peanuts thrive in Malawi s semi-arid climate, require minimal inputs, and provide complete plant-based protein. By integrating training, demonstration plots, and food processing under one roof, we re building a circular, community-led food system that feeds both people and local economies. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition, job creation (particularly for women and youth), and income diversification. Long-term, the project strengthens resilience to climate shocks, supports sustainable farming practices, and builds local expertise in food innovation.

core_fields.title: Scaling SIRDC Upland Rice: Farmer-Led Systems for Nutrition, Equity & Climate Resilience
core_fields.description: Zimbabwe imports 70% of its rice due to shortages of resilient early-generation seed. This project scales farmer-led systems to multiply upland rice varieties released by SIRDC, ensuring affordable access for smallholders. Fifty Village-Based Advisors with extension staff will bulk foundation seed across irrigation plots, while digital extension, postharvest technologies, and regenerative practices boost yields 20 30%, cut losses 25%, lower emissions, and reduce import dependency, transforming upland rice into a food security pillar.
core_fields.abstract: Zimbabwe imports 70% of its rice because growers lack access to affordable, superior-quality early-generation seed (EGS). Even with irrigation potential, productivity remains low due to shortages of resilient seed adapted to drought and heat stress. This innovation breaks the seed bottleneck by scaling farmer-led seed systems to multiply unique upland rice varieties developed and released by SIRDC, ensuring availability, accessibility, and affordability for smallholders. The model integrates four proven components: Farmer-led seed multiplication: Fifty Village-Based Advisors bulk foundation seed across 50 irrigation demonstration plots, guaranteeing 90% purity and germination of SIRDC s upland rice lines. Digital extension: A mobile platform delivers agronomic advisories, pest alerts, and market information to phone-owning farmers, ensuring women and youth inclusion. Postharvest technologies: Village Business Units provide hermetic bags for zero-loss storage and portable huskers that halve labor while reducing aflatoxin contamination risk. Regenerative practices: System of Rice Intensification, conservation agriculture, integrated pest management, and ratoon cropping cut methane emissions by 20%, chemical inputs by 30%, and postharvest waste by 25%. Scientific insight: Combining SIRDC s upland rice genetics with climate-smart agronomy delivers resilience to drought and heat stress while lowering emissions. Immediate benefits: Higher yields, reduced losses, safer grain, lower import dependence. Sustainable benefits: Stronger food security, inclusive market participation, healthier communities, and environmental gains for society at large. Aligned with Zimbabwe s AFSRTS 2 (2026 30), this innovation transforms SIRDC s upland rice into a domestic food security pillar while advancing Seeding The Future s three domains: nutritious food, sustainable production, equitable access.

core_fields.title: Enabling flood-resistant pollination services for food security in extreme weather-affected regions
core_fields.description: Climate-driven flood events destroy millions of beehives each year, destabilizing pollination and threatening global food production. Our project is the deployment of our buoyant beehive system to protect communities most at risk. In particular, the funding of this Award will be used for deployment and research output in the tropical (Terai) region of Nepal, which continues to face recurrent flooding that destroys beehives, disrupts pollination, and undermines regional food production.
core_fields.abstract: Extreme weather events are accelerating worldwide, destroying millions of beehives per year and effectively crippling the 76% of food production reliant on pollination. Traditional wooden hives sink, rot, and fail under rising water levels, leading to food production losses and financial shocks for the agricultural sector. Current hives that survive flooding are further exposed to colony collapse, as well as Chalkbrood, Stronebrood, American Fouldbrood, and European Fouldbrood. Most apiculture happens near agriculture, and most agriculture happens near open bodies of water, most of which are facing nuisance flooding rates 300 to 900 percent higher than 50 years ago. In Nepal, this threatens beekeeping viability and the pollination services of the crop cultivated in monsoon and winter seasons. Our innovation is a patent-pending buoyant beehive system that automatically floats during floods, integrates with standard Langstroth beehives, returns to the ground as waters recede, and protects colonies without human intervention. It is made from recycled HDPE (a common plastic found in ocean garbage), withstands strong water currents, and even enables pollination in regions previously considered too risky for beekeeping. These regions include floodplains, riverbeds, marshlands, and mangroves. With our solution, farmers and beekeepers maintain crop yield and avoid hive losses entirely. Ecosystems retain pollinator services essential for biodiversity and post-flood rehabilitation. Consumers and rural communities benefit from a more stable food supply, as well as more predictable food prices. Regional food security is improved, and agricultural incomes are shielded from flood losses. Our solution works across geographies without any design changes needed.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered IoT Smart Irrigation Monitoring and Controlling system for Climate Resilience in Off-Grid Ethiopia
core_fields.description: ZTN Technology deploys a "Farm-in-a-Box" automation ecosystem designed for infrastructure-poor regions. Our solar-powered, off-grid IoT system automates irrigation to reduce water waste by 50%. Crucially, our AI Intelligence Layer analyzes historical soil data to predict optimal future crop types and precise water requirements before planting. We empower smallholder farmers to transition from subsistence farming to high-yield commercial production, ensuring food security despite climate shocks.
core_fields.abstract: Ethiopian agriculture faces a dual crisis: acute water scarcity and a lack of grid infrastructure prevent farmers from optimizing irrigation, leading to 50% water wastage and frequent crop failure. ZTN solves this with a proprietary, infrastructure-independent ecosystem integrating three layers: Hardware Layer: We deploy rugged, solar-powered sensors that measure soil moisture and NPK in real-time. These communicate via a proprietary LoRaWAN gateway (10km range) that automates water valves without needing the internet or grid electricity. Intelligence Layer (The Brain - AI Analysis): This is our core innovation. Our cloud platform aggregates historical soil and environmental data. We utilize AI and Machine Learning algorithms to analyze this longitudinal data, providing farmers with predictive insights. The system calculates exactly how many liters of water a crop uses and analyzes soil trends to recommend the optimal future crop types that match the specific soil chemistry and predicted climate patterns, maximizing yield potential before planting even begins. Benefits: Farmers: Achieves ~30% yield increase and eliminates fuel costs by optimizing solar pump usage. Environment: Proven 48% reduction in water withdrawal, protecting groundwater. Society: Transforms vulnerable pastoralist communities (like in Afar) into resilient food producers, securing local food supply chains against drought. (215 words)

Surplus produce is sold to nearby markets and restaurants, creating a cross-subsidy that helps keep food affordable for households. core_fields.title: Project Green
core_fields.description: Nasaru Naturals is aiming to be the first in the world to grow spirulina, a nutrient-rich superfood, at scale in its natural environment in Kenya's Rift Valley. Our innovative, low-footprint, modular spirulina farm design is built to scale quickly and has positive impacts on the environment, food security, and the local economy. Project Green is our pilot facility at Lake Natron, set to prove in the wild that open-air spirulina farming is commercially viable.
core_fields.abstract: Nasaru Naturals is addressing three challenges that disproportionately affect the Rift Valley: climate change, poverty and lack of economic opportunity, and malnourishment. Climate Resilience: Though Africa contributes just 4% of global carbon emissions, it is the region most vulnerable to climate change. With diminishing arable land and freshwater access, traditional farming practices are not sustainable. Spirulina naturally sequesters carbon and can be cultivated with minimal, low-impact resources. Importantly, it does not compete with traditional agriculture, requiring neither arable land nor freshwater. It thrives in intense sun and dry conditions, turning a climate challenge into an opportunity. Poverty / Economic opportunity: Rural communities in Africa face poverty rates 3x their urban counterparts a disparity exacerbated by the decline of agriculture due to climate stress. With spirulina farming, Nasaru Naturals aims to build a new, sustainable industry in the region. This model not only creates immediate employment opportunities but will easily and quickly scale, multiplying impact. Malnourishment: Food insecurity affects 58% of Africa, with 20% undernourished. As staple crops become harder to grow and livestock less productive, there is an urgent demand for affordable, nutrient-dense food. Spirulina is rich in essential nutrients and cheap to cultivate and harvest, making it an ideal solution for communities facing nutritional deficits. Climate change, poverty, and malnourishment are deeply intertwined, and their effects are intensifying. Nasaru Naturals's spirulina model presents a triple-impact solution: it leverages the harsh climate instead of fighting it, builds a new economic pathway for rural communities, and delivers a nutritious, accessible food source.

core_fields.title: Underutilized Climate Smart Legumes to Enhance Dietary Diversity and Resilient Farming Systems in Southwestern Uganda
core_fields.description: The project aims at improving legume dietary diversity and nutrition (especially addressing protein and micronutrient deficiencies) and build climate resilience in southwestern Uganda, through scaling of underutilized Climate Smart legumes mainly chickpeas and pigeon peas to supplement common beans. The project seeks to exploit the available genetic diversity sourced from ICARDA and ICRISAT genebanks to create a self-sustaining food system through working with community seedbanks, community-based seed producers, processors and health centers.
core_fields.abstract: Unlike other regions that cultivate a diverse range of legumes, including groundnuts, pigeon peas and cowpeas, the southwestern region faces a unique challenge of heavily relying on only common beans (Phaseolus vulgaris), limiting dietary diversity. Yet farm households frequently sell beans for income, leading to a food security tradeoff. This imbalance disproportionately affects women and children, particularly of reproductive age, resulting in low protein intake and alarmingly high malnutrition rates. According to the Uganda Demographic and Health Survey (2018), southwestern and western districts have consistently recorded the highest prevalence of childhood malnutrition (29.3%), particularly stunting among children under five, largely attributed to low dietary diversity. In these regions, beans are often supplemented with carbohydrate-based foods such as potatoes, sorghum, and millet porridges, offering limited nutritional benefits. To enhance household nutrition and build climate resilience, it is crucial to introduce underutilized climate smart legumes, like chickpeas and short-duration pigeon pea varieties like SEPI 2 to supplement common beans. Both chickpea and pigeon pea are nutrient-rich (protein, essential minerals (iron, zinc, calcium, phosphorus), and fiber, helping to combat malnutrition). Chickpea is valued for its drought tolerance, since it is mainly grown as a post-rainy, dry-season crop, making it a "bonus crop" that does not compete with major rainy season legumes like common beans, In terms of economic benefits, both crops have high demand in domestic and export markets, which can significantly improve household incomes. As nitrogen-fixing legumes, they can improve soil fertility, especially when intercropped with other crops like cereals and banans.

core_fields.title: Farm-to-Market Traceability Platform: Enhancing Food Safety, Farmer Livelihoods, and Sustainable Agriculture in Malawi.
core_fields.description: This project enhances agricultural traceability in Malawi by integrating QR-coded bag tagging into existing rural warehouse technology and the Zaulimi App, enabling crop tracking from farm to market. Targeting 10,000 smallholder farmers across participating FOs, the initiative automates warehouse operations, improves data accuracy, and connects farmers to premium markets demanding traceable products. Through digital literacy training, climate-smart content, and lead farmer networks, we build sustainable capacity while boosting revenues and nutrition through new agricultural practices.
core_fields.abstract: ACE Trust seeks to introduce an integrated digital platform combining expanded agricultural training with crop traceability and live warehouse monitoring, accessible through a single app - Zaulimi. Farmers in Malawi indeed face three main challenges: limited access to up-to-date farming techniques for different crops; inability to prove crop quality and origin to buyers demanding traceability; high stock monitoring costs due to the necessity of physical monitoring. These issues are currently addressed through disconnected systems, creating inefficiencies and limiting opportunities for increased income. We're thus integrating two proven technologies - the Zaulimi App and our rural surveillance system. The platform will offer expanded training modules including additional crops (beans, sunflowers, and other crops requested by users) with climate-smart techniques. For the rural tech system, warehouse cameras and sensors currently monitoring storage conditions at rural warehouses will be upgraded with a traceability component, tracking crops throughout the value chain from farm to market. Tags with QR codes will be added to commodity bags, enabling anyone with a smartphone to trace the bags' origin, including farmers' details. Ultimately, all these features will be accessible through one holistic app. These integrated solutions will create a trusted, comprehensive value chain platform serving multiple stakeholders simultaneously: Farmers: increased incomes through better yields, reduced post-harvest losses, and premium prices for traceable crops; Traders: access to high-quality commodities with possibility to trace them; Farmer groups owning warehouses and collateral manager: reduced collateral management costs; Consumers: assured product origin and safety; Environment: improved soil health through climate-smart agricultural practices.

core_fields.title: Mushroom Production and Value-Addition: Elevating Indigenous Food Heritage Through Regenerative Farming for Safe, Nutritious diets.
core_fields.description: MashLav Foods is scaling its regenerative mushroom powder initiative by turning local agro-waste like maize stalks into nutrient-dense, shelf-stable mushroom powder. Building on our successful fresh mushroom production, we now use solar drying and milling to create a climate-smart product that supports children and families facing malnutrition in Kilifi. By reducing waste and strengthening local food security, MashLav delivers an affordable, reliable source of essential micronutrients through a circular, community-rooted food system.
core_fields.abstract: In Kilifi, Kenya, many children begin their day with thin porridge or black tea, meals that fill the stomach but provide almost no essential nutrients. Families facing recurring climate shocks often cannot access diverse, nutrient-rich foods, contributing to high rates of stunting, anemia, and micronutrient deficiencies among children under five. We cultivate fresh oyster mushrooms using locally available agro-waste such as maize stalks, transforming low-value residues into a high-value, reliable food source. Through simple, controlled-environment techniques and optimized mycology practices such as substrate formulation, high-quality spawn, and strict contamination control, we achieve high yields using minimal water and land. Using our solar dryer and disc mill, we convert fresh mushrooms into shelf-stable powders naturally rich in protein, zinc, iron, and potassium. With this foundation proven, MashLav is now scaling mushroom powders to deliver even greater nutritional impact to children and families. This solution draws on scientific and technical insights from mushroom biology, regenerative agriculture, and, basic food technology. Drying, milling, and careful packaging extend shelf life, preserve nutrients, and ensure year-round availability. Recycling spent mushroom substrate back into farms as organic fertilizer improves soil fertility and reduces the burning of agricultural residues. Immediate and sustainable benefits are accessible, safe, nutrient-dense powders, reduced organic waste, and a strengthened mushroom value chain. Schools, households, and local markets gain a dependable nutrition solution, while communities and the environment benefit from circular, climate-smart food production rooted in Kilifi s realities.

core_fields.title: Safe-Water Agroforestry Innovation for Clean, Nutritious and Trusted Farm Produce.
core_fields.description: This project improves food safety in rural Sierra Leone by using biosand-filtered water to hygienically wash agroforestry crops and vegetables. Building on ACRG s U.S. Embassy funded biosand program, the Ceiba Foundation for Tropical Conservation Seeds of Sustainability agroforestry project, and the Global E-STEM Excellence Prize, the innovation integrates safe water with diversified crop systems. This approach reduces microbial contamination, strengthens nutrition, and increases consumer trust while advancing resilient, youth- and women-inclusive local food systems.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation improves food safety in rural Sierra Leone by introducing biosand-filtered clean water into the washing and post-harvest handling of agroforestry crops and vegetables. ACRG provides strong national validation through its U.S. Embassy funded biosand filtration program, where installations in Kailahun District demonstrated an 80% reduction in E. coli contamination between raw and filtered water and high adoption among households. This proven foundation shows both technical reliability and strong community readiness to integrate safe-water practices. The project also builds on two additional ACRG initiatives that strengthen its relevance: the Ceiba Foundation s Seeds of Sustainability agroforestry program, which expanded diversified crop systems in rural communities, and the Global E-STEM Excellence Prize initiative, which enhanced youth-led environmental learning and improved safe-food awareness. Together, these programs provide the agricultural, educational, and behavioral groundwork necessary for successful uptake of safe post-harvest practices. In many communities, farmers wash moringa, mango, guava, citrus, peppers, and leafy vegetables with untreated stream or well water that frequently contains microbial contaminants. Applying biosand-filtered water directly at this stage addresses one of the biggest gaps in the local food system. Scientific evidence reinforces this approach: Stauber et al. (2006) found 94 99% E. coli removal, while Stauber et al. (2012) recorded 59 60% reductions in diarrheal disease among users. This innovation improves food safety, strengthens nutrition, increases market trust, and advances resilient, women- and youth-inclusive agroforestry-based food systems.

core_fields.title: Women-Led Agroforestry in Indonesia: Tamanu Anchor Crop Model for Nutrition, Livelihoods, and Ecosystem Restoration
core_fields.description: This project expands a women-led Tamanu agroforestry model in Malang, building on Kebumen s success. Regenerative Tamanu systems are intercropped with nutritious staples such as cassava, taro, avocado, beans, banana, jackfruit, ginger, and herbs. Tamanu oil, sold to national and international buyers, serves as an anchor crop that justifies infrastructure investment and processing capacity. More than 150 farmers primarily women will increase income while restoring biodiversity, sequestering carbon, and strengthening local food security and nutrition.
core_fields.abstract: Rural farming communities in East and Central Java face declining soil fertility, unstable commodity pricing, and limited access to nutritious foods. Although Tamanu thrives on degraded land and has been widely planted by government programs over the past 20 years, these trees remain largely underutilized. Our innovation transforms this overlooked resource into a dual-value, women-led agroforestry system. Tamanu serves as a commercial anchor crop providing high-value oil for national and international buyers while enabling investment in post-harvest infrastructure that also supports nutritious intercrops such as cassava, taro, avocado, beans, banana, jackfruit, ginger, and herbs. Scientifically, Tamanu s deep roots, shading patterns, and tolerance for marginal soils make it ideal for multi-strata agroforestry, improving soil structure, water retention, and microclimate conditions for food crops. Socially, anchoring agroforestry to a stable commercial crop makes diversified food production economically viable for smallholder women farmers. Evidence from our Kebumen implementation demonstrates feasibility: 47+ women trained, a cooperative formed, value-added oil processing launched, multi-crop systems adopted, nutritious food availability increased, and income stability improved. Replicating this model in Malang across 300 hectares, the system could produce 300 450 metric tons of staple foods annually supporting the dietary needs of an estimated 3,000 5,000 people per year. Tamanu oil processing at scale could generate $200,000 $400,000 in annual cooperative revenue once trees reach peak productivity, with diversified intercrops adding further income. Immediate and long-term benefits include improved nutrition, higher and more stable women s income, enhanced decision-making power, restored ecosystems, carbon sequestration (>144,503 tons in five years), and scalable, community-led regenerative food systems.

core_fields.title: Enhancing access to affordable and sustainable fish protein in West Africa: Optimising operations in Ghana
core_fields.description: TriMarK Aquaculture Center utilizes treated wastewater to provide a consistent, local supply of fresh fish and vegetables in Ghana, addressing a critical food (protein) deficit and reliance on imports. Our proposal to the Seeding the Future Challenge requests production funding to scale this proven, sustainable model which converts wastewater nutrients for aquaculture, ensuring safe, nutritious food and resource efficiency, while providing equitable access to affordable, trusted food in the Global South.
core_fields.abstract: The Problem and Relevance: The innovation solves the dual problems of inadequate sanitation (untreated wastewater discharged into open drains) and food insecurity in Ghanaian urban communities. This is highly relevant as wastewater pollution causes severe health crises and environmental degradation. How it Solves the Problem (Novelty): We developed a novel, closed-loop business model that collects wastewater via sewer lines to a treatment plant. The key innovation is an integrated system that treats the water and recovers nutrients to sustainably produce high-quality tilapia and vegetables. This creates a circular economy where waste is a resource. Similar Solutions/Insights: While wastewater treatment and aquaculture exist separately, their integration into a financially self-sustaining business model in this specific context is novel. The scientific insight is that with proper treatment and monitoring, pathogens are eliminated, and reclaimed nutrients can safely replace expensive artificial feeds/fertilizers. Specific Benefits: Communities/Environment: Immediate reduction in pollution and disease vectors. Consumers: Access to affordable, safe, FDA/EPA-certified protein and vegetables. Farmers/Producers: Increased profitability and productivity through a reliable, low-cost input stream. Society: A scalable, market-driven solution that provides long-term health, environmental, and economic benefits without relying solely on donor funding

core_fields.title: Boosting Nutrition, Health and Livelihoods Through Instant Porridge in Kenya s Arid and Semi-Arid Lands.
core_fields.description: James & Ben Enteprises (JB) is scaling a patent-pending composite instant porridge made from maize, soybean, sorghum, and orange fleshed sweet potato to improve nutrition, health, and energy savings in Kenya s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs). By reducing cooking fuel use and building community-based distribution, the project supports livelihoods while providing an affordable and easy-to-prepare food for nutritionally insecure households.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition, high food prices, and limited access to convenient, nutritious foods remain major challenges in Kenya, particularly in arid and semi-arid lands. Traditional porridge requires long cooking times and substantial fuel, which is costly for low-income households and environmentally unsustainable. JB addresses these challenges with a patent-pending composite instant porridge flour made from maize, soybean, sorghum,orange fleshed sweet potato, and a locally sourced stabilizing ingredient produced from a crop that thrives in ASALs. The product undergoes an extrusion step that pre-cooks the flour, gelatinizes starches, and improves digestibility, enabling it to reconstitute instantly and mix easily with hot or cold water. This significantly reduces preparation time, fuel use, and labor while maintaining familiar taste and texture. An important technical advancement is milling to achieve a specific particle size distribution, which supports rapid hydration, limits lumping, and produces a smooth, consistent porridge. The stabilizing ingredient further enhances fiber content and prevents phase (solid from liquid) separation, a common limitation in existing instant porridges. While fortified cereal blends exist, most require cooking, exhibit lumping, or phase separation upon standing. Imported instant products are often expensive and not culturally adapted, while local options lack functional innovation and reliable performance. Beyond nutritional value and convenience, the innovation delivers sustainable and economic benefits by sourcing a key ingredient from ASAL communities, creating new income opportunities linked to climate-resilient agriculture. core_fields.title: Complementary Foods for Infant and Young Child Feeding: Addressing Affordability
core_fields.description: The project envisages developing three low-cost, nutrient-dense complementary foods for infants and young children in Zimbabwe, using sorghum, millet, moringa, cowpeas, peanuts, and indigenous fruits. The innovation addresses micronutrient deficiencies, supports child growth, and integrates smallholder farmers into sustainable value chains. It also builds on existing traditional porridge blends from indigenous knowledge systems (IKS) to address child food poverty and malnutrition, promote food security, climate resilience, and equitable access to affordable, appealing, and trusted foods.
core_fields.abstract: Zimbabwe faces high child malnutrition rates, a violation of children's rights. Current statistics show that 27% (577,000) are suffering from stunted growth and development, 1.5% (83,000) suffer from wasting, and 4.3% (> 90,000) are overweight or obese (UNICEF, 2024). The distribution of stunting is 20.7% and 23.8% in urban and rural areas respectively (ZIMLAC, 2025), primarily due to limited access to affordable, nutritious complementary foods. Zimbabwean child feeding practices rely on maize-based diets, which are deficient of essential micronutrients, and 25% (580,000) of children living in child food poverty eat impoverished diets consisting of only one or two food groups a day. Malnutrition undermines child development, permanently alters their development trajectory, arrests cognitive development, leading to long-term consequences such as lower educational achievement and reduced economic productivity. The innovation introduces culturally acceptable, nutrient-dense food blends in which sorghum and millet are supplemented with moringa, cowpeas, peanuts, and indigenous fruits. The grains and legumes are modified, prior to use, to improve digestibility and nutrients availability and production of vitamins through activation of endogenous enzymes and activity of fermenting microorganisms. The fermenting microorganisms also confer probiotic properties to the foods. Processing makes use of low-cost technologies that combine dietary modification (fermentation, sprouting) and supplementation to address the poor-quality-foods cause of stunted growth and development. Resultantly, infants and young children gain access to safe, nutritious foods while caregivers benefit from affordable, trusted products. Sourcing of raw materials improves smallholder farmers' income and market integration strengthening food security and climate resilience in their communities.

core_fields.title: From Waste to Resilience:Empowering Farmers in a Climate-Stressed World
core_fields.description: Our project converts biomass waste into biochar organic fertilizer using pyrolysis technology, Biochar fertilizer: increases yields by 50 100%, improves soil health, sequesters carbon, reduces synthetic fertilizer use, and promotes regenerative agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses critical challenges of poor waste management and declining soil fertility. Smallholders face low crop productivity, declining soil fertility and high costs for synthetic fertilizers, while communities struggle with disposing of waste often burned, causing air pollution and carbon emission. We address this challenge by converting this biomass waste into biochar organic fertilizer through pyrolysis, a controlled heating process without oxygen. This creates a stable form of carbon that enriches soil. Our innovation lies in integrating it into a localized, circular economy model. We produce a context-specific, ready-to-use biochar organic fertilizer blend that is effective, affordable, making it accessible for farmers.The scientific insight driving our solution is biochar s unique porous structure, which acts like a coral reef for soil. It retains water and nutrients, hosts beneficial microbes, and sequesters carbon for centuries. The immediate benefits for farmers and producers: Increase in yield /Farm productivity by 50-100% Cut input costs by up to 40% by using affordable biochar organic fertilizer Reduce dependence on synthetic fertilizer Increased income from increased productivity, which is further enhanced by creating a new income stream by selling their waste biomass to the factory Build farmer resilience against the impact of climate change. The immediate benefits for society and the environment: Promote proper waste management, which is a major challenge, Restore degraded soils, and fight climate change Promote Carbon sequestration Promote regenerative agricultural systems Control soil acidity which makes up 55% of Rwandan farming soil.

core_fields.title: Establishing a High-Capacity Cooler and Value Addition Center to Mitigate Tomato and Mango Waste
core_fields.description: This project establishes a centralized, high-capacity cold storage cooler to combat post-harvest loss of local tomatoes and mangoes at our indigenous communities. By conserving and preserving fresh produce, we will buy, sell, and implement value addition practices such as processing of tomatoes and drying of mangoes using available sunlight. This intervention will stabilize market prices, reduce waste, and increase income and profit for local farmers and entire community.
core_fields.abstract: The core problem is the severe post-harvest losses of high-value crops which are tomatoes and mangoes due to lack of cold storage infrastructure. For now excessive perishability and market gluts lead to over 30% of produce spoiling, leading to significant financial loss for farmers and wastage of food resources. This is relevant because it directly impacts farmer livelihoods, food security, and environmental sustainability such as water and land. The solution is the establishment of a Centralized Cold Storage and Value Addition Hub. The cooling of the produce rapidly reduces the metabolic rate and respiration of harvested produce, hence extending its shelf life from days to weeks. This technical intervention creates a good environment, decoupling harvest from immediate sale. Benefits Farmers- it will lead to immediate financial stability through guaranteed purchase, and sustainable increase in net income by accessing higher-value markets and reducing spoilage risk. Community- they will benefit from immediate access to higher-quality, safer produce over a longer period of time, and sustainable improved local food security. Environment- Immediate and sustainable reduction in food waste, which lowers greenhouse gas emissions from decomposing food and optimizes resource use. Society- Creation of new jobs in cold chain management and value addition, fostering sustainable economic growth.

core_fields.title: "AGGREGATE FARMING, Every Step Counts"
core_fields.description: The importance of Attitude and Value System in our daily living cannot be overemphasized. With the right Attitude and Value for Agriculture a global food system that improves the health of the people and the planet is achievable. Therefore, the birth of an Improved Agricultural system AGGREGATE FARMING, Every Step Counts a platform through which we Sensitize, Train, embark on Infrastructural development and produce food to promote Healthy People and Planet in Ebonyi State Nigeria.
core_fields.abstract: In Ebonyi State Nigeria. Attitude to life occasioned by Ignorance and Poverty has led to Food shortages and the Lack of Economic Infrastructures Including Irrigation system causing both Chronic and Hidden hunger with its associated Social Vices in the State. Therefore, the birth of the farming concept AGGREGATE FARMING, Every Step Counts a simple and easy to implement Farming Concept with huge positive impact on the People and Planet. It provides our Farmer and the general Public with the needed approach to improving Healthy Diet, restoring Biodiversity and increasing Income generation via Sensitization, Training and Food Production. Through this platform, we communicate the need for Farmers to aggregate farming system i.e. Planting of trees/crops with either fishery, Birds or lives stock simultaneously as well as grouping themselves by locations for a more productive output. We also, Identify Existing and Potential Livelihood Opportunities across our various Communities, and train them on how to leverage from such opportunities and seek Partnerships/Funding to harness them for the well- being of our Communities. We also, involves those we call Aggregators who aid spenetration and Monitoring of projects in the communities of intervention. In this Farming Concept, every step from the inception of the farm to Production, Processing, Distribution and consumption up to soil maintenance, Environmental Protection and recycling of waste is considered important as the yield or Income from every activity. Therefore, AGGREGATE FARMING, Every Step Counts can be used as one of the slogans for creating a Fairer World if given the opportunity.

core_fields.title: Empowering Women through Resilient Gender-Just Production Systems
core_fields.description: This project supports rural women in the Philippines to build climate resilience and economic stability through gender-responsive, nutrition-focused agroforestry. By combining climate-smart farming practices, women-led enterprises, and community learning platforms, it helps women adapt to climate risks, increase incomes, and improve local food systems. The initiative promotes equitable, regenerative and inclusive food system transformation in Guinayangan and Bailen.
core_fields.abstract: Climate change disproportionately affects rural Filipino women, who experience greater livelihood losses due to limited land access, heavy unpaid care burdens, and exclusion from climate advisory services. Studies show women farmers face 10 30% lower productivity, reduced access to climate-resilient inputs, and greater economic instability after climate shocks. This innovation addresses these systemic disadvantages by placing women at the center of climate-resilient agroforestry development. The project introduces a gender-responsive, nutrition-sensitive agroforestry model, co-developed with women farmers using local ecological knowledge. It integrates regenerative agriculture, diversified tree crop systems, and women-led processing and value addition. Unlike existing programs that treat gender as an add-on, this model is explicitly designed around intersectional barriers faced by rural women,age, poverty, ethnicity, land tenure status, and caregiving workloads, to ensure that climate solutions are accessible, adoptable, and profitable for women. The approach is novel in three ways: Women-led design and anticipatory adaptation, enabling women to shape climate strategies using seasonal forecasts, risk maps, and community-level monitoring. Integration of nutrition-sensitive, biodiversity-enhancing agroforestry with local women-led enterprises linked to markets. Embedded social infrastructure peer learning groups, savings cooperatives, and community-based M&E teams Immediate benefits include improved climate resilience of farms, diversification of income sources, increased household nutrition, and strengthened control of women over economic resources. Long-term benefits include gender-equitable value chains, restored ecosystems, and local governance models that institutionalize women s leadership in climate action.

core_fields.abstract: Abba Quality addresses persistent malnutrition among children and mothers caused by limited access to affordable, nutrient-dense foods. In many communities, diets lack sufficient protein, essential fats, and micronutrients, contributing to poor health outcomes, stunting, and reduced productivity. This challenge is especially relevant where nutritious foods are available but unaffordable, inaccessible, or poorly adapted to local purchasing power. The innovation lies in producing and supplying locally processed, affordable, and nutrient-rich food products including silver fish snacks and powder, peanuts coated with milk, eggs and cassava flour, peanut butter, and fortified porridge flour. They are distributed through local kiosks and small shops, as well as community health teams, ensuring wide reach to vulnerable families. The solution is guided by nutrition science emphasising the importance of high-quality protein, healthy fats, calcium, iron, and key micronutrients during early childhood and pregnancy. Silver fish provides highly bioavailable calcium and protein, while peanuts, eggs, and fortified cereals supply energy, essential fats, and micronutrients. Simple, scalable processing methods ensure food safety, quality, and long shelf life. Immediate benefits include improved dietary diversity, reduced micronutrient deficiencies, and better maternal and child health outcomes. Sustainable benefits include strengthened local food systems, income opportunities for farmers and processors, community nutrition education, and equitable access to trusted, nutritious foods contributing to healthier, more resilient communities.

core_fields.abstract: Across Caribbean SIDS, up to 40% of fresh produce is lost before consumption due to cosmetic standards, storage challenges and limited market access. core_fields.title: Cultivating Nutrition Sensitive, Regenerative Agri-production through Smallholder s Cluster Networks in Pakistan
core_fields.description: Pakistan s smallholder dominated agriculture faces degraded soils, high input costs, and rising climate risks, undermining access to affordable, safe, and nutritious food. This project drives transformative food-system s change by advancing regenerative practices through Agrihub Cluster Networks. By integrating no-till, residue mulching, cover crops, agroforestry, organic-matter restoration, precision multi-crop planter-mulchers, and efficient irrigation, it rebuilds soil health, reduces emissions, and strengthens resilience, supporting planetary well-being, enhanced livelihoods, safe and competitive production and sustainable food security.
core_fields.abstract: Problem and Relevance: Pakistan s agri-farming is constrained by depleted, alkaline soils, mostly below 0.6% organic matter; rising input costs; water scarcity; and intensifying climate stress and emissions. Smallholders under five acres, holding 64% of farmland, lack modern practices, mechanization, and advisory services, undermining productivity, incomes, food affordability, food safety, and accelerating environmental degradation, threatening long-term resilience and food security. Novel Solution and Comparison to Existing Solutions: The project establishes innovative Agrihub Cluster Networks, anchored by regenerative nucleus farms that deliver demonstrations, training, shared machinery, and advisory services to surrounding smallholders. Each hub enables hands-on coaching and access to regenerative tools. While small pilots exist, none in Pakistan integrate multi-crop precision planter-mulchers, tailored regenerative recipes, and a cluster-based adoption model. This nucleus-farm network introduces a region-first, scalable, practical, and cost-effective approach, reinforced through inclusive access to innovative machinery and services. Scientific and Technical Insights: The solution is rooted in the nature-based algorithm of soil science, which demonstrates that higher organic matter improves water retention, nutrient cycling, microbial activity, and climate resilience. Trials show that no-till, continuous mulching, crop diversification, and composting rebuild soil biology, cut irrigation needs, reduce chemical inputs, and raise yields. Precision multi-crop planter-mulchers accelerate adoption by enabling low-disturbance seeding, biomass retention, and cost-efficient regenerative transitions for smallholders. Benefits to Stakeholders: Farmers gain lower costs, healthier soils, and more stable yields with reduced climate vulnerability. Consumers access safer, affordable, and more nutritious food. The system restores biodiversity, cuts emissions, and builds soil carbon, strengthening long-term planetary health.

core_fields.title: Developing a Sustainable Plant Cell Culture Platform for Functional Food Ingredients
core_fields.description: This project establishes a sustainable plant cell culture platform for functional food ingredients, using rosmarinic acid (RA) as a proof of concept. In collaboration with a specialist technical partner, we will develop and optimise plant tissue cultures, compare suspension and hairy-root systems, and advance the most promising approach to small-scale bioreactor evaluation. This work reduces reliance on agricultural extraction and enables controlled, climate-positive production of consistent, high-quality ingredients for more resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Food manufacturers increasingly depend on botanical ingredients that are extracted from crops under conditions of volatile yield, inconsistent quality, and high environmental cost. Rosmarinic acid (RA), a natural antioxidant used to improve food safety and stability, is a prime example, typically sourced from land-intensive cultivation with significant water and chemical inputs. This project introduces a sustainable alternative: a plant cell culture platform designed to produce RA in controlled, resource-efficient systems. Building on extensive desktop feasibility studies, the innovation evaluates and compares two culture systems, suspension cultures and hairy-root cultures, to determine which offers the strongest biosynthetic performance, stability, and scalability. The optimal system will then be advanced into small-scale bioreactors to generate process parameters, productivity data, and early techno-economic insights that inform future scale-up. Plant cell culture offers a scientifically grounded pathway to higher RA yields per biomass, reduced land and water requirements, and the elimination of pesticides and fertilisers. The RA proof of concept serves as the foundation for a broader platform that can be extended to multiple botanical compounds relevant to food applications. Immediate benefits include improved food safety and cleaner-label formulations through access to consistent, high-purity RA. Long-term benefits include decentralised ingredient production, reduced environmental burden, and more resilient supply chains, particularly valuable in regions with limited agricultural capacity or high import dependence.

core_fields.title: Improving Bio-blend Concentration Through Centrifugation and Assessing Its Sorghum Growth Benefits in Uganda
core_fields.description: Sorghum is a vital drought-tolerant crop for East Africa s food security. Umuntu Agrobiotics Ltd produces Bio-blend , a Bacillus-based biostimulant that enhances nutrient availability, soil fertility, and crop growth. Farmers currently apply 1L per 20L of water, but there s demand for a highly concentrated formulation requiring only millilitres. This grant will support developing a ≥1 10 CFU/mL formulation, evaluating its performance on sorghum, assessing stability and shelf-life, and conducting a cost benefit analysis.
core_fields.abstract: 1. Background Microbial biofertilizers enhance nutrient cycling, plant nutrient uptake, and soil fertility while reducing dependence on chemical inputs. Bio-blend , containing three Bacillus species, promotes cereal growth through phosphorus solubilization, nitrogen fixation, and phytohormone production. However, the current formulation requires large application volumes (1 L per 20 L water), making its use labour-intensive and costly. Farmers have requested a more concentrated product. High-density formulations also improve microbial survival, colonization, and consistency under field conditions, aligning with Uganda s climate-smart agriculture priorities. 2. Problem Statement The existing Bio-blend formulation has low microbial density, requiring high-volume application that is cumbersome and limits adoption. Low density also reduces microbial survival and plant growth promoting effects, leading to inconsistent sorghum yields. Farmers need a concentrated version that can be applied in only millilitres per 20 L of water. Without an optimized high-CFU formulation, the full benefits of microbial biofertilizers for sorghum productivity and soil health cannot be realized. 3. Expected Outcomes A concentrated Bio-blend will reduce labour and input costs while maintaining microbial efficacy. The improved formulation is expected to enhance sorghum growth and yield, strengthen soil health, and reduce reliance on chemical fertilizers. Increased farmer adoption and more consistent field performance will support climate-smart agriculture, stimulate local biofertilizer innovation, and improve smallholder livelihoods.

core_fields.title: Smart Productive Forests Kenya: Digital Agroforestry for Climate Resilience and Farmer Prosperity
core_fields.description: Green Intelligence restores degraded landscapes through digital agroforestry with smallholder farmers. Our mobile app enables 500+ farmers to register trees via GPS photos, receiving incentives that boost survival to 70-85% while enhancing food security. This digital transformation ensures harvest traceability, connecting farmers to premium markets and carbon finance. The Nakuru and Tharaka Nithi pilot creates a scalable model for food system transformation linking transparency, climate resilience, and increased income.
core_fields.abstract: The Problem: Kenya's smallholder farmers face systematic exclusion from both premium agricultural markets and carbon finance, perpetuating poverty and climate vulnerability. International buyers demand traceability that farmers cannot provide; carbon markets require costly verification smallholders cannot afford. Meanwhile, traditional monoculture farming depletes soils, threatens food security, and delivers volatile incomes. The Solution: Green Intelligence's mobile application enables food system transformation through digital innovation. Farmers implement diverse agroforestry systems integrating fruit, nut, and medicinal trees with annual crops while documenting everything via geotagged photos with GPS coordinates. The platform generates harvest traceability through unique QR codes (meeting premium buyer requirements) while simultaneously creating carbon-eligible verification data (meeting registry standards). The Insight: One digital tool solves two exclusion barriers. By empowering farmers as data collectors, we achieve 70-85% tree survival (versus typical 50-60%) while reducing verification costs. This makes smallholder agroforestry carbon finance economically viable while providing traceability documentation that unlocks premium market access -transforming smallholders into eligible suppliers for both ethical buyers and carbon investors. Immediate Benefits: Farmers: Enhanced food security through diversified production; premium prices for traceable harvests; direct mobile incentive payments; potential climate finance revenue streams; Markets: Verified regenerative supply chains; transparent carbon credits for investors Environment: 500 acres restored; 6,067 tons CO₂ sequestered over project lifetime; strengthened ecosystem resilience

core_fields.title: Liberia Aqua-Fruitage for Community Resilience & Empowerment for Climate Adaptations (LACRECA)
core_fields.description: The LACRECA project will create climate-smart aquaponics systems for peri-urban communities to improve food security and nutrition. As we integrate aquaculture and hydroponics, the project will produce fresh fish and vegetables with 90% less water and minimal land use. We will build a central hub, community-operated pilot systems, and educational training to empower locals. We seek Grant funding to build demonstration units and equip community operators for sustainable food production and green jobs.
core_fields.abstract: The LACRECA project is a new sustainable food production and empowerment initiative in Liberia. Urban, Peri-urban, including rural communities in Liberia are struggling with a real food crisis, characterized by food shortages, supply chain vulnerabilities, and resource depletion. Many low-income community members lack access to fresh and nutritious food, while long-distance transportation of food exacerbates carbon emissions and resource scarcity. LACRECA addresses these issues through innovative aquaponics systems, a sustainable method that combines fish farming with plant cultivation in a closed-loop ecosystem. The system takes nutrient-rich water from fish tanks and circulates it to hydroponic grow beds, where plants filter and purify the water before returning it to the fish. This design is modular, adaptable to various urban spaces, and operates within climate-smart greenhouses to ensure year-round production. The integration of affordable IoT sensors allows real-time monitoring and automation, making this high-yield farming method accessible to community members. The benefits are substantial: consumers gain immediate access to healthy, pesticide-free produce, while local operators have a viable entrepreneurship pathway with stable income from higher yields and lower resource costs. Schools can use these systems as living laboratories for STEM education. Also, the environmental impact is significant, reducing food miles, water usage, and agricultural runoff, while sequestering carbon and promoting a circular economy.

core_fields.abstract: Our innovation combines land-based and climate smart aquaculture with energy systems ready for renewable power. It is primarily powered by solar energy and supported by inclusive skills development. Together these elements address three urgent challenges facing many regions today. They respond to disrupted food supply chains, limited rural employment and aquaculture practices that place a heavy burden on ecosystems. Traditional ponds and imported products cannot guarantee freshness, resource efficiency or stable output. Our solution uses RAS-Recirculating Aquaculture Systems with more than 95% water reuse, precise water quality control and low energy demand. The system builds on technical insights in engineering for recirculating production, biosecurity management and energy efficient design. This enables the production of high value crustaceans close to consumers while keeping environmental impact minimal. Solar power serves as the main energy source and is supported by heat recovery systems that reduce costs and the overall carbon footprint. The innovation is strengthened by three complementary components. The first is artificial intelligence and computer vision that act as digital eyes capable of detecting changes in health, growth and water quality at an early stage. The second is a structured education and micro credential program that equips veterans, young people and community members with practical aquaculture skills. The third is a blockchain based transparency layer that records production data, quality metrics and environmental performance in a trusted and tamper-proof form. Communities gain access to fresh protein, producers achieve stable yields and regions gain a scalable food model.

core_fields.title: Saving Ethiopia s Berbere: Fusarium-Resilient Genetics, Clean Seed Systems, and Regenerative Agronomy
core_fields.description: A rapidly expanding Fusarium wilt epidemic is collapsing berbere chili production, threatening Ethiopia s cuisine, cultural identity, and farmer livelihoods. This project integrates resistant Mareko Fana varieties, a pilot clean seed pipeline, and regenerative, Fusarium-suppressive agronomy. With USD 250,000, we establish a scalable, evidence-based innovation model that reduces disease losses, stabilizes yields, strengthens seed systems, and lays the foundation for nationwide adoption and long-term climate resilience.
core_fields.abstract: In 2023, berbere chili was a $1.6 billion USD market in Ethiopia. Production of berbere in Ethiopia has steadily risen since 1993, but has become volatile with shortages during the past five years. Fusarium wilt is devastating Ethiopia s culturally essential berbere chili, causing up to 70% yield loss in major production zones. Informal seed markets spread non-true-to-type seed, while climate extremes increase plant stress and susceptibility. Current solutions, including fungicides fail to provide durable control or protect the iconic Mareko Fana. Our innovation integrates three high-impact components into a unified, scalable model: 1. Fusarium-resilient genetics: Leveraging new resistant donors, purified Mareko Fana, and Ethiopia s first artificial inoculation platform to advance breeding lines and identify pre-release candidates with farmer-preferred quality traits. 2. A clean seed pipeline: Piloting breeder → foundation → community seed production in two hotspots, supported by seed health protocols and QR-based traceability to reduce adulteration and prevent pathogen spread. 3. Regenerative agronomy (RA): Deploying affordable soil health practices, rotations, biofungal treatments, and biofumigation to suppress Fusarium and strengthen climate resilience. Demonstrated with farmers through clusters, women s groups, and digital extension. This integrated approach is novel: no existing initiative in Ethiopia simultaneously improves genetics, seed quality, disease control through, RA for berbere chili. The model yields immediate benefits, reduced crop failure, increased yield, improved seed purity, and creates a replicable blueprint for systems across Africa. Our previously funded FCDO-project provides strong scientific foundations for this work; it enables translation into a validated, farmer-centered innovation capable of national scaling.

core_fields.description: The poultry feed production by smallholder farmers depends largely on fishmeal and imported soybeans which are costfull in most of Tanzanian rural areas. Thus, this project aims to build skills of the smallholder farmers in raising black soldier fly larva as protein rich feed ingredient for chicken production.
core_fields.abstract: The current practice in Tanzanian rural areas has shown that smallholder farmers do not have a reliable and affordable supply of protein rich food for poultry feed formulation. The current supply relies on availability of fishmeal and imported soybeans which are costly. However, many of the smallholder farmers have plenty of supply of agricultural waste such as crop residues, cow dung manure and domestic food remains. Value addition to these plenty available wastes could contribute to the smallholder s income and increase food diversity. Black soldier fly larva production presents an innovative, local cost and environmentally sustainable alternative for the utilization of these locally available resources for poultry feed. This project aims to build the skills of the smallholder farmers in raising black soldier fly larva as protein rich feed ingredient for chicken production. The project will initially build a dedicated facility to produce BSF eggs, which will be distributed to trained smallholder farmers for production of BSF larva through locally available resources as substrates. Then, the project will support the trained smallholder farmers to explore commercialization of the excess larvae frass and chicken products.

core_fields.title: AI Powered Multi Gas Sensing Platform for Reducing Food Loss and Improving Safety
core_fields.description: Global food systems lose over 1.3 billion tons of food annually, costing nearly USD 1 trillion and leaving 2.3 billion people food insecure. Our project introduces an AI-powered multi-gas sensing platform using ultra-sensitive nanohybrid detectors to identify spoilage and chemical risks before they occur. By enabling real time VOC monitoring across storage, cold chains, and agriculture, the system reduces waste, enhances safety, and delivers affordable, scalable technology for sustainable and equitable food access.
core_fields.abstract: Global food systems face severe losses, with more than 1.3 billion tons of food wasted annually, costing nearly USD 1 trillion and contributing to food insecurity affecting 2.3 billion people. Much of this loss originates from undetected spoilage, cold chain failures, microbial activity in grain storage, and quality degradation across supply chains. Current monitoring technologies lack the sensitivity and real-time detection capacity needed to prevent these losses at scale. Our innovation, SmellControl, introduces an AI-powered multi-gas sensing platform that detects spoilage-related volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and critical gases at ppm ppb levels using ultra-sensitive nanohybrid detectors. SmellControl s multi-channel architecture creates unique digital odor fingerprints generated every 1.8 seconds, enabling highly accurate and continuous monitoring. These signals are analyzed through a machine learning pipeline tested across multiple algorithms, where K-Nearest Neighbors achieved 98% classification accuracy, supported by an F1-Score of 0.97 and Recall of 0.98. Inspired by the diversity of human olfactory receptors, SmellControl allows a single low-power sensor ( 1 W) to detect dozens of gases and VOCs. The platform provides immediate and sustainable benefits: For producers & cold chains: early detection of spoilage, reduced waste, safer products. For farmers: soil gas profiling (CO₂, CH₄, NOx, NH₃, O₂, H₂S) enables better fertilization, drainage decisions, and emissions reduction. For consumers & society: safer, more affordable, and more reliable food access. For the environment: lower methane and CO₂ emissions through avoided spoilage. By offering a scalable, low-cost, real-time sensing system, SmellControl supports sustainable, resilient, and equitable food systems, particularly in resource-constrained regions.

core_fields.abstract: This project introduces a holistic innovation that tackles the long-standing challenges of mortality, disease, low productivity, malnutrition, climate stress and weak markets in Tanzania's indigenous poultry sector. Indigenous poultry plays a critical role in rural livelihoods; however, high mortality rates (15-40%), recurrent disease outbreaks, climate-induced feed shortages and inappropriate antimicrobial use significantly constrain productivity and compromise household income, nutrition, and one health outcomes. The project's innovation lies in integrating climate-smart practices, one health solutions and nutrition-sensitive interventions into indigenous poultry systems. This approach is informed by veterinary epidemiology, climate-smart farming, indigenous breed resilience research, ethno-veterinary practices and proven youth and women-led brooding and hatchery models across East Africa. The project addresses these challenges by introducing climate-smart housing, feeding, and water systems tailored to indigenous chickens, strengthening community-level disease surveillance, improving thermal-stable vaccine access and advancing responsible antimicrobial stewardship at community level, advancing herbal and natural feed-based solutions to enhance gut health and reduce antimicrobial misuse, establishing youth and women-led brooding, hatchery and feed micro-enterprises; developing circular systems that convert poultry waste into organic fertilizers and BSF larvae, embedding nutrition education to improve household diets, increase egg and meat consumption and support school-feeding programs. Immediate benefits include reduced mortality, improved egg and meat productivity, increased income, lower production costs, safer food, enhanced child and maternal nutrition. Long-term benefits include resilient, climate-proof poultry systems; empowered youth and women entrepreneurs; strengthened one health capacity; reduced antimicrobial resistance risks; improved soil fertility and dynamic rural markets that remain vibrant beyond the project period.

core_fields.abstract: Kenya s agricultural productivity is threatened by declining soil fertility, loss of Soil Organic Carbon, and rising erosion. Although vast amounts of soil, satellite, and climate data exist, farmers lack an integrated, affordable tool to convert this data into actionable guidance. Current advisory systems are fragmented, costly, and fail to provide predictive, nationally consistent insights. EarthGuard solves this by delivering a unified precision agriculture platform. It integrates AI, Machine Learning, GIS, Remote Sensing, and soil lab data into a single decision-support system accessible to all farmers. The platform creates a nationally scalable soil health framework to generate field-specific recommendations on nutrient management, carbon enhancement, and conservation. Using predictive analytics, it tracks soil carbon changes, identifies erosion hotspots, and assesses crop health. To ensure universal access, critical alerts and summarized insights such as soil health scores, key fertilizer recommendations, and erosion warnings are delivered via SMS, reaching low-tech users instantly. For those with smartphones, a dynamic web dashboard provides rich, real-time diagnostics, detailed maps, and connects farmers to nearby agro-dealers, breaking down adoption barriers. Grounded in the scientific insight that site-specific management boosts yields and resilience, EarthGuard transforms complex data into precise, actionable intelligence for farmers, policymakers, and extension workers. Immediate benefits include accurate fertilizer advice via SMS/dashboard, accessible soil health scores, and timely digital advisories. Long-term benefits are profound: improved soil fertility, reduced erosion, higher carbon sequestration (enabling carbon credit income), increased yields, and a stronger national framework for climate-smart agriculture.

Modern farming practices and imported food preferences have displaced traditional crops such as taro, despite their nutritional and ecological benefits. The project offers an integrated solution through Production - Restore and scale sustainable taro cultivation; Processing - Develop taro-based products (flour, chips, leaves); Market Access - Supply local markets, hotels, and a signature restaurant; Cultural Promotion - Revive Burundian cuisine and food identity; and Environmental Restoration - Rehabilitate wetlands and degraded land. The initiative targets smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and urban consumers while creating market linkages through taro-based food products and a culturally themed restaurant.
