core_fields.title: Healing Harvests: Trauma-Informed Climate-Smart Agriculture for South Sudan
core_fields.description: Healing Harvests pioneers breakthrough integration of trauma healing with climate-smart agriculture through the Psychosocial-Agricultural Integration Protocol (PAIP). In South Sudan, where 7.69 million face food crisis and conflict-induced trauma undermines agricultural productivity, PAIP systematically addresses psychological barriers. The innovation embeds mental health support within Farmer Field Schools, creating resilient communities capable of sustained food production despite adversity.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: South Sudan faces intersecting crises; 57% of population experiencing acute food insecurity, widespread conflict-induced trauma affecting 4 million people, and climate shocks devastating agriculture. Research demonstrates trauma impairs farming through reduced motivation, cognitive dysfunction affecting decision-making, and disrupted social cooperation essential for community farming. Traditional interventions addressing only agricultural techniques fail because psychological barriers prevent adoption. Solution: The Psychosocial-Agricultural Integration Protocol (PAIP) is first-of-its-kind systematic framework integrating evidence-based trauma healing into agricultural extension. PAIP operates through three components: (1) Trauma-responsive Farmer Field Schools where facilitators receive dual training in climate-smart agriculture and psychological first aid; (2) Community Healing Circles integrated within farming cooperatives providing structured peer support; (3) Seed-to-Soul Programming linking crop cycles with emotional processing, using planting and harvesting rituals as therapeutic mechanisms. Scientific basis: PAIP draws from emerging research showing mental health interventions improve food security outcomes by 51.5% compared to 39.7% in agricultural-only controls. The innovation operationalizes the psychological-agricultural nexus identified in Uganda's THRIVE Trial. Benefits: Farmers gain psychological resilience and agricultural skills simultaneously. Communities develop trauma-informed support structures while building food production capacity, addressing root causes for lasting transformation.

core_fields.title: Scaling Regenerative Community Food Gardens for Nutritious Diets and Resilient Institutional Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project advances a proven community food gardens model into a growth phase, expanding its reach, institutional integration, and systems impact. Building on an established implementation platform within a university and surrounding communities, the project scales regenerative food production, structured training, and nutrition-sensitive distribution across multiple sites. The initiative strengthens access to nutritious food, builds youth and community food-system skills, and embeds sustainable practices within institutional settings, demonstrating a scalable pathway for addressing food insecurity.
core_fields.abstract: Food insecurity and limited dietary diversity remain persistent challenges among university students and surrounding communities, undermining health, learning outcomes, and social wellbeing, while institutional spaces such as universities remain underutilised as sites for sustainable food production and skills development. The innovation addresses this gap through a regenerative, institution-anchored community food garden model that integrates nutritious food production, skills training, and environmental stewardship into a single, operational system. Food gardens are established and managed using regenerative practices such as composting, soil restoration, crop diversification, and space-efficient growing systems, enabling reliable production of fresh vegetables while improving soil health and reducing input dependence. These gardens function not only as food sources but also as learning platforms where students and community members acquire practical skills in food production, nutrition, and sustainability through structured training and participatory management. The approach is informed by evidence from agroecology, urban agriculture, nutrition science, and community-based food systems, which shows that integrated production-learning models are more effective and sustainable than short-term food relief or isolated gardening interventions. Immediate benefits include improved access to safe, nutritious food, reduced food insecurity, and hands-on skills development, while longer-term benefits include healthier soils, reduced organic waste through composting, stronger local food systems, enhanced employability, and a scalable, equitable model for sustainable food production within institutional and community contexts.

core_fields.title: Integrated social institutions to catalyze resilient and autonomous food systems in Mesoamerican coffeelands
core_fields.description: The project entails organizing a communal seed bank in Jaltenango, a market town surrounded by dozens of rural communities; establishing a demonstration organic vegetable garden and diversified orchard with a well-advertised farmstand; and circulating (across social media) six short films, developed through a participatory documentary process, each relating a farmer s personal connection to a traditional dish derived from ingredients harvested from local agroecosystems as well as providing a visual recipe to whet local appetites.
core_fields.abstract: For over a decade, CESMACH, University of Vermont, Food 4 Farmers and Equal Exchange have collaborated to address persistent food insecurity among coffee-producing families (Guzm n Luna 2025, Anderzen 2020). These projects empower participants to improve local food practices on their terms, resulting in the formation of an affinity group of farmers motivated to produce a diversity of staple crops, fruits and vegetables for local consumption. These niche actions have yet to influence broader trends undermining the integrity of food systems. Despite local demand for more sustainable, healthier options, diets are increasingly provisioned by industrialized farms and corporate processors operating in distant regions. Building on capabilities and aspirations facilitated through previous projects, we will model how alternative food relations can be scaled up from niche activities by prototyping key social innovations (iPES-Food 2019) that create stimulating spaces where farmers encounter appropriate technology, share genetic material and personal experiences, find inspiration in actionable forms, and forge relationships with consumers. Short films disseminated over social media reinforce these connections, awakening shared cultural memory and reconnecting appetite with territory. Direct benefits are access to locally-adapted seed; new farmer-consumer linkages; living references for creative farm planning; and a revived sense of agency vis-a-vis food futures. More broadly, this approach generates the relational dynamics among actors necessary for co-creating food systems that are responsive to local values and sensitive to the natural resource base (Pachoud 2019).

core_fields.title: Neighbors Nourishing Neighbors
core_fields.description: Neighborhood House Association s Nutrition Services Program alleviates hunger and combats obesity among preschool-aged children, older adults, and homeless veterans. Through the Neighbors Nourishing Neighbors initiative, families gain hands-on nutrition education that emphasizes preparing affordable, scratch-made meals, incorporating seasonal produce, and understanding where food comes from empowering households to make healthy, sustainable food choices that strengthen long-term well-being and community resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The Neighbors Nourishing Neighbors initiative is an innovative, scalable nutrition education model that addresses food insecurity and diet-related chronic disease by shifting from short-term food assistance to long-term food empowerment. The program integrates hands-on cooking instruction, seasonal produce education, and food system literacy to equip families with the skills needed to prepare affordable, nutritious, scratch-made meals at home. The initiative responds to a persistent and highly relevant challenge: preschool-aged children, older adults, and homeless veterans experience disproportionately high rates of food insecurity, obesity, and diet-related illness. Rising food costs, limited access to fresh foods, and insufficient nutrition and cooking knowledge exacerbate these disparities and contribute to long-term health inequities. Neighbors Nourishing Neighbors solves this problem through experiential, community-based education delivered in trusted neighborhood settings. Participants engage in interactive cooking demonstrations, culturally responsive nutrition lessons, and practical training in meal planning and food budgeting empowering them to apply healthy behaviors immediately and sustain them over time. The program is informed by research demonstrating that experiential nutrition education paired with cooking skills and food system awareness leads to measurable improvements in dietary behavior. Immediate outcomes include increased fruit and vegetable consumption, improved food preparation skills, and reduced reliance on ultra-processed foods. Long-term benefits include improved health outcomes, increased household food resilience, greater demand for seasonal produce, and strengthened community well-being. The model is designed for replication, enabling broad and sustainable impact.

core_fields.title: Food-Tech and Nutrition: Revolutionizing Africa's Local Food Supply.
core_fields.description: TerraChop unifies food-tech and nutrition to revolutionize Nigeria's local food supply. Our ChopFoods digital platform helps local vendors manage orders and reduce waste, while TerraDel produces affordable, hygienic snacks and functional drinks using local ingredients. This dual-impact ecosystem formalizes informal vendors, creates jobs, and provides urban communities with sustainable access to safe, nutritious, and certified food at mass-market prices
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria s food system is fragmented, resulting in low vendor productivity and poor hygiene standards. Millions of urban consumers lack access to affordable, nutritious food, leading to a rise in diet-related diseases and high food wastage. Formalizing this informal sector is critical for national food security and economic stability. TerraDel Ecosystem solves this through a unified approach. ChopFoods is a digital platform that provides vendors with AI-driven inventory management and logistics to reduce waste. TerraDel is a manufacturing unit that produces certified, affordable, and nutritious snacks and functional drinks (e.g., fortified buns and Zobo drinks) using locally sourced inputs. The innovation is built on the technical insight that controlling both the digital logistics layer and the physical production layer achieves massive cost efficiencies. By verticalizing the supply chain, we eliminate middle-man costs and guarantee safety standards that independent informal vendors cannot achieve alone. Special Benefits Consumers: Access to certified, hygienic, and nutrient-dense snacks at street-food prices. Producers/Vendors: Increased revenue (target 20%+) through operational automation and reduced spoilage. Farmers: Reliable demand and fair pricing through direct local sourcing of hibiscus and local grains. Communities/Society: Creation of formalized jobs and improved public health outcomes by displacing low-quality, contaminated street foods. Environment: Reduced food waste via inventory tracking and a lower carbon footprint through localized supply chains and eco-friendly last-mile delivery.

core_fields.title: Resilient Circular Food Systems: Symbiotic Sunflower-Apiculture and AI-Driven Green Market Integration
core_fields.description: MGL pioneers a circular food system by integrating symbiotic sunflower-apiculture farming with a digital marketplace. We empower 100 vulnerable women and youth in North-West Cameroon through regenerative agriculture and bio-fertilizer production. Our "Muyang" E-Auction platform streamlines market access, reducing dependence on smuggled oils while building a data-driven framework for future resource recovery, ensuring a resilient, nutrient-sensitive, and nature-positive food value chain.
core_fields.abstract: MGL addresses a triple crisis in Cameroon: Economic Dependence, Public Health, and Socio-Political Instability. The nation currently relies on approximately 1.1 million metric tons of imported vegetable oils annually to meet domestic demand. This massive deficit has fueled a rampant contraband market, with an estimated 500,000 liters of smuggled oil entering the country yearly. This undermines the State s import-substitution policy (SND30) and drains local jobs. Furthermore, the WHO reports that Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) now account for 35% of deaths in Cameroon, a surge largely attributed to high-cholesterol diets reliant on these low-quality, unregulated oils. Concurrently, the decade-long Anglophone crisis has displaced thousands, while the surge in unmanaged e-waste imports, containing documented carcinogens, is directly linked to rising regional cancer rates. Our solution is an integrated, nature-positive farming ecosystem that promotes extensive sunflower cultivation and apiculture. This symbiotic model empowers vulnerable women and at-risk men from conflict zones, providing the financial independence necessary for their social reintegration. By producing premium, non-cholesterol sunflower oil and natural honey, we directly serve the "upper demographics" and health-conscious citizens managing NCDs. This dual-commodity approach ensures high yields through natural pollination while restoring soil health via the production of local bio-fertilizers, reducing the environmental footprint of agricultural production. The technological driver of this system is our "Muyang" E-Auction platform. Beyond streamlining agricultural sales, the platform operates as a "Green Front" using an AI Triage Tool to manage a future "waste-for-wealth" loop. Users are incentivized to collect and sort hazardous Lithium-ion e-waste in exchange for coupons.

core_fields.title: SolarSmart-Preserve: Regenerative, Off-Grid Cold Storage to Cut Food Loss, Improve Nutrition, and Build Climate-Resilient Food-Systems
core_fields.description: This project scales solar-powered, off-grid mobile cold storage systems that preserve fruits and vegetables immediately after harvest and at markets after sales. Using clean energy, antimicrobial protection, and IoT temperature and germs monitoring, the solution reduces post-harvest losses, maintains nutritional quality, and prevents food contamination. The project increases farmer and vendor incomes, lowers methane emissions from food decay, and expands equitable access to safe, affordable, and trusted food in communities without reliable electricity.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation addresses one of the most critical yet overlooked challenges in food-systems: post-harvest food loss caused by lack of cold-storage, unreliable electricity, and high fuel costs. In many farming and market communities, fruits and vegetables begin to spoil within hours of harvest, leading to nutrient loss, unsafe food consumption, reduced farmer incomes, and methane emissions from decayed food. This problem directly undermines food-security, nutrition, climate goals, and equitable access to healthy-diets. The solution is a solar-powered, off-grid, mobile cold-storage system designed for use directly on farms and in local-markets. The system preserves crops immediately after harvest using clean-energy, eliminating dependence on diesel generators or grid electricity. Integrated IoT sensors monitor temperature and contamination levels in real time, ensuring food safety and consistent quality. With anti-bacterial and pest-resistant storage features prevent microbial growth and insect contamination, improving food hygiene and consumer trust. This innovation is novel in its mobility, affordability, and decentralized design, allowing shared use among smallholder farmers/vendors who are typically excluded from conventional cold-chain infrastructure. While cold-storage solutions exist, most are stationary, fuel-dependent, expensive, or inaccessible to informal markets. The technical insight combines solar energy systems, food preservation science, and digital monitoring to create a practical, climate-smart solution tailored to low-resource settings. Immediate benefits include reduced post-harvest losses, preserved nutritional value, higher-incomes for farmers/vendors, and safer food for consumers. Long-term benefits; lower greenhouse gas emissions, reduced air/noise pollution, improved food availability for schools/communities, and stronger, more resilient local food-systems that operate within planetary boundaries.

core_fields.title: Scaling Cluster-Based Agricultural Robotics Services for Smallholder Farmers
core_fields.description: Favrobotics is scaling a cluster-based agricultural robotics service that delivers timely land preparation, planting, and spraying to smallholder farmers. This project will deploy 6 operational robots across 3 farm clusters, providing mechanization as an affordable service rather than equipment ownership. The Growth Grant will accelerate multi-robot operations, operator training, and maintenance readiness, enabling reliable service delivery to thousands of farmers per season through farmer associations and local service hubs.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers across sub-Saharan Africa face persistent delays in land preparation and planting due to labor shortages and limited access to tractors, often resulting in missed planting windows, reduced yields, and unstable incomes. During peak seasons, existing mechanization services are frequently unavailable, unaffordable, or unreliable for farmers with small plots. Favrobotics addresses this gap through a cluster-based agricultural robotics service that delivers mechanization on demand. In this project, 6 modular field robots will be deployed across 3 farm clusters, each supported by trained local operators, maintenance capacity, and service hubs. Farmers access land preparation, planting, and spraying services through farmer associations and cluster agents, paying per acre rather than investing in costly equipment. The innovation combines robotics engineering with field operations and data-driven service delivery. A modular robot platform enables multiple farm operations using the same base unit, while proof-of-work logs, GPS tracking, and operator reporting ensure transparent pricing, reliable execution, and continuous optimization of utilization and uptime. The cluster model enables scalability by adding robots and trained personnel within existing hubs rather than redesigning operations. Immediate benefits include timely land preparation and planting, reducing peak-season delays from weeks to days and improving farm productivity through better planting windows. Early field experience indicates productivity improvements driven by timeliness, along with reduced wasted inputs through preision farming. The model also creates local technical roles per cluster, supporting rural employment and service reliability.

core_fields.title: Turning waste into affordable eggs for healthier communities
core_fields.description: Farm Vora is a community-based poultry farm that tackles child malnutrition in rural areas by supplying families with affordable, protein rich eggs. The farm uses locally sourced feed made partly from food waste, turning waste into nutrition and reducing production costs while feeding both animals and people sustainably.
core_fields.abstract: In Nigeria, malnutrition has become a serious and growing crisis, especially among children. Rising food prices driven by economic instability and weak policies have made basic meals unaffordable for many families. According to UNICEF, over 12 million Nigerian children and 4 in every 5 children under five years suffer from stunted growth and other forms of malnutrition. Long supply chains and middlemen further inflate food prices, making even eggs, once the cheapest source of protein, a luxury for many households. This crisis affects children's health, learning ability, and long-term economic prospects. Our innovation is practical and locally grounded. We produce eggs within the community and sell directly to families, removing extra layers that increase prices. We also produce our own chicken feed using locally available ingredients and food waste, turning waste into value. This approach came from observing how much organic waste is discarded daily while farmers spend heavily on commercial feed. Closing this loop reduces costs, stabilizes egg prices, and makes production more resilient. Technology strengthens this solution. Our mobile app allows families to order eggs easily and provides parents with simple nutrition guidance. Parents can take photos of their children's meals, and the app uses AI to analyze food content, track eating patterns, identify nutrition gaps, and suggest affordable local meal options. The immediate benefits include affordable eggs, improved child nutrition, and reduced food stress for families. Farmers benefit from lower feed costs, while communities gain improved food security, reduced waste, and better health outcomes.

core_fields.title: Integrated Livestock Value-Chain: A Circular Solution for Sustainable Feed and Food Security.
core_fields.description: CPP revolutionizes Central Africa s livestock sector by overcoming the 70% feed-cost barrier through an integrated circular value-chain hub. By combining solar-powered crop cultivation with zero-waste animal production, converting manure into biogas and bio-fertilizer, we eliminate external input dependency. This climate-positive model secures affordable protein and high-quality feed for smallholders, ensuring year-round food security and sustainable economic empowerment for youth and women in urban agricultural communities.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation lies in the transition from a traditional farm to a vertically integrated value-chain hub. The central problem solved is the "Feed Gap" in Central Africa, where volatile, imported feed costs account for up to 75% of livestock production expenses, making essential protein unaffordable. CPP addresses this systemic instability by eliminating external input dependency, ensuring that nutritious protein remains accessible to urban populations regardless of global market shocks. Our solution combines solar-powered irrigation for year-round feed cultivation with a zero-waste livestock model. The core scientific insight is based on nutrient cycling; we utilize anaerobic digestion to transform animal waste into high-quality bio-fertilizer and biogas. By reclaiming nitrogen and phosphorus from manure to fertilize subsequent feed crops, we create a closed-loop system

core_fields.title: Empowering Rural Dairy Producers through Sustainable, Low-Waste Motorized Butter Churning Technology
core_fields.description: The project designs a motorized churning system for three different rural Ethiopian women dairy farmers, reducing churning time from 4 hours to under 1 hour, reducing waste by up to 30%, and enhancing hygiene and yield. Through the manufacture of 15 machines and training of around 100 women, the project enables healthy, sustainable dairy production and equitable access to food and income, advancing safe practices and community empowerment through integrated engineering design.
core_fields.abstract: Traditional butter production in rural Ethiopia is labor-intensive, unhygienic, and inefficient taking up to four hours per batch using clay or gourd churners. The technique yields a small amount of butter and a large amount of organic waste, which is a problem for the women who have to deal with it. This project proposes a motorized butter churner that is made from food-grade materials and is very cheap. The machine has a capacity of processing 3-8 liters per batch, which eventually leads to time and waste reductions as well as up to a 25-30% butter yield increase. The invention combines three different principles: Safety & Nutrition: Food-safe design brings about less contamination and therefore fewer risks. Sustainability: The system allows not only for the reduction of waste but also for the reuse of by-products (whey and buttermilk) as feed for livestock or fertilizers for organic crops. Equity: It gives rural women the chance to earn money with their own technology, which, in turn, fosters their participation in cooperatives and technical training. The solution became available through a survey administered at Arba Minch University on the priority community issues, taking surveys from the local dairy farmers and the energy-efficient design testing. It connects mechanical innovation with the enhancement of community capacity to tackle some of the main limitations within the rural food system in Ethiopia.

core_fields.title: Unlocking the Hidden Power of Neglected and Underutilized Foods through Biomolecular Analysis and Nutrition Education
core_fields.description: This project harnesses advanced multi-omics analysis to unlock the nutritional, functional, and medicinal potential of neglected and underutilized species (NUS). By generating high-resolution biomolecular profiles and integrating them with traditional food composition data, we fill critical knowledge gaps that limit NUS adoption. Leveraging global partnerships and PTFI s standardized methods of data collection, findings will inform evidence-based consumer education, policy, and innovation, driving climate-resilient agriculture, revitalizing regional food systems, and advancing sustainable, biodiverse diets worldwide.
core_fields.abstract: Global food systems depend on fewer than 150 crops out of 30,000 edible species, accelerating agrobiodiversity loss, dietary monotony, and vulnerability to climate shocks. NUS offer exceptional nutritional, ecological, and cultural value, yet remain absent from mainstream agriculture, markets, and food composition databases, limiting their adoption and policy integration. This project will address that gap by combining cutting-edge science with education and capacity building. Leveraging the PTFI, we will apply standardized multi-omics protocols to analyze biomolecular profiles of NUS alongside traditional food composition data. Working with partner labs in Colombia and Thailand, two biodiversity hotspots, we plan to link advanced analytics with agricultural metadata to reveal the nutritional and functional benefits of edible biodiversity. Education and community engagement are central to this innovation. By integrating NUS into curricula, training programs, and community learning environments, we will create scalable pathways for knowledge dissemination. This dual approach, scientific insight plus education, ensures that findings translate into practice, empowering farmers, schools, policymakers, and consumers to make informed decisions. Immediate benefits include accurate dietary assessment tools, culturally relevant nutrition education, and evidence for public health policy. Long-term impacts include diversified diets, climate-resilient farming systems, revitalized Indigenous food cultures, and equitable benefit sharing, building food systems that are nutritionally richer, culturally grounded, and ecologically resilient.

core_fields.title: Integrated Smart Composting and Regenerative Food Systems for Climate-Resilient Communities in Malawi
core_fields.description: The project introduces a small-scale composting system that converts organic waste into safe farm inputs through timed aeration and temperature control. It connects farmers, youth, and women s groups through a digital learning and sales platform. This approach strengthens soil fertility, improves food quality, and builds community awareness on sustainable farming. The model supports cleaner towns, productive farms, and a food system that works within natural limits.
core_fields.abstract: Malawi s food system faces declining soil fertility, low yields, and unsafe waste disposal. Many farmers depend on synthetic fertilizers, yet organic waste remains unused. This project applies a practical composting system that turns waste from markets and households into reliable organic fertilizer using small aerated bins and sensor-based temperature control. The composting unit uses simple timers and low-voltage fans to maintain aerobic conditions, reducing methane emissions and producing stable compost in three weeks. A mobile-based dashboard records the process, tracks temperature data, and links producers with buyers and trainers. Farmers and youth cooperatives manage the compost sites under local supervision. The idea grew from field experience with 360 Research Solutions and EKCOLAB Malawi, where young people already run small waste collection groups. The scientific basis was developed with LUANAR soil scientists who tested nutrient levels and moisture balance under controlled trials. The immediate outcome is better soil structure and higher yields for smallholders. Over time, it supports cleaner surroundings, lower waste volumes, and stronger community engagement in regenerative food production. The model is simple enough for local replication and adaptable for other regions that face similar conditions.

core_fields.title: Digital Traceability and Regenerative Farming for Safe, Nutritious Food in Kasese Rwenzori Region Uganda
core_fields.description: Afri-YieldPro Company Limited proposes a 14-month project in Kasese District to pilot a regenerative, traceable, and low-loss food system for 250 smallholder farmers. Through two Regenerative Farming Hubs, digital traceability, and Food Loss Reduction Kits, the project will improve soil health, reduce post-harvest losses by 20 30%, and enhance access to safe, nutritious foods. Women and youth are empowered as champions, creating a scalable, climate-resilient, and inclusive model for sustainable food production.
core_fields.abstract: Afri-YieldPro s innovation pilots a regenerative, traceable, and low-loss food system for 250 smallholder farmers in Kasese District. The project addresses key challenges: declining soil fertility, unsafe and non-traceable foods, high post-harvest losses (up to 40%), and limited access to markets and nutritious foods. These barriers undermine farmer incomes, food security, and climate resilience. The solution integrates three components: 1. Regenerative Farming Hubs (Regen-Hubs): Community-based hubs where women and youth are trained in soil restoration, composting, crop rotation, mulching, and organic fertilizer use, increasing yields and nutrient density. 2. Digital Value Chain Traceability: A simple USSD/SMS system with QR-coded labels tracks produce from farm to market, ensuring food safety, evidence-based decisions, and access to premium buyers. 3. Food Loss Reduction Kits: Solar tent dryers, hermetic bags, and reusable crates reduce post-harvest losses, preserve nutrients, and improve marketable volumes. Scientific and technical insights from climate adaptation research, regenerative agriculture, and post-harvest studies informed the approach, ensuring environmental sustainability and resilience. Immediate benefits include improved soil fertility, reduced post-harvest losses by 20 30%, and access to digital tools for production and market information. Long-term benefits include enhanced incomes, empowerment of women and youth as hub operators and traceability agents, safer and nutrient-rich foods for communities, and a scalable, climate-resilient model linking production to markets. This innovation delivers economic, social, and environmental impact, creating a replicable pathway for sustainable, nutritious, and low-waste food systems in Uganda s Rwenzori sub-region.

core_fields.title: Soil and Food
core_fields.description: Soil and Food regenerates degraded soils and improves food security by converting organic and food waste into microbial-rich biofertilizers. Our solution restores soil health, boosts crop yields, and reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers while cutting waste and emissions. By empowering small farmers with sustainable practices, we create a circular, low-cost, and climate-resilient food system that delivers healthier harvests and supports rural livelihoods across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Soil and Food introduces a bio-regenerative innovation that transforms local organic and food waste into microbial biofertilizers and soil enhancers, restoring fertility to degraded soils while improving the nutritional quality of crops. The problem it addresses is soil degradation, which affects over 60% of farmland in Sub-Saharan Africa, leading to poor yields, malnutrition, and economic vulnerability among smallholder farmers. Our solution uses a controlled fermentation and microbial enrichment process to convert waste into a living soil amendment rich in beneficial microorganisms, enzymes, and nutrients. This replaces chemical fertilizers that are costly, degrade biodiversity, and emit greenhouse gases. The technology relies on biological insights from soil microbiology and circular nutrient cycles, ensuring nutrients are naturally recycled back into the soil ecosystem. The innovation s immediate benefits include increased crop productivity (up to +30%), reduced input costs (up to -60%), and improved food nutrition through healthier soil. Sustainable long-term benefits include carbon sequestration, biodiversity restoration, and waste reduction, creating a circular, climate-positive agricultural model. For farmers, it means better harvests and income stability; for communities, it ensures affordable, nutritious food; for the environment, it reduces pollution and greenhouse emissions. Soil and Food offers a scalable, low-cost, and locally adaptable innovation that empowers African farmers to regenerate their land while feeding their people sustainably.

core_fields.title: The MUK Bio-Cycle Living Lab: A Data-Driven Model for a Waste-Free, Protein-Rich Campus
core_fields.description: The system converts food waste into two high-value products BSF larvae (for protein feed) and organic fertilizer (frass) thus reducing landfill methane emissions, eliminating pest hazards, and creating a circular, data-driven food system prototype for East Africa. It has three components; A modular Black Soldier Fly (BSF) bioprocessing unit for waste conversion, A solar photovoltaic (PV) system to power dryers, heaters, and sensors, and an IoT-enabled Smart Waste monitoring system for real-time tracking.
core_fields.abstract: The MUK Bio-Cycle Living Lab introduces a data-driven circular bio-conversion system that transforms organic campus waste into high-value insect protein and biofertilizer, creating a zero-waste, energy-efficient food system model. The innovation addresses the urgent challenge of food waste mismanagement and protein insecurity two issues that threaten both environmental sustainability and student nutrition in low- and middle-income settings. At its core is a compact 24 m black soldier fly (BSF) processing unit, integrated with a solar-powered cabinet dryer and a rooftop photovoltaic (PV) array. Organic waste from university kitchens and cafeterias is converted into larvae, which are dried using renewable energy to produce protein meal for poultry and fish feed, while the residual frass serves as organic fertilizer for campus gardens. This solution combines engineering design, renewable energy, and biological recycling in one modular system. The insight driving this innovation is the use of insect bioconversion as a natural, low-cost mechanism to close nutrient loops while reducing carbon emissions and landfill burden. Immediate benefits include reduced waste collection costs, clean energy use, and locally available animal feed. In the long term, the model fosters behavioral change, climate resilience, and food system literacy among students and surrounding communities. The MUK Bio-Cycle Living Lab thus serves as a replicable prototype for sustainable campus-based circular food systems in Africa.

core_fields.title: Empowering Farmers, Powering Communities
core_fields.description: By the project, Nampya aims to build a resilient, equitable food system by connecting smallholder farmers across East Africa to fair urban markets through solar-powered micro-warehouses and a digital trading platform. We aim to cut post-harvest losses, boost farmer incomes, and accelerate the energy transition in agriculture. By combining renewable energy, data-driven logistics, and community-based governance, Nampya turns rural challenges into opportunities, empowering farmers as key agents in driving sustainable, climate-smart, and inclusive agricultural transformation
core_fields.abstract: Nampya Farmers Market addresses a critical problem: smallholder farmers in Uganda and across Africa face post-harvest losses, limited market access, and income instability, while urban markets struggle with unreliable supply of fresh produce. Climate shocks, poor storage infrastructure, and inefficient supply chains trap farmers in cycles of poverty and threaten food security. Our solution combines solar-powered micro-warehouses with a digital trading platform, creating a climate-smart, technology-driven network that connects farmers directly to urban buyers. Solar-powered storage preserves fresh produce, reducing post-harvest loss by up to 70%, while the digital platform ensures fair pricing, transparency, and timely transactions. Farmers receive market information, can plan production better, and sell directly without middlemen. This solution is informed by insights from supply chain management, agricultural logistics, and renewable energy integration. By combining technical knowledge with local farming realities, we designed a system that is scalable, sustainable, and inclusive, particularly for women farmers. Immediate benefits include higher and more reliable incomes for farmers, reduced food wastage, and increased access to fresh produce for consumers. Sustainable benefits extend to climate resilience, energy efficiency, and stronger local food systems, while communities gain opportunities for employment and skills development. Schools and institutions also benefit from a consistent supply of quality produce, supporting nutrition and health outcomes. Nampya s innovation demonstrates that technology, renewable energy, and equitable trade can solve systemic agricultural challenges, empowering farmers, protecting the environment, and creating resilient, inclusive food systems for society at large.

core_fields.title: Women-Led Nature Positive Farming for Food & Nutritional Security in Arid, Drought-Prone Anantapur region
core_fields.description: The project will showcase an innovative, nature-positive Natural Farming model with 800 poor households in drought-prone Anantapur to strengthen local food production, consumption, and sovereignty. It offers a decentralized, low-cost, regenerative alternative to chemical-intensive agriculture, with women as key change-makers in each family. Successful women-led models will catalyze wider adoption and help accelerate the scaling up of Natural Farming across Anantapur and other drought-affected regions.
core_fields.abstract: This project proposes to work with women farmers to demonstrate an innovative Natural Farming model to create food and nutrition security adopting the nature-positive alternative to conventional farming in the arid, drought-prone Anantapur region of Andhra Pradesh. With annual rainfall under 510 mm and evapotranspiration around 2,250 mm, farmers in the region face recurrent droughts, degraded soils, low and unstable incomes, and distress migration. The proposed Natural Farming model combines mixed cropping of cereals, pulses, vegetables, relay sowing, crop rotation, tree crops with locally adapted, drought-tolerant varieties in a regenerative, permanent farming design. The model is derived from the proven agroecology models developed by Andhra Pradesh Community Natural Farming project, Accion Fraterna Ecology Centre and others. The farmers are supported with required technical knowledge, skills and inputs. These models have shown strong results in achieving food and nutrition, self-sufficiency, public health, ecological restoration, and climate resilience and are now ready for scaling up across the country. Scientific evidence shows that Natural Farming improves soil moisture retention, biodiversity, and reduces reliance on irrigation and synthetic inputs, making farms more productive, climate-resilient and sustainable. For proof of concept, please visit the website www.apcnf.in.

core_fields.title: Scaling Circular Parboiling System for Climate-Resilient Rice, Farmer Equity, and Enhanced Nutrition in West Africa
core_fields.description: We are scaling the Climate-Smart Value Chain Protocol (CS-VCP), an innovation replacing high-emission, firewood-based rice parboiling in Ghana with a proprietary circular system. This system enhances climate resilience, improves nutrition (B vitamins), and ensures equitable income for 1,500 farmers (60% women) by cutting post-harvest losses by 30%. The $100,000 Growth Grant is essential to replicate five validated CS-VCP units, doubling our network and accelerating the adoption of this sustainable food system model in West Africa.
core_fields.abstract: The problem solved is the systemic reliance on high-emission, firewood-based rice parboiling in Northern Ghana, which threatens climate stability, women s health, and food quality. This practice perpetuates a crisis where 90% of smallholders suffer up to 45% post-harvest losses, leading to poverty and 70% import dependence in Ghana. How It Is Solved: Our solution, the Climate-Smart Value Chain Protocol (CS-VCP), replaces open-fire methods with a proprietary, standardized Circular Parboiling System. This innovation is novel because its closed-loop design drastically reduces firewood use, parboiling time, and CO₂ emissions, utilizing agricultural waste for energy. It transforms the technology from a health hazard into a sustainable, energy-efficient commercial process. Scientific Insight: We leverage the food science principle of hydrothermal treatment (parboiling). Our standardization ensures the efficient diffusion of essential B vitamins (e.g., thiamine) into the rice kernel, resulting in a nutritionally superior product compared to conventionally milled rice. Benefits to End Users: Farmers gain guaranteed income via up to 30% reduction in post-harvest losses and fair pricing. The system empowers 60% of women processors by reducing parboiling time from 72 to 24 hours, eliminating smoke inhalation risks. Sustainable benefits include mitigating deforestation and cutting CO₂ emissions. Consumers receive FDA-certified, premium-quality rice with enhanced nutrition.

core_fields.title: Omboga Veg Hub: Safe, Nutritious Vegetables for Enhanced Food Security and Climate-Resilience
core_fields.description: The Omboga Veg Hub Project builds a decentralized network of hubs connecting smallholder farmers to reliable markets for African leafy vegetables. Through climate-smart training, organic inputs, and food-safe handling, the project improves productivity and reduces post-harvest losses. Each hub guarantees fair prices, daily offtake, and efficient distribution to schools, hospitals, eateries, and walk-in customers strengthening farmer incomes, community nutrition, climate resiliance, and long-term food security.
core_fields.abstract: The Omboga Veg Hub Project introduces a decentralized hub-and-spoke model that aggregates African leafy vegetables directly from smallholder farmers and connects them to reliable markets. This innovation addresses multiple critical challenges: unpredictable market access, post-harvest losses, inconsistent pricing, poor food safety, and limited availability of nutritious vegetables in schools, hospitals, and communities. The problem is highly relevant as smallholder farmers often struggle to sell perishable vegetables at fair prices, while consumers face shortages of safe, nutritious produce. Traditional supply chains are fragmented, leading to high post-harvest losses of 30 40% and limited income for farmers. The project solves this by establishing localized veg hubs that offer daily offtake, fair pricing, and access to walk-in customers, institutions, and eateries. Farmers receive climate-smart training, digital production management, and organic inputs such as biochar vermicompost fertilizer, improving yields, quality, and food safety. The system leverages insights from agricultural science, post-harvest management, and circular economy principles to integrate sustainable production, handling, and distribution. Immediate benefits include: increased farmer income, reduced post-harvest losses, and improved availability of safe, nutritious vegetables for consumers. Schools, hospitals, and communities gain access to reliable, high-quality produce, enhancing nutrition and food security. Sustainable benefits include strengthened local food systems, climate-resilient farming practices, rural job creation, and environmentally responsible production through organic inputs and waste-to-fertilizer integration. By connecting farmers to structured markets while promoting sustainable and safe agricultural practices, the Omboga Veg Hub Project creates a scalable, inclusive, and climate-smart solution for Kenya s vegetable value chain.

core_fields.title: Parsanda Dry Meat by Musakhel Agro Livestock Farm
core_fields.description: Parsanda Dry Meat by Musakhel Agro Livestock Farm transforms fresh meat into high-quality, long-lasting dry meat, reducing waste and ensuring year-round availability. The project introduces modern processing and packaging to preserve nutrition, support food security, and create sustainable rural employment. By converting surplus meat into shelf-stable products, Parsanda offers a smart solution to Pakistan s post-slaughter losses while promoting national and international market growth.
core_fields.abstract: lack of preservation facilities, seasonal demand, and limited cold chain infrastructure. Thousands of kilograms of fresh meat spoil every year, especially in rural areas and during religious seasons. This waste reduces food availability, economic value, and environmental sustainability. Parsanda Dry Meat introduces a modern, low-energy drying and preservation system that converts fresh meat into safe, long-lasting dry meat with a shelf life of up to six months. The process uses controlled air pressure, natural herbs, and hygienic techniques without chemical preservatives maintaining nutrition, taste, and texture. This innovation bridges the gap between meat surplus and shortage seasons, offering consumers a healthy protein option that does not require refrigeration. It also reduces greenhouse gas emissions from meat spoilage and transport, supporting climate resilience and sustainable food systems. Technically, the project applies scientific drying principles similar to global jerky production but tailored to Pakistan s local climate and meat characteristics. The model can easily be scaled to community or industrial levels. Immediate Benefits: Reduces meat waste and post-slaughter losses. Creates value-added products with export potential. Provides income and employment in rural communities. Sustainable Benefits: Strengthens national food security. Lowers environmental impact through reduced spoilage and energy use. Promotes innovation in Pakistan s meat processing industry and builds a model for other developing regions.

core_fields.title: HARVEST - Harnessing Agroecology, Regeneration, and Value-Enabled Systems for Equitable Transformation.
core_fields.description: HARVEST - pioneers a farmer-driven, technology-integrated regenerative agriculture model that restores soil health, amplifies climate resilience, and improves food and income security. Integrating indigenous knowledge, regenerative farming, and digital nutrition intelligence, HARVEST connects smallholders and youth in Kenya to lead the sustainable transformation of food systems through the creation of circular value chains that nourish people, sustain the planet, and build equitable rural prosperity.
core_fields.abstract: HARVEST- Harnessing Agroecology, Regeneration, and Value-Enabled Systems for Equitable Transformation - presents a new type of hybrid innovation that brings together agroecology, digital intelligence, and the creation of circular value to transform Kenya's food systems from extractive to regenerative. The basic problem is declining soil fertility and increased food insecurity, inequitable access to nutrition due to unsustainable farming and inefficient markets. This is an issue of great concern because the smallholders, who feed more than 70% of Africa, experience worsening climate shocks and depleted soils, leading to erratic income. HARVEST solves this with BioNexus Pods: modular, community-based regenerative hubs that integrate precision soil sensors, AI-driven agro-advisory dashboards, and climate-smart production models. These Pods connect farmers, schools, and local markets into a closed-loop ecosystem, valorizing waste, optimizing nutrient flows, and enhancing productivity within planetary boundaries. Scientifically, HARVEST draws on systems ecology, data-driven agronomy, and behavioral economics - a linkage of local wisdom with frontier science. This allows for real-time monitoring of the health of soils and biodiversity while creating incentives for regenerative practices through digital traceability and fair market access. From this come a host of immediate benefits: increased fertility in soils, reduction of input costs, and farmer income diversification. Long-term benefits will include nurturing climate resilience, improving nutrition from biofortified crops, and strengthening local economies through inclusive value chains. We are creating a self-sustaining, data-smart environment that regenerates land, livelihoods, and trust-anchoring a new model of equitable, climate-positive food futures for Africa and beyond.

core_fields.title: Bridging Surplus and Need Through Smart Food Recovery
core_fields.description: Plenti is a surplus-food app based marketplace on a mission to eliminate food waste by connecting restaurants, bakeries, supermarkets etc. with customers who can purchase unsold food at highly affordable prices (60-70% discount from retail price). By rescuing excess meals that would otherwise be discarded, Plenti reduces environmental impact, supports local businesses, and ensures sustainable abundance for communities. Our vision is to turn everyday surplus into accessible value while driving India towards a zero-waste future
core_fields.abstract: Plenti is an impact-driven app based surplus-food marketplace designed to eliminate food waste by redirecting unsold, perfectly good meals from restaurants, bakeries, and stores to consumers at highly affordable prices. The problem we address is massive: India discards an estimated 68 million tonnes of food in 2024, even as millions struggle with rising food costs. This gap between wastage and need is both an economic and environmental challenge, contributing to methane emissions, lost resources, and financial losses for food businesses. Plenti solves this using a simple but powerful insight: a large portion of food waste occurs not due to quality issues, but due to timing and demand uncertainty. By enabling businesses to list surplus food on its mobile app in real time, Plenti creates a demand channel that did not exist before turning last-minute surplus into value. Our innovation lies in combining technology, behavioural nudges, and local community networks to create a circular food system. With already 150+ partners onboard, Plenti has managed to save 8500 servings of good food, while catering to the demand of more than its 43,000 users in just 2 months since launch. Restaurants have earned in excess of $6000 (INR 540,000) from good surplus food while also saving 12,000kg of CO2 emissions. The immediate benefit is that price sensitive and eco-concious customers are saving money while vendors unlock additional source of revenue. In the long term Plenti will enable a sustainable ecosystem throughout Indian cities where nothing valuable goes to waste.

core_fields.title: Smart Cups Zero-Liquid Nutrition for Global Health and Food Equity
core_fields.description: Smart Cups Zero-Liquid Nutrition Initiative delivers printed hydration, protein, and milk products that provide essential nutrients without refrigeration, heavy transport, or waste. Built on patented technology validated by UCLA sustainability research and commercial partnerships including the U.S. Army this project targets malnutrition in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Kenya, the Philippines, and U.S. inner cities. Founded by Chris Kanik, who faced childhood hunger, Smart Cups aims to transform global nutrition access with dignity and innovation.
core_fields.abstract: Smart Cups Zero-Liquid Nutrition for Global Health and Food Equity provides a breakthrough solution to malnutrition, dehydration, and nutrient scarcity through a patented zero-liquid printed delivery platform. Instead of transporting heavy, perishable liquids, Smart Cups prints electrolytes, proteins, flavors, and micronutrients directly onto recycled paper cups and bowls. When water is added, the printed ingredients instantly transform into hydration drinks, flavored milk, or protein-rich bone broth. This innovation addresses urgent global challenges: more than two billion people suffer micronutrient deficiencies, 340 million children lack access to nutritious diets, and many communities especially in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Kenya, the Philippines, and underserved U.S. school districts face chronic shortages of dairy, protein, and clean hydration. Traditional liquid food systems depend on costly cold chains, generate high emissions, and result in significant waste and spoilage. Smart Cups eliminates these barriers by reducing transport weight by 95 97%, enabling 21 31 times more servings per shipment, and removing refrigeration entirely. A UCLA-led life-cycle assessment confirms 40 57% lower greenhouse emissions, 23 48% lower energy use, and up to 90% less packaging. The scientific insight is the fusion of microencapsulation, precision deposition, and printed ingredient release allowing stable storage of nutrients for 1 2 years, even in hot climates. This provides immediate benefits: affordable, shelf-stable hydration, protein, and milk alternatives for schools, families, clinics, and disaster-response programs. Sustainably, Smart Cups reduces carbon emissions, packaging waste, cold-chain dependence, and food loss while enabling future local micro-factories that empower communities to produce culturally relevant nutrition themselves.

core_fields.abstract: The innovation is the unified Social Production and Health Corridor, a dual network centered on the Social Production Park (PPS). It addresses the urgent problem of severe socioeconomic exclusion in Eastern Santa Fe, where vulnerable populations face fragmented health services and 87.4% of working-age people with disabilities lack formal employment. The solution is an integrated system that combines economic development with comprehensive social services. The Productive Corridor fosters sustainable Social Economy enterprises (e.g., food, textile, construction) to create 250 direct jobs and reduce consumer costs by optimizing logistics and bypassing unnecessary intermediaries. Simultaneously, the Health Corridor provides integrated care mental health, addiction treatment, and disability rehabilitation from nine strategic municipal nodes, centralized at the PPS Health Center. This design explicitly links rehabilitation with secure pathways to job insertion. The key insight is the commitment to prioritizing the explicit social goal over the profit motive, focusing on attending to unmet community needs. This effort is supported by technical assistance and specialized training from the UTN Santa Fe Annex. Specific immediate and sustainable benefits include raising the job occupancy rate for people with disabilities to a projected 22.5% in five years, providing end users with accessible, high-quality health care, and offering secure employment opportunities. Sustainability is further ensured by a durable, triple-impact infrastructure and resilient cooperative management, designed for a 20 25 year lifespan

core_fields.description: The goal of the proposed project is to contribute to the appropriate knowledge on Tilapia fish cage farming, access to inputs and technical guidance. Women and youth groups (outgrowers) will have the opportunity to farm their own fish, ensuring a consistent quantity and quality supply of fish for their business and reducing reliance on external sources, this will contribute to the appropriate income generation, fish increase, easy access to nutrition, employment, and poverty reduction.
core_fields.abstract: Corresponding to Doblin's Ten Types of Innovations, our innovation predominantly touches upon structure innovation': the nucleus-outgrower scheme bundles together human capital and assets in a unique way, creating value to each individual actor. This project is both beneficial for the fisheries industry, retail/catering sector and other off takers, and to the Outgrowers who will be engaged in the project. The uniqueness of this value proposition is the structure of the network that we are setting up: a nucleus-Outgrowers scheme for cage Tilapia fish farming. Through this innovation (such network does currently not exist in the aquaculture sector in Tanzania), the Outgrowers are provided with essential support (inputs and extension services) and comfort (guaranteed market). This will result to employment creation, per capital income generation and increase which will contribute to flourishing economic ecosystem where many different individuals benefit from our innovative structure both inside (e.g., employees, Outgrowers) and outside the core of the model (e.g., off takers, fish feed supplier, fresh fish vendors and all the key actors in fish value chain). The fresh fish market consists for 99% of wild catch and imported fish from China, which have a significant negative influence on the environment: the natural water bodies are being overfished, and the greenhouse gas emissions that arise from importing frozen Tilapia fish are significant. Stimulating the local production of fresh fish, especially by encouraging fishermen to transform to cage fish farming could thus have major positive impact to the environment.

core_fields.title: Scaling Climate-Smart Agroecology for Sustainable Nutrition in Rural Tanzania.
core_fields.description: The project Scaling Climate-Smart Agroecology for Sustainable Nutrition in Rural Tanzania introduces an innovative, community-driven model that combines agroecology, regenerative farming, and nutrition education to transform rural food systems. By empowering women and youth with climate-smart practices, local seed banks, and market access, it enhances nutrition, soil health, and resilience to climate shocks creating scalable pathways toward food security, sustainable livelihoods, and environmental regeneration.
core_fields.abstract: Rural Tanzania faces persistent food insecurity, malnutrition, and declining soil fertility caused by unsustainable farming practices and climate change. Smallholder farmers especially women and youth lack access to climate-resilient technologies, nutritious crops, and sustainable markets. Our innovation, Scaling Climate-Smart Agroecology for Sustainable Nutrition in Rural Tanzania, introduces a transformative, community-driven model that integrates agroecology, regenerative farming, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture to rebuild soil health, restore ecosystems, and improve dietary diversity. By combining scientific insights on soil microbiome restoration, traditional ecological knowledge, and climate-smart technologies (e.g., composting, intercropping, water harvesting, and local seed banks), the project creates low-cost, scalable solutions for sustainable food production. Through demonstration farms, farmer field schools, and digital extension tools, smallholders are trained to transition from chemical-dependent monocultures to regenerative practices that increase yields, sequester carbon, and enhance ecosystem services. Partnerships with local institutions, women s cooperatives, and youth-led enterprises ensure ownership, innovation, and equitable participation across the value chain. Immediate benefits include improved soil productivity, increased household nutrition, and income diversification through climate-resilient crops. Long-term, the innovation builds food sovereignty, climate resilience, and sustainable livelihoods for farming communities, while restoring degraded landscapes and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. This holistic, science-based approach directly addresses the urgent need for sustainable, nutritious, and climate-positive food systems, offering a replicable model for rural transformation across Sub-Saharan Africa.

core_fields.title: Biochar-to-Basket: Regenerative Kitchens for Food Security
core_fields.description: The Biochar-to-Basket project empowers women in Western Kenya to transform farm and household waste into biochar, a natural soil enhancer that regenerates degraded soils and boosts kitchen garden productivity. Through women-led cooperatives, the project promotes circular farming, improved household nutrition, and income generation. By turning waste into wealth, Biochar-to-Basket advances food security, climate resilience, and gender equity across five counties in Kenya.
core_fields.abstract: The Biochar-to-Basket project introduces an innovative, circular approach to food security by converting agricultural and household biomass waste into biochar a carbon-rich soil amendment that restores fertility, retains moisture, and enhances crop yields. In Western Kenya, most smallholder farmers struggle with nutrient-depleted soils, declining productivity, and food insecurity, while large amounts of farm residues are burned, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution. Our innovation solves this dual challenge of soil degradation and waste mismanagement through locally fabricated clean biochar kilns and women-led cooperatives trained in biochar production, application, and value addition. Farmers use biochar-enriched compost to regenerate kitchen and community gardens, while surplus produce is processed into nutrient-rich vegetable powders and flours for market sale, supporting household nutrition and income generation. The scientific foundation of biochar lies in its carbon sequestration and soil regeneration properties, validated globally for improving soil structure, microbial activity, and long-term fertility. By combining this proven science with community-driven enterprise, the project creates a regenerative food system that closes the loop from waste to soil to food to income. Immediate benefits include improved crop yields, reduced waste, and better nutrition for 3,000+ beneficiaries. Sustainable benefits include long-term soil restoration, reduced carbon emissions, women s economic empowerment, and enhanced community resilience to climate change. Biochar-to-Basket demonstrates how grassroots innovation and local knowledge, supported by simple technology, can regenerate both ecosystems and livelihoods.

core_fields.title: Seeds of Connection: A Global Indigenous Seed and Story Library
core_fields.description: Seeds of Connection is a global Indigenous-led initiative collecting 52 culturally significant seeds and their stories from communities worldwide. Through collaboration, documentation, and education, the project creates a digital and physical Seed Library linking nutrition, healing, and cultural knowledge. This living archive promotes food sovereignty, regenerative agriculture, and equitable access to ancestral seeds, fostering healthier and more sustainable food systems globally.
core_fields.abstract: Seeds of Connection addresses the loss of biodiversity, food sovereignty, and cultural knowledge resulting from industrial agriculture and climate change. Many Indigenous communities face the disappearance of ancestral seeds and traditional growing methods that once provided nutrition, healing, and ecological balance. Our innovation reconnects communities to their agricultural heritage by combining art, science, and storytelling to create a Global Living Seed Library. A traveling and digital archive that documents 52 seeds from Indigenous and local communities across continents. Each seed entry includes cultural narratives, ecological data, and regenerative cultivation methods, building an open-access digital platform ( Seedpedia ) for global education and exchange. By merging ethnobotany, digital archiving, and community participation, Seeds of Connection redefines how seeds are valued not just as crops but as vessels of history, identity, and health. The initiative empowers farmers, educators, and youth to grow nutrient-rich ancestral foods, reduces food waste through traditional sustainable practices, and encourages local adaptation to climate shifts. Immediate benefits include revitalized local food networks, improved nutrition, and strengthened community pride. Sustainable impacts include preserved biodiversity, intercultural knowledge sharing, and global partnerships advancing regenerative food systems.

core_fields.title: Smart Hydroponic Towers: Commercial Food Production and Community Empowerment
core_fields.description: EcoHarvest manufactures and deploys IoT-enabled hydroponic farming systems that enable commercial food production while empowering communities through technology access. Our smart towers grow fresh produce 10x faster using 95% less water than traditional farming, with zero pesticides and year-round production. The R500K investment will manufacture 15-20 systems for market expansion, hire critical technical staff, and develop advanced AI features creating sustainable revenue through food sales while democratizing access to urban farming technology.
core_fields.abstract: The Problem: Communities face intersecting crises: food insecurity, limited access to fresh produce in urban areas, educational gaps in STEM and sustainability, and climate change threatening traditional agriculture. Our Solution: EcoHarvest combines advanced hydroponic technology with IoT monitoring and AI optimization to create smart urban farms for commercial production and community deployment. Our systems feature real-time yield monitoring, adaptive resource management, and data-driven growing optimization. Technical Innovation: The breakthrough lies in making professional-grade controlled environment agriculture accessible and commercially viable. Our IoT sensors continuously monitor growth conditions, while AI algorithms adapt water, nutrients, and lighting based on plant needs maximizing efficiency and yield for both revenue generation and community empowerment. Immediate Benefits: Businesses/Institutions: Revenue from fresh produce sales, reduced procurement costs, local supply chains Communities: Access to smart farming technology, local food production capabilities, entrepreneurship opportunities Students/Users: Practical skills in agriculture technology, data science, and sustainability Consumers: Ultra-fresh produce with zero food miles, pesticide-free nutrition Environment: 95% water savings, zero pesticides, minimal carbon footprint Sustainable Impact: Our dual model creates financial sustainability through food sales while democratizing farming technology. Each tower becomes both a revenue generator and a tool for community empowerment, demonstrating scalable solutions to urban food security while building long-term economic and nutritional independence.

core_fields.title: Territorial Food Resilience Through Climate-Smart Savings Circles.
core_fields.description: This project strengthens food system resilience in vulnerable Mozambican communities through climate-smart savings circles. By integrating financial inclusion, regenerative practices, and youth-led innovation, it empowers local actors to access nutritious food, reduce waste, and build adaptive capacity. The model is scalable, community-driven, and aligned with SDGs, offering a transformative pathway for equitable and sustainable food systems rooted in territorial dignity.
core_fields.abstract: In Mozambique, climate shocks, food insecurity, and financial exclusion disproportionately affect rural and peri-urban communities. AAAJC s innovation addresses these challenges through climate-smart savings circles, locally organized groups that combine financial literacy, regenerative food practices, and youth-led planning. These circles serve as platforms for collective savings, micro-investment in food production, and participatory decision-making. The problem being solved is the fragmentation between financial access, food system resilience, and community agency. Traditional aid models often overlook the power of locally governed, low-cost mechanisms to build adaptive capacity. Our solution integrates social finance with agroecological principles and digital tools, enabling communities to co-design food strategies that are nutritious, sustainable, and trusted. Scientific and technical insights include behavioral economics (trust-based savings), agroecology (soil regeneration, waste reduction), and participatory planning. The model has been piloted in post-conflict and climate-vulnerable zones, showing early success in improving food access, reducing dependency, and fostering youth leadership. Immediate benefits include increased access to nutritious food, reduced food waste, and strengthened local economies. Sustainable benefits include enhanced climate resilience, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and scalable territorial governance. End users include women, youth, farmers, schools, and local producers. The model is designed to be replicable across low-income regions, offering a dignified pathway toward food system transformation.

core_fields.title: FoodSec-DSS (Decision Support System for Food Security)
core_fields.description: The research team leads an international simulator that supports food security policies in the face of climate risks, validated in over 3,000 localities across six Latin American countries. The proposal aims to strengthen its development through technological improvements, an MLN-based agent interface, primary data collection, creation of vulnerability indexes, and community participation. It integrates artificial intelligence, satellite data, and local evidence to support preventive public policies in vulnerable territories.
core_fields.abstract: In Latin America, over 186 million people experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2023, and 74% of countries are highly exposed to extreme climate events (FAO, 2024). This combination compromises access to safe and sufficient food, especially in rural and vulnerable communities. Our innovation consists of scaling and territorially validating a regional food security and climate risk simulator, which was recognized with the ALSEA World Vision 2024 award. The tool integrates artificial intelligence, remote sensing, and open data to anticipate scenarios at 10, 30, and 50 years, modeling impacts on health, water access, and nutrition. Its innovative nature lies in the integration of disciplines such as health, environment, nutrition, and data science; the use of APIs to incorporate real-time data; and the implementation of a virtual assistant based on Multimodal Language Models (MLN), which facilitates its use by public decision-makers and community stakeholders. Participatory validation in sentinel communities in Argentina, Paraguay, and Colombia will allow the models to be adapted to local contexts, increasing their social and territorial relevance, with potential scaling to Peru and Uruguay. Unlike other fragmented tools, this interoperable, predictive, and accessible platform informs public policies and their effects with up-to-date evidence. It strengthens preventive planning, resilience to food crises, and access to information for producers, teachers, consumers, governments, and civil society organizations. Its open architecture, together with data governance principles,FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and CARE (Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, Ethics) and territorial validation ensure regional scalability, legitimacy, and sustainability.

core_fields.title: Empowering Bakers and Nurturing Demand: Scaling Up Biofortified OFSP Bread to Improve Nutrition
core_fields.description: This project contributes to all three focus areas by reducing malnutrition and enhancing food systems in Nigeria, with lessons applicable worldwide. It enables bakeries to scale up the production of biofortified sweetpotato (OFSP) bread, a key innovation. OFSP bread is affordable and nutritious, increasing vitamin A consumption among vulnerable low-income households. Through targeted training for bakers, consumer education, and a rigorous impact evaluation, this initiative promotes sustainable agriculture, improved nutrition, and economic growth.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition affects millions of people globally, with disproportionate impacts on developing countries (FAO, 2023; Harttgen & Seiler, 2023). For example, nearly 48% of children under five in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) suffer from vitamin A deficiency, leading to increased risks of blindness, immune system deficiency, and mortality (Amare et al., 2023; Song et al., 2023). Biofortified crops, enhanced with nutrients through crossbreeding or genetic modification, offer a cost-effective solution to micronutrient deficiencies (Avnee et al., 2023). In particular, biofortified orange-fleshed sweetpotato (OFSP) is rich in beta-carotene, a precursor for vitamin A. Sweetpotato is a common crop in most of SSA, but OFSP production remains small despite large-scale adoption campaigns. In puree form, OFSP is a locally-produced and lower-cost substitute for wheat flour in bread, without requiring new baking equipment. Since bread holds a central dietary role in many African countries, OFSP bread could substantially increase year-round nutrition (Wanjuu et al., 2019); we document specific nutritional benefits below. While OFSP bread is a key innovation with the potential to make a huge impact on nutrition and to support food systems in SSA, two main challenges remain. First, most bakers are not aware of OFSP bread and need a short training course to add it to their product line. Second, few consumers are aware of OFSP bread, although many who try it prefer it to regular bread and are willing to pay more for it than for regular bread due to its nutritional benefits (Adesina et al., 2025).

core_fields.title: TAWIAFYA TRACK
core_fields.description: Traceability from farm to consumer that empowers informal vendors (mama mbogas), small holder farmers, and consumers building trust across the food value chain, whilst improving nutrition, and strengthening financial resilience.
core_fields.abstract: TawiAfya Track is a mobile farm to consumer traceability system that makes nutritious food safer, more transparent, and more trustworthy for Kenyan communities. Across Kenya, most food passes through informal, unregulated supply chains where origin, handling, and quality are unknown. This leads to food safety risks, nutritional loss, and low trust. Smallholder farmers and informal vendors (mama mbogas) who feed most households are excluded from digital systems, making them invisible and unable to prove product (food) quality. TawiAfya Track solves this by digitizing every step of the food value chain, thus from farm to consumer Farmers record harvest data, cooperatives and vendors log stock and movement, and consumers scan a QR code to see food origin, nutrition information, and safety history. The system uses simple mobile data, geolocation, and lightweight AI models to verify records, detect inconsistencies, and predict supply trends making traceability reliable and affordable. The solution emerged from the insight that traceability fails in Africa because existing systems ignore the informal market and mainly focus on commercial exports e.g. avocados being exported to the EU traced to ensure it meets EU standards. By designing around real user constraints: low technological literacy, low connectivity, and crowded workflows, TawiAfya Track becomes both practical and scalable. Benefits include: Safer, more transparent nutritious food for consumers. Higher trust and better income for farmers and vendors. Reduced food waste and improved planning for communities. Stronger resilience across local food systems. TawiAfya Track seeks to build trust, nutrition, and equity across the value chain.
