core_fields.title: Sustainable Palm Tree Cultivation for Economic Growth and Environmental Preservation in Abor
core_fields.description: This project focuses on sustainable palm tree cultivation in Abor, aiming to boost local incomes, create employment, and enhance environmental conservation. By introducing modern farming techniques, providing quality seedlings, and training farmers in best practices, the project seeks to increase palm yield and product quality. The initiative also emphasizes value addition, market access, and community engagement, ensuring long term economic growth, food security, and resilience against climate change impacts in the region.
core_fields.abstract: The Palm Tree Cultivation project in Abor introduces a modern, sustainable, and community driven approach to palm farming. Unlike traditional practices, this innovation integrates improved planting materials, optimized spacing, and climate smart agronomic techniques to maximize yield and ensure environmental sustainability. The project employs high quality, disease resistant seedlings, coupled with organic soil enhancement methods, reducing dependency on chemical fertilizers while maintaining soil fertility. Farmers are trained in modern palm management practices, including pest and disease monitoring, pruning, and efficient water use, fostering knowledge transfer and local capacity building. The project also incorporates value addition through processing palm products, such as oil and derivatives, enabling farmers to capture higher market value. By leveraging digital tools for farm mapping, yield tracking, and market information, the initiative ensures efficiency and transparency throughout the value chain. Community engagement is central to the project, with women and youth actively involved in cultivation, processing, and marketing activities, promoting inclusive economic growth. Furthermore, the project addresses climate change adaptation by planting palms in suitable agro ecological zones, enhancing carbon sequestration, and mitigating soil erosion. Overall, this innovation not only increases palm productivity and income for Abor farmers but also establishes a sustainable, scalable, and environmentally friendly model for rural agribusiness development in the region.

core_fields.title: The Jogja Regenerative Food Hub A Public-Private Engine for Nutrition-Sensitive Food Systems
core_fields.description: The Jogja Regenerative Food Hub, led by Inprosula in Indonesia, connects 500+ local farmers with the government free meal programs to provide nutritious food to children. This circular system also collects organic waste from the kitchens and returns it as compost to the farmers, closing the nutrient loop. The project strengthens local economies, improves nutrition, and creates a scalable, sustainable model for food security, funded by a USD 225,000 grant over 24 months.
core_fields.abstract: The Jogja Regenerative Food Hub addresses a critical disconnect: although smallholder farmers in Yogyakarta produce diverse, nutritious foods using agroecological practices, these foods rarely reach children and vulnerable households targeted by the national Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) and village Supplementary Feeding (PMT) programs. Instead, these programs often rely on long supply chains and low-quality ingredients, while farmers face unstable markets and cities depend heavily on imported food. The Hub introduces a novel integrated supply model that aligns production, distribution, and public nutrition programs. It aggregates produce from verified regenerative farmers, coordinates planting and pricing through farmer groups, and supplies SPPG-managed MBG meals and PMT rations directly. A solidarity-based food subscription market enables higher-income consumers to subsidize access for low-income families. The system closes the loop by composting kitchen food waste and returning it to farms, reducing fertilizer costs and emissions. While other farm-to-school or feeding initiatives exist, this solution is innovative in embedding itself into existing national public nutrition infrastructure, using guaranteed demand to scale regenerative agriculture. It draws on insights from Inprosula s decade-long collaboration with farmer cooperatives and community nutrition programs. Immediate benefits include stable income for farmers, reduced food costs for schools, fresher and more diverse meals for children, and reduced household vulnerability to price shocks. Sustainable benefits include improved soil health, lower carbon emissions, stronger local economies, and a replicable model for nutrition-sensitive, climate-resilient food systems across Indonesia.

core_fields.title: AgriPeace Idjwi: Climate-Smart Circular Agriculture for Food Security and Community Resilience
core_fields.description: AgriPeace Idjwi, led by PFUMVUDZA, delivers measurable impact on climate, sustainable development, and community resilience. Through climate-smart circular agriculture, composting, and solar cold chains, the project reduces greenhouse gas emissions, improves food security, and empowers women and youth with income opportunities. By turning organic waste into fertilizer and strengthening local markets, AgriPeace creates a scalable, resilient, and equitable model for sustainable food systems in Idjwi Island and beyond.
core_fields.abstract: AgriPeace Idjwi addresses critical challenges of food insecurity, climate degradation, and poverty on Idjwi Island, where communities often live under $1/day. Conventional farming practices and organic waste mismanagement contribute to soil depletion, methane emissions, and post-harvest losses, while women and youth lack access to sustainable income opportunities. Our innovation combines climate-smart circular agriculture, organic composting, and solar-powered cold chains to create a self-sustaining, regenerative food system. Organic waste and crop residues are converted into biofertilizers, reducing methane emissions and enhancing soil fertility. Solar cold chains minimize post-harvest losses and extend the availability of nutritious food. Training women and youth cooperatives in regenerative techniques ensures inclusive, community-led development. Scientific insights from agroecology and circular economy principles underpin our approach, linking waste management, sustainable production, and economic empowerment. By integrating local knowledge with evidence-based climate-smart practices, AgriPeace Idjwi delivers measurable environmental and socio-economic benefits. Immediate benefits include higher crop yields, reduced food loss, income generation for farmers, and improved nutrition for families. Long-term benefits include carbon emission reduction, resilient soils, empowered communities, and a scalable model for regenerative food systems across the Great Lakes region. AgriPeace Idjwi demonstrates that climate adaptation, food security, and economic empowerment can be achieved together, offering a blueprint for sustainable development and resilient, equitable food systems.

core_fields.title: Turn Waste into Proteins
core_fields.description: Global Cerah (GC) integrates organic waste management and production of alternative protein into a sustainable solution supported by IoT, which allows us to convert the waste from treatment into the final production of fertilizers and feed meals consistently and in high quality control. Application of IoT that connects all robotic process automation (RPAs) started from waste treatment till final production of alternative protein, whereas temperature sensors will control the heating processes in waste treatment.
core_fields.abstract: Our solution tackles the regional challenge of low waste-management awareness among farmers and weak regulatory enforcement by offering a cost-efficient, pollution-free alternative to landfilling and incineration. Farmers across Malaysia and Southeast Asia can collect their organic waste and deliver it to our processing site, where it is treated and upcycled. In return, GC provides subsidized, below-market-rate feed and fertilizer products, enabling farmers to adopt environmentally responsible practices while reducing their operational costs. Our AI-powered sorting system currently under development further increases recycling efficiency by minimizing contamination and maximizing the volume of recoverable materials. The proprietary processing system ensures total quality control from waste collection to final product output. With automated temperature monitoring, sensors, and integrated software, the system maintains ideal processing conditions and preserves up to 70% protein content without the use of chemicals. This automation reduces labor variability, cuts costs by up to 60%, and strengthens productivity through a connected supply chain that minimizes operational disruptions. By implementing this circular, regenerative model, GC significantly reduces methane emissions and environmental impact while improving climate resilience and food security. The system promotes local production of high-nutrition, chemical-free feed and fertilizers, supporting both sustainability goals and rising market demand for organic agricultural inputs. Our long-term vision is to replace landfills with a circular economy framework across Southeast Asia. GC aims to reach 8 million farmers in Malaysia and extend its impact to 50 million farmers region-wide, driving a transformative shift toward sustainable, regenerative agriculture.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Pigs Feed Supply to Improve Meat Quality, Quantity, and Affordability in Rwanda (EPFS-MQQA Project)
core_fields.description: The EPFS-MQQA Project addresses Rwanda's shortage of affordable, nutritious pig feed, which limits growth, carcass yield, and pork quality. As a national distributor and slaughterhouse operator, we aim to boost feed access through processing, farmer training, and partnerships. The project targets a 30% rise in feed availability, 25% reduction in feed costs, and 20% drop in pork prices, improving farmer incomes, household nutrition, and overall value chain sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description and Benefits The EPFS-MQQA Project introduces an innovative, locally driven solution to Rwanda's biggest challenge in the pig value chain: the lack of affordable, nutritious pig feed. This shortage slows animal growth, reduces carcass quality, and keeps pork prices high, limiting farmer profits and consumer access. The innovation combines scientific feed formulation, localized feed processing, and value-chain partnerships to transform how pig feed is produced and supplied in Rwanda. The core idea is to use locally available raw materials maize bran, soybeans, and agro-processing by-products supported by evidence-based nutritional research to produce balanced pig feed tailored to smallholder needs. This scientific insight ensures pigs grow faster, convert feed more efficiently, and produce better-quality meat. The solution is strengthened by technical training for farmers, modernized processing units, and an organized distribution network that brings consistent feed supply to rural communities. The problem is solved by increasing feed availability, lowering production costs through local sourcing, and ensuring farmers understand proper feeding practices. This integrated approach directly addresses production bottlenecks while improving coordination across cooperatives, feed producers, and slaughterhouses. Immediate benefits include lower feed costs, improved pig growth rates, increased farmer income, and more stable pork supply. Long-term and sustainable benefits extend to affordable meat for consumers, stronger rural livelihoods, improved household nutrition, job creation, reduced import reliance, and a more resilient livestock value chain. The project ultimately enhances food security and supports environmentally efficient production through optimal use of local resources.

core_fields.title: Deployment of automated solar micro milling machine for poultry feed production in Nigeria
core_fields.description: Our project provides an affordable, off-grid solution for small- and medium-scale poultry farmers in Nigeria. Powered entirely by solar energy, the system automates grain milling, improves feed quality, and reduces production costs. Designed for urban, rural and peri-urban communities, it enhances feed availability, supports year-round poultry production, and promotes clean, sustainable agricultural practices while boosting farmers income and resilience.
core_fields.abstract: The Automated Solar Micro Milling Machine is an off-grid, solar-powered technology designed to help poultry farmers in Nigeria produce high-quality feed at low cost. Many small- and medium-scale farmers struggle with rising feed prices, poor feed quality, unreliable electricity, and dependence on commercial mills located far from rural communities. These challenges reduce profitability, limit productivity, and threaten food security. This innovation addresses these problems by combining solar energy, automated milling, and locally adaptable engineering into a compact, affordable system. It uses photovoltaic panels to power a motorized milling unit, eliminating fuel expenses and ensuring uninterrupted operation even in areas without electricity. The automated controls allow consistent grain size, better nutrient retention, and improved feed hygiene. The solution emerged from practical field experience, engineering research, and insights gained from farmers who need a reliable, cost-saving alternative to diesel-powered or manual milling methods. Immediate Benefits Lower feed production costs for farmers Reliable milling in off-grid or electricity-poor areas Improved feed quality, leading to healthier and faster-growing birds Reduced reliance on commercial feed suppliers Time savings through automation Long-Term and Sustainable Benefits Higher farm productivity and household income Strengthened food security for communities and schools Environmental protection through clean, renewable solar energy Support for rural livelihoods and local poultry production Reduced carbon emissions and pollution from diesel generators In summary, this innovation empowers farmers, supports sustainable agriculture, and contributes to a more resilient food system in Nigeria.

core_fields.title: Farm Management System (FMS) database for compliance, traceability, and sustainability for Nigerian cocoa farmers.
core_fields.description: CocoaNexus is a digital traceability, compliance, and sustainability intelligence database designed to transform the cocoa sector in Nigeria and across West Africa. The platform tackles critical challenges, including fragmented supply chains, undocumented production, deforestation risks, weak farmer inclusion, and poor market access. CocoaNexus provides an integrated Farm Management System (FMS), digital farmer registry, farm mapping, supply chain traceability, ESG compliance monitoring, and a premium-market linkage engine. By enabling transparency and data-driven decision-making for partners.
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria s cocoa industry employs over 300,000 farmers across 800,000 hectares. It contributes significantly to export earnings, but remains largely undocumented, fragmented, and inefficient, with a lack of farm-level data for traceability records and compliance with global standards and the upcoming EU Deforestation Regulations. CocoaNexus digital infrastructure utilizes a Farm Management System (FMS) database to digitize and centralize farmers and farms, providing geospatial data and deforestation monitoring to ensure compliance with sustainability mandates and farm-level traceability for accessing deforestation-free beans and certification standards. Digitally profiling farmers, mapping farm boundaries, and recording production data, CocoaNexus will create an inclusive platform where farmers can own, access, and leverage their data. This data-driven approach empowers farmers to demonstrate the traceability, quality, and sustainability of their cocoa beans, making them more attractive to premium buyers who demand transparency and compliance with global regulations such as the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). In addition, production records and farm profiles become a form of digital collateral that can unlock access to credit, inputs, and financial services, enabling farmers to invest in productivity improvements. Our system is a digitally-driven, modular, and interoperable FMS for farmers to achieve regulatory compliance and generate real-time data analytics for partners, including cocoa bean exporters, processors, chocolate companies, governments, and NGOs, to make informed decisions on sustainable sourcing of high-quality beans and to provide targeted support programs. CocoaNexus has established a proprietary farm management system for farmer registration and has piloted it with over 1,000 farmers onboarded.

core_fields.title: Climate-resilient Livelihoods for Smallholder Farmers through Village Bank-in-a-Box model
core_fields.description: Our project scales climate-resilient livelihoods for smallholder farmers by combining regenerative agriculture, locally governed Village Banks, and inclusive climate-smart finance. Farmers, especially women and young people from rural farming communities and living on less than USD 2 a day, join Village Banks that provide inclusive, fair credit, savings, and micro-insurance linked to regenerative inputs and climate advisory. As trust and incomes grow, communities improve healthy diets, reduce environmental degradation, and build more resilient, opportunity-rich rural
core_fields.abstract: Village Bank-in-a-Box tackles the problems of climate shocks, low farm productivity, and exclusion from fair finance facing smallholder farmers living on less than two dollars a day, especially women and young people in Kenya. Because unstable rainfall, rising input prices, and predatory lenders lock farmers into low-risk, low-return decisions, households underinvest in diverse, nutritious crops and remain highly vulnerable to food price spikes and drought. Our innovation combines regenerative agriculture, climate-smart community finance, and digital rails into a single locally governed system. Farmers join Village Banks that use the Vermi-Farm Yetu Wallet to pool savings, access climate-linked microloans and parametric insurance, and purchase our organic fertilizers and DigiShamba greenhouse packages on flexible terms. By anchoring credit decisions in group records, agronomic performance, and local climate data, the model rewards climate-smart practices and reliable repayment rather than land titles or formal collateral most smallholders lack. This design builds on our previous work, where regenerative inputs and climate-controlled greenhouses helped 6,400 farmers increase yields up to sevenfold, cut water use by about seventy-eight percent, and reduce chemical input costs by forty percent while improving household incomes. These field results demonstrated that climate-resilient technologies only reach their full potential when bundled with fair, accessible, and trusted finance. Immediate benefits for end users include higher and more stable farm income, reduced crop losses, and improved access to diverse, nutritious food through increased local supply. Over time, communities strengthen soils, reduce waste, deepen financial inclusion, and build climate-resilient food systems replicable across Africa.

core_fields.title: Functional Indigenous Millet Milk: A Protein-Rich, Low-GI Dairy Replacement for the Global South
core_fields.description: Oatey is revolutionizing dairy replacement in the Global South by engineering a functional, indigenous Millet Milk. Our protein-enhanced, low-GI formula specifically addresses critical health crises from CMPA and colic in infants to diabetes and asthma management. Anchored in climate-smart Indian millets, we deliver a superior, sustainable metabolic fuel that offers a safe, nutritious, and affordable staple for millions of lactose-intolerant households.
core_fields.abstract: Oatey addresses the catastrophic failure of industrial dairy: a system that is environmentally destructive and biologically incompatible for millions, driving crises like Cow s Milk Protein Allergy (CMPA) in infants, colic, systemic inflammation (asthma), and diabetic glucose spikes. Our innovation is Functional Indigenous Millet Milk a low-GI, protein-enhanced dairy replacement engineered for the Global South. The Solution & Insight: While plant milks exist, most are nutritionally hollow or rely on water-intensive imports (almonds). We leveraged a scientific insight: Indian Millets are naturally hypoallergenic, drought-resistant, and low-GI, but historically lacked palatability as "milk." Oatey cracked the processing code to create a creamy, soluble millet milk that retains superior functional nutrition without the sugar spike or environmental cost of dairy. Immediate & Sustainable Benefits: Maternal & Infant Health: Provides a safe, hormone-free staple for breastfeeding mothers to eliminate CMPA triggers and colic in infants. Metabolic Safety: A functional, low-GI fuel critical for diabetic management and reducing inflammatory triggers for asthma patients. Planetary Regeneration: By shifting demand to millets (which use ~70% less water than dairy), we support climate-resilient farming while delivering affordable, high-protein nutrition to the community.

core_fields.title: Seed and input credit project
core_fields.description: We leverage an agent network and an AI credit scoring system to enable smallholder farmers access quality drought tolerant seeds and organic agro-inputs on credit without requiring collateral security. We equip every agent with a smartphone to enable tech penetration. Our platform also uses satelite images and geospatial analytics to monitor crop and soil health. It also has free trainings on climate smart practices and an online market place that connects farmers with buyers.
core_fields.abstract: Procurement of quality seeds and organic agro-inputs accounts for over 75% of the farmer production costs which is not affordable to smallholder farmers especially women and the youth who are financially excluded from the mainstream banking and lending due to lack of collateral security and no credit history. Money lenders charge exorbitant fees in form of interest rates and have very unfavourable terms of repayment. They end up planting poor quality seeds and using a lot of hazardous chemicals that not only reduce harvests but also degrade the soil hence worsening hunger and climate change with its associated impact. This reduces harvests by more than 60% and it explains why Africa annually imports more than USD 60B in food despite having more than 65% of the world s uncultivated arable land. We offer farmers unsecured credit in form of quality seeds and organic agro-inputs and allow them pay after harvest in form of produce. We use an AI credit scoring system leveraging farmer data, yield predictions and agent insights to determine the farmer credit worthiness. Our system also uses geospatial analytics and satelite images to monitor soil and crfrop health and offer instant alerts and recommendations. Farmers under our portfolio attest to a 2.5x increase in harvests due to quality seeds planted and access access to fair markets has caused an increase in household income. Our seeds help increase water retention and reduce the use of chemicals hence restoring soil health and fertility.

core_fields.title: Building Resilience by Promoting Agribusiness Through Sandbar Cropping for Displaced Communities in Bangladesh
core_fields.description: Transforming lands, transforming lives: The innovation comprises the demonstration and widespread adoption in two districts of North West Bangladesh of sandbar cropping , an innovative, simple, cost-effective technology which transforms silted barren lands created by flooding and, as a result, helps thousands of displaced, extreme-poor families surviving on the edge of mighty rivers to escape from extreme poverty, hunger; and climate change
core_fields.abstract: Our innovative agribusiness model enables low-cost access to land and water for erosion-affected poor households to cultivate pumpkin, squash, and other high-value vegetables/crops i.e., maize, sunflower, potatoes as safe food while generating reliable income. The model also expands access to finance and cost-efficient irrigation, promoting large-scale sandbar cropping through a woman- and youth-led agribusiness approach. This cuts labor and time by half, doubles productivity and profitability, and improves water-fuel efficiency through solar-based irrigation that reduces costs by 50%. Moderately graduated pumpkin producers, equipped with existing skills, partner with the company to attract commercial investment and shift from traditional charity-based support to a scalable, producer-driven commercial model. The approach is especially transformative as it utilizes climate-vulnerable degraded sandy lands for large-scale pumpkin and high-value crop production., enabling farmers to sell during lean seasons at higher prices and better cope with flooding. Their high vitamin A content products also helps prevent child blindness. Sandbar cropping has been practiced for over two decades, turning barren sandy chars into productive fields with pumpkins, squash, watermelon, and zucchini. The technique requires minimal irrigation as water table is so close on river basin. It is a transformative innovation, not only food security perspectives, but mitigating series of socio-economic, political, and environmental factors. Immediately, it is helping wide range of peoples from grassroots to national and international level to get access to income, employment, safe foods, nutrition and risk management solutions.

core_fields.title: Climate and Wellness Field Days for Youth Food System Innovation

core_fields.abstract: Our innovation strengthens youth food literacy by combining hands-on food system education, school gardens, and simple nutrition learning into a scalable model that supports healthier communities. Many young people lack understanding of how food is grown, what makes a diet nutritious, and how daily choices affect long-term health and the environment. Students learn composting, water-efficient irrigation, biodiversity-friendly planting, and basic crop management, paired with culturally relevant lessons that encourage balanced and responsible consumption. Immediate benefits include improved food knowledge, hands-on skills, and stronger engagement with healthy eating. Students gain confidence in preparing and choosing foods that support well-being. Over time, the program creates more resilient school and community food environments, encourages local food production, reduces waste, and nurtures a generation of conscious consumers who value sustainability, equity, and nutritious diets. By starting early with youth, the innovation builds long-lasting habits and contributes to a healthier, more sustainable food system for society.

core_fields.title: SEEDAR-AGRO: Seed Pelleting and Light Mechanization for Rainfed Cereals in Jordan
core_fields.description: SEEDAR-AGRO brings low-cost seed pelleting and light mechanized micro-catchments to rainfed cereal and forage systems in Jordan s climate-stressed highlands. The innovation boosts germination, early vigor and soil-water capture, reducing crop failures, farm costs and chronic feed shortages. In 24 months the project will field-test the technology, create locally sourced pelleting formulas and establish a community-run pelleting and mechanization service, building a replicable model for dryland resilience.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholders in Jordan s drylands face severe challenges: irregular rainfall, soil crusting and declining fertility drastically reduce germination and yields in rainfed crops. These stresses increase costs, cause feed shortages and heighten financial risks, pressures intensified by climate change. SEEDAR-AGRO offers a scalable, low-cost solution by integrating two complementary innovations into one operational package: 1. Seed Pelleting: Seeds are coated using affordable, locally sourced materials (clay, compost, biochar and binders) to create uniform, water-responsive pellets that improve seed soil contact, protect against early stress and enhance emergence. 2. Light Mechanized Micro-catchments: A modified auger creates low-cost soil depressions that increase water infiltration, boost soil moisture retention and reduce evaporative losses. The novelty of SEEDAR-AGRO is the integrated delivery of both technologies via a community-based service. Unlike unsustainable heavy-machinery or imported-input solutions, this package ensures that seed vigor improvements translate into higher yields by simultaneously improving soil moisture, stabilizing crop establishment, the most vulnerable phase of rainfed systems. Immediate and Lasting Benefits: Higher and more reliable yields with reduced need for re-seeding Lower production costs and better feed availability for herding families New income opportunities through community-run pelleting and mechanization services SEEDAR-AGRO strengthens local food security, supports climate-resilient farming and provides an affordable, replicable model for dryland regions globally.

core_fields.title: SnackOn: Safe and Nutritious Food for All
core_fields.description: Nepal's food system remains heavily import-dependent and nutritionally weak. Farmers lack training and incentives to cultivate high-value, climate-resilient crops such as peanuts. Meanwhile, consumers face rising micronutrient deficiencies, limited access to affordable protein, and a market saturated with about 80% imported processed foods. Similarly, 25-30% of fruits and vegetables are lost post-harvest due to inadequate processing and storage facilities, resulting in economic loss for farmers and reduced access to nutritious foods for consumers.
core_fields.abstract: SnackOn is building Nepal's first agriculture-to-nutrition value chain that links farmers, food processing, and women-led manufacturing. SnackOn began high quality nutritious peanut cultivation in Rautahat after winning the National Youth Agri Innovation Challenge organized by FAO and UNDP, which awarded us USD 1,000. We used this seed capital to launch a pilot peanut farm on 2 hectares of land by employing the marginalized Paswan community of Rautahat district. The pilot has been fully executed where we have had success in harvesting the peanuts and are currently undergoing post-harvest quality assessment. Peanuts are an ideal crop for Nepal for the following reasons: 1) are high-yield and climate-resilient 2) improve soil health (nitrogen-fixing) 3) require low irrigation and survive heat stress 4) provide farmers better income compared to low-value crops 5) reduce Nepal's heavy reliance on imported peanuts 6) directly enhance national nutrition as an affordable protein At, SnackOn, we already manufacture peanut butter and peanut-based snack bars, thereby, guaranteeing farmers a stable and predictable market, and reducing price uncertainty. To address the national problem of post-harvest losses, SnackOn has already procured heat pump dehydration, and other fruits and vegetables processing machines. Similarly, we have partnered with farms and farmers ranging from the Himalayas to the Terai belt that produce high quality fruits bypassing the middleman and tackling the problem head-on. This system helps: 1) stabilize farmers' income 2) extend shelf life by 12-18 months of local product and reduce food waste 3) Create affordable, nutrient dense local snacks.

core_fields.title: Mlimi Wabwino Otsogola: Integrated Agriculture, Nutrition and Food Systems for Vulnerable Households in Malawi.
core_fields.description: We will support 300 vulnerable women farmers in Zomba and Mangochi through the Mlimi Wabwino Otsogola package. This includes climate-smart home gardens, nutrition education, and simple technologies that reduce food waste. Our goal is to increase year-round food production, improve child nutrition, and support small village businesses. This integrated, low-cost model strengthens food systems while protecting the environment and can be replicated in other districts.
core_fields.abstract: The PROBLEM In Zomba and Mangochi, many households face seasonal hunger and poor diets. Most families depend on rain-fed maize, which fails under droughts and weak soils. Women struggle to provide nutritious food for young children, and up to 40% of vegetables and fruits are lost after harvest due to lack of storage or processing. This causes chronic malnutrition, low income, and unstable food systems. Our Innovation: We combine three proven but rarely integrated methods into one household-level solution for vulnerable women farmers: 1. Climate-Smart Home Gardens: Households will adopt drought-tolerant vegetable gardens, keyhole gardens, and simple rainwater harvesting. This allows through out the year production even with limited rainfall. 2. Nutrition and Food Preparation Training: Mothers learn to grow, prepare, and use diverse crops such as orange fleshed sweet potatoes, moringa, vegetables, and legumes. This directly improves child nutrition and dietary diversity. 3. Solar Food Drying to Reduce Waste: Women s groups receive solar dryers to preserve surplus produce. This reduces post-harvest losses and creates new income opportunities. WHY IT'S INNOVATIVE These methods exist separately, but combining them into a single, low cost package led by women is new in this region. It addresses the entire food cycle from production, to nutrition, to reducing food waste. The structure is simple, scalable, and uses local materials. BENEFITS Immediate benefits include more vegetables, better diets, and reduced food waste. Sustainable benefits include improved soil health, higher resilience to climate shocks, women s economic empowerment, and stronger local food systems.

core_fields.title: From Cashew Waste to Circular Power: Empowering Communities Through Sustainable Manufacturing
core_fields.description: We transforms wasted cashew apples into high-value products; nutrient-rich animal feed and clean, locally produced ethanol to strengthen Ghana s food system. By reducing food loss, advancing circular bio-innovation, and supporting smallholder farmers with fair market access, our solution boosts animal production, protects the environment, and expands affordable, healthy food availability for rural and urban communities whilst all the way expanding equitable economic opportunity for rural smallholder farmers.
core_fields.abstract: Every year, Ghana produces thousands of tonnes of cashew apples (240,000+MT - at 2023 count), but only the nut is harvested for commercial use, i.e. just 15% of the fruit. The remaining 85%, the cashew apple, is left to rot on farms or is dumped, releasing methane and causing environmental harm. At the same time, Ghana imports over 70 million litres of industrial ethanol annually for use in cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and industry, draining valuable foreign exchange and raising production costs. Our idea is simple but powerful: convert this overlooked fruit waste into ethanol and other valuable products through a low-cost, locally adapted manufacturing process. At OASAL Ltd, we have developed an integrated model that collects cashew apples from farms, processes them into fermentable juice, and uses microbial fermentation to produce ethanol. The leftover pulp is further broken down to make protein-rich feed for livestock and fish farming, closing the waste loop and increasing rural incomes. This idea addresses two critical global challenges; climate change and wasteful linear production models. By introducing a circular system that recovers energy and resources from agricultural waste, we contribute to climate action (SDG 13), affordable and clean energy (SDG 7), and responsible consumption and production (SDG 12). Moreover, we prioritize women's employment by training them to operate the first-stage machinery in our processing hubs, creating dignified jobs in underserved rural areas.

core_fields.title: Climate-Smart Input Finance and Microinsurance for Resilient Smallholder Farming
core_fields.description: Agpreneur gives farmers input loans, climate-indexed insurance, and direct access to buyers in one system. Farmers receive verified inputs on credit, automatic climate protection, and a guaranteed market at harvest. Our platform reduces loss, improves yields, and secures income for rural families. We already support 50,000 farmers and have unlocked three million dollars in input value with strong recovery outcomes during climate shocks.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers produce most of the food in Africa yet face rising climate losses, limited credit, poor information access, and unstable markets. These gaps reduce yields, weaken income, and limit food system resilience. Agpreneur solves this by delivering input finance, climate-indexed microinsurance, and market access through one digital platform. Farmers receive verified inputs on credit. Each loan comes with AgFlex, an index-based microinsurance that triggers payouts when rainfall, temperature, or flood thresholds are breached. Our climate engine uses satellite data, automated weather alerts, and historical risk models to remove manual claims and speed up recovery. Farmers receive SMS or chatbot guidance on planting, soil care, and local weather conditions. At harvest, the platform links them to industrial buyers, improving prices and reducing waste. This integrated approach addresses multiple pain points at once. Farmers protect their investment, increase productivity, and secure income. Cooperatives reduce default risk through bundled insurance. Buyers gain reliable supply. Communities reduce food losses and strengthen local markets. The environment benefits when farmers use inputs correctly and avoid repeated land clearing after failed seasons. The system already supports 50,000 farmers. It has unlocked three million dollars in input value, insured ten thousand farmers, and delivered strong recovery outcomes after extreme weather events. The innovation brings financial stability, faster climate adaptation, and a clear path to stronger food security.

core_fields.title: MycoSMART: Portable, Affordable Fluorescent Microarray Strip for Detection of Mycotoxins for Safer, Sustainable Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project scales and validates MycoSMART, an affordable, portable device for rapid, multiplex mycotoxin detection in food commodities. By deploying prototypes and conducting train-the-trainer" programs in Ghana, Indonesia, and Thailand, the project strengthens local capacity for on-site testing and data-driven prevention. Field validation will enhance food safety, reduce postharvest losses, and empower communities with accessible, reliable screening. MycoSMART supports safer, more nutritious, and more equitable food systems in low-resource settings.
core_fields.abstract: MycoSMART is an affordable, portable, and field-deployable diagnostic system that enables simultaneous detection of five key regulated mycotoxins: major drivers of food contamination, economic losses, and chronic illness across the Global South. Mycotoxins threaten food safety and nutrition, particularly for smallholder farmers and low-income consumers who rely on rice, maize, wheat, nuts, and other highly susceptible staples. Existing laboratory-based detection is costly, slow, and inaccessible in rural areas, leading to delayed risk management and ongoing exposure. MycoSMART addresses this gap by integrating multiple proven scientific innovations into a single scalable platform. It combines: - Microarray technology for accurate, low-reagent, multiplex detection; - Lateral-flow principles for simple, field-ready operation; - High-affinity monoclonal antibodies for specificity across mycotoxins; - A novel, low-cost fluorescent dye delivering stable, sensitive signals in high heat and humidity; - A portable optical reader designed for rugged field conditions; - A green, rapid sample-prep method safe for non-specialists. These components allow real-time testing in under 20 minutes, enabling farmers, processors, schools, and cooperatives to act before contaminated food enters the supply chain. The benefits are immediate and lasting. MycoSMART increases food safety, prevents postharvest losses, and strengthens sustainable value chains by reducing spoilage and rejected shipments. Its low cost and usability ensure equitable access. Through train-the-trainer programs in Ghana, Indonesia, and Thailand, the project will build local capacity, accelerate adoption, and ensure long-term community ownership. By enabling early detection and informed decision-making, MycoSMART supports safer, more resilient, and more trusted food systems.

core_fields.title: Radiant Green Kitchens: Solar- Powered Food Processing and Women Nutrition Innovation Hub
core_fields.description: Radiant Green Kitchens is a women-led initiative that uses solar-powered food processing to improve nutrition, reduce post-harvest losses, and create income opportunities for vulnerable women in Chuka, Kenya. The project equips women with training, technology, and a community hub where they can safely process, preserve, and package nutritious foods using clean energy. This innovation strengthens food security, supports climate resilience, and empowers women to lead sustainable, market-ready food enterprises.
core_fields.abstract: Radiant Green Kitchens introduces a solar-powered food processing and nutrition innovation hub designed for women in Chuka informal settlements, where food insecurity, malnutrition, and post-harvest losses remain severe. Many low-income families rely on nutrient-poor diets and lack affordable, safe methods to preserve food. Farmers also lose up to 55% of produce due to inadequate storage and processing options. This project solves these challenges by integrating solar dehydration, solar cold storage, energy-efficient milling, and nutrition-focused product development into one accessible, women-led hub. The innovation is rooted in proven scientific insights: solar drying and solar cooling reduce microbial spoilage, extend shelf life, retain nutrients, and significantly lower food waste without reliance on electricity or harmful fuels. Women will receive technical skills in clean-energy food processing, hygienic handling, packaging, product branding, and market linkages. They will create nutritious, shelf-stable foods such as dried vegetables, fruit snacks, fortified flours, and herbal tea products that are healthier, affordable, and in growing demand. Immediate benefits include improved household nutrition, reduced food waste, increased income for women, and accessible clean-energy processing for farmers and schools. Long-term benefits include stronger climate resilience, sustainable livelihoods, a local supply of affordable nutritious foods, and a replicable model for women-led green food enterprises across rural Kenya. Radiant Green Kitchens transforms vulnerable women into clean-energy innovators, food producers, and nutrition champions - advancing both community wellbeing and sustainable food systems.

core_fields.title: Seed-to-Food Innovation: Climate-Enhanced Cowpea for Nutritious Diets and Regenerative Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project delivers a seed-to-food innovation that integrates climate-enhanced cowpea seed technology, regenerative production systems, and consumer-validated food products to strengthen nutritious diets and sustainable food systems in Southern Africa. Using non-thermal plasma and bio-coated seeds, the project improves crop establishment, resilience, and yields in marginal environments while reducing fertiliser dependence. Community-based processing and ready-to-use cowpea foods ensure affordability, acceptability, and scalable nutrition impact.
core_fields.abstract: The problem Food systems in Southern Africa are constrained by protein-poor cereal diets, declining soil fertility, and climate stress. Although cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is a nutrient-dense, drought-tolerant, nitrogen-fixing crop, it remains underutilised due to weak seed quality, poor crop establishment in marginal soils, limited processing, and low consumer uptake. The innovation This project introduces a seed-to-food innovation that unlocks cowpea s full potential by integrating climate-enhanced seed technology, regenerative production, and food-ready product design. At the core is a non-thermal plasma and biodegradable bio-coating seed treatment, a chemical-free technology shown to improve germination, early vigour, drought tolerance, and nutrient-use efficiency. This ensures reliable yields from the seed stage, the most critical failure point for smallholders. How it works Plasma treatment modifies seed surface chemistry and activates metabolic pathways that enhance stress resilience, while bio-coatings improve water and nutrient uptake. These enhanced seeds are deployed within regenerative cowpea systems that restore soil nitrogen and reduce fertiliser dependence. Downstream, cowpea is processed into consumer-validated, ready-to-use foods, removing convenience and acceptability barriers that limit dietary adoption. Why it matters The innovation delivers immediate benefits, higher and more stable yields, affordable protein-rich foods, and reduced input costs, while generating long-term gains in soil health, climate resilience, and sustainable nutrition. Designed for community ownership and scalability, the model offers a practical pathway to healthier diets and regenerative food systems within planetary boundaries.

core_fields.title: Satellite powered and AI Analytics Farm Insight to Accelerate Climate Smart Agriculture and Sustainability
core_fields.description: Rada 360 leverages satellite imagery and AI to give farmers real time crop health monitoring, precise weather intelligence, and actionable insights for climate-smart decision making. The platform guides farmers on optimal spraying and fertilizer timing, provides fertilizer recommendation maps to reduce emissions, and delivers soil classification to prevent degradation through better land-use planning. With accurate yield predictions, farmers optimize resources, minimize losses, and sustainably increase productivity while protecting the environment.
core_fields.abstract: Farmers across Africa face mounting challenges from climate change, soil degradation, unpredictable rainfall, and rising production costs. Limited access to real-time agronomic intelligence forces farmers to rely on guesswork when applying fertilizers, spraying chemicals, or planning irrigation leading to preventable crop losses, inefficient input use, and environmental harm. This reinforces unsustainable farming practices and threatens long-term food security. Rada 360 introduces a satellite-powered, AI-driven platform called Rada space designed to accelerate climate-smart and regenerative agriculture at scale. By integrating multispectral satellite data, vegetation indices, soil models, and localized weather intelligence, the platform delivers actionable insights including remote crop health monitoring, Crop moisture status, fertilizer recommendation maps, soil classification, optimal spraying, fertilizer timing, and accurate yield predictions and Agronomic advice to farmers through Chatbot available in platform . These insights empower farmers to minimize input misuse, prevent land degradation, and make informed, climate-resilient decisions. This innovation is grounded in remote sensing science, geospatial analytics, and predictive modeling calibrated for East African agro-ecological conditions. Unlike drones or manual scouting, Rada 360 provides continuous, affordable monitoring across thousands of hectares making high-quality digital agriculture accessible to farmers and Agri-institutions. Immediate benefits include reduced production costs, lower fertilizer-related emissions, improved yield consistency, and reduced climate vulnerability. Farmers gain the ability to apply inputs precisely, protect soil health, and optimize productivity on existing farmland. In the long term, the platform promotes sustainable intensification, strengthens community food systems, and keeps agriculture within planetary boundaries by reducing environmental pressure and enabling regenerative land management at scale.

core_fields.title: Scaling Smart Pond from MVP to Industrial Standard V2 for Commercial Rollout Pilot
core_fields.description: This project advances Smart Pond from MVP to a fully engineered, industrial standard V2 device ready for commercial rollout pilot. core_fields.abstract: Smart Pond is an intelligent aquaculture management device designed to give fish farmers simple, science based control over pond conditions. The innovation addresses a major challenge in African aquaculture: farmers rely on intuition to manage feeding and water quality, which leads to high mortality, wasted feed, inconsistent yields, and unpredictable income. These problems persist because most farms lack affordable, reliable, context appropriate monitoring tools. Smart Pond solves this by combining water quality sensors, a solar powered IoT device, and an AI model that interprets real time pond data and sends clear, actionable instructions to the farmer. Instead of reading complex metrics, farmers receive simple prompts such as when to feed or when to improve aeration. This ensures stable pond environments, better feed conversion, and healthier fish. The solution is informed by years of hands-on aquaculture work and analysis of biological stress patterns. Field observations revealed consistent relationships between dissolved oxygen fluctuations, temperature shifts, feeding behavior, and fish stress. Smart Pond captures these variables continuously, processes them through our AI engine, and translates them into practical guidance that a farmer can apply immediately. The immediate benefits include reduced fish mortality, higher survival rates, lower operational costs, stable feeding practices, and more predictable harvest cycles. Sustainable long-term benefits include improved water stewardship, stronger farm profitability, expanded local fish supply, and greater resilience to climate related fluctuations. Smart Pond empowers farmers with accessible precision aquaculture, strengthening food production systems while reducing waste and environmental impact across farming communities.

core_fields.title: Climate-Positive Dairy: Producing More Milk and Meat With Lower Methane Emissions and Higher Farmer Income
core_fields.description: We are transforming dairy and meat production by enabling farmers to produce more nutritious milk and meat with significantly lower methane emissions intensity. Using AI, IoT sensors, digital MRV, & scientifically validated feed interventions, we reduce methane emissions by 30% and improve productivity 25 35%, lowering emissions/ litre of milk & per kilogram of meat by 40 50%. The project delivers higher farmer income, climate-positive protein, and improved food and nutrition security for millions of smallholder households.
core_fields.abstract: Global dairy and meat systems are trapped in a cycle of very low productivity and extremely high methane emissions, especially across smallholder farming communities that produce over 70% of milk in emerging regions. Livestock emit methane continuously during digestion, and when nutrition, fertility, and animal health are poorly managed, productivity declines while methane emissions rise sharply. Without tools for heat detection, early disease diagnosis, feed optimization, or methane tracking, animals take longer to grow, produce less milk, and emit far more methane per unit of output. Methane remains invisible, unmeasured, and unmanaged, resulting in 40 60% higher emissions intensity per litre of milk and per kilogram of meat compared to optimized systems. Farmers do not benefit financially from reducing emissions, as MRV is expensive, inaccessible, and carbon markets exclude them, limiting climate action, resilience, and food security. The Solution: eVerse.AI solves this entire chain of problems end-to-end through an integrated AI + IoT + feed science + digital MRV platform that reduces methane emissions while improving milk and meat production efficiency. ConnectedCow integrates IoT sensors, AI heat and health detection, biometric identification, and a SaaS dashboard to improve productivity, fertility, and herd health. GreenCow deploys patented methane sensors, scientifically validated feed interventions, and a Verra-ready digital MRV system to achieve 30% methane reduction and unlock high-quality carbon credits. CowGPT provides real-time AI-based advisory for nutrition, disease prevention, heat cycle optimization, and milk yield. MethaneGPT offers precision methane intelligence and carbon-credit optimization guidance.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Postharvest Hubs for Nutritious Small Fish in Coastal Kenya
core_fields.description: We will co-design and scale solar-powered postharvest hubs for small pelagic fish in coastal Kenya. Each hub integrates solar blanching, hygienic solar drying and solar direct-drive cold storage with food-safety protocols and gender-responsive business models. In partnership with Coastal and Marine Resource Development (COMRED) and Beach Management Units, the project will cut postharvest losses, improve food safety and affordability, and create viable women- and youth-led enterprises that supply nutritious fish to coastal and inland areas.
core_fields.abstract: Coastal Kenya depends heavily on small pelagic fish such as dagaa and anchovies for affordable nutrition, yet these value chains experience 20 40% postharvest losses due to contamination, slow and uneven open-air drying, and lack of cold storage. Women processors, who dominate this segment, rely on sand drying (spreading fish directly on sand, soil or cement) and firewood blanching (boiling over open fires). These practices expose fish to microbes and dirt, produce inconsistent quality, contribute to deforestation, and limit access to higher-value markets in Mombasa and Nairobi. Our solution is a solar-powered postharvest hub that integrates three climate-smart technologies: (1) solar steam blanching, delivering controlled, clean heat for rapid microbial reduction; (2) hybrid solar dryers, which eliminate sand contamination and accelerate drying by 40 60%; and (3) solar direct-drive ice machines and chilled display units enabling short-term storage, value addition and premium sales. A key innovation is the partnership with CompWiz, a Kenyan digital firm, to develop traceability and digital quality logs. This provides batch-level data on blanching temperatures, drying conditions and contamination control, creating safer, standardised and trusted products that meet the requirements of traders, retailers and institutional buyers. Benefits include lower losses, safer food, reduced fuelwood use, stronger climate resilience, and increased, more stable incomes for women and youth processors. The hubs are designed for scalable adoption across Kilifi and Kwale Counties. The model builds on engineering insights and field pilots under the Asia Africa BlueTech Superhighway and COMRED s longstanding work with coastal communities.

By embedding education, production, and distribution into a single coordinated model, the project provides a sustainable, high-impact solution that aligns with national nutrition priorities while advancing global commitment to community health and food security.

core_fields.abstract: Pakistan s rapid urbanization is squeezing farmland and leaving millions of vulnerable families without access to land, causing food insecurity especially among the most marginalized such as women headed, transgender, persons with disabilities and minority families. Many of these households carry valuable farming experience, yet due to lack of access in crowded cities, their skills remain unused. The 2025 cloudburst triggered flashflood in urban areas of Mingora Swat, further worsened food insecurity, market dependence, and livelihood loss. Our innovation introduces hydroponic farming which is a soilless, vertical system that grows vegetables using nutrient-enriched water or mist. This method saves upto 90% water compared to conventional agriculture, eliminates the need for fertile soil, can be deployed in constrained urban spaces such as rooftops, courtyards, and community centers. Building on the locally adapted prototypes developed and validated by the Agricultural Research Institute (ARI) Swat, the technology is proven and climate-appropriate. What remains is bridging the gap between this proven innovation and community-level adoption. The project focuses on delivering access, practical skills, and livelihood integration thereby transforming hydroponics from a technical solution into a scalable, income-generating opportunity for the marginalized urban households. Households (100) gain year-round production of fresh, nutritious food, reducing expenses and creating micro-enterprise opportunities. Communities (125 trained farmers) and one higher secondary school students (500) benefit from demonstration hubs while enabling wider adoption through 05 field days. Environmentally, the system conserves water, prevents soil degradation, and shortens supply chains, thereby building a more resilient, equitable urban food future.

core_fields.title: Harvest for Humanity: Sustainable Venison for Vulnerable Communities
core_fields.description: Harvest 4 Humanity (H4H) addresses food insecurity and ecological damage by transforming an invasive species challenge into a nutritional solution. Led by Charles Sturt University s Gulbali Institute and partners, H4H ethically harvests wild deer, redirecting premium venison into accredited food relief supply chains. This pilot builds hunter capacity, streamlines processing and distribution, and educates communities on venison s benefits. Outcomes include reduced food insecurity, restored landscapes, and scalable model aligning with national biodiversity and wellbeing priorities.
core_fields.abstract: Food insecurity affects thousands of Australians, driven by financial hardship, isolation, and systemic disadvantage. Protein, essential for health and development, is the hardest nutrient for food relief agencies to source due to cost and scarcity. Meanwhile, wild deer, an invasive species causing severe ecological and agricultural damage, are culled annually, wasting tonnes of premium meat protein. Harvest 4 Humanity (H4H), led by Charles Sturt University s Gulbali Institute and a consortium of industry and community partners, transforms this challenge into a novel solution, a first of its kind in Australia. By ethically harvesting wild deer and redirecting venison into accredited food relief supply chains, we deliver affordable, safe, and culturally appropriate protein to vulnerable communities while restoring ecosystems and improving farm productivity. This pilot will upskill hunters to meet food safety standards, enabling surplus venison donations. It will streamline processing, storage, and distribution, educate food relief networks on venison s nutritional benefits, and build capacity for sustainable protein sourcing. Outcomes include measurable reductions in food insecurity, improved landscape productivity, and strengthened rural resilience. Our strategy aligns with national priorities for biodiversity and community wellbeing. With strong governance, sector partnerships, and adaptive leadership, H4H offers a scalable model that integrates environmental management with social impact. By leveraging existing resources and collaborative networks, we ensure sustainability and efficiency. This project delivers long-term impact, contributing to healthier communities and networks, restored landscapes, and a replicable framework for turning ecological threats into nutritional opportunities.

core_fields.title: Resilient Harvest Initiative
core_fields.description: The Resilient Harvest Initiative expands GGEM s partner network from 13 to 30 organisations to help climate vulnerable households shift from maize to resilient, nutritious, income generating crops. GGEM will supply climate smart seeds, provide standardised training, support adaptive farming methods, and collect unified data nationwide. Farmers will grow drought tolerant crops, improve household nutrition, and sell surplus harvests back to GGEM, creating a cost effective, sustainable pathway to food security.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation addresses a central challenge in Malawi: rising climate shocks are undermining food security, yet most households depend on maize a crop that fails rapidly under drought and erratic rainfall. This results in recurring hunger, high relief costs, and unstable food systems. The Resilient Harvest Initiative enables households to shift from maize to drought-tolerant, nutritious, income-generating crops such as sorghum, millet, legumes, and sunflower. The model integrates three components not previously combined at national scale: Affordable resilient seed kits produced through GGEM s Resiliency Development Hub; A coordinated network of 30 NGOs and CBOs that distribute seed, support farmers, and collect unified data; A guaranteed market where GGEM buys back surplus crops, reducing risk and encouraging adoption. This approach transforms a traditional food-aid network into a climate-adaptation mechanism. Instead of distributing costly food parcels after a crisis, partners now supply low-cost seed kits before shocks occur, enabling households to produce their own food. This is 14 times more cost-effective than food relief. Few seed-distribution programs integrate resilient seed supply, partner training, regenerative farming practices, consolidated data, and a guaranteed buyer. Early-maturing, drought-tolerant cultivars grown using micro-dosing, 52-line spacing, and regenerative soil methods consistently outperform maize. Benefits include improved household food availability, diverse diets, higher farmer income, reduced reliance on food aid, stronger seed banks, healthier soils, and a more climate-resilient national food system.

core_fields.title: From Sea to Soil: Upcycling Invasive Seaweed for Regenerative Agriculture
core_fields.description: From Sea to Soil transforms invasive sargassum seaweed that damages coastlines into organic certified agricultural inputs that regenerate soils and strengthen food production. Working with coastal fishing communities, we harvest the seaweed through our patented technology, prevent environmental harm, and upcycle the biomass into biostimulants and soil amendments used by farmers to improve crop resilience and reduce reliance on synthetic inputs. With this circular model we restore marine ecosystems while supporting sustainable, climate-positive agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: Coastal regions across the Global South are increasingly affected by massive sargassum blooms that damage ecosystems, disrupt fisheries, reduce tourism income, and create disposal problems once the seaweed reaches shore. At the same time, farmers face rising costs, soil degradation, and limited access to regenerative agricultural inputs. Our innovation connects these two challenges through a circular solution where we upcycle invasive sargassum into products for agriculture. Working with local fishing communities, we collect excess seaweed before it decomposes on beaches. Through low-impact bioprocessing, the biomass is transformed into bio-based biostimulants and soil amendments that improve soil health, boost crop resilience to stress, increases yield and reduce dependence on synthetic fertilizers. Sargassum naturally contains plant-beneficial compounds such as polysaccharides, polyphenols and other bioactive molecules that stimulate root growth, metabolic performance and microbiome activity when properly processed. Our formulations convert this untapped resource into stable, effective farm inputs aligned with regenerative practices. Immediate benefits for farmers include improved yields, healthier soils, and access to affordable, sustainable products. Communities gain cleaner coastlines and new livelihood opportunities through seaweed collection and processing. Environmentally, the model reduces coastal methane emissions, supports ocean restoration, minimizes agricultural runoff, and strengthens climate-positive food production systems creating tangible impact from sea to soil.

core_fields.title: Food Recovery System through Innovative Food-Waste Processing
core_fields.description: Our project establishes an innovative food-waste processing system that collects leftover food from schools, prisons, refugee camps, hospitals, and butcheries, and safely transforms it into clean, affordable livestock feed. Using solar-powered drying, sterilization, and circular processing, the initiative reduces environmental and health risks, strengthens climate resilience, lowers feed costs for farmers, and creates sustainable livelihoods for vulnerable communities across East Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation introduces a Food Recovery System that uses advanced yet low-cost food-waste processing technologies to convert institutional leftovers into clean, safe, and affordable livestock feed. Across East Africa, schools, prisons, refugee camps, hospitals, and butcheries generate large volumes of organic waste. When unmanaged, this waste attracts disease-causing vectors, contributes to environmental pollution, and increases methane emissions while farmers face rising feed prices that undermine food security and income generation. In East Africa, particularly in Rwanda, our solution tackles both challenges by transforming waste into value. We use solar-powered drying units, high-heat sterilization, nutrient balancing, and pelletizing technologies to process collected leftovers into clean, standardized feed. A small quality assurance station checks moisture levels, eliminates pathogens, and ensures each batch meets safe nutritional standards. This combination of renewable-energy technology, food-safety science, circular processing, and mobile modular design makes the system both highly practical and scalable for low-income communities. The scientific basis for this model is well established: research shows that controlled dehydration, proper heat treatment, and nutrient profiling can safely convert cooked food into livestock feed while eliminating biological contamination risks. By applying circular-economy principles, no material is wasted bones become calcium supplements, vegetable residues become organic compost, and waste oils can be repurposed into biofuel inputs. This creates a zero-waste system that protects the environment, lowers feed costs, and improves community health.

core_fields.title: Empowering Rural Women Through Sustainable Poultry and Agro-Ecological Farming
core_fields.description: This project empowers rural women by providing broiler chickens on credit and access to land within our coffee farm to grow legumes for food and income. Using agro-ecological methods, the farm recycles waste to improve soil health and reduce costs. The project strengthens women s economic independence, enhances household nutrition, and promotes sustainable farming practices that build resilient, violence-free communities.
core_fields.abstract: he project introduces an innovative, integrated agro-ecological poultry model that simultaneously strengthens women s incomes, improves food security, and regenerates the environment. Rural women often lack access to credit, land, and reliable income sources, limiting their ability to support their families and increasing vulnerability to domestic conflict. At the same time, conventional poultry farming generates significant waste, raises production costs, and degrades soil fertility. Our solution combines credit-based poultry distribution, shared land access, and waste-to-fertilizer recycling. Women receive broiler chickens on credit, enabling them to start earning immediately without upfront capital removing the biggest barrier to entrepreneurship. They also gain access to land within our 15-acre coffee farm where they plant legumes, providing food, income, and natural soil enrichment through nitrogen fixation. This integrated system is guided by agro-ecological science, which demonstrates that linking livestock with crop production reduces waste, improves nutrient cycles, and increases overall farm productivity. By converting poultry waste into organic fertilizer, the farm reduces environmental pollution, cuts input costs, and improves soil health for both coffee and legumes. This approach creates a circular economy where every output becomes a resource. Immediate benefits include increased income for women, improved household nutrition, and access to affordable poultry meat in local markets. Sustainable long-term benefits include stronger women-led enterprises, healthier soils, reduced dependency on chemical fertilizers, increased climate resilience, and more peaceful households due to reduced economic stress. This innovation demonstrates how ecological farming and gender empowerment can work together to create lasting social and environmental impact.

core_fields.title: Farm Forward: Soil Health as the Foundation of Food Security
core_fields.description: This project will establish a regenerative agriculture training hub at the Abel Center in Bassam. Using simple, low-cost, nature-based technologies including composting, biofertilizers, and small integrated insect (black soldier fly)-poultry-vegetable systems we will train women and youth to produce nutritious food while restoring degraded soils. Participants will gain practical skills, starter tools, and ongoing coaching to build sustainable livelihoods and strengthen local food security through circular, climate-resilient practices.
core_fields.abstract: Across C te d Ivoire, communities struggle with declining soil fertility, costly chemical inputs, and limited access to nutritious food. In Bassam, these challenges affect women and youth that rely on depleted land and unstable markets. Traditional training programs often overlook practical, low-cost solutions that communities can manage independently. Our innovation combines soil regeneration, organic waste transformation, and integrated micro-farms into a single, easy-to-learn training model. Using scientific insights from agroecology, circular economy principles, and black soldier fly (BSF) biology, we convert local organic waste into high-value inputs: biofertilizers rich in microorganisms and insect protein for poultry. These inputs regenerate soils, boost crop yields, and reduce dependence on expensive chemical fertilizers. At the Abel Center, trainees learn through hands-on practice how to: - Produce compost, biofertilizers, and BSF-based soil amendments; - Manage small integrated farms combining insects, poultry, and vegetables; - Improve soil structure, water retention, and biodiversity using regenerative methods; - Generate income through surplus vegetables, eggs, or natural inputs. This approach is inspired by natural decomposition systems and backed by global research demonstrating the efficacy of organic amendments and circular nutrient flows. It is low-cost, locally sourced, and suitable for small land areas making it ideal for vulnerable communities. Immediate benefits include improved soil fertility, lower production costs, access to fresh food, and new skills. Long-term benefits include stronger food security, new livelihood opportunities, reduced waste pollution, and climate-resilient local food systems that communities can maintain and scale autonomously.

core_fields.title: Social Capital Credits (SoCCs) for Nutritious and Equitable Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project combines organic climate-smart kitchen gardens with our innovative Social Capital Credits (SoCCs) system to tackle micronutrient malnutrition among women and children in remote parts of India. Women earn SoCCs for growing indigenous vegetables, composting, mentoring peers, and making bird perches for improving biodiversity. SoCCs are redeemed for gardening tools and training. Women also sell excess produce. This model improves nutrition, boosts incomes, drives regenerative and community-led sustainable food production, while improving soil health.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses one of India s most persistent but overlooked challenges: micronutrient malnutrition among poor women and children, especially in the drought-affected state of Rajasthan. Although India is the world s second-largest food producer, it also has the second-largest undernourished population estimated at 195.9 million. Nearly 50% of Indian women are anemic, and 1 in 3 children are malnourished, largely due to diets dominated by rice, wheat, and lentils with limited access to vegetables, fruits, and protein. This problem is especially acute in rural and tribal regions of Rajasthan, where local norms prioritize men s food intake and poverty restricts dietary diversity. These deficiencies cause low birth weight, stunting, impaired cognitive development, and intergenerational poverty. Our solution of Social Capital Credits (SoCCs) powered Backyard Kitchen Gardens is simple and transformative. We support under-resourced women to grow diverse, nutrient-rich vegetables and fruits at home while earning SoCCs for climate-smart cultivation, water conservation, composting, and peer mentoring. These credits can be redeemed for agricultural tools, organic inputs, seed banks, connections to markets or micro-enterprise support. This approach not only increases household nutrition but also builds women s leadership and income. What makes this innovation novel is the addition of sustainability aspects to the traditional practice (kitchen gardens) with a behavioral, tech-enabled incentive system (SoCCs). The SoCCs App automates tracking of earned/redeemed credits, creating transparency and enabling scale across partners. Women s families reduce vegetable expenses by 50-70%, earning supplemental income from low-cost food production and sales, and improving household diets dramatically.

core_fields.title: Climate-Smart Greenhouses and Fortified Diets for Food Security in MMC Borno
core_fields.description: In conflict-affected MMC Borno, our project introduces climate-smart greenhouses and fortified local diets to improve food security. By 2026, we aim to reduce child wasting by 15%, increase household access to fresh vegetables by 40%, and cut post-harvest losses by 30%. At least 200 women and youth will gain livelihoods through micro-factories and greenhouse cooperatives. This scalable model strengthens nutrition, sustainability, and resilience, offering replication potential across fragile regions globally.
core_fields.abstract: In Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC), Borno State, conflict and displacement have left families struggling with malnutrition, food insecurity, and limited access to fresh produce. Traditional farming is highly vulnerable to drought, heat, and insecurity, while diets often lack essential nutrients. Our innovation integrates climate-smart greenhouse farming with fortified local diet formulation and packaging to address these challenges in a holistic way. Greenhouses powered by solar-assisted drip irrigation enable year-round vegetable production, conserve scarce water, and protect crops from extreme heat and pests. This ensures a reliable supply of affordable, nutrient-rich produce in local markets and schools. At the same time, fortified cereal-legume blends made from millet, sorghum, cowpea, groundnut, and moringa are processed in micro-factories run by women and youth cooperatives. These culturally familiar foods are enriched with vitamins and minerals to reduce child wasting and micronutrient deficiencies, while affordable sachet packaging extends shelf life and improves accessibility for displaced families. By 2026, the project aims to reduce child wasting in MMC by 10 percent, increase household dietary diversity scores by 20 percent, and raise year-round vegetable availability in local markets by 25 percent. It will establish five climate-smart greenhouses, produce and distribute 250,000 fortified diet sachets, and train and employ 100 women and youth in cooperatives. Immediate benefits include improved diets and livelihoods, while sustainable benefits include climate resilience, reduced post-harvest losses, and a replicable blueprint for fragile contexts globally.

core_fields.title: Transforming agricultural waste into sustainable food security via a zero-waste Modular Biorefinery approach (SADAB)
core_fields.description: This project deploys a zero-waste Modular Biorefinery to transform the massive waste of local products (mangoes, breadfruit, vegetables) in Haiti into sustainable food security. Our innovative approach generates three revenue streams: nutritious food, industrial ingredients, and bioenergy. We build climate resilience and create inclusive prosperity for marginalized farming communities, setting a standard for ecologically regenerative food systems.
core_fields.abstract: The SADAB project addresses the stark paradox of massive agricultural waste (estimated at 40-50% for mangoes, breadfruit, and certain vegetables) in Haiti, which coexists with high food insecurity. This waste is due to the rapid perishability of products and the lack of processing infrastructure. Our innovation is relevant because it transforms a major economic and nutritional loss into a source of sustainable food security and economic prosperity for marginalized rural communities. We are deploying a disruptive approach: the zero-waste Modular Biorefinery. Instead of processing a single product, we enhance the value of the entire fruit or vegetable using green and modular technologies adapted to the Haitian context. For example, for breadfruit, we produce nutritious flour, industrial starch, and biofuel from the residues, resulting in zero loss. This solution is based on principles of the circular economy and agro-ecology, validated by research on the optimal valorization of agricultural co-products. We integrate local expertise (drying techniques) with technical innovations (cold pressing for mango oil, bioreactors for biogas/biofuel) to maximize energy and material efficiency. Farmers/Producers Access to a reliable market, immediate increase in income, and increased economic security. Consumers Year-round access to nutritious, safe, and affordable food. Society/Environment Reduction of food waste, fight against deforestation (biofuel), creation of local jobs, and overall strengthening of the climate resilience of Haitian food systems.

core_fields.title: From Kitchen to Community-Dili's Kitchen Empowered women through Food, Training and sustainable employment.
