Dili s Kitchen aims to train and employ at least 30 women annually, improving household income and community
core_fields.abstract: Dili s Kitchen is an innovative women-led social enterprise that combines food service with skills development to address unemployment, malnutrition, and economic vulnerability in Timor-Leste. Unlike traditional restaurants, this model integrates a training-to-employment pipeline, where vulnerable women receive free, structured training in culinary skills, nutrition, hygiene, and small business management, and are immediately absorbed into paid work through the restaurant and food truck operations. The key problem being solved is the lack of stable income opportunities and practical skills for women, especially single mothers and housewives, alongside limited access to affordable, nutritious meals in urban and peri-urban communities. This initiative is highly relevant in a context where women face barriers to formal employment and communities experience ongoing food insecurity and poor dietary diversity. The solution is guided by scientific and technical insights from nutrition education, food safety standards, and social enterprise models that blend commercial sustainability with social impact. Evidence-based practices in hygiene, safe food handling, and balanced meal planning are incorporated to improve both health and service quality. Immediate benefits include increased income, improved confidence, and employable skills for participating women, access to clean and affordable meals for consumers, and new market opportunities for local farmers who supply fresh ingredients. Schools benefit from healthier catering options, while communities benefit from stronger local economies and role models for women s leadership. In the long term, the project contributes to poverty reduction, improved nutrition, environmental awareness through local sourcing and reduced food waste, and a more resilient, inclusive food system for society.

core_fields.title: Nyenice: Agroecology-Driven Food Innovation Enhancing Nutrition, Livelihoods, Climate Resilience, and Food Waste Reduction in Kenya
core_fields.description: The Nyenice Model transforms surplus indigenous vegetables and climate-resilient cereals into shelf-stable, nutrient-rich foods using agroecology and solar drying, cutting post-harvest losses by 40 60%. Our two products - Nyenice Vegetable Powder and Nyenice Uji Mix, ensure affordable, year-round nutrition while improving farmer incomes. Following a successful pilot with 125 elderly beneficiaries, we seek support to validate the products, expand drying hubs, strengthen supply chains, and reach 50,000 people within 24 months.
core_fields.abstract: The Nyenice Model is an agroecology-driven food innovation that reduces vegetable food waste, improves nutrition, and strengthens climate resilience in Kenyan communities. Indigenous vegetables, such as stinging nettle, amaranth, black nightshade, and spider plant, are highly nutritious but extremely perishable. During rainy seasons, they grow in abundance, yet up to 40 60% spoil before reaching consumers. During dry seasons, they become scarce and expensive, leading to micronutrient deficiencies, especially among children, women, and the elderly. The Nyenice Model solves this problem by drying and preserving vegetables at peak season using solar dryers and hygienic handling, then transforming them into shelf-stable, nutrient-dense products: Nyenice Indigenous Vegetable Powder and Nyenice Uji Mix. These products remain safe and usable for up to a year, providing a reliable source of vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants even in drought periods. The innovation is based on clear scientific insight: indigenous vegetables maintain high micronutrient content when solar-dried, and agroecological farming improves soil health and nutrient density while lowering production costs. Combining agroecology, food preservation, and community-led processing creates a regenerative, zero-waste food system. Benefits: Consumers: year-round access to affordable micronutrients Farmers: reduced post-harvest losses, stable markets, higher incomes Schools & communities: nutritious foods for feeding programs Environment: reduced waste, improved biodiversity, healthier soils Society: better nutrition, climate resilience, local economic empowerment A successful pilot with 125 elderly beneficiaries, 2 schools, and 1 camp for internally displaced people confirms strong acceptability and clear health benefits. The Nyenice Model offers an immediately useful, scalable solution for food security and resilience.

core_fields.title: CREIDBI SAFE : Solar Autonomous Food Ecosystems for Zero-Waste and Nutritious Food

core_fields.abstract: Food loss and waste are critical challenges across the Global South, where up to 40% of fruits and vegetables are discarded before reaching consumers due to limited preservation infrastructure, high energy costs, and lack of accessible processing technologies. This waste not only reduces farmer income but also contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and food insecurity. CREIDBISAFE addresses this challenge through a novel solar-powered, digitally controlled system that transforms perishable surplus into high-value products such as dried fruits, powders, condiments, and functional ingredients. The innovation integrates patented solar thermal design, adaptive air-flow control, and real-time monitoring of temperature and humidity, enabling high-quality processing without fossil fuels. The scientific and technical insight behind this solution lies in optimizing solar energy capture, thermodynamic efficiency, and precise dehydration curves to preserve nutrients, flavor, and food safety. Unlike conventional dryers, CREIDBISAFE operates with zero or near-zero emissions, is modular, portable, and requires minimal technical training. Immediate benefits include: Farmers and producers: Reduced post-harvest losses and new revenue from value-added products. Communities: Access to affordable and healthy foods processed locally. SMEs and cooperatives: Lower operating costs and increased productivity. Environment: Reduced emissions, minimized waste, and promotion of regenerative practices. Sustainably, CREIDBISAFE strengthens local food systems, enhances climate resilience, and accelerates a circular, solar-based bioeconomy

core_fields.description: Samaipata faces malnutrition while large volumes of native, nutritious cupes fruit are wasted and agricultural soils are degrading. Power Green builds on a five-year pilot, solving these issues by constructing a cupes flour processing plant. The project installs equipment, trains 16 indigenous women operators, regenerates cupes -producing land through sustainable harvesting and replanting, supplies the municipal school breakfast program, distributes surplus food to vulnerable families, and engages the community with private investors to expand sustainable production.
core_fields.abstract: Power Green responds to high levels of malnutrition coexisting with large-scale waste of cupes , which grows widely and almost exclusively in this region. The pilot project of Power Green functioned in 2020-2024, through borrowed equipment, manual work methods, and 16 indigenous female farmers who volunteered. The production of cupes flour reached about 3 tons per year throughout this time frame. The improvised production facility faced capacity restrictions, which minimized our production and forced us to control distribution through a waiting list, thus preventing multiple families from accessing our free cupes flour. The innovation lies in converting this pilot into a formal, licensed, community-owned production system. The project follows a clear sequence. First, a sanitary-compliant processing plant is constructed. AMPUAS (Municipal Association of Agroecological Producers of Samaipata), our partner organization, helps us hire skilled technicians who teach local women how to operate machinery and handle safety procedures, quality control, and maintenance during construction. The installation of industrial equipment along with completed training marks the start of production activities. The facility will generate 100 kg of flour each day and produce 27 tons of flour annually. The raw cupes for Power Green will come from AMPUAS-donated land as well as from local farmers who will sell cupes from their own land. Local farmers lack knowledge about cupes 's nutritional and market worth and practice depletive agriculture; Power Green will restore AMPUAS soil by applying regenerative harvesting methods and planting cupes trees to establish a sustainable agriculture system that local farmers can replicate.

core_fields.title: Empowering Perak's Indigenous Communities to shifting into syntropic-regenerative farming practice towards climate and food resilience
core_fields.description: In Perak state of Malaysia, Temiar-Semai indigenous community-farms facing serious climate-threats to their food security due to altered-weather-pattern, extreme-droughts & heavy-rainfall. Our 14-months project introduces syntropic-agroforestry, a regenerative method mimicking forests, to build climate-resilient farms. 40 participants from 4-settlements, representing 300-400 family members, gained hands-on training. Subsequently, we target 16-established productive farms, boosting local food production. This empowers indigenous-food-system, shares knowledge, delivers environmental-benefits, improving soil, water and biodiversity while reducing dependence on vulnerable traditional methods
core_fields.abstract: In Perak's state, Temiar-Semai Indigenous communities face a direct threat to their food security and way of life from climate change, exaggerated by deforestation. Their existing traditional shifting farming practice (which require shifting-forest-clearing & open-burning) are becoming less viable due to altered & unpredicted weather pattern, extreme heat / droughts and heavy floods / extreme raining causing declining yields and soil degradation thus making them increasingly vulnerable from the threats to their food security. Our project introduces innovative solution through syntropic agroforestry, a regenerative farming method that mimics the structure and function of a natural forest. The technical insight is that by strategically integrating multi-layered crops, fruit trees, and native plants, we can create a self-fertilizing, water-conserving, and pest-resilient ecosystem for long term. This moves beyond simple crop substitution to rebuilding the entire agricultural ecology. We target to empower the 40 community participants from 4-settlements representing 300-400 families through site-visit learning & hands-on training leads to the establishment of productive pocket syntropic farms, directly boosting diverse food production and reducing hunger. Sustainable benefits include year-round food security, new income opportunities, and the empowerment of households as key knowledge-holders. Environmentally sustainable - the system immediately begins restoring degraded land, increased soil fertility, enhanced biodiversity, natural water conservation, and a lasting reduction in dependence on practices that drive deforestation and soil loss. This solution is relevant because it simultaneously addresses climate vulnerability, food insecurity, and ecological decline with a single, culturally adaptable model that empowers the community as stewards of their own

core_fields.title: Sustainable Organic Waste Transformation Through Black Soldier Fly Farming and Compost Production
core_fields.description: Our project transforms organic waste into high-quality compost and protein-rich animal feed using Black Soldier Fly (BSF) technology. By linking farmers to waste sources through a digital platform, we improve soil fertility, reduce feed costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. The project also offers training and consultancy to farmers, enabling them to adopt eco-friendly, climate-smart practices that enhance productivity, profitability, and environmental resilience across communities in Rwanda.
core_fields.abstract: Agrithink Tank s innovation leverages Black Soldier Fly (BSF) technology to transform organic waste, including agricultural by-products, into high-quality compost and protein-rich animal feed supplements. Rwanda faces challenges of waste accumulation, soil degradation, and expensive animal feed, which negatively affect smallholder farmers productivity and environmental sustainability. Our solution addresses these issues by converting waste into valuable resources while promoting circular agriculture. The scientific insight behind this solution lies in the BSF larvae s ability to efficiently consume organic matter, rapidly reducing waste volume and producing nutrient-dense biomass suitable for animal feed. Simultaneously, the residue from larvae production becomes premium organic compost, enhancing soil fertility naturally. By integrating a digital platform, we connect farmers, waste suppliers, and local cooperatives, ensuring a continuous supply of raw materials and enabling efficient distribution of products. Immediate benefits to end users include reduced animal feed costs, improved crop yields, access to sustainable fertilizer, and practical training on BSF farming and waste management. Communities benefit from cleaner environments, reduced organic waste, and enhanced local livelihoods through job creation in BSF production, processing, and logistics. Long-term, the project fosters sustainable agricultural practices, climate-smart farming, and environmental resilience, creating a replicable model for circular agriculture in Rwanda and beyond. By turning a pressing environmental problem into economic and ecological opportunities, this innovation delivers tangible social, economic, and environmental impact while empowering farmers and communities with sustainable, science-backed solutions.

core_fields.title: Reducing waste, feeding those in need
core_fields.description: The project includes two main initiatives: 1. Logistics for Good - focuses on reducing food waste by rescuing surplus food that has lost its market value but is perfectly edible and redirecting it to vulnerable communities in peripheries through structured collection, sorting, and distribution weekly; 2. Tastes & Tales - complements this work by promoting educational activities on food and nutrition for the families, based on the Dietary Guidelines for the Brazilian Population.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation integrates two complementary approaches to address food waste and food insecurity in a systemic and sustainable way. The problem is twofold: large volumes of nutritious food are wasted along the post-harvest, wholesale, and retail chain, while millions of people face food insecurity and limited access to healthy diets. This imbalance drives environmental damage, social inequality, and economic inefficiency, making the challenge highly relevant from a climate, social, and ESG perspective. Logistics for Good redesigns food distribution flows by rescuing surplus food that has lost market value but remains safe and nutritious. Through optimized logistics, sorting, and quality control, this food is redistributed to vulnerable communities. The model is data-driven, generating measurable indicators such as food recovered, equivalent financial value, people reached, and avoided greenhouse gas emissions, especially methane from food waste. Tastes & Tales adds a critical educational and cultural layer. Through food and nutrition education, storytelling, and the promotion of local and cultural food practices, it strengthens food literacy, autonomy, and healthier, more sustainable eating habits. This approach is grounded in the insight that food security goes beyond access, encompassing knowledge, culture, and long-term behavior change.

core_fields.title: Food Risk Reduction and Safety Hubs for Informal Urban Produce Markets (FReSH-UP)
core_fields.description: FReSH-UP responds to the challenge of microbial contamination in informal food systems. Building on empirical evidence from an exposure assessment study, FReSH-UP pilots a risk reduction model which integrates two innovations and adapts them to the Ghanaian context: a Wash & Pack Station for the safe decontamination of produce (vegetables), and a QR-coded verification system for vendors. This combination will directly reduce microbial contamination, increase consumer trust, and enable regulators to conduct data-driven oversight.
core_fields.abstract: Informal markets are the primary source of food for most Ghanaians, but also represent the most significant point of microbial hazard exposure. This proposal addresses the food safety challenge of microbial contamination in raw produce (vegetables) in informal urban markets in Accra. TREND, in collaboration with four municipalities, recently deployed the SaniPath Tool (environmental risk assessment tool) under its Food Safety Project. The study identified raw produce as a dominant microbial exposure pathway. Evidence from the study shows that 87.6% of adults and 93.7% of children in Accra are exposed to E. coli via raw produce. Ghana has no structured system to verify produce safety in informal markets, limiting the mandate of the Food and Drugs Authority and municipal assemblies. FReSH-UP addresses this gap by integrating two complementary innovations: 1. Wash & Pack Station a compact, triple-basin wash system with chlorine dosing, foot-pedal handwashing, drying racks, and controlled flow to safely decontaminate wastewater-irrigated vegetables. 2. Digital inspection and QR-coded hygiene scorecards a mobile tool that allows Environmental Health Officers to conduct standardised inspections, log results, and generate visible QR scorecards for certified vendors. This combination is novel in Ghana s informal markets because it links microbial risk reduction with real-time, consumer-visible certification and digital traceability. Existing systems focus on vendor health certificates and paper inspections that provide little assurance of produce safety. FReSH-UP delivers immediate benefits (reduced contamination and illness risk, visible trust signals, better livelihoods for compliant vendors) and long-term benefits (data-driven regulation, scalable protocols, and national policy).

core_fields.title: Climate Resistant Food Crops of Wheat and Maize Promoting Climate Smart Agricultural Practices
core_fields.description: This project strengthens food security and climate resilience for tribal farming communities in North Gujarat by introducing climate-resilient wheat and maize varieties and supporting women farmers to adopt Climate Smart Agricultural practices. Through training, demonstration plots, local seed systems, and regenerative farming methods, the project improves yields, reduces input costs, restores soil and water health, and builds a sustainable, women-led farming model that continues beyond the project period.
core_fields.abstract: Proposed innovation responds to the growing challenge of climate change, which is causing unpredictable rainfall, declining soil fertility, and frequent crop losses for smallholder farmers. In North Gujarat, tribal communities depend heavily on wheat and maize for food and income, yet these crops are increasingly vulnerable to drought, pests, and rising temperatures. This creates food insecurity, financial stress, and limited livelihood resilience. Our solution combines climate-resilient seed varieties of wheat and maize with Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) practices that restore the environment while improving farm productivity. The scientific foundation of this approach comes from research demonstrating that drought-tolerant seeds, regenerative soil practices, integrated nutrient and pest management, and efficient water use significantly increase yields while reducing ecological harm. The project is practical and farmer-led. Tribal women farmers are trained through demonstration plots, peer learning, and technical trainings to adopt methods such as minimum tillage, line sowing, vermicompost, residue management, crop diversification, water budgeting, soil testing, seed selection and package of practices for CSA. Locally produced supply of seeds and market linkages ensure that this innovation is accessible, affordable, and economically viable. Immediate benefits include increased crop reliability, higher crop production, reduced loss, reduced input costs, and improved household food security. Long-term benefits include healthier soil, more resilient livelihood, reduced chemical use, reduced climate vulnerability and empowered women leaders who drive community-wide adoption. For consumers and society, this innovation is a more sustainable, trusted, nutritious, and climate-resilient food system benefiting current and future generations.

Gr ce l application mobile, aux SMS, l USSD et aux services vocaux IA, les agriculteurs vendent plus vite, gagnent davantage et r duisent les pertes. Avec plus de 30 000 m nages atteints, KivuGreen vise 300 000 agriculteurs en trois ans dans toute la RDC.
core_fields.abstract: KivuGreen is an AI-powered digital agriculture platform designed to solve the major challenges faced by smallholder farmers in the Democratic Republic of Congo: limited market access, high post-harvest losses, low productivity, lack of climate information, and exclusion from financial services. Farmers often depend on intermediaries, sell at low prices, and lack reliable data to plan production or access credit. KivuGreen addresses these challenges through a multi-channel digital system accessible via mobile app, SMS, USSD, and AI voice calls for illiterate farmers. The platform connects farmers directly with buyers through an e-commerce marketplace, enabling faster sales, transparent pricing, and secure mobile-money payments. All transactions are recorded automatically, generating financial data that cooperatives can use to access agricultural credit. The solution uses AI to deliver localized weather forecasts, climate-smart agricultural advice, automated voice support, and market price updates. This scientific and technical approach ensures that farmers receive timely information adapted to their location, crop type, and climate risks. Immediate benefits include faster market access (1 3 days instead of 10), increased income (+40%), reduced post-harvest losses ( 60%), higher productivity (+40 60%), and full inclusion of farmers who cannot read or write. Long-term, the platform strengthens food security, enhances climate resilience, improves financial inclusion, and builds a sustainable digital ecosystem supporting farmers, cooperatives, communities, and the environment. KivuGreen aims to reach 300,000 farming households within three years across multiple provinces of the DRC.

core_fields.title: Smart Foods from Senegal s Grains, Fruits, Leafy Greens, and Community Knowledge
core_fields.description: This project scales a community-based extrusion and nixtamalization model that transforms Senegal s traditional grains, fruits, and leafy greens into safe, nutritious, and affordable foods. A hub-and-spoke system links ITA and universities with women- and youth-led processors, reducing post-harvest losses and generating green jobs. Proven pilots, including those supported by AfDB and USAID initiatives, demonstrate strong technical, nutritional, and market performance. Grand Prize funding will enable expansion to reach 20,000+ consumers and establish a trusted African
core_fields.abstract: In Senegal, micronutrient deficiencies, food loss of local crops, and dependence on imported, ultra-processed foods undermine healthy diets and farmer incomes. Our innovation is a decentralized hub-and-spoke food processing model that converts local grains, fruits, and leafy greens into safe, appealing smart foods. Technical hubs (e.g., ITA, universities) host small-scale extruders and nixtamalization units, provide quality control and food-safety protocols, and incubate women- and youth-led enterprises. Community processors (spokes) formulate porridges, snacks, and school-feeding products using millet, sorghum, moringa, baobab, and mango, among other crops. This reduces post-harvest loss, increases shelf life, and enables food-to-food fortification. The model is already operational across 119 processing hubs and 300 community-level processing units, jointly serving value chains in 5 regions of Senegal. A novel feature is adapting nixtamalization, an alkaline cooking process traditionally used for maize, to West African grains. This enhances nutrient bioavailability, reduces anti-nutrients, improves flavor and digestibility, and expands product diversity. The model integrates seed systems so that farmers access varieties selected for both agronomic performance and processing quality, closing the loop from farm to consumer. Compared with centralized factories or imported fortified foods, the model is low-cost, climate-smart, and rooted in local dietary culture. It empowers women and youth as processors, retailers, and innovators. No other initiative in Senegal combines community-based extrusion, nixtamalization of local grains, seed-system integration, and entrepreneurship development at this scale., The model offers a replicable, economically viable pathway for strengthening food and nutrition security across the Sahel.

core_fields.title: XchangeBox: Solving the $300M Liquidity Gap to Unlock Africa s Food Supply
core_fields.description: In Nigeria, farmers/Agrotraders wait for an average 30-90 days for payment, losing 25% of potential yield and forcing a 40% reduction in planted acreage. XchangeBox solves this by guaranteeing payment in 3-10 days. Our platform directly addresses a $300M annual trade finance gap, increasing farmer productivity by 30% and stabilizing supply for processors. It s a financial fix that creates $1,200 in additional annual income per farmer while making local food systems resilient.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Nigeria s agricultural sector has a $300M trade finance gap. Smallholder farmers/Agrotraders (40M+) face a 30-90 day payment delay after supplying processors, causing a 25% loss in potential productivity and forcing 40% to reduce planted acreage. This systemic cashflow crisis results in $1.2B in annual lost production, unstable food supplies, and entrenched rural poverty. Innovation: XchangeBox is a financial circuit breaker. We provide immediate, 3-day payment to farmers/Agrotraders upon verified delivery, using a platform that aligns cash flow. The factory repays us in its standard payment term of 90 days maximum. We turn the most crippling inefficiency, the payment delay, into a lever for systemic growth. Core Insight: The constraint is not land or skill; it is misaligned cash flow timing. Solving this unlocks trapped value across the chain. Benefits: Farmers: $1,200 additional annual income, enabling reinvestment and a 30% productivity increase. Freedom from predatory loans (>120% APR). Food System: Stabilizes supply for processors, reducing operational costs by 15%. Increases local food security. Economic: Unlocks $5,000 in annual trade volume per farmer. Creates a formal, investable asset class from agricultural receivables. Scalability: Model designed to mobilize $2M in diaspora investment within 12 months, scaling to 10,000 farmers and $50M in trade volume. Mechanism: A secure, digital platform that verifies transactions and manages guarantees, making the value chain transparent and bankable.

core_fields.title: Green Ammonia Soil Application Pilot for Sustainable Agriculture in Namibia
core_fields.description: This project will pilot the direct application of green anhydrous ammonia produced from renewable hydrogen at the Daures Green Hydrogen Village across selected Namibian soils. The study will evaluate its effectiveness as an affordable, efficient, and sustainable fertilizer alternative by measuring soil health, crop yield, and environmental outcomes. The results will guide national-scale adoption, supporting Namibia s green hydrogen roadmap, enhancing agricultural productivity, and accelerating climate-smart farming practices.
core_fields.abstract: Namibia faces a critical need for sustainable fertilizer solutions to boost agricultural productivity while reducing reliance on imports and minimizing environmental impact. Traditional fertilizers contribute to greenhouse gas emissions and soil degradation, making them unsustainable for long-term food security. Our innovation introduces green anhydrous ammonia, produced by the Daures Green Hydrogen Village using renewable hydrogen, as a direct soil application fertilizer. This approach leverages cutting-edge green hydrogen technology to create a carbon-neutral nitrogen source, addressing both climate and agricultural challenges. The scientific insight behind this solution lies in ammonia s high nitrogen content and proven agronomic benefits, combined with Namibia s emerging capacity for green hydrogen production. By piloting direct application methods, we aim to validate safety, efficiency, and crop yield improvements under local conditions. This eliminates the need for energy-intensive conversion processes, reducing costs, and accelerating adoption. Immediate Benefits: Farmers gain access to a locally produced, cost-effective fertilizer alternative. Improved crop yields and soil health through optimized nitrogen delivery. Sustainable Benefits: Reduced carbon footprint and dependency on imported fertilizers. Strengthened local agricultural systems and food security. Positioning Namibia as a leader in climate-smart farming and green hydrogen innovation. This project bridges renewable energy and agriculture, creating a model for sustainable development that benefits farmers, communities, and the environment.

core_fields.title: Building a profitable market access platform for smallholder farmers
core_fields.description: Honeyguide is a partner for farmers that does everything after the farm gate to help farmers earn more money. We use our high tech fleet of mobile markets to pickup the farmer's goods at the farm gate, transport them to cities, and sell to consumers at urban prices, then we share profits back to the farmer. The farmer makes more of the money. Honeyguide develops advanced technology that all farmers benefit from. We thrive together.
core_fields.abstract: Across Africa, more than 500 million smallholder farmers lose up to 95% of the value of their crops to layers of middlemen, leaving them trapped in low yields, low income and a cycle of poverty. Honeyguide is the alternate path. We build a new, hyper-efficient supply chain designed around the farmer. Honeyguide is a tech-enabled mobile marketplace: a single smart vehicle that arrives directly at the farm gate, buys produce on the spot, transports it to the city, sells to consumers at the best available price and returns profits to the farmer. Each unit is a self-contained supply chain that integrates marketing, inspection, logistics, planning, and sales all optimized by Honeyguide's AI systems to improve efficiency by 5x and unlock immediate 2-4x income growth for farmers. By cutting out middlemen, Honeyguide ensures farmers capture real value from their work. And by reinvesting in farmer productivity, we multiply that impact over time. Built on technology and designed to scale, Honeyguide represents a new model for agricultural transformation; one where both farmers win and consumers win.

core_fields.abstract: Across the UK, demand for clean, allergen-friendly plant-based foods continues to rise, with 1 in 3 consumers reducing dairy intake and the plant-based market projected to reach 1.1 billion by 2027. Yet many available options remain ultra-processed or nutritionally limited. At the same time, up to 40% of food in the UK is wasted, and underutilised crops account for less than 1% of commercial food products despite their nutritional, environmental and cultural value. Tigernut a naturally sweet, fibre-rich African crop remains one such overlooked ingredient. Root Mylk s innovation is a Circular Tigernut SuperFoods Ecosystem that transforms whole tigernuts into clean plant-based drinks and SuperFlour+ , an upcycled flour made from tigernut pulp. Instead of discarding pulp, we convert it into nutrient-forward blends enriched with five climate-resilient, underutilised African crops: Purple sweet potato high in anthocyanins and fibre Bambara nut 18 20% plant protein Millets rich in iron, magnesium and slow-release carbohydrates Fonio gluten-free with essential amino acids Green banana flour a leading source of resistant starch Planned analytical work with the Natural Resources Institute (NRI), University of Greenwich will evaluate tigernut pulp s prebiotic potential, fibre composition, moisture reduction pathways and suitability for upcycling. NRI will also validate nutritional composition, shelf-life, microbial safety, sensory performance and optimise drying and milling parameters required for scale. Immediate benefits include clean-label, allergen-friendly foods for UK families, schools and wellness consumers. Long-term, this circular model reduces waste, lowers environmental impact and creates future opportunities for responsible sourcing through collaboration with African AgTech partners.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Income and Nutrition through Climate-Smart Aquaculture in the Barind Region
core_fields.description: The project will install 10 climate smart aquaculture units in drought prone Barind region of Rajshahi, Bangladesh comanaged by 100 farmers. Solar powered, recirculating aquaponics will produce 1.2 1.5 tons of fish and 350 500 kg of vegetables per pond annually while reusing 80 90% of water. The intervention strengthens technical capacity, nutrition practices, and market linkages, empowers women, and delivers affordable protein, higher household incomes, and climate resilience for vulnerable communities.
core_fields.abstract: Problem & Relevance: Godagari and Tanore in the Barind region of Rajshahi, Bangladesh face long dry seasons, falling groundwater, and regular crop losses. Many households depend on farming, but water scarcity limits food production, contributing to poor nutrition. A 2019 study showed 44.8% of preschool children in Rajshahi are malnourished, and health data shows high vulnerability in Godagari and Tanore. Fish is the main affordable source of protein, yet local production is declining because ponds dry early, limited inputs, and technical knowledge. Additionally, market linkages and storage facilities are weak. Proposed Solution: The project will expand a Climate-Smart Aquaculture (CSAq) model designed for drought-prone areas that closes the skills gap, ensures dietary diversity, and supports broader market system development. Each group-managed pond will produce 1.2 1.5 tons of fish and 350 500 kg of vegetables per year, with ten families jointly managing each pond. Production volumes are sufficient for home consumption and sales. The model uses innovative technology such as aquaponics, small greenhouses, solar pumps, and recirculating water systems to maintain year-round production using minimal water. Scientific Basis, Novelty, and Benefits: CSAq combines natural nutrient recycling, water recirculation, and solar energy to keep production efficient and low-cost. Microbes convert fish waste into plant nutrients, reducing fertilizer use and pollution. Recirculating systems reuse 80-90% of water, while solar pumps lower energy costs. This integrated model improves biosecurity, reduces climate risks, boosts household nutrition, and can raise annual income by about USD 2,200, with strong opportunities for women s participation.

core_fields.title: Nourish soil ORGANIC MANURE AND FERTILIZERS
core_fields.description: Nourish Soil aims to transform forest excess loops, tops, and dry foliage biomass into valuable organic manure and fertilizers. This initiative not only mitigates forest fire risks but also provides city and urban customers with sustainable farming solutions. Our target market includes home gardeners, rooftop plant enthusiasts, roadside plantations, and nurseries in Pokhara and other urban areas. This enterprise specializes in out passing prevailing chemical fertilizers in effectiveness, application, pricing, and sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Nourish Soil is a mission-driven team committed to restoring soil health and promoting sustainable agriculture while directly supporting high-quality, safe, and nutritious food production. By transforming locally available forest and green biomass into high-quality organic manure and fertilizers, the team aims to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers and help farmers, urban gardeners, nurseries, and municipalities grow healthier crops. The goal of Nourish Soil is to establish a trusted and environmentally responsible organic manure brand in Pokhara Valley, with gradual expansion to other urban areas of Nepal, while advancing circular resource use, soil regeneration, and community-based livelihoods. The innovation addresses two interconnected challenges: declining soil fertility caused by long-term chemical fertilizer use and the underutilization of forest and green biomass that often increases forest fire risks. Simultaneously, urbanization has reduced access to traditional animal manure, limiting the ability of producers to grow quality food organically. Nourish Soil solves this problem by converting excess forest litter, tree loops and tops, dry leaves, and periodically removed green biomass into nutrient-rich organic manure through scientifically managed composting and vermicomposting processes. Forestry and soil science principles such as balanced carbon nitrogen ratios, controlled decomposition, and microbial enrichment form the foundation of this solution. The immediate benefits include affordable, safe, and easy-to-use organic manure that improves soil structure and nutrient availability, leading to healthier plants and higher-quality food free from harmful chemical residues. core_fields.title: Scaling Regenerative Livestock Banks for Nutrition and Sustainable Food Security
core_fields.description: Despite health gains, 38% of Rwandan children are stunted and 24% of households consume no animal-sourced foods; undernourishment rose to 36.8%.This project scales regenerative livestock banks and market alliances to reach 50,000 farmers (≥50% women),strengthen 8 districts, and improve access to nutritious foods for 250,000 households. By expanding livestock assets, finance, extension and demand creation (Orora Wihaze/Gira Itungo), it boosts women s nutrition decision-making and sustainable food security aligned with Rwanda s AIS agenda.
core_fields.abstract: Rwanda continues to face high malnutrition despite strong health-sector progress: 38% of children under five are stunted, and 24% of households consume no animal-sourced foods. Smallholder farmers who produce most livestock lack access to animals, finance, quality feed, animal health services, and reliable markets. These systemic constraints limit production, raise costs, and keep nutritious foods out of reach, especially for women and children. This innovation scales Regenerative Livestock Banks integrated with farmer-led market alliances, building on proven innovations in small livestock and nutrition in Rwanda. Farmers access pigs, poultry, cattle, goats, and sheep as productive assets through lease-to-own and pass-on models, repaying with offspring or market-ready animals rather than cash. This removes credit barriers, accelerates herd growth, and continuously expands participation prioritizing women and youth. The Livestock Bank is embedded in a market-systems approach linking farmers to quality inputs, veterinary and extension services, aggregation and processing, and structured buyers. Regenerative practices locally produced feeds using crop by-products, improved housing and biosecurity, and manure recycling boost productivity while reducing environmental impact. Scientific evidence shows livestock ownership improves food security, small livestock deliver rapid nutrition gains, and coordinated market systems outperform stand-alone subsidies.Immediate benefits include higher farmer incomes, lower mortality, and safer, affordable animal-sourced foods. Long-term benefits include improved women s and children s nutrition, resilient local food systems, reduced import dependence, and lower emissions per unit of protein creating sustainable value for farmers, consumers, and the environment.

core_fields.title: Preserving Local Harvests into Shelf-Stable Nutrition Without Cold Chains - ( pamọ́ O njẹ)
core_fields.description: This project preserves fresh, locally grown fruits and vegetables at harvest to reduce food loss and improve access to safe, nutritious food. Working with smallholder farmers, surplus produce is converted into shelf-stable foods and ingredients that retain nutrition and do not require refrigeration. The approach increases farmer income, lowers post-harvest waste, and provides reliable, affordable food for local and export markets, even in regions with weak cold-chain infrastructure.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description Across many parts of Africa, large volumes of fruits and vegetables are lost soon after harvest due to poor storage, weak cold chains, and limited local processing. This results in wasted food, lost farmer income, and reduced access to nutritious food, especially outside peak harvest seasons. This project addresses that gap by preserving fresh produce at harvest and converting it into shelf-stable foods and ingredients that retain nutritional value and do not require refrigeration. By working directly with smallholder farmers, surplus crops that would otherwise spoil are processed locally into safe, long-lasting products suitable for households, schools, food manufacturers, and export markets. The innovation is built on a practical insight: food loss is highest where cold storage is weakest. Rather than relying on expensive cold chains, this approach stabilizes food through preservation methods that extend shelf life while maintaining quality and safety. Processing close to farms reduces transport losses, lowers costs, and ensures a consistent supply throughout the year. Immediate benefits include reduced post-harvest losses, higher and more predictable income for farmers, and improved availability of affordable, nutritious food for consumers. Over time, the model supports local food systems, reduces reliance on imports, strengthens resilience to climate shocks, and lowers environmental waste from spoiled produce. The solution is scalable, commercially viable, and designed for adoption in regions facing similar food system constraints.

core_fields.title: AgrowSAFE: A Community-Based Verification and Market Access Model for Safer, Trusted Food Systems
core_fields.description: AgrowSAFE is a community-based verification and market access model that helps smallholder farmers produce safer, more sustainable, and trusted food. It combines simple standards, tiered verification, with on-site and digital training and tools for farmers to improve food safety, animal welfare, and climate-smart practices, while providing market access opportunities. This Seed Grant will pilot and refine the model, generating evidence to support scalable, inclusive food systems that build consumer trust and improve farmer livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: AgrowSAFE addresses a core challenge in many LMIC food systems, where poor agricultural and food production practices undermine food safety, ethical standards, environmental sustainability, and consumer trust. Smallholder farmers and agrifood SMEs are often willing to improve food safety, animal welfare, and climate-smart practices, but lack practical knowledge, affordable verification pathways, and market incentives to sustain responsible production. Conventional certification systems, where they exist, are often limited, costly, and exclusionary, thereby resulting in continued food safety risks, low consumer confidence, and restricted market access. AgrowSAFE is a community-based verification and market access model that provides farmers with a clear, progressive pathway to demonstrate responsible production. It combines simple standards, tiered verification, hands-on support, and light digital tools to help farmers improve practices step by step. Verification is embedded locally and linked to buyer demand, transforming compliance from a barrier into an opportunity. This solution emerged from our team s field experience in poultry and aquaculture systems, where buyers increasingly require verified SAFE practices, but producers are unaware of best practices and standards. Also, we found that farmers adopt improvements more effectively when guidance is practical, verification is incremental, and progress is rewarded through real market opportunities. Immediate benefits include improved farm practices, reduced food safety risks, clearer trust signals for buyers and consumers, and stronger incentives for farmers to continue improving. Over time, AgrowSAFE supports safer food, improved food security, more resilient livelihoods, increased consumer confidence, and inclusive, environmentally sustainable food systems that can scale across diverse LMIC contexts.

core_fields.title: Transforming Food Systems Through Innovative Agriculture Resource and Production Centers in Kenya
core_fields.description: City Shamba seeks to scale the establishment of innovative agriculture resource and production centres (i-ARC) in schools and hospitals across the country. The centres present various innovative agroecological farming methods that enhance food production in smaller spaces using nature-based agroecological practices. They provide learning platforms for schools and communities; a source of agroecological farm inputs and technical expertise for those willing to set-up own gardens, enhancing food access and sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: As Kenya grapples with food insecurity and poor nutrition, the unsustainability of the food systems is evident, with a critical need for improved access to safe and nutritious food. Growing own food improves not only affordability and access, but also safety and trust. With shrinking land spaces in rural areas, inadequate spaces in urban areas, poor soil health and biodiversity loss, expensive synthetic inputs and climate change, innovation and agroecology remain the best solutions. However, there is a skills and knowledge gap among communities required for uptake of innovative agroecological techniques. Our proposed i-ARC provides the solution. Since 2019, we have been running i-ARC as a food systems solution in communities. From our main center at Mama Lucy Kibaki Hospital, we have established 17 small centers spread across different institutions in Kenya, including in Nairobi-6, Mombasa-1, Meru-1, Nanyuki-1, Busia-1, Kisumu-1, Kitui-1, Kisii-1, Embu-2, Turkana-1, Nandi-1. The centres provide learning opportunities to school learners and communities on agroecology and innovative techniques that utilize limited spaces, improve soil health and biodiversity. These include vertical gardening techniques, hydroponics, aquaponics, organic pesticides formulation and application of organic fertilizer and feed production through Black Soldier Fly technology, poultry and edible landscaping among others. They are sources of farm inputs and technical expertise for those interested in establishing own gardens. The food produced in the centers contribute to school and hospital feeding programs. We seek support to scale this up throughout the country.

core_fields.title: Vertical Farming
core_fields.description: A literal gift from our hearts EPO is a climate-tech startup that delivers modular hydroponic systems designed for urban households, health-conscious communities, and commercial use. By integrating solar energy and water recycling, EPO tackles food insecurity, energy inefficiency, and water scarcity in developing regions. Our systems are smart, scalable, and highly efficient. We directly are solving climate change issues by recycling water , using renewable energy and producing pesticide free vegetables and plants.
core_fields.abstract: EPO addresses one of the most urgent global challenges: food insecurity driven by climate change, water scarcity, and rising urban populations. Traditional agriculture is increasingly unable to provide consistent, affordable, and nutritious food due to unpredictable weather, degraded soil, and limited arable land especially in cities and climate-vulnerable regions. EPO solves this problem through AI-enabled hydroponic and vertical farming systems that grow fresh produce using up to 90% less water, no soil, and minimal land. Our modular systems can be installed in homes, schools, communities, and urban spaces, enabling food to be grown where it is consumed. AI-driven monitoring optimizes nutrient delivery, light, and growth cycles, ensuring reliable yields year-round regardless of climate conditions. The scientific insight behind EPO lies in combining controlled-environment agriculture with data-driven automation, allowing plants to grow in optimal conditions while drastically reducing resource use. By removing dependency on weather and soil quality, EPO makes food production resilient and predictable. The immediate benefits include access to fresh, pesticide-free vegetables, reduced food costs, and improved nutrition for families, schools, and communities. For farmers and producers, EPO lowers operational risk and input costs while increasing productivity per square foot. Sustainably, EPO reduces water consumption, food miles, and carbon emissions, contributing to climate resilience and environmental protection. EPO s core value is simple: empowering communities to grow healthy food locally, sustainably, and affordably, today and for future generations.

core_fields.title: Poultry Multiplication Initiative (PMI): Scaling Climate Resilient Food Security
core_fields.description: World Poultry Foundation (WPF) is expanding our successful Poultry Multiplication Model (PMI) to emerging economies in Latin America, Africa, and Asia, to bolster household income, food security, and climate resilience for thousands of vulnerable households. PMI, which includes farmer-centric training and MEL, has been tested and implemented in 8 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, with core funding from the Gates Foundation and the Qatar Fund. 2.8 million households have benefitted since 2017.
core_fields.abstract: The Poultry Multiplication Initiative (PMI) generates an ecosystem of training and support for local rural and semi-rural communities to raise dual purpose, high yield chickens. The PMI s theory of change is that introducing high-productivity breeds that are geared towards the low-resource environment can build on production and sales in rural areas already occurring, but inefficiently, tripling meat and egg yields (with similar cost inputs already occurring). Key outcomes: -Improve household income, food security and health for vulnerable households. -Create greater gender parity for women (who are, in 60-80% of cases, the primary poultry carers in households). -Generate new and sustainable businesses for SMEs in developing countries. -Establish stronger food systems that are more climate resilient, as our dual-purpose chicken breeds are climate adaptable and create net ecological benefits. Eighty percent of the world s population raises backyard poultry. Families, especially women who are responsible for chicken rearing, already have the knowhow, the desire, and the space to care for poultry. What they don t have, in many cases, is the right breed of birds, the awareness of production techniques, and market entry to create a viable economic resource from their efforts. The PMI overcomes these barriers by establishing value chains that enable access to improved poultry genetics, affordable quality feed, vaccines, technical extension training, and market development programs for the offtake of the excess meat and eggs produced. Our approach is private sector led, achieving a highly efficient delivery model where a large proportion of farmer revenues remain with communities.

core_fields.title: Empowering Smallholders with Climate-Smart Cassava Processing for Nutritious, Sustainable Foods
core_fields.description: This project empowers 3,000 youth and women smallholder farmers in cassava cultivation using regenerative practices with biochar, while producing safe, nutritious, low-cost cassava crisps through energy-efficient impingement ovens powered by hybrid solar and biomass electricity. By integrating climate-smart agriculture, modern energy cooking, and women-led sourcing enterprises, the project enhances farmer incomes, reduces post-harvest losses, improves food safety, and delivers affordable, high-quality cassava products for local and regional markets.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Nigeria face low incomes, post-harvest losses, and limited access to modern processing technologies, while consumers often lack affordable, nutritious, and safe cassava-based foods. ATMANCorp addresses these challenges with a holistic, integrated innovation: regenerative cassava cultivation, energy-efficient processing, and inclusive value chains. The project introduces 3,000 youth and women to cassava cultivation using biochar-enhanced regenerative agriculture, which improves soil fertility, sequesters carbon, increases yields, and reduces heavy metal uptake in roots, enhancing food safety. On the processing side, cassava crisps are produced using impingement ovens powered by a hybrid solar and biomass electricity system, delivering low-oil, energy-efficient cooking with consistent quality and minimal environmental impact. The scientific insights driving this solution include: biochar s capacity to immobilize heavy metals and enhance nutrient retention in root crops, and high-velocity air impingement for rapid, uniform heating, which preserves nutrients while reducing energy use compared to conventional frying. Immediate benefits include higher farmer incomes, reduced post-harvest losses, safer and nutritious crisps for consumers, and employment opportunities for youth and women. Sustainable benefits extend to soil regeneration, carbon sequestration, heavy metal mitigation, low-carbon food processing, scalable renewable energy integration, and strengthened local food systems. By combining modern energy cooking, regenerative farming, and inclusive sourcing, this innovation demonstrates a replicable, climate-smart, and socially equitable model for transforming cassava value chains and improving food system resilience.

core_fields.title: Integrated Bioconversion System
core_fields.description: Our project develops a first-of-its-kind, containerized system that converts both solid and liquid organic waste into affordable, high-protein animal feed through a zero-waste process. The solution reduces feed costs by 10 15%, diverts waste from landfills, and cuts emissions while supporting local farmers. We are completing laboratory validation and building an MVP to scale this locally produced alternative to imported feed.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation is a containerized, integrated bioconversion system that transforms both solid and liquid organic waste into affordable, high-protein animal feed through a zero-waste process. The problem we address is the rising cost and environmental impact of conventional animal feed, largely driven by reliance on imported soybean meal and fishmeal, as well as the growing burden of unmanaged organic waste that ends up in landfills, producing methane and polluting water sources. This challenge is especially severe for small- and medium-scale farmers, whose profitability and food security are directly affected by feed price volatility. We solve this problem by using a scientifically proven bioconversion approach that converts waste streams into valuable feed ingredients within a single, closed-loop system. Our solution is designed to recycle both solid and liquid waste, enabling higher resource efficiency than existing alternatives that handle only one waste stream. The technical insight behind the system is the integration of complementary biological processes into one modular container, allowing continuous conversion, drying, and milling of feed ingredients close to the point of waste generation and feed demand. The immediate benefits to farmers include a 10 15% reduction in feed costs, improved supply security, and access to locally produced protein feed. Communities benefit from reduced landfill waste, lower emissions, and cleaner environments. In the long term, the system supports sustainable agriculture, strengthens local food systems, creates green jobs, and contributes to climate action by avoiding significant CO₂-equivalent emissions per unit of feed produced.

core_fields.title: Growing sustainable nutrition through circular agriculture and value added mushroom enterprises
core_fields.description: This project transforms agricultural by-products(bagasse) into nutritious mushroom crisps, creating a sustainable, affordable snack. By using locally available materials and simple processing, it reduces waste, supports circular agriculture, creates jobs, and promotes healthier eating. The initiative combines food innovation with environmental sustainability to deliver value for consumers, farmers, and the planet.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation is the production of mushroom crisps made by growing edible mushrooms on agricultural by-products that are usually treated as waste, such as sugarcane bagasse. The problem we address is the high level of agricultural waste, limited value addition in the sugar sector, and the growing demand for affordable, healthy snacks. At the same time, many communities face rising food costs, nutrition gaps, and environmental pressure from waste disposal. This innovation is relevant because it turns a low-value residue into a high-value food product, supporting circular agriculture and reducing environmental pollution. Mushrooms naturally grow on fibrous plant material, making bagasse an ideal substrate. This scientific insight from mycology allows us to produce nutritious mushrooms with minimal inputs, then process them into shelf-stable crisps edible for up to a year. The solution creates immediate benefits for consumers by offering a healthy, plant-based snack rich in protein, fiber, and micronutrients. Farmers and sugar producers benefit from new income streams from by-products. Communities gain jobs in cultivation and processing, while the environment benefits from reduced waste, lower emissions, and more efficient resource use. Over time, the project supports sustainable food systems, improved nutrition, and greener agro-industrial practices.

core_fields.title: Locally Sourced School Meals: A Transformative Approach for Linking Nutrition and Markets for Agroecological Produces
core_fields.description: The project addresses child malnutrition in Karnali Province by transforming Government's mid-day school meal programme toward a local nutrition-sensitive model. It connects schools with local agroecological farmers to provide and supply safe, nutritious meals, strengthens local cooperatives, and promotes household nutrition through home gardens and awareness. By engaging schools, communities and local governments, the initiative aims to create a replicable sustainable school meal model that improves child nutrition, supports livelihoods, and strengthens local food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition remains critical challenges in Nepal, with children being the most vulnerable. To address child malnutrition, the Government has invested in a mid-day school meal targeting students up to grade five. The programme aims to enhance nutrition, reduce dropout rates, and promote the use of locally produced, healthy, and nutritious agricultural and livestock products. However, its implementation has fallen short. Instead of linking school meals with local food production, schools and local governments largely rely on ready-to-eat, processed foods with low nutritional values sourced from distant markets. At the same time, local agricultural production remains disorganized and lacks mechanism to supply on a regular basis. This has led schools to favor available market foods over local produce. Farmers producing at scale depend on unsustainable practices, including excessive chemical use, resulting in unsafe food that can further undermine nutritional outcomes. Conversely, farmers practicing agroecological methods face significant barriers, such as weak market linkages and prices. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a functional homegrown school meal ecosystem, promoting agroecological farming, strengthening farmer groups and cooperatives, and facilitating direct linkages between producers and schools. The project emphasizes improving household-level nutrition through sensitization, capacity building, engagement with parents, school committees and local governments, and support for strengthening agroecological production. Students will be engaged through school clubs and campaigns to counter rising consumption of unhealthy foods. Overall, the initiative aims to establish a replicable, circular, agroecology-based model that integrates nutrition, local markets, and sustainable food systems to achieve better nutrition outcomes.

core_fields.title: Fortified Plantain-Soy Flour Production in Ghana
core_fields.description: Fortified Plantain-Soy Flour transforms excess Ghanaian plantain into fortified plantain-soy flour and removes post-harvest wastage, as well as enhances access to affordable and nutritious foods. The project increases the earnings of farmers, reduces food waste, and resolves the protein-energy malnutrition among children and especially vulnerable populations by using small-scale, solar-powered processing.
core_fields.abstract: Ghana faces two critical agricultural challenges that this project addresses. First, plantain farmers lose approximately 40-60% of their harvest due to the fruit's short shelf life and inadequate storage facilities. Plantains ripen quickly after harvest, and without proper preservation methods, tonnes of this nutritious crop go to waste annually. Second, many Ghanaians, particularly children and pregnant women, suffer from protein-energy malnutrition despite having access to starchy staples like plantain. This project proposes a practical solution by converting surplus and near-spoiling plantains into a nutritious, shelf-stable flour fortified with soybean. This approach tackles food waste while creating a product that addresses nutritional gaps in Ghanaian diets. the project aims to develop a sustainable processing system that converts surplus plantain into fortified flour, thereby reducing post-harvest losses and improving nutritional outcomes for consumers. The production process involves transforming perishable plantains into valuable flour. The project solution is based on the food science, post-harvest physiology, and nutrition systems studies that have shown that within a short period of time, food spoilage can be prevented, protein-energy deficiencies corrected, and food fortified with legumes. Knowledge of the high carbohydrate density and low protein content of plantain with the evidence that processing soybean increases amino acid balance and digestibility led to this composite flour strategy. The immediate advantages include cheap, nutritious foods for consumers; farmers will acquire more income, schools will receive the local nutritional solutions, and communities will receive employment. Sustainably, the environment benefits through the reduction of waste and climate-smart production systems.

core_fields.title: COOL LION AGRICARE FARMER CENTERS: Solar-Powered Post-Harvest Infrastructure for Women Farmers
core_fields.description: COOL LION AGRICARE FARMER CENTERS operate solar-powered hubs that combine cold storage, solar drying, and conversion of mango residues into compost. Built on two successful centers, our model markedly reduces post-harvest losses, improves farmer incomes, and expands access to nutritious food while closing waste loops. Implemented with women at the center and in partnership with GIE TERRE IVOIRE, Cote d'Ivoire s national mango smallholder association, the initiative is designed for structured national scale.
core_fields.abstract: When mango season peaks, farmers know the problem before it happens. Fruit ripens all at once, markets saturate, prices fall, and what cannot be sold quickly begins to rot. Women who manage sorting, storage, drying, and processing carry most of this burden. In our early work with cooperatives, we saw good harvests turn into losses within days. COOL LION AGRICARE FARMER CENTERS were created to address this reality in a practical way. Two centers are already operating successfully and are heavily used during peak seasons. Each center combines solar-powered cold storage to slow ripening and hybrid solar dryers to preserve surplus safely. Next we intent to convert mango peelings and other processing residues into compost and returned to farmers' fields, closing the loop between harvest, preservation, and soil health. A key innovation is the deployment of a warehouse management software, adapted to cooperative use and taught directly to partner farmer groups. This system allows cooperatives to manage intake, storage duration, processing flows, and withdrawals in a structured way, improving traceability, accountability, and planning. It strengthens trust between farmers, cooperative leaders, and buyers while building local capacity to manage modern infrastructure. The innovation is not a single technology but an integrated, circular system designed for smallholders. Benefits are immediate and lasting: losses drop sharply, incomes rise, women gain control over value-added activities, and markets receive safer, more nutritious mango, fruits and vegetables.

core_fields.description: This project transforms underutilised food resources into nutrient-dense, shelf-stable food powders using Vortair s patented technology, enabling the production of affordable, highly nutritious food bars for food-insecure and crisis-affected communities. By reducing food loss and preventing landfill emissions, the project delivers scalable, sustainable nutrition while strengthening food system resilience in developing regions.
core_fields.abstract: Vortair addresses the global challenge of food loss and chronic malnutrition by transforming surplus produce from local farms, households, and businesses into ultra-fine, nutrient-dense powders used to create long-life, highly nutritious bars. Each year, vast quantities of edible fruits and vegetables are discarded, generating emissions and lost nutritional value, while crisis-affected regions struggle to access safe, reliable food. Existing therapeutic foods such as Plumpy Nut are vital for short-term recovery but are only intended for 6 8 weeks of use and do not provide ongoing nutritional security. Many children relapse because long-term, affordable daily foods are unavailable. Vortair solves this through its patented low-temperature vortex-milling technology, which dries and mills organic materials without heat or chemicals. This preserves vitamins and minerals while eliminating microbial activity, producing ultra-fine powders that remain shelf-stable for years. These powders form the base of clean-label, allergen-friendly bars suitable for continuous, everyday consumption. While fortified foods and nutrition bars exist, none provide a long-term, multi-year nutrition solution produced from upcycled plant materials using low-temperature micron-scale milling that maintains natural nutrient integrity. To optimise the exact nutritional blends, ingredients, and micronutrient composition, Vortair will collaborate with CSIRO, Australia s national science agency, leveraging their world-leading expertise in food science, human health, and agricultural innovation. This partnership ensures the formulation meets global nutrition standards while maximising bioavailability and cultural acceptability. Benefits are immediate and sustainable: communities gain reliable daily nutrition; farmers earn value from rejected produce; waste and emissions decrease, strengthening circular food systems.

core_fields.title: Delivering sustainable vaccine solutions to livestock dependant communities in East Africa
core_fields.description: The biopharmaceutical market in Uganda and sub-Saharan Africa remains underdeveloped, particularly for low and middle-income communities reliant on livestock. Livestock diseases severely impact the livelihoods of nearly 700 million people living on less than $4 a day. Key barriers include poor veterinary outreach, lack of affordable and user-friendly vaccines, and unreliable electricity for proper storage. The goal is to eliminate these barriers, starting with poultry vaccines, to help households better utilize livestock and reduce poverty.
core_fields.abstract: In sub-Saharan Africa, poultry farming is a key livelihood for almost every household, supporting both small-scale and commercial operations. However, the sector faces major challenges from Newcastle disease, a highly contagious and deadly viral infection. This disease results in high mortality rates up to 70% in unvaccinated adult birds and 100% in young chicks causing seasonal epidemics that devastate flocks and threaten food security and income for rural families. Although vaccines exist to prevent Newcastle disease, traditional options are heat-sensitive and require constant refrigeration, making them impractical in regions where cold chain logistics are unreliable or unavailable. KUKUSTAR addresses these limitations by offering a thermo-stable vaccine alternative. While it still requires refrigeration for long-term storage to maintain its 12-month shelf life, KUKUSTAR remains effective for up to 21 days at room temperature in its lyophilized form, compared to conventional vaccines that become ineffective within a day under similar conditions. After the vaccine is reconstituted with water, it can be used for up to 72 hours, a significant improvement over the 2-hour usability window of standard vaccines. This extended usability removes one of the main barriers to vaccine access in rural communities, allowing for more reliable and widespread vaccination. To further enhance accessibility and affordability, KUKUSTAR is packaged in smaller, divisible units and distributed through community markets. This last-mile distribution approach ensures that even the most remote and resource-limited farmers can protect their poultry, ultimately supporting improved nutrition, income generation, and poverty reduction in the region.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Fish Cold Storage for Lake Victoria Communities
core_fields.description: GreenTech will deploy two solar-powered cold storage containers in Usenge Beach, Kenya, together with its local partner, Samaki Village. Initial daily throughput of 3 tons will scale to 6 tons within the first year. Today, over 14 tons/day are lost or downgraded due to ice dependency and grid instability. Our Pay-As-You-Store model replaces ice logistics with solar-battery refrigeration, reducing food loss, improving food safety, cutting emissions, increasing fisher incomes, and establishing a scalable blueprint solution.
core_fields.abstract: Usenge Beach, which handles nearly half of Kenya s Lake Victoria fish catch, faces severe cold-chain gaps. This leads to 31% of Samaki Village and 13% of wholesale market daily produce (8 & 30 tons, respectively) being lost, and additional 27% being sold in distress. This local challenge reflects a much wider issue: in emerging markets, up to 40% of food is lost post-harvest (FAO), representing not only wasted nutrition and income but also avoidable emissions. GreenTech addresses this through solar-powered, fully containerized cold rooms, supported by battery storage and optional grid backup. The development of the solution was triggered by a dialogue with World Bank Group staff, highlighting the need for a sustainable cooling solution to be set in rural areas and replace diesel-based solutions. This led IFC to finance GreenTech s successful 2024 pilot of its solar transport cooling units in Nairobi. Unlike current local solutions - typically unreliable, low-capacity, and unaffordable - GreenTech s system is predictable, reliable, and scalable. Containerization enables rapid deployment, easy replication, and synergy with upstream and downstream cold-chain links, including refrigerated transport. Offered as a Pay-As-You-Store service at less than half current cost, cold storage becomes accessible also to small fishers. Benefits are expected to be immediate and lasting: increased cold storage capacity (in Usenge from 1 to +5 ton/day), reduced food loss (IFC pilot showed -75%), higher incomes for fishers, safer food for consumers, and lower emissions from spoilage and transport. The model also creates a replicable blueprint for cold-chain development in emerging markets.

core_fields.title: Nutrigrab App
core_fields.description: Nutrigrab is a digital platform that reduces food waste and improves farmer incomes by redistributing surplus and soon-to-expire food to communities, processors, and social enterprises. The app connects smallholder farmers directly to buyers, enables pay-per-use access to farm equipment, and supports last-mile logistics. By closing food system gaps, Nutrigrab increases food access, cuts waste, and strengthens local circular economies.
core_fields.abstract: Nutrigrab is a digital innovation addressing one of the most persistent drivers of poverty and environmental harm: food loss, fragmented markets, and limited access to productive assets for smallholder farmers. Across low-income communities, large volumes of nutritious food are wasted due to poor market linkages, lack of storage, and inefficient distribution, while farmers struggle to sell produce, access equipment, or earn stable incomes. This paradox undermines food security, household incomes, and climate resilience. Nutrigrab solves this by using a technology-enabled circular food system. The platform aggregates surplus and soon-to-expire food from farmers, food processors, and retailers, matches it in real time with buyers, schools, social enterprises, and community distributors, and coordinates last-mile delivery. Embedded digital marketplaces allow farmers to sell produce directly, bypassing exploitative intermediaries. A pay-per-use equipment module enables farmers to rent machinery on demand, lowering production costs and improving productivity without upfront capital. The innovation is driven by systems thinking and data science insights: inefficiencies in food systems are not caused by scarcity, but by poor coordination. Nutrigrab applies digital matching, demand forecasting, and asset-sharing models to close these gaps. Immediate benefits include increased farmer incomes, reduced post-harvest losses, improved food access for schools and vulnerable communities, and lower food prices for consumers. Long-term benefits include reduced greenhouse gas emissions from wasted food, stronger local economies, improved nutrition outcomes, and scalable circular economy infrastructure that transforms how food is produced, distributed, and consumed.

core_fields.title: Scaling Agroforestry in Schools and Communities of Ludewa.
core_fields.description: PADECO will expand its successful Food and Forest Gardens program by setting up 8 agroforestry Food and Forest gardens in 5 primary schools and 3 farmer groups in Ludewa District. In the pilot phase, the project increased student dietary diversity by 40% and farm household income by 15%. This scale-up will focus on climate-smart food production using agroforestry, water-efficient farming, and crop diversity, benefiting over 2,600 people through better diets and sustainable livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: Since 2020, PADECO successfully implemented the Food and Forest Gardens Initiative in 10 villages in Njombe reaching over 3,000 people. The project improved student dietary diversity by 40%, increased household income by 15%, strengthened local food production using simple, low-cost, nature-based farming methods. Based on this proven success, PADECO seeks to scale this model to Ludewa District, where food insecurity and child malnutrition remain persistent. Many families in Ludewa rely on a narrow range of staple foods like ugali and beans, while schools struggle to provide nutritious meals. Farmers face declining soil fertility, unreliable rainfall, and limited access to extension services (Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey 2022). These challenges continue to limit dietary diversity, productivity, and household income. The project will expand agroforestry-based food gardens in 5 schools and 3 farmer groups using a tree-crop integration system. This includes planting 100,000 perennial fruit trees (papaya, avocado, mango), combined with vegetables (leafy greens, cabbage, carrots, tomatoes). This improves year-round food availability, rebuilds soil fertility, increases water retention, and strengthens biodiversity. The main innovation is the Green Facilitator Network, supported by simple SMS Mobile Knowledge System. 16 trained facilitators will guide daily garden activities, while receiving weekly text messages from PADECO with practical tips and quick support. This low-tech approach uses normal SMS, making it accessible for rural schools and farmers, ensuring learning continues beyond project visits. Immediate benefits include improved school meals, better dietary diversity, and income generation. Long-term benefits include healthier soil, climate resilience, and a self-sustaining food system.

core_fields.abstract: This project addresses poverty, and household malnutrition faced by women farmers in Dalun who depend on rain-fed agriculture. Our innovative solution integrates a 50-30-20 harvest and 50-50 profit model ensuring 30% of produce feeds families, 50% generate income, and 20% secures seeds with a simple technology bundle of motorized irrigation and mobile-based marketing. The immediate benefits include increased household income and improved daily nutrition, and Sustainable outcomes involve a self-funding farm, year-round food security, women's economic independence, and climate-resilient agriculture, creating lasting impact for farmers, families, and the entire community. Savana Signatures have implemented the Innovative for transformative project where we supported 5 women to gain financial independence and conflict resolution skills. We also improved women s loan management within VSLA groups.
