core_fields.title: Empowering the Apiculture Sector in the GlobalSouth with Affordable, Usable AI Quality and Transparency Tools
core_fields.description: HoneyAI empowers apiculture cooperatives, associations, and producers in the Global South (Chile, Argentina, Libya, Emirates) with an affordable, AI-powered device to analyze honey quality and communicate transparency to consumers. Building on proven adoption in Europe, the project democratizes pollen analysis for non-expert producers, enabling classification and valorization of monofloral honeys. By combining on-site analysis with QR-based consumer information, HoneyAI increases producer income, strengthens sustainable apiculture, supports pollination, and improves access to fair and exporting markets.
core_fields.abstract: Pollen analysis (melissopalynology) is a widely recognized method used to determine the botanical and geographical origins of honey. By identifying and quantifying pollen grains present in honey, this technique allows classification of honeys and quality assessment, also supports authenticity control, and helps assign value and labelling. In Europe, pollen analysis is an essential harmonized practice within a mature and well-regulated honey market, where it underpins honey classification, pricing, and labelling constraints. However, pollen analysis is complex, highly manual, time-consuming, and dependent on a very limited number of trained experts. Analyses are expensive (40-110euros), typically outsourced to specialized laboratories, and inaccessible for most producers. Outside Europe, particularly Global South, pollen analysis is rarely used beyond academic research, preventing producers from correctly assessing, valorizing, and/or exporting their honey. HoneyAI overcomes these limitations by automating pollen analysis using artificial intelligence and automated digital microscopy. Our device autonomously scans honey sample, identifies pollen types, and delivers standardized results on-site, without requiring expert users, at 12euros. Originally developed and validated in Europe, HoneyAI is affordable, easy to use, and designed for cooperatives, associations, and honey producers rather than laboratories or universities. Beyond pollen analysis (https://youtu.be/9Yinkq6vXVs), it enables additional quality assessments such as color grading, yeast counting, bees diseases detection and crystallization monitoring. By making this science accessible, HoneyAI allows producers to create value through honey characterization, reduces dependency on laboratories, supports transparency through QR-based consumer information. Increased profitability strengthens the beekeeping sector, reduces fraud, promotes informed consumer choices, and supports agriculture through enhanced biodiversity/pollination.

core_fields.title: Greener Futures: Promoting the Sustainable Adoption of African Indigenous Vegetables and Finger Millet in Zimbabwe.
core_fields.description: The environment, food, and nutritional security are under threat from climate change. This project will focus on the promotion and enhancement of the adoption of nutritious and medicinal African indigenous vegetables (amaranth and spider plant) and finger millet that can thrive in the face of climate change. This will increase its production to meet the recent surge in demand and improve livelihoods, and ensure that nutritious food is produced in a sustainable way.
core_fields.abstract: The environment, food, and nutrition security are under threat, especially in this climate change era and lifestyle shifting that is taking place. Therefore, this project will focus on the promotion and enhancement adoption of nutritious African Indigenous Vegetables (Amaranth and spider plant) and finger millet. Specifically, the project will have components of seed systems, agroecology, value addition, business, and marketing of the products. This will ensure that nutritious food is produced in a healthy environment. On the breeding and seed systems component, there will be an improvement of the finger millet variety (early maturity and high grain Fe and Zn content). This variety will be distributed to smallholder farmers so that they can grow it under our technical advisory services. The agroecology party will be an integration of crop and animal husbandry, where, in this case, finger millet fodder will be used as livestock feed. Furthermore, the growing of spider plant attracts bees during their flowering, hence apiculture will be initiated that will be organic, as the production of spider plant will be merely organic (no chemicals applied). There will be value addition to the amaranth seed to produce gluten-free amaranth flour and popped amaranth seed that will be consumed as a breakfast cereal or snack. On the business side, farmers will be taught how to preserve leaves (amaranth and spider plant) and grain (amaranth and finger millet) to make money out of it. Leaves will be dried to meet both local and international markets.

core_fields.title: Transforming Malnutrition Treatment Through Locally Sourced, Plant-Based RUTF
core_fields.description: This project will test and scale two plant-based therapeutic foods to expand access to lifesaving malnutrition treatment. By using locally available crops instead of imported dairy, these formulations cut costs, strengthen local manufacturing, and significantly reduce environmental impact. A large effectiveness study and strategic policy engagement will generate the evidence needed for national and global adoption, enabling far more children to receive the treatment they need to survive and thrive.
core_fields.abstract: Every year, millions of children suffer from severe malnutrition, but most never receive the treatment they need. The main reason is simple: the therapeutic food (RUTF) used to save their lives is expensive and often hard to produce or transport. Milk powder and peanuts two key ingredients make RUTF costly and vulnerable to supply shortages. When these run out, treatment stops. Our solution is to create new versions of RUTF using locally available, plant-based ingredients such as soy, maize, and chickpea. These ingredients are cheaper, easier to source in the Global South, and far less affected by global supply disruptions. Early research shows that these novel RUTF recipes using plant-based ingredients can be just as effective for treating malnutrition as the standard RUTF, while costing up to 25 30% less. This idea emerged in response to growing interest from governments and global agencies to have less-expensive, locally produced RUTF product options. What makes this innovative is that we are not proposing a single new recipe. Instead, we are creating a flexible set of formulas that countries can adapt based on local supply chains, costs, and preferences. While a few plant-based RUTFs have been tested, results have been mixed: some formulations show promise, others fall short, and none have yet demonstrated the combination of effectiveness, scalability, and evidence needed for WHO approval. The benefits are both immediate and long-lasting: 25-30% more children will be able to be treated given the treatment products are less costly and with simpler and shorter supply chains.

core_fields.title: Turning Africa's Indigenous Food Crops Into Mainstream Nutrition
core_fields.description: Seliroko will establish pilot production of affordable, nutritious packaged foods created from indigenous African food crops. The pilot operation will be based in Nyamira County, Kenya, processing 4 tonnes monthly of cassava, sweet potato, matoke, and other traditional crops into 20,000 packets of snacks and noodles. We source from smallholder farmers practicing monitored regenerative agriculture. Our project will provide the mass market with nutritious, world class foods at prices families can afford.
core_fields.abstract: Africa's indigenous food crops remain marginalized despite superior nutritional profiles. These crops are relegated to subsistence farming and rural consumption while the demand for nutritious foods is skyrocketing, especially in urban markets. Smallholder farmers growing the crops receive minimal value (raw commodity prices), while consumers seeking convenient packaged foods have limited options. This marginalization persists despite indigenous crops offering exceptional nutrition: naturally gluten-free, rich in resistant starch, high in essential vitamins. How We're Solving It: Seliroko establishes a versatile food processing facility transforming indigenous crops into mainstream packaged foods. We process raw crops, then manufacture diverse products: cookies, noodles, chips, dried vegetables, and expandable product lines. Scientific/Technical Insight: Indigenous food crops deliver superior nutrition. For example, cassava provides resistant starch for digestive health, sweet potato delivers high Vitamin A critical for child development, matoke offers sustained energy with lower glycemic impact than refined grains. These crops are climate-resilient requiring 40-60% less water than crops like wheat, thriving in marginal soils. Processing technology is proven globally. Market validation exists: our cookie recipes tested positively with 200+ returning customers in two months. Immediate & Sustainable Benefits: For farmers: Premium markets for indigenous food crops, year-round predictable demand, recognition of crop value beyond subsistence, incentives for regenerative practices. For consumers: Nutritious, gluten-free alternatives, supporting local agriculture through purchasing decisions. For environment: Climate-resilient crops reduce water usage; zero-waste processing converts byproducts into animal feed. For food systems: Demonstrating indigenous crops are commercially viable in processed foods, encouraging investment, and shifting agricultural patterns.

core_fields.title: AI-Powered Digital Twins for Climate-Resilient, Nutritious and Equitable Food Systems
core_fields.description: WeavAir s FoodTwin is an AI-powered digital twin platform that helps farmers and food system actors in the Global South produce more nutritious food using fewer resources. By combining satellite imagery, low-cost sensors, and predictive climate and crop models, the solution increases yields by up to 25%, reduces water and input use by up to 40%, and cuts food loss by up to 20%, while improving farmer incomes and climate resilience at scale.
core_fields.abstract: Food systems in the Global South face growing climate volatility, soil degradation, water scarcity, rising input costs, and high food loss driving lower yields, declining nutritional quality, and unstable farmer incomes. Smallholder and mid-scale farmers, who produce most of the region s food, often lack timely, affordable, and actionable information to manage these risks, resulting in inefficient resource use and reduced food availability. WeavAir s FoodTwin addresses this challenge by creating a real-time, AI-powered digital twin of farms and surrounding food systems. The platform integrates satellite hyperspectral imagery, low-cost field sensors, drone data, and more than a decade of climate, soil, and crop performance data. Advanced machine learning models translate this data into clear, actionable recommendations such as optimal crop and variety selection, irrigation and fertilization timing, early warning of drought, floods, pests, and disease, and improved harvest and post-harvest decisions. The scientific insight behind FoodTwin is that hyper-local environmental signals, when continuously monitored and modeled together rather than in isolation, can accurately predict crop performance, nutritional outcomes, and climate risks weeks in advance. This enables proactive, regenerative decision-making instead of reactive responses after losses occur. Immediate benefits include 10 25% yield increases in nutritious crops, 20 40% reductions in water and input use, 10 20% lower food loss, and 15 35% higher farmer incomes. Sustained benefits include improved soil health, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, greater climate resilience, and more affordable, reliable access to safe and nutritious food for communities at scale.

core_fields.title: Scaling Village Input Fairs: Transforming Last-Mile Agricultural Input Access in Mali through Market-Based Solutions
core_fields.description: The Village Input Fair Fund (VIFF) solves the persistent last-mile market failure of agricultural input markets in rural West Africa. VIFF, through a network of local social enterprises, organizes one-day markets post-harvest, aggregating farmer demand to attract agricultural input dealers to remote villages. Having proven the model through two RCTs in Mali (52% production increase), this project will support scaling to reach 240 villages in Mali in 2027.
core_fields.abstract: The persistent failure of agricultural input markets remains one of the most intractable barriers to food security, economic growth, and poverty alleviation in Sub-Saharan Africa. Fertilizer use in the region is five times lower than the global average, causing low yields and production. Markets fail because farmers lack liquidity during the planting season, and input dealers refuse to serve rural areas due to high transaction costs and uncertain demand. VIFF re-engineers the market structure. ​​We organize one-day markets immediately post-harvest, bringing together farmers to attract agricultural input dealers to remote villages. Farmers place orders with a 10% deposit, securing delivery for the next planting season and aggregating demand to make bulk delivery profitable for dealers. VIFF selects dealers through a transparent license auction system, ensuring sustainability and proving the commercial viability of rural markets. Two rigorous RCTs have served to refine and validate our model. Evidence shows VIFs drive a 24-28% increase in fertilizer purchases and a 52% increase in agricultural production for participating farmers. Agro-input dealers, a group often overlooked, see estimated annual income increases of $16,491. Furthermore, by integrating organic producers like Elephant Vert, we are transitioning farmers toward regenerative practices and low-toxicity pesticides, ensuring long-term soil health and environmental sustainability. VIFF is building on this success by expanding in Mali. We also plan to replicate the model in Ghana and Cote d Ivoire, demonstrating the cross-border applicability of our approach. We will continue to conduct rigorous research to drive consistent enhancements to our model.

core_fields.title: Reviving Degraded Land through Soil Biology
core_fields.description: This project establishes an agri-waste recovery facility that converts organic residues into bio-complete compost for smallholder farmers, replacing chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Farmers receive training on regenerative practices to improve yields and livelihoods. Compost use and impact are tracked through a digital platform using satellite imagery, microscopy, and sensors, creating a living library of farmers restoring soil health and adopting sustainable agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation addresses the growing problem of degraded and compacted agricultural land, declining crop yields, farmer vulnerability, and the reduced nutritional quality of food. Years of heavy reliance on chemical fertilizers and pesticides have damaged soil biology, increased pest resistance, harmed farmer health, and left soils unable to retain nutrients, water, or carbon. At the same time, over 550 million tons of agricultural and organic waste are generated annually in Pakistan, much of which is burned, contributing to smog and climate impacts. This problem is solved by restoring soil health through Soil Food Web based practices, inspired by Dr. Elaine Ingham s internationally recognized methods. Using scientifically developed bio-complete compost and compost extracts, verified through microscopy, the solution rebuilds living soil by reintroducing beneficial microorganisms. Insights from global practitioners, including the recent visit of UK-based Wild Soils founder Nick Padwick, validated the effectiveness of these methods through proven on-farm success.} By converting agricultural waste into high-quality compost instead of burning it, the approach simultaneously tackles waste mismanagement and soil degradation. Healthy soils reduce the need for chemical inputs, improve natural pest resistance, and revive dead, compacted land. Immediate and sustainable benefits include improved yields and reduced input costs for farmers, safer working conditions and better health, nutrient-dense food for consumers, practical learning opportunities for schools and communities, and climate benefits through increased soil carbon storage and reduced methane and air pollution. This nature-based solution strengthens food security while restoring ecosystems.

core_fields.title: Community-Led Biomass Cooling for Affordable, Low-Carbon Post-Harvest Refrigeration
core_fields.description: This project delivers community-led, biomass-powered adsorption refrigeration using cocoa husk waste to cut post-harvest losses in Colombian agriculture. Piloted with Asocpraur (700+ farmers) in Urab , it replaces unstable grid electricity, saving ~1,500 2,000 kWh/ton-year, reducing banana losses by 20 30% (>1,000 t/year), increasing farm-gate prices by 10 15%, and cutting CO₂ emissions. The model advances SDGs 2, 7, 12, 13, and 8 while improving rural income stability and social well-being.
core_fields.abstract: Post-harvest losses and unreliable energy access are critical constraints for Colombian agriculture, particularly in tropical regions such as Urab , where high temperatures accelerate fruit ripening and grid electricity is costly and unstable. Solar alternatives are often ineffective due to persistent cloud cover and heavy rainfall. As a result, small and medium farmers lose product quality, market value, and income. This innovation introduces a community-led, biomass-powered refrigeration system based on double-stage ammonia adsorption cooling, using cocoa pod husk waste as the primary energy source. Cocoa husks are generated in large volumes by farmer associations and currently decompose in the field, creating environmental impacts. Their high calorific value enables efficient heat-driven refrigeration without reliance on fossil fuels or grid electricity. The system converts agricultural waste into reliable, low-cost cooling energy to preserve bananas and other perishable crops at optimal temperatures, slowing ripening and reducing spoilage. Scientific insight from thermally driven adsorption cycles enables refrigeration using low-grade heat rather than electricity, making the solution particularly suitable for rural, energy-constrained environments. Immediate benefits include reduced post-harvest losses, improved product quality, higher and more stable farm-gate prices, and energy autonomy for farmer cooperatives. Long-term benefits include lower carbon emissions, reduced organic waste pollution, diversified farmer income streams beyond cocoa price volatility, and improved community resilience. The cooperative business model ensures equitable access, local ownership, and scalability across multiple crops and regions.

core_fields.title: Empowering small producers through digital traceability for fair and sustainable food systems
core_fields.description: OBENS is a digital traceability platform that strengthens the sustainability and fairness of natural ingredients in food supply chains. By mapping each step from producer to buyer, OBENS brings transparency, verifies good practices, and ensures fair value distribution for smallholders. Our project empowers rural communities, improves market access, and enables companies to source responsibly while monitoring carbon, social impact, and environmental risks, contributing to safer, more equitable, and resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Food supply chains for natural ingredients often lack transparency, which leaves small producers underpaid, buyers without reliable data and consumers unaware of the environmental and social impact behind their products. This opacity leads to unfair value distribution, weak market access for rural communities, and inadequate monitoring of sustainability risks, including carbon emissions, biodiversity loss, and labor conditions. OBENS tackles this problem through a digital traceability and sustainability platform that maps every step of an ingredient s journey, from farm to table. Using structured data collection, automated workflows, geolocation, and real-time dashboards, OBENS captures verified information on quality checks, yields, pricing, carbon footprint, and compliance. This insight came from extensive on-field work with cooperatives in Morocco, where traditional data reporting was fragmented, manual, and inaccessible to producers and buyers. Our solution gives producers visibility into their own operations, strengthens their negotiating power, and helps them meet growing international market requirements. For buyers, OBENS reduces due diligence costs, increases trust in suppliers, and enables responsible sourcing aligned with ESG, EU deforestation regulation, and corporate sustainability reporting needs. Immediate benefits: - Producers gain digital records, fairer pricing, and access to premium markets. - Buyers obtain trusted data on origin, practices, and social/environmental performance. - Communities benefit from increased income and economic inclusion. Long-term benefits: - More equitable value chains that reward sustainable farming. - Reduction of environmental risks through carbon and impact monitoring. - Stronger rural resilience, better food safety, and consumer trust in sustainable products.

core_fields.title: Replacing Crop-Residue Burning with Low-Cost Biochar to Strengthen Smallholder Food Security and Livelihoods in Punjab
core_fields.description: The project deploys a decentralized biochar production and soil application system in Punjab to replace open-field crop residue burning within short cropping windows. Trained village entrepreneurs use flame-curtain pyrolysis to convert residues into biochar that is applied to agricultural soils, reducing smoke pollution and storing stable carbon. The pilot evaluates operational performance, soil response, and labor economics while improving soil function and providing predictable, daily-wage aligned income for smallholder farming communities.
core_fields.abstract: Crop residue burning is a widespread, low-cost practice used by smallholder farmers to clear fields between cropping cycles, but it drives severe air pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and soil nutrient loss. Despite restrictions, many alternatives fail at village level because they do not fit short cropping windows, labor constraints, or smallholder economics. Our innovation is an end-to-end package that enables any village team to manage agricultural waste without burning, improve soil health, and earn predictable daily-wage income linked to verified outcomes. Agronomy innovation: We use a low-capital, manually operated flame-curtain biochar production methodology designed for rapid, decentralized deployment. Crop residues are converted into biochar and applied back to farmland, improving soil function while storing stable carbon. We are pursuing patent protection for elements of this production methodology and operating system. Technology innovation: We integrate field operations with digital MRV that combines an app-based workflow with satellite-enabled oversight. Using PlantVillage, each step is captured with geo-tagged, time-stamped records, automated consistency checks, and audit logs to create batch-level traceability from residue collection to soil application. Financial innovation: We advance carbon-linked payments as stable, daily-wage aligned income at the time of work, rather than waiting for delayed credit sale proceeds. This reduces livelihood risk, strengthens adoption, and aligns incentives with verifiable environmental outcomes. Immediate and sustainable benefits include reduced smoke exposure, improved soil performance, durable carbon storage, and new local jobs tied to climate-smart agriculture.

core_fields.title: Scaling Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices for Resilient Food Systems in Rwanda
core_fields.description: Scaling Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices for Resilient Food Systems in Rwanda aims to revolutionize agriculture by introducing innovative, sustainable practices. By leveraging regenerative techniques like hydroponic fodder and circular farming, the project enhances food security, reduces environmental impact, and supports farmers livelihoods. This initiative addresses climate challenges, fosters resilient food systems, and aligns with global efforts to ensure equitable access to safe, nutritious, and sustainable food for all.
core_fields.abstract: Agriculture in Rwanda faces significant challenges, including climate change, soil degradation, and insufficient sustainable practices, threatening food security and livelihoods. Farmers struggle to maintain productivity amidst erratic weather and resource scarcity, while traditional farming methods contribute to environmental harm. Our innovation, Scaling Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices, addresses these issues by integrating regenerative and circular farming methods. Solutions include hydroponic fodder systems that use 90% less water, goat feedlot farming to optimize livestock productivity, and repurposing agricultural waste into organic fertilizers to improve soil health. These techniques enhance efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and support climate resilience. This approach was inspired by the need to align sustainable food production with environmental conservation. Through scientific insight and practical innovation, we empower farmers to adopt practices that improve yields while mitigating climate impacts. Immediate benefits include increased productivity and reduced resource use for farmers, while long-term outcomes involve improved soil health, higher incomes, and environmental conservation. By fostering sustainable food systems, we contribute to healthier communities, a thriving economy, and a resilient environment, benefiting society at large.

core_fields.title: Empowering Rural Farmers with Precision Agriculture for Sustainable Food Security and Climate Resilience, Awutu Senya, Ghana.
core_fields.description: Ento Organics is empowering rural farmers in rural Ghana through precision farming and agroforestry solutions. Our project integrates advanced technology, including IoT devices and a mobile app, to enhance crop yields, promote climate resilience, and improve food security. By providing training and tools, we enable farmers to adopt sustainable practices, reduce environmental impact, and increase income. This project aims to scale innovative farming solutions, benefiting communities and contributing to a sustainable food system.
core_fields.abstract: Ento Organics is addressing the urgent challenge of climate change's impact on smallholder female farmers in Ghana, particularly those in drought-prone areas like the Awutu Senya East District. These farmers, who make up a significant portion of the agricultural workforce, face declining yields and incomes due to increasingly unpredictable weather patterns. This situation directly impacts food security and livelihoods in these communities. Ento Organics' innovative solution combines precision farming techniques with agroforestry practices. Their digital platform leverages IoT weather stations and AI algorithms to provide farmers with hyper-localized, real-time data and personalized recommendations for crop and pest management. This data-driven approach empowers farmers to adapt their practices to changing climate conditions and optimize their yields. Additionally, the integration of agroforestry, which involves planting trees alongside crops, further enhances climate resilience. Agroforestry improves soil health, conserves water, increases biodiversity, and provides additional income sources for farmers. This holistic approach stems from the recognition that traditional farming methods are becoming increasingly vulnerable to climate change and that empowering women, who are essential to Ghana's agricultural sector, is crucial for sustainable development. The benefits of this approach are significant and wide-ranging: farmers experience increased yields and incomes, contributing to poverty alleviation and improved food security; improved soil health and water conservation ensure the long-term sustainability of agriculture; enhanced biodiversity strengthens the local ecosystem; and the focus on female empowerment promotes gender equality. By combining technological innovation with sustainable practices and community engagement, Ento Organics offers a comprehensive solution for resilient food systems.

core_fields.title: StepUP4Ag
core_fields.description: Intensive farming has degraded soil quality, undermining food production, and is one of the major contributors to climate change, while also bearing the brunt of its consequences. Many organizations aim to scale regenerative agriculture; however, the transition also requires the creation of sufficient, high-quality, independent advisory services. This last element of expert technical advice is often overlooked and StepUp4Ag aims to address this critical knowledge gap to ensure the resilience of our future agricultural systems.
core_fields.abstract: Accelerated by climate change, soil degradation threatens the viability and sustainability of European agriculture. Farming practices are linked to ~11% of Europe s total greenhouse gas emissions, and over 60% of EU soils are considered unhealthy, with soil degradation costing the EU an estimated 50 billion/year. While farmers are at the forefront of this transition, they currently lack the necessary technical support to enact this change and adopt soil-positive practices. Their initial transition phase is fraught with risk but also ripe for transformative change, provided there is adequate support to tackle the Valley of Death and mitigate its challenges. From research conducted through EIT Food s Consumer Observatory, we know that EU consumers feel farmers are continuously blamed for environmental problems and acknowledge that the agricultural transition should not be the farmers sole responsibility. Long-term, consumers are convinced the transition will be beneficial for both farmers and citizens. StepUP4Ag is a collaborative education initiative which builds on EIT Food s existing body of work to scale regenerative agriculture. This program strengthens the capacity and capabilities of technical advisors to support farmers during this critical period, ensuring they have the knowledge to recommend sustainable practices aligned with the farmer s crops, local community, soils, and weather patterns. Based on inputs from our research and industry partners, Poland and Turkey have been identified as two countries currently lacking in sufficiently skilled agricultural advisors. This targeted strategy ensures long-term impact by co-designing solutions with local actors, sharing knowledge and pooling resources for collective progress across geographies.

core_fields.title: Upcycling Crop Processing Wastes Into Nutritious and Affordable Food Products for Sustainable Food Systems in Africa: A Circular Economy Approach
core_fields.description: This project focuses on transforming crop (yam, cassava and potato) processing wastes into nutritious, affordable food products to promote sustainable food systems in Africa. By leveraging innovative upcycling techniques, it aims to reduce food waste, enhance food security and create economic opportunities for local communities, particularly women and youth. The initiative addresses environmental sustainability while improving access to high-quality, cost-effective food options for vulnerable population
core_fields.abstract: This innovation transforms agricultural food waste particularly cassava, yam and potato peels into affordable, nutrient-dense food products. In Africa, where these staple crops are widely consumed, their peels are often discarded improperly, contributing to environmental pollution and the loss of valuable nutrients. Cassava peels alone account for over 14 million tonnes annually in Nigeria, representing 10 15% of tuber weight, while yam and potato peels add another 10 20%, exacerbating food waste challenges. The problem being solved is multi-fold: reducing food waste and addressing malnutrition in resource-limited communities. The solution involves upcycling these nutrient-rich peels, which are rich in dietary fibre, polyphenols, vitamins and minerals, into safe, cost-effective food products using a circular economy approach. Innovative processing techniques, such as detoxification, drying and milling ensure the products are safe, nutritious and suitable for consumption. Scientific and technical insights underpin this solution, including the understanding that food processing by-products contain significant untapped nutritional potential. By leveraging low-cost, scalable food technologies, these peels are repurposed efficiently while achieving 70% waste-to-product conversion and improving fibre content by 20%. The immediate and sustainable benefits include affordable, high-quality nutrition for consumers, particularly in low-income communities and additional income streams for farmers and small-scale producers who supply or process peels. Schools and communities benefit from improved food security, while the environment gains from reduced food waste and lower greenhouse gas emissions. This innovation supports sustainable development and resource use efficiency.

core_fields.title: Transforming Unused Urban Lands into Inclusive Community Farms.
core_fields.description: The project aims to transform unused urban lands into inclusive community farms across seven cities in India. Using innovative techniques like greenhouse farming, aquaponics, and composting, it ensures food safety, climate action, and community empowerment. The initiative engages diverse stakeholders, including women and marginalized groups, connects farms to local markets, and promotes sustainable urban living. By fostering food security, environmental restoration, and economic resilience, the project serves as a replicable model for sustainable city
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Urban areas in India face significant challenges, including underutilized wastelands, limited access to fresh and nutritious food, and increasing environmental degradation. Vulnerable communities, especially in food deserts, struggle with food insecurity, while climate change intensifies these issues. Additionally, urban spaces are often poorly integrated into sustainable food systems, leaving their potential untapped. Solution: This project transforms urban wastelands such as unused land near water bodies, parks, and former waste dumping yards into inclusive community farms. By employing innovative techniques like greenhouse farming, aquaponics, composting, and low-water irrigation systems, the initiative ensures efficient and sustainable food production. It integrates these farms with neighborhood farmers markets, creating a direct supply chain and ensuring fair pricing for both producers and consumers. Innovation and Benefits: The project s inclusivity ensures participation by women, youth, and marginalized groups, empowering them through training in sustainable farming practices and entrepreneurial skills. Community-based organizations (CBOs) will manage the farms with technical guidance from ESAF Foundation, ensuring long-term sustainability. Immediate benefits include improved access to safe, nutritious food, enhanced community cohesion, and the creation of sustainable income opportunities. Over time, the project will foster environmental benefits such as increased urban greenery, reduced waste, and lower carbon footprints through localized food systems. Scientific Insight: The integration of greenhouse farming and aquaponics allows for resource-efficient, high-yield food production, while composting recycles organic waste, promoting regenerative practices. This innovative combination addresses food security, climate resilience, and urban sustainability, benefiting communities, the environment, and society at large.

core_fields.title: 100% solar powered cold rooms for producers and vendors to store and preserve fresh fruits, vegetables and other perishable foods.
core_fields.description: We provide solar powered cold rooms on a Pay-as-you basis for fish, dairy, fruit and vegetable producers. The solar powered cold store is an ideal answer to the needs of Congolese farmers as it adequately addresses the problem of post-harvest losses of fish, dairy, fruit, vegetables and other perishable goods. In these, the harvest is placed in clean plastic crates, which are then stacked inside the cold room.
core_fields.abstract: According to the Rockefeller Foundation; According to the Food Waste and Spoilage Initiative 2014, approximately 50% of all horticultural produce is lost or wasted before reaching the consumer in developing countries, intensifying poverty, hunger and malnutrition. This affects 470 million smallholder farmers, retailers and food supply chain actors. In Congo, food spoilage affects approximately 3 million smallholder farmers and supply chain actors. Reducing post-harvest losses is essential to improve the livelihoods, nutrition and resilience of farmers and communities. The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) estimates that a 10% reduction in global food losses could lead to an 11% reduction in hunger and a 4% reduction in child malnutrition worldwide. In Congo, a 35% reduction in post-harvest tomato loss alone would create a supply of vitamin A for up to 1.1 million children per day. For Congolese smallholder farmers, this 50% loss of fruits and vegetables results in a 25% loss of their annual income. The high rate of post-harvest losses is due to a combination of factors, including the lack of affordable cold storage at key points in the food supply chain and the lack of knowledge on proper harvesting and post-harvest handling. Current post-harvest losses pose a threat to the population in terms of food and financial stability. Post-harvest loss is a threat to food security, economic stability and environmental protection that affects most farming communities in Africa and around the world.

core_fields.title: System fro the treatment of high salinity in irrigation water, and make the water usable for irrigation.
core_fields.description: EZPack s solution for treating high-salinity irrigation water helps stabilize and strengthen local food supply chains. Delivered off-grid and at lower costs, it boosts crop yields for small-to-medium farmers, improving resilience, livelihoods, and gender equity. Its rapid deployment and pay-as-you-use model expand purified irrigation water access, enhancing climate resilience and increasing food security. Over five years, scalable deployments will transform thousands of hectares, underpinning more reliable and diverse agricultural production.
core_fields.abstract: High salinity in irrigation water is a growing global challenge, reducing crop yields and threatening food security. Climate change exacerbates this issue through altered precipitation patterns, increased evaporation, and rising sea levels. More than 1.4 billion people live in water-vulnerable areas, and mounting salinity levels directly undermine farmers capacity to produce food. In regions like Africa, smallholder farmers, including women, suffer from decreased yields, reduced income, and limited access to adequate nutrition. EZPack s solution treats high-salinity irrigation water to boost agricultural output. Its proprietary technology is a fully automated, off-grid water purification system. Supplying around 16 m of purified irrigation water per day enough for 11 to 22 hectares, depending on crop water requirements enables local farmers to increase productivity and enhance their resilience against climate impacts. Access to cleaner irrigation water strengthens the entire food supply chain: it allows farmers to stabilize yields, mitigate the impacts of drought and climate variability, and potentially improve livelihoods, food security, and gender equality. Rapid scaling and pay-as-you-use financing ensure that this technology remains accessible to small and medium growers, ultimately transforming local agriculture and sustaining reliable, diverse food production at scale.

core_fields.abstract: Approximately 47.4 million Americans live in food-insecure households, facing barriers to preparing healthy meals. To address this, EatWell developed the EatWell Community Kitchen, a video-based educational program paired with our meal kits. With support from the Seeding the Future 2021 Seed Grant, EatWell created Season 1, producing six culinary education videos to equip patients with skills to prepare culturally relevant, nutritious meals while fostering culinary confidence. The videos featured local chefs, nutritionists, and community leaders demonstrating EatWell recipes in an engaging, approachable format. Patients praised the relatable style, which made learning practical and enjoyable. Following the success of Season 1, EatWell secured a Small Business Community Champion Grant from Citizens Bank to produce seven additional videos, expanding the program s reach. With this grant, we aim to further improve patient culinary literacy and accessibility. Our plan includes: - Expanding the video library to cover all EatWell recipes (14 additional), empowering patients with the skills to prepare nutritious meals; and - Translating recipe booklets, educational materials, and video captions into five additional languages, ensuring inclusivity for diverse communities. Grounded in Experiential Learning Theory, the program emphasizes active, hands-on learning. Patients build essential cooking skills, develop healthier habits, and enjoy shared family meals that enhance confidence and agency. This approach benefits patients, reduces healthcare costs, and equips dietitians with culturally competent, multilingual resources. By addressing food insecurity and promoting better health outcomes, EatWell Community Kitchen delivers lasting value to individuals, communities, and the healthcare system.

core_fields.title: Ecotashira: Innovating Agro-Systems with Sustainable Substrates and Water-Efficient Solutions for Urban and Sustainable Agriculture
core_fields.description: Ecotashira develops innovative agro-systems for urban and sustainable agriculture, focusing on locally-produced substrates like Dactypeat, made from agricultural residues, as an eco-friendly alternative to imported materials. Our solutions optimize water efficiency and support resource-conscious farming, enabling greener practices in vertical and urban agriculture. By integrating sustainable substrates and economic watering techniques, Ecotashira fosters environmental stewardship and advances circular economy principles in the agricultural sector.
core_fields.abstract: Urbanization, water scarcity, and the improper disposal of agricultural residues are critical challenges facing modern agriculture. Palm tree residues, often burned in fields, contribute to environmental pollution and waste, while urban spaces lack practical solutions for growing food sustainably. These issues are compounded by the need to cultivate organic food in limited urban spaces, such as balconies, terraces, and indoor areas. Ecotashira provides an innovative solution by transforming palm tree residues into lightweight, water-retaining substrates, offering a sustainable alternative to imported materials like coconut fiber and sphagnum moss. These substrates are ideal for urban permaculture, enabling individuals, schools, and communities to grow organic food efficiently in compact spaces. By retaining water effectively, our solution reduces irrigation needs and supports water management in agriculture. This innovation is grounded in the principles of the circular economy, utilizing local agricultural waste to create valuable products. The scientific insight lies in leveraging the unique properties of palm tree residues to create substrates that balance water retention and aeration, ensuring optimal plant growth. Immediate benefits include empowering urban residents to grow their own food sustainably, providing farmers with a cost-effective planting medium, and reducing pollution from residue burning. Long-term benefits extend to improved environmental health, reduced dependence on imported substrates, and enhanced food security in urban areas. Ecotashira s approach integrates sustainability, innovation, and practicality to address key challenges in agriculture and urban living.

core_fields.title: Action for the conservation of Andean ancestral seeds with high nutritional value.
core_fields.description: We propose to transform food systems in Ecuador by adapting native seeds to climate change through plant breeding research in collaboration with an association of indigenous women farmers in the province of Cotopaxi. We promote sustainable agroecological practices, ensuring healthy and nutritious food, and increasing farmers' incomes. We prioritize people's health and the environment, and involve consumers, chefs and intermediaries as agents of change through their purchasing decisions.
core_fields.abstract: Food systems face critical challenges that threaten their sustainability, such as biodiversity loss, excessive use of chemical inputs, soil degradation and climate change. These problems affect soil fertility, increase disease and aggravate malnutrition. Our proposal is to adopt an agricultural model based on the recovery of ancestral knowledge, production and multiplication of native seeds, following the method of Humberto R os Labrada (Goldman Prize 2010), which focuses on participatory plant breeding. This process involves crossing native varieties from different regions through open pollination to select the plants most adapted to the local environment, diversify genetics and increase the nutritional value of the seeds. It also seeks to adapt varieties to the effects of climate change and extreme events. The model promotes collaboration between farmers, chefs, scientists and consumers, and seed exchange fairs facilitate access to knowledge and increase agrobiodiversity and productivity. This innovation is easily replicable as it is the farmers themselves who will be empowered to promote and train new agents of change in their surrounding communities. The transition from an industrial to a farmer-based agricultural system is essential to restore biodiversity, improve soil health, and improve the quality of life of communities. Immediate benefits include increased biodiversity, improved soil health, and greater food diversity, offering healthier and more sustainable food.

core_fields.title: Developing a Togotia digital knowledge platform for improved production, value addition and Utilization in Kenya
core_fields.description: Togotia is an underutilized forgotten African vegetable that is resilient to climate change compromising local and regional food production such as increasing frequency and intensity of drought, erratic rainfall and flooding, soil infertility, outbreak of pest and diseases, among others. It naturally grows in fallow fields maturing rapidly (<3 months), makes it an excellent candidate for exploring alternative land use in the face of climate change. Preliminary result indicates the possible existence of a high and low rainfall Togotia ecotypes with different morphometrics and the seed yield is 900 seeds per plant (Charimbu et al, unpublished data project report). Prototypes for Togotia value added products (dried vegetables seed cake and Togotia vegetable oil have been developed but they have not been validated. Additionally, local Togotia recipes are not well documented or validated. Therefore, the goal of the project is to validate the Togotia value added products (dried vegetables seed cake and Togotia vegetable oil) prototypes, validate the local and improved Togotia recipes and document the recipes and make the available via online platforms as virtual cookbooks.

core_fields.title: Using light for food and clean energy production for sustainable, nutritious, affordable, and trusted food systems.
core_fields.description: The goal of the proposed project is to enhance food security and access to clean energy in semi-arid regions of Kenya. The aim is to use an innovative semi-transparent, photocatalytic panel system to utilize excess solar radiation to enhance hydrogen production and promote crop growth. The panels provide shade, reduce water evaporation, and create a microclimate for dry areas, offering a multifunctional agricultural solution in sun-rich regions.
core_fields.abstract: Climate change causes a significant disruption of food and energy in dry areas due to temperature increases and low rainfall. This project proposes a novel agri-photocatalysis system, leveraging innovative integration of sustainable agriculture and energy production. Central to this initiative is a semi-transparent, photocatalytic panel system designed to utilize excess solar radiation to enhance hydrogen production and promote crop growth. The panels provide shade, reduce water evaporation, and create a microclimate for dry areas, offering a multifunctional agricultural solution in sun-rich regions. This project will produce a scalable, efficient solution to these pressing issues, reducing the land use conflicts between food and feed (energy) and optimizing land use for a sustainable, safe, and nutritious food system that is accessible, affordable, and trusted. The goal is to build a reproducible, upscalable prototype for future innovations in sustainable agriculture and renewable energy. The project aligns with SDG 7 (Clean Energy) and 2 (Zero Hunger.) The design targets an innovative system to optimize water use in agriculture, integrating solar energy solutions for enhanced water efficiency. Focuses on organic fruits and vegetables within the energy-food nexus. I will leverage my knowledge in material science, electronics and artificial photosynthesis to improve energy efficiency and integration within agricultural systems. I will involve a female PhD student in hydrogen production to identify the most efficient chemical pathways for converting solar energy into usable chemical energy, enhancing the project's energy output. The project will provide safe, nutritious food and clean energy to marginalized populations in semi-arid/arid regions

core_fields.title: Farming soil & sun - Agrivoltaic Project in Rural Spain
core_fields.description: We integrate agriculture and clean energy: our proprietary vertical photovoltaic panels enable solar electricity generation without shading the crops or occupying important productive farmlands and we do so by partnering and sharing our revenue with farmers. Our project with GFSC is to build the first agrivoltaic plant (100kWp) to support +5000 farmers and people in rural Spain. Ultimately, we will empower farmers & rural villages, generate clean energy & protect the food supply chain!
core_fields.abstract: PROBLEM: If you had one acre of land, would you use it for solar energy or for agriculture? This is a conflict that is currently exploding: conventional solar farms require large land areas, creating competition between electricity and food.It is clear: we need a solution, and we need it now! This is why we started Eki after 2 years of R&D about this issue in Harvard and MIT. SOLUTION: Standard solar panels are horizontal, and consequently require vast areas of land. In contrast, our solution consists of vertical bifacial panels, which require minimal space allowing farmers to keep harvesting their lands. Besides, horizontal solar configurations produce mostly at noon in contrast, our innovative configuration of vertical East-West orientated panels allows us to maximize electricity production in the morning and evening prime times in energy markets! Hence, Eki s electricity is +30% more valuable than that from conventional players. And this is how we can afford to share our revenue with farmers and offer cheaper electricity! BENEFITS: 1) Farmers: Maintain land ownership and crop yields while generating additional revenue from renewable energy, which stabilizes the food prizes and enables them to invest in their farming practices. 2) Communities: Access to clean energy for irrigation, cold storage, and processing, reducing energy costs. Environment: Significant reduction in carbon emissions (200+ tons/year per site) and improved land use efficiency. This system enables farmers to maximize land productivity for both food and energy, strengthening food security and contributing to a sustainable, resilient future.

Long-term sustainable benefits manifest as better soil health and biodiversity, alongside enhanced community resilience to climate variability. This holistic approach not only invigorates the local economy but also contributes to a more sustainable and resilient global food system, aligning with multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals.

core_fields.title: Turning legume waste into gold
core_fields.description: FABUMIN transforms aquafaba, a legume processing byproduct, into a versatile egg powder substitute with potential to become a key raw-material in the food industry. Our innovative drying technology creates a sustainable alternative to eggs, which have one of the largest environmental footprints among food ingredients. One-ton of FABUMIN replaces 130,000 eggs, offering identical functionality without compromising taste or texture. This circular economy approach upcycles food waste, reduces water usage, and promotes healthier, sustainable global-food systems.
core_fields.abstract: The legume industry faces a significant challenge with the daily generation of substantial wastewater, known as aquafaba. This by-product not only burdens sewage systems but also results in the waste of valuable freshwater resources. Concurrently, the egg industry grapples with a multitude of environmental, health, and economic issues that underscore the urgent need for sustainable alternatives. Egg production carries a hefty environmental footprint, consuming considerable water and land while contributing to carbon emissions. A single egg requires 8 liters of water and 20 square meters of land to produce, releasing 170 grams of greenhouse gases. Moreover, the industry contends with food safety concerns, including the risk of salmonella contamination and the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria due to widespread antibiotic use in poultry farming. Egg allergies, affecting about 20% of food allergy sufferers, further complicate matters, as does price volatility, which hinders effective production planning. Aquafaba, discovered in 2014, has emerged as a promising solution to these challenges. This egg alternative effectively binds, emulsifies, and whips in food production, often outperforming eggs themselves. However, its liquid form and short shelf life have posed logistical challenges for widespread industrial adoption. To address these issues, innovative techniques have been developed to dry legume industry side streams, transforming aquafaba into a new egg replacement ingredient for the food industry. This approach not only provides a sustainable alternative to eggs but also offers a solution to the wastewater problem in legume processing. Combining agricultural science, technology, and consumer behavior insights, this initiative benefits both producers and consumers. Farmers gain access to premium markets and higher incomes, while consumers access safer, more nutritious food. In the long term, the project enhances food security, promotes environmental sustainability through reduced carbon footprints, and offers a scalable model for economic empowerment. Communities experience reduced poverty and greater resilience, while farmers and consumers gain affordable, essential resources. Faso Elevage addresses critical societal challenges with innovation, inclusivity, and sustainability, transforming lives and fostering development in a region deeply affected by poverty and instability.

core_fields.title: Food Rescue Network: Bridging Waste and Nourishment in Communities
core_fields.description: Feed Louisville rescues surplus food destined for waste and transforms it into hot, nutrient-dense meals for food-insecure individuals and families. By collaborating with local farmers, restaurants, and food producers, we tackle both food insecurity and food waste. core_fields.abstract: The dual crises of food waste and food insecurity are pressing global issues. In the United States, up to 40% of food is wasted annually, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, while millions face hunger daily. Louisville, KY, mirrors this national problem, with food insecurity rates exceeding 15%. Simultaneously, food producers and retailers discard vast quantities of perfectly edible food due to surplus or aesthetic imperfections. Feed Louisville provides an innovative, community-centered solution by rescuing surplus food and repurposing it into nutritious, ready-to-eat meals. Collaborating with local farmers, restaurants, caterers, and food distributors, we intercept edible food before it becomes waste. Using our mobile kitchens and community kitchens, we create and distribute meals directly to vulnerable populations, including the homeless and food-insecure families. This approach solves multiple problems: it reduces food waste, addresses hunger, and fosters community resilience. By diverting food from landfills, Feed Louisville lowers methane emissions and promotes environmental sustainability. For local food producers, it offers a sustainable alternative to food disposal, turning surplus into a tool for social good. For recipients, it provides dignity and nourishment, offering a lifeline to those most in need. Our model is scalable and replicable, providing a sustainable framework for tackling food insecurity and waste in other communities, bridging the gap between food surplus and food scarcity while advancing environmental stewardship.

core_fields.title: Ownership Innovation: Strengthening Seeding The Future s Innovation Areas with Perpetual Purpose Trusts for Scaled Impact
core_fields.description: This project empowers mission-driven food and farm businesses to adopt Perpetual Purpose Trusts (PPTs), a groundbreaking ownership model ensuring long-term alignment with regenerative practices, nutritious food production, and conscious consumer choice. Through targeted training, resources, and assessments, we equip consultants and businesses to prioritize mission over profit, fostering a sustainable and innovative food system.
core_fields.abstract: Mission-driven food and farm businesses are essential to advancing innovation in IFT s focus areas. However, traditional ownership structures prioritize shareholder returns over everything else, dramatically limiting scalability of regenerative outcomes. We need alternative ownership structures that prioritize mission over shareholder returns. Perpetual Purpose Trusts (PPTs) offer an innovative solution. By replacing human owners with a trust governed by a stakeholder committee, PPTs legally ensure financial resources advance mission-driven goals over profit extraction. This structure secures the long-term viability of businesses advancing regenerative practices, producing naturally nutritious products, and expanding conscious consumer choice. Despite their potential, consultants and entrepreneurs lack awareness and expertise to guide the adoption of PPTs. This project will address this gap by: 1-Building awareness through established consultant networks. 2-Providing skill-building in structural, legal, and financial aspects unique to PPTs. 3-Offering readiness assessments for businesses interested in adopting this model. This strategy will prepare more farmers, entrepreneurs, and consultants aligned with IFT s three focus areas to understand PPTs and implement this structure, ensuring their missions thrive in perpetuity. Project lead, Food Finance Institute (FFI), has supported food and farm entrepreneurs by training over 460 consultants and 1500 entrepreneurs. In 2025-2026, FFI will train 100+ new consultants, host a regional conference, and provide extensive learning resources. FFI will collaborate with Purpose Trust Partners for PPT expertise and content creation. By leveraging these assets, this project will create a scalable pathway to empower food and farm businesses to continue innovating in IFT s focus areas while ensuring their long-term viability.

core_fields.description: The Feeding Albania Foundation addresses food insecurity through innovative, community-driven initiatives. This project focuses on sustainable agriculture, education, and youth engagement, aiming to establish five organic food gardens in schools or social centers. Benefiting 500 students and 300 families, the initiative promotes self-sufficiency by using cheap gardening methods. Partnering with businesses and municipalities, the project will teach local agriculture, inspire youth and schools to replicate these models, fostering sustainable food systems in Albania.
core_fields.abstract: This initiative addresses the critical challenge of food insecurity by combining community-driven efforts with innovative education to reconnect youth with agriculture. Albania faces significant structural food system issues, including reliance on imports, a decline in local production, and youth disengagement from farming. These challenges are exacerbated by poverty, the pandemic's aftermath, and a lack of systemic support for sustainable food practices. The innovation lies in leveraging community energy and support to create cheap, sustainable programs that integrate traditional farming with modern, technology-driven approaches. A core component is educating youth through hands-on gardening programs in schools and communities, supported by interactive digital tools, workshops, and mentorship from local farmers. These activities are supplemented by distributing DIY gardening kits, including seeds, tools, and instructional guides, to maximize accessibility and engagement. This solution not only fosters food self-reliance by reducing dependency on imports but also revitalizes youth interest in agriculture by incorporating technology and interactive learning. The use of eco-friendly techniques, such as composting organic waste, agroforestry, and permaculture, ensures sustainability and enriches soil for better yields. Immediate benefits include increased access to fresh, nutritious food, improved awareness of sustainable practices, and strengthened community ties. Long-term, the project cultivates a new generation of environmentally conscious individuals, supports local farmers, reduces waste, and enhances resilience in Albania s food systems. This approach provides a replicable model to build equitable, sustainable, and thriving agricultural communities for future generations.

core_fields.title: Reducing Post-Harvest Losses with Sustainable Cooling Solutions for Smallholder Farmers and Vendors in Tanzania
core_fields.description: Freshpack Technologies reduces post-harvest vegetable losses in Tanzania by 40% through sustainable, electricity-free cooling solutions. Our patented Freshpack Boxes extend shelf life by three times, empowering smallholder farmers and women vendors to increase income and reduce food waste. By 2027, we aim to benefit 10,000 users, expand to new regions, and introduce innovative products like solar-powered display boxes, driving measurable social, economic, and environmental impact in the agricultural value chain.
core_fields.abstract: Freshpack Technologies addresses the critical issue of post-harvest vegetable loss, which impacts 40% of produce in Tanzania annually. This loss reduces incomes for smallholder farmers and vendors, particularly women, and exacerbates food insecurity and environmental waste. Our innovation, the Freshpack Box, is a patented packaging solution made from smart fabric technology that mimics the human body s cooling mechanism. It keeps vegetables fresh for up to three times longer than traditional storage methods, reducing spoilage and waste. By using no electricity, the boxes are ideal for off-grid rural areas and cost-effective for end users. This solution is rooted in technical insights into evaporative cooling, adapted to local needs through rigorous field testing. Each Freshpack Box is sold at $21 with a 30% profit margin, making it sustainable for production while remaining affordable for users. The immediate benefits include increased income for 10,000 farmers and vendors by 2027, reduced food waste, and improved food security for communities. Long-term benefits include a 30% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions associated with vegetable spoilage and the empowerment of women vendors in the agricultural value chain. Freshpack Technologies thus delivers measurable economic, social, and environmental impact.

core_fields.title: The Little Gardens of Eden - Creating access to fruits and improving nutrition for Children in Public Schools in Kenya
core_fields.description: Fruity Schools Africa is registered with the NGO s Board as a Non-Profit Organization in Kenya. We grow fruit trees in public schools and hospitals to create access to fresh fruits for Learners. Our goal is to co-create and establish fruity orchards of 100 trees in each selected public school and hospital. By planting certified fruit trees in public schools and hospitals, we not only create access to food but also contribute to climate change mitigation.
core_fields.abstract: Fruity Schools Africa addresses food insecurity, climate change, and poverty affecting marginalized communities in Kenya. Over 7 million children, or 46% of students in public schools, come from impoverished backgrounds. These children come from families with modest incomes, living below the poverty line with earnings of less than $2 a day. Due to their economic circumstances, they lack access to proper nutrition, healthcare, and other essential necessities. This deprivation leads to various health issues and impedes their ability to focus and learn effectively in school. These challenges run counter to the principles enshrined in Kenya's constitution and international policies, which acknowledge the right to education, food, nutrition, and healthcare for all children. Some Children complete Primary School without ever tasting a fruit that can be grown easily within the school compound. Children living in slums scavenge for fruits from market garbage bins and hence risk contracting deadly diseases and infections caused by eating rotten fruits and from these inhumane spaces. Access to nutritious, safe and socially acceptable fruits and food is enshrined in Kenya Constitution 2010 and other international policies and human rights bills clearly stating that ALL CHILDREN SHALL have access to Nutritious, Safe and Socially Acceptable Food.

core_fields.title: Farm2Veteran Meal Program & Agribusiness Empowerment Initiative
core_fields.description: Our solution addresses food insecurity and nutritional deficits among veterans in food deserts by providing nutritious, farm-fresh meals from our 60-acre farm, which employs sustainable practices. We donate 100% of food to veterans and purchase additional produce from local BIPOC and veteran-owned farms. Additionally, we empower communities through education on food systems, nutrition, sustainable farming, and agricultural careers, fostering long-term food security and economic mobility.
core_fields.abstract: Farm2Veteran's Meal Program, Workforce Development, and Counseling Services Initiatives aims to increase veterans access to nutritious food, create viable career pathways for veterans, and address the mental and physical health issues that create barriers for acquiring stable employment in the veteran population. Veterans face a critical lack of access to nutritious food, being nearly twice as likely as the general population to experience food insecurity. Veterans encounter distinct workforce development challenges due to their unique experiences, skills, and needs. They face higher unemployment and underemployment rates compared to the general population, often struggling to translate military skills into civilian job qualifications. This disconnect can hinder their job search and career transition. Additionally, service-related disabilities and mental health issues like PTSD can impact job performance and well- being. Our solution aims to address the specific food insecurity and nutritional deficit challenges faced by Veterans living amidst food deserts in marginalized communities across the country. Home to a variety of livestock, a greenhouse, and a garden, our 60-acre farm produces nutritious, farm-fresh, better-than-organic meals while employing sustainable farming practices aimed at protecting the environment, maintaining soil fertility, and promoting biodiversity. We donate 100% of food to veterans nationally. Secondly, we endeavor to resource, empower, and equip local BIPOC and veteran-owned farms. So we purchase additional produce from these farms to include in our meal program. Thirdly, we are keen on educating impacted communities about food systems, nutrition, agricultural production, environmental impact, and career pathways in the agricultural sector.

core_fields.title: Beyond the Bean: Promoting Sustainability and Food Security in Coffee Farming
core_fields.description: This project aims to enhance food security and promotes sustainable agriculture in coffee-growing communities. By producing biochar and cultivating nutrient-rich beans and corn, the project improves soil fertility, boosts agricultural productivity, and enhances local diets. This integrated approach fosters regenerative agriculture and ensures access to safe and nutritious food.
core_fields.abstract: This project focuses: 1. Rotating Community Biochar: Coffee plant residues and pulp generated during coffee processing will be transformed into biochar, a valuable soil amendment. Biochar improves soil quality, enhances water retention, and contributes to carbon capture. The implementation of rotating community biochar systems will ensure equitable and efficient access to this technology for multiple coffee-growing communities. This approach maximizes the benefits of biochar while promoting collaboration and resource sharing. 2. Food Security with Bean and Corn Seeds: The project will promote the cultivation of local bean and corn varieties with high nitrogen fixation capacity. These crops improve soil fertility, reduce the need for chemical fertilizers, and ensure the sustainable production of staple foods, enhancing local diets and nutrition. Studies by Cenicaf highlight the benefits of these crops in increasing agricultural productivity and promoting sustainable farming practices. Innovation and Benefits Integrating biochar with bean and corn cultivation creates a circular model of sustainable agriculture. This innovative approach transforms coffee waste into valuable resources, enriching the soil and enhancing productivity. By combining technical knowledge in carbon management, crop rotation, and climate-smart agriculture, the project promotes a holistic and sustainable approach to coffee farming. Sustainable Impact In the short term, farmers will benefit from more fertile soils, increased yields, and equitable access to innovative technologies. In the long term, the project will strengthen climate resilience, enhance food security, and promote environmental sustainability. This integrated approach will reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve livelihoods, and enhance the overall quality of life in coffee-growing regions.

core_fields.title: Ocean Growing of Asparagopsis in South Korea
core_fields.description: We seek to complete a pilot project to conduct ocean-growing of Asparagopsis in South Korea. Asparagopsis seaweed reduces methane emissions and increases livestock productivity. This makes beef and dairy farming more economical and environmentally sustainable. Asparagopsis grows naturally in many locations including South Korea. To begin scaling production to feed cattle and reduce methane emissions, Asparagopsis will need to be grown commercially in locations with good conditions such as South Korea.
core_fields.abstract: One of the biggest climate change issues is the methane emissions from agriculture. Livestock, produce about 12% of total global greenhouse gases, with a large amount of those being from enteric emissions due to microbes that make methane in the cows first stomach, the rumen. Asparagopsis, a type of red seaweed found around the world, contains bio-actives that disrupt this methane production. FutureFeed has created a solution where a small amount of Asparagopsis (less than 1% of total feed) is added to ruminant livestock diets. Scientific studies have shown this can reduce methane emissions by greater than 80% in certain settings. By stopping methane production, the energy saved is used more efficiently by the animal, improving feed conversion efficiency (FCE) by up to 7% as per recent published scientific studies. This means animals grow better on the same amount of food. Asparagopsis is safe for animals, with no negative effects on their digestion. Meat and dairy products from these animals are also safe for humans, with no changes in quality or taste. In addition, the commercial production of Asparagopsis will enable a seaweed species to be farmed for a purpose, enabling marine and aquaculture industries. This will drive employment and development of coastal communities to grow and produce this climate-changing feed additive.

core_fields.title: G-Green: Enhancing Biodynamic Vegetable Farming through Cooperatives in Northern Nigeria
core_fields.description: Our project will establish biodynamic vegetable farming for carrots, cabbages, and potatoes in Northern Nigeria, utilizing a cooperative model to empower local farmers. The cooperative will enhance resource-sharing, provide access to training, equipment, and markets, and improve productivity through collective decision-making. By integrating sustainable farming practices, the initiative will boost soil health, increase yields, and promote economic resilience, benefiting both the environment and the community.
core_fields.abstract: The ongoing farmers-herders conflict in northern Nigeria has significantly disrupted agricultural productivity, food security, and community cohesion. This conflict arises from competition particularly over arable land and grazing areas, exacerbated by climate change and unsustainable farming practices. Traditional farming systems often deplete soil nutrients, further aggravating land scarcity and community tensions. Our project introduces biodynamic vegetable farming as an innovative solution to these challenges. Biodynamic farming integrates organic methods with ecological and spiritual principles, emphasizing soil regeneration, water conservation, and diversified cropping. By adopting this approach, farmers can enhance soil fertility and maximize land use efficiency, reducing the pressure for expansion into grazing territories. This solution is relevant because it offers a practical pathway to sustainable agriculture while addressing underlying resource-based conflicts. Training programs and workshops will equip farmers with the knowledge and tools to transition to biodynamic methods. Farmers will also learn to collaborate with herders on land-sharing arrangements, fostering peaceful coexistence and mutual benefit. Immediate benefits include improved crop yields, reduced dependency on chemical inputs, and strengthened community resilience. Over time, the initiative will promote environmental regeneration, restore degraded lands, and create stable livelihoods, reducing conflict triggers. For consumers and society, the availability of chemical-free, nutrient-rich vegetables enhances public health, while the environmental benefits contribute to climate change mitigation.

core_fields.title: Scaregrow: Transforming Farming with AI and IoT for Climate Resilience and Food Security
core_fields.description: At Green Eden Farms, we develop technology to empower smallholder farmers with climate-smart solutions. Our flagship product, Scaregrow, is an AI-powered farm management platform using IoT sensors to deliver real-time insights on soil health, weather, and crop conditions. Scaregrow helps farmers make data-driven decisions, reduce resource waste, and improve climate resilience. Tested in Nigeria with support from the African Development Bank (AFD), it has impacted over 100 farmers and seeks to scale for greater reach.
core_fields.abstract: Agricultural productivity in sub-Saharan Africa is heavily impacted by erratic weather, water scarcity, degraded soils, and inefficient farming practices. Smallholder farmers, who contribute over 80% of agricultural production in the region, face significant challenges that result in annual losses exceeding $10 billion, according to the FAO. These losses are driven by pest outbreaks, poor resource utilization, and climate variability. Compounding the problem is the limited access to agronomic and weather data, which leaves farmers vulnerable and food systems unstable. At Green Eden Farms, we have developed Scaregrow, an AI-powered farm management system designed to address these critical issues. Scaregrow integrates IoT sensors with AI-driven analytics to provide real-time insights on soil health, moisture levels, weather patterns, and crop conditions. Farmers can access this data through a user-friendly mobile application, empowering them with actionable advice on irrigation scheduling, pest control, and resource optimization. This solution is tailored specifically for Nigerian farmers, building on insights from global agricultural innovations like Microsoft s FarmBeats and CGIAR s Big Data Platform. Its solar-powered sensors ensure accessibility in off-grid regions, overcoming energy limitations. Scaregrow has demonstrated immediate benefits for farmers, including increased crop yields, reduced water usage, and significant cost savings. By optimizing farming practices, it also reduces greenhouse gas emissions and builds resilience against climate change. Supported by the African Development Bank, Scaregrow has already positively impacted over 100+ farmers in Nigeria. With a clear pathway to scale, it has the potential to transform agricultural systems and empower millions of farmers across Africa..
