core_fields.title: Gawad Kalinga s Food Productivity Hubs: Building Sustainable, Food-Secure, and Healthy Filipino Communities
core_fields.description: Gawad Kalinga s Food Productivity Hubs are regional hubs that centralize and harmonize multiple interventions for food security, health, and sustainability, all of which contribute to achieving zero poverty, zero hunger, and net zero carbon in Filipino communities in a three to five year timeframe. The productivity hubs are strategically located in regions with high incidence of poverty and hunger, and are primarily led by community members, mission workers, and young leaders from the region.
core_fields.abstract: Half of the Filipino population is food-poor, and the nation s food producers, farmers and fisherfolk, are the hungriest. In a country where hunger and food insecurity are pervasive, there is an urgent need to empower communities to be food productive, collectively working towards a community-based solution promoting sustainable food production practices and improving community health. GK s food productivity hubs harmonize multiple initiatives targeting food security, health, and livelihood. The hub begins with an economic model called BayanAnihan, translated as community harvest , where farmers are organized to plant a crop whose production is directly invested in by the market buyer, and where the farmers share in equity and profit. Alongside this, GK establishes a community food farm program, where young farm organizers from GK s agricultural school, SEED Philippines, teach mothers and children to plant organic vegetables for consumption or sale. Vegetables harvested from the farms are cooked into nutritious meals for a central community kitchen, which provides nutrition supplementation to children and pregnant mothers. Finally, youth from the community are sent to study agri-entrepreneurship at SEED Philippines to be able to sustain the gains of the community. All of these initiatives work in harmony to achieve sustainable, food-secure, and healthy Filipino communities. The productivity hubs that GK has established in two Philippine provinces so far have proved its capacity to transform the lives of Filipino families, who now earn a better living, produce their own food, and live healthier lives.

core_fields.title: NEGLECTED AND UNDER-UTILIZED SPECIES CULINARY INNOVATION THROUGH THE GFM KITCHEN (NUS-CI)
core_fields.description: The Kitchen by Ghana Food Movement (GFM) is a food education hub equipped with a Training Kitchen, Food Innovation Lab and Urban Demo Farm to train and empower actors in the food sector. Through the NUS-CI program, the kitchen by GFM aims to: Enhance the biodiversity of 1000 cocoa farmers through the cultivation of NUS by 2027 and Improve the Nutrition of 200,000 School children through the inclusion of NUS ingredients in school diet.
core_fields.abstract: Enhancing food security and climate resilience in Ghana requires developing the Neglected and Underutilized Species (NUS) value chain. NUS crops, such as cocoyam, plantain, tiger nuts, taro, jute mallow, are nutrient-rich, drought-tolerant, and pest-resistant, but their potential is still unrealized due to a lack of awareness, insufficient investment, and poor integration into agricultural policies. With 22.6% of Ghanaian households experiencing food insecurity (World Food Programme, 2022), promoting NUS crops through improved cultivation and culinary innovation will diversify diets, and improve rural livelihoods. The NUS-CI program stands out as it bridges the gap between farmers and offtakers, facilitating to connect increased supply of NUS ingredients with schools and households and influencing growing consumption of NUS ingredients. The main objective is more nutritious meals with local ingredients on the plates of school children and increased incomes for farmers. To achieve this, we use a multifaceted approach of technical skills training for 1000 cocoa farmers in sustainable cultivation of NUS ingredients, culinary skills training of Matrons of schools in NUS ingredients recipe development in areas such as developing meat substitutes or plant-based milk and creating consumer awareness on NUS ingredients and its health benefits. In our pilot program, the Kitchen by GFM trained over 150 NUS farmers to integrate NUS crops in their cocoa farms in 2 communities in the Eastern Region of Ghana (Adawso and Bawjiase).

core_fields.title: IMMERSE: Integrated Multisectoral Model for Enhancing Resilience in Shock-prone Environments
core_fields.description: This project seeks to improve the availability, affordability, and desirability of nutritious, sustainable foods during climate-related shocks by integrating private-sector value chain actors into sub-national shock early-warning and response systems. The initiative leverages innovative AI technology and multi-sectoral coordination, building on ongoing work to improve shock response in collaboration with county governments and value chain partners. The project will create a scalable model for enhancing nutrition and climate resilience in vulnerable communities.
core_fields.abstract: The State of the Climate in Africa 2022 report shows that over 110 million people in Africa were directly affected by weather, climate, and water-related hazards in 2022, resulting in more than $8.5 billion in economic damages. Climate-related shocks are increasing in both magnitude and frequency year-on-year (Richardson, K et al., 2022). The immediate and medium-term impacts of climate shocks disproportionately affect the most vulnerable and marginalised communities. In Kenya, the growing frequency and magnitude of climate-related shocks puts local administrators under increased pressure to maintain nutrition security and climate resilience. Bringing the private sector into these systems will help governments relieve this pressure, and constitutes a clear win-win for food system resilience: this approach ensures that social protection systems can deliver timely support to shock-affected communities, and also supports local food enterprises to stay profitable and adapt to evolving market conditions during shocks. GAIN s ongoing work to engage private sector actors in sub-national early warning systems in Kenya has generated compelling evidence that engaging the private sector in these systems is feasible, scalable, and that it can make food systems more resilient to shocks. In this project, we aim to capitalise on our existing successes to reinforce and scale a public-private partnership model for shock-responsive social protection, which integrates artificial intelligence (AI) technology, consumer insights, and private-sector mobilization.

core_fields.title: Empowering Communities for Sustainable, Equitable, Ecological, and Diverse Food Systems through Seed Sovereignty (ECOSEEDS Project)
core_fields.description: The ECOSEEDS Project intends to transform the landscape of agroecology and regenerative systems by restoring the tradition of farmers saving their own seeds. The dominant agro-industrial model has led to the loss of traditional agricultural practices and local seed varieties. Seed sovereignty as an innovative approach and seeks to promote a sustainable, equitable, and diverse seed system that empowers farmers, conserves biodiversity, and fosters resilient and nutritious food systems. We have two main strategies, Participatory Seed Governance (PSG) and Farmer-Consumer Hubs. The ECOSEED Project revitalizes traditional knowledge and farming practices by granting seeds back to the farmers to save, use, exchange, and propagate. This approach is unique and disruptive to the prevailing industrialized agriculture model that resulted in monocultures and the erosion of biodiversity. Through the seed-saving communities, seed production centers, seed entrepreneurship, and farmer-consumer hubs, the ECOSEEDS project will foster knowledge-sharing and empower communities to become stewards of their agricultural heritage. By increasing access to diverse locally adapted seed varieties, communities will have a reliable source of nutritionally rich crops, reducing vulnerability to food shortages and malnutrition. No seeds, no farmer, no food, no future.

core_fields.title: Seeding Community Power for Sustainable, Equitable, and Diverse Food Systems and Policies (Seeding Power)
core_fields.description: Seeding Power leverages local partnerships between government units, smallholder farmers and academia to promote seed sovereignty as an innovative approach to address food insecurity and the impacts of climate change. Seed sovereignty promotes sustainable, equitable seed systems that strengthens Filipino smallholder farmers, conserves biodiversity, and advances resilient, nutritious food systems. Seeding Power establishes new seed saving communities (SSCs), creates seed policies that transform the seed system, and ensures resilient seed libraries.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: The Philippines is the most climate vulnerable country in the world, experiencing up to 20 typhoons per year, numerous floodings and droughts and additional impacts of slow on-set climate change. These impacts place the Philippines in a critical agricultural biodiversity and climate crisis that threatens food security and economic growth of small-scale farmers. Further catalyzing these threats, corporate control of seeds and current policies challenge the livelihood of farmers. Solution/Innovation: To combat climate change and strengthen farmers, Seeding Power s model develops a resilient seed system supported by a network of seed libraries and local seed policies that promote long-term agricultural sustainability. Furthermore, Seeding Power focuses on its innovative approach of seed sovereignty and the traditional practice of saving open-pollinated varieties (OPVs). GSS utilizes local insight, seed sovereignty and OPVs as a solution because it provides a multifaceted approach to climate changes, systemic barriers and food insecurity. Benefits: OPVs and seed sovereignty provide wide-ranging benefits, impacting those most vulnerable: ● Economic wellbeing of farmers. OPVs increase yields for small-holder farmers and help plants withstand climate disasters. Additionally, local seed policies encourage farmers to save and replant their own OPVs, making them less dependent on commercial seeds. ● Enhanced food security for communities. OPVs help reduce climate-related disruptions in the supply chain and create opportunities for more diverse, locally accessed nutritious food. ● Environment. The wider genetic diversity of OPVs result in increased biodiversity and plants that are adapted to their specific growing conditions and naturally resistant to pests and diseases.

core_fields.title: Transforming Institutional Food Systems Through Scalable Meatless Monday China Initiatives
core_fields.description: The Meatless Monday China Institutional Dining Transformation Initiative engages institutions to reduce meat consumption through interactive workshops, chef training, and behavioral nudges. By fostering plant-based dietary shifts, the project promotes sustainable, nutritious, and affordable food systems. This scalable model will drive meaningful reductions in meat consumption, empower institutions to adopt sustainable practices, and establish a framework for broader implementation, aligning with IFT s mission of advancing innovative food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Rapidly increasing meat consumption in China has led to significant challenges. In 2020, urban residents consumed 58.3% more meat than recommended by dietary guidelines, contributing to chronic health issues 88.5% of deaths in China are linked to chronic diseases. Additionally, China s vast geography and diverse culinary traditions make it difficult for a single dietary guideline to be universally effective. Tailored, region-specific approaches are needed to drive meaningful dietary change. Historically, efforts to educate consumers on food literacy have focused primarily on raising awareness. However, to shift consumption patterns, individuals require actionable guidance and practical tools to integrate sustainable practices into daily life. The Meatless Monday China Institutional Dining Transformation Initiative offers a solution by addressing these gaps. Through interactive workshops, chef training, and behavioral nudges, the initiative empowers institutions to implement plant-based dietary practices tailored to local preferences. Workshops combine gamified activities and hands-on meal design to make dietary recommendations tangible and accessible, while chef training equips culinary teams to create appealing, regionally appropriate plant-based menus. Behavioral nudges like Meatless Monday offer simple, actionable steps for gradual yet impactful change. This approach not only reduces meat consumption but also promotes healthier diets, lowers the environmental footprint, and aligns with local dietary traditions. By bridging the gap between awareness and action, the initiative provides a scalable and sustainable model to address the interconnected challenges of health, culture, and environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Promotion of Biofortified Grains to Reduce Malnutrition and Improve Food System
core_fields.description: The project promotes bio-fortified grains, Iron Pearl Millet (IPM) and Zinc Wheat (ZW), as a sustainable solution to combat malnutrition and enhance food systems in Uttar Pradesh. By engaging 100 farmers in nutrition-smart, climate-resilient practices, it aims to improve grain production and livelihoods. Additionally, 200 school children will benefit from bio-fortified meals, fostering better health outcomes and demonstrating scalable, impactful solutions for nutrition security and sustainable agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation centers on the promotion of bio-fortified grains, Iron Pearl Millet (IPM) and Zinc Wheat (ZW), to address hidden hunger caused by micronutrient deficiencies, particularly iron and zinc. This problem is critical in India, where anemia and stunted growth impact millions, especially women and children. Malnutrition weakens immunity, hampers cognitive development, and perpetuates poverty. Bio-fortified grains offer a sustainable and innovative solution by enriching staple crops with essential micronutrients. The project introduces nutrition-smart and climate-resilient agronomic practices to improve grain production, engaging 100 farmers, SHGs, and FPCs in Uttar Pradesh. Scientific advancements in biofortification, combined with improved farming techniques, ensure these grains thrive even in challenging climatic conditions. The benefits are multifaceted and immediate. For farmers, bio-fortified grains enhance yields, improve soil health, and increase market value, ensuring sustainable livelihoods. Schools and communities benefit from healthier, well-nourished children, improving cognitive development and school attendance. Governments and producers gain from reduced healthcare costs and a more resilient food system. Societal gains include better public health and economic stability. Environmentally, bio-fortified grains reduce the need for synthetic supplements and fertilizers, promoting eco-friendly farming. The project also aligns with climate-resilient goals, ensuring sustainable food security amidst changing climatic patterns. By addressing malnutrition and empowering farmers with innovative practices, the initiative delivers lasting health, economic, and environmental benefits to communities and society at large.

core_fields.title: Reducing Stunting through Community Empowerment in Southwest Papua, Championing the Exploration and Education of Endemic Food Sources
core_fields.description: This project addresses stunting in Southwest Papua (30%+ rates) by educating communities on the nutritional value of endemic plants like moringa and purslane. Through sustainable processing tools, a Food Lab prototype, and community activation, it improves diets, food security, and livelihoods. By promoting biodiversity, strengthening local food systems, and fostering sustainable practices, this initiative provides a scalable solution to malnutrition, reducing stunting while enhancing health and resilience in vulnerable communities.
core_fields.abstract: Southwest Papua faces stunting rates exceeding 30%, significantly higher than Indonesia s national average, driven by limited access to affordable, nutritious food and the underutilization of local nutrient-rich plants such as purslane (Portulaca oleracea) and moringa (Moringa oleifera). Communities lack the knowledge and tools to incorporate these plants into their diets, while reliance on nonlocal staples like rice worsens malnutrition and food insecurity, displacing traditional, nutrient-dense diets. This initiative empowers local communities through education, capacity-building, and the establishment of a prototype Food Lab. It identifies and trains key stakeholders mothers, youth, and educators on the nutritional value, processing techniques, and culinary uses of underutilized wild plants. By leveraging insights from nutritional science, the program positions these endemic plants as affordable, sustainable superfoods. The program delivers immediate benefits, including improved dietary diversity and reduced stunting rates, alongside enhanced community knowledge and self-reliance in using local food resources. In the long term, it preserves biodiversity through sustainable use of native plants, strengthens local food systems to reduce dependence on external food, and supports small-scale farmers by integrating wild plants into value-added products. By addressing immediate nutritional needs and fostering long-term resilience, this initiative aligns with sustainable food system goals. Utilizing local resources, promoting community engagement, and advocating sustainable practices, it creates a scalable model to combat malnutrition in similar regions globally. This holistic approach ensures health, food security, and economic opportunities for vulnerable communities.

core_fields.title: ASALs Smart Nursery
core_fields.description: The ASAL Tree Planting Initiative promotes food security through agroforestry by planting indigenous trees and integrating sustainable farming practices in arid and semi-arid regions. By using greenhouses and technology to boost tree survival rates, the project creates jobs, enhances biodiversity, and supports local communities with shade, soil improvement, and resources for crops and livestock.
core_fields.abstract: The ASAL Tree Planting Initiative addresses the challenge of low tree survival rates in arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL) by leveraging solar-powered technology to improve agroforestry outcomes. In these regions, harsh climatic conditions, limited water, and pest infestations hinder tree growth, threatening food security and environmental stability. Our innovative approach involves using solar energy to power water-saving irrigation systems, temperature and humidity sensors, and greenhouse operations. These technologies create optimal growing conditions for seedlings, reduce water wastage, and protect young trees from extreme weather and pests. By enhancing tree survival rates, the initiative ensures the establishment of robust agroforestry systems. This solution is rooted in scientific understanding of plant growth requirements and the adaptation of renewable energy for sustainable agriculture. Solar energy is both affordable and accessible, making it ideal for resource-constrained regions. The benefits are significant and far-reaching. Farmers and communities gain resilient agroforestry systems that improve soil fertility, increase crop yields, and provide shade and fodder for livestock. Schools and local groups benefit from training opportunities and environmental education. Society at large experiences improved food security, economic opportunities, and reduced carbon emissions. The environment benefits from enhanced biodiversity and restoration of degraded ecosystems. By increasing tree survival rates through solar-powered technology, this innovation creates a sustainable, scalable solution to agroforestry challenges in ASAL, promoting resilience and long-term prosperity.

core_fields.title: Scaling Sustainable Cool Chain Solutions in Kenya
core_fields.description: In this project we plan to scale up existing activity in Kenya from one delivery truck to a small delivery line of four trucks. This activity has been supported by the IFC and conducted in collaboration with a local distributor, Farm to Feed. We also plan to integrate one solar cooling container to be stationed in rural environment, demonstrating horizontal and vertical scalability of our sustainable cool chain solutions for developing countries.
core_fields.abstract: The cold chain industry is crucial for delivering fresh, nutritious food, yet it faces two major challenges: Food Losses: In developing countries, up to 50% of fresh produce spoils due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure. This not only limits access to affordable, healthy food but also impacts farmers' livelihoods. GHG Emissions: Cold chains account for 3-4% of global greenhouse gas emissions, primarily due to their reliance on fossil-based energy. Additionally, food spoilage contributes 8-10% of global emissions through methane release and wasted resources. GreenTech s innovative solar cooling solutions are designed to provide reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable cooling options. These include community cooling hubs, portable cooling units, and transport refrigeration solutions. Our solutions are specifically tailored to serve rural and remote areas with limited electricity and infrastructure, helping extend the shelf life of fresh produce, reduce food waste, and improve access to healthy, nutritious food for consumers. At the same time, our approach significantly reduces the environmental impact of both food losses and cooling operations. This strategy benefits farmers by lowering post-harvest losses, strengthens communities through increased food availability, and supports consumers with more affordable, nutritious produce. Environmentally, it reduces emissions from refrigeration and food waste, while enhancing resilience against climate change. This innovation not only provides immediate savings by reducing spoilage and energy consumption but also contributes to building long-term, sustainable food systems that support livelihoods, promote healthy diets, and protect the planet.

core_fields.title: The Green Menu Movement: Plant-forward Menus for Global Health and Sustainability
core_fields.description: Greener by Default (GBD) plans to expand our Plant-forward Menu Program across the globe, improving healthy diets and outcomes for individuals and communities, increasing access to nutritious, healthy food options for consumer choice, and promoting sustainable practices that reduce institutions carbon footprints and benefit the environment.
core_fields.abstract: Food lies at the crux of many of the most pressing issues facing our world, from climate change and deforestation, to pandemics and antibiotic resistance, to the suffering of tens of billions of farmed animals, to many chronic diseases. Plant-forward diets are a critical part of the solution to ensuring the wellbeing of people and the planet, but transforming the way people eat is a big lift. The recent slump in US plant-based meat sales shows that simply adding options is not enough to shift consumer behavior. Choice architecture - organizing the decision-making environment to lower the barriers to making sustainable choices - is one of the most effective ways to create widespread behavioral change. Making plant-based foods the easiest and most appealing option for all diners, not just vegetarians, drives down demand for industrial meat production and normalizes plant-based eating, while offering options to meet everyone s needs. By promoting nutritious, plant-forward menus at trusted, wide-reaching institutions, Greener by Default drives transformative food systems change, advancing powerful health and environmental outcomes at scale. Through this work, we are generating a meaningful impact that will have a multiplier effect, promoting healthy diets, sustainable practices, and an empowered consumer base throughout the world.

core_fields.abstract: Grenoh Food Lab s innovation lies in producing a sustainable cocoa substitute and biofertilizer using microbial fermentation technology. The primary problem it addresses is the environmental and ethical challenges of traditional cocoa farming, including deforestation, excessive water and energy use, and unsustainable agricultural practices. Additionally, there is increasing demand for affordable, halal-certified food products. By using oil palm leaves an underutilized and abundant resource and halal-certified microorganisms, Grenoh reduces the reliance on traditional cocoa farming, which consumes significant land, water, and electricity. The fermentation process produces a high-quality cocoa substitute in just 7 days, requiring 90% less water and 80% less electricity compared to conventional methods. The process also yields biofertilizer as a byproduct, offering a natural, eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilizers. This innovation is grounded in microbial fermentation science, which efficiently converts organic materials like palm leaves into valuable products. The technical insight stems from optimizing fermentation techniques to produce a cost-effective and scalable solution, while maintaining the desired flavor and functionality of traditional cocoa. The benefits to end users are profound: Consumers gain access to affordable, sustainable, and halal-certified cocoa alternatives. Farmers benefit from the biofertilizer, which supports sustainable agricultural practices without harmful chemicals. Producers reduce costs by adopting a resource-efficient production method. Society and the environment experience a reduction in deforestation, resource depletion, and carbon emissions, promoting a more sustainable food system for future generations.

core_fields.title: Laser Weeding Technology
core_fields.description: LUXEED Robotics is building a machine for farmers that uses lasers and AI to burn weeds, completely eliminating the need for herbicides and significantly enhancing farmers' profit margins. The fully functional AI that detects where the lasers need to hit is built inhouse and is now working on onions, one of the crops vulnerable to weeds. We're making laserweeding accessible to small and medium scale farmers.
core_fields.abstract: Weeding is a global chronic challenge for farmers. They rely heavily on expensive and scarce manual labor and on herbicides, which are harmful to crops, the soil, and the environment. Even advanced farms still lose up to 50% yield on crops vulnerable to weeds, like seed onions. Our innovation reduces weeding costs over 10 years for farmers with 200 hectares around 7 million USD and enhances yield gain from 5 to 30%, thereby significantly affecting the farmers' profit margins and almost doubling produce on the same plot. The biodiversity and underground water channels will greatly benefit from the elimination of herbicides, as well as the soil and crops, which will contain 0 chemical residues when farmers adopt our technology. This technology as it exists today is bulky, expensive, and power-hungry, making it accessible to large-scale farmers (500 hectares and more), with only one commercial company, Carbon Robotics, in the market. Our innovation is 50% more affordable thanks to many aspects of the technology being developed to suit the demands and needs of small and medium scale farmers.

core_fields.abstract: The Cholistan Desert (Bahawalpur district), located in southern Punjab, Pakistan, faces severe desertification and significant challenges in producing sustainable food due to erratic climatic conditions, water scarcity, unsustainable, and limited agriculture infrastructure. The project will introduce a combination of traditional knowledge and modern scientific methods to enhance food security, improving livelihoods, and mitigating environmental degradation. In order to raise awareness among local communities of farmers about the importance of sustainable farming practices, soil and water conservation will be through training programs and workshops. The food security can be improved by promoting climate-resilient agricultural practices tailored to the local environment, such as cultivation of drought-resistant crops, better irrigation techniques and carbon credit. core_fields.title: Transforming Water Management for Food Security in Northern Territory, Australia
core_fields.description: This project leverages Leakster's real-time water leak detection technology to address water scarcity challenges in Northern Territory, Australia. In collaboration with PowerWater, we will design and manufacture 20 sensors to be deployed in drought-prone areas for proactive leak detection. By reducing water loss in critical regions, this initiative aims to preserve resources for agricultural use, enhance food security, and build climate resilience for communities in the Northern Territory.
core_fields.abstract: Leakster s real-time water leak detection technology addresses the critical challenge of water scarcity caused by leaks in aging infrastructure. In regions like Northern Territory, Australia, where drought is a constant threat, up to 30% of treated water is lost before reaching its intended use. This wasted water limits availability for agricultural production, threatens food security, and increases operational costs for utilities and communities. The innovation combines advanced IoT sensors and AI-driven analytics to pinpoint leaks in real time. These sensors monitor pipeline acoustics, identifying even the smallest leaks with high accuracy. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud-based platform where utilities can visualise leak locations and prioritise repairs. This proactive approach eliminates the inefficiencies of traditional reactive methods, which often fail to address water loss until major failures occur. This solution is the result of advancements in acoustic analysis and IoT technologies, tailored for the harsh conditions of drought-prone regions. By deploying 20 sensors in collaboration with PowerWater, this project will target high-leakage areas in the Northern Territory, ensuring sustainable water management. Benefits: Immediate Benefits: Reduced water loss, lower operational costs for utilities, and improved water availability for farmers and communities. Sustainable Benefits: Increased resilience to drought, support for sustainable agriculture, and decreased environmental impact through reduced energy use for pumping and treating water. Leakster empowers communities with reliable access to water, directly improving food security and climate resilience.

In Baltimore, the community in need is prevalent in almost all communities, Black, Latinx X, Immigrant, Refugee or others that can benefit from this amazing fresh leftover food. Leftover Love is solving the problem of getting food into the hands of those that need it, by providing the transportation and logistics to get it from Point A, the food donor to Point B, the food recipient organizations. This results in less food wasted, more food getting directly into the hands of those in need and also gives food donors a tax benefit and helps compliment the impact Leftover Love is able to make. Our founders started asking in their neighborhood, "What happens with leftover food at close of business?" and the answer was the same. They decided to bring together the community to help solve the problem by enlisting volunteers to make an impact for the city they care about. Those in need are able to get this fresh food from organizations they're already familiar with, feed their families and help the environment by wasting less perfectly good food.

core_fields.title: Expansion of K-12 STEAM Classroom Composting Program in Gulf Coast Region of the U.S.
core_fields.description: The Gulf Coast region of the United States faces severe climate challenges, including hurricanes, flooding, and food insecurity, disproportionately impacting low-income communities. Landfill methane emissions exacerbate these issues. Funding would support public school food waste reduction efforts in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida for the 2025-2026 school year. We aim to deliver K-12 STEAM curriculum, educational supplies, and teacher training to economically disadvantaged areas, empowering schools to address waste reduction and environmental education effectively.
core_fields.abstract: The program solves the lack of environmental education in Title 1 schools, where underfunding prevents students from learning about waste reduction and climate issues. This problem perpetuates cycles of environmental degradation, health risks, and economic inequality. Addressing this gap is critical because it equips underserved communities to mitigate food waste and its impacts, including methane emissions from landfills. Our low-cost, low-tech solution is innovative because it is practical, accessible, and address real-world challenges effectively, without need for subscriptions or technology. The solution involves implementing a K-12 STEAM classroom composting program that provides reusable composting supplies, curriculum aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS), and teacher training. Students actively divert food waste from landfills, reducing methane emissions, creating compost, and learning about waste management, sustainability, and climate adaptation. Teachers and cafeteria staff collaborate to integrate these practices into daily routines. The insight behind this solution comes from understanding the link between food waste, landfill emissions, and disproportionate health and environmental burdens on low-income communities. Research on landfill methane emissions and the role of composting in waste reduction shaped the program s design. Immediate benefits include reduced landfill fees, fewer greenhouse gas emissions, and practical climate education for students. Long-term benefits include improved community sustainability, enhanced environmental stewardship, and workforce development opportunities in composting and waste management. Schools save costs on waste disposal, students gain career-ready skills, and communities experience reduced health risks. The program creates lasting impact through its scalable, affordable model, enabling underserved schools to address environmental challenges while fostering resilience.

core_fields.title: Lex Icons : A digital infrastructure for the positive impacts of food systems
core_fields.description: Lex Icons offers a common language for food system actors to visualize their impacts in six key areas and share it with their partners. The infrastructure enables metadata embedding, real-time updates, and compliance tracking, promoting standardized, scalable icon use across various platforms. We will scale up the digital infrastructure for Lex Icons (https://lex-icons.org), a respected, inclusive visual language of machine-readable icons that catalyzes support for positive impact projects.
core_fields.abstract: A challenge facing global food systems is the lack of a common language. Our website and tools fix that. Food businesses, charities, and social enterprises, use Lexicon of Food and the Lex Icons to build trust and align their activities with the mission-driven needs of potential clients, funders and partners. Especially when crossing boundaries across the Global South, scientists and knowledge creators who struggle to make their findings actionable and usable by those who must implement them we offer solutions. These producers can direct organizations, customers and funders Lexicon tools to deepen unity around complex topics. Lexicon s system approach lets users express the full range of benefits offered in almost every domain. Visualizing positive impacts helps everyone involved in a food venture or non-profit initiative whether funders or intended communities on the ground to more easily and clearly understand the aspirations and outcomes of their collaborative activities. Lexicon of Food tools accelerate alignment and consensus on priorities, paving the way for catalytic capital to flow effectively. While organizations working on the ground (and the measurement tools they use) excel at providing quantitative data, they often lack a shared language to visualize qualitative attributes effectively. Lex Icons bridges this gap by helping actors in the food system articulate their practices and the benefits they create or support across six key areas of positive impact valued by investors, funders, clients, and policymakers: air, water, soil, biodiversity, equity, and carbon. This standardized format, or expression layer, can be integrated across data capture, storage, management, distribution.

core_fields.title: LimaBot AI
core_fields.description: LimaBot AI empowers African farmers with AI-driven tools to diagnose crop diseases, analyze soil health, and access actionable farming insights via SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile apps. core_fields.abstract: In Africa, where over 40% of the population relies on farming for livelihood, limited access to agricultural experts, known as Bwana Shamba, poses a critical challenge. For instance, Tanzania has only 4,000 agricultural officers for over 2 million farmers, creating a ratio of one expert per 500 farmers. This gap leaves farmers vulnerable to crop diseases, pests, and poor soil management, exacerbated by climate change and limited access to accurate, real-time farming information. LimaBot AI addresses this issue by leveraging artificial intelligence to provide farmers with instant, actionable insights. Through SMS, WhatsApp, and a mobile app, farmers can diagnose crop diseases, receive recommendations for pest control and fertilizers, and access weather forecasts. Our innovation also includes a soil sensor to analyze soil health and optimize farming practices. The solution is built on advancements in AI and machine learning, enabling accurate diagnostics and tailored advice. Immediate benefits include reduced crop losses, increased productivity, and better-informed decision-making. Over the long term, LimaBot promotes sustainable farming, improves food security, and enhances farmers' resilience to climate change. By empowering communities with accessible technology, LimaBot drives economic growth and aligns with global sustainability goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

core_fields.title: Valley Bee For Food Security

core_fields.abstract: Valley Bee addresses the challenges of declining bee populations, food insecurity, and low agricultural productivity by introducing IoT-enabled smart beekeeping systems and sustainable honey production practices. Our solution involves equipping rural farmers with IoT-enabled smart hives that monitor and self-regulate hive health, temperature, and humidity in real-time, enabling proactive hive management, increased honey production and pollination to food crops in thousands of hectares around each hive. Our project is built on scientific insights into bee behaviour, environmental conditions, and pollination dynamics, providing a scalable, sustainable, and impactful solution to food system challenges. Our approach directly benefits farmers, improves food quality/security, and enhances environmental health.

core_fields.title: AI-Powered Pest Surveillance and Advisory for Paddy Farmers in India
core_fields.description: Rice is a vital global food crop and India is the world's largest exporter. With increasing demand for rice, improving production is critical. Small farmers who cultivate most of the paddy are the most vulnerable to yield loss due to pests infestation. To address this, an AI-powered pest surveillance solution, already used for cotton, will be adapted for paddy. It will offer real-time, localized pest identification and advisory via image analysis combined with science-based recommendations.
core_fields.abstract: Rice, the most cultivated crop in India, suffers an estimated 32.2 million tonnes of annual yield loss (25% of total yield). Marginal, small, and medium-scale farmers, who account for over 90% of cultivated land, often lack access to timely, reliable, and localized pest advisories. This results in overuse or mistimed use of pesticides, increasing costs, reducing effectiveness, and causing environmental damage, including soil and water contamination. Climate-specific pests significantly exacerbate this challenge, as changing weather patterns and extreme conditions create favorable environments for the proliferation of pests and diseases in rice crops. Our proposed AI-powered pest advisory and surveillance solution aims to address these challenges for paddy farmers, building on our existing solution successfully deployed for cotton through a light-weight smartphone application. The AI model will provide real-time, accurate, and localized pest identification and actionable advisories based on images of pests/diseases taken using ordinary smartphones. Our solution will target 10+ pests and disease combinations of relevant importance in paddy crops. The solution enables farmers to make informed decisions on pesticide use, preventing overuse and ensuring timely action to mitigate crop losses. This minimizes input costs, reduces environmental degradation, and enhances sustainable farming practices. We will leverage partnerships and insights from a similar AI solution for cotton pests that we deployed with over 20,000 smallholder farmers and recorded an increase in net income due to lower pesticide expenditure. By providing scalable, accessible technology, this innovation empowers smallholder farmers to protect yields, improve profitability, and contribute to sustainable agriculture.

core_fields.title: Scaling MAMLO FOODS Micro-Factory Model to Empower Women Smallholder farmers and Transform Peanut Processing
core_fields.description: MAMLO FOODS seeks to revolutionize Africa s peanut value chain by scaling its innovative Micro-Factory Model, empowering 500 women smallholder farmers while transforming peanut processing. This localized approach enhances efficiency, reduces post-harvest losses, and ensures farmers earn fair incomes. The $25,000 grant will be pivotal in procuring advanced equipment, delivering targeted training programs, and upgrading infrastructure, enabling us to produce premium peanut-based products and foster sustainable economic growth, gender equity, and community resilience.
core_fields.abstract: Africa s peanut value chain has long-standing challenges. Each year, 30% of peanuts are lost post-harvest, largely due to inefficient processing, poor storage, and limited market access. Women smallholder farmers, who make up 70% of the agricultural workforce in Africa, are particularly affected. Despite their efforts, many earn less than 20% of the market value of the final product, a situation perpetrated by unscrupulous brokers who exploit non-farmer-centered tactics, keeping them trapped in cycles of poverty. At MAMLO FOODS, we re addressing this challenge using our transformative Micro-Factory Model. Our pioneering micro-factory located in Amagoro, western Kenya processes up to 9 tonnes of peanuts each day. By bringing peanut processing closer to the farming communities, we are not only increasing farmers earnings but also cutting down post-harvest losses by up to 30%, effectively improving livelihoods and transforming peanut processing. Our solution also involves equipping 500 women farmers with advanced training in farming techniques, post-harvest handling, and value addition. This way, they can produce high-quality peanuts that meet market standards. We re also investing in efficient processing technology, which reduces waste and improves yields. This approach benefits not just farmers, but the entire community. Immediate benefits include: A 30% increase in farmer incomes. A 30% reduction in peanut losses. Creation of 10 local jobs in processing and distribution. In the long term, this model strengthens local economies, empowers women, and improves food security. Consumers get access to affordable, high-quality peanut products, while the environment benefits from reduced waste.

core_fields.title: Cassava for food and nutrition security (CAFNS) project.
core_fields.description: Cassava is a staple food in many parts of the world. It lacks protein, lipids, and many micronutrients and contains antinutrients. Consumption of cassava products without nutrient enrichment leads to malnutrition and development of some diseases that shorten the lifespan. This project seeks to increase the nutrient density of cassava-based food products; develop recipes from cassava composite flours; improve consumer awareness about diseases associated with the consumption of unfortified ( not enriched) cassava diets.
core_fields.abstract: Improving the nutritional quality of cassava diets is a research priority since cassava is a major staple in many parts of the world and its consumption without appropriate complementation leads to malnutrition and development of diseases, promoting food insecurity. Most cassava diets provide carbohydrates and energy. They need to be complemented with proteins, lipids and micronutrients. We intend to further our on-going research on improving the nutritional quality of cassava diets by formulating ready to prepare cassava composite products and recipes using (a) innovative technologies (modified solid state fermentation) to increase the protein and vitamin content of cassava (b) producing cassava flours with modified functional properties using safe levels of gamma irradiation to produce nanoparticles (c) complementing cassava with protein and micronutrient rich foods and developing recipes from them. Some enriched cassava products have been developed in our laboratory and by other researchers. Two new products will be developed. The knowledge of cassava consumers about its nutrient deficiencies and associated ailments and the need to prevent them will be improved, Consumer acceptability of newly developed nutrient dense cassava recipes will be evaluated in four states in Nigeria. Cassava producers and farmers increase their production and income. Cassava consumers will live healthier lives with diversified cassava diets. Nutritious cassava diets will be introduced into school feeding programmes. This project will address sustainable development goals (SDG.s) 2, 3, 10 1nd 12).

core_fields.title: EMPOWERING TURKANA COUNTY IN KENYA THROUGH FOOD INNOVATION
core_fields.description: Tender Mercies (TM) innovation is a low cost, balanced, single complete nutrient-dense meal formulated to address hunger and malnutrition in nutrient-deficient communities in Kenya. In Turkana, a severely food-insecure arid to semi-arid county, TM will be utilized in school feeding programs, at early childhood development centers and a girls high school to maintain attendance, thereby reducing teenage pregnancies and early marriages. Additionally, it will support women s entrepreneurship programs, fostering local sustainable solutions.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation, Tender Mercies (TM), was formulated to address the problem of hunger and malnutrition in underserved communities like Turkana county that are food insecure, have persistent drought, hunger and have limited access to nutritious food. Turkana county has a hot, dry climate and is categorized as arid and semi-arid land. Due to low agricultural productivity, and low access to nutritious food, chronic malnutrition remains a critical issue with high rates of stunting; prevalence of 23% of children under 5 years, which is above the national average (18%) and wasting at 31.7%. (Kenya Demographic Health Survey, 2022). This leads to developmental delays, reduced cognitive abilities, lower productivity, and weakened immunity, resulting in school drop-outs, teenage pregnancies, and early marriages. To alleviate this, TM will be used in school feeding programs in Early Childhood Centres and Milimatatu Girls' Secondary School. TM is a single meal formulation mix of textured soy protein, rehydrated red beans, rice, salt, and enriched with vitamins and minerals. Nutritionally; it provides macronutrients; 38.9% daily value allowance for protein per serving, 301 kilo calories per serving, and micronutrients; Vitamin A, Zinc, Iodine, Selenium, the B vitamins, among other vital nutrients, thus is ideal for Turkana. Economically; it saves on fuel and time, thus is ideal for low income communities. Environmentally; the reduced cooking time to 10-15 minutes due to precooking ingredients and soybean extrusion, reducing firewood use and in turn deforestation and carbon emissions. Sustainability will be addressed through local women s entrepreneurship programs.

core_fields.title: Zero-Waste Food Production: Circular Economy Models for Sustainability
core_fields.description: his project creates a zero-waste food production model using circular economy principles to repurpose food waste into bioenergy, fertilizers, and upcycled products. By reducing waste, cutting emissions, and promoting sustainable practices, it enhances environmental health, economic resilience, and food security. Through innovation and collaboration, the initiative offers scalable solutions for a sustainable global food system.
core_fields.abstract: Food waste is a global issue, with nearly one-third of all food produced being discarded. This waste contributes to environmental harm, including greenhouse gas emissions and wasted resources like water and energy. Furthermore, food waste in landfills represents untapped opportunities for repurposing valuable by-products into useful products. This project offers a solution by implementing a circular economy model, transforming food waste into bioenergy, fertilizers, and upcycled products. By using technologies such as composting and bio-digestion, food waste is converted into renewable energy and nutrient-rich fertilizers for agriculture, reducing the need for chemical inputs and enhancing sustainability. The scientific insight behind this solution comes from the understanding that food waste can be an invaluable resource rather than a burden. Circular economy principles enable the repurposing of waste into valuable products, benefiting the environment, economy, and society. Benefits include: Farmers gain affordable, eco-friendly fertilizers. Communities benefit from redirected surplus food, increasing food security. Consumers enjoy access to affordable, sustainable products. The environment sees reduced greenhouse gas emissions and optimized resource use. Producers gain economic benefits from utilizing food waste as a resource. By reducing food waste and repurposing by-products, this project supports a more sustainable, efficient, and resilient food system for all stakeholders.

core_fields.title: Organic manure and biogas production from the market organic waste for improved food security, energy access and sanitation
core_fields.description: The economy of Malawi is agro-based, as more than 70% of the people are dependent on agriculture as their main source of livelihood. However, farmers and traders alike experience very high postharvest loss, which affects their income and also contributes to food insecurity. The problem is severe for perishable goods, such as, vegetables. Large quantities of vegetables can usually be seen dumped in open spaces, which contributes to poor sanitation of the markets.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation involves the development of biodigesters in community markets, which use market waste as feedstock. The biogas plants produce biogas, a clean cooking fuel, and liquid organic manure, which is used by smallholder farmers for vegetable cultivation. Therefore, the technology solves multiple challenges for the community. The use of market waste as a feedstock contributes to sanitation and helps to reduce the risks of waterborne diseases. The technology also helps to control GHG emissions from the waste sector. The surrounding community members also benefit from the organic manure and biogas produced from the market waste. Currently, smaller-holder farmers are increasingly relying on organic manure, considering that inorganic fertilizers have become less affordable. Thus, the use of the liquid organic fertilizer produced from the plant helps to improve food security and increase farmers income. On the other hand, biogas produced is considered a renewable and clean fuel that is used for cooking and heating. Currently, only 25% of the population in Malawi has access to electricity, and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is less affordable and not widely accessible. Therefore, due to a lack of alternative sources of energy, the majority of households are increasingly relying on dirty cooking fuels, which are blamed for indoor emissions that cause respiratory illnesses. However, due to high rates of deforestation, firewood is becoming scarce and less affordable, and women and girls, who are tasked with households chores, spend more time searching for firewood instead of focusing on agriculture.

core_fields.title: Value Addition of De-Oiled Rice Bran Using Yeast Fermentation for Antibiotic-Free and Omega-3 Enriched Broiler Meat Production
core_fields.description: This project develops a yeast-based fermentation technology for value-adding underutilized agro by-product de-oiled rice bran (DORB) as a sustainable feed ingredient for broiler feed industry. This approach integrates Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Yarrowia lypolytica to produce quality feed ingredients, probiotics (yeast), and prebiotics (yeast metabolites). This reduces antibiotic dependency in broiler production, promotes omega-3 enriched meat, and addresses feed import dependency, ensuring safe, healthy broiler meat production in Bangladesh and other developing rice-producing countries.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Broiler farming is critical in developing countries like Bangladesh to meet the people s protein demand. However, limited availability of affordable quality feed ingredients and reliance on costly imported feed ingredients, overuse of antibiotics, and at the same time inefficient utilization of local agricultural by-products hinder the growth of the industry. These issues contribute to risk in human health, including antibiotic resistance, compromised meat safety for human consumption, increased production costs, and environment burdens. Additionally, there is a growing demand for healthier meat enriched with omega-3 fatty acids, which is rarely addressed in traditional broiler production systems. Moreover, agricultural by-products like de-oiled rice bran (DORB), a by-product of rice milling industry, remain underutilized, despite their potential as a valuable feed ingredient. Solution: This project aims to address this challenge by enhancing the value of DORB through yeast fermentation technology, utilizing Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Yarrowia lypolytica. This process enhances the nutritional value of DORB, and the fermented DORB will serve as a sustainable, nutrient-rich feed ingredient for broilers. Yeast and its metabolites (beta-glucan, Mannan oligosaccharides, chitin, peptides, etc.) will act as probiotics and prebiotics, reducing the reliance on antibiotics while enhancing broiler gut health, immunity, and meat quality. Additionally, utilizing yeast in broiler diets enriches broiler meat with omega-3 fatty acids, meeting the consumer demands for healthier and safer poultry products. This approach promotes local resource use, reduces feed costs, and supports small-scale poultry farmers, aligns with consumer health trends, and contributes to global efforts to achieve sustainable food systems.

The initiative addresses major challenges, like a lack of storage facilities and unreliable energy access. These issues often lead to significant food loss. By providing an affordable way to keep perishable goods fresh, the project aims to ensure that more harvested crops reach consumers. This will boost
core_fields.abstract: The implementation of solar-powered cold storage technology in rural Tigray addresses a critical issue: post-harvest losses, which severely affect farmers' livelihoods and food security. The absence of adequate storage facilities and unreliable energy access often leads to considerable food waste, particularly concerning perishable goods. The proposed solution entails installing solar-powered cold storage units on farms, which will enable farmers to maintain their produce at optimal temperatures. This approach takes advantage of the abundant solar energy available in the region, presenting a sustainable and cost-effective method to extend the shelf life of perishable items. Solar-powered cold storage systems utilize photovoltaic panels to generate electricity that powers refrigeration units. This technology is particularly well-suited for off-grid areas, as it diminishes reliance on diesel generators and reduces carbon emissions. Research has demonstrated that such systems can significantly decrease post-harvest losses and enhance the quality of stored produce. By reducing spoilage, farmers can store produce longer, sell at higher prices, and boost their income. A Nigerian study showed that cold storage increased farmers' net sales by nearly 70%. Improved storage leads to fresher produce, enhancing food quality and safety. Additionally, using solar energy reduces reliance on fossil fuels, lowering greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainability. Hence, by adopting solar-powered cold storage technology, rural Tigray can improve food security, increase farmers' incomes, and contribute to environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Making chocolate from the desert: mesquite beans as an emerging staple legume in the future of our food system.
core_fields.description: Mesquite is often only associated with barbecue sauce in the current food system, but we think mesquite s headline should hone in on its delicious, nutrient-packed fruit. Mez Foods is dedicated to increasing access and awareness of this super food through thoughtfully crafted CPG products - starting with chocolate alternatives. This project will use grant funding to grow manufacturing capacity to positively impact the mesquite bean farmers of the Southwestern United States, Argentina, and Peru.
core_fields.abstract: Cacao, the foundation of chocolate products, faces a crisis due to climate change, labor exploitation, and unsustainable farming. With demand for cacao expected to double by 2033 and growing regions shrinking, the industry is under pressure to maintain flavor, affordability, and availability. These challenges call for innovative, sustainable alternatives that address both supply chain vulnerabilities and consumer health concerns. Mesquite offers a game-changing solution. This climate-resilient tree thrives in arid conditions, transforming barren land into thriving forests. Its beans are naturally sweet, high in fiber, and rich in protein, making them an ideal ingredient for crafting healthier alternatives to cacao-based products. Unlike traditional chocolate, mesquite-based bars provide indulgent flavor without bitterness, which allows us to use less sugar in our products and while offering essential macronutrients. Mez Foods partners with farmers who harvest mesquite beans as a supplemental crop, particularly valuable during periods of low soy or wheat yields. The challenge isn t producing mesquite beans but creating finished products that utilize them effectively. Mez Foods has bridged this gap, developing mesquite-based chocolate alternatives that provide the sensory appeal of chocolate while promoting health and sustainability. Our approach supports farmers with diversified income, offers consumers a guilt-free indulgence, and reduces environmental impact by preventing deforestation, combating desertification, and promoting agrobiodiversity. With this grant, Mez Foods will scale production and expand our product offerings, establishing mesquite as a key player in reshaping the global food system and providing a sustainable, healthy alternative to cacao.

core_fields.title: FarmHive Market: Transforming On-Farm Marketing Through Digital Innovation
core_fields.description: We plan to expand the FarmHive platform to include the FarmHive Market, an online market linkage tool for publishing expected harvest information to potential buyers. We propose to test and release these features in India and Nigeria while measuring the uptake of the tool among farmers, agricultural extension workers and produce buyers.
core_fields.abstract: Farmers and produce offtakers are often unaware of real-time supply and demand information, contributing to post-harvest losses and reduced efficiencies. Due to low information access, both sides suffer missed market opportunities, leading to food waste and reduced income. Our innovation consists of implementing a real-time data sharing platform that connects farmers with other value chain actors. We will adopt an existing platform developed at the Migal Galilee Research Institute called FarmHive (www.farmhive.co), a mobile friendly application and website for facilitating information sharing among farmers, agronomists and researchers. These features include a basic social network (Feed, Posts, Chat, Connections, etc) along with three features specialized to the agricultural sector: the Forum, for agricultural questions and answers, the Library, for agronomic resources, and the Farm Journal. The Farm Journal tool is a digital record of the farm, including cropping history and main activities, that can be easily shared with others such as farm advisors in order to accelerate knowledge sharing and collaboration. This tool will be finalized and adopted for this project to include a market linkage tool as well, FarmHive Market. This platform will enable real-time sharing of buyer and seller information along with contact information. Farmers, or their agricultural advisors, can share on-farm production information including expected and actual harvest quantities. Market players will be given access to the platform to receive the information and contact relevant sellers via phone - increasing market exposure to farm produce while it is still in the ground.

core_fields.title: Milk with Dignity: Building a Sustainable Dairy Industry for Workers, Farmers, and Consumers Alike
core_fields.description: For the past thirteen years, Latinx immigrant farmworkers in the U.S. Northeast have successfully organized through Migrant Justice, achieving a string of transformative victories. In 2017, Migrant Justice launched Milk with Dignity, a worker-driven program that wins binding agreements with corporations to raise wages, improve labor conditions, and ensure enforceable human rights protections in their dairy supply chains. Funding will support the continued implementation and expansion of the Program.
core_fields.abstract: Immigrant farmworkers are among the most marginalized and excluded people in the United States. As a legacy of chattel slavery, agriculture work continues to be performed by racialized groups excluded from basic rights afforded to other workers. The dairy industry is no exception, relying on undocumented workers laboring seven days a week, for below minimum wage, living in inhumane housing conditions, and subject to injuries, harassment, and violence. The Milk with Dignity Program is based on the global model Worker-driven Social Responsibility, which leverages the joint power of workers and consumers worldwide to put pressure on corporations to reform their sourcing practices, redistributing wealth and power throughout their supply chain. The Program partners with corporations and institutions that buy dairy products. Buyers commit to sourcing their milk from farms enrolled in the Milk with Dignity Program and agree to pay a premium to the farms in their supply chains. The farms, in turn, agree to use that premium to improve wages, benefits, health and safety standards, housing conditions, and increase protections against violence, sexual harassment, discrimination, and retaliation. The Milk with Dignity Program is transforming an industry plagued by severe and persistent human rights violations and putting power into the hands of workers themselves to determine and achieve dignified conditions. Milk with Dignity has resulted in the investment of millions of dollars into improved conditions on dairy farms, building a sustainable dairy industry in which consumers can buy dairy products with the knowledge that they were produced in fair conditions.

core_fields.title: Take a Teacher To Lunch

These communities typically lack access to fresh produce, sustainable food options, and educational resources about healthy eating habits, perpetuating cycles of poor nutrition and health outcomes. Teachers are provided with healthy sustainably sourced meals and participate in "lunch-and learn" sessions featuring keynote speakers who are experts in the field and activities that focus on food sustainability, healthy eating, and practical tool they can integrate into their classrooms to also educate their students. This innovative approach empowers teachers to serve as community ambassadors for food education, directly influencing students and families. The solution is grounded in the understanding that educators are trusted community leaders, as well as consumers. By equipping them with knowledge and resources, we extend the impact of our efforts beyond the individual to entire school ecosystems. Immediate benefits include teacher appreciation, professional growth, and improved access to healthy meals. Long-term benefits include fostering healthier eating habits, supporting sustainable local food systems, and reducing the environmental impact of food choices. This approach strengthens consumer trust in sustainable practices, improves access to nutritious food, and builds healthier, more informed communities while supporting local producers and reducing environmental strain.

core_fields.abstract: Innovation in food farming has been critical to addressing the challenges of feeding a growing global population, ensuring sustainability, and improving food security 1)By optimizing water use, fertilizer application, and pesticide use, precision farming reduces waste and increases crop yields. 2)Sustainable Farming Practices: Techniques such as agroecology, permaculture, and regenerative agriculture focus on soil health, biodiversity, and reducing chemical inputs, which help sustain ecosystems and enhance long-term productivity. The agricultural sector in Ghana faces several challenges which affects our business as well. 1)Low Productivity and Traditional Farming Methods: Many farmers in Ghana still use traditional farming techniques, which are labor-intensive and less efficient. The lack of access to modern farming technologies and equipment, such as tractors, irrigation systems, and high-yielding seeds, leads to low productivity. 2)Pests and Diseases: Farmers often struggle with crop pests and diseases, which can destroy entire harvests. 3)Lack of finance to invest in good agricultural practices and management. Solution we are providing and hope to expand with our farm. By focusing on climate resilience, technological adoption, financial access, infrastructure development, and sustainable practices, Ghana s farming sector can overcome its challenges. These solutions, combined with strong government policies and international cooperation, can create a more productive, sustainable, and prosperous agricultural future for the country. Benefits of our business: Consumers and schools : most of our raw grains and processed palm oil is supplied to schools for meals. Farmers/community: we buy from small holder farmers to support their work providing earnings.Also adopting safe environment practices.

core_fields.title: Empowering Women and Smallholder Farmers to Transform Food Systems with Sustainable Production of Biofortification Foods
core_fields.description: Our project empowers smallholder farmers through biofortification farming and supports market access via Moppet's nutritious, affordable foods production. The Moppet Champion initiative trains consumers to promote, sell, and earn income from Moppet products, driving conscious consumer choices and enhancing household income. Additionally, the Moppet WEM Hub provides women entrepreneurs with renewable energy facilities for food safety training and production. Together, these efforts enhance food security, reduce post-harvest losses, and foster economic resilience in underserved communities.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition in children, nutrient deficiency, and food insecurity remain critical challenges in communities in Nigeria, compounded by climate change, unreliable energy for food production, and post-harvest losses among smallholder farmers. Nutrient-deficient diets have led to widespread health issues, particularly among children, while climate change disrupts agricultural productivity, further worsening food shortages and economic instability. Our innovation addresses these interconnected problems through a biofortification farming program that is climate resilient and nutrient rich. We train and provide seeds to smallholder farmers to grow nutrient-rich crops. These crops not only combat nutrient deficiencies but are also more resilient to climate change. Farmers are equipped with sustainable practices to optimize yield and reduce environmental impact. To solve the major challenge of lack of market access, Moppet s solar-powered production facilities provide a consistent market for these farmers, ensuring a steady income, and making affordable food accessible. Additionally, the Moppet WEM Hub empowers women entrepreneurs with production facilities for food product and safety training , building economic resilience and community-driven food systems. The solution is based on scientific insights into biofortification s role in addressing malnutrition and the need for renewable energy to tackle climate-induced challenges. By integrating agricultural innovation with energy efficiency, this approach provides a scalable and sustainable model. Immediate benefits include improved farmer incomes, access to affordable and nutritious food, and reduced food waste. Sustainable benefits encompass improved public health, strengthened local economies, climate-resilient agriculture, reduced carbon emissions, and a food system that ensures equitable access to safe and nutritious food for all.

core_fields.title: Empowering Communities through Sustainable Agriculture Innovations for Healthier Futures
core_fields.description: This project aims to develop sustainable agricultural practices that enhance food security and health in local communities. By introducing innovative techniques and providing training, we will empower farmers to increase yield, reduce environmental impact, and improve nutrition. Our approach will foster collaboration among stakeholders to ensure long-term benefits for consumers, farmers, and the environment, ultimately creating resilient communities equipped to face future challenges.
core_fields.abstract: The project addresses the pressing issue of food insecurity and unsustainable agricultural practices that compromise health and environmental integrity. Many local farmers face challenges such as low crop yields, poor soil health, and limited market access, leading to economic instability and inadequate nutrition for their communities. Our innovative solution integrates regenerative agriculture techniques, such as agroecology and permaculture, to enhance soil fertility, biodiversity, and resilience against climate change. By utilizing organic composting, crop rotation, and cover cropping, we can improve soil health and increase yields sustainably. Training workshops and resources will empower farmers with the knowledge and skills to implement these practices effectively. The scientific foundation of our approach is rooted in the understanding that healthy ecosystems lead to productive agriculture. Research shows that regenerative practices not only boost crop productivity but also enhance carbon sequestration and reduce the reliance on chemical inputs. Immediate benefits include higher yields and improved farmer incomes, while long-term advantages encompass enhanced community resilience, better nutrition, and a reduced environmental footprint. Schools will also benefit from access to fresh, locally sourced produce, fostering healthier eating habits among students. Ultimately, this initiative will create a sustainable agricultural model that supports farmers and nourishes communities, paving the way for future generations to thrive.

core_fields.title: Solar Energy for reduced malnutrition
core_fields.description: We are a food processing company, we buy raw materials from farmers, process them into nutritious food which we sell to retail shops and NGOs. Currently malnutrition in Malawi is at 36% among children leading to stunted growth and poor health. We would like to expand our food processing efforts. Invest in solar dryers to process moringa and grains into highly nutritious porridge flour aimed at reducing malnutrition and work with 1,000 farmers.
core_fields.abstract: Malawi is an agrobased economy relying on rain fed agriculture, most farm produce end up wasted or exported raw without being processed, on the the hand, Malnutrition is very high, affecting children the most. To address this we established a food process business, where we make highly nutritious food especially baby porridge flour. Our efforts to process and add value to agro produce are constantly disrupted by limited access to electricity. Our country has one of the lowest electricity generation, persistent blackouts affect value addition and innovation around food. We are looking to finance solar equipment such as dryers, roasters and mixers that will enable add to process Moringa based food products such as porridge flour, spices and oil. These are highly nutritious food products that can help reduce malnutrition. In this project we plan to partner with 1,000 rural farmers who will supply the us with farm produce such as maize, Soya and Moringa, in turn we will use our solar powered appliances to process these farm produce into highly nutritious food products. These farmers will not only benefit from the access to market, we will also offer them trainings in Good Agricultural Practices and also offer them farm inputs, such as certified seed. Our food products are already in retail shops across the country and we are also selling to NGOs that run child feeding programs. In this project we expect to increase our customer base and start exporting our products.

core_fields.title: "Enhancing Climate-Resilient Sunflower Farming for Sustainable Livelihoods and Environmental Regeneration"
core_fields.description: This project empowers smallholder farmers in semi-arid regions through climate-resilient sunflower farming practices like deep mulching, organic manure application, and crop rotation. By enhancing soil fertility, mitigating drought effects, and restoring degraded land, the initiative boosts crop yields and farmer incomes. It promotes sustainability, environmental regeneration, and community resilience while contributing to global food security and the development of sustainable agricultural value chains.
core_fields.abstract: Problem Description Smallholder farmers in semi-arid regions face declining productivity due to drought, degraded land, and unsustainable farming practices. These challenges lead to low yields, reduced incomes, and food insecurity. The lack of climate-resilient strategies and limited value addition opportunities exacerbates these issues, threatening rural livelihoods and the environment. Solution Description This project integrates climate-resilient sunflower farming techniques, including deep mulching to conserve moisture, organic manure application to enrich soil fertility, and crop rotation to regenerate degraded land. To maximize benefits, we also focus on value addition by producing cold-pressed sunflower oil and sunflower seed cake animal feed supplements. The innovation leverages scientific insights on water retention, soil structure improvement, and sustainable land management. Deep mulching minimizes water loss, regulates soil temperature, and prevents weed competition, while organic manure improves nutrient availability and soil health. Value addition transforms raw sunflower seeds into high-quality products, boosting profitability and creating diversified income streams. Benefits Farmers: Increased yields, stable incomes, and access to value-added markets for sunflower oil and animal feed supplements. Environment: Regeneration of degraded land, enhanced soil health, and reduced carbon footprints. Communities: Strengthened food security, job creation, and economic resilience. Society: Contribution to sustainable agricultural value chains and global food system transformation. This solution ensures immediate benefits, such as higher yields and value-added revenue, while addressing long-term environmental and socio-economic challenges, positioning farmers as leaders in climate-smart and value-driven agriculture.
