core_fields.title: Reducing post-harvest losses with solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and sustainable preservation technologies
core_fields.description: Our project combats post-harvest losses by providing solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and a plant-based edible coating, extending the shelf life of perishable produce from 2 to 21 days. By offering affordable, sustainable solutions, we empower smallholder farmers, market grocers, and cooperatives to reduce waste, increase incomes, and enhance food security. With a growing customer base and proven impact, we aim to revolutionize agricultural value chains in Uganda, Zimbabwe, and beyond.
core_fields.abstract: In Uganda and Zimbabwe, over 50% of perishable produce spoils due to inadequate storage and cooling facilities, leading to significant post-harvest losses, reduced incomes for farmers, food insecurity, and environmental waste. This challenge is particularly relevant in rural and peri-urban areas where access to electricity and modern storage solutions is limited. Our innovative solution combines solar-powered IoT cooling hubs and MunaFresh , a plant-based edible coating, to address this issue. The cooling hubs extend the shelf life of perishable produce from 2 to 21 days, while MunaFresh further preserves fruits and vegetables by reducing moisture loss and microbial growth. These technologies are affordable and accessible, with farmers paying as little as $0.40 per crate per day, ensuring widespread adoption. This solution is driven by insights into renewable energy, IoT technology, and agricultural science, designed to provide a sustainable, off-grid alternative to conventional cooling systems. Immediate benefits include a 40% reduction in post-harvest losses, a 30% increase in farmers incomes, and improved food availability for consumers. Long-term, it supports environmental sustainability by reducing food waste and greenhouse gas emissions, and it boosts rural economies by creating jobs and supporting agribusinesses. By transforming agricultural value chains, this project empowers smallholder farmers, grocers, and communities to achieve greater food security, economic resilience, and environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Improving pumpkin production and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil for improved food, nutrition, and income security in Uganda
core_fields.description: The project aims to combat malnutrition and address lower urinary tract syndrome in mature males by contributing to the sustainable production of pumpkins through the precise identification of disease-causing pathogens and the extraction and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil as a functional food for culinary uses. Furthermore, the project is aimed at increasing a critical mass of professionals in pumpkin plant pathology for sustainable pumpkin production in the region.
core_fields.abstract: The project aims to enhance disease prevention for sustainable pumpkin production through the precise identification of pathogens causing the diseases and to build a critical mass of human resources for improved pumpkin production. The project also aims at the formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil for culinary purposes. Pumpkins are priced for their nutritious fruits, leaves, and seeds. In Uganda, the production of pumpkins is compromised by several diseases (Masika et al., 2022), affecting the quantity and quality, limiting their usage (Savary et al., 2012). Disease control will lead to increased production hence spurring value addition efforts towards production of pumpkin seed oil. Advanced molecular and sequencing techniques will be used to detect fungal pathogens for improved management. Sequencing allows for the identification of previously unknown and novel microbes (Ansorge, 2009). The project is further aimed at the formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil, which has been used in culinary and traditional medicine for millennia as a functional food (Ceclu et al., 2020). In our previous study, viruses affecting pumpkin production were identified in pooled samples, and study for the formulation of pumpkin seed oil and its use in the management of lower urinary tract infections in rats has shown great promise. Identification of pathogens affecting pumpkin production will lead to better management of diseases and improved production. Formulation and commercialization of pumpkin seed oil for culinary purposes will increase access to notorious foods in schools and communities. This will lead to increased food, nutrition and income security.

core_fields.title: Empowering Communities by Transforming Agricultural Waste into Nutritious Food, Renewable Energy, and Soil Health Circular Economy Solutions
core_fields.description: Our project empowers Ugandan rural farming communities to convert agricultural waste into valuable resources within a circular farming model. We transform waste into substrates for producing nutritious mushrooms and generate renewable energy through biogas systems using spoiled and subpar mushrooms. Additionally, contribute to soil health improvement with champost. This circular economy approach addresses food insecurity, creates income opportunities, and promotes sustainable agricultural practices, contributing to environmental resilience and community well-being while fostering regenerative farming methods.
core_fields.abstract: Uganda faces significant challenges related to food loss, food insecurity, and poverty, exacerbated by practices such as bush burning, inadequate waste management, climate variability and environmental degradation. Approximately 797,000 people in Uganda are currently experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, with projections indicating this number could rise to 953,000 by mid-2025 if no interventions are made. Additionally, about 20.3% of the population lives below the poverty line, and one in four children under five is stunted due to malnutrition. Our project addresses these critical issues by transforming agricultural waste into valuable resources through a circular economy model, reducing the environmental impact of agricultural systems and reclaiming value for the poor rural agragrian communities. We convert agricultural by-products, such as husks and stalks, into substrates for growing nutritious mushrooms to enhance food security by providing access to nutrient-rich food. Furthermore, we generate renewable energy from spoiled and subpar mushrooms using biogas systems, which mitigates reliance on traditional energy sources. The scientific insight behind our solution is rooted in waste valorization principles that emphasize reusing agricultural by-products to create sustainable systems. The immediate benefits for farmers include increased income opportunities through mushroom sales and improved soil health via the production of champost. Ultimately, our initiative promotes sustainable agricultural practices, enhances community resilience, and contributes to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2 (Zero Hunger), 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), fostering long-term benefits for society and the environment.

core_fields.title: Nagida leverages technology to optimize the staple food value chain for businesses & individual consumers while supporting local farmers with access to affordable inputs, financing & technical support
core_fields.description: NAGIDA is a tech-driven platform optimizing the staple food value chain end-to-end. It empowers individuals and businesses with access to fresh, affordable, & hygienic staples with "customized processing" options while supporting local farmers with affordable inputs, financing, and technical assistance. Focused on sustainability and efficiency, NAGIDA addresses food inflation, supply chain inefficiencies, and operational challenges, promoting rural & urban economic impact & creating a scalable solution with a clear competitive edge in local and global
core_fields.abstract: 70% out of the 80% of smallholder farmers in Nigeria live below $5 and 58% of this live below the extreme poverty line despite their hard work, amounting to over 40 million local farmers across the 6 geo-political zones of the country. With Nigeria's Inflation reaching over 39%, These farmers face significant challenges such as High input costs, finance support, post-harvest losses which have spiked suicide rates among rural farmers, limited access to sustainable farming techniques, logistic support & direct off-takers leading to inefficiencies, Inequality & exploitation from middle-men living with them within same community who pay these farmers stipends to farm on their own land and take over all harvests. In addition, Over 19.8 million unemployed Women and youths in both rural and urban living below the poverty line lack adequate training, resources, and market access needed to explore small-scale agribusinesses that could boost their incomes and stabilize local food supplies. These challenges further exacerbate food insecurity, Social breakdown, and inequalities in society. Through an innovative and state-of-the-art technology-driven platform supported by AI, IoT & Blockchain, Nagida bridges these gaps by empowering farmers with affordable inputs, financing, technical support, logistics, and direct market access. Unemployed women and youths receive training and are onboarded as SME suppliers, fostering economic stability. For consumers and businesses, Nagida offers customizable solutions for accessing fresh, affordable, and hygienic staples tailored to specific preferences, from fresh produce-preprocessed-processed-meal kits. This helps individuals save time and navigate inflation, while businesses optimize operations, cut costs,and manage inventory efficiently.

core_fields.title: Building a post-harvest chain platform that allows rural farmers to store, manage and monetize their produce
core_fields.description: Intended to address key agricultural challenges related to poor post-harvest management, recognizing the multi-dimensional nature of poverty where technology is one of the factors contributing to livelihood improvement, the project will enable effective management of post-harvest processes for at least 2000 farmers cultivating maize, beans, rice and grains/pulses, so they will scale to deliver surplus harvests to markets with a peace-of-mind.
core_fields.abstract: The agricultural supply chain in Uganda is unnecessarily long, intricately disconnected and disintegrated. The mostly smallholder farmers suffer a significant gap in connectedness and infrastructure, and as a result, they lose 30-50% or 120-170kgs (over 1.3 billion tons) of produce annually to post-harvest spoilage. Add climate change to this scenario, problems multiply because the food spoilage process is often quickly expedited, forcing farmers to quickly sell what they can - and at huge discounts, or risk their produce rotting, keeping them trapped in poverty cycles. In addition, urban dwellers also find it hard to access quality, safe and fresh food due to massive distribution delays and poor handling by third parties, leading to massive food waste the cost of which is passed on to end consumers who are paying high price points, often 200% on average for semi-fresh food from food retailers. To protect food security in Uganda, Nampya Farmers Market provides solar-powered micro-warehouses near farm clusters, making it easier and more affordable for smallholder farmers to store and insure more of their harvest. We also run a USSD-based, tech-enabled food supply platform connecting rural farmers directly to urban food retailers and off-takers, bypassing exploitative middlemen. This allows farmers to sell their produce at fair prices, promoting economic self-sufficiency and supporting sustainable food supply chains. With mobile money payments integrated into the system, Nampya facilitates smooth, direct transactions, helping greengrocers, hotels and restaurants source better-quality and competitively-priced food straight from the farmgate to their doorstep.

core_fields.title: Nandi hills animal feeds junction
core_fields.description: Nandi Hills Animal Feeds Junction, founded in 2019, specializes in producing affordable, quality animal feeds and silage for smallholder farmers. We aim to scale operations by acquiring advanced equipment to improve production, efficiency, and accessibility, empowering farmers to maximize their yields and profits.
core_fields.abstract: Nandi Hills Animal Feeds Junction has developed an innovative solution to transform animal feed production and silage management for smallholder farmers. The initiative focuses on acquiring advanced machinery such as a pellet-making machine, modern silage chopper, silage baler, and feed mixer, alongside a tractor for transport and field operations. Problem Solved: Smallholder farmers struggle with inefficient feed production, poor feed quality, and high transportation costs. These challenges lead to lower livestock productivity and reduced income. Relevance: Access to high-quality, affordable feed is critical for sustainable livestock farming, especially in regions reliant on small-scale agriculture for food security and income generation. Solution: The innovation combines modern equipment with localized expertise to produce pelletized animal feeds, uniformly mixed rations, and baled silage. This approach ensures affordability, consistent quality, and ease of transportation. Scientific/Technical Insight: The adoption of pelletization enhances feed digestibility and reduces wastage. Balers preserve silage for extended periods, while mixers ensure nutrient uniformity, directly addressing feed quality issues. Benefits: 1. Farmers: Increased livestock productivity and income through affordable, high-quality feed. 2. Communities: Improved food security due to enhanced livestock production. 3. Environment: Reduced feed waste and efficient use of by-products like maize stalks. 4. Society: Economic empowerment of rural communities by reducing dependence on imported feeds. This solution fosters immediate benefits while supporting long-term sustainability, resilience, and environmental stewardship.

core_fields.title: Lamatu Precision fertilization for sustainable food system and soil health
core_fields.description: Lamatu champions AI-navigated, advanced non-polymer nanoparticle as the core component of its technology for controlled-release fertilizers. By integrating smart nutrient delivery systems, the project aims to enhance crop yields, improve soil health, and reduce environmental impacts resulting from fertilizer inefficiency, primarily nitrogen pollution. Through precision fertilization, Lamatu warrants environmentally responsible fertilization practices, ensuring long-term food security while fostering harmony between agriculture and the planet's ecosystems.
core_fields.abstract: The global agricultural system faces significant challenges related to the inefficiency of traditional chemical fertilizers, with nitrogen fertilizers among the key contributor. These fertilizers are subjected to nutrient loss, often observed through leaching, volatilization, and runoff. As a result, plant nutrient uptake decreases creating a starvation situation besides, contributing to environmental pollution. Fertilizer inefficiency results in farmers needing to apply fertilizers multiple times throughout the growing season, which increases labor costs and fuel consumption. This is compounded by the rising prices of chemical fertilizers, which have been heavily impacted by global supply chain disruptions and the increasing cost of raw materials, such as natural gas, which is a key component in fertilizer production (Haber process). Chemical fertilizers are primarily derived from non-renewable resources, such as phosphate rock and natural gas. As these resources become scarcer and more expensive, the long-term sustainability of conventional fertilization practices is increasingly questionable. Furthermore, the labour shortage in agriculture exacerbates the problem, as farmers struggle to manage multiple fertilizer applications and additional labour costs. Lamatu offers a sustainable solution by using controlled-release fertilizers (CRFs) with coatings made from nanoparticles derived from rice husk agro-waste. This renewable material gradually releases nutrients, improving fertilizer efficiency and reducing nutrient loss due to leaching and runoff. By minimizing the need for multiple applications, it reduces labor, fuel, and equipment costs. Additionally, the rice husk coating provides secondary nutrients like silica, benefiting soil health. This approach not only cuts production costs but also supports environmentally friendly and sustainable agricultural practices.

core_fields.title: Enhancing household nutrition through adoption of climate resilient greengram and sorghum varieties and biodynamic manures in drier regions of Uganda
core_fields.description: The semi-arid regions of Uganda are faced with high malnutrition and extreme household poverty due to low crop productivity caused by declining soil fertility, frequent droughts, and the cultivation of low-yielding varieties with low levels of nutrients. Therefore, the proposed project intends to validate and promote climate-resilient greengram and sorghum varieties that are high in nutrient levels, and locally made biodynamic manures to enhance crop productivity and address the household food and nutritional insecurity challenge.
core_fields.abstract: The semi-arid regions of Uganda are characterized by low agricultural productivity, high malnutrition, and extreme poverty (UBOS 2017). The main causes of this are; frequent droughts, declining soil fertility, and cultivation of varieties that are low yielding and low in nutrient content. Given that agriculture is the dominant occupation of farmers in the regions, validating, disseminating, and promoting improved agricultural technologies adapted to semi-arid conditions is key in addressing household food and nutritional insecurity. Adopting resilient greengram and sorghum varieties with a high level of nutrients could enhance crop productivity and household food nutrition. The National Agricultural Research Organization has developed greengram and sorghum varieties lines that are tolerant to drought and rich in iron, zinc, calcium, and carbohydrates. The improved greengram and sorghum lines and locally made biodynamic manures are ready for on-farm evaluation before they can be disseminated to the farming communities in the region. The inclusion of these greengram and sorghum varieties in diets will lead to the well-being of children, expectant and lactating mothers, and school children. Greengram is known to enrich soil fertility, therefore, its cultivation and application of locally made biodynamic manures would improve and sustain soil fertility. Therefore, this project proposal is submitted to the Institute of Food Technology for financial support to enable the project team to conduct on-farm evaluation and dissemination of the developed improved greengram and sorghum varieties and locally made biodynamic manures to the farming communities to enhance household nutrition and income security in the project area.

core_fields.title: Scaling-up sorghum value addition with climate-smart food products, post-harvest management, and sustainable production in Siaya County, Kenya.
core_fields.description: Our innovation transforms sorghum (a staple cereal) into more nutrient-dense products that are affordable, accessible, and desirable. Central to our success is collaboration and building a circular economy to ensure that our fortification ingredients are organic, locally available, and culturally accepted. We support farmers in growing climate-smart crops that support soil health, millers in knowing the correct ratio to create a nutritious sorghum flour and ensure that children find the fortified porridge and products appealing.
core_fields.abstract: According to the 2020 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey (KDHS), 41% of children under five and 24% of women of reproductive age suffer from anemia (Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, 2020), leading to poor birth outcomes, maternal mortality, and developmental delays. Furthermore, chronic malnutrition has led to stunting in 18% of children under five nationwide, with Siaya (19.2%) recording among the highest rates, affecting children's growth, cognitive development, and future productivity. Promoting indigenous crops like sorghum, amaranth, and orange-fleshed sweet potatoes that are rich in iron, zinc, and vitamin A offers a sustainable solution. This project utilizes organic acid-rich plant foodstuffs and beta-carotene-rich plants, such as guava fruit and amaranth leaves, to improve the mineral bioaccessibility of whole grain sorghum flour and porridges in order to help reduce malnutrition in the target communities. Findings from our proof of concept proof stage show a formulation/recipe ratio of 100:1 (sorghum: natural plant fortificants) citric acid to iron molar ratio would yield maximum nutrient bioavailability in a fortified flour/porridge. This experience will guide the recipes/formulations developed during the current project scale-up. The tropical plants (such as mango, guava, and amaranth leaves) that will be used in the fortification exist in the community but have not been used in food-to-food fortification. Most of these nutritious fortificants (fruits and indigenous vegetables) go to waste due to their perishable nature. The project will, therefore, assist with both food wastage management and the integration of climate-smart, nutrient-dense plants into the food system through food-to-food

core_fields.title: Enhancing Sustainable Healthy and Safe Food Production in Tanzania
core_fields.description: The Project aims to address the critical challenges of food insecurity, malnutrition and environmental degradation in Tanzania by enhancing sustainable, healthy and safe food production. Leveraging the Global Food System Challenge framework, the initiative will promote innovative agricultural practices, empower smallholder farmers, and strengthen value chains to ensure nutritious food for all while safeguarding the environment. The project prioritize vulnerable groups, including women and youth, aligning with Tanzania s national development goals and SDGs
core_fields.abstract: Tanzania s agriculture sector employs over 65% of the population, contributing approximately 25% to GDP. However, the sector faces significant challenges, including low productivity, climate change impacts, and limited access to markets and inputs. These challenges have resulted in food insecurity, with over 34% of children under five experiencing stunted growth. The Global Food System Challenge provides a unique opportunity to transform the sector by integrating sustainable practices, fostering innovation and ensuring equitable access to healthy food. Tanzania s food production systems are under pressure from climate change, poor agricultural practices, and limited infrastructure, leading to food insecurity, malnutrition, and environmental degradation. This project addresses these challenges by introducing climate smart agriculture and agroecological practices, empowering farmers with knowledge, and improving value chains. The innovation integrates scientific and traditional insights, such as drought resistant crops and sustainable land management, ensuring productivity while protecting natural resources. Immediate benefits include increased yields, reduced post-harvest losses, and improved access to nutritious food. Sustainable benefits include enhanced soil health, resilience to climate change, and long-term food security for communities. End users, including farmers, schools, and society, will gain through higher incomes, better health outcomes, and a cleaner environment. This approach ensures inclusive growth, directly benefiting vulnerable groups while contributing to national and global development goals.

core_fields.title: Empowering Local Organic Growers: Certification & Capacity Building for Sustainable Growth
core_fields.description: This project empowers local organic grower groups to meet certification requirements and supports the certification process for premium pricing. Many regions in Nepal are organically farmed but lack evidence to assure consumers. The project trains Internal Inspectors to assist growers and offers certification services. After this period, the groups will be fully certified and self-sustaining, able to continue the certification process independently.
core_fields.abstract: The demand for organic foods is rapidly growing, however, many local organic grower groups of in rural Nepal remain uncertified. This stems from two key challenges: a lack of skilled personnel to guide farmers in certification processes such as Internal Control Systems, inspections, and documentation, and the high cost of organic certification at least at the initial stages. Nep.Cert addresses these issues by training local human resources and certifying products without imposing financial burdens on farmers. Over three years, farmers achieve full certification, enabling their products to bear the certification logo and command premium market prices. This boosts producer confidence and equips them to continue certification independently, creating a self-sustaining model. Successful examples inspire replication in other regions without external support. The project emphasizes organic farming by utilizing local renewable resources, contributing to increased farmer income, better food quality, and biodiversity conservation. Local certification forms the foundation for international accreditation, enabling farmers to transition from seasonal crops to high-value herbs and spices with global market potential. Nepal, rich in medicinal and aromatic plants, holds immense potential to supply niche Himalayan products globally. By empowering farmers with certification and market access, this project strengthens rural economies, enhances food security, and positions Nepal as a leader in sustainable organic farming.

core_fields.title: Climate-resilient nutritious crop irrigation system
core_fields.description: Provide climate-resilient Nutritious crop irrigation system powered by solar and artificial intelligence driven to optimize energy and water use for farming, helping millions Nutritious crop growers/vegetables, fruits and cereal farmers adapt to unpredictable climate patterns while enhancing nutritious crop yields eliminating acute food insecurity and malnutrition. The system uses Chabot and bulk SMS technology sending SMS to Nutritious crop growers with tailored tips and reminders for optimal long term sustainable Nutrition crop irrigation farming.
core_fields.abstract: Problem; Currently, less than 5% of cultivated land in sub-Saharan Africa is irrigated. The reliance on rainfed agriculture prevents farmers from cultivating high-value nutritious crops that often need large amounts of water that are applied more frequently. Some vegetable crops consist mostly of water, and their yield and quality, deteriorate rapidly under water stress. Rainfed agriculture limits smallholder production and profitability, particularly under climate change. It is therefore associated with higher food insecurity, poor diet quality, and high seasonal variability in diets. Solution; Provide climate-resilient Nutritious crop irrigation system powered by solar and artificial intelligence driven to optimize energy and water use for farming, helping millions Nutritious crop growers/vegetables, fruits and cereal farmers adapt to unpredictable climate patterns while enhancing nutritious crop yields eliminating acute food insecurity and malnutrition at the same time mitigate carbon dioxide emissions. The system uses Chabot and bulk SMS technology sending SMS to Nutritious crop growers with tailored tips and reminders for optimal long term sustainable Nutrition crop irrigation farming. Nutritious crop growers are registered to data base and receive electronic cards which saves as digital wallet used for paying irrigation bills on pay as you irrigate or pay per use. Nutritious crop growers who are youth and women with serious financial limitation have access to on credit and installment purchase as a special program allowing use the irrigation service and pays later after harvesting. We provide training to Nutritious crop growers using FAO climate smart irrigation training curriculum ensuring Nutritious crop sustainable farming.

core_fields.title: Scaling Sustainable Aquaponics for Food Security and Climate Resilience in Africa
core_fields.description: Our project scales innovative aquaponic systems (growing both fish and soilless crops in one system) to empower smallholder farmers in Africa with sustainable food production. By combining fish/crop farming, our solution optimises resource use, enhances food security, and builds climate resilience. By also integrating AI-driven monitoring and solar energy, we ensure efficiency, affordability, and sustainability. This project addresses food insecurity, promotes economic growth, and creates scalable impact for underserved communities, aligning with global sustainability goals.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovative aquaponic system addresses critical challenges of food insecurity, resource inefficiency, and environmental degradation in underserved regions. The problem is urgent: conventional farming consumes excessive water and land, depletes soil fertility, and struggles to meet the demands of growing populations, especially in climate-vulnerable areas. On average smallholder farmers earn $160/yr putting them under the poverty income line. Our system integrates fish farming and hydroponics, creating a closed-loop system where fish waste nourishes crops and plants purify water. This drastically reduces water usage by up to 95% compared to traditional agriculture, requires less land, and eliminates harmful chemical fertilisers. Solar-powered AI-driven monitoring ensures optimal production, reduces operational costs, and empowers farmers with real-time insights for decision-making. The innovation emerged from scientific and technical insights into circular food production systems and the need for scalable, low-cost solutions in resource-limited environments. Our solution directly benefits smallholder farmers by increasing yields, diversifying income streams, and improving food security. Communities gain access to affordable, nutritious produce while reducing environmental impact. The scalable design enables rapid adoption, creating ripple effects of economic and social resilience. Immediate benefits include increased food production efficiency (3000% more fish and 700% more crops in the same space), reduced resource consumption (using 95% less water), and farmer empowerment through accessible technology that increases their income by up to 10x! Long-term, our innovation builds climate resilience, fosters sustainable agricultural practices, and contributes to global food system transformation.

core_fields.title: Wood to Food: Building an enduring alternative to animal-based food products
core_fields.description: We develop highly sustainable meat alternatives by transforming woody biomass waste streams into fermentable substrates, grow specialty mushrooms on them and process the mushrooms into delicious food products. When scaling up we will partner globally with the forestry industry to produce the substrates, with farmers to cultivate the mushrooms and produce the fungal protein food, and with food services to serve delicious, affordable, healthy and easy to use food to their customers.
core_fields.abstract: The problem is that animal-based protein production has massive negative impact on climate, environment, biodiversity and animal welfare, and uses too much land. In addition, many of the currently available meat alternatives have issues with taste and texture, have too many ingredients, making them unhealthier again, are too expensive and use the same agricultural land to be produced. By using woody biomass as the main feedstock, we require virtually no agricultural land to produce our products, while replacing meat will free up large areas of agricultural land, that can then be used for reforestation, nature development, extensivation of other agricultural production. (sustainable benefits) Prior research and development in using wood as a carbon source for food and feed production led to the idea and insight that wood-based edible mushrooms can do exactly this. The technological process development involves developing optimal pre-treatment conditions for the woody biomass to obtain the most productive substrates. By partnering with farmers to participate in this production they will play a more meaningful role in the protein transition by producing higher margin products that just soybeans or peas for the protein industry. By partnering with food services they will get more and better options to serve their (vegan, vegetarian, flexitarian) customers delicious food, and the products can be easier tailored to their customers taste and preferences compared with meat alternatives produced in large centralized industrial factories.

core_fields.title: Promoting Bio-Fertilizer Adoption for Sustainable Farming in Tanzania's Drought-Prone Regions
core_fields.description: NovFeed Project combats soil degradation in Tanzania by introducing biofertilizers that restore soil health, boost crop yields, and reduce dependence on chemical inputs. The initiative enhances food security, creates jobs, and increases farmer incomes by leveraging Local Service Providers (LSPs) for farmer training, technical support, and market access. This sustainable approach empowers communities, fosters economic growth, and strengthens resilience against climate challenges, ensuring a more productive and environmentally friendly agricultural system.
core_fields.abstract: Soil degradation affects over 65% of Tanzania s arable land, driven by erosion, nutrient depletion, and heavy reliance on chemical fertilizers. These fertilizers worsen soil acidity, reduce productivity, and contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, threatening food security and farmer livelihoods. Crop yields, such as maize, have declined by 40% over two decades, further exacerbating food insecurity. Our innovation introduces biofertilizers as a sustainable alternative to chemical inputs. These eco-friendly products restore soil health by enriching it with essential nutrients and beneficial microorganisms. Unlike chemical fertilizers, biofertilizers reduce soil acidity, improve fertility, and enhance water retention, creating sustainable conditions for agriculture. The solution draws on scientific insights into microbial soil enrichment and its ability to stabilize yields under changing climatic conditions. The project integrates Local Service Providers (LSPs) to ensure farmers access biofertilizers, receive training, and adopt climate-smart techniques. This decentralized model promotes adoption, enhances technical support, and creates income-generating opportunities for LSPs. Farmers benefit immediately through increased yields, reduced input costs, and improved incomes. Long-term benefits include healthier soils, reduced emissions, and greater food security. Communities gain from resilient agricultural systems, while the environment benefits from reduced chemical runoff and enhanced biodiversity. This innovation empowers farmers with sustainable tools, addressing pressing challenges while fostering economic growth and environmental protection.

core_fields.title: Innovation for a Healthy Diet in Uganda: NutriPosh Program
core_fields.description: NutriPosh Program has already incorporated consumer feedback during the development of affordable, trusted, safe and nutritious fortified composite flours for complementary feeding and school feeding programs in Uganda. Besides providing enhanced nutrition through the inclusion of pumpkin seeds in stable composite maize flours, NutriPosh sources ingredients produced through regenerative agricultural practices, utilizes solar powered dehydration technologies in its composite flour production and uses biodegradable packaging. NutriPosh approach ensures environmental sustainability across the entire supply chain.
core_fields.abstract: In 2023, 37.7 million Ugandans could not afford a healthy diet. Malnutrition accounts for 4 in every 10 child deaths in Uganda. 764,576 children are underweight (too small for their age), 228,584 are wasted (too thin for their height), and 2.4 million Ugandan children are stunted (too short for their age) (UNICEF, 2024). Mandatory fortification applies to large mills with an output capacity of >20 metric tons (MT) per day, in Uganda. But most schools and households usually prepare meals using unfortified maize flours purchased from small mills, who according to the Food and Drugs (Food Fortification) Regulations, 2005, are not required to fortify as their daily output capacity is 20 MT. Most students in Uganda come from "food insecure households and often depend on school meals to meet their daily energy and nutritional requirements. If the school meals remain innutritious, the risk of children suffering from micronutrient and omega 3 deficiencies is increased; and this negatively impacts their cognitive health and educational outcomes. NutriPosh program benefits include; Farmers: NutriPosh Program accelerates uptake of regenerative agricultural practices; increases crop resilience against extreme weather and climate change; improves crop yields; and diversifies income streams. Schools: NutriPosh Program increases conscious consumerism; minimizes age-for-grade heterogeneity; and helps schoolchildren perform academically well. Society: NutriPosh Program increases conscious purchasing among nursing mothers and caregivers with post-6months old infants; stimulates cognitive development; and increase children s chances of academic success. Environment: NutriPosh Program promotes sustainable carbon capture and storage, at every step of the value chain.

core_fields.title: Solar UV Technology for Cocoa Honey Preservation and Transforming By-products into Superfoods in Regenerative Food Systems
core_fields.description: Our project uses solar UV technology to preserve cocoa honey, transforming agricultural by-products into high-value superfoods within regenerative food systems. By empowering smallholders with innovative processing and traceability solutions, we enhance sustainability, reduce food waste, and improve livelihoods in the cocoa value chain. With strategic partnerships and a scalable model, we aim to deliver nutritious and deliciosus upcycled products while setting new standards in sustainable food innovation.
core_fields.abstract: Our project tackles the pressing issue of waste and inefficiency in the cocoa supply chain, where 52,000 tons of byproducts are discarded annually in Brazil. Among these, cocoa honey a nutrient-rich byproduct with natural sweetening and antioxidant properties is often wasted due to microbial spoilage and inadequate preservation methods. To address this, we developed an innovative mobile solar UV technology that stabilizes cocoa honey directly on farms, reducing microbial activity, extending its shelf life, and preserving its properties for transformation into a natural sweetener for superfoods, including the world s first zero-fat chocolate enriched with vitamins and antioxidants. This is especially relevant as the global food system struggles to meet the nutritional needs of 10 billion people by 2050 while reducing waste and environmental impact. Our solution utilizes the germicidal effects of UV light to disrupt microbial DNA, combined with a custom-designed pilot reactor to enhance UV penetration and microbial inactivation. Computational modeling optimizes this scalable process under varying environmental conditions, ensuring efficiency. The preserved nutritional and functional properties of cocoa honey are maintained in superfood formulations. The benefits are wide-ranging. Smallholder farmers gain a sustainable revenue stream, increasing their income by up to 35% per harvest. Consumers and industries benefit from healthier, nutrient-rich alternatives to cane sugar, which is linked to obesity and diabetes. Environmentally, our approach reduces cocoa waste by 40% and promotes regenerative food systems. By transforming waste into high-value products, our innovation reduces environmental impact, supports healthier diets, and fosters sustainable consumption, setting new standards in food innovation.

core_fields.title: Food Identity: a path to a food system s approach with future
core_fields.description: This project aims to empower knowledge on food identity upon multiple stakeholders in the food sector. It focuses on three main objectives: provide specialized training to various entities (municipalities, schools and restaurants) to improve their food offer; promote food identity among producers to preserve ancient seeds; inspire individuals to make food choices with more social and environmental responsability. Together, these efforts aim to build resilient and sustainable food systems for the future.
core_fields.abstract: The food identity of a territory is the essence that allows it to be recognized in terms of food. It consists of the characteristics that, despite the normal dynamics of change, remain and enable continuity. This project addresses the decline of primary sectors like agriculture, challenges associated with rural depopulation, the underutilization of local resources, and the loss of food traditions that are intrinsic to territorial food identity. Additionally, it responds to consumer trends seeking more local and authentic experiences, starting with the food they eat. Promoting and providing training on food identity of a territory is essential in the context of building sustainable and resilient communities. This systemic approach benefits the environment and economy and reinvigorates local pride and the sense of belonging, promoting a vision where territories are recognized as exemplary models of balance, sustainability, and innovation. It s relevant since it aligns with global priorities, such as the preservation of cultural heritage, sustainable development, and food security. The solution is grounded in the insights and methodologies developed from the creation of Manuals of Food Identity, which involved comprehensive territorial and anthropological studies across 31 portuguese municipalities. An aspect of this approach was the individualized mentorship, effective in unlocking stalled dynamics, reactivating suspended initiatives, and crafting forward-looking strategies. Immediate benefits of this project include improved market access and training for farmers, education on sustainability for schools and facilitated link between tourism and agriculture. Long-term benefits feature economic resilience, healthier communities, biodiversity conservation, and strengthened local food systems.

Addressing gaps in education and employment, the initiative empowers youth to become leaders, role models, and agents of change within their communities. The solution is deeply rooted in cultural relevance, ensuring all resources and programs honour Indigenous traditions while providing modern skills necessary for success. The initiative enhances the community's ability to grow sustainably by uniting Indigenous wisdom with contemporary competencies. The advantages include heightened educational achievement, better job prospects, and increased community participation. Indigenous youth will develop confidence, acquire skills, and gain cultural pride, which will contribute to their communities' overall resilience and development. This project has a far-reaching impact on individuals and fosters broader societal objectives by encouraging equity, diversity, and inclusion. It meets immediate needs while establishing sustainable opportunities for the upcoming generation of Indigenous leaders.

core_fields.title: OKRA&KALE
core_fields.description: The global food system faces multidimensional challenges environmental degradation, dietary imbalances, unsustainable resource use, vulnerability to climate change, and lack of transparency. No single solution area can fully address these issues in isolation. Instead, integrating Protein Diversification, Sustainable Agriculture, Targeted Nutrition, and Circular Food Systems can create a more holistic and adaptive framework. By aligning interventions across these four areas, the food system can transition towards improved health outcomes, environmental stewardship, economic viability, and social equity.
core_fields.abstract: These interconnected issues threaten food security and public health while exacerbating environmental harm. Addressing these problems demands a holistic and adaptive approach that promotes health, sustainability, and equity across the food ecosystem. OKRA&KALE tackles these challenges by producing premium, sustainably cultivated spirulina in a certified organic farm. Spirulina is a nutrient-dense, eco-friendly superfood containing 70% protein by weight, along with iron, vitamins, and antioxidants. Spirulina is grown in an environmentally friendly manner, offering a scalable solution for nutritious and sustainable food sources. The innovation extends beyond production through a Machine Learning platform that unites consumers to the full lifecycle of spirulina. This platform ensures supply chain transparency via QR code tracking, provides tailored recipes to promote dietary health, and integrates tools to minimize food waste, optimize nutrition, and assess environmental impact. Scientific insights into spirulina s exceptional nutrient density and its low environmental footprint compared to traditional protein sources form the foundation of this solution. Immediate benefits include healthier diets for consumers, reduced food waste, and carbon footprint awareness. Long-term impacts include improved health outcomes, we have a catalogue of spirulina infused products which we hope to ship in the upcoming future i.e Spirulina Honey.

core_fields.title: One Smart Kitchen (OSK) Hub: User Field Trials for An AI-Enhanced Camera System to Reduce Food Waste in Home Kitchens
core_fields.description: The proposed field trial provides a fundamental step towards validating that the OSK AI technology encourages conscious consumer choices to reduce food waste. Users will be given prototype camera systems that track food items, suggest meals, and issue spoilage alerts to optimize food utilization. The trial data will help us train our AI and understand user behaviors to minimize waste. The knowledge gained will enable OSK to scale and maximize the overall food system impact.
core_fields.abstract: Solving the global food waste challenge requires changes at the individual level, yet consumers are often disconnected from the global impact of their daily choices. Globally, the UN estimates that approximately one-third of all food produced for human consumption is lost or wasted, contributing to nearly 8% of global greenhouse gas emissions. The average American consumer wastes about 260 pounds of food annually or approximately $1800 per household. According to EPA estimates, food waste is the largest category of items in disposal facilities in the USA. About two-thirds of household food waste occurs due to improper storage, lack of visibility in refrigerators, unused ingredients, and misjudged food needs. OSK translates the global food waste problem into a meaningful format to promote change at the individual level by enabling conscious consumer choices. The OSK hub is an AI-enabled camera system that can be placed on top of a refrigerator to track perishable items. Using AI, we segment the images from the camera to identify the items as they are placed into the fridge or pantry and track when they will spoil. Busy individuals and families receive timely alerts and suggested recipes when food needs to be used. This empowers consumers to make conscious choices to reduce food waste and build sustainable habits. Our affordable smart device prioritizes consumer choice, prevents vendor-lock to an appliance manufacturer, and supports habit changes over time. The OSK hub leverages recent advances in low-cost computing, camera sensors, and AI to enable conscious consumer choices.

core_fields.title: Commercializing indigenous Bambara Groundnuts as an alternative protein source to empower farmers and promote nutrition security in Kenya
core_fields.description: OnlyPlants is an alternative protein startup harnessing indigenous African crops to drive protein intake and empower smallholder farmers (SHFs). We have developed a novel enzymatic formulation for plant-based milk from Bambara groundnuts, a protein-dense legume traditionally cultivated by women SHFs. A key barrier to commercialization is the lack of high-quality seeds. OnlyPlants is partnering with KALRO and Egerton University to identify high-yielding varieties, train farmers on cultivation best practices, and establish an outgrower program.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: OnlyPlants addresses a critical food security challenge in Kenya- the growing need for accessible and nutritious protein sources amidst a changing climate and growing population. Kenyan agriculture, heavily reliant on rain-fed systems, faces increasing vulnerability due to unpredictable rainfall patterns, impacting crop yields and farmer livelihoods. Simultaneously, increasing awareness of health concerns and high lactose intolerance rates (approx. 85% across Sub-Saharan Africa) are driving demand for alternative proteins. OnlyPlants tackles this challenge by innovating new products that drive market demand for Bambara groundnuts (BGN), a drought-resistant, indigenous crop with high nutritional value. Solution: OnlyPlants tackles the underutilization of BGN by promoting their commercialization. We have developed proprietary enzyme-based process for BGN milk, ensuring cost-efficiency, high nutritional value, and optimal flavor. It brings out the milk s natural sweetness without added sugar and delivers strong functional attributes incl. heat stability and foaming capacity. Compared to oats, almonds and soy, BGN milk offers key advantages. BGN are grown locally, improve soil fertility through nitrogen fixation, and are drought-resistant. This creates an opportunity locally, where the product will be more affordable than imported alternatives, and for export markets, due to its strong nutrition and sustainability benefits. Benefits: Formalizing the BGN supply chain will empower women SHFs by providing access to higher-yielding seeds, technical support, and guaranteed market access. Furthermore, BGN are drought-resistant and fix nitrogen in the soil, allowing for lower input costs and improving yields of other crops grown in rotation. Finally, consumers benefit from n accessible, affordable, and nutritious protein source.

Oorja proposes to scale its climate-smart advisory by bundling services into a comprehensive package, including soil testing, seed supply, on-farm training on sustainable practices, and a mobile app, enabling farmers to access training schedules, agronomy advice, weather updates, and personalized recommendations.
core_fields.abstract: Oorja s innovation is a farm-based service package powered by decentralized solar energy, using a unique Pay-Per-Use (PPU) model. It addresses smallholder farmers' challenges of high irrigation costs, inadequate access to reliable energy, and unsustainable farming practices. In India, 30 million farmers rely on costly diesel pumps, consuming 12% of the country s diesel. The poorest farmers often rent pumps, paying 20-60% more than diesel costs, leading to under-irrigation, reduced yields, and limited cropping seasons. Unsustainable farming practices further degrade soil health and perpetuate poverty, with climate change exacerbating these issues. Oorja installs, owns, and operates solar pumps on farms, offering irrigation at 3-4 INR/m (4-5 US /m ), 20-60% cheaper than diesel. Farmers pay only for the water they use, measured by flowmeters. This model reduces costs, enables year-round cropping, and increases yields. Oorja complements irrigation with climate-smart advisory services, including soil testing, seed supply, and on-farm training in sustainable practices like natural input preparation and climate-resilient cropping. By bundling these services, including a mobile app for agronomy advice, weather updates, and training schedules, Oorja empowers farmers to adopt profitable, resource-efficient practices. This holistic approach improves productivity, enhances income stability, and reduces environmental impact, offering immediate and sustainable benefits to farmers, communities, and the environment.

core_fields.title: Public Procurement Toolkit for Health, Sustainable, and Economically Inclusive School Meal Programs
core_fields.description: This project will apply open contracting principles to create a practical toolkit for governments to enhance the inclusiveness and sustainability of school meal programs. It will provide guidance and procurement strategies for using data to engage small and local vendors. The toolkit will include actionable recommendations to improve access to affordable, healthy, locally produced food and offer practical tools, such as guidance on creating a catalog of healthy foods and implementing inclusive procurement policies.
core_fields.abstract: This project addresses exclusionary and unsustainable procurement practices in school meal programs, which waste resources, serve unhealthy food, and exclude small-scale farmers and minority producers. According to a survey conducted by the Global Child Nutrition Foundation, globally, 408.2 million children received school meals in 2022, yet only 13% of school-aged children in low-income countries benefit, compared to 48% in high-income countries. Per-child budgets in low- and middle-income countries dropped from $35.70 in 2017 to $28.04 in 2022, while only 10% of programs link small-scale farmers to school feeding. We will develop a bilingual toolkit (English/Spanish) leveraging open contracting principles to improve inclusiveness and sustainability in school meal procurement building on lessons from Colombia and Mexico. Bogot expanded vendors from 14 to 55, saved 10-15% in costs, and served 800,000 meals daily by exposing price-fixing. Palmira boosted vendor diversity by simplifying procurement processes for local and women-led businesses. Mexico City s Mi Tiendita Virtual streamlined vendor registration for SMEs, Indigenous groups, and rural producers. The toolkit will include: 1. Vendor Empowerment Tools: Templates for simplified procurement processes and guidance for showcasing locally produced and sustainable foods. 2. Data Frameworks: Strategies for identifying and engaging women-led businesses, rural producers, and Indigenous groups through procurement data. 3. Policy Roadmap: Step-by-step guidance for governments to implement inclusive and sustainable policies. Outcomes include healthier meals for children, stable markets for smallholder farmers, empowered marginalized producers, and more sustainable food systems. These changes will strengthen local economies, improve nutrition, and reduce environmental impact. Pitch video: https://youtu.be/52I4hja0YT4

core_fields.title: "Transforming Community Behaviors and Health Systems for Sustainable Nutrition in Bussi Islands, Wakiso District"
core_fields.description: This project seeks to address high rates of malnutrition in Bussi Islands, Wakiso District, by strengthening community health systems alongside behavioral change. Interventions like targeted nutrition education, improved health services, and community-based interventions will reduce stunting, wasting, and underweight conditions among children and improve maternal and child nutrition. Through harnessing local knowledge and integrating evidence-based practices, we will be improving nutrition at community levels toward contributing to the national goal of reducing malnutrition by 2030.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition remains a critical public health issue globally and in Uganda, contributing to high rates of child mortality and impaired development, especially among children under five and pregnant or breastfeeding women. Despite some progress, approximately 25.4% of children in Uganda are stunted, while 3.6% suffer from wasting, and 32.8% of women are affected by anemia. These figures reflect a broader crisis, as the country grapples with a triple burden of malnutrition undernutrition, overnutrition, and micronutrient deficiencies. In Bussi Islands, Wakiso District, the situation is dire, with 16.1% of children underweight and 7.8% experiencing wasting. Contributing factors include food insecurity, large household sizes, poor sanitation, and weak nutrition practices. Furthermore, insufficient community-based interventions, limited health-seeking behaviors and impacts of extreme weather event due to climate change exacerbate the problem. The solution proposed in this project uses several innovative approaches, including: Digital tools like an interactive USSD platform to share nutrition tips with farmers and local community to increase knowledge on food and good diet. Capacity building through training Village Health Teams (VHTs) on using digital tools like the GIS mapping and for malnutrition detection and timely referral. Sustainable Practices like demonstration gardens with biofortified crops, regenerative agriculture techniques coupled with food preservation training to reduce waste. These initiatives will have Immediate benefits to the community as they will gain knowledge of nutrition, better detection and treatment of malnutrition, and improved food security. In the long term, outcomes will include sustainable health systems, climate-resilient agriculture, reduced child mortality, and empowered communities.

core_fields.title: Cultivating Resilience: Promotion of Cover Crops for Sustainable Agriculture in West Africa
core_fields.description: Cover crops offer a scalable solution to the chronic problem of land degradation in West Africa. By covering and protecting the soil, they minimize erosion from rainfall and wind, and they can be quickly planted across many acres of fields. Cover crops add nitrogen and organic material to fields without the need for transport or agricultural chemicals. This project builds upon the 2023 seed grant to further expand cover crop seed production and implementation.
core_fields.abstract: Throughout West Africa, subsistence farmers face a soil degradation crisis. Previously fertile fields are now so tired that they can no longer produce sufficient harvests, even with significant applications of expensive chemical fertilizer. Before, farmers would often allow fields to fallow for several years between periods of cultivation. Now, due to population pressure, most agricultural lands are farmed or grazed every year. Eventually, these fields become exhausted and are abandoned, forcing people to migrate to more productive areas or move into crowded cities. Across the Sahel countries of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, the long term impacts of soil degradation are evident. Ten of thousands of farmers have been displaced and the resulting instability and poverty makes it easier for violent militant groups to capture territory and conduct attacks on vulnerable rural populations. Finding few options for gainful employment in rural areas, many young people move into cities that are already struggling with overcrowding and high rates of unemployment. Cover crops allow farmers to continue to cultivate their fields, while simultaneously repairing and improving the soil. They grow quickly, and throughout the growing season add significant amounts of nitrogen and organic material to soil. Over several seasons, they can rehabilitate previously exhausted fields. Planting cover crops offers an ecological alternative to the overuse of agrochemicals. With time, they can help revitalize rural communities as farmers are able to produce healthy food with fewer costly inputs. This promotes stability and can provide an alternative to migration or relocation to urban areas.

The harvest will provide low-cost fresh food, and Cereal crops to underserved communities, supporting Poryalma's mission to empower children with essential resources. core_fields.abstract: In Burkina Faso, a developing country plagued by poverty and hunger, many families struggle to provide their children with three safe and nutritious meals a day. This project addresses the critical issue of food insecurity by utilizing 2 hectares of land to produce sustainable, organic food. The innovation lies in integrating agriculture with community support, offering low-cost, nutritious food directly to families in need, especially children. The project benefits from a sustainable farming model that focuses on organic practices, ensuring healthy, environmentally friendly produce. By growing food locally, we reduce dependence on external markets and stabilize food prices, making it accessible to families who would otherwise not afford proper nutrition. Additionally, the project creates economic opportunities within the community, empowering local farmers with agricultural training and access to resources. The scientific insight behind this solution is rooted in agroecology, focusing on environmentally sustainable farming techniques that improve soil health and crop diversity, while also addressing nutrition and food security issues. This approach ensures the production of food that is both nutritious and affordable, benefiting children, families, and the local economy. The immediate consumer benefits include access to affordable, safe, and nutritious food. Long-term benefits for farmers include increased agricultural knowledge and capacity, while the community will experience improved food security and economic resilience. Ultimately, this initiative promotes a healthier, more self-sufficient society, helping to break the cycle of poverty and hunger in Burkina Faso.

core_fields.title: Budigot, From waste to Sustainable food Security
core_fields.description: Budigot. From Waste to Sustainable Food Security. This project is a revolutionary solution in organic and food waste management using BSF maggots. This project not only reduces greenhouse gas emissions, but also produces high-quality protein-rich animal feed and organic fertilizer. With an efficient and sustainable circular economy approach, Budigot supports global food security, strengthens environmental sustainability, and drives greener and more resilient local economies.
core_fields.abstract: Budigot is an innovative solution that processes organic waste, especially food waste, using BSF (Black Soldier Fly) larvae to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. By 2023, FAO recorded that around 1.3 Billion tons of food is wasted every year worldwide, resulting in a loss of USD $990 Billion, contributing to pollution and resource waste. The project addresses this problem by converting food waste into high-protein animal feed and high-quality organic fertilizer that can be used by farmers. The global demand for animal feed and organic fertilizer continues to increase, but many countries are unable to meet the demand. The soaring prices of chemical fertilizers and non-organic animal feed make it difficult for farmers and producers. In addition, the use of chemical fertilizers has a negative impact on soil and ecosystem health, while non-organic feed risks reducing the quality of livestock and human health. Budigot offers a relevant and sustainable solution by utilizing BSF larvae to process food waste into high-value and environmentally friendly products. The circular economy approach implemented ensures efficient waste management and produces affordable, high-quality animal feed and organic fertilizer. In this way, Budigot not only helps reduce waste and greenhouse gas emissions, but also supports global food security and environmental sustainability for communities and future generations.

core_fields.title: Harnessing the Potential of Seaweed As Versatile Packaging Material to Stop Nanoplastic Contamination in Human Body
core_fields.description: We convert seaweed into versatile bio-packaging options, such as edible sachets, cups, and cookie envelopes. Our goals are to address the environmental crisis and mitigate plastic waste pollution by providing sustainable alternatives that safeguard consumers from nanoplastic contamination and ensure convenience. By establishing a new market sector for seaweed and utilizing surplus seaweed, we are also improving the livelihoods of disadvantaged populations in coastal areas, particularly seaweed producers.
core_fields.abstract: Nanoplastic contamination is a growing global concern, with food packaging being one of its largest contributors, alongside plastic utensils, toothbrushes, and clothing. When tea bags, coffee cups, and instant meal containers come into direct contact with hot water, they unintentionally expose consumers to nanoplastics, which they then consume along with their food or drink. Indonesia is the world's largest consumer of microplastics and the fifth-largest plastic waste contributor. We offer four uncompetitive advantages. First, Indonesia ranks as the second-largest seaweed producer globally, with over 80% of its oceanic potential still untapped. Unlike bioplastics from terrestrial crops, Biopac does not contribute to food scarcity or deforestation. Second, we have been pioneers in seaweed-based packaging development since 2010 and established our innovative edge with four patents on flexible packaging and one on seaweed-based tableware. Comprehensive certifications, including compostable, food packaging, and conformity certificates, back our products, ensuring their safety for human consumption and the environment. Third, Biopac eliminates the risk of nanoplastic contamination in food and beverages, ensuring safer daily consumption. Environmentally, Biopac significantly reduces plastic waste pollution while offering fully biodegradable solutions that align with SDGs. For local communities, seaweed cultivation creates jobs and drives sustainable economic growth, especially in coastal areas with untapped marine resources. Fourth, our product price is affordable compared to the total cost of conventional plastic, as reported by WWF. By combining sustainable innovation and eco-conscious practices, we aim to redefine packaging while addressing critical global challenges like microplastic contamination and environmental degradation.

core_fields.title: Empowering Dryland communities through Climate-Resilient Cacti-Farming: Regenerative Farming for food security, Nutrition and Sustainable Livelihoods.
core_fields.description: Dunia Bora leverages the drought-resilient cactus to produce nutrient-dense foods and converts waste generated into organic fertilizer. We convert the prickly-pear opuntia cactus fruit into nutritious juice and jam. The ingredients used in fortification are locally sourced and reduce food waste whereas the waste generated is treated into a Vermi-culture which produces a liquid fertilizer. Through this innovative value addition, we address food system challenges through nature-based solutions while restoring degraded soils and conserving water.
core_fields.abstract: Dunia Bora is addressing the problem of food insecurity and environmental degradation in arid regions by transforming the invasive prickly pear cactus into nutritious juice and jam. This innovation is particularly relevant as many communities face challenges related to drought, malnutrition, and the spread of invasive species that threaten local ecosystems. The prickly pear cactus, which thrives in dry conditions, offers a sustainable solution to these issues. By utilizing this resilient plant, Dunia Bora not only provides a source of nutrition but also helps mitigate the negative impacts of the cactus on local grazing lands. The process involves harvesting the fruit to create juice and jams, which are rich in vitamins and can be marketed both locally and internationally. This approach is rooted in scientific insights about the cactus's nutritional benefits and its capacity to grow in poor soils with minimal water. By focusing on value addition rather than eradication, Dunia Bora promotes a circular economy that benefits local farmers and consumers alike. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition for communities, new economic opportunities for farmers through crop diversification, and reduced reliance on water-intensive crops. Sustainable benefits encompass enhanced food security, environmental restoration by controlling invasive species, and increased resilience against climate change impacts. Overall, Dunia Bora's innovation fosters a more sustainable food system while empowering local communities.

core_fields.title: Circular Economy for Sustainable Food Security Using Ezee DIY Aquaponic System (EDAS)
core_fields.description: The project addresses climate change challenges, such as flooding, by enabling communities in Kedah and Perlis to produce food sustainably in small spaces. EDAS uses a controlled, regenerative aquaponics system that minimizes water use, eliminates chemical fertilizers, and upcycles waste, contributing to planetary health. Through community-wide adoption, the project ensures that local agricultural produce meets or exceeds industrial crop yields, enhancing food security and resilience to climate impacts.
core_fields.abstract: Food insecurity, environmental degradation, and climate change impacts such as flooding are major issues for underserved communities in Kedah and Perlis, Malaysia. Approximately 25% of global food production is lost or wasted annually, worsening food insecurity (FAO, 2019). Climate change is further straining agriculture, with increased flooding and unpredictable weather patterns threatening crop yields. The Ezee DIY Aquaponic System (EDAS) offers a sustainable solution. Aquaponics, which integrates aquaculture and hydroponics, uses up to 90% less water than traditional farming (FAO, 2020), making it ideal for water-scarce and flood-prone areas. The system recycles water and nutrients in a closed-loop, optimizing space and resources. Research shows that aquaponic systems can yield up to 10 times more food per square meter than conventional agriculture (University of Arizona, 2020), enabling high-density food production in small spaces like homes or schools. EDAS also reduces the need for synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, helping protect the environment by lowering chemical runoff and greenhouse gas emissions. Studies show that aquaponics generates fewer greenhouse gases compared to traditional farming (UC Davis, 2018), contributing to environmental sustainability. For communities in Kedah and Perlis, EDAS offers immediate benefits such as increased local food production, improved climate resilience, and reduced environmental impact. It empowers communities to produce their own nutritious food, strengthening food security while promoting sustainable, regenerative farming practices and contributing to planetary health.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Seafood, Resilient Coasts: Harnessing Marine Aquaculture to Empower Mangrove Restoration and Novel Crops
core_fields.description: Pine Island Redfish technology is a blueprint for the future of resilient coastal communities, where ecosystems thrive, people enjoy nutritious, traceable seafood, and communities are strengthened for the future. Our land-based, regenerative aquaculture farm technology is replicable in seaside communities worldwide. We utilize recirculating aquaculture systems to grow redfish, a native fish harvested to the brink of extinction. Our fish nourish more than our community; the waste products are fertilizer, growing mangroves for coastal restoration.
core_fields.abstract: 40% of the world s population lives within 100km of the coast and are facing multiple threats: unpredictable weather, sea level rise, fewer economic opportunities supported by commercial fishing, ecosystem declines and deteriorating ocean water quality. In the South coast of the US, evidence of these threats is everywhere, from high water temperatures fueling the strongest and costliest storm seasons ever recorded to increased algal blooms fueled by agriculture runoff. Yet, people s will to stay, continuing their coastal livelihoods is stronger than ever. Worldwide, coastal migration is increasing at twice that of inland areas. The future is not abandonment of the coast but creating environmental and economic resilience in the face of these challenges - creating diversified economic opportunities that work in harmony with restoration and strengthening of the coastal ecosystems. Pine Island Redfish s regenerative aquaculture solution is based on Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) technology; producing sustainable, traceable, and locally grown marine protein while cultivating nutrient-dense and carbon sequestering plants. Circularity of our technology is unique; it addresses a major challenge for aquaculture saltwater waste mitigation, which is currently capex intensive and operationally complex. Our technology captures nutrient dense waste to be repurposed for carbon-sequestering mangroves and nutrient-dense halophytic vegetables. We are on-course to restore thousands of mangroves equaling hectares of habitat and additional carbon sequestration capacity. The end result reaches beyond this; application of our regenerative practices will become the requisite approach to seafood production, with regionally relevant fish providing healthy protein and fueling restoration of coastal ecosystems.

core_fields.title: Full Circle Hubs for Cassava Processing and Farming
core_fields.description: We want to operationalize of a utility that creates a safe, profitable, and future-proof cassava value chain for smallholder farmers. By integrating renewable energy, advanced agronomy, carbon removal, and digital chain-of-custody innovations, it reduces food loss by 60%, eliminates carcinogenic molds, and doubles selling prices for farmers and processors. It also revitalizes soil health through biochar and unlocks climate financing opportunities.
core_fields.abstract: Cassava farmers in Africa face significant challenges, including limited access to drying infrastructure, difficulty meeting market standards, severe pest and disease pressures, lack of clean seed and improved varieties, inefficient fertilizer use, and increasingly frequent droughts. These interconnected issues contribute to an estimated annual revenue loss of $3 billion across Sub-Saharan Africa, leaving farmers among the world s poorest and most climate-vulnerable populations. Due to the low market price and slim profit margins for cassava, farmers have little means and motivation to invest in proper agronomic practices. Many therefore opt for other crops like maize that are more marketable, which is however also more dependent on synthetic fertiliser and less climate resilient, thus leading to food insecurity. Low-cost greenhouses and hybrid systems with nighttime heating via furnaces have been introduced, but they fail to achieve the drying speed and quality needed to preserve cassava roots effectively. Our solution centers on a clean, decarbonized pyrolysis system that transforms cassava stems and excess biomass into energy for rapid drying. This innovation reduces processing costs, sterilizes diseases, and produces biochar a valuable soil amendment. Biochar supports disease-free plantlet propagation and generates additional income through carbon credit sales. By addressing key bottlenecks and promoting sustainable practices, our approach boosts farmer incomes, enhances resilience, and creates a cost-effective, climate-smart cassava value chain. This integrated model delivers immediate benefits while fostering long-term agricultural and economic sustainability for cassava-growing communities."

core_fields.title: Feeding Our Neighbors
core_fields.description: Plenty! Farm and Foodbank nourishes the community, valuing freshness in food with the goal of providing access to healthy food for all. Located in and serving Floyd Co., VA, Plenty! distributes over 6,000 pounds of food a week via our drive through pantry and year-round home delivery and mobile pantry program. It is imperative that Plenty! find and receive funding to continue its life changing mission and goal of "Feeding Our Neighbors".
core_fields.abstract: During 2023 Plenty! served a record number of Floyd County residents. 2024 have continued to set new records. Plenty! conducted its biannual patron survey in the Fall of 2022 and found that in the past 12 months Floyd County residents were more food insecure than in 2020. Patrons reported the following, 47% reported being Moderately Food Insecure (i.e., skipping meals), more than double the rate in 2020, and 29% reported Severe Food Insecurity (i.e., going a day without eating), nearly double the rate in 2020. Patrons also reported that since coming to Plenty! their experience of food insecurity decreased and they were able to eat a greater variety of foods, (61%), eat more fresh foods and (62%) and do more "From Scratch" cooking. To address these needs Plenty! has pantry hours available three days a week, Monday's 1-4PM, Tuesdays 10AM-1PM and Thursday's 4-6PM. Pantry is set up similar to a drive thru where patrons can select items via menus that are distributed while individuals wait in line. When the patrons reach the pantry, they have the opportunity to step out of the vehicle and shop our outdoor farmers market area and large produce fridge to select fruits and veggies as well as breads and baked goods. Plenty! also offers year-round home deliveries and mobile pantry to families that do not have adequate transportation to come to the pantry.
