core_fields.title: Establishing a Pawpaw Research & Breeding Orchard Network in the USA
core_fields.description: Project Pawpaw will establish its second research orchard at a site in Wisconsin as part of a nationwide network of pawpaw orchards. Each planting will feature rootstocks from a shared seed lot, and will be grafted with all available named cultivars and progeny from elite crosses. These orchards will generate performance data, develop breeding tools, support market development with fruit production, and provide a disease-free scion source for nurseries, advancing pawpaw cultivation and industry growth.
core_fields.abstract: Project Pawpaw addresses the challenges of underutilized perennial tree crops by creating a USA-based network of research orchards to advance breeding and market development for the North American pawpaw (Asimina triloba). Despite their potential as a high-value, climate-resilient crop, pawpaw cultivation faces barriers such as limited improved cultivars, a lack of performance data, slow breeding cycles, and short fruit shelf life. This application seeks funding to establish a second orchard in Wisconsin, featuring replicated plantings of named cultivars and progeny from elite crosses. This orchard will conserve rare varieties, generate performance data, and provide disease-free scion wood for nurseries. It will also supply fruit for market development and strengthen local food systems by reducing reliance on globalized supply chains. Over time, this orchard network will enable the use of advanced genomic tools like Genomic Selection (GS) and Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS), now accessible due to falling genotyping and computing costs. These tools allow us to screen large populations at the seedling stage and make more informed breeding decisions. This approach will accelerate the development of superior cultivars tailored to diverse environments. Pawpaws are not only gaining popularity in the U.S. but are also fueling emerging industries in rural Croatia, Slovenia, France, Italy, and Canada, showcasing their adaptability and market potential. Immediate and lasting benefits include empowering farmers with high-performing cultivars, increasing rural economic opportunities, conserving biodiversity, and promoting regenerative systems that enhance soil health. This orchard will position pawpaws as a climate-smart, equitable, and globally relevant crop.

core_fields.title: Isolation & purification of functional leaf protein "RuBisCO" isolates from agricultural waste leaves
core_fields.description: The project seeks to improve our patent pending lab-scale methods for RuBisCO extraction and purification, aiming to achieve higher yield and purity at pilot scale, thereby clearing the path for commercial scale. Key objectives include optimizing technology for large-scale production including commercial viability and enhancing the nutritional value and environmental sustainability of our RuBisCO isolates. The isolates fill a critical market gap and position Proleri as a leader in innovative, sustainable, plant protein solutions.
core_fields.abstract: Current Plant proteins like Soy, Pea and Wheat have allergens, are incomplete proteins and have significant off notes making it difficult for plant product companies to compete with animal products. For decades, this has led to extensive growth in animal agriculture causing significant environmental damage. Leaf Protein "RuBisCO", often referred to as "Holy Grail of Plant Protein", is allergen free, has all essential amino acids, perfect digestibility and great functional properties. It is a true replacement of animal proteins. And the best part is that it is present in all leaves making it the most abundant protein in the world. At Proleri, we have developed proprietary technology to isolate RuBisCO protein isolates from waste leaves. It represents a significant breakthrough in protein extraction technology. Unlike traditional methods that yield green or brown isolates, this process produces high-purity, white/off white protein isolates ideal for health drinks, protein bars, and other food applications requiring a neutral colour and taste. Our current technology focuses on two methods for extracting RuBisCO protein from plant leaves. The first method uses a combination of coagulation & precipitation to isolate the protein. The second uses homogenization, sieving, centrifugation, depigmentation and dialysis to obtain depigmented and purified RuBisCO protein. Both methods are efficient, scalable, and free of harmful by-products, utilizing agricultural waste from crops like broccoli, cauliflower, sweet potato etc.. The resulting white/off-white RuBisCO isolate functions as a versatile ingredient in plant-based foods, serving as a protein booster or substitute for chemical binding agents or thickeners

core_fields.title: Geospatial Mapping of Soil Microorganisms: Tracking Soil Microbial Biomass In Pursuit of Sustainable Soil and Food production
core_fields.description: The relationship between plant-microbe nutrient exchange is unknown by most food producers, hindering soil regeneration efforts. Microbiomes' invisibility prohibits transitioning to organic practices while retaining profitable yields. MicroBIOMETER's affordable technology enables crop-specific guidance, and predictive modeling for improved agricultural choices. Implementation includes standardizing sampling, upgrading mobile apps, while fostering collaborations. We will deliver a spatially explicit microbial biomass analysis to soil stewards, aiding food producers in vulnerable regions facing economic and climate-related food shortages.
core_fields.abstract: The MicroBIOMETER test kit revolutionizes soil health assessment, offering an accessible method to measure an elusive but key indicator of soil health: microbial biomass carbon(1-2). The brainchild of Dr. Judy Fitzpatrick, this innovative tool has evolved over a decade, enhancing its global reach and precision. The kit addresses soil microbiome health invisibility, which often leads to harmful practices like the overuse of pesticides and chemical fertilizers(3). It allows soil stewards to test the effects of their regenerative practices over time(4-5). This project will introduce groundbreaking integrative, statistical, and spatially explicit results with predicting capabilities to aid food producers and soil stewards. Our global soil microbiome database (>10K entries from over 7,000 customers) and biogeographical and statistical analyses will help food producers link soil health to yield projections on their land. Adding spatial mapping to the soil microbiome will allow us to identify patterns at local-to-landscape scales, which will deliver data-driven decision-making for targeted soil management strategies(6). Our affordable tests allow growers to conduct testing over wide-geographic ranges and across different periods, providing rich datasets for analysis. Improving soil health aligns with the 'One-Health Concept '(7-8), a holistic approach that recognizes the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. This concept posits that better soils lead to better human health and environmental well-being, as healthy soils support carbon accumulation in soils(9) on top of supporting the growth of nutrient-rich crops and reducing the need for chemicals. This project represents a significant leap forward in precision, sustainable agriculture of nutrient-rich food production

core_fields.title: Sustainable Feed Solutions and Regenerative Farming
core_fields.description: Our project focuses on creating sustainable feed solutions and integrating regenerative farming practices to improve food production efficiency. By utilizing innovative upcycling methods for agricultural byproducts and implementing eco-friendly technologies, we aim to reduce waste, enhance soil health, and increase yields. This approach empowers farmers, supports resilient food systems, and provides nutritious, affordable food to communities while protecting the environment.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation introduces sustainable feed solutions and regenerative farming practices to address food insecurity and agricultural inefficiency. Many farmers face challenges like high feed costs, poor soil health, and post-harvest losses, which hinder productivity and sustainability. These issues are particularly relevant in regions where access to affordable, nutritious food is limited, and environmental degradation threatens long-term agricultural viability. We solve these problems by upcycling agricultural byproducts, such as crop residues and animal waste, into high-quality, nutrient-rich animal feed. This reduces dependency on expensive commercial feed while minimizing agricultural waste. Additionally, we implement regenerative practices like organic fertilization, intercropping, and precision irrigation, which enhance soil health, conserve water, and improve yields. This innovation is rooted in insights from circular agriculture, demonstrating that sustainable resource use not only benefits the environment but also lowers costs and boosts productivity for farmers. Life Cycle Assessments reveal that upcycling reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 25% and agricultural waste by 40%, making it both practical and impactful Immediate benefits include lower costs for farmers, increased productivity, and improved food availability. Over time, regenerative practices restore soil fertility, reduce the environmental footprint of farming, and ensure a more resilient food system. These benefits extend to consumers through more affordable and nutritious food, to communities by creating local economic opportunities, and to the environment by promoting sustainability. This comprehensive approach ensures both immediate and long-term impacts on food security and environmental health.

core_fields.abstract: Tajikistan, a low-income country, faces critical agricultural challenges due to its mountainous terrain, with only 7% of arable land available. Rural communities live in difficult socio-economic conditions, relying on traditional farming methods that are insufficient to meet their needs. This scarcity, combined with climate change impacts such as unpredictable weather and resource degradation, exacerbates food insecurity and limits economic opportunities, particularly for women-led households and disadvantaged groups. This project addresses these challenges by introducing a 500-square-meter vertical hydroponic greenhouse as a demonstration and training site. This innovation optimizes land use by growing crops in vertically stacked layers, using 90% less water than traditional methods. Hydroponic systems allow precise control of nutrients and growing conditions, leading to higher yields and better-quality produce year-round. Comprehensive training and capacity-building programs will empower 500 rural beneficiaries with hands-on skills to replicate this solution. Participants will learn greenhouse operations, crop management, and market engagement strategies. The greenhouse serves as a model for sustainable farming, fostering adoption of climate-resilient techniques while creating economic opportunities. Immediate benefits include increased food production and enhanced incomes for beneficiaries. In the long term, this approach builds resilience to climate impacts, improves resource efficiency, and contributes to regional food security. The project aligns with scientific advancements in vertical farming and hydroponics, providing a scalable, practical solution to land scarcity and economic vulnerability in rural Tajikistan.

core_fields.title: Empowering Mothers: Optimizing Breastmilk Storage for Improved Infant Outcomes and Planetary Health
core_fields.description: PumpKin is developing an affordable, sustainable solution using upcycled ingredients to preserve breastmilk and reduce waste. This project will analyze our formulation's impact on breastmilk's composition during household storage. By extending shelf-life and ensuring optimal nutrition, we democratize access to this vital resource, empower mothers globally, minimize spoilage, and promote a healthier planet. Our innovation supports maternal and infant health while addressing climate challenges associated with breastmilk waste and the environmental footprint of formula production.
core_fields.abstract: The World Health Organization recommends infants be exclusively breastfed for the first 6 months of life. Fewer than half of all infants meet this guideline, and 60% of parents fail to accomplish their breastfeeding goals. Many mothers are full-time employed at the time of childbirth and rely on freezer storage to enable continued breastfeeding. However, stored breastmilk loses nutritional value and can become rancid, leading infants to reject it. Challenges with feeding stored milk force parents to switch to formula, which is an imperfect breastmilk substitute and environmentally costly to manufacture. PumpKin's patented solution combines three safe, food-derived ingredients into an easy-to-use liquid concentrate that, when added to pumped breastmilk, extends frozen shelf-life. Our innovation preserves breastmilk nutritional value by reducing >60% of fat breakdown a property associated with rancidity for >6 months of storage. Our primary ingredient is sustainably sourced from citrus peels derived from existing waste streams. Unlike freeze-drying and pasteurization, which are expensive, energy-intensive, and often inadequate to preserve nutritional content, PumpKin's solution provides an affordable and sustainable at-home method for breastmilk preservation. Breastmilk is a scarce resource, yet 75% of US parents report discarding breastmilk. Assuming this waste represents 10% of their supply, over 1 billion ounces are discarded annually. PumpKin's innovation will reduce infant rejection of freezer-stored breastmilk, reduce breastmilk waste, and enable women to participate in the workforce. By lowering reliance on commercial formula, our solution conserves water and energy, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and decreases packaging waste associated with formula production.

core_fields.abstract: In Nigeria, financially vulnerable smallholder fish farmers face critical barriers such as limited technical knowledge, financial constraints, and high upfront costs for adopting innovative technologies. This limits their productivity, profitability, and ability to meet the country s fish demand, which has a gap of 3.6 million metric tons annually. Thriving Aquaculture, powered by Pysis Technologies, addresses these challenges with the Smart Pond, a groundbreaking AI-driven fish farming co-pilot. This solution combines extension outreach and training programs to equip farmers with the technical skills needed for precision fish farming. Additionally, we provide 400 Smart Pond units at subsidized rates and offer flexible, 12-month installment payment plans. Continuous technical support ensures sustained success. The innovation leverages AI insights to optimize water quality, feeding, and fish growth, thereby reducing operational costs by 39% and increasing profitability by 32%. Smallholder farmers gain immediate benefits, such as increased productivity and reduced costs, while enjoying long-term sustainability by scaling their operations. Communities and society at large benefit from improved local fish production, adding 10,850 metric tons of high-quality exportable traceable fish over two years. This helps bridge the fish demand gap, enhances food security, and creates employment opportunities. Environmentally, the Smart Pond promotes resource efficiency, reducing waste and encouraging sustainable aquaculture practices. This holistic approach fosters equitable access to innovation, empowering farmers to thrive while contributing to a sustainable food system.

core_fields.title: Empowering Tanzania s Cashew Farmers Through Sustainable Processing and Global Market Integration
core_fields.description: Our project transforms Tanzania s cashew industry by creating a decentralized, farmer-centric processing ecosystem. Currently supporting 2,000 smallholder farmers, the initiative increases farmer incomes by 40%, reduces post-harvest losses by 25%, and ensures access to global premium markets. By integrating sustainable practices, including zero-waste processing and regenerative agriculture, the project aligns with global food security goals. With a scalable model, we aim to empower 50,000 farmers, create thousands of jobs across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Tanzania, the fourth-largest cashew producer in Africa, faces significant barriers in realizing the full value of its industry. Over 95% of cashews are exported raw, resulting in an estimated $200 million annual loss in potential revenue. This dependency on raw exports limits value addition, job creation, and economic empowerment, particularly in rural communities where cashew farming is a primary livelihood. Smallholder farmers face low incomes, supply chain inefficiencies, and market access challenges, while the environment suffers from unsustainable farming practices and waste mismanagement. Our innovation addresses these challenges through a decentralized, farmer-centric processing ecosystem. By establishing six rural primary processing centers and a central processing facility, we integrate smallholder farmers into the value chain, ensuring immediate cash payments, reduced post-harvest losses, and improved quality control. Cutting-edge technology enables zero-waste processing, converting byproducts into Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) and organic fertilizers, promoting environmental sustainability. Scientific and technical insights drive our approach, leveraging regenerative agriculture and advanced processing techniques to optimize efficiency and quality. Immediate benefits include a 40% increase in farmer incomes, a 25% reduction in post-harvest losses, and the creation of 2,500 jobs, 95% of which are for women. Sustainable outcomes include enhanced food security, reduced environmental footprints, and economic empowerment for rural communities. This scalable model aligns with global food security and sustainability goals, transforming Tanzania s cashew industry into a driver of inclusive growth and environmental stewardship.

core_fields.abstract: Rahsa Nusantara addresses Indonesia s pressing stunting problem, which affects 30.8% of children under five, by introducing a plant-based innovation using Moringa leaves. Despite being abundant in East Nusa Tenggara area, Moringa remains underutilized. Known for its high content of vitamins, minerals, and protein, Moringa offers an effective natural solution to combat stunting and improve maternal and child health. The project partners with women and young women in Rote Ndao to develop Moringa-based supplements that boost maternal nutrition, particularly during pregnancy. Rahsa Nusantara provides training, tools, and equipment to empower these women to process Moringa leaves into versatile raw materials and supplements. This initiative not only addresses stunting but also creates economic opportunities, diversifies the local economy, and strengthens community resilience. Scientific insights into Moringa s nutrient richness led to this solution, combined with the use of solar drying technology for efficient, eco-friendly processing. The immediate benefits include better health outcomes for pregnant women and their children, increased income for women and local farmers, and greater nutrition awareness. The sustainable impacts are equally significant, including reduced healthcare costs, a stronger local economy, and a more resilient food system. By focusing on empowering women and leveraging local resources, Rahsa Nusantara s project addresses stunting, improves maternal health, and help to develop economic and environmental sustainability. This holistic approach ensures the innovation delivers measurable benefits to families, communities, and the broader society, creating a healthier and more equitable future.

core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses two major challenges: the environmental damage from agricultural waste burning and excessive use of chemical fertilisers, which degrade soil and pollute ecosystems. Farmers often resort to open burning, releasing harmful emissions, and rely on chemical fertilisers due to lack of alternatives, causing long-term soil harm and water contamination. We transform agricultural waste into biochar, a carbon-rich soil enhancer, through a sustainable and decentralised production model. Our proprietary digital platform app ensures transparency and is fully automated, enabling farmers even those with low literacy to produce biochar with ease. By tracking every step, the app simplifies access to carbon credit markets, providing farmers with additional income streams and huge upfront CAPEX. We also conduct on-site trainings to train farmers to produce Biochar sustainably without any adverse effects to the environment. Biochar improves soil health by reducing acidity, retaining moisture, and enhancing nutrient availability, reducing dependence on chemical fertilisers. This not only supports better crop yields but also restores degraded lands, contributing to long-term agricultural sustainability. The scientific process of pyrolysis underpins this solution, locking carbon in biochar for centuries while preventing emissions from waste burning. Immediate benefits include reduced air pollution, healthier soil, and an accessible income boost for farmers. In the long term, it supports communities and the environment by fostering a circular economy, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and mitigating climate change. core_fields.title: Regenerative agriculture for a planetary health: Community supported agriculture in Colombia
core_fields.description: Our project seeks to expand agroecology and regenerative agriculture in Colombia through the growth CSA Colombian Network with new communities of farmers and consumers, that join the exchange model that guarantees fair incomes, diversified organic foods, creates seed guardians of adapted crops to climate conditions and additionally we ll implement an educational strategy to highlight the benefits of the CSA model in society, biodiversity and the planet.
core_fields.abstract: Despite Colombia's extraordinary biodiversity and agricultural potential, food insecurity persists, affecting around 30% of the population. Violence, inequality, and the degradation of natural resources further deepen this crisis. In response, the CSA (Community-Supported Agriculture) Colombian Network emerged as a collective of farmers and urban families. Its purpose: to empower small-scale farmers by transitioning from conventional agriculture to sustainable, agroecological practices. The CSA model stands out as an innovative economic framework and a practical option for small farmers to commercialize their production while fostering direct connections with consumers. By bridging urban and rural communities, the network has redefined food sovereignty and created a pathway for farmers to earn 50% more than the national minimum wage, ensuring financial stability in vulnerable rural economies because they sell at a fair price their product and avoids food waste. This approach goes beyond economics. Today, 14 active CSAs serve over 400 families, promoting agroecological knowledge-sharing through workshops on biodiversity, soil regeneration, and sustainable practices tailored to local contexts. A cornerstone of the model is the conservation of native seed guardians of agrobiodiversity and key to achieving true food sovereignty, responding to climate change and the biodiversity crisis. Moreover, the network has catalyzed the empowerment of women and youth by providing training in project management, decision-making, and technology use. It emphasizes sustainability not only in farming practices but also in the relationships it nurtures between growers and consumers.

core_fields.title: Diamond Matrix Bioconversion: Revolutionizing Farming with Sustainable Crop Solutions
core_fields.description: Our project transforms organic materials, including sargassum seaweed and tithonia, into innovative sustainable crop inputs like biostimulants, fertilizers and composts. These solutions significantly enhance soil biodiversity, nutrient cycling, and health, while boosting crop yields and reducing reliance on synthetic chemicals. By leveraging natural resources, we provide chemical-free, cost-effective, eco-friendly inputs that support regenerative agriculture, improve food security, and address environmental challenges, revolutionizing farming practices for a sustainable and resilient food system.
core_fields.abstract: For over five decades, the agrochemical industry has relied heavily on synthetic, fossil fuel-derived products such as fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides. These chemicals have failed to meet expectations, causing significant environmental damage and deteriorating soil health across regions like Barbados and the Caribbean. The widespread use of these products has led to nutrient-depleted soils, polluted ecosystems, and harmful impacts on public health, including rising chronic diseases due to poor-quality food. In response to this crisis, I founded Red Diamond Compost with a mission to provide sustainable, organic alternatives to toxic agrochemicals. Our key innovation is the Diamond Matrix Bioconversion (DMB) system, transforming organic materials including invasive plant species and compost crops like sargassum seaweed and tithonia into high-quality, sustainable crop inputs. By harnessing natural processes, our products support the growth of beneficial soil microbes, improve soil structure, and promote nutrient cycling. This results in healthier, more fertile soils, enhanced water retention, and improved crop yields without the harmful effects of synthetic chemicals. Our solutions benefit a wide range of end users, including home gardeners, farmers, landscapers, and communities seeking to improve food security and environmental sustainability. Through our innovative approach, we empower consumers with access to clean, nutritious food, while supporting regenerative farming practices that restore and protect ecosystems. This work is deeply personal to me as I ve seen firsthand the damage caused by conventional agricultural practices, having to overcome by own health crisis and the potential of organic solutions to drive positive change for both people and the planet.

core_fields.abstract: Regasis is an innovative solution designed to address the challenge of regulatory compliance for food manufacturers in Africa. Food businesses, particularly small to medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), often struggle to keep up with the constantly changing regulations across various African countries. This complexity consumes time and resources, while non-compliance can lead to costly fines, legal issues and wastage in production. Regasis solves this problem by offering a user-friendly digital platform that eases the compliance process. The platform integrates with national regulatory data, tracks in national legislation, and provides real-time updates on regulatory changes, ensuring that food manufacturers are always compliant. It features intuitive tools, automated reminders for audits and certifications, and country-specific guidance tailored to each food product. The scientific and technical insight behind Regasis is its ability to streamline regulatory management through automation and data integration, minimizing human error and manual tracking. By leveraging technology, the platform significantly reduces the compliance burden. Immediate benefits include time savings, risk reduction, and cost savings for manufacturers. Sustainable benefits include enhanced food safety standards, improved industry transparency, and greater confidence in local food supply chains. For end users, including consumers and communities, this means safer food products, better consumer protection, and a more efficient food production system. Regasis fosters growth in the food industry while supporting the regulatory frameworks that ensure public health and safety.

core_fields.title: RemAI: Empowering households to make data-driven decisions to reduce household food waste
core_fields.description: The IFT Seed Award would be used to develop and scale Remy s own advance AI agent: RemAI. The aim of the RemAI is to enhance Remy s mobile application to further increase the user experience through AI, thus, maximising the impact, usability and savings Remy can produce for its users. The project will last 10 months and will have a total cost of $131,000, encompassing the research, development and implementation phases of RemAI.
core_fields.abstract: Household food waste is the leading driver of waste along the food supply chain, causing around 65% of the total generated waste. At a global level, food waste would be the third-largest emitter of GHG if it were a country, only following China and the USA. European avoidable household food waste causes approximately 73Mt CO2e and costs households 170bn annually. Food waste reduction is the second-biggest impact households can make to fight climate change, yet there is no viable, comprehensive and usable digital solution; Remy wants to change this. Remy is Europe s first automated, AI-driven household kitchen management application that helps users know what ingredients they have at home, when it s going to expire, how they can incorporate them into their meals and lets them buy anything that s missing directly from their smartphones. In doing so, Remy saves households 2000, 100+ hours and 3000kg CO2e per year and can reduce 25.6Mt CO2e per year at scale by ensuring they only buy what they need and cook what they buy before it expires. Through the app, Remy can collect novel user emissions and behaviour data, which can be leveraged by retail partners to satisfy upcoming scope 3 reporting regulations and build data-driven waste prevention strategies. Unlike prior attempts, Remy works because the commercialisation of AI and the change in reporting regulations for retailers make the proposition seamless for end users while providing leverage to scale cost-effectively through large retailers.

core_fields.title: Mixed Bean Tempeh: A Local Solution for Global Food Sustainability
core_fields.description: This initiative promotes mixed bean tempeh using jack beans and soybeans as a sustainable alternative to reduce Indonesia's reliance on imported soybeans (90% sourced from Argentina, the U.S., and Brazil). Incorporating jack beans supports local farmers through fair trade, improves livelihoods, and enhances soil health via regenerative and organic farming practices. This approach strengthens food security and builds a resilient, eco-friendly, and inclusive agricultural ecosystem.
core_fields.abstract: Indonesia relies heavily on soybean imports, with 90% of its 2.2 million tons consumed in 2023 sourced from the U.S., Argentina, and Brazil. This dependency creates economic vulnerabilities, environmental degradation, and high greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The intensive soybean production in exporting countries often leads to deforestation, soil degradation, and unsustainable farming practices. Additionally, transporting soybeans across continents generates significant carbon emissions, contributing to climate change and undermining efforts for sustainable food production. Our initiative addresses these challenges by introducing mixed bean tempeh, combining jack beans with soybeans as a sustainable alternative. Jack beans have a nutrient profile comparable to soybeans, making them a suitable ingredient for tempeh production. Consumer tests have shown the taste of mixed bean tempeh to be well-accepted, ensuring market viability. Jack beans are nitrogen-fixing legumes that naturally enhance soil fertility, reducing reliance on synthetic fertilizers and their associated emissions. By cultivating jack beans through regenerative and organic farming systems, we empower local farmers with sustainable practices that improve soil health, reduce input costs, and diversify their income sources. This solution strengthens food security while offering consumers a nutritious, locally produced alternative to conventional tempeh. Reducing reliance on imported soybeans lowers carbon footprints and supports a transition to a resilient, self-sufficient food system. Our initiative mitigates the environmental impact of imports, improves farmer livelihoods, and promotes sustainable, health-focused food, aligning with global goals to combat climate change and enhance community well-being.

core_fields.title: Shifting from wet to dry granulated organic wastes composting with incentives to farmers for behavioral change toward compost application
core_fields.description: Our project is bringing new approach to transform organic waste into granulated compost through EM-tech innovative, climate-smart practices that reduce landfill pressure from waste accumulation. Wastes are recycled into eco-friendly agro-inputs to promote natural-based crop nutrients and soil organic matter (SOM). The project aims at changing farmers distrust of organic wastes generated from waste by considering them garbage. This means from wet to dry and granulated compost similar to chemical fertilizer.
core_fields.abstract: Organic wastes generated from domestic and urban public landfills may cause to 25% of GHGs emission. IPCC 6 assessment report shows that around 2.01 billion tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) are annually produced. According to Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA) 2023 reports, estimated 1,800 2,000 tons of wastes are produced per day. Of which more than 70% are organic and 50% of them are of good quality for compost use. However, only 2% of these organic wastes are managed and recycled. In combination with very high unemployment statistics from National Statistics of Rwanda (NISR report, 2022), of which Youth unemployment account 20.5% where females represent 19.8% of the total, Rwanda Government and partners have made a lot of efforts to attracted SMSs-SMEs in recycling of organic wastes to agro-inputs. However, despite the efforts made, SMSs-SMEs invested in waste recycling has failed due to high number of farmers distrust of waste compost due to its wet-form, which makes farmers consider it as lifetime garbage. After our 2022 preliminary discussions with 120 farmers, about 100% of them have mentioned that wet form of compost are always looking like garbage. And suggested that if is dried and transformed to look or mimic chemical fertilizer, farmers are willing to change and adopt new product. In this context, our project aims at shifting from wet to granulated organic waste composting with certain incentives to farmers for behavioral change toward compost and awareness on its adoption as new locally made agro-input.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Sustainable Cassava and Maize Production for Improved Food Security and Nutrition in Tanzania
core_fields.description: This project focuses on enhancing sustainable cassava and maize production in Tanzania to improve food security, nutrition, and livelihoods. It will implement regenerative agricultural practices, reduce food waste, and promote nutritious, affordable food. Empowering local communities and refugees in Kigoma, the project aims to ensure equitable access to safe, nutritious food, contributing to environmental sustainability and improving the well-being of over 100,000 individuals.
core_fields.abstract: In Kigoma region, Tanzania, food insecurity and malnutrition are significant challenges, particularly in rural areas, refugee camps, and host communities. Limited access to nutritious, affordable food, compounded by unsustainable agricultural practices, exacerbates these issues. The lack of proper post-harvest management techniques leads to high food waste, further reducing food availability. Our project tackles these challenges by enhancing sustainable cassava and maize production through regenerative agricultural practices. This includes improved crop management, efficient resource utilization, and the reduction of food waste. By incorporating innovative post-harvest techniques and promoting nutrient-rich, affordable food, the project ensures that vulnerable populations have access to safe and nutritious food. It also focuses on empowering local farmers and refugees through education and capacity-building, enabling them to adopt sustainable farming practices that increase productivity while preserving the environment. The scientific and technical insights underpinning this solution stem from agroecology and regenerative agriculture, which emphasize soil health, water conservation, and minimizing the environmental footprint of food production. These practices are projected to increase crop yields by 2,000 tons annually, reduce reliance on chemical inputs, and mitigate the impact of climate change on agriculture. Immediate and Sustainable Benefits: Consumers will have access to healthier, more affordable food. Farmers will experience improved livelihoods through increased productivity (an additional 2,000 tons annually) and better income opportunities. The environment will benefit from reduced agricultural waste and more sustainable land use, saving up to 30 million liters of water annually. Communities will see enhanced food security, reduced malnutrition, and stronger local economies.

core_fields.title: "Bridging the Climate Gap: Solar Solutions for Resilient Farming"
core_fields.description: Our project, "Bridging the Climate Gap," empowers smallholder farmers to adapt to climate change by providing affordable PAYGO solar irrigation systems and community agricultural solar hubs. These hubs offer rentable Solar Irrigation energy needs, with payments aligned to crop harvest cycles. By improving access to sustainable energy and water solutions, we enhance agricultural productivity, reduce environmental impact, and build climate resilience in rural farming communities.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation, "Bridging the Climate Gap," addresses the critical challenge of climate change adaptation for smallholder farmers by providing sustainable, affordable energy and irrigation solutions. Many farmers lack access to reliable irrigation and energy, resulting in low productivity, vulnerability to erratic weather patterns, and increased dependence on unsustainable practices like fossil fuels and over-extraction of groundwater. We solve this problem through two key solutions: PAYGO Solar Irrigation Systems Affordable, pay-as-you-go solar-powered irrigation tailored to farmers' income cycles, ensuring year-round crop production. Community Agricultural Solar Hubs Centralized hubs offering Solar solutions for rent, enabling farmers to power tools, equipment, and processing activities. Farmers pay for these services after their harvests, aligning costs with their income flow. This solution is based on insights into smallholder farmers' challenges with upfront costs for renewable energy systems, access to irrigation, and energy storage. Advances in solar technology, battery efficiency, and PAYGO financing models make this approach both feasible and scalable. Benefits: Immediate: Farmers access affordable energy and irrigation, increasing yields and incomes. Sustainable: Reduced reliance on fossil fuels, enhanced climate resilience, and improved food security. Social: Empowered communities with better livelihoods and more equitable access to technology. Environmental: Promotion of renewable energy and water conservation, reducing carbon footprints. This project not only improves farmers productivity but also fosters environmental stewardship and community resilience, creating long-term impacts on society and the planet.

core_fields.title: Optimization, purification and processing of a precision fermentation derived protein based natural sweetener Brazzein.
core_fields.description: Biofect Innovations is revolutionizing the food industry by harnessing the power of microbial precision fermentation technology to produce sustainable, high-value ingredients; starting with Brazzein, a natural, high-intensity sweetener. In order to be adopted by the larger food & beverage industry, it must first be presented in a widely adaptable format such as a powder where it can be easily adapted to various product formulations such as cereals, beverages, and gummies.
core_fields.abstract: The evolving landscape in dietary habits has consumers closely focusing on packaging labels and ingredients in food and beverages. As a staple ingredient, sugar is the most commonly scrutinized as consumers seek healthier alternatives to reduce the risk of future health complications. This demand has resulted in manufacturers and distributors to search for new sweetener alternatives like sucralose, aspartame, and erythritol. However, these non-caloric sweeteners are not satisfying consumer demands due to recently uncovered health risks associated with consumption. Brazzein is a potent, natural, and emerging protein-based alternative sweetener that was originally discovered in the West African fruit of Oubli Pentadiplandra brazzeana). Brazzein is reported to be up to 2000x sweeter than sugar (w/w), providing a superior alternative without compromising on taste and health profile. Attempts have been made to commercialize this ingredient using traditional agricultural techniques but have largely remained unsuccessful due to the demanding climate requirements combined with the difficult purification processes involved resulting in a non-existent global supply. Precision fermentation technology differs from traditional fermentation because microbes are engineered to facilitate the conversion of carbon (i.e., sugar) to a specific product (i.e., protein) instead of alcohol. Leveraging this technology allows for sustainable production of ingredients that uses less water, carbon emissions, and land usage compared to traditional agriculture. The immediate benefits to end users is the availability of a novel ingredient that has the potential to reduce the usage of sugar while still maintaining similar sweetness potentials in the food and beverage products we consume.

core_fields.title: IRIF: Intelligence, Resilience, and Innovative Farming For Africa
core_fields.description: IRIF, an AI-powered platform, is revolutionizing African agriculture by empowering smallholder farmers to adapt to climate change and thrive. Combining real-time data, personalized recommendations delivered via SMS, and market access, IRIF demonstrably increases yields, conserves precious resources, and boosts farmer incomes. IRIF's innovative "pay-on-harvest" model ensures affordability and widespread accessibility, creating a truly sustainable and equitable food system, starting in Ethiopia and poised to impact millions.
core_fields.abstract: Climate change is devastating African agriculture, impacting millions of smallholder farmers the foundation of the continent s food security. Erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts, and emerging pests and diseases are causing significant crop losses and reduced incomes, exacerbating poverty and hindering economic advancement, especially among young people. Projections paint a grim picture: agricultural productivity could decline by up to 30% in some regions by 2050, and water stress threatens up to 250 million Africans by 2025. In Ethiopia alone, over 90% of farmers are already affected, battling erratic rainfall and devastating crop losses. These challenges hinder access to nutritious food and sustainable practices, impacting the health of both people and the planet. These challenges are compounded by limited access to modern technologies, climate-smart information, and profitable markets. IRIF (Intelligence, Resilience, Innovative Farming), our AI-powered platform, is transforming this challenge into an opportunity. By combining real-time data, personalized recommendations, and market access, IRIF empowers farmers to adapt to climate change and build a more equitable and regenerative food system. On-farm sensors, satellite imagery, and AI generate tailored advice, optimizing irrigation, predicting pest outbreaks, and guiding crop selection, ultimately increasing yields and incomes. Direct market connections ensure fair prices and build trust with consumers seeking sustainable, locally-sourced food. Our "pay-on-harvest" model makes IRIF accessible and affordable, ensuring widespread adoption and maximizing our impact on nutrition, sustainability, and accessibility within the food system. IRIF is not just adapting to the future of food; it is the future of food, starting in Ethiopia.

core_fields.title: Bloom Network

core_fields.abstract: Local food systems lack effective mechanisms to scale successful sustainability initiatives, preventing widespread adoption of proven practices that could transform our food system. While individual communities have developed powerful solutions, their innovations often remain isolated, limiting their transformative potential for global food security and environmental challenges. Bloom Network's innovation combines two powerful elements: our Local Love campaign and our digital platform (bloomnetwork.earth). The Local Love campaign activates communities through hands-on food system engagement - from farm tours to cooking classes to harvest festivals. Our social networking platform then captures these successful initiatives, providing tools for documentation, replication, and scaling. Through blockchain technology, we efficiently distribute grant rewards to participants, creating financial incentives for food system transformation. Building upon the success of our existing 30 Local Bloom hubs across every continent, this integrated approach delivers specific, measurable benefits: - Farmers gain expanded market access and increased revenue through direct community connections - Consumers receive easier access to healthy, local food and practical knowledge for sustainable living - Schools access proven curriculum for food system education - Communities build stronger local economies through enhanced food system infrastructure - Producers connect with peer support and proven growth strategies - Society benefits from more resilient regional food systems - Environmental impact scales through widespread adoption of regenerative practices By bridging the gap between local innovation and global implementation, we're creating lasting transformation in how communities feed themselves.

core_fields.title: HFSL-Africa: Healthier Foods and Sustainable Livelihoods Africa
core_fields.description: HFSL-Africa s mission is to ensure Diverse, Safe, Nutritious, and Affordable foods for the urban poor communities. The project is applying innovative production techniques to set up aquaponics and urban gardens such as vertical gardens in Kisumu city. This initiative enables women and youth to grow vegetables and fish for home consumption and surplus sales, improving dietary diversity and economic opportunities. Complemented by nutrition education, the project empowers communities to adopt healthier diets and sustainable livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: In Kisumu,a Kenyan port city on Lake Victoria, low-income residents face limited access to nutritious foods, resulting in poor diet quality. This is a serious problem not just for the health and wellbeing of individuals especially among women and children, but also carries detrimental social, economic and environmental consequences. Overcoming these challenges and achieving Zero Hunger (UN Sustainable Development Goal 2) requires a multi-sectoral approach. This is exemplified by the Healthier Foods and Sustainable Livelihoods Africa (HFSL-Africa). The project is applying innovative production techniques to set up urban gardens and aquaponics. In urban gardens, women and youth produce vegetables primarily for home consumption, and sell to neighbors and other consumers when there is a surplus. These gardens provide access to nutritious produce that is often too expensive for low-income households to purchase and consume on a regular basis. Likewise, aquaponics increase access to fish and vegetables for home consumption and for additional sales. Nutrition education further increases consumer awareness on what they need to eat to attain a healthy diet, and why this is important. Scientific insight behind this solution is rooted in urban agriculture's potential to combat food insecurity and improve nutrition, alongside sustainable agricultural practices like integrated pest management and efficient water use. Aquaponics and urban garden systems are particularly valuable in urban areas with limited land and water resources. The project's immediate benefits include improved access to fresh, affordable, and nutritious foods, enhanced dietary diversity, and increased economic opportunities through surplus sales for the Kisumu urban community.

core_fields.title: Harvesting Food Security: Redefining Food Systems with Climate-Resilient Aeroponic Agriculture
core_fields.description: Boundless Haven revolutionizes agriculture through an innovative aeroponic system that maximizes nutritious food production while drastically reducing water and input consumption. Our technology combines cutting-edge equipment with eco-friendly, plant-based agricultural inputs to ensure optimal productivity. This accessible solution strengthens local food security while contributing to sustainable agricultural practices, addressing the urgent challenges of climate change and resource scarcity.
core_fields.abstract: East African agriculture, particularly in Djibouti, faces a critical food security crisis due to insufficient local production, depleted soils, and extreme climate conditions. This has led to heavy dependence on expensive, poor-quality food imports, straining communities with limited purchasing power. Traditional farming methods compound these challenges through excessive water consumption and harmful chemical usage, degrading the environment and endangering public health. Recognizing that conventional solutions couldn't adequately address these interconnected challenges, we turned to NASA's aeroponic technology a soilless cultivation system originally designed for space stations. We've revolutionized this technology by developing a unique system that integrates nanotechnology-based nutrients with smart automation in fully controlled environments. This scientific breakthrough enables precise control of growing conditions while minimizing resource usage, making it ideal for arid regions. Our performance metrics demonstrate unprecedented efficiency: tomato yields reach 7.7 harvests annually (compared to 1.5 in traditional farming and 3 in hydroponics), while reducing water usage by 95% and fertilizer costs by 80%. The system's adaptability to all crop varieties ensures year-round production of diverse, nutritious foods. The World Bank has recognized this potential, financing our pilot project in Djibouti. The successful pilot demonstrated the effectiveness of our system in extreme climate conditions, proving our technology's viability. Once implemented at scale, this solution will provide immediate and lasting benefits: healthy and affordable food for consumers, reduced costs and increased yields for producers, decreased dependence on imports, and environmental protection. This sustainable approach transforms local agriculture from a challenge into an opportunity for resilient, climate-adapted food production.

core_fields.title: Fermentation-Powered Microalgae: Advancing Affordable and Sustainable Protein Solutions
core_fields.description: Brevel s innovative technology combines sugar-based fermentation with light to create a paradigm shift in microalgae protein production. This mixotrophic process delivers unmatched efficiency, scalability, and sustainability by leveraging the strengths of both photosynthesis and fermentation. By optimizing extraction methods, Brevel produces multiple high-value fractions, including proteins, oils, and pigments, at significantly reduced costs. This breakthrough addresses critical barriers in alternative protein production, setting new standards for sustainable and scalable food innovation.
core_fields.abstract: Brevel s innovative mixotrophic technology addresses the urgent need for sustainable, scalable protein solutions. Traditional protein sources like meat and soy require extensive resources, contributing to deforestation, greenhouse gas emissions, and biodiversity loss. For example, producing one ton of microalgae protein emits only 0.9 tons of CO₂ and uses 25 tons of water, compared to soy s 9 tons of CO₂ and 170 tons of water per ton of protein. Brevel s unique process combines sugar-based fermentation with light, merging the efficiency of fermentation and the sustainability of photosynthesis. This enables cost-efficient production of high-quality microalgae proteins and co-products like oils and pigments, maximizing both economic and environmental value. Brevel achieves cost parity with pea and soy protein (as low as $3 5/kg) while delivering a neutral taste, full amino acid profile, and allergen-free functionality. The benefits are immediate and impactful. For consumers, Brevel enables better-tasting, healthier plant-based foods. Producers gain access to a versatile, affordable ingredient that aligns with sustainability demands. Schools, communities, and regions facing food insecurity benefit from nutritious, eco-friendly options. At scale, Brevel's innovation supports reduced deforestation, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and improved biodiversity, advancing a sustainable global food system.

Our solution integrates advanced beekeeping techniques with community training, especially targeting women, to build their capacities as skilled apiarists. By deploying precision-engineered beehives and leveraging AI-powered tools for hive health monitoring and pollination optimization, the project ensures sustainable, scalable impacts. Scientific insights into the symbiotic relationship between bees, crops, and ecosystems underpin this solution, offering a nature-based approach to improve livelihoods and ecological balance. Long-term, the project enhances biodiversity by preserving bee populations and promotes climate resilience by fostering pollinator-dependent ecosystems. By bridging science, technology, and community empowerment, POLLINATE transforms rural economies while contributing to global goals for sustainable agriculture, biodiversity preservation, and gender equity. This innovative approach ensures a win-win for farmers, communities, and the environment, creating a ripple effect of positive socio-economic and ecological change.

core_fields.title: Digital Traceability for Safe, Transparent, and Trusted Food Supply chain in Africa.
core_fields.description: JANI AI is a cloud platform that offers end-to-end digital traceability of the food supply chain from farm to fork in Africa. JANI provides real-time supply chain mapping, ensuring transparency, quality assurance, and compliance. Our platform offers Farm Mapping, Farmer Management, and Inventory Management software. We target off-takers, exporters, food processors, and farmer cooperatives in the farming industry. JANI AI transforms how data in food systems is collected, managed, and utilized.
core_fields.abstract: Kenya generated $3 billion from tea, coffee, and horticulture exports in 2023. However, nearly 60% of food produced in the region cannot be traced due to fragmented supply chains and inadequate data collection systems. Traceability methods used by exporters in Kenya are predominantly manual, relying on reverse traceability by paper-based systems and Excel sheets are outdated, inefficient, and prone to errors. With the implementation of new EUDR and FDA regulations around food traceability, many exporters and cooperatives who source their produce from small-scale farmers struggle to meet these standards. JANI is designed to collect Key Data Elements (KDEs) including data on inputs, storage, and harvest dates. JANI monitors critical tracking events throughout the farming process, from production to aggregation, providing a clear activity timeline. Our Farm Mapping Software allows for precise geolocation of farms, capturing GPS points and polygon data for land use verification. Our Farmer Management System assigns unique identifiers and lot numbers to products and producers, ensuring traceability and transparency in the supply chain. Our Inventory Management Software optimizes produce collection and aggregation by consolidating produce into larger batches. The supply chain mapping data helps producers and exporters generate Due Diligence assessments that meet regulatory requirements. JANI supports critical agricultural value chains in East Africa, including tea, coffee, nuts, and horticulture (fruits and vegetables). We empower farmers, cooperatives, and exporters to meet global standards and build consumer trust. JANI provides real-time supply chain mapping, offering a comprehensive view of the movement of goods from production to market.

core_fields.title: Farm to Market Program
core_fields.description: The Farm to Market program aims to train 2000 farmers on using digital tools to sell their products easily, reducing waste that is estimated at 15% of the total produce. This project will train farmers and sensitize civil society and policymakers via the publication of a report to educate and sensitize policy makers and civil society actors. This will reduce waste and ensure greater financial inclusion and access to food for citizens
core_fields.abstract: The Farm to Market program addresses significant barriers faced by smallholder farmers in accessing markets and selling their products efficiently. By training 2,000 farmers to utilize digital tools, such as mobile applications designed for market access, the initiative aims to reduce waste and enhance financial inclusion, particularly in remote areas. Problem and Relevance: Smallholder farmers often struggle with limited market access, resulting in high levels of food waste and economic exclusion. This issue is particularly relevant as it affects food security and livelihoods in vulnerable communities.Solution: The program will implement digital platforms that connect farmers directly with buyers, thereby bypassing intermediaries. These platforms offer essential services such as market pricing information, agricultural advice, and logistics support, empowering farmers to make informed decisions about their produce. Scientific and Technical Insights: The development of these digital tools is informed by research indicating that localized solutions tailored to farmers' specific needs can significantly enhance adoption rates. For instance, tools that provide offline capabilities and are designed with local languages and cultural contexts in mind have proven effective in increasing usage among smallholders. Benefits: The immediate benefits include increased income for farmers through better market access and reduced post-harvest losses. Sustainable advantages encompass improved food security for communities, enhanced economic resilience, and greater participation of marginalized groups, such as women and youth, in agricultural systems Ultimately, the program fosters a more inclusive agricultural ecosystem that benefits society and the environment by reducing waste and creating long-term opportunities for financially excluded farmers.

Designed as an affordable aftermarket addition to food storage locations, this visual inventory helps busy individuals and families reduce food spoilage, follow healthy diets, and source local produce.

core_fields.title: Supply of clean CO2 from the air directly to indoor farms with innovative S DAC systems
core_fields.description: Our project focuses on developing modular Solar Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology for on-site CO2 utilization in greenhouses. This innovation aims to utilise the power of solar heat energy to capture CO2 from the air and directly supply it to greenhouses, enhancing plant growth and productivity while reducing carbon footprints. Key goals include finalisation of the designs and creation of the full-scale 10t DAC system, that would be ready for pilot implementations.
core_fields.abstract: Farmers need CO2 to promote their plants' growth. But the CO2 they use now is neither sustianable, nor affordable. Direct Air Capture offers amazing alternative with the CO2 from the air, but not all DAC companies can match the demand cost-wise. Direct Air Capture faced criticism for its high energy demands, operational costs and therefore minimal environmental impact. Carbominer's novel S-DAC innovation addresses the high energy requirements of traditional DAC technologies, making it more attractive for communities worldwide from both economic and environmental perspectives. Solar DAC (Direct Air Capture) harnesses the power of sunlight to significantly reduce the system's energy dependency from the conventional power sources. By utilizing solar heat to meet most of the system's needs, Solar DAC is particularly suited for warm, sunny regions, turning abundant solar geographies into a valuable tool for Direct air Capture. Potential benefits include cost savings for communities, particularly in solar-rich regions, as they can redirect energy to other critical needs. Farmers, for example, can lower operational costs, increasing profit margins while reducing their emissions.

core_fields.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as Farmers' Smarter Management Tools for Climate Smart Agriculture to Attain Sustainable Food Security.
core_fields.description: The project envisions Artificial Intelligence for resilient agricultural development to attain sustainable food security in Bangladesh. The project will be conducted in salinity-affected 2000 farmers. Multi-dimensional strategic methods would be adopted in developing the model like Artificial intelligence-based vulnerability index development for agricultural land (Farmer plot to plot vulnerability assessment), Forecasting crop suitability with microclimate data through crop simulation model (WOFOST mechanistic model), Application of artificial intelligence in the development of SWAC model.
core_fields.abstract: Saline water intrusion is a common problem in the coastal areas of Bangladesh. Climate change-induced hazards including sea-level rise, cyclones, storm surges, and tidal inundation are contributing to this problem causing salinity ingression into water and land (Baten et al. 2015). The coastal region of Bangladesh is a food deficit area where net food production and the diversity of food production have declined significantly over recent decades due to the salinity problem. Regular devastating cyclonic storm surges, sea-level rise, and tidal inundation have changed the level of salinity and these have increased the risks associated with normal crop production. Many agricultural resilient options are being practiced in Bangladesh to adapt to climate-induced agricultural disasters like salinity, floods, waterlogging, and drought. Some of these innovations are devised by local communities through their Indigenous knowledge, and some are planned interventions promoted by different government and non-government organizations (Rahaman et al. 2018, Rahaman et al., 2020)). Thus, several studies related to resilient agriculture and climate change have been promoting different salinity-tolerant crop varieties such as salinity-tolerant rice varieties. Different authorities are only promoting climate-resilient variety in coastal regions that will benefit the farmers of a certain period. However, there is no integrated platform and Application of artificial intelligence in Bangladesh for developing a climate-resilient agriculture system to attain food security.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Payment for Environmental Services in Rukeria Watershed to Support Upland Farmers and Tea Plantations
core_fields.description: The project will introduce a Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) scheme in the Rukeri watershed to tackle erosion, flooding, drought, and poverty. It will train 200 lead farmer families to create agroecology plans, including an assessment of current and desired conditions and an action plan. The project will support the planting of 30,000 agroforestry trees, link farmers to buyers of products and services , and promote small women-led agroecology businesses to foster sustainable.
core_fields.abstract: The Rukeri catchment, primarily covered by tea plantations in the valley and seasonal crops uphill, faces significant challenges of climate change impacts such as erratic rainfall, soil erosion, flooding during rainy seasons, and droughts in dry periods, gap in farmers' skills to adapt to these changing conditions, and a lack of coordination between uphill and downhill farmers, This has led to reduced agricultural productivity, poverty and biodiversity loss To address these issues, the project proposes implementing a Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) scheme, promoting agroecology practices, particularly agroforestry, in the uphill areas. This innovation will enable uphill smallholder farmers to adopt sustainable land management techniques that diversify their income, reduce soil erosion, enhance water infiltration, and mitigate flooding and droughts in downhill. Tea farmers cooperative will benefit from improved water management, reduced maintenance costs, and increased productivity due to healthier upstream ecosystems. agro ecology family planner tool will be adopted as apprach that will be used in the project, wife and husband will be trainined in agroecology planning and implementation. The PES scheme incentivizes uphill farmers by compensating them for the environmental services they provide, such as increased tea yields and reduced environmental degradation. The solution is rooted in agroecological principles, supported by scientific insights into the interconnectedness of ecosystems and the need for integrated farming practices. Immediate benefits include improved income, better water management, and soil conservation for farmers, while long-term benefits extend to the entire community, enhancing resilience to climate change and promoting sustainable development.

core_fields.title: Transforming Waste to Wealth: Sustainable Solutions for Agriculture and Food Security
core_fields.description: CESDA and its technical partner EcoProtein Innovations Limited are introducing Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming to transform organic waste into protein-rich animal feeds and nutrient-dense fertilizers. This scalable and eco-friendly innovation addresses food insecurity, environmental degradation, and high feed costs for small-scale farmers. It reduces feed expenses by 15%, increases yields by 20%, and diverts waste from landfills, cutting emissions. Targeting 10,000 farmers initially, the project envisions producing 60 tons in 12 months
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation focuses on using Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming to transform organic waste into high-quality, sustainable agricultural inputs. This process addresses the critical challenges of high feed costs, environmental degradation, and food insecurity. Farmers in Nigeria spend 65 85% of their costs on animal feeds, a major barrier to profitability. At the same time, over 32 million tons of organic waste end up in landfills annually, contributing to environmental degradation and climate challenges. With 88.4 million Nigerians living in extreme poverty and 25 million at risk of food insecurity, there is an urgent need for affordable, sustainable solutions. Using BSF larvae, we convert organic waste into protein-rich animal feeds and nutrient-dense organic fertilizers. This innovative approach reduces feed costs by at least 15% and boosts yields by 20%, improving farmer profitability and productivity. BSF farming is highly resource-efficient and scalable, utilizing scientific insights into entomology and biotechnology to create a circular economy. The benefits are immediate and far-reaching. Farmers gain access to affordable, high-quality inputs, boosting their productivity and economic sustainability. Communities benefit from reduced waste, cleaner environments, and new job opportunities. Consumers enjoy healthier, more affordable food products. Additionally, society and the environment benefit from lower greenhouse gas emissions, improved waste management, and enhanced soil fertility. This innovation delivers economic, social, and environmental benefits, driving sustainable agricultural practices and creating resilient food systems for the future.

core_fields.title: SOFADRICLIMATE App: Transforming Smallholder Farming with Bundled Digital Climate Services for Resilience and Sustainability
core_fields.description: The SOFADRICLIMATE App empowers smallholder maize farmers in Nigeria with affordable, bundled digital climate services, offering personalized climate information and user-friendly weather index micro-insurance tailored to crop producers' needs. By providing real-time, data-driven insights, the app enhances farmers' decision-making, boosts resilience to climate change, and supports sustainable productivity. It promotes climate-smart practices to ensure food security, improve livelihoods, and foster long-term prosperity. Leveraging on preliminary evidence we aim to scale to other states in Nigeria.
core_fields.abstract: The SOFADRICLIMATE App addresses the challenges faced by smallholder maize farmers in Nigeria due to climate change, unpredictable weather patterns, and limited access to timely, actionable agricultural advice. Many farmers struggle to make informed decisions about planting, irrigation and harvest timing, which directly affects their productivity and livelihoods. This app provides affordable, bundled digital climate services, integrating personalized, data-driven weather forecasts, and weather index micro-insurance tailored to the specific needs of crop producers. By offering real-time insights, the app empowers farmers to make informed decisions, enhancing their resilience to climate-related risks and improving their crop management practices. The solution is grounded in scientific research and data analysis, leveraging local climate data, weather patterns, and agronomic knowledge to deliver relevant, actionable information from the Nigerian Mereological Agency (NiMet). The app s user-friendly interface ensures accessibility for farmers with varying levels of digital literacy, while the integration of weather index insurance provides an additional layer of security against climate risks. Immediate benefits include increased crop yields, better resource management, and reduced losses due to climate-related events. In the long term, the app promotes sustainable farming practices, food security, and improved livelihoods by enhancing farmers' ability to adapt to changing climatic conditions. This comprehensive, data-driven solution is highly relevant as it tackles pressing challenges in agriculture, ultimately fostering prosperity and climate resilience in farming communities.

core_fields.title: Empowering Women in Sustainable and Nutritious Food Production through Agroecological Practices
core_fields.description: The project addresses the intersection of empowering conscious consumer choices, sustainable regenerative practices, and ensuring safe, nutritious food for healthy diets by equipping women farmers in rural Ghana with the knowledge, tools, and support to adopt agroecological practices that enhance food security, improve nutrition, and regenerate the land. This initiative will empower women as key drivers of change in the local food system, ensuring that the food produced is nutritious, affordable, and environmentally sustainable.
core_fields.abstract: In rural Ghana, many women smallholder farmers face limited access to sustainable farming techniques, markets, and resources. This results in low crop yields, poor nutrition, and economic insecurity. Traditional farming methods often degrade soil health, reduce biodiversity, and harm the environment. Additionally, access to nutritious, affordable food remains a significant issue, contributing to malnutrition and poor health outcomes, particularly among women and children. CeWaFS-Ghana s initiative seeks to address these interconnected challenges by empowering women farmers with the knowledge and tools to adopt agroecological practices. Agroecology focuses on sustainable, regenerative farming methods that restore soil health, conserve water, and increase biodiversity, while providing nutritious, diverse crops that improve food security. By training women in organic farming, crop diversification, and food preservation, we equip them to enhance household nutrition and generate income through value-added products. This solution empowers women as leaders in the local food system, restores the land, and creates a more resilient food economy. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition, increased food production, and economic empowerment for women farmers. Over time, the project will scale regenerative practices, improve local ecosystems, and create lasting community networks, ensuring sustainable access to safe, nutritious food for all.

core_fields.title: Harvesting Horizons: Cultivating Resilient Food Systems for Tomorrow
core_fields.description: Harvesting Horizons is a transformative initiative aimed at revolutionizing global food systems through sustainable agricultural practices, innovative technologies, and community empowerment. The project addresses critical challenges like climate change, food insecurity, and urbanization by promoting resilient, equitable, and inclusive food systems. Through research, pilot programs, capacity building, and policy advocacy, "Harvesting Horizons" seeks to create a sustainable, adaptable food network that ensures access to healthy, affordable food for future generations.
core_fields.abstract: Harvesting Horizons addresses critical global challenges, such as food insecurity, climate change, and unsustainable agricultural practices, by promoting innovative solutions that transform food systems. The primary problem being solved is the growing threat to food security, especially in vulnerable regions, driven by environmental degradation, population growth, and changing climate patterns. These factors make current farming practices less effective, unsustainable, and inequitable. The project provides a comprehensive approach to solving these problems by introducing cutting-edge agricultural technologies like precision farming, vertical farming, and climate-resilient crops. These innovations enable farmers to optimize resource use, reduce environmental impact, and adapt to changing climate conditions. For instance, drought-resistant crops and water-efficient farming techniques allow farmers to maintain productivity even in harsh environments, while vertical farming maximizes space and minimizes land use in urban areas. The scientific insight behind this approach includes advances in biotechnology, data analytics, and sustainable farming practices. Precision agriculture leverages real-time data to improve decision-making, while regenerative practices restore soil health and biodiversity. The immediate benefits include increased food production, reduced environmental impact, and enhanced resilience to climate change. For end users like farmers, this means higher yields, lower costs, and improved livelihoods. Communities benefit from more affordable, nutritious food, while society at large enjoys a more sustainable, equitable, and resilient food system. The environment also benefits from reduced resource depletion and biodiversity preservation.

core_fields.title: "VANASPATIGUARD: AI-Driven Pre-Harvest Disease Detection and Sustainable Crop Management Platform"
core_fields.description: VANASPATIGUARD is an AI-powered platform that detects pre-harvest diseases in fruits and vegetables, providing real-time recommendations to farmers. By leveraging advanced technologies, it reduces crop losses, boosts yields, and promotes sustainable farming practices. The platform ensures smarter, data-driven agricultural decisions, enhancing productivity and contributing to global food security while fostering environmental sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description and Benefits: VANASPATIGUARD addresses the critical issue of pre-harvest losses in agriculture, which threaten food security and farmer livelihoods. Traditional disease detection methods are often reactive, resource-intensive, and insufficient to mitigate crop damage effectively. This innovation introduces an AI-powered platform that uses advanced imaging and machine learning techniques to identify early signs of diseases in fruits and vegetables during pre-harvest stages. The solution leverages cutting-edge scientific insights, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and spectral imaging, to analyze plant health and predict disease onset with high accuracy. By providing real-time, actionable recommendations, the platform empowers farmers to make proactive decisions, such as optimizing pesticide use and improving crop management practices. Relevance and Benefits: This solution is critical in addressing global challenges like food insecurity, climate change, and unsustainable farming practices. Farmers gain immediate benefits through reduced crop losses, enhanced yields, and lower input costs. Schools and communities benefit from access to healthier, more abundant food supplies. Producers enjoy improved productivity and profitability, while society and the environment benefit from reduced chemical usage and waste. The platform fosters long-term sustainability by promoting environmentally friendly practices, conserving resources, and ensuring resilient food systems. VANASPATIGUARD is a transformative step towards smarter agriculture, enabling stakeholders across the supply chain to thrive in a competitive, resource-constrained world.
