core_fields.title: CAFRESH+-Connecting the Food Supply Chain
core_fields.description: CAFRESH+ integrates patented polymer membrane packaging and blockchain solutions to revolutionize the food supply chain. By extending shelf life, enhancing transparency, and streamlining SNAP/WIC payment integration, it reduces food waste, empowers smallholder farmers, and improves consumer access to fresh, sustainable produce. With pilots in the U.S. and India, CAFRESH+ addresses global challenges of inefficiency, waste, and accessibility, promoting a resilient and equitable food system for all stakeholders.
core_fields.abstract: CAFRESH+ combines patented polymer membrane packaging and blockchain technology to tackle food waste, inefficiency, and inequity in the global food supply chain. The innovation addresses critical challenges: up to 40% of fresh produce is wasted annually, farmers earn less than 10 cents per consumer dollar, and low-income communities face barriers to accessing fresh, nutritious food. The CAFRESH+ solution extends produce shelf life by optimizing oxygen and carbon dioxide levels with polymer membranes, reducing spoilage during storage and transit. Blockchain technology ensures traceability, transparency, and trust across the supply chain, while also streamlining SNAP/WIC payment integration to improve accessibility for low-income consumers. These features empower smallholder farmers by reducing postharvest losses and increasing market access, improving their income and sustainability. Scientific insights into controlled atmosphere packaging and blockchain applications underpin CAFRESH+, creating immediate benefits for stakeholders. Farmers gain higher income and reduced waste. Consumers enjoy fresher, traceable produce. Schools and communities access reliable, nutritious food, while the environment benefits from reduced greenhouse gas emissions and water usage. By improving efficiency, sustainability, and equity, CAFRESH+ transforms the food supply chain into a transparent, resilient system that delivers measurable economic and environmental impact for society.

core_fields.title: Agroecological Hydroponic Gardens: Nutritional Innovation and Sustainability for children and their families in the rural valley of Cochabamba
core_fields.description: This project aims to implement agroecological hydroponic gardens and small rainwater harvesting systems in childcare centers and schools in Valle Alto, Cochabamba, to improve the nutrition of children and their families. Participants will learn to harvest rainwater to grow fresh, nutritious food for self-consumption using agroecological techniques. and will receive training to replicate gardens at home. The initiative addresses drought and malnutrition, promoting food security and nutrition, agroecology, environmental education, and efficient water use.
core_fields.abstract: The Valle Alto region of Cochabamba faces significant food security challenges due to recurring droughts exacerbated by climate change. Water scarcity has reduced agricultural output, worsening malnutrition, particularly among children and women, with iron deficiency threatening development. In Bolivia, chronic malnutrition affected 12.2% of children under five in 2019, and anemia reached 43.5%, primarily in rural, low-income areas. In girls, food insecurity can disrupt menarche, while mothers face risks to reproductive health. Additionally, many rural families depend on unsustainable agricultural practices due to water scarcity and lack of access to technology. Educational institutions like boarding schools and wawa wasis (childcare centers) are vital in this context. Childcare centers provide food for children under 5, and boarding schools offer meals and lodging for adolescents during the week. However, meals lack diversity and essential nutrients, relying on staples like noodles, rice, potatoes, or corn. This project introduces rainwater harvesting systems and agroecological hydroponic gardens in schools and childcare centers. These gardens, made with recycled materials, will supply fresh vegetables, improve diets with local crops, and integrate ancestral agricultural knowledge. Hydroponics, which use up to 90% less water, are ideal for this drought-prone region and align with FAO recommendations for arid areas. The initiative enhances children's nutrition, trains teachers and parents to replicate gardens at home and teach agroecological practices and nutrition, and promotes food security and self-sufficiency. Community food fairs and a nutritional recipe book foster knowledge exchange, family involvement, and sustainable practices to address malnutrition effectively.

core_fields.title: From Farm to Fork: Enhancing Value Chains Through Tech-Enabled Market Linkages
core_fields.description: ChipChip is an agricultural e-commerce platform transforming how fresh food reaches consumers' tables while empowering those who grow it. Launched in Ethiopia in mid-October 2023, ChipChip leverages a unique "social buying" model inspired by the traditional Ethiopian concept "Kircha," encouraging people to make purchases in groups. This approach allows farmers to sell agri-foods in bulk directly to end consumers, pooling demand and delivery to increase sales for producers while reducing food costs for customers.
core_fields.abstract: Ethiopia's rural households earn their livelihood through agricultural practices, yet farmers face many challenges, ranging from market penetration to pricing, due to an underdeveloped supply chain, which often results in diminished returns for farmers and inflated prices for consumers. At ChipChip, we recognize that producers and end consumers are the most critical stakeholders in the supply chain. Instead, the existing supply chain dynamics often result in lower prices for farmers while leading to higher costs for consumers. Asymmetric power balances in supply chains often favor markets over farmers, suppressing their ability to reduce waste. We tackle this issue by providing a digital marketplace that connects farmers directly with consumers. We use a group buying model that allows consumers to aggregate their demand and purchase straight from farmers at prices that are 25-30% lower than market rates, while potentially reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 10-20% through decreased transportation and fewer intermediaries in the supply chain. Our platform hosts three integrated apps that focus on specific portions of the supply chain. Our Sellers App enables producers to directly connect with end users, manage stock levels, set prices and ultimately turn each producer to digital storefronts. Our logistics App allows drivers to manage multiple orders in a single trip, optimizing delivery routes and reducing fuel wastage. Finally, our consumers App is our cornerstone product that allows consumers to browse and purchase products directly from farmers and can buy items individually or participate in group purchases offering better pricing on bulk orders.

core_fields.title: Advancing Sustainable Packaging Solutions for Local Businesses and Environmental Preservation
core_fields.description: Our company develops cost-effective, high-quality biodegradable packaging solutions for small and medium-scale enterprises. Replacing plastic with environmentally friendly material helps us minimize environmental pollution, ensures sustainability, and encourages local business enterprise. By innovation, strategic partnerships, and engaging the community, we are developing solutions to address the growing demand for sustainable packaging, contributing to a greener future.
core_fields.abstract: Chipatso Eco Packagers is offering the world an innovative solution to plastic waste with the provision of affordable, biodegradable packaging targeted at small and medium-scale enterprises. Plastic pollution has risen to a critical point, from the destruction it causes to the environment, wildlife, and human health. Most of the biodegradable packaging available in the market is costly and mainly targets large companies, thus leaving limited options for smaller businesses. Our innovation utilizes locally available agricultural waste products like sugarcane bagasse and maize husks for producing high-quality, sustainable packaging. We do research and technical development to incorporate environmentally safe binders and additives that ensure strength and functionality without compromising on eco-friendliness. This approach contributes not only to a reduction in plastic use but also to the reusing of waste that otherwise would not be put into productive use. These include cost-effective packaging for small businesses, increased environmental sustainability, and landfill waste reduction. Over the long term, our solution would encourage a circular economy, create a market for the agricultural by-products for local farmers, and educate the communities on the value of eco-conscious living. Chipatso Eco Packagers addresses a vital need in an innovative manner that is bound to contribute toward a healthy environment and support the local economies.

core_fields.title: Community Farming in Brazil
core_fields.description: Our project supports urban agriculture and family farming initiatives in several cities in Brazil to generate jobs and healthy food for needy communities
core_fields.abstract: According to the Brazilian National Statistics Center (IBGE), in 2023 60 million Brazilians are in a situation of food insecurity, 25 million of them in a situation of hunger. Brazilian agriculture is focused on commodity exports and there is little support for food production for the domestic market, which results in expensive food that not everyone can afford. To solve this problem, since 2004, the Cities Without Hunger Organization has been building urban gardens in large unused spaces in cities using local labor, building gardens in public schools to improve student nutrition and supporting the work of small family farmers. As a result, we were able to (1) generate jobs, (2) income, (3) supply of healthy food in the neighborhoods and cities where we operate, (4) food for public school students (5) a new market for family farmers to increase their income in addition to (6) producing a large amount of food using healthy techniques and with low environmental impact. Our NGO is recognized in Brazil and around the world as a reference in agricultural projects that involve the use of urban and rural areas for sustainable agricultural production, encompassing income generation, healthy food, food supply for peripheral communities and food school.

core_fields.title: Building Resilient Food Systems in Kaduna
core_fields.description: The Building Resilient Food Systems in Kaduna project empowers 700 smallholder farmers in Kaduna North with regenerative agricultural practices, one solar-powered cold storage hub, and biofortified crops. We believe by addressing soil degradation, reducing post-harvest losses, and improving nutrition, the project improves food security, boosts incomes, and fosters gender-inclusive, sustainable agricultural development, creating lasting resilience in Kaduna local government communities.
core_fields.abstract: In Kaduna North, smallholder farmers face declining productivity due to widespread soil degradation, post-harvest losses, and limited access to resources. These challenges, exacerbated by climate change, result in food insecurity, malnutrition, and economic instability for farming households in the communities. Women and youth are disproportionately affected, as they often lack access to resources and opportunities to improve their livelihoods. The Building Resilient Food Systems in Kaduna project introduces an integrated solution to address these pressing issues. It combines regenerative agricultural practices, solar-powered cold storage hub, and biofortified crops to create immediate and long-term benefits for farmers, communities, and the environment. Scientific insights highlight that regenerative practices, such as crop rotation and composting, can restore soil health and increase yields by up to 25%. Solar-powered cold storage hubs reduce post-harvest losses by 30%, ensuring that farmers retain the value of their produce. Biofortified crops improve nutrition, particularly among children and women, addressing micronutrient deficiencies sustainably. The immediate benefits of the project include higher incomes for farmers, reduced food spoilage, and improved dietary diversity for 1,300 households. In the long term, healthier soils and climate-resilient practices will sustain agricultural productivity and environmental health. This project empowers communities by promoting inclusivity, resilience, and economic stability, in line with Nigeria s National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Plan and global sustainability goals.

core_fields.title: The Ujamaa Cafe
core_fields.description: Ujamaa Cafe is a cashless, de-surveilled grab-and-go vending option located in food apartheid communities with healthful nutrition options to close the gap on food insecurity. Our Ujamaa kiosks offer an innovative model for offering healthy meals and sharing nutritional information. Through Ujamaa Café we get instant user-feedback on our communities’ dietary preferences and nutritional habits, including the preference for grab-and-go foods, or specific taste, which enables us to create a virtuous feedback loop to our Ujamaa restaurant affiliates, tailoring highly curated meals for our communities.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Cold Storage to Reduce Post-Harvest Losses in Kano
core_fields.description: ColdHubs Limited will install a 100-ton solar-powered cold storage unit at Yankaba Fresh Fruits and Vegetables Market in Kano, Nigeria. This sustainable solution will reduce post-harvest losses, enhance food security, and increase incomes for 50,000 smallholder farmers and traders. Additionally, the project will create employment opportunities for women and youth, utilize renewable energy to minimize environmental impact and support economic growth in the agricultural sector.
core_fields.abstract: In Nigeria, up to 50% of fresh fruits and vegetables are lost post-harvest due to inadequate storage infrastructure. This significant loss undermines farmers incomes, exacerbates food insecurity, and contributes to environmental degradation through methane emissions from rotting produce (USAID, 2021; FAO, 2020). The lack of reliable cold storage is particularly detrimental to smallholder farmers and traders in regions like Kano, where agricultural productivity is vital for livelihoods but hampered by storage inefficiencies. ColdHubs Limited addresses this challenge by deploying a 100-ton solar-powered cold storage unit at Yankaba Fresh Fruits and Vegetables Market in Kano. This innovative solution leverages renewable solar energy to power walk-in cold rooms, eliminating dependence on unreliable grid electricity and reducing carbon emissions (ColdHubs, 2023). The ColdHub technology extends the shelf life of perishables from 2 days to up to 90 days, significantly reducing post-harvest losses. The scientific and technical insight behind this solution lies in combining sustainable energy with advanced refrigeration technology. Solar panels provide a consistent energy supply, while energy-efficient refrigeration systems maintain optimal storage temperatures. Additionally, real-time monitoring through the CARMS system ensures operational efficiency and minimizes downtime. Immediate benefits include preserving the quality of produce, increasing farmers and traders incomes, and enhancing food availability for consumers. Sustainable benefits encompass environmental protection through reduced greenhouse gas emissions, empowerment of women and youth through job creation, and strengthened local economies. By ensuring a stable supply of fresh, nutritious food, ColdHubs supports community health, economic resilience, and long-term agricultural sustainability (World Bank, 2021; UNEP, 2020).

core_fields.title: Eco-friendly Food Security for Indigenous People around the "Cestos-Senkwen & Krahn-Bassa KBAs" in South-eastern Liberia.
core_fields.description: This innovation is to empower indigenous people scale eco-friendly aquaculture and irrigation swamp-rice farming in 24 months, by: (1) Constructing a fish hatchery, cold storage/seed bank, and expanding the existing site to one-hectare to generate US$132,000.00; (2) Conducting feasibility surveys on soil and water, and empowering farmers with skills, seeding and start-up funding to boost tilapia and swamp-rice farming and generate over US$259,200.00. (4) Using income for sustainability and carbon-financing investment for long-term socioeconomic development.
core_fields.abstract: Poverty, food insecurity and biodiversity loss (shifting cultivation, poaching and illicit logging) remain unabated in indigenous communities around the Cestos-Senkwen & Krahn-Bassa KBAs , as people are playing a leadership role in the global fight against climate. Key factor, exacerbating poverty, food insecurity and biodiversity loss, is the lack of sustainable livelihood programs to enable indigenous people conserve their natural environment, in compliance with Article 29 of the United Nations Declaration for the Rights of Indigenous People (UNDRIP) . CARD s innovation is to scale highly productive, safe, affordable, climate-resilient and regenerative aquaculture and irrigation swamp-rice farming to enhance food security without harming nature and people, as follow: (1) Engage indigenous people, through town-hall meetings, to promote eco-friendly food security, biodiversity conservation and climate-change mitigation. (2) Construct a fish hatchery, designed to supply 40,000 healthy tilapia fingerlings to smallholder farmers to boost tilapia production and mitigate the poaching of protected animals. (3) Construct a cold storage, including seed bank, to preserve harvested tilapia products and other perishable food. (4) Conduct feasibility surveys on soil and year-round-water supply, and empower farmers with skills; seeding and start-up funding for aquaculture and irrigation swamp-rice farming on a harvest-and-pay basis to motivate farmers abandon their traditional shifting cultivation and illicit logging for livelihood. (5) Supply affordable tilapia products to market women, on a Sell-and-pay basis to improve women s economic empowerment. (6) Use income from fish hatchery and tilapia production site to sustain project activities and enhance ecological restoration to attract carbon-financing investment for long-term socioeconomic development.

core_fields.title: Scaling & Streamlining Access to Transformational Aquaponics of All Scales Where it Matters Most Through Supply Chain Development and Educational Solutions
core_fields.description: The project primarily aims to capitalize on ten years of aquaponics R&D and successful operations using a modular approach. It will scale up the components of this operational food system and broaden the reach of its educational program. Lastly, the project involves studying the financial and non-financial impact of aquaponics of scale at the household level. These objectives are based on Community First aquaponic farmers input and requests.
core_fields.abstract: Modern Cambodia is still reeling from its dark past. This can be seen throughout its infrastructure, educational system, and, most importantly, its value chain for food. Despite 80% of the population living in rural areas, many farmers can only participate in the food economy by farming rice. This is aggravated by soil quality not being compatible with fresh produce. As a result, most of it is imported from Thailand and Vietnam, leaving farming families out of this market opportunity. Perhaps more concerning, this lingering situation has created food security and safety problems for most Cambodians, leading to alarming rates of childhood stunting. All the imported produce is directed to large ports of entry into Cambodia and, ultimately, urban markets. This leaves those who could grow food with limited availability and choice for themselves, as they cannot compete with this kind of volume. Aquaponics offers a chance to change this, offering an off-soil alternative to conventional farming. Community First aquaponics has been successful in helping dozens of families transition their homestead to this innovative agricultural technique. The only feedback trainers are receiving is that food systems as they are currently designed are not large enough. This project aims to use Community First s ten years of experience to help families turn their homesteads into scaled-up aquaponic production sites that can both feed & enrich families while addressing the market demand for safe and abundant fresh produce.

core_fields.title: harnessing of solar energy to preserve indigenous foods and promote nutrition, equity and sustainability through decentralized drying hubs
core_fields.description: This project aims to harness solar energy to preserve indigenous foods by establishing decentralized drying hubs. These hubs will enhance food security and nutrition, reduce post-harvest losses, and promote equity by empowering local communities, especially small-scale farmers and marginalized groups. Using sustainable solar technology, the initiative fosters environmentally friendly practices while preserving biodiversity and traditional knowledge. By decentralizing food processing, the project ensures accessibility, affordability, and resilience in food systems, advancing healthier and equitable future.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation addresses the critical challenge of food loss, nutrition insecurity, and limited access to sustainable food systems by introducing decentralized solar-powered drying hubs. These hubs focus on preserving indigenous foods, vegetables, and herbs, which are rich in nutrients and culturally significant. Food loss is a global issue, with post-harvest spoilage particularly severe in rural and underserved areas due to inadequate preservation methods. By leveraging solar energy, a clean and renewable resource, these drying hubs enable communities to dehydrate surplus crops efficiently, extending shelf life and reducing waste. The scientific principle of solar dehydration ensures nutrient retention, maintaining the nutritional value of indigenous foods. The decentralization aspect empowers local farmers, schools, and small producers, fostering inclusivity and equitable access to food preservation technology. Immediate benefits include improved food security, increased farmer income through value-added products, and enhanced dietary diversity for consumers. Sustainable benefits include reduced reliance on electricity or fuel, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthened local economies. Schools and communities gain access to healthier food options, while society benefits from a more resilient and equitable food system. This solution not only mitigates post-harvest losses but also promotes environmental sustainability, cultural preservation, and social equity, making it a transformative approach to tackling food and nutrition challenges globally.

core_fields.title: Alliance for Sustainable Food Systems in Oodweyne District
core_fields.description: Concern aims to enhance food and nutrition security for vulnerable agropastoral Somaliland communities through a technology-driven, evidence-based farming system. In partnership with IGAD Technical and Veterinary School (ISTVS), Observatory Development and Welfare Organization (ODAWO), and Telesom Communication, the project strengthens research-farmer linkages, conducts on-farm research, and disseminates knowledge via IVR and SMS. By integrating crops and livestock farming, it boosts productivity and ensures access to safe, nutritious, and reliable food for vulnerable communities.
core_fields.abstract: Somaliland faces chronic food insecurity, driven by erratic rainfall, droughts, and land degradation, which severely undermine the productivity of agro-pastoralism vital for over 85% of rural livelihoods. With recurring droughts and volatile weather patterns, crop and livestock yields are dramatically reduced, leading to economic instability, undernutrition, and heightened vulnerability. As of 2025, regions within Concern s program are projected to face IPC3/4 (crisis and emergency) levels of food insecurity. Additionally, the lack of extension services (educational and resource support), especially for remote and nomadic agro-pastoralists, limits access to essential climate adaptation knowledge, leaving farmers unprepared to cope with these challenges. This project addresses these issues by introducing Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) practices through innovative partnerships and technology. Drawing on previous successes such as reducing soil erosion by 77% through manuring and intercropping the project integrates mobile phone services to deliver real-time guidance on CSA practices like soil retention, composting, mulching, and optimal sowing times. In collaboration with ISTVS, the project supports on-farm research, training, and seasonal weather alerts via IVR and SMS. Focusing on mixed crop-livestock farming, the project promotes sustainable practices by using crop residues for livestock feed and animal manure to improve soil health. This integrated approach ensures long-term food security, improved nutrition, and enhanced incomes, while fostering resilient agricultural systems. Farmers will gain access to tailored, real-time agricultural knowledge, boosting crop and livestock productivity, food security, and diet quality. The use of drought-tolerant seeds, alongside CSA practices, will improve soil fertility, reduce dependency on expensive fertilizers, and help mitigate climate change.

core_fields.title: Developing an NIR Tool for Rapid Screening of Aflatoxin-Resistant Groundnuts to Combat Aflatoxin Contamination.
core_fields.description: This project aims to reduce aflatoxin contamination in peanuts by utilizing two naturally occurring antifungal metabolites, 2,5-dihydroxybenzaldehyde and ferulic acid, found in peanut seed coats. Through targeted metabolomics and Near-Infrared (NIR) predictive modeling, resistant peanut germplasm will be identified, validated, and screened for aflatoxin resistance. This innovative approach will enhance peanut quality, protect public health, and improve marketability, offering a sustainable solution to farmers in sub-Saharan Africa, especially northern Ghana.
core_fields.abstract: Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) is a vital crop across sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Northern Ghana, where it contributes to food security and alleviates malnutrition as a key protein source. However, its production is severely impacted by Aspergillus flavus, a fungal pathogen that produces carcinogenic aflatoxins during pre- and post-harvest stages. Aflatoxin contamination poses serious public health risks, including hepatocellular carcinoma and impaired growth, while reducing peanut quality and marketability. In many African countries, including Ghana, aflatoxin levels often exceed the European safety threshold of 4 g/kg, resulting in economic losses from export rejections and reduced crop value. Alarmingly, about 40% of children in Africa are exposed to aflatoxin-contaminated peanut products, increasing their risk of long-term health effects. This proposal seeks to address this issue by utilizing naturally occurring secondary metabolites in peanut seed coats to inhibit A. flavus and reduce aflatoxin contamination. Research has identified two key metabolites, 2,5-dihydroxybenzaldehyde and ferulic acid, as potent antifungal agents (Commey et al., 2024). These compounds form a protective barrier on peanut seeds, preventing fungal colonization and reducing aflatoxin accumulation. The economic and agricultural benefits are significant. For plant breeders, this approach offers a reliable tool to screen for aflatoxin-resistant germplasm, accelerating resistant variety development. For farmers, it provides a natural, cost-effective method to reduce aflatoxin contamination, improving crop quality and marketability. This innovation has the potential to reduce post-harvest losses, increase access to premium markets, and enhance farm income, promoting sustainable agriculture and economic resilience in African peanut production.

core_fields.title: Empowering Women Farmers with IoT-Enabled Drip Irrigation for Biofortified Sweet Potatoes and Cowpeas cultivation.
core_fields.description: This project promotes drought-resilient and regenerative agriculture by intercropping biofortified sweet potatoes with nitrogen-fixing cowpeas grown under Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled drip irrigation systems. Project outcomes are increased food security, water conservations, biodiversity, and soil health. The project trains 60 women on sustainable agricultural practices to improve yields, and creates equitable market opportunities. Using an award-winning, flexible pay-as-you-use model, the project provides fortified seeds, training and irrigation systems gradually repaid using crop profits
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Zambia face severe challenges, including water scarcity, degraded soils, malnutrition, and limited access to financing. Over two-thirds rely on rain-fed maize farming, limiting productivity to one cycle annually, leaving households vulnerable to food insecurity. Droughts worsen the situation, and financial exclusion hinders investment in climate responsive practices, particularly among women. This project introduces IoT-enabled drip irrigation systems combined with intercropping biofortified Vitamin A Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potatoes (OFSP) and iron-rich cowpeas. IoT (Internet of Things) allows devices like soil moisture sensors and automated irrigation controllers to communicate and optimize water use. This precision ensures crops receive adequate water even during droughts, supporting up to four crop cycles annually. Burney et al., 2010 demonstrates that drip irrigation reduces water use by up to 80% compared to conventional methods while increasing yields by 50%. Intercropping enhances soil health through nitrogen-fixing abilities and sweet potato broad leaves suppress weeds-reducing chemical fertilizer and herbicide application. Furthermore, both sweet potato and cowpeas are versatile in local diets: the sweet potato leaves and tubers, as well as cowpea leaves and pods, are all edible, nutrient-dense, and culturally familiar. This integration supports improved nutrition, addressing deficiencies in vitamin A, iron, and zinc. Immediate benefits include year-round farming, improved incomes, and increased food security, especially for women farmers through a pay-as-you-use model that eliminates upfront costs for technology, inputs and training. For consumers, nutrient-dense crops offer affordable, locally sourced options to combat malnutrition. Environmental benefits include reduced water use, restored soils, lower carbon emissions

core_fields.title: Future Proofing Decapod Crustacean Aquaculture Practice: Promoting High Welfare, Sustainable Seafood, Low Waste, and Human Health
core_fields.description: The project will evaluate current decapod aquaculture practice, identify areas of weakness (welfare, environmental impact, food waste, food policy/procedure, nutritive value), providing a Code of Best Practice and White Paper for industry-wide adoption. The issue remains that the decapod aquaculture industry is currently unregulated and hence liable to be inherently damaging. A systematic review of process and production of Codes will enable practitioners to promote welfare, food safety, human and animal health and sustainable production.
core_fields.abstract: The global fishing industry employs approximately 38 million persons with an extra 20 million in aquaculture. It is further estimated that 600 million livelihoods rely on fisheries and aquaculture (Organisation Internationale du Travail lio.org). The current march towards industrialisation is not taking account of the many examples globally of poorly introduced aquaculture systems which are documented to create severe animal welfare issues, negatively impact local and global biodiversity, produce food waste, lead to concentrated environmental pollution, lessen apparent human health benefits, reduce consumer choice, and damage regional economies. Early observations in Salmonid farming led to inherent issues that are still to be resolved. It is only after 20 + years of damage that some change is being recognised. It is hence imperative that prior to huge expansion of decapod aquaculture (as is predicted) that impacts are considered and a best practice approach created. With further growth expected it is important that impact is considered and best practice developed to support the following improvements in : i. Animal health and welfare ii. Environmental responsibility iii. Food safety iv. Social accountability v. Traceability Immediate benefits will be to farmers and producers enabling appropriate high quality, high welfare food production; good food policy, environmental protection, waste management and value addition, societal support for sustainable and welfare led food, local (and often marginal) community economic support.

core_fields.title: The 1,000,000 Closed-Loop Homes & Farms Project
core_fields.description: D-Olivette, a pioneer in AI and IoT-enabled biodigesters, transforms organic waste into renewable energy and agricultural inputs. Its flagship Kitchen Box empowers women, farmers, and refugees with multilingual AI support for clean cooking fuel and fertilizer production. Through its 1,000,000 Closed-Loop Homes & Farms Project, D-Olivette collaborates with global organizations and governments to deliver sustainable energy, regenerative agriculture, and economic growth to underserved communities, aiming to impact 1,000,000 households and farms by 2030.
core_fields.abstract: Africa faces worsening energy and food crises due to global conflicts, economic instability, and climate extremes. In Nigeria, essentials like kerosene and cooking gas have surged by over 300%, forcing low-income communities to rely on firewood. With over half of Africa s 1.52 billion people living on less than $1.90 per day, affordable energy solutions are vital. Notably, air pollution from biomass stoves releases harmful pollutants. Prolonged exposure to these toxins is linked to respiratory, eye, and adverse pregnancy diseases. Shockingly, biomass stoves pollution ranks as the second leading cause of death in Africa, claiming over 500,000 lives of women and children annually while contributing to deforestation and climate change. D-Olivette addresses these issues with AI and IoT-powered biodigesters that transform organic waste into clean energy, including cooking gas and electricity, as well as livestock feed and fertilizers. By utilizing about 1 billion tons of agricultural waste produced annually in Africa, our closed-loop system reduces farming costs by 50%, enhances clean energy access, and strengthens food security. D-Olivette empowers rural women, farmers, and communities to manage waste sustainably, lower emissions, and build resilient livelihoods.

core_fields.title: Hi-tech & Carbon-Free Energy Solution for Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: In the last 3 years, we build from scratch, Affordable & Clean Hi-tech Lithium Solar generators ranging between 180whr to 5kwhr, that can provide an average farm or household with electricity backup between 5 to 24 hours daily to reduce reliance on fossil fuel. Our project addresses food security challenges through provision of clean energy and will offset over 100,000 tons of CO2; emissions in 5 years in contribution to Seeding The Future Foundation s Vision.
core_fields.abstract: PROBLEM From 2015 till date, agriculture and food processing account for 50% of the global Green House Gas (GHG) emissions & Nigeria accounts for 5% of global agricultural carbon emissions due to the fact that more than 80% of farmers are still using fossil fuels generators to power their farms. This has contributed to an increasing climatic change and food shortages. SOLUTION We design and build from scratch 4 varying capacities of portable solar generators ranging between 180whr to 5kwhr, the solar generators can provide an average farm or household with electricity backup between 5 to 24 hours daily in powering productive and income generating activities. We use the following 2 innovative methods: 1. We buy raw & new lithium-ion battery cells to build our solar generators. 2. Modular Lithium-ion Battery Design: By salvaging functional components, we disassemble degraded laptops and vacuum cleaners batteries, remove the useful cells and reboost using intense technology to build our products. This prevents the need to discard the entire batteries into the soil or water bodies. The bad cells are then transferred to battery recyclers approved by environmental agencies in Nigeria (e.g Hinckley). BENEFITS TO END-USERS In 5 years, our solution will: 1. Lower GHG emissions by 20%, thus, reduce the health and safety risks on 100,000 Nigerian farms associated to the use of fossil fuel generators by 100%. 2. Create Energy Independence for Nigerian farmers by reducing costs of high electricity bills by 70%, thus, reducing production costs, and lowering food prices.

core_fields.title: Bolivar County Good Food Revolution
core_fields.description: The Bolivar County Good Food Revolution aims to transform the local food system in the Mississippi Delta by increasing access to healthy, locally-grown produce. Through sustainable land use, youth development, and partnerships with local organizations, we seek to empower communities to achieve better health outcomes, economic opportunities, and food sovereignty. By investing in soil health, food education, and equitable distribution, we are fostering a culture of health and wellness for underserved BIPOC communities.
core_fields.abstract: The Mississippi Delta faces systemic challenges, including limited access to fresh produce, high rates of diet-related illnesses, and economic inequities. These issues disproportionately impact BIPOC communities, who have historically been excluded from sustainable food systems. The Bolivar County Good Food Revolution addresses these challenges by transforming soil health, supporting Black farmers, training youth in food systems, and building partnerships with health clinics and schools. This multi-faceted approach fosters equitable access to nutritious food and sustainable economic growth.

core_fields.title: Regenerating soil health and boosting food security for vulnerable women through sustainable legume farming in Ghana
core_fields.description: The project aims to empower vulnerable women farmers in the Daffiama-Bussie-Issa District, Upper West Region, Ghana by promoting conservation agriculture to regenerate soil health and boost legume yields (soybean, cowpea, groundnut). Through sustainable farming practices, the initiative will address low soil fertility, enhance food security, and improve livelihoods. By leveraging innovative techniques and community engagement, the project seeks to create a resilient agricultural system that supports both environmental sustainability and socio-economic empowerment.
core_fields.abstract: The district faces severe agricultural challenges, including low soil fertility, declining crop yields, and climate variability. Women, who make up 70 percent of the agricultural workforce, are particularly vulnerable due to limited access to resources, extension services, and sustainable farming practices. These challenges have contributed to persistent food insecurity and poverty, with over 64 percent of households in the region living below the poverty line. The project will target four communities namely Tabiase, Pulbaa, Duang, and Daffiama. These areas were selected due to their significant issues with low yields, pest and disease challenges, and the concentration of vulnerable women in need of support. Conservation agriculture practices such as minimum tillage, crop rotation, and organic soil amendments will be introduced to address these challenges. These techniques restore soil health, improve water retention, and enhance nutrient availability, directly tackling the region's declining soil fertility. Scientific insights, including evidence that conservation agriculture can improve yields by 20-50 percent in degraded soils while reducing greenhouse gas emissions, underpin the solution. Additionally, soil health testing and tailored agronomic advice will empower farmers with evidence-based strategies to increase productivity sustainably. Immediate benefits include increased yields and incomes for women farmers, improved food security, and strengthened community resilience. Long-term benefits include sustainable soil management, reduced land degradation, and greater adaptation to climate change. By empowering women in these communities, the project fosters socio-economic equity while contributing to a healthier environment and more resilient food systems.

core_fields.title: Promoting the production and conservation of red-necked Pennisetum purpureum to positively transform Food Systems in the Sahel
core_fields.description: Our project aims to promote and popularize the cultivation of Pennisetum purpureum (Maralfalfa) and its processing to satisfy the high demand for fodder and to increase milk production, which is used in many household diets, especially during the dry season, and slow down soil degradation and the loss of biodiversity in Diffa. Maralfalfa, also known as the miracle herb , is a little-known plant in Niger that represents a real agro-ecological solution in the Sahel.
core_fields.abstract: Over 3/4 of Niger's population are agro-pastoralists. In the Diffa region, this proportion reaches 95%. The main problem is the shortage of quality fodder and milk, especially during the dry season, and the ongoing degradation of grazing areas. This situation affects livestock, dairy and agricultural production, and plunges communities into vulnerability. Many households are forced to sell off their livestock in order to keep a number they can feed during the lean season. Miracle grass is a real solution to this problem. Popularizing and conserving this plant throughout the Sahel, and building the capacities of agropastoralists in the production and cutting and silaging of this grass will enable three main results to be achieved: a) Improved fodder production and processing (Quantity & Quality); b) Soil stabilization, ecological restoration of grazing areas; c) Improved production (milk & meat) and milk processing. Maralfalfa is a fast-growing grass, resistant in arid zones, rich in livestock feed and a natural solution for preserving biodiversity and restoring degraded soils. Young people and women will be able to increase their incomes through press-cutting and the sale of this grass, which represents a real economic opportunity. In addition, the availability of milk in the hot dry season will increase the income of women milk processors, whose activity remains continuous throughout the year, as well as fatteners and farmers through agroecology.

core_fields.title: Empowering Communities through Sustainable Agriculture and Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Africa
core_fields.description: This project integrates sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient technologies, such as Deep Winter Greenhouses, to improve food security and nutrition in Colorado and Africa during the rainy season. By empowering women and youth with training, tools, and resources, the initiative fosters economic growth, reduces poverty, and builds resilient food systems. It focuses on producing affordable, nutritious food sustainably while creating scalable models to address food insecurity in both climate-vulnerable and resource-constrained regions.
core_fields.abstract: Description of the Problem and Its Solution Problem: Food insecurity and malnutrition are critical challenges in Colorado and Africa, particularly in climate-vulnerable and conflict-affected regions. In Colorado, harsh winters limit agricultural productivity, while in Africa, seasonal rains lead to inconsistent food supply, soil degradation, and unsustainable farming practices. These issues disproportionately affect women, youth, and marginalized communities, exacerbating poverty and reducing access to affordable, nutritious food. Solution: The Diar Foundation addresses these challenges through an innovative integration of Deep Winter Greenhouses (DWGs) and sustainable farming practices to create year-round food production systems. DWGs utilize passive solar heating and thermal mass to enable sustainable food production during Colorado's harsh winters. In Africa, the Foundation employs rainwater harvesting, organic farming, and agroecological practices to optimize agricultural output during the rainy season while preserving soil health. Scientific and Technical Insights: DWGs harness solar energy to minimize energy use, while rain-fed agroecology in Africa addresses water scarcity and land degradation. By combining these approaches, the Diar Foundation ensures a steady food supply, reduces reliance on imported produce, and promotes local resilience to climate change. Benefits: Consumers: Access to affordable, nutritious, and locally produced food. Farmers and Producers: Training, improved yields, and increased income. Communities and Schools: Strengthened food security and educational opportunities through agricultural programs. Environment: Reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved soil health, and sustainable water use. The Diar Foundation s innovation empowers communities, fosters economic growth, and creates scalable solutions for sustainable agriculture globally.

core_fields.title: SUPPLY CHAIN OPTIMIZATION
core_fields.description: We provide tools and services that provides input for agrifood businesses and take their output to the next level desired stakeholder in the value chain, while ensuring transparency and traceability of all activities. For example, we will provide a farmer with tools to succeed in their production while providing them with market to sell to, all of this being done under a traceable ecosystem.
core_fields.abstract: The first product is a business management software for food and agricultural companies with in-built traceability features to manage inventory, sales, procurement, e-sales etc. The second product is an B2B platform for businesses in the agroecosystems to work with each other and partner for success. With this platform, a processor can find warehousing and logistics partners, meet farmers to offtake their harvest, construction and maintenance companies for their facility development and management, meet other companies that their own products serve as input for e.g. distributors. We provide production, procurement and business intelligence support services for our direct clients across the value chain i.e. farmers, processors, distributors and consumers with a technological edge to ensure efficient output allocation and transparency. We are setting up hubs to work with farmers for quality control and practices standardization for supply chain access and post-harvest protocols, combined with prefinancing as part of our supply chain activities. Our proprietary core is built around the supply chain data-as-a-service product for real time supply chain risk management systems across nutrient profiling, inventory vigilance, raw material source reporting etc. We have profiled yam and paddy rice to various locations and can use our historical data to trace inventory. This also works as a business intelligence tool for product registration health certification.

core_fields.title: Dream Vault Innovation
core_fields.description: The Dream Vault parallels the Amazon Hub Locker by providing a box of high-quality fruits and vegetables available to neighborhood residents served by Dion's Chicago Dream. Each vault provides a year's worth of food security for up to 175 households within a 2-mile radius of the vault. Residents have an electronic code sent via SMS text/email that allows them to access the Dream Vault.
core_fields.abstract: Dion's Chicago Dream is revolutionizing food insecurity solutions through its innovative Dream Vault initiative. Inspired by the Amazon Hub Locker model, the Dream Vault is a food locker system strategically placed in local businesses in close proximity to food-insecure neighborhoods. Each vault offers high-quality fresh fruits and vegetables, providing food security for up to 175 households within a 2-mile radius. Access is seamless residents receive a personalized electronic code via SMS or email, ensuring convenience and dignity in accessing food. The Dream Vault is uniquely impactful because it bridges scientific principles with lived experiences. Rooted in behavioral science, the program emphasizes accessibility, frequency, and consistency factors critical to healthy eating habits. By collaborating with residents to design the program, it reflects their needs, prioritizing ease of use and trustworthiness. The immediate benefits are substantial. Residents gain dependable access to nutritious food, improving health outcomes and reducing the stress associated with food insecurity. Local producers benefit as the program sources from regional farms, fostering economic growth and strengthening food systems. The environment sees long-term advantages through reduced food waste and minimized carbon footprints, as the localized distribution cuts down on transportation emissions. This sustainable approach ensures food equity while revitalizing communities, making the Dream Vault a replicable model for addressing food insecurity nationwide. By centering science and community voices, Dion's Chicago Dream sets a new standard for innovation in hunger relief.

core_fields.title: AG DRIED TOMATO POWDER
core_fields.description: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project focuses on the production of high-quality, nutrient-dense tomato powder using sustainable, efficient processing methods. By harnessing local agricultural resources and leveraging innovative drying techniques, the project aims to reduce post-harvest loss, enhance food preservation, and provide a value-added product for both local and international markets. This initiative seeks to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, create job opportunities, and contribute to sustainable food systems while addressing global food security.
core_fields.abstract: The AG Dried Tomato Powder project addresses the significant issue of tomato post-harvest loss, which is a widespread problem in many agricultural regions, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. Tomatoes are highly perishable, and poor storage, transportation, and handling contribute to up to 50% of losses annually. This results in wasted resources, financial losses for farmers, and limited availability of nutritious food. The innovation provides a sustainable solution by turning fresh tomatoes into a long-lasting, nutrient-rich tomato powder. This method not only preserves the tomatoes but also adds value by creating a versatile product that can be used in cooking, food processing, and other industries. The drying process reduces water content, extending shelf life and making the product easier to store and transport. The solution is driven by a combination of sustainable farming practices and modern drying technology, which retains the tomatoes' flavor, nutritional content, and versatility. It offers a win-win for both consumers and farmers. For consumers, it provides an affordable and convenient option for accessing high-quality tomatoes year-round. For farmers, it opens new markets and increases their income by offering a value-added product that can be sold locally and internationally. The immediate benefits include reduced food waste, improved food security, and increased incomes for local farmers. Long-term, the initiative will contribute to sustainable agricultural practices, climate resilience, and greater access to affordable, nutritious food, helping improve the livelihoods of communities and creating positive environmental impacts.

Fish flour production plays a major role in food value addition. Flour availability, goes a long way to provide school going children with good food for the growth of brain to perform well in school, helps to have health communities and source of income to women groups whilst protecting environment.

core_fields.title: ARVUM I - Indoor Plant Factory Pilot
core_fields.description: AGRA is looking to construct a pilot of its indoor Plant Factory technology that is unique in its ability to sustainably grow crops at the same price as traditional methods. AGRA s Plant Factories grow without sun or soil, using artificial light and a nutrient rich mist, powered by renewable energy. The pilot will validate the technology at scale, paving the way for private investment, offtake from supermarkets and commercialisation.
core_fields.abstract: Crops are responsible for 11% annual GHG emissions, 30% of global water withdrawals, deforestation, habitat destruction, species extinction, land degradation, water contamination and eutrophication. Farming as a profession is in decline (11% between 2006 and 2011 in Australia), crop yields are expected to decline by 10-20% by 2050 while our production needs to increase by 70%. Farmers face uncharacteristically high instances of mental health issues and suicide (tied to a rural job ruled by the weather) with the FAO reporting Agriculture as one of the most hazardous jobs worldwide. If we do nothing, we will face challenges in feeding the population while doing untold damage to our world. Plant Factories are unique in that they can address all of these problems in one solution, something well established in industry and academia. However, they are historically expensive to build and operate. If the sustainable option remains expensive, we will never be able to solve agricultures challenges. Looking at the underlying costs, this doesn't have to be the case, its just extremely challenging to achieve and thus requires the efforts of a company with a strong ideological motive. Through several years of rigorous R&D, AGRA have developed Plant Factory technology that, for the first time, can produce crops at price parity with the field. Able to grow consistently year-round independent of climate or weather, using 70% less N2O & CO2, 90% less water, 84-168x yield/m2, no pesticides/herbicides, 40% longer shelf-life, higher quality produce, located near urban centers and powered by renewable energy.

core_fields.title: Cold Chain as a service (CaaS) for Rural farmers in Offgrid Communities
core_fields.description: Our solution takes off the burden of acquiring cold chain infrastructure by small holder farmers which is quite expensive, and in turn provides Cooling as a Service (CaaS) with a pay as you go model to rural small holder farmers who cannot afford the upfront cost of a reefer, but yet get to enjoy cooling service for their farm produce. We provide cold storage assets at the farmgate and coldrom trucks for distribution too.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: 200 words KIPITFRESH addresses lack of access energy access for productive uses in off-grid rural farming communities; lack of access to sustainable cooling; and prevalence of post harvest losses with fruits and vegetables. Post harvest losses is more prevalent with fresh fruits and vegetables which have low shelf live and are highly perishable. Over 50% of fresh fruits and vegetables(FFV's) end up wasted in Nigeria due to lack of adequate cold storage facilities. In Nigeria alone, farmers lose over 9 billion dollars annually from post harvest losses. These losses play a critical role in influencing the life of millions of smallholder farmers by impacting the available food volumes and trade-in values of the commodities. Post Harvest losses results in increased carbon emissions with negative impacts on the environment. A report by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) using the life cycle perspective, estimated about 3.3 Gtonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions due to food waste, aside from land use changes. Furthermore, Postharvest losses reduces income of smallholder farmers, as harvested produce has to be sold at unfavorable prices due to lack of cold storage. Solution: KIPITFRESH provides cold storage and distribution services to small holder farmers located in underserved communities with no access to grid connection, to help reduce post-harvest loss in Nigeria s fruits and vegetable sector. KIPITFRESH is a mobile cold chain solution comprising solar powered mobile reefers for storage, and hybrid cold trucks for long long haul distribution from farmgate to the final offtaker.

core_fields.abstract: The Democratic Republic of Congo faces significant challenges related to poverty and food insecurity, particularly in rural communities where many depend on subsistence farming. The Alphome Community Farms initiative addresses these pressing issues by implementing community agribusiness activities aimed at empowering socioeconomically disadvantaged groups, including widows, women, orphans, and youths. Through best practices training workshops and the provision of agricultural inputs, this program seeks to enhance the productivity and sustainability of small-scale farmers. This innovative approach is relevant as it not only tackles immediate food shortages but also fosters long-term economic resilience within vulnerable populations. By equipping farmers with essential skills and resources, Alphome Community Farms facilitates increased crop yields and diversification of produce. This not only alleviates hunger but also generates income for families, thereby reducing poverty levels. The scientific insight underlying this solution stems from agricultural research that emphasizes sustainable practices such as crop rotation, organic farming techniques, and integrated pest management. These methods promote soil health while minimizing environmental impact. The immediate benefits include improved food security for families and communities; sustainably cultivated crops contribute to local markets, enhancing economic stability. Ultimately, this initiative presents a holistic model for addressing food insecurity while empowering marginalized groups within society.

core_fields.title: Emattahu - Resilient Agriculture for Nutrition and Sustainability
core_fields.description: Emattahu empowers communities through sustainable agriculture and nutrition-focused solutions. By training 240 women in eco-friendly farming practices and improving school meals for 3,368 children, the project enhances food security and community resilience. Leveraging APOIAR's expertise in health, education, and community development, alongside specialized partners in agriculture and environment, it establishes a scalable model to combat food insecurity, support local economies, and promote environmental sustainability across Mozambique.
core_fields.abstract: In Niassa, communities face persistent food insecurity (UNOCHA, 2024) and low agricultural productivity due to traditional farming practices, climate vulnerabilities, and limited access to resources, as highlighted by Matavel et al. (2019) and confirmed through APOIAR s fieldwork. These challenges entrench cycles of poverty, malnutrition, and environmental degradation, undermining community resilience and sustainable development. Reliance on water-intensive crops, limited access to climate-resilient farming techniques, and unsustainable practices worsen soil exhaustion, water scarcity, and biodiversity loss. Inadequate food preservation and seed-saving knowledge further expose communities to seasonal shortages and malnutrition, disproportionately affecting children, pregnant women, and new mothers. APOIAR presents an innovative approach to fostering sustainable agriculture and food security leveraging science, traditional knowledge, and community engagement. Our solution addresses root causes of food insecurity by promoting climate-resilient practices, enhancing local food system nutrition, and integrating sustainable resource management. This includes supporting communities to transition to drought-resistant crops, intercropping to improve soil health and biodiversity, and adopting seed preservation and food conservation techniques for year-round nutritious solutions. Grounded in a comprehensive understanding of environmental, social, and economic dynamics, our solution empowers communities with the tools, knowledge, and support to transform local food systems into innovative, resilient, and nutritionally robust frameworks. This strategy fosters long-term self-sufficiency, ensuring profound and sustainable impact. Emattahu benefits: Farmers and families: increased yields, improved nutrition, and new income opportunities. Children, pregnant women, and new mothers: access to nutrient-dense foods supporting maternal and child health. Environment: reduced soil degradation, biodiversity preservation, and optimized water use.

core_fields.title: Regenerative Agriculture in Oil palm production
core_fields.description: AQUA-OSUK Enterprises Limited is an agribusiness from Nigeria in Oil Palm Production. We are promoting Regenerative Agriculture in oil palm production to reverse deforestation and biodiversity loss caused by monoculture cultivation of oil palm. We are unique because we integrate regenerative agriculture in oil palm production via waste management, oil palm agroforestry system, and Fertilizer Drawn Forward Osmosis (FDFO). Collectively, they promote a circular economy in oil palm production.
core_fields.abstract: The African oil palm is a crop used to produce palm oil and palm oil is mainly used for cooking, production of cosmetic products, and as a source of renewable energy (palm oil biofuel). We promote regenerative agriculture in oil palm production via a. Waste Management: We sell oil palm seedlings to oil palm farmers in Nigeria. We integrated waste management into our production by collecting used plastic water sachets and reusing them as polythene pots for the seedlings and we also collect oil palm ash from oil palm mills and reuse them as organic fertilizers for the seedlings. We have been able to reduce the indiscriminate dumping of plastic and agricultural waste. Integrating waste management into our seedling production has reduced our operating costs and enabled us to sell high-yielding seedlings at a price below the market price giving us a competitive advantage. b. Oil palm Agroforestry: This system has been shown to reverse deforestation and biodiversity loss. With our affiliation with the American University in Cairo (AUC), we conducted a study on how the use of oil palm ash and brackish water can enable oil palm farmers to transition from the monoculture system to the agroforestry system. We also intend to build the first oil palm agroforestry system in Nigeria as a pilot project for its adoption by smallholder farmers in Nigeria.

core_fields.title: Tilapia mass production as a supplement for the protein consumption among the populace
core_fields.description: The project seeks to establish fish farms in three key locations, using the ponds to train local fish farmers on sustainable tilapia production. It aims to empower farmers to diversify into tilapia farming, providing a nutritious food source for the public and a profitable income stream. Through training, the project will equip farmers with the skills needed to produce tilapia sustainably, supporting national food security while improving the livelihoods of farming communities.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation and Its Benefits: The innovation is the introduction of **sustainable tilapia farming** in Nigeria s fishery sector, specifically aimed at empowering local fish farmers to diversify their production. Traditionally, many Nigerian fish farmers rely heavily on other species like catfish, which often face supply and demand challenges. Tilapia farming offers a solution to these issues, providing a highly nutritious, fast-growing fish that meets the increasing demand for affordable, protein-rich food while offering farmers an additional, profitable income stream. Problem Being Solved: The project addresses the challenges of over-reliance on a limited range of fish species, inconsistent fish supply, and limited access to sustainable farming techniques. Additionally, it combats the lack of training and resources for farmers to transition to more sustainable, profitable farming practices. How the Problem Is Being Solved: The project establishes fish farms in key locations to serve as training hubs. Farmers will learn sustainable tilapia farming techniques, including efficient feeding practices, water management, and disease prevention. By adopting these practices, farmers can improve yields and profitability while reducing environmental impact. Scientific and Technical Insight: Research into tilapia farming reveals its potential as a sustainable and low-maintenance fish species. Tilapia can thrive in diverse environments and grow quickly, making it ideal for small- to medium-scale farmers. Benefits: This innovation delivers immediate benefits such as increased farmer income, food security through affordable fish production, and community empowerment. Long-term, it promotes environmental sustainability, reduces overfishing pressure, and supports local economies.

core_fields.title: Abisal Foods
core_fields.description: Abisal Foods is Nigeria based innovative agricultural company transforming local crops into nutritious food products for local and global markets. We empower youth, women, and persons with disabilities through technology-driven farming, training, and SME support. By partnering with women-led contract farmers, we ensure traceable, sustainable supply chains while producing products like G-Corn Millet, Vitamin A Maize Flour, and Plantain Flour. Our mission is to foster inclusive growth and enhance food security through sustainable agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: Abisal Foods addresses core issues faced by Nigerian population on food insecurity, unemployment, and supply chain inefficiencies through an innovative approach to agriculture. By leveraging technology-driven solutions like irrigation, hydroponics, and precision farming, we enable consistent, high-quality crop production, even in challenging conditions. This approach empowers youth, women, and persons with disabilities, providing them with skills, resources, and income opportunities. Our model integrates women-led farmers into the value chain, fostering traceability and sustainability. These farmers cultivate proprietary seeds supplied by Abisal Foods for crops like millet, maize, and plantain to process them into nutritious products such as Vitamin A Maize Flour and G-Corn Millet. This ensures steady demand for farmers, reduces post-harvest losses, and creates nutritious food options for consumers. The solution arose from the need for more inclusive agricultural practices and healthier food products. We ve combined scientific insights into crop fortification with practical, technology-driven farming techniques to achieve these goals. The benefits are extensive: farmers gain stable income and support, communities access affordable, nutritious food, and schools benefit from healthier meal options for students. Consumers enjoy high-quality, locally-sourced products, while society sees reduced unemployment and enhanced food security. Environmental benefits include more efficient land use and reduced waste through sustainable farming methods. In summary, Abisal Foods is creating a transformative impact by connecting agriculture, technology, and inclusivity, benefiting individuals and communities while fostering a resilient and sustainable food system.

core_fields.title: Nourish Ebonyi: Empowering Communities with Sustainable Farming and Nutritious Food Choices
core_fields.description: Nourish Ebonyi" aims to empower rural communities in Ebonyi State by promoting sustainable farming practices and enhancing access to nutritious food. The project focuses on educating farmers and community members about sustainable agricultural techniques, improving food security, and fostering healthier eating habits. By combining education with practical farming solutions, the initiative will support long-term community well-being and contribute to the development of a more resilient and self-sufficient rural economy
core_fields.abstract: "Nourish Ebonyi" addresses the pressing challenges of poor nutrition and unsustainable farming practices in rural Ebonyi State. Many communities in this region suffer from limited access to nutritious food and depend on traditional farming methods that degrade the environment. This project offers a solution by introducing sustainable farming techniques, such as agroecology, crop diversification, and organic farming, alongside education on nutritious food choices. The innovation lies in the integration of sustainable farming with community education to empower farmers to adopt practices that preserve the environment, improve crop yields, and increase access to nutritious, locally grown food. By using organic farming methods, farmers can reduce dependency on harmful chemicals, enhance soil fertility, and grow more diverse, nutrient-rich crops. Additionally, the project will provide education on healthy eating habits, particularly focusing on the nutritional needs of children and vulnerable groups. The solution is relevant because it addresses both environmental sustainability and food security. By educating farmers and communities on sustainable agricultural practices, the project tackles soil degradation, water scarcity, and food insecurity. The immediate benefits include increased food production, improved health outcomes due to better nutrition, and greater economic stability for farmers through diversified income streams. In the long term, the project will foster self-reliant, resilient communities with sustainable farming practices, contributing to healthier families, stronger local economies, and a healthier environment.

core_fields.title: Eliminating Aflatoxin from Haiti's Peanut Supply Chain
core_fields.description: Acceso is tackling aflatoxin contamination in peanut supply chains in Haiti using an innovative and integrated system that incentivizes farmers and buyers. Farmers receive financing and guaranteed purchase agreements, while buyers enjoy stable prices and customized delivery schedules. Acceso connects farmers and buyers and deploys on-site quality control, traceability, and warehousing. Without Acceso’s innovation, aflatoxin management in developing countries like Haiti is nearly impossible.

core_fields.title: Turning waste into food (WIF): Integrated Multi-Trophic Farm (IMTF) in a circular economy
core_fields.description: Fish and poultry have the potential to improve the nutrition and income of the population and also contribute to the health of the environment. However, capture fisheries has passed its peak and the costs of the feed for aquaculture and poultry have skyrocketed. The growth and sustainability are dependent upon looking for alternative sustainable ingredients to the commercial feeds. This project will realize the potential of Microalgae and Black Soldier Fly Larvae as feed ingredients.
core_fields.abstract: The future growth and sustainability of aquaculture and poultry is dependent upon the industry stepping away from its reliance upon animals as major feed ingredients. Microalgae have the highest areal biomass productivities among photosynthetic organisms and microalgal production has a low water and arable-land footprint, making microalgal-based feed environmentally sustainable and climate resilient. Several compounds in algae have confounding effects, providing a source of protein, amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins and minerals. Similarly, Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL) are rich in protein, fats, and oil with added environmental advantage requiring less land and water; lower greenhouse gas emissions; transforming low-value organic by-products into high-quality food or feed. BSFL are also efficient bio-converters that can be mass-reared on low input resources. They are also used in the production of compost that can reduce the rather expensive cost of inorganic fertilizers. Therefore, the project will conduct experiments showcasing the safe and effective benefits that microalgal and BSFL products (fresh, dry, proteins, lipids, fertilizers) have for fish and poultry growth. The project will also train Microalgae/BSFL farmers/entrepreneurs to enable them to incorporate these products into the feeding regimen of their fish and poultry farms. Finally, the ultimate aim is to reach the goal of using microalgal and BSFL products by farmers to reduce the quantity of conventional feed used in producing fish and poultry and, in turn, reduce the cost of production and become environmentally friendly. Ultimately, this should lead producers to acquiring improved economic status, nutritional quality and resilience to climate change.

core_fields.title: Beles (Cactus pear): A Key to Sustainable Food and Nutrition Security in Tigray
core_fields.description: The Beles (Cactus Pear) project promotes sustainable food and nutrition security through cultivation of the drought-resistant cactus pear. Cactus pear is climate-resilient crop that can help combat food scarcity and provide nutrient-rich fruits for local communities in the drier areas. By fostering sustainable farming practices, the project aims to enhance livelihoods, conserve water, and contribute to environmental sustainability, offering a viable solution for arid and semi-arid regions.
core_fields.abstract: The Cactus Pear (Beles) cultivation project introduces an innovative approach to food security by leveraging the unique properties of this drought-tolerant plant. The primary problem it addresses is food and nutrition insecurity in Tigray region, where traditional crops fail due to water scarcity and poor soil quality. This is particularly relevant as climate change exacerbates these conditions, threatening global food systems and livelihoods. The project solves this issue by promoting the cultivation of cactus pear, a low-input crop that thrives in harsh climates. Its fruits are rich in essential nutrients, while its pads (cladodes) serve as livestock feed, ensuring dual benefits. The plant s ability to conserve water and prevent soil erosion enhances environmental sustainability. The scientific insight behind this solution lies in the cactus pear s unique physiology, which enables efficient water use and resilience to extreme weather. Research has demonstrated its potential to improve food production and diversify agricultural systems in water-stressed regions. Immediate benefits include increased access to nutritious food for communities and cost savings for farmers due to low water and fertilizer requirements. Long-term, sustainable benefits include enhanced soil health, reduced environmental degradation, and strengthened resilience against climate change. The project supports farmers, schools, and communities by providing training, resources, and market opportunities, creating livelihoods and improving societal well-being. By integrating this sustainable innovation, the project offers a scalable solution to global food challenges.

core_fields.title: Roots of Resilience
core_fields.description: The Roots of Resilience program transforms Tanzanian agriculture by training youth in regenerative farming practices. Through a Train the Trainer model, the initiative empowers 25 master trainers to integrate indigenous knowledge with modern regenerative agriculture techniques, using a mobile Future-Farm bus. The program restores soil health, promotes food security, and creates economic opportunities while preserving cultural heritage. It integrates hands-on farm training, research, and digital tools to ensure accessibility, job creation, and community empowerment.
core_fields.abstract: Problem Being Solved: Tanzania faces critical agricultural challenges, including food insecurity, climate change impacts, and soil degradation. Over-reliance on chemical fertilisers and pesticides has compromised soil health, increased climate vulnerability, and created dependency on unstable supply chains. This situation threatens long-term agricultural productivity, public health, and rural economic resilience. Solution Approach: The solution is a comprehensive regenerative agriculture education program that: - Trains youth as agricultural transformation leaders - Integrates indigenous knowledge with modern sustainable practices - Reduces chemical (farm input) dependencies - Promotes soil regeneration and biodiversity - Creates economic opportunities in rural communities - Develops resilient, local food systems By training 25 master trainers who will subsequently train hundreds of farmers, the project addresses multiple interconnected challenges: environmental degradation, food insecurity, economic instability, and limited agricultural innovation. The approach empowers communities with knowledge, practical skills, and a sustainable pathway to agricultural transformation. Scientific/Technical Insights: - Experiential learning methodology - Permaculture and agroforestry principles - Indigenous agricultural knowledge - Health and medicinal value of plants for humans - Digital technology integration - Data-driven monitoring Benefits: Farmers gain reduced farming input costs, improved soil health, and increased crop diversity and food security. The environment benefits from reduces emissions, soil restoration, biodiversity preservation, and carbon sequestration. Communities experience agriculture all job creation, youth empowerment, improved public health through chemical-free farming and economic resilience. By creating a holistic, replicable approach, the Roots of Resilience program transforms agricultural education while simultaneously addressing environmental, economic, and social challenges through regenerative farming practices.
