core_fields.title: Farm-In-A-Tank (Pilot Stage)
core_fields.description: AARC is a pioneering agribusiness concern, developing a commercial smallholder aquaculture-value-chain. At this Pilot Stage: we shall establish a 'Smallholder Outgrower Scheme' with 100 farmers, equip them with a Farm-In-A-Tank (FIAT) a high-yielding fish-tank, provide inputs and extension services. As the sole off-taker, AARC will buy, process and sell the fish.. The goal is to ascertain the economic, social and financial viability of the business model and position the project for scaling.
core_fields.abstract: Problem Statement: Notably, one-third of the worlds droughts occur in sub-Saharan Africa. Considering that smallholder farmers contribute over 80% of food supplies, and over 90% of agriculture is rain-fed, the impact of climate change is deeper and longer lasting in Sub-Saharan Africa than any other continent in terms of food production, livelihoods, health and water security driving more people into multi-dimensional poverty. Currently 60% of the continent s population is experiencing food insecurity with rate of malnutrition at 47% in some regions . Against this backdrop, AARC identified commercialisation of smallholder aquaculture as the agricultural value-chain with the most potential to accelerate the production of high-protein food at scale, raise incomes for smallholder farmers, create jobs especially for women and youth, while improving their climate adaptability and resilience. Our Solution combines (3) strategic pro-poor interventions that address the issues that deter smallholders from participating in commercial aquaculture: a) Technology Innovation: We have developed a cost-effective, high-yielding, semi-intensive fish-tank (FIAT)- that intensifies smallholder yields from 200Kg/year [using earthen ponds], to commercial level of 2,000 Kg/year. b) Inclusive Business Model: To scale production, we have adopted the Smallholder Outgrower Model- where AARC provides each outgrower (60% women) a FIAT, inputs and extension services- -purchases the fish, processes and sells providing outgrowers a reliable monthly income. c) Credit Line: AARC provides the FIAT on lease and inputs on credit hence outgrowers can focus on fattening the fish to market size without worrying about costs the key deterrent to commercial aquaculture.

core_fields.title: Empowering Nigerian Soybean Farmers: Training Cooperatives for Sustainable Farming, Value Addition, and Market Access
core_fields.description: Our project aims to train Nigerian soybean farmers' cooperatives on sustainable farming techniques, value addition, and market strategies to boost production and income. With Nigeria producing 1.35 million metric tons of soybeans annually and demand exceeding supply by 20%, the initiative will enhance yields, reduce post-harvest losses, and create value-added products, such as soybean oil and flour. By linking farmers to profitable markets, the project promotes food security, rural development, and economic empowerment.
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria's soybean industry faces significant challenges, including low yields, post-harvest losses, and limited market access, despite a growing demand for soybean products driven by the food and feed industries. Current production of 1.35 million metric tons annually falls short of domestic demand by 20%, creating missed economic opportunities for farmers and food insecurity for the population. The problem is compounded by inadequate knowledge of modern farming techniques, lack of value addition, and poor market integration. Our solution is to train soybean farmers cooperatives on sustainable farming practices, value addition, and market strategies. The training will introduce innovative techniques, such as soil nutrient management, pest control using environmentally friendly methods, and precision farming technologies. Value addition will focus on transforming raw soybeans into high-demand products, including soybean oil, flour, and animal feed, reducing post-harvest losses and increasing profitability. Farmers will also be equipped with marketing strategies to connect with reliable buyers, cooperatives, and regional trade platforms. The innovation leverages insights from agricultural best practices and value chain development studies, demonstrating that education and technical support significantly enhance yields and income. By applying this model, immediate benefits include increased production, reduced waste, and improved farmer incomes. Long-term benefits include enhanced food security, rural economic growth, reduced reliance on imports, and environmental sustainability through eco-friendly farming practices. Consumers gain access to affordable, nutritious products, while society benefits from strengthened local economies and reduced environmental impact.

core_fields.title: Innovative Liquid bio-fertilizers from Black Soldier Fly Larvae: A Sustainable Solution for Agriculture in Kenya
core_fields.description: We rear Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae and transform them into organic liquid fertilizers, addressing the inefficiency and unprofitability of selling larvae as animal feed. This innovation will increase BSF farmers' income tenfold while reducing biofertilizer costs for organic farmers by two-thirds. Enriched with nutrients and chitin, our fertilizers enhance plant resistance, reduce organic waste, and provide a sustainable, locally sourced alternative to imports, supporting environmental and economic sustainability for Kenyan farmers.
core_fields.abstract: We rear Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae commercially, producing over 1 ton of larvae monthly. Currently, we sell the larvae as animal feed protein, but this is unprofitable(and is the case for BSF farms of all sizes) due to a poor feed conversion ratio of 1:20 requiring 20 kg of organic waste to produce just 1 kg of dried larvae, with 70 80% of the mass lost during drying. This inefficiency makes BSF farming financially unsustainable despite its potential. Recognizing a growing demand among Kenyan farmers for organic liquid biofertilizers most of which are imported we shifted our focus to producing fertilizers directly from BSF larvae. This pivot was driven by the unexpected popularity of frass, a solid organic fertilizer and a byproduct of BSF farming, of which we have sold nearly 20 tonnes. Transforming BSF larvae into liquid fertilizers will increase our income tenfold compared to selling them as feed. These nutrient-rich fertilizers, containing bioactive compounds like chitin, enhance plant resistance to pests and diseases, offering benefits beyond conventional options. They also reduce biofertilizer costs for organic farmers by two-thirds, providing an affordable, locally produced alternative to imports. Additionally, this approach enables an out-grower model, where small-scale farmers supply larvae, increasing their profitability and promoting sustainable livelihoods. This innovation addresses two critical challenges: reducing organic waste and improving access to high-quality agricultural inputs. By repurposing BSF larvae into liquid fertilizers, we aim to support Kenyan farmers in boosting productivity, promoting environmental and economic sustainability, and creating a scalable, profitable model for BSF farming.

core_fields.title: Empowering Mukta Haliyas and Nourishing Lives by upgrading the value chain of Turmeric: The Nutritional Powerhouse
core_fields.description: This project empowers Mukta Haliyas (a marginalized community of freed people in Nepal) in Far-Western region of Nepal by developing a sustainable turmeric value chain. We engage Mukta Haliya farmers in organic turmeric cultivation, while a multidisciplinary team conducts research and develops innovative products, including culinary delights, health supplements, and beauty care items. We establish robust domestic and international markets, ensuring fair returns for farmers and promoting the nutritional power of turmeric globally.
core_fields.abstract: This project aims to innovate by creating a comprehensive and sustainable value chain for turmeric, specifically focusing on empowering Mukta Haliya communities in the Far-Western Region of Nepal. Recognizing the challenges faced by this marginalized community, including limited economic opportunities and social exclusion, this project aims to provide sustainable livelihoods for Mukta Haliya farmers while contributing to improved nutrition and health outcomes due to increased access to and consumption of turmeric-based products. To achieve this, we will empower farmers by directly engaging Mukta Haliya communities in organic turmeric cultivation, providing them with training, technical support, and access to fair markets. We have identified turmeric genotypes that exhibit high yields at low cost and are also suitable for high-value essential oil extraction. We will cultivate these specific genotypes in Kailali and Dadeldhura districts, respectively. Furthermore, we will establish a robust value chain by: collaborating with experts from diverse fields (agriculture, biotechnology, food science, engineering, and ayurveda) to develop a range of high-value turmeric products, including culinary delights, medicinal supplements, and cosmetic items; and building strong domestic and international markets through partnerships with retailers, distributors, and exporters. The immediate and sustainable benefits of this project include increased income and improved livelihoods for Mukta Haliya farmers, enhanced social inclusion, economic development within the communities, job creation, improved community health, and access to high-quality, ethically sourced turmeric products for consumers.

core_fields.title: YIBIBOA: Empowering Women Through Waste Management and Improving Food Security
core_fields.description: The project tasks itself with providing women in identified households specifically designed containers for collecting their organic waste and set up a system for collecting filled containers. These waste materials will be converted into organic fertilizer using Black Soldier Fly technology. 10% portion of the fertilizer will then be given to the women along with seeds accompanied with best practice training for their backyard gardens.
core_fields.abstract: Rural areas often grapple with the consequences of inadequate waste management systems. The absence of regular waste collection services leads to widespread improper waste disposal, resulting in severe environmental degradation. This crisis has far-reaching implications for public health, with a direct link to the prevalence of diseases like malaria and dysentery, which disproportionately affect young Africans. Additionally, this contributes to the emission of tons of Greenhouse Gases (GHG), dealing a negative blow to our planet. Moreover, the economic burden of poor waste management is compounded by limited access to fresh food products and increased cost of production, contributing to escalating malnutrition and food insecurity rates in these communities. With a structured system, we are able to channel the waste being generated in these communities to a central facility where the black soldier fly is used to transform the waste into organic fertilizer, with the larvae as byproduct, enriched in amino acids that can be used for animal and pet feed. Subsequently, 10% of the fertilizer produced is given out to women to set up backyard vegetable gardens, thus augmenting their household nutrition. With this technology we are able to produce organic fertilizer that not only improves soil health and combats the effects of nutrient depletion but also reduces the amount of methane and CO2 being released into the environment.

core_fields.title: Resilient Ecosystems and Sustainable Inclusion for Socioeconomic Transformation (RESIST)
core_fields.description: The RESIST project aims to enhance community resilience in Katakwi District through climate-smart agriculture, sustainable livelihoods, and inclusive socioeconomic initiatives. Over three years, it will promote ecosystem restoration, empower marginalized groups, and strengthen local capacities to adapt to climate change. By fostering collaboration and innovation, RESIST will drive sustainable development, reduce poverty, and build a climate-resilient future for the community.
core_fields.abstract: The project will introduce an innovative, community-driven approach to address the pressing challenges of climate vulnerability, environmental degradation, and socioeconomic exclusion in Katakwi District. katakwi faces erratic weather patterns, reduced agricultural productivity, and limited opportunities for marginalized groups such as youth, women, and persons with disabilities. These challenges threaten livelihoods, food security, and community resilience. RESIST will integrate climate-smart agriculture, ecosystem restoration, and inclusive economic empowerment. Climate-resilient crop varieties, agroforestry systems, and water conservation techniques are employed to enhance productivity and restore degraded lands. Digital inclusion and vocational training equip marginalized groups with skills for alternative livelihoods. Community groups and schools participate in environmental education, fostering long-term stewardship. This solution is rooted in insights from successful community-based adaptation models and technical evidence supporting agroecological practices. For example, agroforestry systems can improve yields by up to 50% in degraded areas (FAO, 2020), while climate-resilient crops can increase food security for vulnerable populations. Immediate Benefits: Increased incomes for farmers, improved food security, and enhanced knowledge of sustainable practices. Sustainable Benefits: Restored ecosystems, stronger climate resilience, and reduced poverty and inequality across communities. RESIST will ensure a scalable and replicable model for building resilient communities and ecosystems in climate-vulnerable regions.

core_fields.title: Young City Farmers Initiative.
core_fields.description: Agrisiti Nig Ltd, through YCFI establishes solar-powered, IoT-enabled school farms across Nigeria. These innovative smart farms provide students with hands-on training in sustainable, high-tech agriculture, transforming schools into hubs for modern food production. Our approach further aims to use the projects and school farms to nurture skilled, eco-conscious leaders ready to drive positive change, tackle youth unemployment and food insecurity, while strengthening local food production, and enhancing community nutrition.
core_fields.abstract: Agrisiti Nig Limited, through its Young City Farmers Initiative (YCFI), addresses key challenges in Nigeria youth unemployment, food insecurity, and outdated agricultural practices. Currently, youth unemployment in Nigeria exceeds 33%, affecting over 90 million young people, while agriculture, a sector employing 37% of the population and contributing 22.35% to GDP, is largely seen by youth as labor-intensive and low-paying due to limited access to modern technology. Additionally, with food inflation at 41%, urban areas face restricted food supply and rural farmers struggle to meet national nutrition standards, leading to $300 million in economic losses annually due to malnutrition. Agrisiti s innovation introduces solar-powered, IoT-enabled smart school farms that engage students in hands-on, technologically advanced farming practices, transforming agriculture into a dynamic and attractive career choice. By this, students learn modern techniques that boost productivity and reduce traditional barriers to food production. This shift makes agriculture more accessible and appealing to youth, who gain valuable skills that increase their employability and productivity to impact their rural farming communities/parents. Benefits Immediate Impacts: For Students: Hands-on training in modern, efficient farming methods. For Communities: Improved access to fresh, nutritious food. For Schools: Integration of technology, sustainability into education and the development of crucial technical skills. Sustainable Impacts: For Youth: Enhanced employability and perception of agriculture as a profitable, high-tech career. For Communities: Stronger local food systems and reduced food insecurity. For Society: Environmentally sustainable food production and healthier communities. For the Economy: Reduction in malnutrition costs and promotion of long-term economic resilience.

core_fields.title: Empowering Small Farmers with Sustainable and Affordable Farm Mechanization Solutions
core_fields.description: Our project develops affordable, innovative farm machines tailored for small and marginal farmers. These gender-friendly, eco-efficient solutions enhance productivity, reduce resource use, and restore soil health. By addressing labor shortages and enabling sustainable practices, we empower farmers to improve their livelihoods, adapt to climate challenges, and produce nutritious crops. Focused on inclusivity, we support women farmers and tribal communities, driving economic growth and resilience in farming communities.
core_fields.abstract: Small and marginal farmers, constituting over 86% of India s farming population, face critical challenges including labor shortages, high costs of farming, and lack of access to efficient machinery. Soil degradation affects 30% of agricultural land, reducing productivity and resilience to climate change, while women and tribal farmers are disproportionately impacted by these challenges, limiting their economic opportunities. Our innovation addresses these issues by developing affordable, eco-friendly farm machines tailored for small-scale farming. Examples include mechanized seed drills, threshers, and solar-powered equipment, which enhance productivity by up to 40%, reduce manual labor by 60%, and lower farming costs significantly. Designed with gender-friendly features, these machines empower women farmers by providing lightweight, easy-to-use solutions. Leveraging insights into local farming challenges, our machines integrate precision farming techniques, cutting water usage by over 50% and reducing chemical input dependency. core_fields.title: Enset Cultivation, Development and Utilization in Ethiopia and Kenya - Determining the Impact of Enset on Food Security
core_fields.description: Due to the impacts of climate change, war, and the COVID-19 pandemic, food insecurity has become a dire issue worldwide, highlighting the need for innovative and diverse agricultural solutions that focus on localization and regional collaboration. Our research collaborative project focuses on developing climate-resilient and genetically diverse crops for marginalized and drought-prone regions in Kenya and Ethiopia needing food alternatives. Ensete ventricosum, commonly known as Enset, is a versatile and drought-tolerant crop that can be harvested year-round, withstanding temperature, altitudinal, and rainfall changes. Despite being used as a sustainable food source for approximately 20 million people in Southern Ethiopia, Enset’s potential is under-researched and it remains an underutilized food source. Our aims include: 1) determining the regional versatility of Enset through analysis of Kenyan and Ethiopian wild Enset strains; 2) analyze and compare domesticated Enset (currently only grown in Ethiopia) and wild Enset to understand how to scale its utilization as a food source; 3) develop advanced agricultural and scientific technologies to establish Enset as a food security crop.

core_fields.title: Enset Food Security Initiative
core_fields.description: The Enset Food Security Initiative enhances food security in Ethiopia and Kenya by promoting the cultivation of Enset, a drought-resistant crop. Our project focuses on improving agricultural practices, increasing access to this vital food source, and helping communities adapt to climate change. By empowering local farmers, particularly women, our initiative promotes sustainable agriculture, improves nutrition, and strengthens food systems in communities vulnerable to poverty, food insecurity, and climate-related challenges.
core_fields.abstract: In many parts of Ethiopia and Kenya, food insecurity is a pressing issue, worsened by climate change, which brings erratic rainfall and droughts. Traditional crops are becoming increasingly vulnerable, putting communities at risk of malnutrition and economic instability. Our Enset Food Security Initiative addresses this by promoting the cultivation of Enset, a drought-resistant crop native to Ethiopia. Enset is rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals, and it thrives in harsh climates and degraded soils, making it a resilient solution to climate extremes. The innovation behind this initiative is scaling up Enset cultivation and integrating it into local food systems. Combining traditional agricultural knowledge with modern techniques, we help farmers increase yields and improve processing methods, ensuring Enset becomes a sustainable food source. This solution is inspired by local agricultural practices but addresses the challenges communities face in expanding Enset cultivation due to limited resources and knowledge. Our Enset Food Security Initiative is grounded in four principles: regenerative agriculture, promoting biodiversity, empowering smallholder farmers, and introducing climate-smart crops. These principles are essential to positioning Enset as a sustainable, climate-resilient solution to food insecurity. Despite Africa contributing only four percent of global greenhouse gas emissions, the continent is experiencing climate change faster than anywhere else in the world, which is why our initiative focuses on helping communities adapt to these changes. Immediate benefits include improved food security, increased income, and greater community resilience. Over time, the initiative will foster sustainable agriculture, promote economic growth, and strengthen local food systems.

core_fields.title: Alnarps Agroecology Farm: a living lab & model farm for the future of our food systems
core_fields.description: The project seeks to develop a sustainable farm model by integrating market gardening, poultry, agroforestry, in CSA scheme. Serving as a living lab, it fosters innovation, research, and practice, to develop a resilient, replicable model for Scandinavia. As a community hub, it invites consumers to connect with their food, the land, and farmers, building stronger relationships and shared responsibility.
core_fields.abstract: Globally, conventional food systems face multiple crises simultaneously, not limited to global warming, soil degradation, energy crises, low profitability, changing customer awareness and geo-political instability. Policy makers, scientists and activists are urgently calling for novel food production methods to help address these challenges whilst guaranteeing food security, resilience, accessibility, improving dietary health and mitigating climate change. Alnarp s Agroecology Farm (AAF) employs bio intensive market gardening guided by agroecological principles, merging indigenous subsistence farming with modern horticultural methods to prioritize prolonged soil health and fertility. This approach balances nutrient extraction and recycling while fostering multifunctionality within the farm ecosystem, enhancing resilience and environmental sustainability. To ensure social and financial sustainability, AAF uses a Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) model, enabling customers to directly engage with local food production by financing upcoming seasons and sharing the harvest. CSA fosters community building, food security, and consumer awareness. Contrasting with conventional farming reliant on fossil fuels and synthetic inputs, AAF s methods address issues like soil depletion, biodiversity loss, and disconnection from the land. With modern farming contributing to environmental and social crises, viable alternatives like local vegetable production and agroforestry are critical. Agroforestry integrates trees and crops, offering benefits like improved biodiversity, carbon sequestration, soil health, and resilience. Combining CSA, market gardening, and agroforestry presents a model for circular economies that enhance food security and ecosystem services while addressing socio-economic and environmental challenges.

core_fields.title: "Ultrasonic Locust Repellent: A Sustainable Solution for Crop Protection and Food Security in Africa"
core_fields.description: The Ultrasonic Locust Repellent is an innovative, eco-friendly solution that uses ultrasonic frequencies to protect crops from locust infestations without harmful pesticides. Designed for affordability and scalability, it ensures increased agricultural productivity, reduced environmental pollution, and improved food security for vulnerable farming communities. Powered by solar energy, this technology offers a sustainable and cost-effective approach to combating locust invasions, fostering resilient agricultural systems across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Locust infestations are a major agricultural threat in Africa, devastating crops and causing food insecurity for millions. Existing solutions, such as chemical pesticides, pose health risks, harm the environment, and are costly for small-scale farmers. This challenge is particularly relevant as locust outbreaks continue to escalate due to climate change, endangering livelihoods and economic stability. The Ultrasonic Locust Repellent addresses this problem through an innovative, sustainable approach. It uses ultrasonic sound waves at specific frequencies to repel locusts without harming crops, humans, or the environment. Powered by solar energy, the device is cost-effective and suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Its automatic operation ensures continuous protection, reducing farmers labor and dependence on harmful chemicals. This solution is rooted in scientific studies demonstrating locust sensitivity to ultrasonic frequencies, combined with advancements in electronics and renewable energy technology. The system integrates affordable components, including ultrasonic transducers and solar panels, to ensure durability and ease of use. The immediate benefits include reduced crop losses, increased agricultural productivity, and healthier ecosystems due to the elimination of chemical pesticide use. Over time, the repellent fosters sustainable farming practices, enhances food security, and improves livelihoods for vulnerable communities. By empowering farmers with an environmentally friendly and scalable solution, this innovation contributes to resilient food systems, reduced environmental degradation, and strengthened economies in locust-affected regions.

core_fields.title: Nutricare by Alunna to prevent anemia in women of childbearing age
core_fields.description: Nutricare by Alunna is a program to reduce anemia among women of childbearing age in Indonesia, addressing its link to increased stunting risks in future generations. Through innovative products like our antioxidant and iron-rich Date Seed Drinks, we empower women to improve their health and well-being. This initiative aims to create a lasting impact by tackling anemia as a key factor in breaking the cycle of malnutrition and promoting healthier families.
core_fields.abstract: Anemia is a widespread issue among women of childbearing age in Indonesia, with significant health consequences. Anemic women face reduced productivity, impaired cognitive function, and higher risks during pregnancy. Critically, anemia increases the likelihood of stunting in children, perpetuating a cycle of poor health and malnutrition across generations. This issue is highly relevant, as addressing anemia not only improves women's health but also contributes to the nation s development by ensuring healthier future generations. Nutricare by Alunna offers an innovative solution through its Date Seed Drinks, a functional beverage rich in antioxidants and iron (Fe). This product addresses anemia by improving hemoglobin levels and combating oxidative stress, which is a contributing factor to the condition. Date seeds, a sustainable and underutilized resource, were chosen based on scientific insights into their high iron and antioxidant content, making them an effective yet affordable ingredient for anemia prevention. The program is designed to provide immediate benefits to consumers by enhancing their health and quality of life. Women gain access to a practical and enjoyable way to meet their nutritional needs, leading to better productivity and well-being. On a larger scale, Nutricare promotes sustainable practices by utilizing date seeds, reducing waste, and encouraging eco-friendly production. Communities benefit from the reduced prevalence of anemia and its associated economic and social costs, fostering a healthier and more prosperous society. Nutricare combines health innovation with sustainability to address anemia effectively and inclusively.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Hydroponics for Accessible and Regenerative Environment (SHARE)
core_fields.description: SHARE Hydroponics" is a solar-powered, resource-efficient farming system that addresses food security, water scarcity, and sustainability. With a modular and scalable design, it produces healthy, safe food for farmers, consumers, and communities. This innovation enhances climate resilience, promotes food inclusivity, and fosters environmentally sustainable agricultural practices, making it a vital solution for modern farming challenges.
core_fields.abstract: SHARE Hydroponics" is a solar-powered, resource-efficient farming system designed to tackle some of humanity s greatest challenges: food insecurity, water scarcity, and environmental degradation. Traditional agriculture is resource-intensive, consuming large amounts of water, energy, and land while contributing to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental damage. As populations grow and resources dwindle, sustainable farming solutions have become critical. This innovation combines hydroponic farming, which replaces soil with nutrient-enriched water, and solar energy to reduce reliance on non-renewable resources. It addresses water scarcity, particularly in arid regions, by recycling up to 90% of the water it uses. Free from harmful pesticides, it produces safe, non-toxic crops while minimizing environmental contamination. By reducing greenhouse gas emissions, SHARE Hydroponics provides an eco-friendly alternative to traditional farming methods. The system is powered by Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA), a scientific approach that precisely optimizes factors like temperature, light, and nutrient delivery. This ensures higher crop quality, increased yields, and reduced resource consumption. SHARE Hydroponics benefits consumers by providing affordable, safe, and healthy food. Farmers gain reduced input costs and higher yields, while unproductive or poor soil regions become viable for cultivation. Schools and communities access fresh produce and gain education in sustainable farming practices. Environmentally, it enhances climate resilience by conserving water, lowering carbon emissions, and promoting regenerative agriculture. By upcycling agricultural byproducts into useful resources, SHARE Hydroponics offers a holistic solution, strengthening sustainability and food security while addressing the needs of a growing global population.

core_fields.title: Leveraging Bioengineered Microbial Consortia Incorporating Ciliated Protists for Advancing Sustainable Agriculture Practices.
core_fields.description: An innovative biofertilizer combines bacteria (Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas fluorescens), fungi (Talaromyces albobiverticillius HNB9), and protozoan ciliates (Sterkiella cavicola, Euplotes affine, Colpoda inflata) to synergistically enhance nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and pathogen suppression. Leveraging natural microbial interactions, it boosts crop yields by 25%, promotes sustainable agriculture, and offers an eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilizers, supporting soil health and long-term productivity.
core_fields.abstract: The innovation introduces a groundbreaking biofertilizer that combines bacteria, fungi, and protozoa to revolutionize sustainable agriculture. It addresses the pressing problem of chemical fertilizer overuse, which depletes soil health, reduces biodiversity, and exacerbates climate change. As the demand for eco-friendly solutions grows, this biofertilizer offers a transformative alternative to ensure food security while protecting the environment. This solution leverages synergistic interactions between its components. Bacteria like Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens enhance nutrient availability and boost plant resilience. The fungal strain Talaromyces albobiverticillius HNB9 solubilizes minerals like phosphate, zinc, and silica while producing auxins for root growth. Protozoa, such as Sterkiella cavicola and Colpoda inflata, stimulate microbial activity and nutrient cycling by consuming other microorganisms, unlocking vital nutrients for plant uptake. Together, these components amplify the production of plant growth-promoting compounds like indole-3-acetic acid and biofilms. The formulation demonstrates a two- to three-fold yield increase compared to conventional biofertilizers. Farmers benefit from reduced dependence on synthetic fertilizers, improved soil fertility, and higher crop productivity. Environmental benefits include reduced chemical runoff, enhanced microbial diversity, and healthier ecosystems. This scalable, eco-friendly innovation aligns with global sustainable agriculture goals, ensuring long-term economic and ecological stability for farmers, producers, and communities worldwide.

core_fields.title: Propagation of perennial grain Kernza (a wheat hybrid) through tissue culture and field trials.
core_fields.description: This project aims to propagate Kernza (a wheat hybrid), a perennial grain, using tissue culture techniques and field trials. By producing virus-free, genetically consistent starter plants, it ensures a reliable supply for research and cultivation. Field trials will validate plant performance in diverse conditions. Leveraging Dr. Abed Choudhury's expertise (a global expert in grain breeding) , the project incorporates insights from rice and wheat prototypes to address food security and promote sustainable agriculture practices.
core_fields.abstract: Modern agriculture faces pressing challenges such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and climate change. Traditional annual crops exacerbate these issues through intensive farming practices. Kernza, a perennial grain, offers a sustainable alternative with its deep root system that improves soil health, reduces erosion, enhances water retention, and sequesters carbon. However, Kernza s adoption is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality planting materials and inconsistent cultivation practices. Our project addresses these barriers through tissue culture propagation and field trials. Tissue culture enables year-round production of virus-free, genetically consistent Kernza plants, ensuring a reliable supply for researchers and farmers. Field trials will validate the performance of tissue-cultured plants under diverse environmental conditions, providing critical insights for optimal cultivation practices. Immediate benefits include reliable planting materials for researchers and early adopter farmers. Long-term outcomes include improved soil health, reduced environmental degradation, and expanded opportunities for sustainable agriculture. This innovative approach lays the groundwork for broader adoption of Kernza, contributing to global efforts in combating climate change and enhancing food security. This project can be replicated to other regionally suitable areas globally eg. Bangladesh, India, Africa etc.

core_fields.title: Reducing post-harvest fresh produce loss using green engineered seaweed ingredients and processes
core_fields.description: Atlantic Sea Solutions has developed an edible coating technology to reduce food loss. Our immediate hurdle is field testing this technology which is limited by the small scale of our precision sprayers. We propose to engineer a scaled-up sprayer and test it in a greenhouse to de-risk our technology, validate value propositions, and obtain metrics for impacts of reducing food loss in real-time fresh produce supply chains to help accelerate our journey to commercialization.
core_fields.abstract: More than one-third of fresh produce is lost before reaching the consumers. This costs the US economy >20 million tons of food and >$40 billion in just one year - tangibly affecting growers and distributors. More than 90% of this lost food material ends up rotting in landfills contributing to about 8% of the total greenhouse gas emissions exacerbating climate crisis. This problem is compounded after considering food waste at consumer level in addition to food loss. Existing approaches to reduce food loss include cold chains, fumigants, synthetic coatings, sophisticated polymer packaging, and gene modifications among others. The material solutions take a major toll on terrestrial material and energy feedstocks such as forestry and farmlands, minerals, and petroleum reserves. We discovered that the seaweed industry is highly underdeveloped in Connecticut with immense growth potential and that seaweed can be a carbon neutral or carbon negative feedstock. We devised green engineering processes to derive seaweed extracts of commercial interest, of which one forms an invisible and flavorless edible coating that can reduce desiccation and spoilage in fresh produce by more than 50% over control. We also devised a precision spray process that minimizes material use to form coatings that can dry >4x faster than conventional coating. Our technology can reduce post-harvest losses to improve the profitability of produce growers, distributors, and improve value for money for consumers, while incentivizing the underutilized seaweed industry with a large and steady demand, removing the onus of sourcing away from dwindling land resources.

core_fields.abstract: Come summers, forests in the entire sub-Himalayan region become carbon-spewing-factories due to massive forest fires spread by high-calory pine needles that fall during dry summer months, destroying biodiversity, diminishing CO2 draw down capacity of the forests and ground water recharge. Lack of adequate nutrients and ground water, combined with erratic weather patterns, is negatively impacting agriculture. Our project aims to give economic value to fallen pine needles and agricultural waste/wood and bamboo chips/coffee husk, which farmers traditionally burn, by converting it into biochar and usable electrical/thermal energy. We are using downdraft gasification specially designed for these low density materials to produce biochar for soil amendment and carbon removal. The project is an innovation in high quality biochar production from such abundantly available waste biomass, a very difficult material to process. The technology of continuous raw material feeding and biochar removal/collection mechanism is unique for converting this difficult to handle biomass into biochar with ease. This innovation also uses the gases produced in the biochar production process, which otherwise are emitted contributing to non-CO2 gas emissions, for production of clean electrical/thermal energy eliminating the non-CO2 emissions harmful for atmosphere and generating additional revenue for the business. While this conversion of waste biomass regenerates biodiversity and eco-system, use of biochar not only directly benefits the farmers in developing climate resilient agriculture by rebuilding soil ecology, its nutrient-water retention capacity, decreasing farm input costs, and increasing agriculture productivity, but also uses technology to actively remove and store carbon in the soil.

core_fields.title: Millets For Growth (M4G): Combating Malnutrition through Nutritious and Climate-Resilient Crops
core_fields.description: Baobab Superfoods proposes to help address Rwanda s triple burden of malnutrition stunting (33%), anemia (37%), and micronutrient deficiencies through millet-based fortified foods. Our solution leverages millet, a climate-resilient crop, to create fortified products enriched with essential nutrients, partnering with farmers for sustainable practices, and educating communities on dietary diversity. This approach improves nutrition, boosts farmer incomes, enhances school meal programs, and promotes climate-smart agriculture, supporting Rwandan Government s goal to reduce stunting to 10% by 2030.
core_fields.abstract: Problem Rwanda faces a triple burden of malnutrition, as highlighted in the National Family and Nutrition Policy 2024. Stunting (33%), anemia (37%), and micronutrient deficiencies are particularly severe among children under five, adolescent girls, and pregnant women. These challenges are partly attributed to sub-optimal minimum acceptable diet rates, which limit dietary diversity and nutrient intake. Innovation To reduce stunting rates to 10% by 2030, the Rwandan Government emphasizes the "cultivation, supply, and consumption of nutritious foods". Baobab Superfoods leverages millet, a climate-resilient and nutrient-rich crop, to create and distribute fortified products like flours for porridge and pastries. Our proposed solution focuses on three domains: 1. Fortify Millet-Based Products with: (a) Iron + Vitamin C + Vitamin B12: To combat anemia. (b) Zinc + Vitamin A: To support growth and immunity. (c) Protein + Lysine: To address wasting and improve muscle development. 2. Establish Farmer Partnerships: Engage small-scale farmers through fair contracts and training in regenerative practices, such as intercropping millet with legumes to enhance soil health. 3. Do Consumer Awareness Campaigns: Educate target groups on product use and dietary diversity through direct awareness campaigns and in partnership with frontline health workers. Benefits Consumers gain access to safe, nutritious foods that combat stunting and anemia. Farmers benefit from improved incomes through sustainable practices. Schools enhance meal programs, boosting children's nutrition and academic outcomes. Communities adopt healthier eating habits, reducing malnutrition. The environment benefits from millet s low ecological footprint, promoting climate-smart agriculture.

core_fields.title: Backyard Farms: Using Lyophilization to Empower Underserved Regenerative Agriculture Farmers to Feed Food Insecure Population in Food Deserts Across New Mexico.
core_fields.description: Backyard Farms leverages lyophilization an advanced freeze-drying technology to combat food insecurity in New Mexico s food deserts. By extending the shelf life of perishable foods while preserving their nutritional value, this innovative solution mitigates logistical challenges faced by underserved communities, particularly Native American tribes and Hispanic populations. Our initiative integrates cultural traditions and local farming practices to provide nutritious, year-round food options. By partnering with small farmers and community organizations we reduce food waste and create markets.
core_fields.abstract: Enormous amounts of fresh foods are lost between the farm and the consumers in food deserts. This results in large amounts of food waste and food banks and disaster relief organizations stockpiling dried, canned, or frozen foods. This surplus of shelf-stable junk foods are preserved with lots of sugar, salt, or subject to heat in a canning process that destroys the nutrition of these foods. New Mexico is the largest rural state and suffers socioeconomic conditions that force some to live in conditions that would shock most Americans. The Colonias is a region along the southern border with residence routinely living without electricity or running water and similar conditions exist on the Navajo Reservation. Many have to travel 30-60 minutes to buy groceries when summer heat reaches over a 100F, a family can only get as many cold foods as can fit in a cooler. These problems are universal food desert issues that we found a solution using lyophilization (freeze-drying) technology developed by NASA for space travel to transport foods across food deserts! We have developed a model that can be scaled and used in any state, country, or nation and any ecozone where food can be grown, and hungry people live. This model empowers small local farmers, and preserves 97% of the nutrition of the fresh foods, removes perishability barriers for storage and transport to reduce food waste and get more healthy food back into the food system without extra acres being tilled, water usage, etc.

Scientific insights include the efficient conversion of agricultural waste into fuel and the implementation of certification processes that meet global standards. core_fields.title: Sea-Land Symbiosis
core_fields.description: SOS transforms invasive seaweed into sustainable, nutrient-rich agricultural products that enhance crop yield, reduce chemical fertilizer use, and improve soil health. By upcycling invasive seaweed, we support regenerative practices that reduce ocean pollution and empower coastal communities through job creation. Our approach addresses food security, environmental resilience, and sustainable agricultural growth, helping build a more sustainable food system from the Caribbean outward.
core_fields.abstract: SOS addresses the critical problem of invasive sargassum seaweed in the Caribbean, which devastates marine ecosystems, threatens coastal economies, and leads to significant waste and environmental pollution. Leveraging biotechnology, we sustainable harvest and transform this seaweed into nutrient-rich, eco-friendly products that support agriculture, aquaculture, and soil health, effectively turning a harmful waste product into a resource. Our innovation replaces synthetic fertilizers with an organic, nutrient-packed alternative that improves crop yield, enhances soil microbiome health, improves crop nutritional value and reduces greenhouse gas emissions. This process not only benefits farmers through higher productivity and lower input costs but also contributes to regenerative agricultural practices that restore soil vitality and reduce dependency on harmful inputs. The scientific foundation of our solution comes from understanding the biochemical richness of seaweed such as sargassum, which is naturally high in polysaccharides, antioxidants, and other growth-promoting compounds such as phytohormones. By converting sargassum into valuable products like crop enhancers and hydroponic substrates, we provide immediate benefits to farmers, communities, and ecosystems. Coastal communities gain economic opportunities through sustainable seaweed harvesting and product development, while society at large benefits from a healthier ocean, reduced environmental damage, and greater food security. This approach is immediately impactful and scalable we are already working in 6 countries, providing sustainable benefits across agricultural, environmental, and economic domains. Our end-users, including from small to big farmers and coastal communities, gain both environmentally-friendly solutions and economic resilience, making our innovation a model for transforming ecological challenges into sustainable development.

core_fields.title: Farm Urban App: Simplifying urban farming for a healthier and more resilient food system
core_fields.description: With Farm Urban, we re building a sustainable future where cities can grow their own food, one farm at a time. By incorporating AI technology to enhance urban farming, Farm Urban App connects urban farmers with all the resources needed to farm successfully within cities farmable landowners, weather & indoor information, AI harvest calendar, compost makers, and regenerative knowledge while providing a platform to sell harvested fresh produce directly to city dwellers.
core_fields.abstract: Africans do not have equal access to healthy food. Poor health outcomes related to unhealthy food consumption such as diet-related illnesses, including obesity, diabetes, and heart disease, do not reflect food preferences but are tied to poor accessibility to healthy foods due to the displacement of agriculture to forested rural areas far from the cities where 80% of food produced is consumed. If the rates of diet-related illnesses are to decline, we must increase the accessibility of healthy foods within our cities. We are solving this problem with Farm Urban App. Our app uses geotagging to quickly locate urban spaces and evaluate them on farming potential. A user can find a location listed by urban space owners, mark the outline of their desired farm space, choose a farming method, and a selection of produce to grow on the farm. The AI algorithm on the app will then let the user know how much of each product the farm can produce and how many people can be fed. The profitability of the farm is calculated by the app based on real calculations of the harvest calendar, allowing everyone with an interest in urban agriculture to discover the feasibility of farming in their cities and connecting them to the landowner, organic fertilizers, regenerative knowledge etc. During harvest, the app notifies consumers about the new harvest, connecting the closest farms to buyers. We are helping our target customers to increase access to healthy, locally grown, and culturally appropriate food sources.

core_fields.title: Building Capacity For a Safe and Transparent Dairy Supply Chain in the Rwandan Eastern Province
core_fields.description: This project focuses on distributing the Safi device to 60 dairy farmers in Rwanda s Eastern Province. Complementary to the device are educational efforts that will teach farmers and their communities about the importance of selling/consuming pasteurized milk. If successful, this pilot will open up the opportunity for Safi to work with the Rwandan National Dairy Platform, Heifer International and Ripple Effect Rwanda, and the 15,000 dairy farmers in their networks.
core_fields.abstract: East Africa has the highest global incidence of milk-borne disease. Alarmingly, 30% of deaths in children under 5. This is due to a lack of access to safe and quality milk, with up to 90% of milk in East Africa being sold raw by small scale milk sellers in the unregulated, informal market. The challenges of the current dairy supply chain are burdened by many factors but most importantly the lack of adequate traceability and tools to ensure safety. At Safi, we have patented the world's first, small-scale pasteurization control unit targeted towards small-scale dairy farmers and vendors. The device kills milk-borne diseases all while retaining the key nutrients of milk. It is affordable, powered by renewable energy sources, and allows farmers to easily pasteurize their differentiating daily yields. To address inadequate traceability, at the core of the product is a digital tracking system that remotely records milk pasteurization data and centralizes production information for regulators and governments. The Safi solution ensures that the ability to pasteurize milk is democratized to smallholder farmers who supply up to 90% of milk sold in these markets. This allows farmers to earn more money per litre of milk, and also makes pasteurized milk more accessible and affordable to the general public. Safi is also looking to collaborate with the One Cup, One Child school feeding program in Rwanda to get a cup of safe milk to every school child in Rwanda. Therefore, Safi provides clear benefits to farmers, consumers and their communities.

core_fields.title: KENYA MARA Regenerating Traditional Foods, Lands & Livelihoods through Maasai Conservancies
core_fields.description: GFSC funding will help regenerate 100,000 hectares of communally-managed Maasai conservancies in Kenya s Mara region. Through the scaling of ongoing, successful implementation of Holistic Management, this project is helping Maasai herders incorporate regenerative practices into traditional livelihoods. This project will increase resilience for 8,000+ people through improved land health, food security and nutrition, and tourism-driven income, all while restoring iconic wildlife habitat of the Maasai Mara and sequestering ~180K tons of carbon.
core_fields.abstract: The Maasai have historically been pastoralists, relying on a traditional diet primarily composed of blood, milk, and meat. However, since the 1950s when British colonial administration imposed restrictions on cattle grazing, a substantial number have been pushed to transition to government-supported farming programs, leading to a replacement of traditional dietary staples with maize, grains, and cereals, and subsequently to notable increases in both BMI and diabetes (Pressier et al. 2022). Addressing these challenges is integral to our project's mission, which is empowering the Maasai to regenerate land-health and productivity through Holistic Management which, in turn, contributes to improved nutritional well-being by bolstering access to traditional animal-based dietary staples and improving livestock health. While research evaluating associations between land health and food s nutrient density is still in its infancy, Provenza et al. 2019 notes that circumstantial evidence supports the hypothesis that phytochemical richness of herbivore diets enhances biochemical richness of meat and dairy, which is linked with human and environmental health. By enhancing forage biodiversity through properly-managed grazing, the Maasai will simultaneously enhance nutrient density of traditional foods. Further, widespread exclusion of people and livestock from designated conservation areas, driven by colonial and post-colonial policies and economic forces, has led to significant reductions in grassland productivity with numerous consequences such as diminished livelihoods and associated social challenges, and diminished wildlife habitat and associated tourism income. This project is implemented through conservancies, where livestock is holistically-managed by pastoralists to regenerate land health, presenting a win-win solution for both environmental and socioeconomic outcomes.

This multi-faceted approach leverages evidence-based insights like Large-Scale Food Fortification (LSFF), which improves dietary quality, and the Enabling Business for Nutrition Index (EBANI), which identifies opportunities for policy enhancement. Immediate benefits include improved access to fortified foods, enhanced food safety standards, and better workplace nutrition practices, positively impacting workers health and productivity. Sustainable benefits extend to systemic changes in food systems, such as reduced food waste, eco-friendly production, and expanded geographic reach, contributing to broader nutrition security and environmental resilience. SBN Ethiopia s solution aligns with the Global Food System Challenge by addressing food affordability, accessibility, and consumer trust. The initiative promises significant, measurable impacts for consumers, producers, and society at large, creating a foundation for healthier diets and a sustainable food future. core_fields.title: YieldSync: Precision Agriculture, Perfectly Timed
core_fields.description: YieldSync is an innovative GeoAI-powered suite of digital tools revolutionizing agriculture. It combines advanced satellite imagery, 17 specialized indices and machine learning to optimize productivity, sustainability and resilience. With features like grid-based scoring, yield estimation (macro and micro) and global carbon credit modeling through BiomeSync, YieldSync empowers stakeholders with actionable insights. Designed for scalability, it addresses inefficiencies, reduces environmental impact and fosters food security, with global pilots set for Q1 2025.
core_fields.abstract: YieldSync addresses critical challenges in agriculture, including inefficiency, yield variability, environmental degradation, and a lack of precise tools for informed decision-making. Traditional practices often rely on intuition and static data, leaving farmers and stakeholders ill-equipped to tackle complex issues like climate variability, resource mismanagement, and unsustainable practices. These inefficiencies contribute to food insecurity, economic instability, and environmental harm. YieldSync offers a transformative solution with four integrated components: Agricultural Excellence Tools: Using 17 indices, YieldSync generates classified maps, time-series data, and actionable insights for resource optimization. AgriShield AI: A patented (application in progress) system employing grid-based scoring, dynamic recommendations, and geospatial analytics to monitor and improve farm performance. Yield Estimation System: Macro-level predictions support regional planning, while micro-level tools offer plot-specific yield forecasts to guide precise interventions. BiomeSync: A carbon credit estimation platform, currently under patent discussions and validation with leading organizations, quantifies carbon sequestration, enabling sustainable practices and financial incentives for farmers. This innovation combines advanced geospatial technologies, machine learning and environmental insights, offering immediate benefits such as improved yields, efficient resource use and data-driven decision-making for farmers. Its sustainable impact extends to society and the environment by reducing carbon footprints, enhancing food security and fostering resilient agricultural ecosystems. YieldSync empowers users to navigate global agricultural challenges with cutting-edge tools and actionable insights, driving meaningful change in the industry.

core_fields.title: Development of non-toxic oxygen absorbers to prolong food shelf life
core_fields.description: We are developing non-iron-based oxygen absorbers for the prolonging of food shelf life. We already have a minimum viable product with our patented technology called the MSN (Mesoporous Silica Nanosphere). This is a non-toxic, bio-compatible alternative to existing products in the market. We are also developing a film-based product that could be applied on fresh harvests. Our next step is to scale up by finding suppliers and clients for our products.
core_fields.abstract: Food loss and waste present a significant global challenge, with one-third of all food produced lost to spoilage. A substantial portion of this occurs during post-harvest and storage before reaching consumers. Current preservation methods for processed foods typically reduce oxygen levels to only 0.5 2 vol%, which still leads to deterioration over time. Additionally, preserving fresh fruits poses a major challenge, affecting food availability and causing considerable economic losses and environmental waste. Our patented technology utilizing mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) offers a faster, safer, and more efficient solution for oxygen absorption in food preservation. Our oxygen scavengers can effectively reduce oxygen levels to 0.1 vol% in packaging headspace, which is optimal for maintaining food quality. Unlike traditional iron-based absorbers, our solution is biocompatible, ensuring safety for consumers. We are also developing a film-based product that incorporates MSN technology. Currently in the proof-of-concept stage, this innovation adapts to the specific respiration and transpiration rates of the produce, naturally achieving equilibrium gas concentrations within the packaging to extend shelf life. Both our sachet-based and film-based products can significantly prolong the freshness of food items, benefiting food companies by minimizing economic losses and providing consumers with safer preservation options. Ultimately, our technology contributes to reducing food waste, leading to less environmental impact and promoting a more sustainable food cycle.

core_fields.title: Nourishing a Sustainable Future: Regenerative Agriculture for Affordable, Healthy, and Climate-Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: Our project will support 2,000 smallholder farmers (SHF) adopt regenerative agriculture (RA) practices by offering training, practical support, and incorporating resilience-building initiatives, enabling a sustainable transition that increases biodiversity, restores soil health, and mitigate climate change. SHF income will increase by 20% through contract farming, connecting farmers to aggregators, and establishing local markets exclusively for regenerative agriculture produce. This will also improve access to affordable, sustainably grown, nutritious food and promote healthier diets.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation is transforming the food-production system in sub-Saharan Africa by enabling SHFs to become economically & environmentally resilient. We do this by building a scalable and financially self-sustaining business model that transitions SHFs to regenerative farming and providing assured income increase leading to economic transformation (income increase), biodiverse farms, while improving food security & diets. We make money through the offtake and subsides the cost of training & production through the margins from that. The problem we set out to solve is that of SHFs being economically and environmentally vulnerable. SHFs in sub-Saharan Africa are classified as extremely poor ( 1.5 USD/day) and their situation is expected to worsen with accelerating climate change, dropping productivity of land due to unsustainable practices, and already being food insecure and they are wholly unprepared for this. There are an estimated 5M SHF in Kenya (and 500M in sub-Saharan Africa) who face this problem, leading to unprecedented food insecurity & climate migration. Regenerative agriculture provides a slow take-back of biodiversity, improved yields, improved nutrition, and improved incomes. It has been proven in desert landscapes and arid regions to regenerate plants, soils, animals, and insects critical to a healthy ecosystem. We would like to replicate this at the SHF level in a way that is economically and commercially viable both to the SHF and our scalable business model

core_fields.title: CAPREDICT: AI-Powered Solutions for Reducing Food Waste, Enhancing Transparency, and Empowering Farmers in the Agri-Supply Chain
core_fields.description: CAPREDICT leverages AI to reduce food waste, improve supply chain transparency, and empower farmers with actionable insights. By predicting the shelf life of perishables using image analysis, environmental data, and advanced algorithms, it enables smarter decisions, reduces losses, and increases profitability. CAPREDICT s innovative solution fosters sustainability, enhances food security, and creates equitable opportunities across the farm-to-fork supply chain.
core_fields.abstract: CAPREDICT addresses the global challenge of food waste, which affects one-third of all food produced annually, costing $2.6 trillion and contributing 8% of greenhouse gas emissions. Smallholder farmers lose up to 40% of their produce before it reaches consumers, while high-income countries waste an average of 20 pounds of food per person each month. This waste undermines food security, harms farmers livelihoods, and contributes to environmental degradation. CAPREDICT solves this problem using AI-powered technology to predict the shelf life of perishables through image analysis, environmental data, and bruising indices. This innovative approach enables farmers to make informed harvesting and market decisions, reducing waste and increasing profits. It also provides retailers and consumers with tools to optimize freshness and minimize losses. Scientific insights from image processing, machine learning, and agricultural research informed this solution. By integrating advanced algorithms with on-the-ground knowledge, CAPREDICT provides precise, actionable predictions tailored to different crops and conditions. Immediate benefits include reduced food losses, improved profitability for farmers, and better access to fresh, nutritious food for consumers. Sustainable benefits include a significant reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, water usage, and resource wastage across the supply chain. CAPREDICT empowers communities, schools, and producers to enhance food security, promote transparency, and build a resilient and equitable food system. By marrying technology with sustainability, CAPREDICT creates value for all stakeholders while addressing critical global challenges.

core_fields.title: KaFresh: Feeding the Next Billion
core_fields.description: Sio Valley Technologies' project, Feeding the Next Billion, is designed to expand the use of KaFresh in existing markets and reach new regions both across Africa and beyond. The project will support the growth of SVT's sales team and increase end user awareness of KaFresh through strong marketing campaigns and promotional events. The project will allow SVT to establish lasting impact evaluation and quality control measures.
core_fields.abstract: SVT is solving the lack of efficient post-harvest management systems in Africa, where 40-60% of harvested crops are lost annually due to spoilage caused by pests, mold, and moisture. SVT focuses on post-harvest management in Sub-Saharan Africa because food spoilage not only represents a major financial cost but also a grave humanitarian concern. Approximately 1.3 billion tons of food are wasted or lost globally each year, equating to $940 billion (FAO 2021), while about 735 million people face hunger (FAO, 2022). SVT's first to market product, KaFresh, significantly reduces these losses which enhances food availability, eases pressure on resources, combats hunger, and provides pathways to improved farmer livelihood. KaFresh is an innovative solution using a proprietary blend of natural ingredients to extend the shelf life of fruits and vegetables at room temperature by up to 500%, eliminating the need for expensive cold storage solutions. KaFresh's technology creates a very thin, edible coating that inhibits cell wall breakdown and regulates respiration rate & ethylene production, slowing down the ripening process. Additionally, KaFresh empowers farmers by democratizing access to food storage technologies, enabling them to grow their income through reduced post-harvest losses and improved produce quality at market. By minimizing spoilage, KaFresh combats food waste, in turn reducing GHG emission from landfills. Ultimately, this enhances food security and promotes a more sustainable food system within communities.

core_fields.title: Enhancing Food Safety Through Affordable Quality Testing Kits for SMEs.
core_fields.description: This project aims to develop affordable, portable food testing kits tailored for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to ensure compliance with global food safety standards. These kits will test for contaminants like heavy metals, pesticides, and microbial pathogens, empowering SMEs to produce safer food products while reducing costs and reliance on third-party testing facilities. The initiative promotes accessibility, sustainability, and global food security.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description: The project introduces affordable, portable food testing kits designed to help SMEs ensure food safety by detecting contaminants like heavy metals, pesticides, and microbial pathogens. These kits address the high cost and inaccessibility of laboratory testing, which often hinders SMEs from complying with food safety standards. Problem and Relevance: Food safety is a critical issue globally, with unsafe food causing illnesses, economic losses, and reduced consumer confidence. SMEs, particularly in developing regions, struggle with costly testing and lack of access to certified laboratories, leading to undetected hazards in their products. This gap in quality assurance affects public health and limits market access for these producers. Solution: The portable kits leverage advances in biosensor technology, immunoassays, and colorimetric detection to offer reliable, user-friendly, and cost-effective testing. They allow producers to test raw materials and finished products on-site, ensuring compliance with food safety standards without expensive equipment or specialized training. Scientific Insight: The solution draws on research in rapid, field-deployable diagnostic tools, which combine sensitivity, specificity, and simplicity. These innovations address the unique needs of SMEs by reducing dependency on third-party facilities. Benefits: Immediate benefits include safer food, reduced production costs, and increased market access for SMEs. Long-term, the kits empower communities, improve public health, and promote sustainability by reducing foodborne illnesses. This innovation supports farmers, producers, schools, and society by making food safety accessible, fostering trust in local products, and contributing to a safer global food supply chain.

core_fields.title: Healthy Climate & Fresh Food for All
core_fields.description: Sky High Farm works to ensure everyone has access to the resources they need to sustain themselves, including nutrient-dense, culturally-appropriate food. Simultaneously, we seek to improve the ecological integrity of a large plot of conventionally farmed land with climate-forward farming methods (including soil health studies, native grasses and pollinator protection) while providing high-quality meat, eggs, and produce to those in our community suffering food insecurity.
core_fields.abstract: In 2020, amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, food insecurity was exacerbated for our region's most marginalized communities, with many families and individuals facing insufficiency for the first time. Layered on the cascading issues of the pandemic, we are also facing untenable food prices due to inflation. Our responsibility to provide culturally relevant, high-quality vegetables, meat, and eggs to our community not only for free, but on a consistent year-round basis, has become increasingly urgent in recent years. We recognize the serious consequences of environmental racism and how the climate crisis most impacts marginalized communities. In this context, we are committed to regenerative farming practices that honor the land, prioritize the health of our farmers, and produce quality food with minimal inputs. These practices work to counterbalance the harm of industrial farming, while giving our environment and our people the care they deserve. To accomplish this, we are planting a variety of cover crops into former corn and soy fields to address soil health improvement in advance of planned native grass and wildflower plantings. Ultimately, we will establish a perennial stand of native plants for pollinator habitat and grazing beef cattle, promoting pasture diversity and restoring soil health on nearly 200 acres of perennial pasture. This work is a reflection of our deeply held belief and responsibility to not only feed our community, but to do so in a way that cares for the long lasting impacts on our neighbors and the future of our planet.

core_fields.title: Innovative Peanut Root-Breaking Technology for Sustainable and Efficient Post-Harvest Farming
core_fields.description: Our Peanut Root-Breaker Machine reduces the tedious peanut harvesting process from 8 12 hours of manual labor per acre to just 3 4 hours. Traditionally, farmers spend long hours sitting and separating peanuts by hand, a slow and exhausting task. Our machine cuts labor costs by 40% reduces post-harvest losses by 30%, and increases efficiency. By leasing at TZS 3,000 per sack, we aim to transform peanut farming for 5 million farmers in Tanzania.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation: Skyverse Solutions has developed a peanut root-breaking machine that revolutionizes the peanut post-harvest process. It simplifies the traditionally labor-intensive and time-consuming task of separating peanuts from roots and branches, improving the efficiency of peanut harvesting for smallholder farmers. Problem: In Tanzania, over 5 million smallholder peanut farmers face challenges with high post-harvest losses (up to 30%) due to outdated separation methods, which are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Traditional methods can take up to 15 minutes per sack, leading to long working hours and significant labor costs. Solution: The peanut root-breaking machine reduces the time required for separation to just 4-5 minutes per sack, cutting harvesting time from 8-12 hours per acre to 3-4 hours per acre. This saves 50% of time and reduces labor costs by 40%. The machine also reduces post-harvest losses by making the separation process more efficient. Scientific Insight: The design leverages mechanical engineering principles to effectively break the peanut roots in bundles, enabling faster collection and separation. It s built with a focus on affordability and sustainability, allowing farmers to lease it at a cost-effective rate. Benefits: Farmers benefit from reduced labor costs and increased productivity, leading to higher profits. Environmental impact is positive as fewer peanuts are wasted, and sustainable farming practices are promoted. Communities gain through improved food security and enhanced local economies. This innovation is a scalable solution that can drive long-term change in Tanzania s agricultural sector.

core_fields.description: The solar taxi initiative aims to provide affordable, sustainable transportation by using electric vehicles powered by renewable energy. It addresses the growing demand for mobility, rising fuel costs, and environmental concerns by offering clean, efficient, and cost-effective alternatives. The project will create job opportunities, reduce carbon emissions, and promote cleaner cities, benefiting communities, drivers, and businesses in Ghana and potentially across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Transportation demand across Africa is expected to double in the next decade, creating a need for affordable and efficient mobility options in sectors such as private, public, delivery, agriculture, health, and waste management. To address this, electric vehicles (EVs) will be developed and made affordable, offering an alternative to expensive fuel-based options. Consumers, businesses, and transportation services will benefit from more affordable, efficient, and sustainable mobility. Fuel prices in Ghana have risen from $0.50 per liter in 2015 to $1.10 per liter in 2023, placing a financial burden on drivers and transport services. The solution is to provide electric vehicle transportation services at affordable rates, reducing reliance on costly fuel and making sustainable mobility accessible. Drivers, vehicle owners, and consumers will benefit from lower transportation costs and reduced financial strain. Vehicular emissions from fossil fuels contribute to air pollution and climate change, negatively impacting public health and the environment. By accelerating the use of renewable energy to power electric vehicles, this solution will reduce emissions and promote cleaner, sustainable transportation. Society, communities, and the environment will benefit from improved air quality, leading to healthier communities and a more sustainable future.

core_fields.title: Transnational Black Women s Food Sovereignty Re-Imaging & Re-Imagining
core_fields.description: This photography-based project connects Black women gardeners in Mwanza, Tanzania to Black Indigenous Garifuna sustenance farmers in Punta Piedra, Honduras. Connecting through images of women s farms, gardens, and food, these women will see the beauty and feel the inspiration of Black women s efforts to provide their communities with fresh, healthy food. Through a website-based photo gallery and social media campaign, Black women globally will be invited to share their connections to land and food.
core_fields.abstract: Language is often a barrier when people share their stories. However, photography is a universal language that can communicate across the barriers of spoken language, providing a sense of deep connection. In many countries, Black (and Indigenous) women are marginalized in (patriarchal) stories of (white or mestizo male) farmers and their strength. This photography and social media campaign intends to support a #TransnationalBlackWomensFoodSovereignty social media that highlights the difficult and beautiful labor that is behind Black women s efforts to provide their families and communities with fresh, healthy meals. By leveraging social media technologies to share images, we will shift the image (and ultimately the narrative) around Black women s agricultural labor and relationship to fresh produce. Too often, Black communities (especially in non-Black majority countries) are stereotyped as eating fried and unhealthy foods. These stereotypes result in discrimination against Black women and inattention to (non-diet-related) health concerns. This project will show encourage and inspire Black women s global connections to each other and gardening and farming with fruits and vegetables. The project will focus on two communities of Black women on different continents. They will share their local traditions, closing the distance between them with the power of mobile technology. The immediate benefits are pride in the agricultural and food traditions of these communities that will inspire broader appreciation of their contributions to food sovereignty and greater encouragement among women. In the best case scenario, what begins as a year-long campaign will become a viral social media trend.
