core_fields.title: Ikemon Green Rural Community: Agro-Business Incubation, Training, Seeding, Networking, and Services to empower West African youth's socio-economic development.
core_fields.description: This proposal establishes the "Ikemon Green Rural Community" in Benin as a sustainable agro-food hub, technology park, and incubation center for West African youth. Using the integrated Songhai model, it will train 2,000 youth in the region in regenerative agriculture, biotechnology, and IT, creating ecosystems for systemic growth, wealth, and employment. The initiative combats soil degradation, restores productivity with climate-smart practices, and leverages IT and biotechnology to unlock regional potential within a transformative $500,000 budget.
core_fields.abstract: Songhai s innovative approach represents a groundbreaking, zero-waste agricultural ecosystem that seamlessly integrates regenerative agriculture, sustainable technology, and community empowerment to address Africa s most pressing food system challenges. This dynamic model not only combats poverty, unemployment, and food insecurity but also reverses land degradation, positioning agriculture as a transformative engine for socio-economic and ecological progress. At its core, the Songhai model synergizes three interconnected sectors: the primary sector (a harmonized system of crop production, livestock, and aquaculture), the secondary sector (value addition through agro-processing and renewable energy solutions), and the tertiary sector (market access enhanced by digital platforms). By closing resource loops and recycling organic by-products, it achieves unparalleled efficiency, reducing dependency on harmful chemical inputs while fostering environmental resilience. We produce more and better with less. Rooted in scientific principles of biomimicry and circular economies, Songhai employs environmentally friendly practices such as agroforestry, polyculture, and soil regeneration to restore soil fertility, enhance biodiversity, and mitigate climate change. Cutting-edge technologies like IoT sensors, solar-powered systems, and e-commerce platforms further amplify productivity, streamline supply chains, and connect farmers to markets in real time. This paradigm creates immediate benefits higher yields, lower costs, and expanded job opportunities for youth and women while establishing a foundation for long-term impact: empowered communities, equitable food access, and a reinvigorated ecological balance. For consumers, it ensures affordable, nutritious food, aligning with sustainable practices that protect planetary health. Songhai s integrative model offers a scalable blueprint for sustainable, resilient, and inclusive food systems, capable of transforming Africa and inspiring global change.

core_fields.title: Ensuring food security for migrant families in Turkana, Kenya and Ciudad Juarez, Mexico using AI precision and regenerative agriculture practices
core_fields.description: Building on pilot activities, our project will expand regenerative agriculture and AI precision farming practices. Working with experienced partners and migrants/refugees in shelters and camps, in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico and Turkana County, Kenya, our aim is to increase and diversify production to secure healthy diets, provide participants with life skills, and share learning widely. New tools will maximize crop yields, improve nutritional status and reduce water use, leading to more sustainable food systems
core_fields.abstract: South North Nexus (SNN) works in two similar geographical locations with refugees and migrants. The camps and shelters are situated in dry ecosystems that face many challenges, including food and nutrition insecurity and access to clean water due to harsh climatic conditions, minimal rainfall and limited infrastructure. The food and nutrition challenges faced by refugees in Kakuma Camp in Turkana County, Kenya include lack of nutritious foods, including fruits, vegetables and insufficient proteins. The camp is home to almost 300,000 people, with many settlements. The other location is Ciudad Juarez, a U.S. Mexico border point of entry for asylum seekers. In border shelters, food and nutrition security depends heavily on the church community to provide donations to cover basic food and water needs. Most shelter residents are fleeing violence and political instability. SNN has been partnering in both locations for the last three years, introducing practices that allow residents to participate in growing nutritious foods. Women are significant players in food production however, they still lack access to farming skills and new agricultural technologies. With a focus on sharing technologies and learning, the project will integrate AI and regenerative practices with: 1) HOBOware to monitor soil humidity, temperature, dissolved nutrients and pH; 2) solar-powered pumping systems, including for irrigation; and 3) indigenous crops, using agroforestry techniques among other practices. Training topics for families, local officials and stakeholders, will include: tool use and maintenance, nutrition, agriculture practices and financial literacy. Special attention will be given to women s skill enhancement.

core_fields.title: From farms to global stages: Telling the Untold Stories of Women in Agriculture.
core_fields.description: "From Farms to Global Stages" is a transformative project by Spring Agric aimed at empowering women farmers by amplifying their untold stories. Through storytelling, media campaigns, and training, the initiative will elevate women s leadership in agriculture, promote climate-smart and sustainable farming, and build global networks for advocacy. This project seeks to increase visibility, provide resources, and influence policies, ultimately enhancing the economic empowerment and resilience of women farmers while contributing to sustainable food systems worldwide.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation Description: Spring Agric is introducing a holistic approach to empower women farmers through climate-smart agriculture, agroecology, and value addition practices. The project focuses on providing women with the tools, training, and market access needed to boost agricultural productivity, reduce post-harvest losses, and increase resilience to climate change. Problem Being Solved: Agriculture in Kenya is highly vulnerable to climate change, with women, who make up 80% of smallholder farmers, facing increased challenges such as crop failures, water scarcity, and soil degradation. Additionally, women often lack access to resources, information, and markets, which hinders their economic potential and food security. Solution: Spring Agric addresses these issues by training women farmers in sustainable farming practices, including water conservation, soil fertility management, and crop diversification. The integration of value-added products such as dried fruits and flours reduces post-harvest losses and increases income. The use of mobile technology provides real-time climate data, market updates, and farming tips, enhancing decision-making and productivity. Scientific/Technical Insight: The solution is based on agroecology and climate-smart agriculture principles, which emphasize soil health, water conservation, and biodiversity. Leveraging digital tools ensures farmers receive timely information to adapt to changing conditions, improving their ability to respond to climate shocks. Immediate and Sustainable Benefits: Increased yields and income for farmers through sustainable practices. Reduced post-harvest losses, ensuring more food for communities. Improved food security and nutritional diversity. Empowered women who become leaders in their communities. Enhanced environmental resilience by promoting eco-friendly farming practices.

core_fields.title: Dynamic Sprouting: Sustainable AI-Driven Superfood Production
core_fields.description: Our project is design and development of AI-driven, automated mini-factories to produce nutrient-rich, safe sprouted superfoods sustainably. Using 3L water/kg, no pesticides, and eliminating biohazards, these scalable factories reduce emissions and offer 2-6x more bioavailable superfoods locally. Targeting the $12B global superfood market, our innovation addresses critical needs in nutrition, food safety, and sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Sprout Dynamics addresses critical challenges in food safety, malnutrition, sustainability, and scalability through AI-driven mini-factories for sprouting seeds. These automated systems use 3L water/kg, require no pesticides, and eliminate biohazards like salmonella via real-time AI monitoring, producing safe and affordable superfoods. Problem Solved Malnutrition and Chronic Illness: Limited access to safe, nutrient-dense food. Scalability Issues: Current sprouting is an artisanal $5B industry, lacking scalable and mass-production solutions. Resource Inefficiency: High water, pesticide, and land use in traditional agriculture. Food Safety: Biohazards like salmonella and mold in conventional sprouting processes. Vegetarian Nutrition Gaps: Lack of plant-based omega-3 sources; sprouts offer a sustainable, nutrient-rich alternative to fish. Target Groups and Benefits B2B (Food Producers & Retail Chains): Affordable, scalable solutions for producing nutrient-rich superfoods. Opportunities to launch products like frozen sprout mixes, meeting consumer health trends. B2B2C (Resellers & Supermarkets): Expanded product portfolios with high-nutrition, sustainable options. Access to scalable, mass-produced sprouted seeds for growing superfood demand. Diabetes Patients and Associations: Low glycemic, high-fiber foods for managing blood sugar levels. Tailored products for specialized dietary needs. Vegetarians: A sustainable, plant-based omega-3 source with flaxseed sprouts, rich in alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and essential nutrients. Nutritional replacement for fish with high bioavailability of fiber, protein, and fatty acids. Chefs and Food Innovators: Unlimited creative possibilities with nutrient-dense sprouted ingredients. Consistent supply of safe, high-quality seeds for culinary innovation. Communities and Schools: Affordable, healthy meals improving dietary outcomes. Local, decentralized production ensures food security and reduces transportation emissions.

core_fields.title: Innovative Students Engagement in Nutritious Food Production, Preservation and Processing in Uganda
core_fields.description: The project empowers Students to engage in Nutritious Food Production, Preservation and Processing (NFPPP) through operating; a. smart-urban gardening of nutritious vegetables; supported by solar-irrigation and composting for bio-fertilizers; b. post-harvest food preservation and processing; c. rearing chicken, pigs, rabbits and fish; enabled by recycled food-waste and black-soldier-fly-larvae. Recycling redeems over 768 tons of food-waste generated daily (in Kampala city alone) and facilitates the bridging of the current nutrient deficits in schools and communities.
core_fields.abstract: Students in average Ugandan schools lack sufficient nutrients; only 28% energy needs, 64% proteins, 40% vitamins, and 42% iron. The deficiency, which affects health and academic productivity, is caused by high costs of nutritious foods attributed to post-harvest food loss and waste (FLW) along the critical value chains. For instance, between 30% 50% of harvested fruits and vegetables and 20-25% of root-crops are lost annually (Fingo 2023). Small and medium-level farmers stockpile their harvests because of lack of basic skills and technologies for postharvest handling, food preservation and processing (FAO 2019; Viola 2017). FLW is associated with foodborne illnesses and food poisoning (caused by aflatoxins, molding and microbial pathogens). Part of the project activities is to skill students to engage in availing nutrient-rich human feeds through operating two types of projects; 1. Producing nutritious food components whose specific activities include; a. smart-urban farming of vegetables (mushrooms, onions, tomatoes, variety of greens); b. producing organic pesticides; c. composting for bio-fertilizers; d. rearing chicken, rabbits, fish, and pigs (off-campus); e. food-waste recycling and black-soldier-fly-larvae rearing (to secure nutrient-rich feeds for the livestock); 2. Post-harvest food preservation and processing whose activities include; a. food processing/preservation via shredding, drying, heat-sterilization; b. food fortification (mixing various nutrient components); c. generating clean energy (solar and briquettes) to power preservation and processing processes. Besides boosting nutrition, the project promotes circularity and enhances environmental sustainability. The green entrepreneurship nurtured by the project enables income generation and job creation along food production and distribution value chain.

core_fields.title: A Community Bakehouse: Transforming Lives through Social Enterprise
core_fields.description: The proposed Bakehouse will produce nutritious snacks, buns, biscuits, cakes, and bread using millets like ragi, bajra, and whole wheat. It aims to 1) support immune-compromised care home children, infants, and patients, 2) offer baking and entrepreneurship training for rural youth, especially women, and 3) provide affordable, healthy baked goods for the rural community. This initiative fosters nutritional awareness and community empowerment while establishing a sustainable social enterprise.
core_fields.abstract: St. Gregorios Dayabhavan prioritizes food security to support immune-compromised care home children, HIV/AIDS patients, infants, and caregiving staff. Additionally, it serves 425 non-residential children from rural, disease-affected households, providing meals, education, and medicines. Beyond the campus, nearly 10,000 beneficiaries, including slum dwellers, elderly poor, and migrants in Tumkur district, receive dry food kits and meal parcels as part of its community outreach. This project aims to produce nutritious snacks buns, cakes, biscuits, and bread using millet-based ingredients like ragi and jowar. It will address hunger relief and dietary needs while promoting a healthy diet. Rural women will play key roles in food production, packaging, and sales, gaining entrepreneurial skills and fostering a sustainable social enterprise model. The initiative involves installing baking equipment dough mixers, ovens, bread slicer, chiller, and storage facilities in a 1,625 sq. ft. existing building at the Kunigal campus. Automation ensures hygienic, fatigue-free operations, minimizes waste and simplifies processes for rural women. The production will meet the needs of care home residents and disease-affected families while generating a surplus for affordable sales to rural households and nearby communities. With low operational costs and energy-efficient tools, the project ensures economic viability and scalability. Cost estimates are USD 19910 (kitchen equipment, stipend for trainees, food license) with a 12-month timeline. The project will serve over 10,000 beneficiaries annually, fulfilling a mandate of community service while fostering nutrition awareness and economic empowerment.

core_fields.title: Sustaining Village Livelihood Project
core_fields.description: The project will provide a start-up flock of five goats, and a package of mindset change sessions to 20 vulnerable families. When the goats reproduce, the initial beneficiaries will pass the off-springs and skills to another set of 20 households who will also pass on the off-spring and skills until all the ultra-poor households are reached. The Project will promote use of goat dung to produce organic fertilizer for use in beneficiaries fields.
core_fields.abstract: According to the 2018 Population and Housing Census, Balaka District s poverty level is at 66.9% against the national incidence of 58.8%. Between 2010 and 2019, the contribution of agriculture as the main source of household-level income declined from 70% to below 50% (Escaping Poverty in Malawi Requires Improved Agricultural Productivity, Climate Resilience, and Structural Transformation - World Bank . Ironically, information about weather forecasts does not reach the communities, and they end up cultivating crops which do not fit into the weather pattern for the particular year thereby experiencing perpetual food insecurity. Additionally, ultra-poor households have challenges in adopting other livelihood options such as animal husbandry because of both affordability and mindset factors. Malawi Government effects unconditional social cash transfers to ultra-poor households in order to cater for basic needs. However, about two thirds of the households 73% for the Comparison group) have transfer shares of less than 20 percent, which is considered the recommended level for expecting widespread impacts (Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme Longitudinal Impact Evaluation: Baseline Report, December 2022). Even so, SCTP beneficiaries are usually prevented from accessing additional humanitarian support on the pretext that they should let others benefit as well. The project will support ultra-poor households including women and persons with disabilities with goats, mindset change sessions and support towards climate-smart agriculture practices, so that they should transition to more secure livelihoods, and start building their asset base. Community awareness will address issues of food-waste and inadequate capacity on agro-processing, value addition and utilization.

core_fields.title: An outreach project: Leveraging circularity in fish farming through BSFL production using horticultural waste.
core_fields.description: The proposed project is intended to promote fish farming through the application of circularity principles. The project aimed at empowering farmers; enhance waste management by conducting outreach activities. Specifically, a demonstration model on Black Soldier fly larvae (BSFL) production and fish farming will be developed, farmers will be trained and finally extension manual and policy brief will be developed. Production of fish using BSFL produced using organic waste will increase fish while maintaining clean environment.
core_fields.abstract: One of the challenges facing the aquaculture sector is the excessive cost of feed. The production of black soldier fly larvae will function as an alternative source of feed protein. Research has been conducted on the production, applicability, and benefits of black soldier fly larvae using circular economy principles. Different bio-waste has been used in BSFL using livestock manure (Dzepe et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2013), crop residues (Mutafela, 2015), and brewery waste (Eggink et al., 2022). BSFL has been used in aquaculture, poultry feed, and waste management. Despite voluminous scientific publications on the production and use of BSFL, small-scale fish farmers and environmental officers are not conversant in the production of BSFL and its advantages in animal nutrition and waste management. The proposed project is intended to use the existing scientific knowledge to address the future challenge of food and environment using innovative outreach activities. Immediate benefits include reduced feeding expenses for farmers, improved farm profitability, and a clean environment. Long-term sustainable benefits include reduced reliance on fishmeal and lower carbon footprints in aquaculture operations. The beneficiaries of this project will include fish farmers, poultry keepers, extension agents, environmental officers, and the community at large. Fish farmers and poultry keepers will benefit from access to affordable, high-quality black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) feed. Extension agents will gain knowledge and tools to promote sustainable aquaculture practices, while environmental officers will benefit from improved waste management. It is envisaged that this project will contribute significantly to food security.

core_fields.title: Empowering Communities with Sustainable Food: Mushroom Grow Blocks and Free Bareroot Plant Distribution
core_fields.description: Our project provides free oyster mushroom grow blocks and bareroot starts of herbs, berries, vegetables, and fruit trees to communities. By building a greenhouse for propagation and distribution, we aim to nourish families, teach sustainable food cultivation, and promote self-sufficiency. Partnering with schools, churches, missions, and community groups, we empower individuals to grow their own nutritious food, fostering healthier communities and addressing food insecurity sustainably.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses food insecurity by combining sustainable food cultivation with community empowerment, aligning with the Seeding The Future Global Food System Challenge. By providing free oyster mushroom grow blocks and bareroot starts of herbs, berries, vegetables, and fruit trees, we empower individuals and families to grow their own nutritious food, fostering self-sufficiency and reducing reliance on external sources. Problem and Relevance: Food insecurity impacts 13.5% of U.S. households, up from 12.8% in 2022, with rural areas disproportionately affected. Nine of the ten counties with the highest food insecurity are rural. Traditional food assistance programs address immediate needs but lack sustainable, long-term solutions. Solution: Our ready-to-fruit oyster mushroom grow blocks are nutrient-dense, fast-growing, and easy to use. Bareroot plants diversify food options and ensure long-term sustainability. Oyster mushrooms, rich in protein, essential amino acids, B-vitamins, and minerals, improve diets while requiring minimal resources. A greenhouse will support year-round propagation and distribution, increasing food security in underserved areas. Scientific and Technical Insights: Oyster mushrooms efficiently convert agricultural waste into nutrient-dense food within weeks. Bareroot plants, propagated during dormancy, adapt well to diverse climates and optimize water and nutrient uptake, supporting localized food production and resilience. Alignment with Challenge Goals: Transformational Impact: Empowers communities to address food insecurity sustainably. Sustainability and Health: Promotes eco-friendly cultivation and reduces waste. Equitable Access: Ensures fresh, nutritious food for underserved populations. This scalable solution fosters sustainable food systems, improves nutrition, and builds community resilience.

core_fields.title: Liberian Farmers' Empowerment Initiatives (LFEI).
core_fields.description: SYCADI's Liberian Farmers Empowerment Initiative (LFEI) project focuses on sustainable agriculture. The key areas are improving agricultural productivity, introducing modern agriculture techniques, and providing good livelihoods. Through the availability of resources such as full training, distribution of farm inputs and the practicing of the farmers, the objective is to develop, stabilize, and secure food as well as create economic opportunities throughout Liberia.
core_fields.abstract: The Liberian Farmers' Empowerment Initiative (LFEI) project solves the worst problems of food insecurity, low agricultural productivity, and unemployment that Liberia is facing. A very large number of farmers find themselves in difficulties because of outdated farming methods, little access to resources, and the risks of changing climates resulting in poor production and economic instability. The problem is being solved by the application of modern and climate-smart farming techniques and establishing a sustainable agricultural system. SYCADI applies greenhouse technology and precision farming practices to the high yield, low resource use varieties of seeds and newly introduced farming methods. Apart from that, training programs enable farmers to acquire more practical skills, thereby ensuring the transmission of the knowledge to them and the empowerment of the community. The short-term benefits comprise higher crop yields and greater incomes for the farmers as well as increasing food availability for the communities. It is the one that guarantees environmental sustainability, facilitates education by establishing demonstration sites in schools, and creates employment that leads to economic growth in the long term. In the process of empowerment of farmers, this initiative also promotes social fairness and helps communities step out of the vicious circle of poverty and dependence. This project is not only a reinforcement of the Liberian agricultural sector but also a presentation towards the global sustainability efforts, thereby, the individuals, the communities, and the environment will benefit.

core_fields.title: PROMOTION OF GRAIN AMARANTHUS CULTIVATION (A.cruentus) AND COMPOSITE FLOUR PRODUCTION FOR SUSTAINABLE NUTRITION AND ECONOMIC EMPOWERMENT IN TANZANIA
core_fields.description: Potential of grain amaranth in meeting nutrition needs makes our project promotes its cultivation to smallholder farmers , focusing on producing nutrient-rich composite flour using grain amaranths for local consumption. Formulating, scaling, grain amaranths food products and environmentally friendly processing methods, will improve food security, create economic opportunities to women, youth, SMEs, provide affordable, nutritious food. The initiative also promotes climate resilience, offering scalable solution to address malnutrition and support sustainable agricultural development.
core_fields.abstract: This project seeks to develop a nutritious composite flour (NCF) for a healthy diet based on underutilized amaranth grains, maize, and millet as an alternative to traditional diets. The innovative NCF will avert the problem of malnutrition and food insecurity, which is the effect of global food system challenges. The NCF will be formulated using linear programming at a specified ratio to provide 50-70% of Recommended Daily Allowances (RDA) of iron and zinc, safety and sensory done to ensure trust for consumers. By integrating the innovative composite flour into local diets, fosters a contribution initiative to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of zero hunger and no poverty by 2030. An education will be provided to raise awareness on the versatility and ease of cultivating amaranths for the sustainable production of innovative NCF while improving planetary health. Women and youth farmers will be supported to cultivate grain amaranths, encouraged to enter contract farming agreements with small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in food processing. SMEs will purchase amaranth grains from farmers, creating a reliable market for the crop and providing economic opportunities for local farmers. Amaranth roots, stems, and leaves will be used for poultry feed, poultry rewarding manures to grain amaranths. The model warrants NCF sustainable production, affordability, and equitable access by marginalized communities. Advocating decision-makers to integrate grain amaranths into food systems and public health programs. Solving these problems is critical because malnutrition not only causes needless human suffering but also reduces physical work productivity, learning capacity, and innovation

core_fields.title: Regenerative Agro-Solutions for Equitable and Nutritious Food Systems in Tigray
core_fields.description: This project proposes to empower disabled veterans and their communities in Tigray through innovative, scalable food system solutions. It focuses on sustainable regenerative agricultural practices, increasing access to nutritious and culturally acceptable foods, and fostering consumer consciousness about healthy and sustainable diets. Leveraging innovative technologies and community-driven approaches, the initiative aims to create a resilient and inclusive food system, ultimately benefiting vulnerable populations and contributing to planetary health.
core_fields.abstract: This project addresses food insecurity, environmental degradation, and socio-economic marginalization in Tigray, focusing on disabled veterans and their communities. The region s degraded lands, limited access to nutritious food, and lack of sustainable farming practices make it critical to develop innovative solutions. The proposed solution integrates regenerative agriculture, inclusive value chain development, and community education. Techniques like agroforestry, intercropping, and biochar application restore soil health, increase productivity, and sequester carbon, revitalizing degraded lands. Digital platforms and interactive workshops educate communities about sustainable diets, empowering them to make conscious food choices. Additionally, disabled veterans receive training in farming, processing, and marketing, creating inclusive economic opportunities and enhancing community resilience. The innovation lies in combining advanced regenerative practices, culturally tailored education, and inclusive economic models. Immediate benefits include improved soil fertility, increased crop yields, and better access to nutritious food for 10,000 community members. Long-term, the initiative enhances food security, boosts livelihoods, and establishes scalable models for sustainable agriculture. By restoring 100 hectares of land and equipping 500 veterans, the project fosters environmental and social sustainability while contributing to a global transition toward equitable, nutritious food systems.

core_fields.abstract: The core problem is that low-income families spend most of their household income on food, and yet, 735 million people are malnourished. Our current food system structure prioritizes large-scale production, global connectivity, and the concentration of industry stakeholders. Animal-sourced foods are expensive and out-of-reach for low-income families but are seen as aspirational purchases, especially as household incomes increase. Current food system transformation programs include social behavior change campaigns that explain to low-income families why animal sourced foods are nutritionally important, resulting in low-income families spending large proportions of their household expenditure on small portions of expensive animal sourced foods that most often get consumed by the men of the household, and not by female household members or children. To address these problems Tailored Food will: Evidence Based Council Create an EAT-Lancet style research report, that will exist as a resource for all food system stakeholders and community-based advocacy groups, widely recognized as the evidence-based data needed to prove that children do grow to be healthy and thriving adults on a diverse range of plant-rich diets in different cultural and economic contexts around the world. Multi-year Entrepreneur Partnerships Scale bottom-up impact, collaborating with small-scale entrepreneurs in the countries most impacted by malnutrition, we launch and scale nutritious low-cost food products, with over 7.3 million meals produced and sold to date. Strategic Consulting Projects for Larger Organizations Scale top down impact, we complete food systems mapping, investment cases and strategic partnership building for clients such as UNICEF.

core_fields.title: Enhancing functionality of insect-based ingredients through sustainable processing
core_fields.description: This two-year project aims to design functional insect-based ingredients through sustainable processing techniques. We focus on characterizing and enhancing the nutritional and technological functionalities of insect flours using physical, biotechnological, and combined treatments. This innovation will improve consumer acceptance of insect-based foods, generate new product development, and contribute to the circularity of agriculture, aligning with global efforts to create a sustainable, nutritious food system.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses the challenge of sustainable nutrition by developing functional insect-based ingredients through advanced processing techniques. As livestock farming significantly impacts climate change, insect proteins offer a low-environmental-footprint alternative with superior nutritional qualities. We enhance the digestibility and functionality of these proteins using a combination of physical and biotechnological methods. This approach not only improves the appeal of insect-based foods by incorporating them into familiar products but also optimizes their nutritional and functional properties for broader application in the food industry. The insights from studying the effects of various processing methods on insect flours have revealed that tailored treatments can significantly enhance their applicability as ingredients in the food industry. The immediate benefits include increased protein and fiber intake for consumers, while producers and farmers gain from the expanded use of sustainable protein sources, increasing circular agriculture practices. Schools and communities might benefit from access to more nutritious and sustainable food options, contributing to overall environmental health and food security.

core_fields.title: Upcycling whey into biofertilizer and livestock feed using black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens)
core_fields.description: This project proposes the development of an innovative system to collect and upcycle whey from cheese production by integrating a logistics optimization system and Black Soldier Fly Larvae (Hermetia illucens). This project will result in: 1) an efficient collection system for whey from small rural dairy facilities, 2) conversion of this byproduct into nutrient-rich biomass, ideal for supplement for livestock feed and 3) transformation of fermentation residues into organic fertilizer (high nitrogen content).
core_fields.abstract: Whey, a byproduct of the cheese industry, poses a significant environmental challenge if not properly managed, leading to soil and water contamination due to its elevated biological oxygen demand (BOD) and chemical oxygen demand (COD), which converts whey into a major pollutant worldwide. Globally, the cheese industry produces approximately 115 million tons of whey annually, with nearly 47% being discharged untreated into wastewater systems. In rural communities and in small dairy facilities in Mexico, this issue is further exacerbated as whey is often discarded without treatment, intensifying pollution problems while overlooking its potential as a valuable resource. Additionally, whey production is highly dispersed, making its efficient collection and transportation a logistical challenge. Addressing these issues provides a critical opportunity to transform whey from an environmental liability into a key component of sustainable and circular economy solutions. This proposal employs black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens) to transform whey into nutrient-rich biomass and organic fertilizers. This biotechnological process leverages the larvae's ability to metabolize organic matter and convert it into high-quality proteins and lipids, ideal for livestock feed. Additionally, the residual material from larval cultivation is rich in nitrogen compounds, making it suitable for sustainable agriculture as fertilizer. Immediate and long-term benefits: 1) Reduction of environmental pollution in rural communities, particularly by reducing waste disposal problems from small-scale cheese producers; 2) Generation of sustainable, low-cost products for farmers and livestock producers; 3) Strengthening of economic development of rural communities.

core_fields.title: Demonstrating Impact for Growth: Charlie Cart s Evaluation of Hands-on Mobile Food Education
core_fields.description: The Charlie Cart Project (CCP) Evaluation of Hands-on Mobile Food Education will analyze the impact of CCP programming on children participating in CCP lessons. We seek to understand our effectiveness in changing kids attitudes and behaviors towards healthy food and in making food choices supportive of their health and of the environment. Understanding our impact on participants will enable us to bring hands-on food education to scale and help transform the food system.
core_fields.abstract: Food and cooking education is recognized as an effective prevention measure for children at risk of diet-related disease. Yet, most children receive just 8 hours annually, far below the 40 hours needed to make healthy, informed choices. Complicating this issue, most existing food education programs lack affordable, sustainable strategies to address the practical barriers to hands-on cooking instruction. At The Charlie Cart Project (CCP), we believe that if we can t bring kids to the kitchen, we can bring the kitchen to the kids. CCP provides an innovative and accessible food education program, improving culinary literacy and nutritional access for communities nationwide. Our compact, mobile kitchen-on-wheels includes all the tools and equipment needed to get 30 participants cooking. Our program also includes training and resources for educators, and a 54-lesson K-5 standards-aligned curriculum. Our skills-focused curriculum is designed to expose students to a variety of new flavors and ingredients, while building their ability and confidence to prepare healthy meals from scratch. Currently in 600+ communities in 47 states, CCP reaches 500,000 children each year with foundational skills to lead healthy, thriving lives. In a recent evaluation, over half the students tried a new food; the number of students who loved a food after a CCP class increased by 25%; 69% of participants want to make the recipe again. With support from IFT, CCP will fully measure impact on educators and participants, provide the evidence-base for exponential growth, and bring hands-on food education to scale across the country.

To resolve this challenge, GLF has included to its agro-processing operations the production of feeds, fertilizers and pesticides from black solider flies and wishes to expand this investment by equipping it with the technologies required to increase the quality and quantity of these products. The products from the BSF facility will be sold to the smallholder farmers that GLF works with across Uganda. To assist them to access these products at a reasonable cost while at the same time enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness with which they serve the marketplace, the smallholder farmers will be organized into Cottage Industries with facilities through which they can collectively produce and sell their products and services to the marketplace. The Cottage Industries will be supported to digitize their operations for greater levels of productivity and profitability, organize their communities into business groups that can support their production and distribution efforts and establish collaborations with BDS providers that can support their advancement. core_fields.title: "Bee the Change: Ghana s Cashew & Honey Impact Project"
core_fields.description: Our project empowers smallholder cashew growers and women beekeepers in Ghana by improving pollination through bee feed supplements, increasing cashew yields and honey production. Through locally produced nutritious cashews and honey, this sustainable solution increases farmers' income, improves access to a healthy diet, promotes better food diversity, nutritional security for local communities, and creates jobs for rural women. By strengthening bee colonies, we promote climate-resilient farming.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses a critical challenge in global food security: the decline in bee populations due to environmental stressors such as climate change, pesticide exposure, and habitat loss, which reduces crop yields and threatens smallholder farmers' livelihoods. We offer a comprehensive pollination solution, combining our bee feed supplement with professional agricultural and beekeeping consultancy. The supplement strengthens bees colonies, making them more resilient to stress and effective in pollination. This results in higher crop yields, better quality produce, and increased farmer income. Our technical support and training programs ensure farmers can integrate pollination strategies effectively, maximizing impact. The scientific insight behind our solution is that stronger bee colonies lead to better pollination performance. Trials in apples, onion seeds, and coffee have shown yield improvement up to 40% The immediate benefits include higher yields for smallholder farmers, increased honey production, and improved biodiversity. In the long term, the project supports food security, nutrition improvement, job creation for women beekeepers, and sustainable farming practices. We also see potential for impact beyond farms, including schools and community centers, by promoting pollination education programs and establishing small-scale beekeeping initiatives. These efforts can enhance local food diversity, improve nutrition through daily balanced diets, and empower communities to integrate sustainable, climate-resilient agricultural practices. In Ghana, our focus on cashew farmers and women-led beekeeping addresses both economic and nutritional needs, helping vulnerable communities build climate-resilient livelihoods while enhancing access to healthy, local food sources.

core_fields.description: Harcourt Farm empowers farmers by converting organic waste into valuable resources using black soldier flies. core_fields.abstract: Problem Statement: In Kenya, the reliance on imported protein sources for animal feeds has led to high costs and compromised quality. This situation negatively impacts the affordability and nutritional value of animal feeds, posing a challenge for farmers. Additionally, the extensive use of inorganic fertilizers has degraded soil health, resulting in poor crop yields and financial losses for farmers. When farmers cannot produce quality feed, there is no food security and nutrition, leading to hunger. The lack of proper waste disposal systems further exacerbates the issue, as organic waste accumulates in landfills, producing methane gas and contributing to greenhouse gas emissions. Solution Statement: Harcourt Agri Eco Farm Limited addresses these challenges by utilizing black soldier flies to convert organic waste into valuable resources. By producing high-quality, affordable animal protein, Harcourt ensures that animal feeds are both nutritious and cost-effective. The farm also generates frass fertilizer, which repairs and enriches the soil, leading to improved crop yields and increased profitability for farmers ensuring farmers are producing quality and healthy food. Furthermore, Harcourt's waste collection and conversion process reduces the environmental impact of organic waste, mitigating methane emissions and promoting a sustainable ecosystem. Through these innovative practices, Harcourt Agri Eco Farm Limited supports the health and prosperity of both farmers and the environment and ensures food nutrition and security.

core_fields.title: Regenerative Food Systems For Planetary Health: Scaling Insect Farming To Sustain The Manombo Rainforest Of Madagascar
core_fields.description: HIH collaborates with rainforest communities to reverse deforestation and enhance livelihoods through scalable, community-driven solutions. Our Black Soldier Fly (BSF) farming project, supported by rigorous research and community-based pilots, addresses food security, regenerative agriculture, and reforestation. Insect frass fertilizer improves crop yields and seedling survival, while behavioral studies highlight the growing acceptance of insect-based foods. Field trials validate BSF farming s feasibility, empowering smallholder farmers and contributing to sustainability, biodiversity conservation, and a climate-resilient future.
core_fields.abstract: Rainforests, vital for planetary health, face destruction due to unsustainable farming and economic pressures on local communities. These communities, disproportionately affected by climate change, often lack access to sustainable agricultural resources and funding. Health In Harmony addresses this by integrating innovative, community-driven solutions. Black Soldier Fly (BSF) frass as an organic fertilizer has shown the ability to enhance vegetable yields and seedling survival rates for agriculture and reforestation efforts compared to traditional cattle manure. Minimal doses of BSF frass improve crop productivity, reduce dependence on cattle manure and chemical fertilizers, while promoting ecological restoration. By providing high-quality health care, communities no longer needed to extract resources from the forest to pay for it. Instead, they became partners in forest conservation by establishing a non-cash payment system with seeds and seedlings, as showcased by Jones et al., 2020. Food systems became responsible for turning communities that relied on slash-and-burn agriculture and bush meat into active partners in protecting and recovering tropical forests, promoting food security, and reducing spillover risks, as shown by Huntington et al., 2024. Recently, WHO and IUCN also spotlighted HIH's successes in using agriculture to connect human health and biodiversity conservation in Madagascar (WHO-IUCN, 2024). By investing in locally relevant, scalable solutions like frass-based fertilizers and reforestation initiatives, Health In Harmony collaborates with communities to protect their rainforests while improving food security. This holistic approach, rooted in Indigenous knowledge and data-driven insights, ensures immediate benefits like increased agricultural productivity and long-term impact through climate resilience and biodiversity conservation.

core_fields.description: In Rwanda 33% of children are stunted, most of them are from rural areas, and with families below the poverty level We aim to bring fresh eggs, egg nutrition education, and cooking demos closer to them at affordable prices, in addition, we aim to produce whole egg powder to increase the variety of feeding the egg. core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses the critical issue of child stunting in Rwanda, where 33% of children are affected (RDHS 2020), primarily in rural and low-income areas. Poor access to affordable, nutrient-rich foods like eggs exacerbates this problem. We aim to bring fresh, affordable eggs closer to remote and vulnerable families, particularly those with at-risk children to improve their nutrition. By establishing local egg kiosks and delivering them directly to these communities, we ensure accessibility and promote consistent egg consumption. Additionally, we plan to introduce whole egg powder, providing a shelf-stable, versatile option to diversify egg consumption for households, schools, and community programs. Our approach combines affordable pricing, nutrition education, and cooking demonstrations to empower families with knowledge and tools to improve dietary habits. This innovation improves the high nutritional value of eggs, addressing protein and micronutrient deficiencies that contribute to stunting. Immediate benefits include improved child nutrition, better dietary practices, and enhanced food security in vulnerable communities. In the long term, this initiative supports healthier generations, reduces stunting rates, and empowers local economies through job creation. The environment also benefits from reduced food waste due to whole egg powder production, ensuring the nutritional value of eggs reaches more people. By bridging the gap between egg producers and underserved families, we create a sustainable model to fight malnutrition and promote health equity in Rwanda's 2 most districts with high rates of malnutrition which are Nyabihu and Burera districts.

core_fields.abstract: The global food system faces critical challenges, including nutritional deficiencies, unsustainable agricultural practices, and environmental degradation. Himalayan Hemp Nutrition addresses these issues by utilizing the extraordinary properties of hemp to create nutrient-dense, eco-conscious products, such as protein-rich hemp seed powder, cold-pressed hemp seed oil, and hemp seed hearts. These products deliver essential nutrients, including Omega 3-6-9 fatty acids, plant-based proteins, and micronutrients, addressing gaps in dietary health and fostering wellness. Hemp s regenerative agricultural benefits, such as soil restoration, carbon sequestration, and low water usage, offer a sustainable farming alternative. The project empowers rural farmers and artisans, creating equitable livelihood opportunities while preserving indigenous hemp varieties. By implementing controlled, environment-friendly farming and post-harvest practices, it reduces greenhouse gas emissions and enhances soil health, promoting sustainability. The solution emerged from the scientific understanding of hemp’s nutritional and environmental advantages. Hemp s high nutrient density addresses dietary imbalances, while its sustainable cultivation supports planetary health. The project creates immediate benefits for end-users by providing affordable, nutritious food alternatives and long-term environmental benefits through regenerative farming. Himalayan Hemp Nutrition directly benefits farmers by offering a profitable alternative crop, schools and communities through education on hemp s health and environmental advantages, and society by promoting sustainable agriculture. The solution also appeals to conscious consumers, fostering a shift toward sustainable diets. Overall, the innovation strengthens food security, enhances nutrition, supports rural livelihoods, and contributes to global environmental sustainability.

core_fields.title: Home Chocolat Mass-Production Readiness
core_fields.description: Home Chocolat empowers consumers to create personalized, high-quality chocolate at home with regenerative cacao kits, innovative tools, and engaging content. This award will enable us to finalize The Chocolatier appliance for mass production and develop compelling marketing materials to secure funding for its launch. core_fields.abstract: Home Chocolat addresses the lack of personalization, transparency, and sustainability in traditional chocolate production. Conventional chocolate is mass-produced, often containing additives and processed ingredients, while its supply chain faces significant ethical and environmental challenges, including deforestation, child labor, and lack of transparency in indirect sourcing. This system disconnects consumers from the chocolate-making process, limiting their awareness and engagement. Our innovation, the patented CocoaBlox kits, and The Chocolatier appliance, empower consumers to create high-quality chocolate tailored to their preferences using regenerative cacao and clean ingredients. Each CocoaBlox is a single ingredient processed in cocoa butter, designed for easy melting and mixing. Paired with The Chocolatier appliance, this system simplifies the traditionally complex process, providing a seamless, professional-grade chocolate-making experience at home. This solution is based on the insight that breaking chocolate-making into manageable, high-quality natural components can empower consumers while addressing sustainability. By shifting the final stages of production to the consumer s home, we reduce the environmental impact of large-scale processing and transportation, while engaging the consumers. Immediate benefits include healthier, customizable chocolate, with consumers controlling ingredients to meet dietary needs. Schools and communities gain educational opportunities in sustainability and chocolate-making, while farmers benefit from the promotion of regenerative cacao, encouraging eco-friendly practices. In the long term, Home Chocolat fosters sustainable consumption, reduces environmental impact, and connects consumers to the artistry of their food, transforming chocolate into a conscious, creative, and sustainable experience.

core_fields.title: AQUAPONICS ACCELERATED: A model to transform global systems for nutritious food security and sustainable livelihoods in marginalised communities in South Africa and beyond
core_fields.description: INMED Aquaponics Social Enterprise is a hub-and-spokes network of physical and virtual sites which mentor farmers from established INMED Aquaponics systems and learning centers in schools and universities. This initiative is supported by a production, consolidation, and training hub, along with satellite farmers, and offers real-time support through web- and app-based platforms. Building on INMED's expertise in climate-smart aquaponics, the initiative empowers vulnerable communities including individuals with disabilities, women, and youth, helping them achieve food security.
core_fields.abstract: Although often argued to be the least contributor of greenhouse gas emissions, the Southern Africa region is one of the most affected regions by climate calamities which causes serious drawbacks in these thriving economies including unpredictable rainfall patterns, prolonged droughts, and declining soil fertility threatening food security. These challenges make traditional farming methods less viable, especially in regions where water is scarce and arable land is limited. In response to these growing pressures, aquaponics offers a sustainable solution that could revolutionise food production in these vulnerable areas. Aquaponics combines fish farming with soil-less plant cultivation in a closed-loop system, where fish-waste provides nutrients for plants, and plants naturally filter and purify the water for the fish. This method uses up to 90% less water than traditional farming, making it especially relevant for water-scarce regions. It also doesn t rely on soil, enabling farming in areas with degraded land. This innovation solves the twin problems of water scarcity and food insecurity by creating a highly efficient, eco-friendly farming system. The scientific principle behind aquaponics is based on the natural symbiosis of ecosystems, where organisms support each other's growth. The technical insight lies in applying this balance to a controlled, productive environment. For farmers, aquaponics provides an opportunity to grow food year-round with fewer resources. Consumers benefit from fresh, locally sourced produce and fish, while schools and communities use aquaponics as a tool for education and empowerment. Overall, aquaponics contributes to long-term sustainability, resilience, and food security in the face of climate change.

core_fields.title: Savanna Flours: From Nature to Nourishment
core_fields.description: This project transforms Mozambique s underutilized native resources, canhu nuts and wild green bananas, into sustainable, gluten-free flours with high nutritional value. By addressing food security, generating income for rural women, and promoting environmental conservation through sustainable practices, it fosters economic empowerment while aligning with multiple Sustainable Development Goals. Through scalable production, strategic market integration, and active community engagement, it offers a replicable, impactful model for inclusive, sustainable development and improved livelihoods across Mozambique and beyond
core_fields.abstract: Mozambique faces a multifaceted challenge encompassing food insecurity, economic reliance on imported wheat flour, and environmental degradation. Despite the abundance of canhu nuts and wild green bananas, over 95% of these resources are discarded, representing a significant loss of nutritional and economic potential. This untapped opportunity exacerbates the country's vulnerability to food shortages and perpetuates dependency on expensive imports. This project offers an innovative solution by transforming these underutilized native resources into high-value, gluten-free alternative flours. Canhu nut flour is rich in proteins, healthy fats, and fiber, while wild green banana flour provides resistant starch, a key component for digestive health. Together, these flours enhance dietary diversity, providing affordable and nutrient-rich food options that address local dietary deficiencies and reduce Mozambique s reliance on imported wheat flour. The initiative also integrates sustainable harvesting and scalable production methods to ensure environmental conservation and climate resilience. Training local communities in resource management and establishing cooperatives fosters equitable participation in the value chain, creating stable income opportunities, particularly for women and youth. By reducing food waste and conserving biodiversity, the project promotes a circular economy while contributing to the country s Sustainable Development Goals. In addition to its local impact, this project lays the foundation for broader socioeconomic benefits. Through community engagement, market integration, and replicable practices, it not only addresses Mozambique s immediate challenges but also positions the country as a model for sustainable development, ensuring long-term environmental, economic, and social resilience.

core_fields.title: Smart Technology for Agricultural Resilience and Sustainability (STARS) in Flood-prone areas of Northern Bangladesh
core_fields.description: Our STARS project is a data-driven farm analytics solution, powered by AIoT and predictive agro-scientific models, delivers actionable insights to smallholder farmers, enhancing productivity by 15%, reducing costs by 19%, and carbon emissions by 4.3%. Our scalable solution bridges data gaps in agriculture, links farmers to B2Bs, and fosters sustainable practices, impacting 23,000+ farmers in Bangladesh. By 2026, we aim to serve 100,000 farmers globally, revolutionizing agriculture and ensuring food security.
core_fields.abstract: The lack of actionable data on soil, weather, and sustainable practices drives rapid soil degradation, poor productivity, disrupts food security and generates massive carbon footprints for 7M small farmers in Bangladesh and 600M globally. Human-dependent extension services in the global south are inadequate, unscalable and often inaccurate, failing to deliver timely & critical insights to farmers and B2B stakeholders like banks, buyers, and suppliers, hampering productivity, limiting profitability for all and ultimately disrupting the food supply system. So, this data scarcity across the entire agricultural ecosystem is a global challenge and a trillion-dollar opportunity to transform agriculture and ensure food security with smart, scalable, and data-driven solutions. We see the data gap in agriculture as a trillion-dollar, global opportunity. That s why we re building the Google Analytics of Agriculture a scalable and 1500x faster, farm analytics engine powered by IoT, predictive agro-science models, and proprietary devices like soil testers and weather stations. It delivers site & crop-specific farm analytics to the farmers mostly using digital channels to improve their agronomy. The engine also tracks the farmers activity and facilitates targeted lead generation, and direct farmer-linkage for our B2B partners, increasing profitability for all, which eventually ensures food security. Reduced carbon emissions and lower soil degradations are the by-products of our solution. With proven results, including a 15% yield improvement and a 4.3% carbon reduction, iPAGE s scalable model not only uplifts farming communities but also fosters regional food security by bridging the critical data gap in agriculture.

core_fields.title: Empowering 10K smallholder primary food producers with Climate-Smart Agro-advisory and Early Warnings for Resilient Food Systems.
core_fields.description: Ignitia wants to provide climate risk and early warning solutions to enhance food security for smallholder farmers in Kenya and Uganda. Through our automated climate smart agro- advisory tool to farmers, we deliver localized, actionable weather forecasts and agricultural guidance to help farmers make informed decisions, reduce crop loss, and improve productivity. Our service empowers farmers to adapt to climate variability, fostering sustainable food systems and strengthening resilience against climate-related challenges.
core_fields.abstract: Ignitia addresses the growing challenge of climate risks in agriculture, which significantly impact food security in tropical regions. By processing 33 years of meteorological data (1991 2023) at a high resolution (1-9 km), Ignitia provides hyper-localized, predictive insights on rainfall, temperature, and other critical climatic factors. This innovation integrates these insights into an automated Climate Smart Advisory system, offering actionable recommendations tailored to smallholder farmers needs. Our solution identifies and mitigates key risks, such as extreme rainfall events, prolonged dry spells, and erratic temperature patterns. These insights, delivered through digital platforms, empower farmers with real-time guidance on planting schedules, water management, and pest control strategies. The benefits are immediate and far-reaching. Farmers gain resilience to climate variability, improve yields, and reduce losses. Over time, this fosters sustainable agricultural practices, strengthens food security, and safeguards livelihoods. Additionally, by reducing food production's environmental footprint, Ignitia contributes to planetary health. Grounded in advanced data analytics and validated by on-ground impact, our innovation translates complex climate data into accessible, actionable advice. This empowers millions of smallholder farmers to thrive amidst climate uncertainties, transforming vulnerable communities into resilient contributors to the global food system.

core_fields.title: AXES: Sustainable Market Access for Agrifood MSMEs in Colombia
core_fields.description: The AXES program facilitates market access for Colombian agrifood MSMEs producing sustainable, nutritious, and affordable innovations. AXES addresses structural barriers and promotes deforestation-free supply chains, enhances rural incomes, and builds climate-smart capacities. Through tailored coaching, ecosystem collaboration, and capacity-building, the project ensures 30 MSMEs in scaling their impact, improving livelihoods for rural communities, youth, and women, while fostering resilience and contributing to sustainable food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Colombian agri food MSMEs face challenges that interfere with their growth and integration into sustainable food systems. While MSMEs represent 99.6% of firms in the country, they contribute only 5% of export value [1]. Compliance with international regulations poses additional barriers, particularly for MSMEs lacking technical capacity to adopt traceability and deforestation-free practices [2]. Moreover, financial access remains limited, with only 10% of MSMEs able to secure formal credit, restricting investment in infrastructure, innovation, and sustainable production [1]. Knowledge gaps exacerbate these issues, as most MSMEs lack expertise in regenerative agriculture further limiting their competitiveness [3]. Additionally, Colombia loses 174,000 hectares of forest annually, largely driven by unsustainable agricultural expansion [4]. Fragmented supply chains and weak market linkages isolate MSMEs, increasing transaction costs and reducing their ability to meet consumer and international market demands [2]. Addressing these challenges is critical to fostering resilient, competitive, and sustainable food systems in the country. The AXES program facilitates market access for agrofood MSMEs, promoting sustainable, nutritious, and affordable innovations. The program specifically supports 30 MSMEs by addressing structural barriers through activities such as capacity-building workshops, personalized coaching, and ecosystem activations. These interventions focus on deforestation-free, climate-smart practices, regenerative agriculture, and traceability systems that comply with EUDR (European Union Deforestation Regulation) standards and meet global market demands. The program emphasizes creating sustainable value chains, fostering investments, and enhancing MSME competitiveness. Immediate outcomes include generating 240 new jobs and boosting rural incomes, while long-term impacts focus on building resilient food systems and ensuring equitable opportunities.

core_fields.title: Agroecological Innovations for Climate-Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: This project aims to empower farmers, especially women and youth, to adopt sustainable agroecological practices. By combining traditional knowledge with modern techniques, we will improve food security, biodiversity, and climate resilience. Our approach involves research, training, and community-based initiatives to create a more sustainable and equitable food system.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Kenya Baringo County face significant challenges, including climate change, declining soil fertility, and limited access to markets. These challenges threaten food security, rural livelihoods, and environmental sustainability. Our project addresses these challenges by promoting innovative agroecological practices. By combining traditional knowledge with modern scientific techniques, we empower farmers to adopt sustainable farming methods that enhance soil health, conserve water, and reduce reliance on chemical inputs. Specific benefits include increased crop yields, improved soil fertility, reduced pesticide use, and enhanced biodiversity. Farmers will have access to new markets, fair prices, and improved livelihoods. Additionally, these practices will contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation, ensuring a sustainable future for generations to come

core_fields.title: Promoting a Home-Centered Circular Food System to Ensure Affordability, Accessibility, and Sustainability of Animal Feeds in Rwanda.
core_fields.description: Indintambwe Feeds is a Rwandan-based social enterprise revolutionizing livestock farming by commercializing black soldier fly larvae over the last 4 years and offering seven insect-based feeds to 14,500 smallholder farmers. Now, we plan to train farmers to grow black soldier fly larvae themselves, ensuring a consistent maggot supply for our feed production. Our cost-effective, nutrient-rich solution is 30% cheaper and 50% more nutritious than conventional feeds, boosting productivity and incomes of livestock farmers.
core_fields.abstract: In Rwanda, agriculture is the backbone of the economy, employing over 70% of the population. However, livestock farming critical for food security and rural livelihoods is underperforming due to the lack of access to affordable, high-quality animal feeds. Over 8 million livestock farmers depend on feed for their animals, yet 6 million remain underserved due to high costs, inconsistent supply, and poor feed quality. This gap contributes to low livestock productivity, reduced farmer income, and persistent rural poverty. Currently, the animal feed market is dominated by imported feeds, which are costly and often inaccessible for smallholder farmers. Moreover, local feed production primarily relies on traditional ingredients like maize and soybeans, which are not only expensive but also contribute to competition with human food consumption. This results in a market where small-scale livestock farmers are unable to achieve optimal yields or profitability, limiting their ability to invest in better farming practices. Indintambwe Feeds Ltd is addressing the twin challenges of inaccessibility and high costs of quality animal feeds for small-scale farmers, by leveraging black soldier fly larvae to produce insect-based feeds that are 30% cheaper and 50% more nutritious than traditional options. By leveraging insect-based feed technology, we provide an innovative solution that is: Affordable and accessible: Our feeds are 30% cheaper than traditional options. Nutrient-rich: 50% more nutritious feed products, improving livestock growth and productivity. Sustainable: Utilizing locally sourced black soldier fly larvae, we reduce reliance on conventional feed ingredients, alleviating environmental pressure and ensuring a consistent supply.

core_fields.title: Development of Community-Supported Agriculture Based on Multi-stakeholder Cooperative with Millennial Farmer as an Actor
core_fields.description: The development of Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) through multi-stakeholder cooperatives integrates millennial farmers as key actors. This model fosters collaboration among producers, consumers, and other stakeholders, ensuring shared responsibilities and benefits. Millennials bring innovation, digital proficiency, and sustainability focus, revitalizing agricultural practices. By connecting directly with communities, CSA enhances food security, supports local economies, and promotes eco-friendly farming. Multi-stakeholder governance ensures inclusivity, making the model resilient and adaptable to evolving societal and environmental needs.
core_fields.abstract: Traditional agricultural models face declining engagement from younger generations, leading to aging farmer populations and a lack of innovation in farming practices. Community-Supported Agriculture (CSA) often struggles with scalability, limited stakeholder engagement, and fragmented supply chains. Consumers demand transparency, sustainability, and locally-sourced produce, yet current systems lack effective collaboration between farmers, consumers, and supporting entities. Millennial farmers, equipped with digital skills and a sustainability mindset, are underutilized due to limited access to resources and networks. Without a comprehensive approach to integrate diverse stakeholders, agriculture risks losing its capacity to address food security, economic resilience, and environmental sustainability challenges effectively. A multi-stakeholder cooperative-based CSA offers a transformative solution, uniting farmers, consumers, and enablers in a shared governance model. Millennial farmers take center stage, leveraging their digital expertise to modernize operations and improve transparency. The cooperative framework ensures equitable decision-making, resource sharing, and financial sustainability. Digital platforms enable direct consumer engagement, strengthening trust and demand for locally-sourced, sustainable products. By integrating diverse stakeholders, the model enhances scalability and resilience, addressing supply chain gaps and promoting eco-friendly practices. This approach revitalizes agriculture, empowers younger generations, and aligns with contemporary demands for sustainability, collaboration, and community-driven solutions, ensuring long-term agricultural and societal benefits.

core_fields.title: My F&V: Navigate Your Way to Healthy Food Environments
core_fields.description: My F&V is a system designed to enhance access to diverse quality fruits&vegetables (F&V) while supporting local value chain actors. It helps users navigate food environments, track and locate F&V sources, especially mobile vendors. The system records supply-demand flow to optimize value chain efficiency. With personalized consumption goals, healthy diet information, and a reward system, it motivates healthier habits among adolescents and encourages vendors to sell quality produce, ensuring sustained F&V availability and economic benefits.
core_fields.abstract: F&V are components of a healthy diet and contribute to overall health. However, their consumption remains low among any population group in the Philippines. Our recent project and study confirmed poor dietary diversity due to low F&V intake among consumers, particularly adolescents. High F&V prices, supply chain issues, accessibility problems, and consumers' general lack of knowledge of the benefits of F&V are the key barriers to encouraging increased consumption. My F&V addresses these challenges by offering an innovative, user-centered solution. My F&V is a mobile app with Google Maps-like interface that visualizes the food environment of F&V in real-time, distinguishing between static sources (e.g., permanent market stalls) and dynamic sources (e.g., mobile hawkers, rolling stores). By integrating real-time tracking and local F&V data, the platform enables consumers to locate vendors, track routes, and plan purchases effectively toward their "F&V consumption goals". This means My F&V is also planning tool designed to empower consumers to meet regular (e.g. weekly) F&V consumption targets in line with personalized dietary goals, with reward systems and motivating interface with accurate nutrition and dietary information. The system will involve F&V vendors, vendors association and local government units, who regularly update the platform with information on stock availability, vendor routes and even value chain-related information. Vendors also benefit from increased visibility and optimized routes. Adolescents, being the less consuming age group of quality F&V and the more tech-savvy, are a key focus of the system, benefiting from improved exposure to nutritious options.

core_fields.title: Terra Doce Program: Inclusive environmental prosperity
core_fields.description: Terra Doce promotes environmental, economic, and social transformation in degraded Atlantic Forest lands by replacing harmful practices with sustainable and regenerative agroforestry. This approach produces high-quality, pesticide-free food rich in complex nutrients while providing financial benefits to many rural families. Working on a landscape scale, we will offer our products with a Terra Doce certificate, which tells the story of this life-changing movement and provides consumers with the opportunity to make more conscious choices.
core_fields.abstract: Instituto Terra is located in the Doce River basin, Minas Gerais, Brazil, originally home to the abundant Atlantic Forest. Over the years, this region has suffered significant damage due to deforestation, mining, extensive agriculture, and livestock farming, causing soil degradation, silting up of rivers, reduced water infiltration and biodiversity losses. More recently, in 2015, the collapse of one ore tailings dam in Mariana, Minas Gerais, caused profound socioeconomic and environmental impacts across the region. In the social sphere, there has been an intense rural exodus, resulting from the impoverishment of the soil and living conditions in the countryside. As a result, various problems related to unemployment, urban violence and the poor urban structure in terms of basic sanitation, health and education mean that the region is classified as having an average human development index (HDI). We aim to transform the Doce river basin into an example of socio-environmental resilience by integrating conservation, forest restoration, and income generation, while promoting water security and the well-being of local communities. We offer technical assistance to transform rural productivity, implementing agroforestry systems to improve farm's productivity and produce quality while restoring soil and water. We also offer environmental education to children, adolescents and young adults, showing them a different perspective on their own land and how they can engage and improve it. With this project we aim to provide financial gain to many rural families, while restoring water springs, forests and the soil, all being realized by the people from that land.

core_fields.description: Nutrient-rich small fish production project intended to produce dried, small fish powder for the preservation of nutrient-dense fish for a healthy and affordable option for consumers especially those who need it most such as young children, and pregnant and lactating women.
core_fields.abstract: With poverty levels in Myanmar predicted to rise from 25% to 50% of the population, the impact on human nutrition will be dramatic in terms of reduced calorific intake, dietary diversity and micronutrient intake. While in Zambia, poverty and food insecurity are high, particularly among rural populations. Forty-two percent of people live in extreme poverty and more than half (54%) experience hunger where they do not have enough food to eat. Malnutrition is high among under 5 year children, as 54% have vitamin A deficiency while 58% have anaemia, and 35% are stunted. Malnutrition is more prevalent in northern region of Zambia. Ten percent of women (8% urban and 11% rural) are underweight (creating a double-burden of malnutrition. The development and marketing of food products enhanced with dried small fish offers a novel solution to address major nutritional problems that affect young children and women in many developing countries. Small fish are a nutritional powerhouse rich in vitamins and minerals that are important for growth and cognition. When added to food products, this increases micronutrient intake among the most vulnerable groups. The project aimed at significantly expand and scale up the availability of nutritious products, and some of the accompanying systems that make them possible. Focused on Zambia and Myanmar, two markets with significant potential for uptake and impact, the project worked with a range of partners, including private companies to manufacture and distribute affordable and highly nourishing fish-based nutrition solutions for poor households, especially women and children. The project utilized innovative models at each step, from how the products are developed, to the methods for their distribution.
