core_fields.title: Glycemic Reduction and Added Integrated Nutrients - Scaling the Low GI rice with increased protein content for the vulnerable Filipino population (GRAIN+)
core_fields.description: Asia faces a double burden of diabetes and malnutrition, particularly in low-income, rice-dependent communities. With diabetes cases rising, improving rice s nutritional quality is crucial. Our "Low GIPlus rice," with low glycemic index and high protein content, can regulate blood sugar with enhanced protein content. Challenges remain in scaling production and market uptake, requiring standardized testing and effective marketing strategies to make low GIPlus rice accessible and affordable for vulnerable populations.
core_fields.abstract: The Low GIPlus rice innovation addresses two critical challenges: the rising prevalence of diabetes and malnutrition in rice-dependent, low-income communities. Rice, a staple food, is often low in essential nutrients and has a high glycemic index (GI), contributing to elevated blood sugar levels and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes. This is especially relevant as diabetes cases are rising globally, with 4.3 million Filipinos diagnosed with diabetes in 2021. The solution involves developing rice varieties with both low GI properties with extra protein. These rice varieties help regulate blood sugar levels and address protein deficiencies, improving diabetes management and overall nutrition. Scientific insights into rice breeding have enabled the integration of low GI traits into high-yielding varieties, maintaining productivity and taste. The immediate benefits include improved health outcomes for consumers, especially those with diabetes and malnutrition. For farmers, the innovation provides a sustainable crop with low GI varieties having high yield potential, and early maturity requires minimal agricultural inputs, enhancing profitability as consumers are willing to pay a premium for low GI rice. Environmentally, the adoption of early maturity and nutritious varieties reduces water use and greenhouse gas emissions compared to traditional long-maturity crops. The stable low GI trait ensures sustainability, allowing these varieties to be grown across multiple seasons. By addressing both health and environmental challenges, Low GIPlus rice provides lasting benefits to individuals, communities, and society, promoting better health and a more sustainable food system.

core_fields.title: Deployment of High Zinc Rice to Address Zinc Malnutrition in Nepal
core_fields.description: This project will test and deploy high Zn rice lines in Nepal to improve national food and nutrition security. Deployment of high Zinc (Zn) rice is one of the cheapest and sustainable food-based solutions to address Zn malnutrition in the mass population. IRRI has developed high Zn rice breeding lines with additional 8 to 10 ppm grain Zn content over the popular rice varieties along with high yield and grain quality traits.
core_fields.abstract: Zinc (Zn) is a crucial micronutrient for human biological processes and good health, and Zn deficiency is a major micronutrient malnutrition globally-about 19% of people in Asia are at risk of inadequate zinc intake. Zinc deficiency causes stunting, diarrhea, compromised immunity, and cognitive impairment among children. In Nepal, 22.9% of preschool children and 24.7 % of non-pregnant women suffer Zn deficiency associated-health problems. Thus, providing nutrition to vulnerable target populations is a priority sustainable development goal in Nepal and globally. Rice is the most important staple food of Nepal s 31 million population accounting 40% of the total daily calorie uptake. Therefore, nutrition enriched biofortified rice is a cost-effective and sustainable solution to address malnutrition in Nepal. Efforts to supply Zn through supplementation and rice fortification are limited by scale and effectiveness. While Zn biofortified rice varieties supply Zn on a daily basis in a readily available form, it is a food matrix; hence easily absorbed by the body and proven to be efficient in reducing Zn malnutrition in the target groups. It is cheaper and sustainable as the farmers can multiply and use their own seeds, without recurring investments needed, scalable, easy to reach out to remote populations, and there are no barriers to consumer acceptance. Using this approach, it is possible to reduce the health burden significantly. An increase in a healthy population can contribute to the economic development of a nation. This initiative is the first attempt to introduce Zn biofortified rice in Nepal.

core_fields.title: Resilience through Regeneration
core_fields.description: Itanya Africa Group empowers smallholder farmers in semi-arid Kenya through regenerative agriculture, water infrastructure, and climate-smart solutions. We train farmers on sustainable practices like syntropic agroforestry, construct water pans to reduce reliance on rain-fed agriculture, and establish vertical gardens to enhance food security. By fostering social capital and leveraging community-driven initiatives, we aim to restore degraded lands, improve livelihoods, and build resilient, self-sustaining agricultural systems.
core_fields.abstract: Itanya Africa Group's innovation addresses the critical challenges of degraded soils, unreliable rainfall, and food insecurity faced by smallholder farmers in semi-arid Kenya. By integrating regenerative agriculture, syntropic agroforestry, and water-smart technologies, we provide a holistic solution to enhance productivity, resilience, and environmental restoration. The problem is highly relevant as climate change intensifies, threatening agricultural livelihoods and ecosystems. Our approach combines scientific insights on soil regeneration with practical, locally adapted techniques. For example, composting agricultural waste into biofertilizer rejuvenates soil health, while syntropic agroforestry mimics natural ecosystems, increasing biodiversity and water retention. Additionally, water pans and vertical gardens reduce reliance on rain-fed agriculture, enabling year-round farming and optimizing water use. Farmers benefit immediately through increased yields, diversified income streams, and enhanced knowledge. Long-term, the innovation promotes sustainable land use, combats desertification, and mitigates climate change impacts. Communities gain access to improved food security, economic stability, and a healthier environment. Society benefits from a replicable model for resilient agriculture that reduces emissions and supports local ecosystems. This integrated, science-backed approach not only empowers farmers but also strengthens the social fabric of communities, fostering collaboration and shared growth.

core_fields.title: Ensuring Food Security for Tribal Communities: Empowering Sustainable Practices and Community-Based Solutions in Kandhamal district of Odisha, INDIA

These communities face challenges such as limited access to resources, low agricultural productivity, environmental degradation, and a lack of proper infrastructure. The aim of this project is to improve food security for tribal communities of Kandhamal by empowering them with sustainable agricultural practices, community-based solutions, resource access to ensure long-term food security and nutritional health.
core_fields.abstract: Strategies of solution and sustainability of food security and environment Improved Food Security: Increased availability of nutritious food, reduced hunger, and better access to markets. Enhanced Agricultural Productivity: Higher yields through sustainable farming methods and better access to quality inputs and training. Increased Community Resilience to climate change and economic fluctuations through diversified livelihoods. Health and Nutrition Improvements: Reduction in malnutrition rates and improved dietary diversity in Kandhamal district. Economic Empowerment: Enhanced incomes for small farmers through better access to markets and value-added agricultural products. Promotion of food basket: a. Sustainable Agricultural Practices Introduction of Climate-Resilient Crops: Provide seeds for drought-resistant crops, such as millet, sorghum, and legumes, which are well-suited to Kandhamal climate. core_fields.title: Connecting Farms to Tables: Innovation for Nutrition and Malnutrition Solutions for Africa
core_fields.description: Our Farm-to-Consumer platform combats malnutrition by linking farmers to consumers with biofortified, nutritious foods. Using blockchain and AI, it ensures traceability and food safety. Farmers gain market access, increased income, and sustainable farming training. Consumers benefit from reliable, healthy food, addressing food security and reducing post-harvest losses. This initiative supports the UN SDGs of Zero Hunger, Good Health, and Responsible Consumption, enhancing public health and economic opportunities in Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Malnutrition remains a pervasive issue globally, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where many communities lack consistent access to affordable, nutritious food. This problem is exacerbated by fragmented supply chains, inadequate market access for farmers, and limited food traceability. Despite Africa s vast agricultural potential, millions suffer from poor diets, contributing to stunted growth, disease, and other health issues. Our *Farm-to-Consumer* (F2C) platform offers a solution by connecting farmers directly to consumers using blockchain and AI technologies to ensure traceability, authenticity, and safety of food. This innovation guarantees that biofortified, nutrient-dense foods reach consumers reliably and securely. Farmers benefit by gaining access to premium markets, real-time sales data, and training in climate-smart agriculture, increasing their income and productivity. The immediate benefits of this platform are evident: - **Consumers** receive verified, nutritious food, reducing malnutrition risks. - **Farmers** gain market access and improve livelihoods through training. - **Society** enjoys better public health and food security, while **environmental** sustainability is enhanced through efficient, low-carbon agriculture. This approach addresses multiple SDGs, including Zero Hunger, Good Health and Well-Being, and Responsible Production, contributing to long-term sustainable development by transforming food supply chains and empowering smallholder farmers.

core_fields.title: Agro-Processing
core_fields.description: This project aims at providing nutritious products from processed orange fresh sweet potato to refugees, displaced communities and host communities in Rwanda to confirm whether sweet potato flour can be adaptable to daily Rwandan meal. It will be executed by JIF CBC (orange sweet potato flour processor and main implementer) and Spirit of Peace and Solidarity (SPS, a Non-Profit-Refugee-Led Organization (second implementer) from January 2025 to December 2026.
core_fields.abstract: Sweet potatoes are massively grown and produced by almost each Rwandan household. They are even among major and commonly consumed food every day, particularly in rural and refugee camps areas. However, because sweet potatoes are generally produced once year with very few parts of the country that can produce twice per year and at large quantity. The marketplace becomes very saturated with these produces especially at the harvesting time, which often lead to the decrease of cost at 85% (MINAGRI, 2022) and also to poor nutrition (33%, MoH 2023) since they are forged to eat all of them within short time due to limited capacity for long term conservation. JIF CBC has availed the proccessing plant to rwandan farmers to process Vit A fresh sweet potato into flour and noodles so that the flour can be accessible to the communities yearlong. The factory was launched and preliminary production actvities have already started. This project aims at testisting if the product will be liked as a sustitute of orange fresh sweet potato for improved nutrition. It will also be executed alongside with other empowerement programs that will promote micro-climate resilence (waste recycling, composting&agro-forestry), increase their food purchase power in addition to income generation from fresh sweet potato farming (Business mentorship, Saving& Credit Groups). It will be executed by JIF as primary implementor and SPS as a non profit organisation acting as a mediator between JIF and MIDMAR (Ministry in charge of refugees) and UNHCR, Rwanda.

core_fields.title: Empowering Consumers with Sustainable Food Choices
core_fields.description: This project empowers consumers to make informed and sustainable food choices. We will provide easy-to-use resources and tools, such as educational materials, online platforms, and community partnerships, to help people understand the environmental and social impacts of their food choices. By making it easier to choose sustainable options, we aim to create a more just and sustainable food system for all.
core_fields.abstract: Innovation: This project leverages digital technology and community engagement to empower consumers to make informed and sustainable food choices. Problem Solved: Lack of consumer awareness: Many consumers are unaware of the environmental and social impacts of their food choices. Limited access to information: Finding reliable information on sustainable food practices can be challenging. Difficulty in making informed decisions: Navigating complex food labels and understanding sustainable farming practices can be overwhelming for consumers. Relevance: Environmental impact: The global food system contributes significantly to climate change, deforestation, and water pollution. Social impact: Many farmers and food workers face challenges such as low incomes and unfair labor practices. Human health: Sustainable diets are linked to improved human health and reduced risk of chronic diseases. Solution: Develop an interactive online platform: This platform will provide personalized recommendations, track food consumption, and calculate environmental impacts. Create educational resources: Easily digestible information, infographics, and engaging videos will educate consumers about sustainable food systems. Build partnerships: Collaborate with local businesses, farmers, and community organizations to provide access to sustainable food options. Benefits: Consumers: Gain knowledge, make informed choices, and reduce their environmental impact. Farmers: Increased demand for sustainably produced food, improved livelihoods, and access to new markets. Environment: Reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved soil health, and greater biodiversity. Communities: Stronger local food systems, increased access to healthy food, and improved food security.

SUTTI is designed for middle to large-scale smallholder programs. The SUTTI initiative mainly activates three complementary levers to deliver impact: • Program design and management (technical assistance) • Digital solutions: "low-tech" application for farmers, "back-office" for field instructors and community leaders and "reporting dashboard" for sponsors. • Innovative and inclusive impact finance (inclusive finance, carbon credits, blended finance) The SUTTI solution is designed to support the transformation of farming activities by providing access to vocational training, market access, and financial services, and by supporting farmers in implementing a technical itinerary established on the basis of an in-depth initial diagnosis.

core_fields.title: Wasteless-to-feedwell
core_fields.description: Our wasteless-to-foodwell project tackles hunger and malnutrition in west Africa starting with Kano Nigeria by converting excess vegetable waste into nutritious food. Our 3-in-1 bioconvertion hub features a community garden, eco-factory, and eco-mart, providing a safety net for vulnerable communities, economically empowering individuals, and establishing sustainable food waste management systems. This innovative approach breaks the poverty cycle, ensuring food security and dignity for the poorest, while promoting environmental sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Wasteless- to- feedwell project is Addressing hunger & malnutrition in Africa starting with Nassarawa LGA, Kano State, where institutionalized begging is prevalent via the Alma Jiri systems (under aged street begging) Ironically in communities situated around abundance of organic waste like Yankaba Market (largest vegetable market in NE Nigeria) which we use as pilot and feasibilty study face: - Severe hunger/malnutrition - Excess vegatable waste (daily tonnes) According to FAO 1/3 of global food produced is wasted and Over 40% of Africa waste is organic. Our waste-to-food project tackles this paradox with goals to; - Improve food security for vulnerable communities by creating an alternate food path that serves as a safety net for the poorest in low income slums and ghetto communities like mine . - Economically empower vulnerable individuals and households to break the poverty cycle. - Establish sustainable systems that facilitate food waste collection, recycling, upscaling, and redistribution. our approach to providing this solution is a 3-in-1 bioconvertion Hub, comprising; 1. Community Garden: A shared space for; green houses, arable land parcels for group crop cultivation and free range space for poultry. 2. Eco Factory: A facility for recycling vegetables and organic food waste into useful inputs like biofertilizers, pesticides, BSF larvae and biodiesel. 3. Eco Mart: A makeshift structure serving as a weekly food-subsidy sales outlet for grains, vegetables, and agricultural inputs to our membership base, alongside a daily restaurant-food bank for feeding the homeless and needy using repurposed leftovers donated by food and hospitality businesses.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Transformation of Cashew Fruits: Zero Waste Solutions for Farmer Income Boost, Rural Employment, and Reduced Carbon Footprint
core_fields.description: Kamireddy Agro Foods Pvt. Ltd. is a zero-waste, sustainability-driven company transforming underutilized cashew apples into high-value products like vinegar, NATA de Cashew, beverages, and feed supplements. By integrating cutting-edge technology and engaging 1.5 million farmers, it creates economic, environmental, and social impact while catering to growing markets in food, cosmetics, and animal nutrition.
core_fields.abstract: India generates approximately 4 million tonnes of cashew apples annually, most of which are discarded as waste. This not only leads to significant resource underutilization but also contributes to environmental issues, such as 20 million kg of methane emissions from rotting fruits. Additionally, cashew farmers face limited income opportunities due to the lack of value-added processing for this byproduct. Simultaneously, there is a high reliance on imported products like NATA de coco, while gaps exist in the market for innovative, cashew-based products such as beverages, vinegar, and feed supplements. Addressing these challenges can transform waste into economic value, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and empower rural communities. Zero-Waste Philosophy: Kamireddy Agro Foods embodies a zero-waste model by converting underutilized cashew apple by-products into high-value products, addressing the environmental and economic inefficiencies in cashew farming. Innovative Product Line: NATA de Cashew: The first-of-its-kind alternative to NATA de coco, made using cashew apples instead of coconuts. Cashew Vinegar: Offers 80% metabolic similarity to apple cider vinegar, catering to a health-conscious market with a unique raw material base. Cajuice: A novel, palatable beverage created through innovative detannification technology. Cavita: A high-nutrition animal feed supplement derived from cashew fiber, supporting livestock industries. Environmental Impact: By utilizing cashew apples, the company prevents the release of 20 million kg of methane emissions, aligning with sustainability goals. Farmer-Centric Approach: Direct engagement with 1.5 million cashew farmers boosts their income by up to 40%, creating significant social impact.

core_fields.title: Resilient and Regenerative Villages (R2V)
core_fields.description: R2V will scale-up tested regenerative agricultural models in Kenya which were tested under 2-SCALE project and the on-going IKEA Foundation regenerative rice project. The focus will be adoption and structuring trade of the groundnut varieties (Mwangaza and Ndovu) tested in Eastern region of Kenya in partnership with Batian Nuts Ltd under 2-SCALE project. Other than promotion of the groundnut varieties, R2V will also promote regenerative agriculture technologies tested through R4iCSA Project.
core_fields.abstract: Eastern region of Kenya is prone to high occurrence of aflatoxin on grains with groundnut affected the most, for example, samples that were taken from this region in 2020 before the implementation of 2-SCALE groundnut project, had as high as 150ppb levels of aflatoxin. The area is also prone to drought as it is Semi-ASAL with many of the community members experiencing perennial famine, thus need to have an introduction of crop varieties that can easily adapt to low rainfall levels. Groundnut intrinsic valuable crop for both rural and urban communities in Kenya. Its absence in the agrarian ecosystem exacerbates socio economic challenges that suppress growth and development in many ways. Malnutrition typically evident through goiter and rickets are common deficiency symptoms seen in parts of the Eastern Region of Kenya. Kilimo Trust in partnership with Batian Nuts Ltd and Egerton University tested new groundnut varieties that were able to grow well and are liked by both the community members and the groundnut off-takers (Markets). These groundnut varieties are more resilient to both aflatoxin and drought thus presenting the community with an alternative of having energy dense and aflatoxin free products from groundnut. This initiative will see structuring and promotion for adoption of these improved groundnut varieties in Eastern region of Kenya for healthier lives and climate resilience in the region.

core_fields.title: Kilimomax BSF farming
core_fields.description: KilimoMax Solutions, in partnership with Dodoma City Council, is implementing a Black Soldier Fly (BSF) project at Chidaya Landfill to transform organic waste into sustainable animal feed and organic compost. This innovation addresses waste management, enhances soil fertility, and improves food security. By empowering marginalized communities, the project promotes environmental sustainability and economic opportunities while offering a scalable solution to tackle pressing agricultural and environmental challenges in Tanzania.
core_fields.abstract: Dodoma City generates approximately 350 metric tons of solid waste daily, with over 60% being organic. This waste remains underutilized, contributing to environmental pollution, methane emissions, and poor public health. Simultaneously, farmers face challenges like declining soil fertility, expensive animal feed, and limited access to sustainable agricultural inputs. KilimoMax Solutions' Black Soldier Fly (BSF) project addresses these issues by transforming organic waste into valuable resources: nutrient-rich animal feed and organic compost. Through an innovative process, BSF larvae consume organic waste, rapidly converting it into high-protein larvae for livestock feed and compost that rejuvenates degraded soils. This solution is grounded in scientific insights on BSF's ability to efficiently recycle waste and improve circular economies. It reduces waste pollution, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and provides affordable alternatives to chemical fertilizers and conventional animal feed. The project offers immediate benefits to farmers by increasing yields and reducing input costs, while communities experience cleaner environments and reduced health risks. Long-term, the initiative fosters environmental sustainability, strengthens food systems, and empowers marginalized groups such as youth and women. This scalable and replicable model not only addresses Tanzania's pressing waste management and agricultural challenges but also contributes to achieving global sustainability goals, making it a transformative solution for food systems and environmental health.

core_fields.title: BRAVE
core_fields.description: This project KUECHO South Sudan shall an enable and support local communities and their South Sudanese partners to build inclusive, equitable and resilient value chains and agri-food enterprises, grounded on their entrepreneurial ideas, with specific attention for local seed security, rural entrepreneurship, and stakeholder collaboration. Food system transformation in South Sudan is not easy, because of multiple shocks and stressors, persisting conflict and violence , and natural resource deterioration. For many years, external aids.
core_fields.abstract: Main problems in the targeted county that need to be solved to achieve the desired impact: 1) Lack of good quality seed, in demand by local farmers, provided in a timely manner for affordable prices, 2) Poor agri-value chain and agri-food enterprise development to narrow the food gap and provide a diversity of healthy foods (including lack of participation by women and youth in seed production, agri-value chain and agri-food enterprise development), and 3) Lack of knowledge, learning and evidence-based programming in support of food systems transformation. The project will directly work with 20 local case owners, coordinating the development of 15 practical cases in a certain sub-sector and value chain in a specific context. The Sustainable Food System project counts with an average of 100 farmer households per case, targeting a total of 2,000 smallholder food producer households/entrepreneurs (projected at 15,000 individuals), of which 350 will be seed producer farmers (organized in 24 seed producer groups), with a keen interest in improving their production and scaling value chains and agri-business. Although the target groups are predominantly farmers, they are likely to include agro-pastoralists and (potentially) herders as well as wider communities (for example, agro-input dealers and extension officers) through development of seed systems, value chains and agri-food enterprises which contribute to the resilience of local food systems, and social cohesion notably in farmer-herder contexts. Intervention strategy South Sudan s National Food Systems Dialogues (at different levels) show that there are ample opportunities to build food systems resilience.

core_fields.title: Fostering a sustainable poultry value chain: Reducing waste, and prioritizing public health
core_fields.description: This project seeks to commercialize a novel poultry feed formulation that utilizes the natural antibiotic properties of cloves as a substitute for human-grade antibiotics commonly used in poultry farming. $25,000 shall be directed towards equipment acquisition, certification and packaging which clearly communicates the safety of the product with its potential to reduce antibiotic resistance amongst chicken consumers. The project will also include training programs for small-holder farmers on sustainable poultry farming practices.
core_fields.abstract: Uganda faces a critical food security challenge, with malnutrition remaining widespread despite agricultural potential. While chicken offers a valuable protein source, the industry is challenged by high waste generation and rampart utilization of antibiotics, posing significant risks to human health (antibiotic resistance and non-communicable diseases). Kisakye Poultry Farm addresses Uganda's food security and health challenges by producing and promoting organic, antibiotic-free chicken through efficient feed formulation that utilizes essential oils. It was discovered that poultry farmers excessively add antibiotics to poultry feeds because the birds grow faster due to elimination of bacteria in the birds' gut. We add natural phytogenic additives such as cloves which have antimicrobial properties thereby eliminating harmful bacteria in the birds' gut thus promoting bird growth without posing a public health challenge. Through farmer training, market creation, and skill development programs for marginalized communities, we foster a sustainable and equitable poultry industry which provides chicken consumers with safer chicken on the market thereby reducing chances of antibiotic resistance.

core_fields.title: Healthy Vegetables for All: Empowering Communities with Nutritious Vegetables to Tackle Malnutrition and Food Insecurity.
core_fields.description: Healthy Veggies for All is a vegetable farming initiative in Baleofiili, Ghana, providing organic vegetables like cabbage, tomatoes, and green peppers. We recycle food waste into compost, practice climate-smart farming, and empower smallholder farmers with training and market access. Our eco-friendly packaged vegetables are delivered to consumers doorsteps. Through community programs, we promote healthy eating and combat malnutrition, ensuring accessible, nutritious food for all.
core_fields.abstract: Growing up in Baleofiili, a rural community in the Upper West region of Ghana, accessing fresh vegetables was extremely challenging. Farmers traditionally focused on growing grains such as maize and groundnuts, with less than 10% cultivating vegetables. Prolonged dry seasons and poor post-harvest management exacerbated the situation, leading to malnutrition, particularly among pregnant women and children. This scarcity and its effect on nutrition inspired my commitment to vegetable farming. According to a 2020 World Health Organization report, Northern Ghana has the country s highest malnutrition rate at nearly 48%, largely due to insufficient consumption of nutrient-rich foods like vegetables. The few vegetables available are often cultivated using inorganic fertilizers and sold under unhygienic conditions, making them unsafe for consumption. Healthy Veggies for All addresses these issues using a multifaceted approach. We grow vegetables such as cabbage and green pepper year-round using climate-smart methods, including compost from recycled food waste and solar-powered irrigation. Through our vegetable out-grower system, we empower smallholder farmers by connecting them to inputs and markets and training them in organic farming practices like composting. Additionally, we educate communities on the importance of vegetable consumption to combat malnutrition. Our initiative allows consumers, especially children, pregnant women, and low-income families, to access affordable, nutritious vegetables, improving nutrition and health. Farmers reduce costs and improve yields by adopting climate-smart methods. Communities benefit from integrated nutrition programs that promote healthy eating habits. Environmentally, the initiative reduces greenhouse gas emissions, enhances soil health, and minimizes waste through sustainable practices.

core_fields.title: Development of Activated Carbon Waste Water Purification System for Illegal Mining Communities in Ghana
core_fields.description: Illegal mining is rampant in Ghana. This has led to pollution of ground and surface water for drinking and agricultural production in affected rural communities with associated health and environmental concerns. The project aims to develop and test low-cost water purification systems for mining-affected rural communities. Waste organic materials such as rice husk and saw dust will be developed into Organic Carbon (Activated Charcoal) for purifying polluted water for consumption and vegetable crop production.
core_fields.abstract: Illegal mining in Ghana affects the quality of surface water and groundwater. This is poses a threat to women and children in affected communities (Gardner et al., 2015). A study by the Commission of Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) of Ghana revealed that many rivers and streams providing safe water for the mining communities have been destroyed, polluted or dried up. Illegal small-scale mining is also increasing environmental pollution while affecting health, aquatic life, and agriculture (Nasirudeen, 2015). There is the urgent need to sustain the environment, agriculture, food systems and the health of vulnerable groups (Bansah et al., 2016). Heavy metal pollutants, such as mercury, cyanide, cadmium, and/or arsenic from these illegal activities is appearing in the food chain. These pollutants affect humans ranging from mild eye, nose and skin irritations, severe headache, stomach ache, diarrhea, hematemesis, vomiting, dizziness, and organ dysfunction (cirrhosis, necrosis, low blood pressure, hypertension, and gastrointestinal distress) (Inyinbor et al., 2018). Cognitive impairment, among others, have has been reported in some children. Babies have been born with their legs forming around the chest, neck and stomach while some are also born with one eye, without genitalia or suffer from kidney and hypertensive-related conditions as reported by a pathologist (Prof. Paul Poku Sampene Ossei). Drinking contaminated water or eating aquatic organisms or farm produce with the accumulation of these toxins also pose major threats.

core_fields.description: The Living and Learning Labs are innovative spaces transforming education through experiential learning, integrating indigenous practices and a heritage-based approach. These promote environmental stewardship and sustainability while fostering interdisciplinary learning across all subjects. They empower young people as citizen scientists to co-create solutions for their communities. With a focus on inclusivity and gender equity, the labs envision a South Africa where experiential learning inspires cultural restoration, academic excellence, and sustainable practices for a better future.
core_fields.abstract: The Living and Learning Laboratories (L3 Labs) transform schools into experiential learning environments that address educational, social, and environmental challenges. These innovative spaces integrate indigenous knowledge and sustainable practices into interdisciplinary education, empowering students as active citizens and environmental stewards. Problem and Relevance: L3 Labs tackle two critical issues: a lack of engaging educational methods and the pressing need for sustainable practices in the face of climate change. Traditional teaching often fails to prepare students for real-world challenges, and communities face food insecurity and environmental degradation. Solution and Insight: L3 Labs employ heritage-based approaches and modern sustainability techniques, such as organic gardening, permaculture, and waste reduction. These spaces integrate life sciences, history, and environmental studies into hands-on learning, enabling students to explore solutions for real-world issues. By linking curriculum with practical applications, students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Immediate Benefits: The labs produce fresh, nutritious food for school kitchens, improving health while teaching sustainable food production. Students and teachers engage in project-based learning, fostering academic excellence and environmental awareness. These spaces also help reframe perceptions of food gardens from spaces of labor to essential tools for sustainability and health. Sustainable Benefits: L3 Labs promote long-term environmental stewardship by teaching regenerative practices, water conservation, and waste reduction. The initiative extends to communities, empowering families to grow nutritious food and fostering local food security. By building a culture of sustainability, L3 Labs create enduring positive impacts for students, schools, and society, aligning education with real-world environmental and social needs.

core_fields.title: Integrated Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihoods and Climate Change Resilience in Northern Ghana
core_fields.description: Northern Ghana is noted to be the most affected by climate change in the country. This project, therefore, seeks to strengthen the resilience of smallholder farmers through climate SMART technologies such as integrated fish and vegetable farming, energy saving cooking stoves, tree planting, farmer managed natural regeneration, organic pesticides and household manure preparation and utilization. It will also focus on improving nutrition through the promotion of orange flesh potato and nutritional educational program.
core_fields.abstract: Climate change severely impact women, children and the most vulnerable population in northern Ghana exacerbating existing social, economic, and political inequalities and threatening sustainable livelihoods. Due to climate change impacts, the agricultural sector in northern Ghana which relies heavily on rain-fed farming has become vulnerable due to rising temperatures, changes in rainfall patterns and extreme weather events. The vulnerability in northern Ghana's agriculture has led to reduced crop yields, food insecurity, water scarcity, and increased poverty. To mitigate these impacts, innovative approaches that enhances agricultural resilience are crucial. Notably, aquaponics has immerged as the best recognized solution, offering a sustainable solution for producing fish and vegetables, and paving way for a transformative shift in northern Ghana s agricultural landscape. The Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihood and Climate Resilience initiative is a closed-loop system that combines aquaculture with hydroponics to provide sustainable fish and vegetables farming, enabling farmers to adapt to climate change and improve their livelihoods, thereby promoting climate-resilient agriculture. The heart of this innovative system is the symbiotic relationship between fish and plants. In this relationship (mutualism), waste produced by the fish is transformed into nutrients for plants, enabling nutrient cycling to occur with minimal waste and water usage. It is in leveraging this natural process that Aquaponics for Sustainable Livelihood and Climate Resilience develops such an efficient and sustainable production system for food. The immediate benefits of this solution will be increased access to nutritious food, better livelihoods farmers, and increased climate resilience while concurrently reducing environmental degradation

core_fields.title: Empowering1000Women
core_fields.description: The Empowering Women for Climate Resilience and Economic Independence project strengthens vulnerable women s economic self-reliance and climate resilience. By providing training in financial literacy, climate-smart agriculture, and environmental stewardship, the project enables women to lead sustainable, income-generating activities and adapt to climate impacts. Through community-driven initiatives like Village Savings and Loan Associations and Women s Climate Action Groups, the project builds lasting resilience, supporting food security, economic growth, and climate justice in rural communities.
core_fields.abstract: In Sierra Leone, rural women face economic insecurity and heightened vulnerability to climate impacts, which include soil degradation, erratic rainfall, and loss of biodiversity. These challenges, combined with limited access to resources, perpetuate cycles of poverty, food insecurity, and environmental decline. Women, who are primary contributors to agriculture, often lack training in sustainable practices and financial resources to transition to resilient, eco-friendly livelihoods. Our solution empowers these women by providing training in climate-smart agriculture, financial literacy, and leadership, equipping them with tools to adapt to climate change and achieve economic self-sufficiency. Through establishing Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) and Women s Climate Action Groups, participants can save, access small loans, and invest in sustainable farming and small businesses. Agroforestry and soil conservation practices are introduced, improving yields while protecting the environment. The innovation lies in combining economic empowerment with climate resilience, addressing both immediate needs and long-term sustainability. Women gain critical skills, increasing food security and reducing dependency on environmentally damaging practices. Communities benefit from improved ecosystem health, greater economic activity, and resilience to climate shocks. This solution not only elevates the role of women as community leaders but also fosters sustainable development, aligning economic growth with environmental conservation.

core_fields.title: Scaling in Kenya and expanding into other African countries: Breakthrough bioherbicide technology improves food and economic security for small-scale farmers
core_fields.description: Toothpick Project's innovative bio-herbicide technology uses a selected strain of host-specific fungus to protect crops from Striga witchweed, Africa's worst pest threat to food security for small-scale farmers. Our selected fungal strain is a unique nature-based herbicide distributed to farmers and applied as a seed coating to restore their crop yield. One of the first bioherbicides to be commercialized in the world, the game-changing agri-tech is a safe, effective, affordable alternative to traditional chemical herbicides.
core_fields.abstract: Striga, an invasive parasitic weed, attacks the roots of staple crops like maize and sorghum, reducing crop yield up to 100%. 50 million hectares of croplands (~40 million farms) in sub-Saharan Africa show Striga infestation, causing $9+ billion in crop loss annually. Striga forms an intense soil seed bank by adding over 50,000 seeds per season. The seeds spread easily across farms through wind, human and animal traffic, and farming tools. Our beneficiaries, smallholder farmers, are generally below the poverty level of $2.15/person per day. After decades of research and development with team members from three continents, our technology uses a strain of endemic Kenyan fungus, Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. strigae, selected for over-production of specific amino acids to kill striga but not crops. The resulting product, Kichawi Kill (kichawi means magic in Swahili), is a groundbreaking approach to striga management and global weed management. Proof-of-concept trials took place in 2014-2015, showing a 42-56% increase in yield. The fungi were originally grown on toothpicks and delivered to the village level for a secondary inoculum production. The pilot social enterprise in Kenya launched commercial distribution in 2021. In 2023, the seed coating product was approved in Kenya, significantly reducing the price and increasing the shelf life. TCL is expected to break-even in Kenya in 2025. Expansion efforts to Uganda started in 2024, followed by other sub-Saharan Africa countries in 2025. The technology improves food security and economic stability for farmers and reduces biodiversity loss caused by synthetic chemical herbicides.

core_fields.title: Scaling and Improving UVC LED Water Disinfection for Global Impact to Protect Vulnerable Communities Against Waterborne Diseases
core_fields.description: Further develop, validate and deploy advanced mobile water disinfection kits that utilize germicidal ultraviolet light (UVC) LED technology in combination with pre-treatment cleaning modules. These kits are sustainable, low cost and safe alternative for plastic bottles and designed for easy transport, operation and distribution, making them ideal for displaced families and vulnerable communities facing water scarcity due to conflicts and environmental degradation.
core_fields.abstract: Global climate change and geopolitical conflicts are closely tied to issues of water accessibility and quality. Natural and human-made disasters can destroy or contaminate water supplies, increasing the risk of diseases. Currently, distributing water in plastic bottles is a common emergency solution. However, the high costs of production and transportation, along with plastic waste, microplastics contamination of water and soil make it an unsustainable option in crises. Germicidal ultraviolet (UVC) light is known as effective nonthermal nonchemical nonionizing physical method at killing waterborne pathogens. UVC LED systems are compact, efficient, safe and easily installed as plug-and-play solutions for point-of-use water purification. UVC LEDs, combined with necessary pre-treatment methods, can clean and disinfect water from local sources such as rivers, lakes, and wells, providing microbiologically and chemically safe drinking water. This local water treatment ensures fast, cost-effective, long-term access to clean water, reduces call and reliance on plastic, chemical disinfection and minimizes environmental pollution. Access to safe drinking water in crisis situations reduces the risk of waterborne diseases like diarrhea, typhoid, and cholera, leading to better diets, health and fewer medical expenses. UV4Good collaborates with local scientists and engineers to create customized solutions, guided by community input. We use local resources and test solutions to ensure their effectiveness. By adapting innovative technologies to address climate change and human-made disasters, we can protect human health, save lives, provide access to better diets and reduce environmental pollution.

core_fields.title: Micronutrient profile and household use of Indigenous Crops in Tanzania
core_fields.description: The food supply chain positively affects food and nutrition security for sustainable development. Moreover, supply chains are a point of influence for agriculture to improve nutrition, particularly by focusing on micronutrient-rich foods. The project aims to explore indigenous crops that provide opportunities to diversify farming systems, ensure food and nutrition security and alleviate poverty while increasing income and improving human health. This can be achieved by unlocking indigenous crops' full potential during processing, distribution, and marketing in an eco-friendly environment. Therefore, understanding the value chain of indigenous crops and their nutritional contribution provides essential aspects for most developing countries' sustainable food systems, livelihoods, and dietary benefits. Some of the identified indigenous crops' micronutrients (iron, zinc, and vitamin A) are targeted because they are the most prevalent problem in Tanzania and several other African countries. Thus, using a mixed-method approach, this research has the potential to contribute more and significantly alleviate poverty, stabilize food and nutrition security, and improve people's welfare as targeted by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Tanzania's 2021–2026 National Development Plan, and Tanzania Development Vision 2025.

core_fields.title: Empowering Rural Communities of Namibia through Introducing Sustainable Kalahari Melon Oil Processing Methodology
core_fields.description: The Kalahari melon, native to Sub-Saharan Africa, offers rural communities economic and nutritional potential. This project seeks to improve the efficiency and sustainability of oil extraction from Citrullus lanatus seeds through engineering solutions. Oil extraction will be optimized by introducing the cold-press method to produce high-quality virgin oil with defined chemical and nutritional characteristics. Reducing labor intensity and enhancing oil quality and yields, the project empowers women farmers, improves income generation, and fosters sustainable livelihoods.
core_fields.abstract: The Problem Rural communities in Namibia, Botswana, Zambia, and Zimbabwe heavily rely on traditional agriculture. The Kalahari melon, a drought-resistant crop, has untapped potential as a sustainable source of cooking oil and income. Current oil extraction methods are labor-intensive, environmentally unsustainable, and economically restrictive, particularly for women producers. Firewood-dependent processes contribute to deforestation, while low yields and market access challenges hinder income generation. Moreover, the quality of the produced oil is not determined. The Russia-Ukraine conflict has exacerbated regional cooking oil shortages, making affordable alternatives like Kalahari melon oil increasingly relevant. However, traditional methods involve arduous steps, including manual pounding and boiling, which can take over a week to complete, leaving women producers inadequately compensated for their labor. The Solution This project addresses these challenges by introducing cold-press technology for oil extraction and utilizing byproducts effectively. Key solutions include: 1. Efficiency: Streamlining the oil extraction process to reduce time and labor demands. 2. Sustainability: Minimizing reliance on firewood, reducing deforestation, and maintaining oil quality by avoiding thermal degradation. 3. Economic Empowerment: Enhancing oil yields and quality to create market opportunities and improve income for women producers. 4. Community Engagement: Integrating traditional knowledge with modern technology through co-design with local stakeholders, ensuring cultural relevance and sustainability. Immediate and Sustainable Benefits For Farmers: Reduced labor, increased yields, and improved income. For Consumers: Access to high-quality, locally produced cooking oil. For Communities: Job creation, gender empowerment, and enhanced food security. For the Environment: Reduced deforestation and carbon emissions

core_fields.description: This proposal aims to address challenges faced by dairy farmers, including the low quality of milk that fails to meet national standards, leading to rejection by dairy processing industries. By implementing Good Dairy Farming Practices (GDFP), diversifying dairy products, and improving marketing and branding strategies, the initiative seeks to enhance milk quality, increase farmers' income, and contribute to sustainable economic growth. The project aligns with keys UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs),
core_fields.abstract: Problem Statement Dairy farmers in the Cooperative KTT (Kelompok Tani Ternak) face significant challenges as their milk fails to meet the Indonesian Fresh Milk National Standard (SNI 3141.1-2011), primarily due to low fat content ( 3%) and high microbial contamination (>1 x 10⁶ CFU/ml). Consequently, the milk is rejected by local dairy processing industries (IPS), leading to financial losses for farmers who lack the resources to process milk into higher-value products. Proposed Solutions 1. Implementation of Good Dairy Farming Practices (GDFP): GDFP establishes standards for optimal dairy farming, including daily maintenance, feeding, sanitation, disease prevention, and milk handling to produce high-quality and safe milk. This practice ensures healthy and productive livestock. 2. Product Diversification: Developing diverse dairy products tailored to consumer preferences will increase marketability and provide farmers with alternative revenue streams. 3. Marketing Strategies and Branding: Strategic marketing and branding will enhance product competitiveness, expanding market reach and ensuring better returns for farmers.

core_fields.title: Vertical Block Farming for Urban Land-constrained Communities
core_fields.description: This project targets land-constrained urban communities, including refugees and stay-at-home mothers in Kampala. This innovative project will install vertical farms in greenhouses using a block farming model to optimize space and productivity. The initiative aims to combat hunger, starvation, and malnutrition by empowering beneficiaries to grow their own food sustainably. By integrating organic gardening training, market linkages, and value addition, VMG aims to strengthen food security and build economic resilience within urban vulnerable communities.
core_fields.abstract: Uganda faces a critical food insecurity challenge. As of January 2023, approximately 16.4 million Ugandans struggled with insufficient food consumption (EPRCUG). Alarmingly, 28% of households experienced food insecurity in 2022, with three in ten skipping meals or going a day without food (Monitor). This issue is exacerbated in urban areas, where limited land availability compounds the problem. Globally, solving food insecurity would require farmland almost the size of Brazil an impractical solution. VMG s Vertical Block Farming provides an innovative response to this crisis by maximizing food production in land-constrained urban environments. Through installing vertical farms in greenhouses under a block farming model, VMG transforms small urban spaces into highly efficient food production units. This approach addresses hunger and malnutrition while reducing the environmental footprint of traditional farming. The system integrates vermicomposting, ensuring sustainable nutrient recycling. Beneficiaries, including refugees and stay-at-home mothers in Kampala and Wakiso, receive training in farming techniques, value addition, and market linkages to improve livelihoods. Immediate benefits include increased access to fresh, nutritious food and enhanced household income. Over the long term, the solution promotes food security, reduces urban hunger, and contributes to climate-smart agriculture by optimizing land and resource use. VMG s innovative approach transforms food production, providing a scalable and sustainable solution for urban food insecurity.

core_fields.title: Smart biocapsules for sustainable agriculture: reducing agrochemical use and enhancing food safety globally.
core_fields.description: Vexxel develops innovative protein-based biocapsules that enable precise, on-demand delivery of inputs in agriculture. These biodegradable, non-toxic capsules reduce agrochemical usage by up to 90%, enhance crop protection, and improve food safety. By integrating biosensors that detect pathogens or environmental conditions, our technology promotes sustainable farming, lowers costs, and minimizes environmental impact. This project advances global food systems by improving access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food while addressing planetary health challenges.
core_fields.abstract: The global food system faces critical challenges: excessive agrochemical use leads to environmental damage, high costs, and growing resistance from pathogens, while only 1-5% of applied chemicals reach their intended target. This problem is relevant because it exacerbates environmental degradation, compromises food safety, and increases economic burdens on farmers, hindering sustainable agriculture worldwide. Inefficiencies contribute to unsafe food, soil degradation, and climate change, as highlighted by the FAO, which reports that agrochemical overuse is a major driver of agricultural environmental harm. Vexxel addresses this with smart, protein-based biocapsules, an innovative, biodegradable, and non-toxic solution. These biocapsules integrate advanced biosensors to detect pathogens or environmental conditions and release active compounds precisely when needed. Pilot tests have demonstrated a 90% reduction in agrochemical usage, cutting farmers' costs by 60% while ensuring effective pathogen control. This minimizes environmental impact and makes sustainable farming more accessible and profitable. This solution is rooted in cutting-edge protein engineering, leveraging proprietary nanotechnology that ensures scalability and adaptability to existing agricultural practices. Unlike traditional methods, Vexxel s technology empowers nature to decide when inputs are required, reducing waste and increasing efficiency. Immediate benefits include safer food, healthier soils, and reduced farmer costs, enabling compliance with regulations and access to premium markets. Treating 30,000 hectares with Vexxel's biocapsules reduces 77,000 tons of CO₂eq equivalent to avoiding 320,833 short-haul flights or 17,500 flights around the world per passenger. Validated eco-impact studies demonstrate this significant impact aligns with global climate goals.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Agriculture for the Batwa Community: Cultivation of Irish Potatoes and Beans.
core_fields.description: Land access and food security are leading challenges of Batwa. The $18,000 US dollars grant is vital in, enabling land access, friendly gardening practices that improve soil health and increase crop yields for sustainable food source for the community. Trainings will focus on organic gardening practices, post harvest management, access to indigenous vegetables, saving groups and resilience to climate change. Overall, the project will address nutritional needs, bio-diversity, awareness, improve well-being and achieve self-reliance.
core_fields.abstract: The indigenous Batwa community of Kisoro-Uganda are part of originally hunter-gatherers and pygmies of Africa, lived in harmony with nature and wildlife. In 1991-92 Batwa were forcefully evicted from forests because of need to gazette Bwindi and Mgahinga National Parks, and international interests in mountain Gorilla conservation. The Batwa received zero compensation and their source of livelihood interrupted. They have faced numerous challenges like loss of cultural heritage, landlessness, food shortage, extreme poverty and marginalization. This gardening project aims to empower the Batwa people through sustainable agriculture, focusing on cultivation of Irish Potatoes and Beans. These crops are nutrient-dense, easy to grow, and can improve food security while providing a potential income source. Virunga Massive Community Conservation in partnership with Global Food System Challenge GFSC will support the Batwa to revive their traditions, improve food security and strengthen connection to cultural heritage/identity through sustainable gardening practices and land access. Objectives: To provide access to seedlings for food security and improve the nutritional intake of the Batwa community. To empower the Batwa community with potential access to gardening space. To provide education and training on sustainable agricultural practices and conservation. To enhance the Batwa community through potential post-harvest management of seed and sale of surplus produce.

core_fields.title: Strengthening the Resilience and Economic Empowerment of Marginalized Women in the South
core_fields.description: The project will focus on value chains with significant commercialization potential in the national and international markets for certain sectors. Aims to contribute to improving the food and nutritional security of the population in Southern. Specifically, the action will increase the income and economic empowerment of women by contributing to the reduction of vertical and horizontal socio-economic inequalities, while increasing their resilience as well as that of their families, communities through food and nutritional growth.
core_fields.abstract: The aim is to address the recurring financial issues faced by women with their low resilience, economic marginalization, lack of empowerment, low productive capacity (production and agricultural processing) to improve food and nutritional availability in their region. About 44% of Haitian households are headed by women, and most of these women live in extreme poverty. Women are concentrated in the informal sector, particularly affected by unemployment, and hold unskilled and poorly paid jobs. 61% of micro and small business leaders are women, especially in trade, one of the few survival strategies available to impoverished women. For most marginalized women living in urban areas, small trade is a survival option that meets an immediate need. Due to gender-based discrimination, lack of mobility, and lack of access to markets, women are often excluded from value chains. Women who engage in value chains are more inclined to manage work and income from production with low-cost equipment, due to discriminatory access to capital and property, especially land. Here, these statistics show the magnitude and urgency of the issues to be addressed for the benefit of women and the entire Haitian economy.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Seeding Program for Rural Farmers in Northeastern Nigeria
core_fields.description: The Sustainable Seeding Program for Rural Farmers in Northeastern Nigeria develops, introduces, and ensures access to improved, regenerative seeds for small- and large-scale farmers through research. It integrates greenhouse technology and climate-smart farming to enable year-round production of nutritious vegetables and fruits. Addressing food insecurity, promoting sustainability, and enhancing livelihoods, the program benefits women and youth, improves market access, and builds resilience against climate change in the region.
core_fields.abstract: The Sustainable Seeding Program for Rural Farmers in Northeastern Nigeria is an innovative solution that addresses food insecurity, low agricultural productivity, and climate vulnerability. The program focuses on providing improved, regenerative seeds and introducing greenhouse technology to enable year-round production of nutritious vegetables and fruits. This is particularly relevant for small- and large-scale farmers who face challenges such as climate unpredictability, poor soil health, and limited access to quality seeds. The program leverages research-based, regenerative agricultural practices that restore soil health and enhance crop resilience, ensuring better yields and a more sustainable farming model. The integration of greenhouse technology ensures a controlled environment, reducing dependency on seasonal variations and promoting consistent food production. The solution is rooted in climate-smart farming principles, utilizing water-efficient irrigation systems and organic fertilizers to minimize environmental impact. The adoption of improved seeds also promotes crop diversity and long-term soil regeneration. Immediate benefits include increased food availability, improved income for farmers, and enhanced market access. Farmers, particularly women and youth, will experience greater empowerment through skill-building and job creation. Sustainable benefits include improved food security, resilience to climate change, and the restoration of local ecosystems through regenerative practices. Communities will benefit from better nutrition, local economic growth, and a more sustainable food system. This approach not only supports farmers but also contributes to broader environmental sustainability and societal resilience.

core_fields.title: Waste to Nutrition: Women-Led Sustainable Manufacturing for Safe, Nutritious, and Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: Our project empowers low-income women to build sustainable food manufacturing businesses using renewable energy-powered hubs and waste-to-wealth solutions. By converting organic waste into biogas for energy to power the hub, and biofertilizer for farming by our farming partners, we improve clean energy access, food safety, and climate resilience. Through training, resources, market access, and sustainable practices, we help women transform homegrown ideas into thriving enterprises, driving food security, economic growth, and sustainable communities.
core_fields.abstract: In rural communities in Nigeria, women possess homegrown knowledge of food production, but a lack of funds, resources, and training prevents them from turning this knowledge into viable enterprises. As a result, farm produce goes to waste due to the absence of processing facilities, while communities depend on imported, additive-filled foods. Additionally, these communities face drought, flooding, and low farming yields, further threatening food security and livelihoods. WEM HUB Africa addresses these challenges through a holistic solution that combines: Renewable Energy-Powered Manufacturing Hubs: Providing access to shared facilities powered by biogas and solar energy, reducing costs and enabling sustainable food production even during drought-related power disruptions. BIOCOIN Program: Transforming organic waste into biogas for energy and biofertilizer for farming. This improves soil health, boosts crop resilience to drought and flooding, and enhances moisture retention, leading to higher farming yields. Training and Market Access: Equipping women with skills and pathways to produce safe, nutritious food and bring products to market, reducing dependence on imported foods and minimizing post-harvest losses. This innovation mitigates flooding by reducing organic waste clogging drainage systems and ensures access to clean energy and biofertilizer, supporting sustainable agriculture. Immediate benefits include improved livelihoods, food security, and health outcomes. Long-term benefits include climate resilience, reduced environmental pollution, and stronger local economies. By empowering women and transforming waste into resources, WEM HUB Africa builds resilient communities where everyone has access to safe, nutritious, and affordable food despite environmental challenges.

core_fields.title: Shameta; From Tradition to Maternal Nutrition to Improve Nutritional Status of Lactating Mothers in Ethiopia
core_fields.description: Shameta is a traditional porridge made from grains, commonly consumed by lactating mothers for recovery, strength, and breast milk production. However, research has highlighted a gap between community perceptions and the actual nutritional value and safety of Shameta. This initiative seeks to enhance the nutritional status of lactating mothers through food-to-food fortification and the development of starter cultures. By incorporating nutrient-dense ingredients such as high-quality protein maize, soybean, barley, and linseed, the project aims to boost Shameta's nutritional profile. Additionally, it focuses on improving shelf life, creating effective packaging materials, and developing starter cultures. To raise awareness about the improved Shameta, the project will organize workshops, and training sessions, and produce a documentary showcasing the preparation process and utilization benefits.
core_fields.abstract: The nutritional status of lactating mothers in Ethiopia is influenced by food insecurity, poverty, cultural practices, and poor dietary diversity (Haileslassie et al., 2013; Alemayehu et al., 2015; Moges et al., 2018; Kejela et al., 2019; IFRC, 2021). To address this, a multifaceted approach is needed, including better access to nutrient-rich foods. Upgrading traditional fermented foods like Shameta, porridge made from grains and used for lactating mothers to the purpose of recovery, strength and breast milk production can provide affordable and nutritious food. However, studies revealed a gap between community perceptions and the actual nutritional value and safety of Shameta (Kitessa et al., 2022a; 2022b; 2024), indicating the need for further research on its impact on mothers and infants. Optimizing the processing conditions and ingredient ratios of Shameta is crucial for ensuring its safety, quality, and nutritional values. Using high-quality protein maize (rich in lysine and tryptophan), barley ( -glucan), soybeans (packed with protein, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and calcium), and linseed (rich in omega-3 fatty acids) enhances the flour nutritional profile for shmaeta preparation. A well-defined starter culture further improves fermentation control, safety, and consistency. Exploring its potential to promote breast milk production and support infant growth is also a topic of interest. Additionally, evaluating the shelf-life of flour used for Shameta preparation and selecting appropriate packaging materials are essential for efficient distribution and transportation across regions. Upon successful project completion, end users will gain immediate access to affordable, optimized flour and starter cultures to prepare Shameta at home or for business purposes. This will promote enhanced maternal and infant health, boost breast milk production, support optimal infant growth, and foster job creation. Over the long term, the product becomes affordable throughout the country, and both mother's and infant's health benefits, and economic empowerment.

core_fields.title: Climate Resilient Digital Agronomy Platform for the Farmers and Professional Growers
core_fields.description: This platform delivers climate-resilient crop advisory and agronomy solutions to smallholder farmers and professional growers, enabling cost savings on inputs like agrochemicals and fertilizers, efficient use of natural resources (soil and water), and reduced greenhouse gas emissions from agricultural activities.
core_fields.abstract: Problem: Scientific Information gap in the farmer and growers communities for climate resilient farming practices. Less crop diversification among farmers causing commoditization of crop output leading less market price. No incentive is given to farmers for growing crops through climate friendly farming practices Innovation and Solutions : This innovation bridges the scientific information gap among farmers and growers by providing tailored climate-resilient crop advisory and agronomy practices. It equips smallholder farmers and professional growers with actionable insights, ensuring efficient use of inputs like agrochemicals and fertilizers, optimizing soil and water usage, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The platform addresses two critical problems: low crop diversification and lack of incentives for climate-friendly practices. Limited crop diversification leads to market saturation, reducing profitability, while traditional farming methods often exacerbate environmental degradation. Through advanced digital tools, IoT devices, and real-time data analysis, the platform offers precise recommendations for crop diversification, sustainable resource management, and climate-smart farming techniques. These insights are based on cutting-edge research and climate modeling, ensuring actionable and region-specific solutions. Immediate benefits include: For Farmers: Lower input costs, increased profitability through market-relevant crop diversification, and incentives for adopting eco-friendly practices. For Consumers: Access to sustainably grown, high-quality crops. For the Environment: Reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved soil health, and water conservation. For Society: Promotion of sustainable agriculture, enhancing food security and resilience against climate change. This innovation transforms agriculture into a sustainable, climate-resilient practice, benefitting farmers, consumers, and the planet.

core_fields.title: Empowering marginalized Ugandan communities with sustainable farming and entrepreneurship from farm to fork.
core_fields.description: Women Smiles Uganda s "Farm to Fork" project empowers marginalized communities, including women with disabilities, by providing training in sustainable urban farming and entrepreneurship. The initiative enhances food security, promotes income generation, and fosters self-reliance through tailored support and resources. By focusing on vulnerable groups, the project addresses poverty and food insecurity, equipping participants to grow food, sell surplus produce, and build sustainable livelihoods while strengthening community resilience and environmental sustainability.
core_fields.abstract: Women Smiles Uganda s innovation, the "Farm to Fork" concept, addresses food insecurity and poverty among marginalized Ugandan communities, including youth and women with disabilities, by introducing sustainable urban farming and entrepreneurship. The problem it solves is twofold: limited access to nutritious healthy food and insufficient income opportunities in informal settlements and rural areas. This is especially relevant as urbanization and economic challenges strain local food systems and livelihoods. Our solution leverages vertical farming techniques, which maximize food production in small spaces using minimal resources like water and soil. Participants are trained to grow high-yield crops, manage post-harvest processes, and market their produce. Entrepreneurship skills further empower them to sell surplus products and create sustainable businesses. Our approach is based on insights from sustainable agriculture and urban resilience studies, highlighting how low-cost, eco-friendly techniques can transform small spaces into productive farms. By integrating farming with entrepreneurship, our model ensures both immediate and long-term benefits. Benefits: Immediate: Access to fresh, nutritious food, reduced household food expenses, and new income streams. Sustainable: Improved livelihoods, self-reliance, community food systems resilience, and reduced environmental impact through resource-efficient farming practices. End users, including women, youth, schools, and communities, gain economic independence, better nutrition, and environmental awareness. Our innovation contributes to societal progress by reducing poverty, empowering vulnerable groups, and fostering sustainable development

core_fields.title: Farmers Post: Getting Food from Farms to Families
core_fields.description: Farmers Post aims to transform our food system by directly connecting farmers to consumers using the United States Postal Service (USPS) reducing food waste, supporting small farms, and delivering fresh produce to those in need. WWF has advanced Farmers Post from concept to reality through research, partnerships, and pilots. With the USPS on board, we re poised to expand pilots and test packaging solutions, gathering critical insights to scale Farmers Post for a nationwide roll-out.
core_fields.abstract: Across the US, some of the most food-insecure counties are the same ones producing abundant fresh produce yet much of it never reaches those in need. Our current food system fails to connect farms directly to consumers, leaving small farmers struggling to profit while millions lack access to healthy food. Just one in ten adults in the US eats enough fruits and vegetables, yet up to 40% of fresh produce grown in this country is wasted. There is increasing recognition of this problem and a broader push to address it through Food is Medicine (FIM) initiatives, which focus on local food systems and preventative healthcare through healthy diets; however, last mile delivery and consumer reach remain major pain points. Farmers Post addresses these challenges by leveraging USPS logistics expertise to deliver fresh produce from farms to consumers, reducing waste, improving access to nutritious food, and supporting small farmers. With IFT s support, WWF has advanced this from concept to reality. What started as research on viable solutions and feasibility has now moved into the planning and implementation stages. Through key partnerships and pilot programs with 4P Foods, a Virginia-based food hub, and Healthy PlanEat, a Connecticut-based sustainable food tech platform, we have refined the Farmers Post model, inspiring USPS to explore a full Farmers Post program. By creating avenues for small farmers to ship directly to consumers, while leveraging the work of food hubs and FIM initiatives, Farmers Post offers a transformative path forward for farmers, consumers, and the environment.

core_fields.abstract: Agro-Match addresses the critical challenges facing Africa's agricultural sector, where smallholder farmers and traders struggle with limited access to financing, inefficient supply chains, and post-harvest losses that reduce income and contribute to food insecurity. Traditional lenders often reject agro-traders due to perceived risks, while farmers face barriers to entering larger markets. These issues, compounded by a lack of infrastructure and market transparency, hinder growth and sustainability. Agro-Match aims to bridge these gaps by providing an innovative platform that connects agro-traders with investors, ensuring access to capital, reducing waste, and fostering sustainable trade practices. This solution not only boosts farmer incomes but also strengthens food security and resilience in the agricultural value chain.

core_fields.title: Garden To Table Pipeline (G2T) Chicago
core_fields.description: The G2T Pipeline is a sustainable and circular food system that revolves around nutrient rich locally grown produce from 23 community gardens on 8,100 sf of land, strategically distributed across the community. Five local nonprofit partners support gardens and distribute food to anyone in need. By working together this partnership grows 13,000 pounds of produce, distributes 48,000 prepared meals, rescued 250,000 pounds of food and serves 87,738 individuals each year.
core_fields.abstract: North Lawndale is a community of 35,000 individuals served by one sub-par mid-size grocery store. While we are located in the city of Chicago, there is no traditional local food supply in our community. The G2T Pipeline is the community s response to simply feed our neighbors by growing the most nutrient dense locally grown produce and distributing it at 23 local gardens and three community food hubs. Statistical data can be provided to support this reality if requested. Based on the lines of individuals forming early for fresh produce and prepared meals at our 3 food hubs the need is dramatic. In 2023 more than 112,000 human encounters occurred at G2T Pipeline food/meal distributions. This number is 3 times larger than the community we serve. Our non-traditional food supply is growing exponentially in terms of production, distribution, growing capacity, manpower and financial support; however the lines of individuals waiting for food exceed the supply we have.

core_fields.title: Waste4Food
core_fields.description: Waste4Food is an innovative program that tackles plastic waste and food insecurity by exchanging plastic waste for farm produce. Partnering with local farmers and waste collectors, we aim to reduce plastic waste, promote sustainable agriculture, and provide affordable nutritious food to underserved communities.
core_fields.abstract: Plastic waste and food insecurity are two pressing issues affecting communities in Lagos and Ogun States, Nigeria. In these regions, plastic waste clogs waterways, harms wildlife, and exacerbates flooding, while many families struggle to access nutritious food. Waste4Food addresses these challenges by creating a closed-loop system where plastic waste is collected and exchanged for farm produce. Our innovation partners local farmers, waste collectors, and community groups to: - Reduce plastic waste in landfills and waterways - Increase access to fresh, nutritious produce for underserved communities - Support sustainable agriculture and boost local economies Our solution leverages insights from circular economy principles, behavioral economics, and community-based initiatives. By providing an economic incentive for waste collection and offering affordable produce, we empower individuals and communities to make sustainable choices. Benefits include: - Reduced plastic waste and pollution - Increased food security and nutrition - Economic benefits for farmers, waste collectors, and local communities - Community engagement and education on sustainable practices By addressing these interconnected challenges, Waste4Food creates a more sustainable, equitable food system for Lagos and Ogun States.
