core_fields.title: PANGAN Program: Revitalizing indigenous farming and building a sustainable food system for a climate-resilient bioeconomy and community
core_fields.description: The PANGAN Program addresses food insecurity in West Timor by revitalizing indigenous farming practices, promoting diverse and nutritious local food, and utilizing effective technologies. PANGAN s next phase pilots a Local Food Hub, a scalable model connecting farmers and micro-agribusinesses regenerative produce to local markets, building community bioeconomy and improving access to nutritious food. It will also continue raising awareness and building knowledge on indigenous regenerative farming s role in creating a resilient, sustainable food system.
core_fields.abstract: In West Timor, food insecurity is a critical issue exacerbated by the climate crisis, disproportionately affecting underserved communities. Limited access to diverse and nutritious food leads to widespread malnutrition, with the region experiencing the highest stunting rates in Indonesia. Degenerative farming practices, such as monoculture and excessive use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, degrade soil health and reduce productivity. These challenges are further compounded by post-harvest losses due to inadequate storage and preservation. While initiatives like community gardens and regenerative farming have been introduced, many lack economic sustainability and fail to align with local livelihoods. This results in low adoption of sustainable practices, perpetuating vulnerable food systems, poor food access, and worsening community health. Addressing these issues requires solutions that integrate sustainability with economic incentives. The PANGAN Program has been working with farmers to test post-harvest technologies such as solar dryers and black soldier fly cultivation, while also revitalizing indigenous regenerative farming practices to enhance sustainability, productivity, and resilience in local agriculture. Building on two years of implementing this program, we have designed a Local Food Hub as a scalable, community-based solution to strengthen the local economy and food system. This hub will connect smallholder farmers and micro-agribusinesses practicing indigenous regenerative farming with local markets, facilitating access to fresh produce and value-added products. It will also serve as an education center, run by local food producers, offering economic empowerment opportunities while improving food availability and nutrition, and building a resilient, sustainable bioeconomy for the region s underserved populations.

The innovation is based on scientific insights into sustainable farming techniques, such as agroecology and precision agriculture, which promote biodiversity, enhance nutrient delivery, and ensure long-term agricultural productivity. Furthermore, we will engage communities through educational campaigns to raise awareness about sustainable practices and healthy food choices. Immediate benefits include improved crop yields, better soil health, reduced food waste, and increased access to nutritious, affordable food. Over time, the project will help create a more resilient food system that benefits farmers, consumers, and the environment. By fostering local food production, the initiative will strengthen community food sovereignty, improve public health, and reduce the environmental impact of agriculture

core_fields.title: Damila Children Nutrition Flour
core_fields.description: The Damila Children Nutrition Flour project aims to combat malnutrition in children by providing fortified flour enriched with essential vitamins and minerals. The project supports local farmers by supplying high-quality seeds and training, ensuring a sustainable supply of nutritious ingredients. This initiative helps improve children's health and supports community development.
core_fields.abstract: Child malnutrition is a critical issue that results in stunted growth, weakened immune systems, and cognitive impairments, primarily due to the lack of nutritious and affordable food. Damila Children Nutrition Flour offers a solution with a blend of silver fish, carrots, Irish potatoes, milk, yellow maize, and soya beans, providing a balanced mix of proteins, vitamins, and minerals. This product enhances child health, cognitive development, and supports local agriculture by empowering farmers with quality seeds and training. Immediate benefits include improved nutrition and economic empowerment, while sustainable benefits encompass poverty reduction, community resilience, and positive environmental impact. This initiative is highly relevant as it meets the urgent need for accessible nutrition, leveraging local resources for long-term sustainability and community empowerment.

core_fields.title: Ensuring Food Security of the Gurage Zone through Modern Agricultural Practices
core_fields.description: Gurage communities are facing environmental and climate change vulnerability following degradation of soil, change in weather conditions, occurrence of crops and animal diseases put their livelihood in all rounded vulnerability. Majority cannot feed themselves and living in a question of survival. The situation could be transformed with minimum support to the households with basic inputs such as seedlings of high-value crops, soil conservation and climate change adaptation and mitigation technologies, and trainings on sustainable agriculture.
core_fields.abstract: Incidence of poverty in Ethiopia is among the highest in the world. In some regions of the country, it reaches as high as 70% and close to 85% in the worst case. The country suffers from serious environmental degradation due to effect of population pressure, expansion of croplands, and reliance on fuel-wood as the major source of energy supply and over grazing. Productive safety-net program of the government and resilience-relief-rehabilitation-development programs of a number of civil society organizations and non-governmental supports are vital pillars that maintain the survival of the society. Guraghe Zone is one of the most vulnerable areas in the country. The community is highly dependent on subsistence agriculture as justified by 88% of the population engaged, but incredibly unable to feed itself and dependent uniquely on its children in towns and on safety-net program. This calls for attention to curb the problem and transform the sector. For this, innovative and strategic agricultural direction should be pursued. Zebidar, in collaboration with the local government, has come up with a mid-term strategic plan to address the problem. Hence, the project s overall objective is to ensure food security and conserve the natural environment via integrated watershed management by introducing improved varieties of perennial trees of Avocado, Papaya, Apple, Mango and selected vegetables. A seedlings nursery design will be studied to establish the site with a capacity of 500,000 seedlings. The government is willing and committed to avail necessary land for the nursery. Project infrastructure and irrigation scheme will be constructed.

core_fields.title: Digitally Empowering Smallholder Farmers for Agroecological Transitions and Resilient Food Systems in Africa
core_fields.description: Our project leverages digital financial tools and market access pathways to empower Africa s smallholder farmers in transitioning to agroecological practices. Through a mobile wallet, multi-account debit card, and AI-powered credit scoring, we provide tailored savings, working capital, and insurance. By connecting farmers to verified buyers, we enhance productivity, reduce post-harvest losses, and boost incomes. This approach fosters sustainability, resilience, and inclusivity, transforming agri-food systems across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers, who produce 70% of Africa's food, face significant financial exclusion and limited market access, with over $250 billion in unmet annual financing needs. These barriers hinder the adoption of agroecological practices essential for improving productivity, resilience, and sustainability. Farmers struggle to access secure savings, working capital, and insurance, while inefficiencies in market linkages reduce their income and increase post-harvest losses. eMaisha Pay solves this problem by leveraging digital financial tools and market linkages. Using a mobile wallet and multi-account debit card, farmers access tailored financial solutions, including secure savings, working capital for climate-smart inputs, and insurance to safeguard against climate shocks. Our AI-powered credit scoring system assesses creditworthiness, enabling farmers to access loans without collateral. Additionally, the platform connects farmers to verified buyers, ensuring better produce prices and reducing reliance on exploitative middlemen. This innovation is driven by insights from eMaisha Pay s extensive work with over 14,000 farmers in Uganda, revealing that access to tailored financial tools and reliable markets significantly improves agroecological adoption. Immediate benefits include increased productivity (up to 28% per acre), reduced post-harvest losses (18%), and higher incomes (25% increase in produce prices). The platform also promotes inclusivity, with 68% of credit accessed by women and youth, fostering equity and resilience in rural communities. Sustainably, the innovation drives agroecological transitions, supporting food security, environmental health, and socioeconomic development, transforming Africa s agri-food systems into equitable and resilient ecosystems.

core_fields.description: Our project uses SMS agricultural advisory services to support over 550,000 smallholder farmers in building climate resilience, improving productivity, and reducing food waste. By providing real-time weather and crop/livestock management information, we help farmers optimise sustainable practices, enhance nutrition, and strengthen food security. Our solution empowers farmers with actionable data, promoting healthier diets and more sustainable food systems. With digital tools, we aim to drive both environmental and economic benefits for communities facing food
core_fields.abstract: iShamba provides farmers with tailored agricultural advice via SMS, helping them improve productivity, reduce food waste, and enhance sustainability. In regions with limited access to agricultural extension services, our solution bridges the information gap, offering weather updates, crop/livestock management tips, and market insights. By empowering farmers with practical, real-time information, we help them make informed decisions that increase yields and reduce environmental impact. This solution addresses the challenge of low productivity and food insecurity, especially in areas vulnerable to climate change. iShamba s approach is rooted in agricultural best practices and local knowledge, ensuring relevance to the farmers we serve. Through our service, farmers can adopt climate-smart practices, reduce post-harvest losses, and improve food safety. The innovation is based on the insight that smallholder farmers in remote areas face significant barriers in accessing relevant, timely information. By leveraging mobile technology, we are able to deliver high-impact solutions without requiring internet access or complex devices. The immediate benefits include increased quality crop yields, reduced food waste, and improved income for farmers. Over the long term, our service contributes to a more resilient food system, enhanced environmental sustainability, and healthier communities. This solution benefits not just farmers but also consumers/communities by ensuring more nutritious, affordable food through efficient agricultural practices.

core_fields.title: Enhancing subsistence agriculture and food exports in Africa through iWina Lab's Digital Compliance Platform
core_fields.description: Iwina Lab empowers African agricultural SMEs with innovative digital tools to tackle export rejection, optimize value chains, and ensure compliance with international standards. By integrating real-time data, predictive analytics, and AI, we boost competitiveness, enhance market access, and promote sustainability. Our solutions align with SDG goals, driving economic growth and fostering trade across borders.
core_fields.abstract: Our innovation addresses the persistent challenge of export rejection in Africa s agricultural sector, where stringent international standards hinder access to lucrative global markets. This issue disproportionately affects SMEs and smallholder farmers, who often lack the technical expertise, resources, and real-time information necessary for compliance. Our solution leverages advanced digital technologies, including real-time data integration, predictive analytics, and AI-driven insights, to tackle these challenges. By providing a platform that monitors compliance, forecasts risks, and offers tailored recommendations, we empower agricultural SMEs to meet international standards, reduce waste, and enhance productivity. This approach stems from a deep understanding of the systemic gaps in trade compliance and market access, gained through research and engagement with stakeholders across the value chain. Our technology offers immediate benefits by reducing rejection rates, increasing profitability, and enabling seamless access to global markets. In the long term, the platform fosters sustainable practices by minimizing post-harvest losses, promoting eco-friendly farming methods, and reducing environmental social and governance issues from inefficient processes. Communities benefit from increased income, job creation, and a more resilient agricultural economy. For society and the environment, the innovation supports food security, sustainable development, and aligns with global climate goals. By bridging the gap between local agricultural producers and international markets, our solution drives inclusive economic growth and sustainable trade.

core_fields.title: Sustainable Farming
core_fields.description: This project aims to establish a sustainable yam farm that prioritizes environmental conservation and economic viability. By implementing sustainable farming practices, we aim to increase yam production, improve soil health, conserve water resources, and reduce reliance on harmful chemicals in Obode Ainu, Oju Local Government Area Benue State, North Central Nigeria. This initiative will contribute to food security, generate income for farmers, and promote sustainable agriculture in the local community and beyond.
core_fields.abstract: Yam, a staple food crop in many African countries, faces challenges such as low yields, soil degradation, and water scarcity. To address these issues, this project proposes a sustainable yam farming approach that integrates innovative techniques and environmentally friendly practices. By implementing sustainable farming methods like crop rotation, organic fertilization, and efficient irrigation systems, we aim to: Increase yam production: Enhance soil fertility, optimize water usage, and minimize pest and disease outbreaks. Improve soil health: Restore soil nutrients, reduce erosion, and promote long-term agricultural sustainability. Conserve water resources: Implement efficient irrigation techniques to minimize water usage. Reduce reliance on harmful chemicals: Promote organic farming practices to protect the environment and human health. This innovative solution leverages scientific knowledge and local expertise to develop a sustainable farming model that benefits both farmers and consumers. By increasing yam production, improving food security, and promoting environmental conservation, this project contributes to the overall well-being of the community in Obode Ainu, Oju Local Government Area, North Central, Nigeria and beyond.

core_fields.title: Empowering Smallholder Farmers with Climate-Smart Practices for Improved Food Systems and Resilience in West Africa.
core_fields.description: We will leverage our digital platform, input delivery, and tailored agricultural training to scale a pilot that increases smallholder farmer adoption of agroecological practices in Mali. Our focus will be on supporting farmers to improve their yields and income while investing in the long-term health of their soils by reducing reliance on chemical fertilizer and maximizing soil fertility through regenerative agricultural practices.
core_fields.abstract: In West Africa, there are 60 million farmers, a large proportion of whom live on less than $2 per day. Farmers face numerous challenges that keep them in a cycle of poverty: -Farmers don t have money when they need it for planting. Their cash flow is strongest at harvest time; however, they lack access to bank accounts to save money to reinvest in their farms the next planting season; -Farmers lack access to high-quality inputs; -Farmers lack access to training on improved agronomic practices; -Many farmers depend on one rainy season for their farming and have no other income. myAgro s solution disrupts this cycle: -Our mobile layaway platform allows farmers to save money in small increments toward purchasing a package of high-quality seeds and fertilizer; -myAgro procures and delivers the inputs to farmers in time for planting season; -myAgro provides farmers with climate-smart training to improve soil fertility and maximize harvests; -myAgro provides farmers with access to dry season products that diversify their food sources and income. This model was created by innovating on ideas generated by farmers. Our founder, Anushka, was working on microloan repayment for smallholder farmers at an organization in Africa. When some farmers asked her if they could pre-pay their loans, she recognized they were describing savings and designed a platform to help them save. myAgro s solution is proven to increase yields and income at scale. In 2023, our 200k farmers, on average, grew 2.5 times more food and earned $164 more than control farmers.

core_fields.title: JH 7
core_fields.description: The project will involve sinking/drilling a borehole, installation of solar powered water pump installing a 40 cubic meter raised fabricated steel tank and reticulation of water to the project beneficiaries to ensure enough water for domestic, livestock and drip irrigation for 0.25 acres drip irrigation systems at household level, starting of a community tree/ fruit nursery to enhance tree cover.
core_fields.abstract: The project targets 100 Households who will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme with an average of 5 members per household increasing the number of beneficiaries to 500. The population is increasing with new settlement of absent land owners and acquirement of land through purchase. Drilling of the Wiumiririe borehole and distribution of water to Wiumiririe Centre and 100 households will greatly alleviate the suffering of women and young girl children who have to walk far in search of water for domestic and livestock This will save time and money which can be used to attend to some other domestic chores and economic activities as small-scale farming. Improvement of farming through 0.25 acres drip irrigation system per family will initially translate to 25 acres additional irrigated land under commercial horticultural crops which will promote small scale farming. The health and safety of the target community will be improved through consumption of balance diet and adequate food; thus, food security will be enhanced and reduction of malnutrition. Selling of the produce from the irrigated plots will ensure there is adequate food on the table and money in pockets thus triggering the development in the area. Capacity building mainly on farming practices which will target all the families will go a long way in transforming the community from pastoralists as a way of life to commercial farming. Starting of a tree and fruit nursery will improve the tree cover which is very low in the area, provide materials for construction and fencing.

core_fields.title: CLEAN ENERGY SOLUTIONS FOR POST HARVEST PROCESSING
core_fields.description: RVM Nepal is implementing clean energy solutions for post-harvest processing in Nepal, focusing on reducing energy consumption, improving storage conditions, and minimizing post-harvest losses. By integrating thermal energy storage systems, solar-powered solutions, and AI-driven monitoring, RVM Nepal aims to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and increase the sustainability of agriculture and agro-processing. This initiative will benefit smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and rural communities, contributing to food security and sustainable agricultural practices in Nepal.
core_fields.abstract: RVM Nepal addresses the critical problem of high post-harvest losses and inefficiency in cold storage and food processing systems, especially in rural Nepal. Inadequate post-harvest management, energy-intensive cold storage, and lack of reliable solutions to preserve agricultural produce contribute to significant food waste and financial losses for farmers. This problem directly impacts food security and economic stability in rural communities. RVM Nepal s innovative solution involves integrating clean energy technologies, such as solar power, thermal energy storage systems, and AI-driven monitoring, to reduce energy consumption and extend the shelf life of perishable agricultural products. By implementing Phase Change Materials (PCM) for energy storage, RVM Nepal provides a sustainable, cost-effective alternative to traditional refrigeration methods. These systems use solar energy to generate cooling and store excess energy for use during off-hours, thus ensuring optimal storage conditions for perishable products. The solution is scientifically backed by advancements in renewable energy and thermal energy storage, addressing both environmental concerns and operational inefficiencies. Immediate benefits include reduced energy costs, increased profitability for farmers, and a significant reduction in food waste. Long-term advantages include improved food security, enhanced sustainability, and greater economic opportunities for rural communities. This approach not only benefits farmers and producers but also has positive effects on the environment by reducing the carbon footprint of traditional cold storage methods.
